title: I would recommend taking 5 minutes to read the instruction before beginning ...
text:
This is one product that you will never be sorry you purchased. The name should be “Freaky Fast” and not PROBOX.
For years I struggled with external SATA drives but limited by the USB interface. Even USB 3 gave only about 35 MB real through put and required 4 separate external enclosures, with power cables and USB connections. It was a mess but it did work.
As an option I created a server 16 with several internal drives. The through put was over 100 MB/sec. I use Acronis backup and on nights when a full backups were done, an average was 14 hours.
I purchased the PROBOX for under $100, less than I had paid for the USB to SATA enclosures. Added a Vantec PCIe card with 2 external channels for under $30.
Now, my 4, 4 TB drives are located in a small, professional looking PROBOX with a footprint only slightly larger than a 3.5 inch drive. Through put from Acronis backup software as measured by “Task Manager” is over 380 MB/sec. Sometimes peak speeds may reach as high as 430 MB/s.
Now I can do a near 1TB backup in slightly more time than eating breakfast.
I do not know how or why the through put is so high. In my 50 plus years in this business, I have never been so thrilled with any product.
This is not a standalone raid box though it may be configured as such.
I would recommend taking 5 minutes to read the instruction before beginning installation. If you are like me, and believe “Instructions are Useless so why bother” then don’t, however these instruction are clear, concise, easy to read and they WORK.
This is cute little box with a ton of personality.
YOU WILL NOT BE DISAPPOINTED.

title: more durable but at the cost of some versatility
text:
If you're a "long time" Peak Design user, you'll find the new anchors are a mashup of their 2nd and 3rd gens, combining the thicker, less flexible cord from the 2nd gen with the faceted, easier to use disc of the 3rd gen. Sadly, this means the new 4th gen anchors will not fit in the strap eyelet of most cameras without a split ring. Apparently this change is due to increased reports of premature wear on the outer weave of 3rd gen anchors when attached in certain ways and was done out of an abundance of caution. A preemptive redesign likely to prevent possible future legal trouble.

Because Peak Design includes a lifetime warranty on their products, owners of accessories that utilized the 3rd gen anchor were emailed a link to report the number of, now superseded, anchors they owned. Within days, owners received new anchors, with split rings, equal to the number of anchors they had at no charge. Their choice to redesign the anchors before a costly accident hit the news and proactively contacting owners, in addition to an announcement, is a testament to how they choose to conduct business. Pursuing their customers rather than quietly dropping a news release and waiting for them to appeal is obviously the costlier decision, but is the morally correct one, and impressed me.

if you're new to Peak Design, welcome to one of the most reliable strap adaptation systems on the market and there's nothing to really see here. The anchors for sale here are their latest, 4th gen design, and will serve you well.

*The photo is of the warranty replacement 4th gen anchor packs sent to owners of their 3rd gen anchors.

title: Great solution for getting website-streamed content to your TV!
text:
I'd like to have cable or satellite service, but wouldn't like giving all that money to the providers, especially when I'm not interested in 75% of the programming. Online content is plentiful, and we don't mind watching NCIS a few weeks behind the curve. What we *didn't* like was having to watch it on a 14.5" laptop setting on the coffee table when we had a very nice 60" Samsung LCD in the family room. The Chromebox has turned out to be a great solution to watching website-based streamed content. Coupled with a Logitech wireless mini keyboard, anything we could view via the Chrome browser on the PC, can now be streamed to the big screen.

Its extremely small footprint fit well into our entertainment center. The unit generates very little heat itself, but note that it did not like being set atop the home-theater receiver, and locked up in protest. I moved it to stand vertically beside it, and all is well. It also generates very little noise. I have actually never put my ear to it to determine how much, and have never noticed it otherwise. The unit is left powered on 24/7, and automatically goes into standby mode after a period of inactivity. While in standby, there is no HDMI output, so your TV may protest, but a swirl of the touchpad-mouse on the Logitech keyboard brings the Chromebox back to life, and you're ready to go. (As a matter of course, I've taken to activating the Chromebox *before* turning on the TV, which has eliminated the Samsung-scolding.)

I don't recall any issues (stuttering, re-stating, buffering) with streaming video, whether using web-based streamed content, or locally-stored files. Some people have asked about memory additions, etc., but I've found no need for any upgrades for our admittedly limited use. I'd term the Chromebox an appliance, more than a computer. Turn it on, it works. Leave it on, it works. A PC? Not so much (sometimes). :-)

title: Anker Always Producing!
text:
First off, for me Ankers customer service is second to NONE. They back their product with fierce customer support. Their product is always priced right. I own, batteries, cables, bluetooth speakers. I work in the IT Field and am a audiophile. I appreciate quality in everything. Phones, Computers, speakers, cars - you name it. I don't want to HYPE up this speaker just because I bought it and like it. This review will be to the best of my unbiased opinion. I've owned/Own everything from cheap no names to Bose & Infinity. I have JL Audio in my car, bose and sony in my home. I've owned other BT speakers such as JBL flip, Planet Audio, Sound Freaq, Harmon Kardon, Altec Lansing, Oontz Angle, Angle 3 and other Anker. At $40 this like waterproof guy is WELL worth it.

It all depends on what you are looking for from a bluetooth speaker, budget, size, how and where you will be using it and so on.

BUILD: I love the the look, feel and size of this speaker. Its compact but with good solid build and size. 360 mesh and smudge free surface are beautiful.

Connectivity: This thing stays connected period! It connects fast and easy with subtle sounds & w/ out voices. I can use this in my bathroom with the door closed, my master BR door closed with my phone in the kitchen and it doesn't skip a beat. Now this can be because of my phone and its connectivity, BUT paired with this speaker it stays connected.

Sound: I use the Soundcore Motion Q with either a ZTE Axon 7 mini (which has GREAT sound processing and Dolby ATMOS) or the Huawei Honor 8. Both work great with this. The Axon 7 Mini boosts the sound from it and decent amount and makes the music FLAWLESS at ANY volume level. With my Honor 8 at MAX volume gets the LITTLE bit of shaky voice sound from the passive radiators most likely, but NOT a deal breaker and its very subtle! I just tick it down ONE notch from MAX and its all good still great sound and volume. The sound is LOUD and crisp when using it in a small room such as the bathroom, being an average bathroom (5x10) this thing shines, bass, mids and highs! When we rock it in the kitchen or living room it still cranks without a doubt. 360 sound is on point, it fills a small to medium sized room perfectly with warm rich sound. The bass isn't going to knock your walls down, but impressive for its size and price point. I see reviews where people are saying "it falls short on bass". All depends on its environment, just like any sound system. Whether its a car sound system or movie theater. A 12" woofer will perform better in a small car VS a larger Movie theater hall. This is a small footprint speaker with 2-8 Watt drivers. If you need more bass and volume to fill a larger room, get a larger more powerful speaker - pretty simple. This unit doesn't fall short on bass for what it is. Its very clean and loud for a speaker for its size. I got this for $40, for me this makes this thing an excellent purchase for what I like to use it for. My sons Oontz Angle 3 is a very tiny bit TAD louder with the mids and highs but to me a bit harsh- the warm smooth sound and bass doesn't match that of the Anker, overall much better. The Motions Q produces smooth rich music with good volume. If you know of 'Skrillex' a solid test song "Summit - Feat Ellie Goulding". Highs are clean, mids are soothing and bass punches smooth. Battery life is as advertised, also volume can play a roll in longevity, I pay it loud most of the time - I usually get 8-9 hours. For me this speaker does what I need, BUT if you are a super bass head or want something louder to fill a larger living room may want to shop with a bigger budget.

Thank you Anker for giving us great product selection with our budgets in mind & solid solid customer service.

title: Great product with excellent customer support backing it up...
text:
I came across the Pinpoint AM-20 (on Amazon, of course) as I was exploring the possibilities for mounting a Klipsch Quintet to a pre-wired ceiling having standard single-gang junction boxes. After doing a bit of hand-wringing over the cost of these mounts, I bit the bullet and purchased five of them. Suffice to say, I'm extraordinarily happy with that decision.

These are high quality steel mounts, precision-fabricated to allow for one of four mounting possibilities (two wall and two ceiling configurations). I have to admit that I did some initial head-scratching over the instructions, which are long on illustration and short on text, but once I figured them out, things went smoothly. The end result is a professional looking and very secure installation for my 6+ pound center channel speaker and 4 pound satellites.

I did hit one snag, however: the AM20 comes with an adapter which is designed to allow the device to attach to a speaker having dual connection points. Unfortunately, in the case of the Klipsch Quintet center channel speaker, the bracket is not wide enough. My speaker's two connection points are spread 6 1/2 inches apart, but the dual-point adapter only allows for mounting to speakers having connection points which are 2 inches (minimum) to about 2 3/4 inches (maximum) apart. Confronted with this problem, my first thought was to fabricate my own bracket, but since the instructions encouraged me to contact Pinpoint customer support with installation issues, I decided to call their bluff. And once again, I was very pleasantly surprised. This is a company which clearly understands what the term "customer service" means. One of their agents answered my call on the second ring, understood my issue immediately, and gave me a thorough explanation of what Pinpoint would do to solve my problem. He told me their shop would immediately fabricate an adapter specifically for my speaker, paint it to match my white mounts, and ship it to me forthwith. He said I'd probably have it in my hot little hands in about a week - even allowing for the Labor Day holiday and two days for the paint to dry. And the best part was - wait for it - all this would be done free of charge. That, my friends, is customer service!

At bottom: if you're looking for top-drawer ceiling or wall mounts for your speakers (up to about 12 pounds, they say), spend a few extra dollars and go with Pinpoint mounts.

title: An excellent computer.  VERY glad I purchased it
text:
I purchased this ASUS (N705UD-EH76) 4 months ago. I work in IT for a living and spent 2 months researching before committing to this one. Because it predominantly be used for programming and remote support, a large screen and backlit keyboard were my primary needs. Overall performance and initial boot time were also important.

This ASUS has exceed my expectations in all areas but one. I find that every "TrackPad mouse" I have ever encountered has been well below acceptable. I find clicks to be intermittent at best. The cursor movement tends to hang intermittently (lift finger and move again fixes it.) I have encountered these issues on EVERY laptop I have ever used, so I don't consider it a big negative on this one specifically. The video display is crisp and bright and very fast. It is also very consistent across the entire display. The dedicated video card makes the entire system that much quicker ( I will never purchase a machine without one.) I find the keyboard easy and comfortable and the back light is great without being distracting. I read a number of complaints about the keyboard layout, but I find it very useful and easy to use. The compressed number pad (I don't use them that much) provides room for a normally spaced main keyboard layout that I find very natural.

The AC wireless is very fast and reliable and has a very good usable range. The wired ethernet connection is also useful to me. RAM and processor speed are more than enough for any use, including mid-level gaming. I don't do a lot of gaming on computers, but have done some for testing purposes. The SSD drive allows the system to fully boot in less than 10 seconds (not using Sleep/Hibernation.) I have encountered many corrupted systems resulting from sleep/hibernation issues so quick boot without them was important to me.

The system remains very cool even after 8 hours of use and there is almost no fan noise to speak of. System weight is very light for any laptop, but when you consider it's a 17" display the weight is exceptional.

Between work and personal, I have purchased over 200 laptops in the last 10 years, and I can honestly say this is the best under $2K I have encountered.

text:
These are the DJI Goggles - Racing Edition.
I purchased these to get into FPV. I purchase and use DJI products because of their quality and value.

These work with Analog drones too over 5.8ghz and DJI provides 2 antennas with the goggles. Latency is typical over Analog at 50ms.
While Fat Sharks seem to dominate the goggle market I've always felt they were kind of slapped together (Dominater Mod make you look like a borg) and are not as immersive as these. With the full package they also cost as much as these.
I have only used for a few minutes of flight but these are awesome in the FPV role on a DJI drone...

title: ... many people report having problems with this Conair Travel Smart adapter/converter. I just got back home after using ...
text:
I don't know why so many people report having problems with this Conair Travel Smart adapter/converter. I just got back home after using it for a week long trip to Shanghai and it worked absolutely perfectly. It was a complete no-brainer - plug it into the 220 volt wall socket in my hotel room and then plug my electronic device into the Conair adapter/converter. I used it literally every single day of my trip and it worked flawlessly.

I suspect that many people have been overloading the power conversion circuitry by plugging in high current things like a hair dryer and hence the bad reviews. Here's another bit of travel advice - get a travel hair dryer that works off of 220 volts so you won't need this adapter/converter unit. I use a Conair 124ANP 1600 Watt travel hair dryer (also bought from Amazon for my trip to Shanghai) and it works off of 110 and 220 volts without a separate voltage converter so I will never plug it into my Conair converter and overload it.

Note that I only used low current electronics with this converter so I never got anywhere near its 1875 Watt power rating. I only used it for my shaver, electric toothbrush charger, and my wife used it for her curling iron. All that I know is that mine works great and I would not hesitate to buy another one if I needed to.

text:

At the same time, I had an original Pebble, and I disliked the boxy cheap body, as well as those on the new Pebble Time watches, as well as poor pairing with my iphone and poor fitness apps like Misfit that were never updated and unreliable to track steps. Then I found the Pebble Time Round, which solves all my Pebble issues. Setup was easy with the new Pebble Time app, the lightness of the watch and non-rubber band and round face make it comfortable and a pleasure to wear, and best of all, Pebble just introduced their own fitness app, and since they are competing against all the fitness tracker makers, they have an incentive to improve and upgrade their fitness app.

Then, too, the drop in price for the Time Round drops it into the price range of being affordable and at a price where I won't get upset if it gets a scratch or gets lost, unlike with the Apple Watch where I was constantly afraid of hitting my wrist on a wall or something, or of getting a scratch on the screen. If the leather band gets battered or worn, I can just get an easy replacement, so that's not an issue for me. Neither is the dim e-ink screen, since the backlighting works fine, especially lighting up automatically when I get a text or call, but unlike the Apple Watch, it's always on whenever I want to glance at it, and I don't need to constantly clean the watch face to wipe off smudges and fingerprints (I also found the Apple Watch screen slow to respond and often wouldn't work at all when trying to pause an exercise app or answer a call, so having physical buttons is great).

title: H80i w/ 6700K review
text:
H80i v2 Review
Intel i7 6700K Skylake

Idle temps: 22-23 C
Max 2000 MHz: 63 C
Max 4700 MHz: 78 C

Easier to instal than in the past. It seems that Corsair has improved the radiator to handle screws better.

The instructions say:
1) Plug the fans into the Pump
2) Plug the Pump into the CPU header on the mobo

This doesn't work with my motherboard, or I'd have to change things I don't want to change.

My setup:
1) Plug fans into CPU_Fan Header using splitter
2) Plug pump into the PUMP Header on the mobo.

This works brilliantly, allows for ASUS Q-Fan/Fan Xpert control.
Allows for monitoring with Asus or CPUID HWMonitor or with CorsairLink partially. CorsairLink won't report on Pump Speed or Fan Speed, but the motherboard will.

In the past the H80i had shorter radiator tubes. Now they are longer. But I'd prefer shorter because cases are generally able to be smaller now with SSDs, etc. I have an In Win 303. Pic attached.

Happy computing/gaming!

text: I'm already a big fan of Roku, so when I saw this, I decided to give it a try. One thing to keep in mind, this one is 720p and 1080p, no 4K. Works for me, all of my TVs are 1080p. It's small size is great for when we go on trips. All you need is the USB cable as it can draw power from it, no need to bring the power supply. In a hotel room just plug it up, connect to the WiFi, and I have all my Netflix, Hulu, etc. for relaxing in the room at the end of the day. Since it draws power from the TV, it turns on and off with the TV. This is great for when I'm going to bed at night, I just set the sleep timer on the TV, and when the timer turns the TV off, the Roku also turns off. I read reviews stating that it was slow, so I was a little worried, but that is not the case. Yes, since it is powered by the TV, it takes a minute for the Roku to power up and be ready to go. But let's be realistic, it's like 30 second or so, not a big deal. Once up and running, works just as well as my other Rokus. It comes with a strip of Velcro so you can attach it to your TV. As with other Roku models, you can control it through an app on your phone, which works via the WiFi, not line of sight. So, you can basically attach it to the back of the TV, plug the included USB cable into the USB port on the TV for power, connect the HDMI cable, and you're all set. I'm super happy with the Roku Express and should I need another Roku, this is the one I will buy, I highly recommend it. Enjoy!

title: Really Great Wear OS Watch
text:
This is basically a really clean, really good implementation of Android's Wear OS system. The watch looks really good, and it does everything Google's Wear OS system is supposed to do. Fossil's contributions are the three controls on the side - the middle spinner can be pressed or twisted to cycle through choices, and the outside two buttons can be programmed to launch your favorite apps.

Two quick caveats, then I'll get to how awesome this watch is:

First, it has the classic problem with smart watches with active screens - limited battery life. I am not playing music or using the GPS much, but using periodic HR monitoring and notifications, I get about 30-36 hours of battery life. It charges fast (under an hour) using the included proprietary charger, but you almost certainly won't get two days' use out of this.

Second, I found that I didn't like the metal band. It was easy to remove links, but if you want to use the heart rate monitoring, you want a snug fit, and I found that the links left me choosing between a little loose and a little tight. Unless you're sure you want a metal link band, I'd recommend getting this watch with the leather band - if you don't like that, the band is easy to replace with almost any 22mm band.

Accessories - I added [[ASIN:B07HHXKNWF this tempered glass screen protector]] and [[ASIN:B07B5M91V7 this sports band]] and like them a lot. I strongly recommend the screen protector - the glass is tough, but sooner or later oil from your fingers will be hard to remove, and if I get a scratch somehow, I'd much rather just swap screen protectors than have to live with it. (As I said above, if you're planning to swap bands, get the Fossil with the leather band, which is less expensive).

Impressions: The more I use this watch, the more I love it. I can control which music tracks are playing while I drive. If I get a text, a score update, or another phone notification at dinner, I can glance at my watch to see if it's important, then move on. I can reply to texts using canned replies or the tiny virtual keyboard. (Note - replying is only available if you have an Android, although most of the other functions also work with an iPhone).

It doesn't have a speaker, but everything else is great. It's waterproof, it has a heart rate monitor, a GPS, a step counter, customizable watch faces, it can store and play music to your headset, etc.

I find that I love this watch more every day - highly recommended.

It came partially charged and after about 1.5 hours of charging, it reach 100%. After running the laptop (XPS 12) for 1.5 hours on the battery, it still has 65% charge left. Looks as good as the Dell original.

title: Much Bang for the Buck
text: A buddy has a pair and I was impressed with them so I bought a pair also.  I am not an optics critic or an expert in binoculars.  I hunt with them and its very simple.  Are they clear in low light situations, and can I see stuff far away with them.  The answer is yes.  I can't say that I compared these to $1000 binos, because I could not afford $1000 binocs even if they kicked the crap out of the Vortex.  I have tried others in this price point and hands down Vortex wins that group.  So if you have a fat wallet and can afford super premium glass, you can probably get a better set.  For average joes who have other things straining the hobby budget I think these are the best you can get at this price.  I use them on a binoc harness and I will warn you.  Do not leave the lens protectors on when hunting or walking around.  They will fall off.  Use the protectors for transit and leave in the car once you hit the field unless you carry them in a case.  I used these over a 6 week bow season in Iowa.  Hot, cold, sunny, cloudy, drizzle,dawn, dusk, name it these were used and I had no failures.  No fogging, focused easily and the glass is clear and bright.  I comes with a hard case, strap and cleaning cloth.  I am happy with the purchase, would buy again and recommend these to friends.

title: ... TV for 2 months now and have been very happy with my purchase
text:
I have had this TV for 2 months now and have been very happy with my purchase. Everything I have watched on the TV has met or exceeded my expectations. I researched TVs for a few months prior to purchasing one. I really needed a new TV this year, but wanted to not jump into the UHD scene too hastily and be outdated before UHD truly arrived. This TV at least has HDMI 2.0., HDCP 2.2, 4:4:4 which not all 4k TVs had. While there is no such thing as full future proofing, this TV from my own research was the best out at the time of my purchase.

I was afraid I might need some custom calibration for the picture quality to look like it did at the store (checked out at Best Buy before purchasing at Amazon), but I am just using the out of the box movie setting and it is perfectly fine. I had a 51' Samsung plasma before this and I was afraid the LED might not be a crisp or colorful, but this TV has not disappointed me yet. HDTV looks crisp and clear. Live sports looks really good as well. Blu-ray content is superb. The PS4 also looks very nice. I have only streamed a few 4k samples, but they look really good as well. 3d has been pleasantly better than my Samsung Plasma TV. On my last 3d TV my eyes would feel stressed about half way thru a movie. The 3d on here is very clean and my eyes do not feel tired/stressed watching it. I did turn down, but not off, the Auto-motion because I dislike having everything look 'live' or 'soap opera-ish". I found a setting I was pleased with in between that live and movie feel.

I don't even notice the curve on the 65 inch screen. I have it setup in the corner which might help detour from any horizontal lines that would run horizontal to the TV. I do not notice any bowtie-ing, and if I look for it it is so minor I don't even care. I was afraid football fields might look odd with the curve, but it doesn't hinder the experience. As far as I can tell the curve doesn't do anything at all which seems to be what most people say as well. Maybe it would feel or look different mounted on a wall, but my setup didn't allow for it and I really like this TV on my corner stand.

I read about glares on the TV which I was a bit concerned with before purchasing. It can pick up any lighting fairly easy and does reflect it across the screen. Just be mindful in your setup. I prefer watching the TV in a dim room anyways so this ended up not being a problem for me as I usually turn down or out the lights and I have blinds on all my windows. I would just be careful placing it in a very bright room with lots of reflections. (Reflections are the problem, not natural lighting). TV looks fine in a bright room, its just any lamps or window reflections on the screen you need to watch out for.

title: not quite perfect, with two work-arounds it is pretty close to perfect
text:
I'm using a Dell 27 Ultra HD 4k Monitor - P2715Q at 3840x2160 @ 60Hz. I love the monitor. I have a windows 10 desktop, a linux desktop, and a windows 10 laptop. Obviously, all these connections are display port (out of the dock for the laptop). I'm not using the audio features of the KVM switch so I can't comment on those. My USB keyboard and wireless mouse are typical mid-range, nothing special. Can't comment on the problems people have had with high-end keyboards. Mine work perfectly. I use the double scroll lock protocol to change computers.

This is an expensive product, so you'd want it to work perfectly. It doesn't quite. However, with a couple of tweaks, it's nearly perfect.

I've had help from IOgear support and am running new firmware that hasn't been released yet. It's called GCS1932_1934_TEST_170519. You may want to see if the work-arounds I mention below solve your problem before working through the layers of IOgear support to get to someone who knows about this firmware and will give it to you. I got the new firmware before I changed the power on detection setting. I can't tell whether I needed the firmware, but they did seem to think it would be helpful for my problems. My problems were always about what happens when a computer powers down a display for energy savings and the KVM doesn't restore the display properly when the computer powers it back up.

If all your screens are always powered (you don't have power down on timeout for energy savings), then it does work perfectly as far as I can tell. Once you enable monitor energy saving power down, you get into trouble when the KVM automatically switches to the next computer when the computer powers down the monitor. There is a setting you can change for that (you will have to read the manual to find the procedure to switch this setting to off -- it is called "power on detection" under "advanced settings"). Disable that "auto-switch on power down" and you're mostly home.

My remaining problm is this. My windows 10 laptop and the KVM don't agree with each other when I switch away and then back. Sometimes the monitor just goes into low power mode as if the laptop isn't driving, but if I check the display settings on the laptop's built-in screen, I can see that the laptop thinks it is driving the display. It turns out that there is an easy work-around for this case (two actually). Either 1) disconnect and reconnect the displayport cable on the monitor (between monitor and KVM, not between laptop and KVM) and the KVM initializes correctly and the the laptop display returns, or 2) using the monitor settings, switch to another input (e.g., HDMI) and immediately switch back, and the same exact thing happens -- the KVM initializes the connection correctly and you have the laptop display again. I can tell the laptop thought it was driving the large display the whole time because the windows and desktop icons haven't been moved the way they would be if I actually pulled the displayport connection from the back of the laptop. Windows responds to the screen size by moving things around.

As an added note, if the laptop is set to power down the display after some time for energy savings (as mine is), and you switch away from the laptop and don't switch back until that time has passed (so the laptop will have powered off the monitor it thinks it is connected to), then switching back to the laptop always works correctly (with a minor delay for some reason). The only real problem is switching to the laptop when it thinks the monitor is powered on and you have actually been connected to a different computer using the KVM. That's when I use the trick of switching input source on my monitor to HDMI and back to DP (using monitor control buttons) and the screen comes back up.

I do not have the problem with the desktops, but only once I disabled the auto-switch feature (in other words, I did have problems before that, possibly related to the original firmware).

My screen is gorgeous from all three sources and I'm very happy with the KVM in general.

All the cables needed (even audio) came with it and are all very decent quality.

This KVM is expensive but less expensive than two other choices out there and who knows what quirks they would have. The others cost the same or more and don't come with cables so your total cost can be a lot more.

title: Perfect, finally.
text:
Purchased for my husband at Christmas so I do not have a long-term perspective yet, but I can say a few things. First, I sympathize with anyone trying to find the perfect leather laptop/brief. I think I looked at nine thousand of them but had a strict list of "musts." He has a 17in laptop (large) and I insisted the bag have laptop padding (they don't necessarily, which is weird.) I wanted pockets or places for pens, business cards, and maybe a few extras. The shoulder strap had to be detachable, the buckles had to quick release, and I stayed away from anything with reviews of hardware wearing out or dye transferring from the bag to clothing. I also really tried to find something made in the United States. I ordered one bag from ebags billed as "leather," and sent it back because it was 75% nylon mesh. This bag from Texbo was my second purchase and it's so far, perfect.

The leather on this bag is sturdy with a soft surface. It's obvious over time a patina will class up the appearance. The hardware is solid and not awful brassy. It almost has more of a darkened gold tone to it. The strap is plenty long (hubs is 6'3) and the interior of the bag appears to be put together well. The external stitching is also strong. My husband loves the appearance and versatility; it's subtle and handsome. His laptop fits perfectly and no reports of color transfer. We did not treat the leather despite living in the rainy NW but it isn't like he's taking it hiking, either. We'd rather have the natural finish of the bag; it's lovely.

I almost gave up on this bag while it was in transit. Maybe it was the time of year, but it appeared to be stuck in California for over a week, with no updates, before showing up at my door unexpectedly. The packaging was great. Texbo first had the item in a breathable mesh sack type thing and then bagged and boxed. It was ready to be wrapped and given as a gift. There is no horrible odor as mentioned in reviews of some other bags.

I unfortunately couldn't find anything online about Texbo beyond Amazon. I'm hoping it is truly a Texas-based producer of cowhide goods.

Based on the initial quality of the bag, my guess is it will last a very long time.

title: Nice, but some build irritants. Tips inside.
text:
I'm pleased with the overall quality of the case, but there were some unnecessary build irritants:

The case came with exactly the number of motherboard standoffs and screws to attach an ATX board, not a single extra. And when I tried to use them, I discovered that the screws would spin in the sockets, never quite tighten, and could be pulled straight out without twisting. After some experimentation, I realized that the standoffs were threaded for 6-32 case screws, not the more typical M3 motherboard screws. Your choices are therefore to use bulkier (included) case screws to tighten down the motherboard, or buy your own set of standoffs and screws and have them ready before you build. Get extras if you plan to use the PCI-E extension, as the standoffs are used there also..

If you mount a hard drive on the front, you'll need to use a motherboard standoff on the top hole (not immediately obvious; it just seems like the supplied screw is too short). This is isn't mentioned in the instructions, and you'll also be short one standoff unless you scavenge one from one of them PCI-E extender cable brackets. If you mount the hard drives inside the case, they have permanent standoffs inside. Also, if you do use the necessary standoff, the hard drive bracket does not sit flush with the case, and is at a slight angle. This detracts from appearance somewhat.

You're probably going to need at least one motherboard and CPU power cable extender (24-pin and whatever your CPU needs). If your CPU is 8-pin, and you haven't use an extender before in a build, be aware that 8-pin CPU cables and 8-pin PCI-E cables are not interchangeable.

Everything else was as expected. The case was more of a matte neon because of the powder-coat style of paint. I had expected it to be glossy, and the powder finish was a pleasant surprise. The green case actually looks better in person than in the pictures.

title: It has grown on me.
text:
Okay. This is a revised review. Initially, the plastic smell and the surface of the case made me think it was PU leather. My wife told me I'm an idiot (and who am I to argue, after 25 years, she is the expert) and handed me one of her high-end purses that had the same finish. As I've used it for a day, the plastic smell has gotten better, and I think I smell a hint of leather. All of the other leather goods that I have a much more porous surface and, over time, develop nicks and patina, which is what I *like* about leather. My wife assures me that this is simply "higher class leather" than I'm used to (grumble, I'm tempted to take sandpaper after this to make it more to my liking, but I think that would create a mess).

I use my iPad a LOT, so in 24 hours, the stiffness has started to go out of the spine and closure. Hence. I agree, I was/am still an idiot, and I was dead wrong about this not being leather. If you like the way that the Apple leather case ages, scuffs, and patinas, this case may not be for you. If you like the same thing about the Twelve South cases, this one may not be for you (they haven't released their 9.7 Pro case, and I can't seem to figure out how the )#@$@$ the camera would work on it in their pictures, when they do), this may not be for you.

BUT, the design, protection, and function are very good. I like the feel, aside from the surface. The pencil holder works very well, but I *wish* it was down the spine, not at the top (and I knew I'd prefer that when I ordered).

Now, to go off and un-do my panning of the seller....yep, I'm an idiot....

I'm not an audiophile, I just love music. I needed a new pair of headphones for my iPod, and every pair I tried disappointed me. These headphones have great sound, and are a tremendous value. I mostly listen to alternative rock, shoegaze, and ambient, and it's all fantastic. I can go from Nirvana and Smashing Pumpkins to The Smiths and Lush to Hammock and The American Dollar without any loss in sound quality. I've tested some pretty complicated layers of music, and these headphones never sound muddy. The noise cancellation is also much better than I was expecting at this price point.

I reiterate: I'm not an audiophile. Perhaps someone who likes another type of music wouldn't find these as amazing as I do, but for the average listeners like me, I highly recommend.

title: Working great, if you don't have a hybrid.
text:
So far everything is working great (one issue noted below), I could wish for better Trip functionality from the tracking screen though (explained below). Also note, this device does everything all of the other ones do, you just have to "upgrade" your account for an additional annual fee for each extra feature you add. (Compared to the device my co-worker uses, it still comes out cheaper to use this product, even with the "extra" costs added!)

As such, I highly recommend adding the GPS 1 minute updates, 3min updates is only good if you are tracking a vehicle that constantly travels on interstates only. once the vehicle gets in to a town area, it is possible to completely miss a stop.

My issue with the Trip screen, and only real problem is that my car is a hybrid, and when the electric engine takes over for an extended timeframe it causes the tracker to think the car is turned off. this stops a trip and then starts a new "trip" once the electric engine turns back on. As for what constitutes "an extended timeframe" I "believe" this is anytime the car is in electric mode DURING a GPS pole. So if the car slips to electric, then hops back to gas before the GPS updates, it does not break the trip up. This problem occasionally causes my vehicle to show 15+ trips in a day (in the worst case, and 4 or 5 trips on the good end) when it was only driven to work and then home without stops.

title: Mac Users Beware
text:
For some reason, this Transcend drive did not want to cooperate with my Mac. No matter what I tried, I couldn't get the Mac to accept it for use as a Time Machine backup, so I just ended up treating it as a giant USB drive and dragging and dropping all my files onto it. Not exactly what I wanted to use a 1TB drive for.

I do not know what the issue was. I've got a 2016 Macbook Pro 13", correctly formatted the drive for Mac, and the Mac explicitly reported that I could not use it for Time Machine.

I guess I'll need to buy another Toshiba for that.

Now I'm beginning to wonder about my previous Transcend drive. I have another one that I bought for use as a Time Machine backup, and it worked fine for a long time, then quit. I don't mean that the drive quit -- Mac will no longer read it as a Time Machine backup. I thought maybe that was because I had added other files to it, but now I wonder if this isn't an across-the-board issue with Macs and Transcend drives.

I wouldn't advise Mac users to buy this brand. Toshiba is about the only brand left I trust. Seagate and WD both screwed me over royally, and the Porsche drive crapped out almost instantly.

title: Slingbox is great!
text:
I absolutely love my Slingbox. I am a TV addict, but I also travel a lot and this has allowed me to watch shows that I want no matter where I am located. I only use it on my iPad, so I have no issues with the ads (there are none). I have used slingbox while traveling out of the country - to the UK and Mexico - and the picture has been great. I have it linked to a Tivo and it even has the same remote on the screen to use to control my device at home. Tivo also has an app that allows you to stream, but I find that SlingBox works better and I default to it. I have been able to:
-Watch the most recent episode of "The Walking Dead" from London and Mexico
-Watched the new episode of "This is Us" from my TV in Chicago hours before it aired when I was in San Francisco
-Watch live regional sports events that aren't being televised in the area I am traveling in (Sunday afternoon Bears game vs. whatever the local team is)

If you travel and like to watch TV, I think it is great! If you are streaming from one tv to another in your home...there are probably better options (Tivo does that just fine for me).

Replacement battery comes with the necessary tools to remove the back panel of the laptop which is very convenient (requires a special tiny screwdriver, T4 I think). Fits perfectly, we have the the XPS 13 L322X model.

As it turns out our old battery was not the issue though, we had a defective AC adapter which needed to be replaced too. However now we have a new battery to go with it. If you're getting the "plugged in but not charging" battery message on your Dell laptop, it's going to be one of the following problems:
1) sometimes just removing and reinstalling the battery will resolve this message (try this first)
2) failed AC adapter plug (get a new one)
3) failed battery (get a new one)
4) failed or shorting out AC adapter receptacle (can be replaced on the motherboard for about a $10 part but somewhat technical repair)

title: It's a bit awkward when relatively cheap feature-packed headphones destroy name-brand headsets that cost 4x more
text:
So, I bought these to replace my 6 year old bose noise cancelling over ear headphones because after their 2nd ear cup replacement and 3d cord replacement, the bose headset finally died. This review will be about how a pair of modern wireless over ear headphones from china at an $80 price tag stacks up to one of the leading brands in quality audio with their old but good $300 headphone design.

First things first. These are not noise cancelling. Big whoop. The bose headphones also weren't rechargeable, wireless, NFC enabled, light, or cheap. Unlike the Avantree Audition Pro's.

These headphones I would say are at 90% of the sound quality and clarity of the bose headset, with slightly more bass. (this is a subjective pro/con depending on your preference). However, I was shocked to hear subtle and new sounds in songs I was very familiar that I never once picked up on listening to the bose headphones. This surprised me greatly.

Sound quality: bose (B) 9/10- avantree audition pro (AAP) 9/10
Bass: tie
Treble: B:9.5/10, AAP:8.5/10
Mid: Tie,
Clarity: B:8.5/10, AAP: 9.5/10

Features:
B:5/10, AAP 10/10

Build Quality:
B:9/10, AAP:8/10

Battery Life:
No numerical metrics here as they are irrelevant. Because of the noise cancelling feature of the bose, they require 1 AAA battery to operate at all, period. That kinda sucks. As for the Avantree AP headset, the integrated USB rechargeable Li ion battery lasts for about 35hrs or loud usage on one charge, and only takes a mere 3 hours to charge fully. Additionally, when the battery is dead, you can use the included (albiet crappy) 3.5mm stereo cable to listen to your music the old school way. Meanwhile I found myself using 1 AAA battery every 40 hours of use from the bose just to operate at all, FYI.

Design:
Apples and oranges, i like them both. The AAP feels like more of a classic design, the bose looks sleek but also like something that belongs in the early 2000's on Keanu Reeves' head in the matrix. Take that at face value.

Weight:
Bose: weighty but comforting, AAP: gravity-defyingly ultra-light, you often forget you're wearing them.

Comfort: The second biggest difference IMO
Bose: like your GF's touch when you're feeling down. Exactly what you need. Soft, comforting, present. , AAP: slightly foreign at first, definitely not as soft but the lack of weight helps a bit here. I felt that the bose headset did a better job 'cupping' my ears, but the AAP wasn't lacking at all, and you quickly get used to its feel. It's just different, yet not quite as refined; just not at the same level.

Verdict: it's 2016, you have no business spending $349 on the masterful newest model bose noise cancelling aluminum wireless headphones (unless you literally sh*t cash) when for nearly 1/5 of the price you can have an excellent pair of headphones that look better, have more features, are lighter, and better looking (IMO).

As a final note, the voice feedback of the avantree headphones is super annoying, yet also frustratingly helpful. I can't help but feel that a key of beep patterns outlined in the manual would have been better than hearing "welcome to avantree" or "paring" or "connected" or "goodbye" in a feminine robotic voice every time you turn on/off or pair the headset, but what does it really matter?

Bonus: NFC works wonderfully with android devices on this product. Love this feature.

I would buy these as my go-to headphones for the < $250 price tag, even though they're only $80. That's how good they are.

As a result the panning is difficult, in that the resistance to to high compared to other ball heads I own.  After about 30 minutes I was able to fix the problem and now it is usable.  It remains to be seen if the fix is permanent or not. So in the end if you are looking for a low cost basic small ball head you should consider this product. Also I would trust this ball head with heavy loads like a DSLR with a 70-200 2.8 zoom, but it is more than fine for mirrorless cameras with kit or fixed lenses should not be a problem. title: Need for Speed -- A comprehensive review of the fastest microsd cards
text:
I had the opportunity to compare the performance of the fastest microsd cards currently available from top manufacturers. All cards mentioned in this review are obtained from Amazon during the last week or two except when noted otherwise.

Test Setup:
Lexar Professional workflow UR1 microsd card reader was used for all tests except when noted
CrystalDiskMark 5.0.2 x64 was used to produce all the test results and was set up with 2 passes and 100MB read/write size
All cards up to 32GB are formatted as FAT32 with 32KB allocation unit size, all 64GB cards are formatted exFAT with 128KB allocation unit size

Test Results (Numbers are Sequential Read, Sequential Write, 4K Random Read, 4K Random Write in MB/s, speeds greater than 10MB/s were rounded to the whole numbers)

* The Lexar 1000x card is the only UHS-II card available and tested, the bundled USB reader has extra pins for reading UHS-II card
** Came bundled with a device

**** old model tested, not the current U3 model

Fastest Sequential Read:
All tested cards were able to accomplish > 90MB/s, with the Lexar 1000x able to take advantage of UHS-II speed when using the bundled USB reader and leading the pack

Fastest Sequential Write:
Sandisk Extreme Pro, Samsung Pro+, Transcend Ultimate 633x

Fastest Random Read:
Kingston 90R/80W.

Fastest Random Write:
Samsung Pro+

Best overall:
Samsung Pro+ and Sandisk Extreme Pro

Other observations:
Performance and price are not proportional when it comes to selecting a microSD card. Some of the worst performing cards in this review also happen to be the most expensive.
Not all 633x cards are created equal. The two cards reviewed from Lexar and Transcend are both marked as 633x but vary in performance greatly.
4k video recording using action cams and drone cameras have a typical bitrate of 60mbps or 100mbps, corresponding to 7.5MB/s to 12.5MB/s. All cards in this review should theoretically be able to handle this usage easily.
Using microsd card as supplemental phone storage potentially could benefit from a faster card,

title: Very Disappointing -- Should Have Been 5 Stars
text: This would have been 5 stars except that it cannot decode DTS-HD Master Audio. It only supports Dolby Digital and Linear PCM 2ch. I didn't realize the ramifications when I bought it. The audio on most Blu-ray discs is DTS-HD Master Audio. Unless there's other options on your disc, or you can read lips, you're out of luck. The only way around this is to switch the TV audio from the soundbar to the TV speakers then back again when the movie is over. Alternatively, you can "permanently" switch your TV audio from "Auto" to "PCM". title: Known issues the tech admits
text:
I don't hate it, hence the two stars. I am frustrated with the kindle and tech support and the "known issue" that they kept hidden. Had I known about the issues we are experiencing, I would not have bought this product for my son.

A "known issue with Kids Freetime"

I start with this one because, after reading many reviews, this seems to be a big issue that has people frustrated and upset.

Has your child went to read a book or play a game and the kindle is demanding an internet connection? The content has been removed and it's demanding internet access so that you can re-download it. This happens to the books, games and apps that you get from the Freetime selection, as well as any apps you get from the app store. While looking at the icons on the carousel, if you don't see a little check mark on the bottom corner, it's been removed and needs to be re-downloaded. It's so bad, we're doing this three times a day at times.

It took multiple phone calls, and suggestions to reset to factory default, and to remove and re-add my sons profile as a "work-around", before the Kindle tech support admitted that this is a known issue.

"The developer of Kids Freetime is working on a fix and it should be in the February update." This is what I was told on my very last phone call.

Downloads and installs updates while NOT connected to the internet.

The first time this happened, my son and I were on the freeway, driving out of town. The kindle started downloading three games all by itself while he was reading a book, and it really freaked him out. The wifi was NOT on. A phone call to Amazon support resulted in a very confused support person who didn't know what was going on.

Later that same day, in an area with NO WIFI at all, the Kindle downloaded and installed an update. Another call to Amazon support again resulted in a confused support person who had no idea what was going on.

One week later, the Kindle again downloaded and installed an update while NOT connected to Wifi. A third call, yet again, resulted in a confused person who couldn't help me.

I told my son I would buy him a new tablet. He has asked that we wait to see if the "fix" with work when it comes in February. I'll spend my time until then researching and deciding on a new tablet for my son, just in case the fix doesn't work.

title: Not so Universal As Hoped:
text:
The product arrived folded in a box and had texture similar to a car floor mat.
There are prefab punches on the back and edges to gain access to USB ports that would otherwise be covered. Once removed they can’t be reattached.
The issue I have is it simply did not fit my HP Beats Special Edition 15.6” Laptop.

I patiently tried to stretch the unit around but I was about 2” short.
I just repaired the screen on the laptop at a cost of $320 for parts and was looking for way to add more protection around the screen area. Covertop was the only game in town.

I believe the Covertop was design for older and standard vanilla laptops but not stylized ones like my HP Beats.
It may be over due for a design refresh since most laptops these days don’t have USB ports in the back but on the sides.

I ended up returning the item to Amazon.
I've attached photos of my efforts.
If you can get one that fits, please do.

The maker was going to charge me the price of the laptop to repair the broken screen after having it for only 30 days.
I regretted not getting the Canopy insurance option. I chose to repair the screen myself with great successfully.

I gave it two stars because it was advertised as Universal. You have to be really sure that your product works for 99% of the laptops out there. Many of the reviews have some issue with fit or functionality where a port was covered with no punch-out.

One-size doesn't fit all.

title: Very comfortable, sound great.
text:
They are "open back", meaning that they do not isolate outside sound. If you want passive or active noise-canceling headphones, look elsewhere! These headphones will allow you to listen to music without completely isolating you from your environment.

These headphones are very comfortable. They have large over-ear cups with soft fabric. I found other over-hear headphones, especially the closed-back variety to cause my ears to get sweaty, likely from the lack of airflow that is necessary for noise isolation. I can wear these open-back headphones for hours with no discomfort.

These are wired headphones. No microphone, no audio controls. No volume knob. As convenient as an in-line volume adjustment knob is, you'll notice that high-end wired headphones don't come with them. That's because using a potentiometer to reduce the volume also impacts the sound quality in a negative way. The right way to reduce the volume is at the source (amplifier), which cannot be done with a knob on the cable.

A minor gripe with this headphone is that the end of the cable terminates in a 1/4" (6.35mm) plug rather than a 1/8" (3.5mm) plug. It comes with a rather large adapter to convert down to 1/8". The adapter included with the headphones to convert to a 1/8" plug is relatively large, and doesn't have any strain relief.

I solved this issue by purchasing a short cable adapter to go from 1/4" to 1/8", rather than using the included adapter. There are a lot of poor quality no-brand adapters out there, so I opted to purchase the Sennheiser-branded one (part number is 561035). Amazon has it for $20, but B&H photo has it for around $8.

Another alternative is to replace the entire headphone cord with one that terminates in a 1/8" plug, as the cable is detachable at the headphone end.

Here is some data from my testing:

Original Panasonic Camera Battery (5/2014): 3.6V, 895mAh, 3.3Wh Li-Ion
This STK Replacement Battery (7/2017): 3.7V, 1200mAh, 4.4Wh Li-Ion

Original Battery Tests (MM:SS)
Test 1: 73:31
Test 2: 71:50
Test 3: 68:56

New Battery Tests (MM:SS)
Test 1: 69:45
Test 2: 67:16 (deleted a couple test videos, reformatted memory card)
Test 3: 69:35

I don’t have a way to test the power output/draw/etc of the new battery, but I don’t believe the specs printed on the original battery. It does seem to be evening out after the third test, but not where it feels like it should be with those higher specs than the original. title: Cable works as intended but Flash drive may cause issues.(Fixes inside)
text:
I have a Kindle Fire HDX 8.9 64 GB (4th edition)

Issues I've ran into using this cable:
Unsupported SD Card: The file system or size of your external device is not supported.
Cannot Mount USB 3.0 FD IN13120600000000000000001
These errors were received using a PNY Turbo USB 3.0 128 GB Flash drive formatted to exFat or NTFS.
Fix: Format any Flash drive to fat32. If your flash drive is larger than 32GB you cannot format to fat 32 in windows. You must use fat32format and instructions can found here: http://www.ridgecrop.demon.co.uk/index.htm?fat32format.htm

Blank SD card: SD card is blank or has unsupported filesystem.
Error given when your flash drive is formatted NTFS.
Fix: Format to fat32 if possible but you'll get the error that follows this one.

Cannot Mount fbfb
Error given when you insert a fat32 formatted flash drive using a Sandisk Cruzer 8GB and PNY Turbo USB 3.0 128 GB with a fat32 format. For some reason the Kindle thinks that the flash drive wasn't mounted when it actually was. If you install a file explorer program like File Expert HD you can copy and paste your files from the flash drive to the kindle.

I give this 5 stars because ultimately I got it to work and after doing some research the issue is not with the cable but the Fire OS. The Fire OS will read pictures, video's, Music without the use of a file explorer. Video's you have to go into your private video's. OS main screen/Video's/3 horizontal lines top left/Personal Video's. Music you click on Music/Device. Photo's you just click on Photo's though it may take a while for them to show up depending on their file size. There is no option to copy objects from the USB device to the Kindle itself without the use of a file explorer app like File Expert HD which is the one I use.

I also connected a Microsoft Xbox 360 Wired controller and a Logitech M705 wireless mouse. Both devices worked flawlessly and plugging in the mouse brought up a mouse cursor just as you get on your computer. The scroll mouse, forward + back buttons all function as they would on the computer. The only negative would be not having any settings to adjust the mouse speed or buttons on either device. Since the Kindle detected the Unifying USB dongle this may allow the Kindle to connect to multiple Logitech Unifying devices at the same time but I have not been able to test it since I don't have another device. I will try more devices later as I come across them but the main reason I purchased this was to be able to use a flash drive in order to carry more files with me on trips without a laptop and this allows me to do that.

title: A Solid Four-Star Purchase for the Price, Quality,  and Included Items
text:
I was interested in owning a pair of over-the-ear wired headphones that don’t need charging, as I have a number of bluetooth wireless headphones, which you have to charge. So, when Lasmex offered me the opportunity to review their C45 Foldable On Ear Headphones, I couldn’t turn down the opportunity. After thoroughly testing them, here are my findings.

Pros: The headphones are packaged in an elegant, sturdy, black gift-ready box with a tasteful picture of the C45s on the front and the device specifications on the reverse -- it is, by far, one of the nicest packages I’ve come across. When you open the packaging you will find a black, hard foam case with purple stitched highlights in the zipper. Upon opening the case, you see the headphones wrapped in protective film and cradled by a form-fitting enclosure. You then see a mesh webbing on the other side, which holds (shipped in their own protective bags) two cables, one without an in-line remote and one with. The hard foam case is quality and cleanly executed -- both inside and out, from materials to stitching. Moving to the cables, at about ' of an inch thick they offer tangle-free cabling with a nice, rubberized feel. Cable ends, one of which is a straight 2.5mm jack that goes into the left headphone cup (see Cons) and the other an angled 3.5mm jack that goes into your device, are gold plated and sturdy with reinforced cable fittings. Jack housings are metal with an anti-slip graphite feel to them. Again, quality. I had no problems plugging the 3.5mm jack into my Droid Turbo, which is protected by a TPU case with jack recess. Lasmex obviously considered devices with cases when they created these jacks. Now for the headphones. Again, they scream quality. The cup housings are the same metal used on the headphone jack housings. They are solidly built and (at least the ones I purchased) are a sleek gun metal gray. The cups, which offer very comfortable, cushioned ear pads, fold outward, rotate 45 degrees and click into place when listening to them. Hinges are executed well. The cups have about ½ inch of play in them to conform comfortably to the angle of your ears. Sliders seem well-built and offer a satisfying click when you adjust the size of the headband. The headband is also well-built with a cushion that, while comfortable, also seems sturdy. While plastic, the part between the slider and the cups offers a color-matched finish just as nice as the cups and seems quite durable to boot. Also, wherever two pieces need married, Lasmex used screws (not glue) to marry them. Again, from top to bottom, the C45 presents well. Now, you’ve read about what they look like and what they feel like, but what about the sound? They don’t disappoint here either -- during calls or when listening to music. Regarding call sound, I called my son while I was in another room. He said the sound was clear and clean. And, he sounded great too. During the call, controls on the in-line remote worked as expected and as outlined in the instructions. Regarding music, sound is subjective. To say the C45s have good bass or great treble means little, as my definition of good bass and great treble might be different from yours. So, I test all my buds and headphones using the an audio test site, hoping to offer less subjective results, to start. Afterward, I offer my more subjective thoughts. Here are my findings:

***Frequency Response:
10Hz-200Hz sweep: Headphones picked up at 20Hz and swept clean and crisp.
22kHz-8kHz sweep: Picked up at 16kHz and swept clean to 8kHz.
***Spectral Flatness: Passed with flying colors.
***Dynamic Range: I was able to hear at 72db below full scale.
***Bass Shaker: The headphones did okay here. Yes, they have great bass; however, the drivers did show signs of slight rattling, although they compensated quickly.
***Driver Matching: Passed with flying colors.
***Wiring (Left, Right, Center, Twisted): Responded as expected.
***Binaural Test: Performed well. Try this one out if you get the chance. It’s freaky.

Overall thoughts: This is the subjective part, discerned after testing songs including genres such as adult alternative, acid rock, electronica, quadraphonic classic rock, pop, classical, country and rap. The C45s, while not comparable to headphones in the $300 and up range, certainly do the job and will immerse you in the right music. I would compare them to headphones I’ve experienced in the $100-$300 range. Bass-wise, they simply hit well. No, they won’t shatter your eardrums; however, the bass is not muddy in the slightest, as I experienced with most earbuds I review in this price range. Mids, while apparent, are not as pronounced. It’s not that mids are not there. It’s certainly not that they weren’t “tight;” and, it’s not that the songs I listened to seemed too lacking because of the issue, it’s just that I would have liked to experience a more apparent mid. Highs were fairly pronounced and clean. But, I believe they could have been a little more crisp. Again, this is subjective; but, I’d have to say the C45s lean more toward a v-shaped profile (focusing more on bass, followed by treble, and then mids). This is consistent with headphones and buds in this price range and what most people who casually listen to music seem to appreciate. Again, though, what sets the C45s apart from every other bud or headphone in this price range I tested so far is, bar none, the clean, crisp, deep bass.

Cons: The cable connects to the left ear cup. On all wired devices I used, the cable goes in the right cup. While not a major issue, it makes it harder for someone right-handed like myself to use the wire with the in-line remote; and, it’s just, well, different. In addition, given the headphones come with a cable providing an in-line remote with a mic, a cable lapel clip would be a nice, inexpensive add to keep the mic near your mouth when talking to someone on the phone. However, nowadays, most people are used to moving in-line mics closer to their mouths when talking in them.

General Comments: The following was a Con; however, it turned out to an Android vs. iPhone issue, as I'll explain. I originally tested the device on a Droid Turbo 1st generation and my Windows 10 PC. Some of the remote functions did not work on my Droid (i.e., volume up and down and previous track -- three quick consecutive taps on the play/pause button). None of the functions worked on my PC, but no surprise there. Still you never know, so I tried it. I was just about to write the Android issue as a Con when I asked to borrow my son’s iPhone 6s. All functions worked perfectly on his iPhone. So, I can't call it a Con, given a) the instructions noted that some functions would be unavailable depending on your device and b) all functions worked on my son's iPhone. However, I'm a Droid guy; so, despite it not being a Con, it's a little disappointing. Also not really a Con, I’m not sure why the company used a 2.5mm jack to go into the headphone cup. A better option would have been to provide 3.5mm jacks (more common) on both cable terminations -- although adapters and replacement cables with similar terminations exist and are inexpensive.

Recommended Purchase?: The great thing about the C45s is they sound good, without the need for an EQ. They’re perfect for casually listening to music at home or when you are out and about; and, they’re being sold at a good price point with some nice adds, like the two cables and the quality case to keep everything safe when throwing them in your backpack, etc. When I wrote this review, Lasmex was selling the C45 with an MSRP of $76.99 and a sale price of $39.99. You need to know that I’m frugal. Rarely will you ever see me say the following (look at my other reviews if you have doubts), I would actually pay the $76.99 MSRP for these headphones, given how good they sound, the quality build, and the adds they offer. At $39.99, I believe they are a steal. I can’t rate them as a five-star, given the issues I experienced in the Cons and the Android-related issue offered in the General Comments sections; however, they are a solid four-star purchase for Android/PC users (and, I believe a five-star if you have an IOS device and don’t mind the cable hanging on your left vs. the right).

Disclaimer: I don't work for the company for whom I wrote this product review. However, I did receive the product at a discount in exchange for a truthful review, which I strove to offer here. Stars are not bought or sold -- a product receives the stars I believe it deserves. I only offer reviews for items I personally use and test. Please know I did the best I could at the time I wrote this review and always welcome both constructive feedback (to make future reviews better) and all questions related to this review (to make it better and help where I can). I will try to address both as time allows, within a reasonable period from the date I posted the review. I'm a family man; so, my time isn't always my own. Thanks for understanding.

title: Arrived earlier than expected and exactly as described. Able to use Adopted Storage
text:
OK. I'm overly impressed. I got this today and yet to find any real downers. I purchased a Samsung 64GB EVO MicroSDXC US-I card to go along with it. If you read the reviews, David L has the right answer on getting this tablet to "Adopt" a memory card. It seems to work great. I have yet to have any stuttering or failures from Adopting the card, and have 82+ GB of "internal" memory. I love the screen on this tablet. There is a newer model, but the screen doesn't seem to be as "clear" (ppi) as this one. It isn't a 16x9 display, and I like that. It makes it easier to see web pages as well as docs. Maybe I'm old-school. It just seems to work better for me. Opened the box, powered-on, asked me to update. I did. Shows as 6.0.1 with the latest ASUS firmware. Speakers seem to be quite good (did the Metallica YouTube test and it rocked for the size). Camera is not the greatest, but I didn't get it for that. Hopefully it lasts for a while. Very pleased.

Added 12-5-16: Have used the tablet and the battery life is better than expected. Let my twins play all their games on it (some are graphics intensive) and the tablet lasted about 5 hours of solid playing. I do wish that it would charge faster....maybe a separate power plug that charges at twice the USB rate....just a suggestion. Still no problems with the "Adopted Storage" and have loaded about 8 gig of games/apps. I swear the screen gets better each time I look at it. Quite pleased with the purchase.

Added 12-12-16: How to make an Asus ZenPad 8 (Z580C-B1-BK) use adopted storage. Thanks to DavidL for all of the legwork to bring this to you. I used a Samsung EVO 64GB Micro SDXC (MB-MP64DA/AM) for this journey.

=============
Acquire tablet.

Go to: Settings | About | Build Number and tap on "Build Number" 6 times (tap quickly and it will keep count for you).

Go to: Settings | Developer Options and turn "USB Debugging" on.

Download ADB's Android Studio ([...]).

Run "ADB SHELL" program from the command line/prompt (may be located in C:\Program Files (x86)\Android\android-sdk\platform-tools). Make sure you type "adb shell" (no quotes and put a space between each word) at the command prompt.

Check the tablet and answer all prompts about letting it connect (look on the tablet).

Enter the following at the shell command line: "sm set-force-adoptable true" (no quotes, spaces and hyphens are required).

Enter "exit" to quit the shell program and return back to the command prompt (no quotes).

Go to device and you should have a draw down menu from the top of the screen. Pull it down.

Select to set up memory card.

Select "Use as internal storage."

Allow tablet to format SD card (it may take a few minutes to complete).

If it tells you the memory is too slow, select OK to continue.

Once the format/procedure is complete, go ahead and reboot/restart the tablet.
=============

You should now have the Internal 32 GB + whatever your SD card has for usable internal memory for apps and data. The tablet now has a massive amount of storage of apps, games, pics... you name it. Shame on manufacturers that don't have Micro SD slots. For example, I installed a 64 GB SD card, now my tablet shows as 82 GB available (factor in the reserved memory and pre-installed programs). Go ahead and download games to your heart's content.

I have not had any problems with slow performance or any stuttering.

This is an identical purchase to another I made two weeks ago. I "tested" the other one and was so pleased, I got the exact same one... again. I had older 4.4 tablets and the kids kept filling them up with games. Hopefully, this tablet will allow everyone to keep all the apps/games and not go through the "delete-then-download" cycle because the tablet's memory is always full.

I am very pleased with this tablet. When I first powered it up, it downloaded an update. I did not check the version before the update, but it is now 6.0.1 Marshmallow with Security Updates through Sept 1, 2016. The screen is nice. I do wish the tablet could charge faster. It only has USB input, but I'd pay another $10 to have a higher amperage adapter just to charge. It seems to get along with all the USB chargers I have. Of course, the higher output chargers will charge it faster, but I doubt it will charge any quicker with anything higher than 2A.

My "official" testing shows that it will play 5 hours of solid kids games on a full a charge. Again, I wish it would fully charge in 2-3 hours. I don't really ever let it sit and charge without messing with it, so it takes about 5 hours to fully charge the way I use it.

The Asus IU Launcher doesn't seem to get in my way. Sorry, but I'm not a big fan of Samsung-ized Android Interfaces. I grew up on the basics and that's what I want. There are plenty of apps and options to "pretty" up the interface. The whole Asus UI is a pig, but that's why I installed the memory card.

The device seems "snappy" for touch commands. I have yet to really notice any lag or "variable response time" while using the tablet. Everything just seems to work.

I like the 4x3 ratio screen. It makes it easier to see more than just movies. Docs, sheets, pics, web pages... everything just has more real estate. Of course, there is wasted space/smaller screen when using it for movies. I like that I have a choice to be tall and wide at the same time...just rotate and see what you want. The screen is sharp/clear and the color saturation is excellent for the price... did I mention the screen is really nice.

For protection, I purchased the Cooper Trooper "Asus ZenPad 8.0, S 8.0 case, COOPER TROOPER 2K Shoulder Strap Rugged Heavy Duty Tough Protective Drop Shock Proof Rubber Silicon Carry Kids Toy Work Holder Cover Bag, Stand" and like it.

I am very pleased with this purchase. I think that Asus did a good job for the price point. I'm not sure it will ever see Andriod 7, as Intel seems to be pulling a Microsoft on support for portables.... I'm sure this is seriously root-able and have seen lots of message boards for hot-rodding it. It is a great tablet out of the box and has lots of web support to help customize. You won't be disappointed either way.

Cheers.

Added 4/12/2018--- The tablets are still going strong even with 8 yr olds playing and charging them. The battery life doesn't seem to be any less than when first purchased... still about 5 hours of use and 5 hours to charge. I have noticed that the tablet is kinda picky with the charger. The best one that charges the fastest is an Amazon Basics Dual 2.1A. I like the memory adoption trick from above as the tablet "sees" it all as internal memory (older apps sometimes can't run from non-internal memory). The bumper/protectors listed above have held up great and saved the tablet a few times. The screen is still amazing. This tablet has endured some bad drops and no problems. Unfortunately, no updates since whatsoever. Asus appears to have abandoned this...the saga of Android and older devices. Still...the best value. Very pleased.

title: Sapphire Radeon Fury X
text:
Product came in good shape....packaged well. All parts came as advertised.

Fits in my CM Storm Scout Gen 1 case very well w/ Arctic Freezer i30F 2011 CPU HSF on my CPU.
The performance of this card hits all the metrics & then some that I was looking for playing the games that I play. My using the much better Cat WHQL 15.7.1 drivers vs the Cat 15.15 beta drivers when the Fury X launched may have something to do w/ it.

I knew it wouldn't benchmark as well as most Nvidia cards due to common knowledge that most benchmark utilities as a general rule will score a vid card that has a higher GPU ROP count\better ROP thruput overall higher than 1 that doesn't due to polygon output (fill rate) performance metrics written into the utilities & so a benchmark score will not necessarily translate to real world performance concerning this Fury X's capabilities vs the Nvidia GTX 980Ti. The 980Ti is the better overall performing card but w/ a lead on avg of just 2-7 FPS across many review sites knowing that the Fury X's Fiji GPU is somewhat capped from the start isn't a compelling enough of a lead for me to by-pass the Fury X & the tangible features that it does bring that the Nvidia 980Ti doesn't.....yet. Funny that you're seeing a hybrid cooling version kit come out for the 980Ti shortly after this card's release......

Card is extremely quiet in my case....I have to put my ear within a couple of inches to actually pick up the cooling pump running noise over my front case fan....warmest I have noted this card get while gaming is 54*C...most of the time it is in the mid 40's in my box.........HUGE plus here! The PCH temps on my mobo VRM's are actually running COOLER @ 57*C w/ this Fury X (w/ TDP of 275W) under load than it does when I'm running my Nvidia GTX 780Ti vid card @ 58*C-59*C on the exact same box setup playing the SAME games at the same res @ 2560x1440 @ 60Hz (this card's TDP is 250W....the same as the 980Ti) than it does when I'm running my XFX BE Radeon R9 290X vid card @ 60*C-61*C under the same criteria (this card's TDP is 290W)! This is a BIG improvement for AMD!

So far I have absolutely nothing negative to say about it at all....only high praise! I love new tech & the HBM mem isn't disappointing! This tech will fully come to fruition when 4K is more widely being used.

As AMD updates it's drivers & hopefully start coding the Cat CCC utility to allow consumers access to more of the driver features that control the GPU's performance\features (like Flip Query Size for 1, there are others) instead of having for consumers to rely on 3rd party software to get this access this Fury X vid card is going to get better as there is a lot of upside built into this beast but AMD is not allowing it to be accessed at the moment.

This is my 1st purchase thru Amazon & so far I like how this web site functions & what I have experienced & will look to purchase more of my computing needs here in the future.

However, same issue with the new headset. I found out the problem is caused by the 2.5mm to 3.5mm adapter. The headset has a sub-mini (2.5mm) auxiliary cord and comes with an adapter to convert it into a standard 3.5mm auxiliary. I plugged it into my house phone, which has a 2.5mm aux connection, and the echo problem disappeared. If you are wondering whether using a different, higher-quality, adapter would help; unfortunately it does not. I wasted a lot of time figuring out the echo problem and even bough additional hardware to try to fix it.

title: Does Not Fit : Current (Dec '16) HTC Vive
text:
I purchased this cable for use with an HTC Vive, in order to extend the length from the Vive interface box ; to my computer. I chose this specific model based on information I got from both REDDIT and Amazon customer reviews.
This cable DOES NOT FIT the HTC Vive!
The Vive was purchased in late Dec 2016 and some of the Amazon reviews were dated as late as Oct. I don't know if there has been a hardware change by the cable manufacturer or HTC. Both the male and the female ends of the cable are simply too big for either side of the Vive interface box.
I measured the males ends of both this cable the stock Vive cable (computer connection side): 5.42mm (5.5mm spec.)/3.75mm (Vive) and 2.1mm (2.1mm spec./1.35mm (Vive)
I DO NOT claim that these measurements for the Vive are completely accurate. The inner diameter (1.35mm) was very difficult to measure with my calipers due to the small diameter of the hole.
As the cable is less than $10, just not worth returning.
