title: Nice for couch potatoes
text:
These are really good headphones if you find headbands frustrating. The neckband keeps tension off of the headphone cords, which reduces cable noise. The silicone bands can be adjusted to manage the cables, and magnets hold the earbuds to the ends of the neckband when not in use.

I used them for a few hours in one sitting, and found them comfortable. The neckband is flexible, and the ends are weighted, so it sits on the collar bones. As with nearly all earbud headphones, they have trouble at high volumes. At normal listening levels, the sound quality is very reasonable, and they perform well. The wireless works fine within 10 feet without cutting out. Surprisingly, there is almost no audible background noise from the Bluetooth radio operation. There is a large media button on the left side, which is easy to find and press with the right hand. There is a plastic on off switch, and a plastic rocker for setting volume.

I gave these to my brother, as he uses headphones every day to watch videos on his computer. He usually lays down while doing so, and finds the headband of most headphones irritating. He likes these ones a lot, as they sit out of the way behind the neck. He used them 10 hours or so over the past few days, and decided they are better than his traditional headband headphones with 40mm drivers.

title: Increased Speed and Range Multiple Fold
text:
This Velop Tri-band is quite impressive, bringing internet to where I had experienced poor reception in my home previously, and increasing download and upload speeds by 3-4 times what I had been able to achieve prior to install (pic of speedtest screen is the after- I started at very low speeds at more remote parts of my home). The 2-node package came with two white rectangular boxes, one ethernet cable, and 2 power cords, one for each node/box.

The instruction guide had only 3 directives w big pictures: 1) three options to download the Linksys App: website to Linksys, Apple App Store, or Google Play; 2) That you should search for and download "Linksys App" and 3) to follow the App instructions to complete set up. I suppose they could have condensed that down to just one sentence: download "Linksys App" and follow instructions for set up, but then what would they have done with the rest of the blank space on the 4.5"x 9.25" rectangular instruction card.

The App basically leads you by the hand for setup, depending on whether you have a modem/ router combo or separate devices like I have. The primary steps included the App telling you to plug in the power to your first node and it searches for it, creating a purple blinking light on top of the white node when found. You are then directed to unplug just the router from power and ethernet, power your modem on and off, and then I plug in the ethernet from my modem to the node using the cord provided. The App searches for your modem- this took nearly 5 min. for me, and I was getting concerned that my modem would not be found, but the App finally picked it up. You pick your SSID and password; firmware is checked and updated and the set up is completed. At this point, you are prompted as to whether you want to install another node, and you repeat the process. During the setup of further nodes, there is an additional step, where the App tests the speed of your internet from the physical location you chose for the node, and lets you know whether the location is optimal. At each node setup, including the first, you are prompted to add a named location (family room, master bedroom, etc..) for your node, for ease of reference on the App. You can add guest access from the App, as well as activate functions such as Parental Controls or Device Prioritization. Advanced Settings include options for Internet and Port Settings and MAC Filters. This was a very smooth and hands-free set-up, light years from the old ways of hooking up your computer, getting to the URL, manually adjusting your device settings and hoping it all works.

I could tell immediately that my speed had been boosted, even before using the speed test. Just downloading new apps or searching for my Phillips Hue lights was much, much quicker, so this mesh system really made a noticeable difference. On the other hand, I've still had a lot of cut-outs from my Hue lights (which were not reliable even under my old system), an inability to reconnect and see my LIFX colored bulb for several cycles, and some minor wankiness reconnecting Alexa. Still, just the massive speed increase and the extension of the physical space for internet coverage has me singing this Velop Tri-Band praises.

title: VPN does not work as advertised
text:
Netgear is faking it on this one. It does not work as advertised. It is supposed to provide a secure VPN connection to our home IP from a remote location. It does not. Sure, it lights up the green light indicating that it is, but it is not doing so. You can test it by going to network-tools.com (or wherever) and see your reported IP. If it reports the local IP, rather than your home IP, you know Netgear is faking it.

This defect was reported to Netgear last April, along with proof of this flaw, yet no patch has been issued to correct it. This router has been out about 10 months and still isn’t fully functional. Got an email from tech support mentioning the various factors involved in an EOL decision. I wonder if Netgear will continue to refuse to fix this and then go direct to End of Life and not provide any support.

If you don’t need a VPN then this router may be acceptable. But the rest of us shouldn’t believe what Netgear tells us. Test and return if it doesn’t do what Netgear advertises.

title: Great Product!
text: I bought the AC Infinity Aircom T9 and an AC Infinity Multifan S-3 and have never been happier. The Aircom fit perfectly on top of my older JVC Receiver and now keeps it cool. I had to have it previously repaired due to heat issues.  This receiver sits inside an enclosed cabinet with a glass door on the front. It was getting way too hot in there. If you look at the pics I attached, I took a 4" hole saw and cut a hole on each side of the cabinet area. On the left side, I attached the Multifan S-3 as an exhaust (which conveniently gets its power from the Aircom's external USB port).  On the right side, I cut a 4" passive hole to allow air into the area. I took off one side of the Multifan's fan guard/grill (the side that was against the cabinet), and I used that grill for the covering of the hole on the right side.  Cutting the holes on each side worked for ventilation because there was a 3" air space between the cabinets that is open to the top. For testing purposes, I didn't run the fan for an hour just to see what the temp would do because I had never known how hot it got in there. After an hour, it was approaching 95 degrees. So then I set the fan to come on and maintain the cabinet to 80 degrees in "Smart Mode" and the temp came down in about 15 mins and has now maintained 80 degrees with front glass door shut for a week now. This is a great product and very quiet.  I was initially very hesitant on buying this setup due to not knowing if it was going to be loud. Well I can tell you it's very quiet and it keeps everything cool! You won't be disappointed.

title: A wonderful experience, right out of the box, and everything I was looking for...
text:
What a difference a different model makes. I purchased a DJI Phantom 3 Professional earlier this year, and it was a nightmare from the moment I opened the box. I tried everything to get it to work, and no luck. I ended up writing a one-star review of the product. I said I'd never try the brand again, but I'm glad I didn't listen to myself. I took a step down in features by going from a 3 Professional to a 3 Standard, but I'm very happy with the results. My out-of-the-box experience was absolutely perfect, and everything went very smoothly. I was flying and shooting video within four hours. I found it extremely easy to learn, and was flying comfortably across water and through congested areas in no time.

I've read a few reviews here that warn about the drone just flying away, and drifting with the wind. These issues sound like certain steps weren't followed, such as calibrating the compass EVERY time you fly, even if it's at the same location. No matter where I go, I always recalibrate the compass before flying, and always wait for the GPS lock confirmation. I've never had my drone drift in the wind, or show the slightest signs of flying away. It's always completely within my command. It's important to pay attention to people in user groups who've had lots of experience with this drone. These tips I mention come from them, and when you follow them, you don't have problems.

Probably the four most important things you can do when flying are calibrating the compass every time you fly, always waiting until you get a GPS confirmation, keeping the drone in your line of sight, and not allowing other things to come between you and the drone (which can break the connection and cause all sorts of problems). If you follow these simple rules every time, I doubt you'll have many problems, if any. The people who have been using these drones for some time speak very highly of them and their reliability, so if you're having problems, you might be doing something wrong, or expecting too much from the drone.

This is an excellent first drone for someone who wants or needs great image quality. I am very pleased with the 2.7k video and 12 megapixel stills. You really don't need better video resolution unless you're running it through editing programs, or if you're a professional. I bought this for doing real estate and event videos, and see no reason to upgrade to 4k at this time.

A word of warning. Before purchasing, I asked if this model had a holder that would handle an iPad Mini. Six people answered and all said Yes, it would. Well, it doesn't. Not even close. The mobile device holder is designed for cell phones only. It will not hold an iPad Mini. If you're going to use an iPad Mini to run the DJI app, get the SUMOMOTO [[ASIN:B01ALLV03S "SUMOMOTO" DJI Phantom 3 Standard 2V+ 2V Controller Bracket Holder Support for 7.9 inch Mini Pad ( 1PC, White, 3D Printed)]]. It's awesome.

I think this drone's simplicity is its saving grace. It doesn't quite have all the fancy features of the 3 Professional (which I thought I needed), but it has everything I need and it's a breeze to fly. And make sure you buy an extra battery or two. That's one of the first things you'll find yourself wanting if you don't. This drone restored my faith in DJI.

And one last word of warning: When reading these reviews, always check to see if the reviewer has a "verified purchase." Many of the really bad reviews are not verified purchases, which is highly suspicious. The drone market is a lucrative one, and many of the reviews are an attack on the company and its products in an attempt to hurt their sales. Click on the reviewer's profile and see how many reviews they've done on Amazon. Typically you'll find one or two, and little more...these are fake accounts just added to attack and hurt the product and company.

--Inside organizer has a tendency to bow. I have highlighters and a pen light in the inside organizer and it tends to bow inwards towards the bag, makes it to where you have to be careful when sliding a notebook in the bag that it doesn't snag against them.

Other than this minor issue the bag is overall a great product and has served me as a great messenger bag replacement.

text:
I bought this TV from a big box store and got the extended coverage through Geek Squad. After two months the panel went bad; there is a 3-inch horizontal bar along the bottom of the television that flashes random colors. I contacted for service. My television was inspected by Geek Squad, who confirmed that the panel is bad. I was told I would receive a repair or replacement within 14 days. That was three weeks ago. Geek Squad said it's in the hands of Sharp. Sharp punted to Amtran, the manufacturer. Amtran doesn't trust Geek Squad's assessment and wants to send their own inspector. It goes on and on. Obviously Sharp does not stand behind their product.

**Edit: Follow-Up**

Amtran wanted to do everything again: inspect again, have me send receipts and pictures of the damage again, etc. After all was said and done they offered me a factory refurbished TV. I pointed out that I had bought a new TV that functioned for only two months, and that if I wanted a used TV I would have paid a lot less. They wouldn't budge. So Geek Squad came through for me and offered to replace the TV. They gave me a store credit, and I got a different brand, new. The only problem is that the replacement "consumed" the Geek Squad warranty on the first TV. I think it was $80 when I bought it, so that's $40.00 a month I paid to insure my TV against stupid manufacturing, over and above the cost of the TV. Still, when I got the replacement I did buy the Geek Squad coverage again -- it was the only thing that worked!

With any luck there will be a class-action lawsuit against Amtran at some point to which I can be a party.

title: Disappointing all rounder
text:
Apart from all the technical jargon the bottom line is always whether the product will or will not do what you expect it to do.

Do NOT buy this drive if you need the following:-

1- Write speeds which are least average. By "average" I mean the write speeds you would expect even from a cheap alternative. For example, this drive takes 11 hours to copy a 2 TB SQL data base where an average competitor took 3.5 hours (Western Digital 4TB) and 2.4 hours (Hitachi 4TB)
2- This HDD took 13 hours to do a full format where a Hitachi 8TB took 3.5 hours.
3- Latency and access speeds are at least average, this drive has truly horrible performance on both counts.

It is too early to decide on the reliability of these drives since they are a new product, but, given the new technology I would not put good money betting on the long term reliability of these drives?

So what are the positives? Price, and believe me, the less you pay for them the closer you get to what you are paying for.

These are just disappointing drives generally, but, if you need a drive to store old data which you will rarely access, meh, maybe these are what you might consider, but even then, be prepared to take forever to transfer data to them.

Another use could be a family style outing. A lot of people go camping in the winter, and bring a camper or travel trailer. What you could do is wrap the projector around a tree branch and then have it project on the side of the camper. Grab some lawn chairs and the whole family could enjoy some james bond flicks.

Conclusion: If you're looking for a TV that could fit in your pocket, I would highly recommend getting this projector. It's got a quality image, okay sound, and a long lasting battery, all for the size of an iPhone.

Both times it would not work again until I did a factory reset on all three and had to set up the network again from scratch - took about 30 minutes.
As a side note - each time I spent over an hour trying all manner and combinations of modem and router power cycles and nothing worked except the factory reset and re-setup. I am hoping since it is now on a battery backup I won't have to worry about it anymore.
I have contacted EnGenius support and am waiting on a reply, if they resolve the issue I may change the rating.

Again, this is a great router, solid, relatively easy to use, just be prepared to spend 30-60 minutes re-setting it all up if the main device loses power,

title: Terrible for the 2016 Macbook Pros.
text:
This is a terribly thought out product. It probably works fine for other laptops, but not for the new 2016 Macbook Pros.

First problem: The filter is very thick. It is thicker than the rubber trim on the screen. The magnet along the top edge doubles the thickness yet again. With the filter installed, you cannot close your laptop. The screen sticks up about an 1/8" from being closed. If you press it further, you will be stressing the hinge or potentially damaging the display along the lower edge of the screen.

Second: Unless the filter is pressed directly against the display, everything is milky. Because of the design, when you are showing the Glossy side, the thick magnet on the top causes the filter to sit above the top surface of the screen, meaning the menu bar is always milky. Without the optional sticky strips to anchor the bottom, the screen will not lay flat against the screen because of the gap at the top which guarantees the filter is floating, for the most part, above the glass. But if you use the optional sticky strips, you cannot close your laptop.

Third: When using the Matte side, the screen is always milky.

Fourth: When using the Matte side, the screen can lay flat. However, because the filter is now between the screen and the magnet, the filter slips around easily. Again, you could use the optional sticky strips, but then you cannot close your laptop.

This filter, at best, can only be used when the laptop is open, and only if you don't mind a milky display. Not recommended.

title: Outstanding upgrade from my HD 1080P viewing experience!
text:
I put quite a bit of research into this before making the decision to buy the LG 60UH6150 4K Ultra HD television. I sold my existing Samsung 50" HD (1080P) television, so that I could upgrade to 4K. The Samsung was a great buy, but this New LG is way better.

I did pick up 10 more inches of screen real estate, and do notice the difference in size, which may be attributed in part to the extremely thin bezel on the LG. Comparing HD from my Samsung to the 4K with this LG is absolutely noticeable and delightful. Blacks, whites and the color palette is much improved. For those of you interested in moving to a 4K television, the noticeable improvement is not so much in sharper resolutions, but more in overall color sharpness and richness. This is a Smart TV, so it comes with several Apps, i.e., Netflix, YouTube, etc., which broadens the viewers options for watchable content. Additionally, this television can be networked to your home either wirelessly or via an Ethernet cable. The LG menu can be overwhelming, but overtime can be adjusted to and for most; you will find that once you have selected your favorable viewing options, and are accustomed to navigating to the Smart TV Apps, you have learned all that you need.

I have a 7.1 home theater setup and understood that once I had invested in a 4K television, I would need to upgrade my surround sound receiver, and upgrade to a 4K Blu-ray player. I purchased the Denon AVR-X2300W surround sound receiver, and the Philips BDP7501 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray player. Each of these components offered 4K signal pass-through, with the ability to up-convert the video signal for programming or media that was not originally produced in the 4K format. The Denon also offered Dolby Atmos, which is amazing for home theater surround sound, and the Philips was a "True" 4K Blu-ray player, not an up-converter. There are lots of 4K Blu-ray up-convert players available, but I did not want to invest in a television that was 4K capable, and then up-convert video signals to it. I did not feel I would be getting the full benefit of the LG 4K television. Also, make sure that as you move into 4K, all of your components tied to your setup support HDR (High Dynamic Range). This is a must, because this option greatly improves the color palette of your video!

Watching 4K Blu-ray videos on the LG television is taking some getting used to. Some movies that I have watched in 4K UltraHD appear to have the "Soap Opera" effect. What I mean is the picture is so clear, the colors are so vibrant, the (in my opinion) movie loses that "Theatrical" type appearance. In other words, it is like watching video in a style typically seen on a sports event, local news cast or soap opera, that is not similar to going to a theater to watch a movie. I would imagine taking the time to calibrate the TV, would allow me to cater the look to a more personal preference. This is not a criticism, rather my best explanation of the clarity, color improvement and resolution that 4K offers over HD. And for me it is taking some getting used to.

All in all, I am happy with the LG 60UH6150 4K Ultra HD television and without hesitation would recommend it as a choice if you are close to making a purchase. It offers so many features, you may find it overwhelming. Picture quality is stellar, and it has made a definite improvement to my viewing experience, along with meeting my expectations very well.

title: You will like these bino's !
text:
To begin, I will briefly summarize that these are the best lightweight, compact bino's I have come across & I would highly recommend them !
I like to hike with a small pair of bino's on my belt, and this winter after a snowshoeing day I left my pair on the top of the car, drove off and they were history. (I didn't like them much anyway...) I then needed to get a new pair, so internet "research" and a workingman's budget resulted in my purchase of the Bushnell Trophy XLT 8x32's. I found them to be exactly what I wanted ! But...

Subsequently, I had a chance to purchase some Vortex's at manufacture's cost. I took my Bushnell Trophy's down to a large outdoor sports retailer and "test drove" them against Vortex Diamondbacks & Crossfire, as well as that retailers own brand. I fully expected to be selecting my next hiker bino's to replace the Trophy's, and was prepared to spend up to double what I spent on the Trophy's (including my discount).

Low & behold, the Bushnell Trophy's outperformed them all ! And believe me, I put them through a thorough test - repeatedly. So to conclude, if you're looking for a pair of lightweight, compact bino's that don't cost an arm & a leg, get these. Additionally. the case is appropriately sized, the swivel out eyecups do their job, they feel comfortable in your hand, and they've not fogged in below freezing nor hot & humid weather. Also, they ride well on my hip, and the optics, as I've confirmed, outperform similar bino's over twice the price. The only negative aspect is that they do not come with any lens protector caps, but a lightweight "drawbag" is provided instead. This I don't like, but maybe Bushnell reps will have read this comment repeatedly, and will address this issue...

title: I pretty much knew what to expect
text:
As the owner of 2 Acer Predators XB270HU's, I pretty much knew what to expect. I've read all the reviews and did all the research on all the PC forums and knew coming in that I might have to play the panel lottery. Well, I lost that lottery and received a panel with dust behind the panel and 1 minor dim spot in the middle of the display.

While many owners have been reporting that they've been receiving panels with dead pixels, horrible backlight bleed and IPS glow, what's more disconcerting is that some many forum members are speculating that Asus has been taking many returned units, adding a "QC Passed" sticker and resealing it and shipping it as new. If that were true, then a question of ethics would come into play.

Basically what it comes down to is this:

AU Optronics (A subsidiary of Acer) who makes this panel and sells it off to Asus, has completely horrid quality control. A few receive good panels but many receive panels with some inherent flaws. The Acer Predator XB270HU, Asus VG279Q and Acer XB271HU all share a similar panel type with the two latter have a slightly more updated panel. Many owners have gotten monitors with dead pixels, dust specs and blobs stuck behind the panel and horrible backlight bleed/IPS glow. The Asus PG279 is basically a $800 monitor with flaws that my $200 monitor doesn't have.

Yes, my 2 Acer Predator XB270HU's both had a spec of dust behind the screen but I was able to eventually flick it away to the end of the bezels with my finger and a cloth. I tried that method with this PG279Q and the dust just would not budge. That's right, I'm trying to actually flicking away dust embedded underneath a panel that cost $800.

If you have the time to play the panel "lottery" in hopes of getting a good one, then by all means, keep buying this monitor until a good one pops up. The problem is that we don't really have much of a choice when it comes to 27", 1440p, 144Hz+, IPS, G-Sync monitors with only AU Optronics producing the panels so which ever you end up purchasing, just make sure it has a good return policy like Amazon's.

And ASUS, if you're reading this, and you really are taking returned monitors and adding a "QC Passed" sticker and selling them as new, then shame on you. That is a very dishonest thing to do and it would alienate many of your loyal fans.

I've had a few Chromebooks before this Toshiba 2, including the Pixel (fabulous....WAY overpriced) and for the money this Toshiba is unbeatable. Edit 2/20/14: I remain very impressed with this Chromebook (the screen in particular), and I believe it is a great machine for the price. I still like this machine, but this is the last Chromebook I'll buy without a Core i3 processor or better.

title: Good monitor, 2 caveats; bad for COLOR accuracy, not photo-worthy
text:
It is an excellent unit. There are two major caveats, but for the most part, the design and build quality are very good.

Caveat 1: No DVI port. This is both a progressive move from Samsung and a backwards move. DVI is being phased out, but the new display connections have not stabilized in the market, yet. This was a premature move on Samsung's part, so I really don't like this choice. The advantages to this choice, however, are a less expensive and less weighty unit.

Caveat 2: Light bleed. This unit (or mine at least) has several noticeable areas with light bleed on the edges. This is probably due to having such a thin chassis design. The light bleed is something that can be ignored, unless you're working on dark parts in a photo near the edge of the screen or watching dark movie scenes.

A general rule: This unit needs calibration, just like any other unit. It cannot be calibrated properly with only its internal display controls. The color temperature needs to be left at its default value (Normal). This is approximately 7000 Kelvin. The Gamma should be adjusted to Mode 1 (Gamma 2.2). Mode 2 is Gamma 2.0, and Mode 3 is Gamma 2.4 or 2.6 (I don't remember). The contrast on the device needs to be adjusted to 50. After this, it can be calibrated using a color-calibration puck and software.

EDIT:
After using the device for half a year, I have added what is below.
I received this monitor as a gift and had intended to use it as a photo editing monitor. This monitor CANNOT serve your purposes if you are a serious photo editing enthusiast. It has major color fidelity issues and is nowhere near as color-accurate as an IPS panel monitor. Not all IPS panel monitors are the same, but they are in general a much bigger step up in terms of color accuracy. This monitor's colors seem really muddy and indistinct, so it is difficult to notice gradual changes in color. Additionally, the backlight on this monitor seems to be a major culprit in its inability to "do colors" correctly.

I have to take back what I said before about color-calibrating this device. I am very disappointed in this panel's quality. The color calibrating software I used was Spyder5 Pro, which is by no means a bad piece of equipment and software. What I noticed is that my monitor's gray-levels assumed a color cast and were severely affected by the calibration. This is all fine and dandy in the middle of the day, surrounded by daylight in a well lit room, and it is technically accurate in that moment, but at night, especially, it causes a color cast relative to the backlight's color temperature, which throws off your color perception. All color is perceived relative to the highest Kelvin temperature light source. Your brain's visual cortex automatically picks up on the difference between the light source's color temperature and the adjusted gray-scale colors, so you may have trouble determining what is an accurate color, and this will affect your photo editing on color-sensitive work. This problem is primarily because the panel is NOT a high-quality panel. With respect to low-quality panels, the Spyder Pro software has a warning sign that says that adjusting the RGB levels in the on-screen display (OSD) of low-quality panels will cause unfavorable color casts to show up. This phenomenon also occurs if the program calibrates the monitor's gray scale (without adjusting the RGB levels).

To avoid this complication, I recommend NOT CALIBRATING the monitor, so as to see the colors represented correctly relative to the native backlight's color temperature. This monitor just cannot handle having its colors adjusted. This kind of task is better left to the IPS panels that are made for color-sensitive work.

In all, I was hoping for a good monitor, and hoping that Samsung's research into the PLS (Plane-to-Line Switching) technology would prove a viable competitor or middle ground between regular T/N panels and IPS panels. It may accomplish this to some degree, but it still pales in comparison to IPS panels for image editing and color-sensitive work. As far as gaming goes, this monitor has none of the appropriate features that make dedicated gaming monitors exceptional at what they do.

If you have to choose a monitor, know your intended usage pattern FIRST, and do not attempt to compromise between the two. You will just get a jack of all trades with no hope of doing anything well.

title: Fast And Compact
text:
Short version: this thing allows me to move data every bit as quickly as having my USB drive plugged directly into the computer. Since hubs can't magically increase the speed of the devices connected to them, that's really all you can ask for.

Long version: I tried copying a few files back and forth to a flash drive - first with it plugged in directly, then through this hub. The difference in how long it took was statistically insignificant (less than 2%). As anyone who uses a flash drive regularly knows, the time to copy files can vary by a few seconds every time, due to one of a hundred factors. I'm sure with a hundred different tests we could control for most of those variables, but I'll leave that to you.

The build quality of this thing is pretty good, too. The pictures show a reinforced connection between the cable and the hub itself, and you can tell that it's true. The cable itself is very thick and sturdy, and although you can see a sligh gap if you press hard enough on the connection, you can tell that's purely cosmetic - this thing isn't going anywhere before the hub itself breaks.

I would have like to have seen a USB 3.0 extension cable included for use with a desktop, but I guess that's probably not their general target audience with something like this - a super compact hub like this is more of a laptop accessory. The hub does have a light blue LED in one of the front corners. It's always helpful to know that the device is indeed connected and powered on, but if you're looking to use this in a bedroom, be aware that you'll have one more LED adding to your light pollution. Then again, these days, what's one more LED?

The design is overall very attractive and compact. I'd have no qualms at all about using this in a professional setting, in a college, or anywhere else I can think of. The cable is just long enough to easily be flexed 90 degrees to better fit on a desk, but not so long as to get in the way.

The only thing I'm not sure about is longevity. This is a newer brand, but from its build quality and performance, I have no reason to think it's going to die on me anytime soon - this looks to be a well-made product. If this review hasn't been updated to say otherwise, you can safely assume this thing hasn't crapped out on me yet.

title: Great screen protection with 1 downside (your resutls my vary)
text:
These screen protectors are nice, thick plastic (like a projector transparency). Installation was comparable to other screen protectors I've installed - the key is to take it slow, make sure the screen surface is absolutely pristine, and a good quality microfiber cloth (not included) can really help. The included sticky pads and spot cleaning tools also helped with producing a bubble/debris free installation. Removing and readjusting the screen protector during installation is easy and does not stretch or distort it's shape.The adhesive backing is not aggressive and does not separate from the screen protector or leave residue on your screen. Overall fit and finish are great, the spacing around the edges are uniform and the camera hole is centered on the camera.

Customer service is outstanding. The seller contacted me via email to ensure I was totally satisfied with the product, and offered to send me additional screen protectors if I had problems during installation.

My issue is with the user experience after the screen protector was installed. It might be "too" thick because my (your results may be better than mine) Lenovo Tab 2 had a hard time registering some screen taps and swipes. The tablet still worked and inputs could still be made, but I could tell a difference in the screen sensitivity. In the end I removed the screen protector after about 10 days of use. I prefer the more sensitive screen versus the protection of a screen protector. That said, I would still recommend this to someone who wants/needs a screen protector.

They're fine for watching TV shows though if they're not music-driven, but I wouldn't even want to watch a movie with these. Bottom line, if you LOVE music and are picky about sound, look elsewhere.

UPDATE: I was sent a replacement pair and the bass levels were much better on these. I must have gotten a dud pair before. However, the mid levels still aren't up to par for my taste. The treble is way to pronounced. Some people do prefer this sound, but it is a very different sound than you would get at a concert or theater. I have had other in ear headphones in the past that have managed to accomplish near perfect sound, so I know it is possible, it's just not quite there with these. They are a great choice though if you're on a budget, and they look really cool!

title: No bubbles, love the material!
text:
Nice thick material, helped eliminate the bubbles. I got the retail package which came with plenty of sticky pieces of tape that allow application and micro-fiber cloth for cleaning. Everything worked as expected. 99.999% bubble free (nothing visible to my naked eye) application in 7 minutes!

NOTES: Lots of people complain about bubbles (this goes for ALL screen protectors). My suggestion please take the time to understand the process of bubble free application (or pay a teenager $2 to you apply it for you). I am writing a section on my technique of how to achieve bubble free application below. Hope somebody will find it useful.

STEPS FOR BUBBLE FREE APPLICATION
1. Understand what causes bubbles. Two things -- dirt (see step 3), and air (see step 7).
2. Start with several 1-1.5 inch of clear tape cut into pieces, I suggest about 5-6. This is included with several pricey version of the screen protectors, otherwise you can use any clear tape. Cut them before you go to next step, and have them ready by sticking them on a piece of wood or metal that you can easily access.
3. Start by cleaning the screen surface with micro-fiber cloth, or you can use an old cotton piece of cloth that has been washed. Do not use paper towel. Goal here is to avoid the fuzz. You can use 1 drop of water (on cloth) to reduce static that attracts dirt. Be careful not to pour water into the sides of the screen!
4. WITHOUT taking any layers off, position your screen protector to your satisfaction. Now using cut piece of tape (from Step 2), hold the protector in place such that half the piece of tape is on the protector and half on your laptop edge. Use 2 or 3 pieces (ONLY on one side), so that you can swing the protector like opening a door.
5. Swing the protector away from screen. Clean the screen again to remove all visible pieces of dirt (don't work too hard). Apparently, rubbing causes static and pulls airborne dirt towards the screen.
6. Now take the layer 1 off the screen protector (this is between your laptop and the protector) while the screen protector is opened like a door.
7. Starting from applying the protector from side with temporary pieces of tape (see step 4 above) gently apply the protector to laptop screen. It should self stick, if you position it correctly. Move slowly. I recommend going at speed of about 2 seconds/inch. THE GOAL her is not let any air-pockets be created. If you do get trapped air or bubbles, pull back 1 or 2 inches of protector and apply again slowly.
8. Depending upon your patience level in last step, your environment, and the quality of screen material -- you will have some bubbles. I get about 1 small bubbles per 10-20 sq. inches at this stage.
9. If it is pure air-pockets towards edges, you are press with a credit card and they should go away. IF you have large air pockets, then I recommend going back and repeat step 7, and remove only half or more of the screen protector to remove the bubbles.
10. Now you can take the second layer of plastic off (layer 2) and this should remove the pieces of tape applied in step 4. You can remove the piece of tape from laptop now or later.
- You should now have a satisfactorily positioned screen, with no air-pockets but may be small bubbles due to dirt --
11. For removing pieces of hair/dirt (or fuzz, bread crumbs, silver, gold etc.), you need to use a small piece of tape on closest corner to lift the protector, and another piece of tape on other hand to reach the hair. Be patient and think of your happy childhood memories, and it will work.
12. Gently release the screen protector like Step 7 and things will work.
13. Enjoy your new screen protector!

If these steps do not give expected results, I can say there can be at least three causes (in addition to thousands others).
ONE: There is too much dirt in the room, or your screen and or screen protector is charged to attract dirt. Gentle cleaning with 1 drop of water (step 3) reduces static charge for me.
TWO: The quality of protector is not good or thick enough :(
THREE: You need more practice (sorry this is true, I use to think it was the problem with screen protector till my friend showed me and since then I am doing well).

title: A bridge camera that beats some DSLRs!
text:
The Panasonic DMC-FZ1000 is such an amazing bridge camera, it eclipses entry level DSLRs! It is a 1 inch sensor, has good zoom range, decent aperture size, image stabilization (you only get this on the Nikon D3200 with $700+ lenses), 4k Video, 4k Photo screen grabs, and RAW. Best of all is the fast autofocus, which is the best in its class and even some DSLRs. If you are not looking to spend thousands on extra lenses, then seriously consider this option instead. You will not be disappointed!

I had purchased a Nikon D3200 a couple years ago to take my photography to the next level. I just shoot family stuff like sports, events, and outdoor scenery when we go hiking or something. I was displeased with the auto focus speed of photo mode, and the focus always taking forever to adjust in video. Don't get me wrong, the Nikon with the kit lens and a prime 1.8 can take amazing photos! However, it was not getting the job done for sports and video. I decided to check out bridge cameras more, as my coworker showed me his new FZ1000. I was immediately amazed by the zoom, optical image stabilization, and auto focus speed! To top it all off, it shot 4k and videos 10 mins longer. Nikon was limited to 20 mins.

I am loving my decision to drop down to a bridge camera so far, as the FZ1000 can take just as amazing photos. However, the catch is that it can be a challenge to get the right settings. I have had issues with hi levels of noise for low light photos. I am sure that it is my fault, as I did not adjust the corrects settings. Furthermore, some of the pictures taken at 400mm seemed a little blurry to me. Again, I am sure that it is due to operator error. So be warned that it can take some getting use to. I feel that I was able to get achieve competency faster on the Nikon platform, than the Panasonic.

LED represents this TV 55" at full calibration, Plasma represents the Samsung 8500 51" full calibration. You can be the judge.

Side note: The plasma is expensive unless you find a bargain deal like I did for about $800, otherwise most sell it between $1500-3000.

title: small tablet good for casual use, small recessed usb port
text:
I have the Wacom Intuos Pen and Touch Small (CTH480). I like it in general and it works fine for my purposes.

I mostly use the gesture touch features. I am not a graphic designer although I work long hours on the computer (doing engineering and programming work) and have some discomfort after awhile which might be indication of RSI (repetitive strain injury). I have tried a few different mice, such as a vertical mouse and trackball, although the touchpad is nice since it does not require any tension in my hand for gestures and is similar to a laptop touchpad interface.

I like using the pen features to make markups of drawings or other diagrams to help explain things to others quickly and easily. The SketchBook Express software that is included is very easy to use. I think that it is great for making sketches or importing images to markup. Since the small tablet doesn't have a lot of surface area, usually I will need to zoom in or shrink the sketch later.

I use multiple monitors, so considering that, I wish I would have gotten one of the larger tablets, although couldn't really justify spending a lot of money. You can set up the software so that for certain applications the extents of the touchpad only go to the edges of one monitor instead of two. The tablet sensor surface area is about 6" wide x 3 3/4" tall, so if you divide that up accross two monitors, 3" wide is not much larger than a typical laptop touchpad. So if you use multiple monitors or have a large monitor, you may want to consider a larger tablet. On the other hand, I've not used the shortcut keys much, but apparently you can assign a button to toggle displays, so that might be an alternative to help with using multiple monitors.

My major gripe is that the cable connection port is a 'non-standard' small recessed micro USB. When I say 'non-standard' I am referring to the size of the black plastic around the connector. Whoever designed this must not have been thinking about the rubber molding around the plug, or else did it on purpose so that people would buy the wireless accessory kit. The cable provided is only about 3ft long. It has been nearly impossible for me to find an extra micro USB cable that will fit inside the recessed port. There are other USB cable products listed on Amazon with the description that state that their cable will work with this particular tablet, however the pictures shown indicate that they probably will not fit.

UPDATE: The micro USB cable that is provided with the tablet has a black plastic connector that is approximately 3/8" wide by 3/16" high (0.37" X 0.18" / 9.4mm X 4.6mm). Most micro USB cables I have found are approximately 1/4" high (0.25" / 6mm). After looking at some of the Amazon Answer discussion posts, I found that you can remove the back cover in order to get a different USB cable to fit. I was able to remove the cover to use an Anker micro USB cable that I already had, which was approximately 3/8" wide by 1/4" high. Removing the back panel in order to connect a different USB cable is an extra step that takes more time, which goes against the philosophy that USB cables are fundamentally easier to connect, however this method would be an OK workaround so that you would be able to use a longer cable.

Sure, the EVF and LCD are not as sharp as other cameras, but the Leica V-Lux 1 I replaced had an EVF and LCD that are similar in quality.  Perhaps it isn't a fair comparison between digital cameras of disparate vintages, but what I suggest is that the EVF and LCD (by far the biggest complaint of naysayers) are usable.  Image quality (IQ) is superb, the lens delivers, and I like the ergonomics (I've got big hands).  It is very light but some plastics feel cheap.  I'm concerned about light, rhythmic vibrations in the camera body as if it were constantly engaging auto focusing or stabilization motors or something.  I think that charging the battery through the camera is inconvenient.  Every camera will have its faults, but the sum of the A3000's positive marks makes it a good buy in which I have no regrets.

[[VIDEOID:d246ee971723826fd916258ba0a02d95]] Since my husband and I are both retired, this isn't a bag that we would use for work, but it's great when we want to take a laptop or tablet with us on our day trips. For us, this bag will be used to carry purchases at flea markets or fairs. If you work, and need a tote bag to carry a laptop, this bag is perfect. It is very well made, and you don't have to worry about weight in the bag tearing off the handles. The handles are a nice leather that are sewn onto the entire length of the bag. In the video, I show the fit of the laptop pouch for my 13" Dell Inspiron laptop. There is still a couple of inches of space on the sides of my laptop. So I believe it would comfortably hold a 14 " laptop or a very slim 15", but a 15" laptop would be tight. If you have a 15" laptop, it would also fit in the main compartment with a case. If you keep your laptop in the main compartment, the center compartment would be perfect for folder, books, paper, etc., and they would all be secured into the pocket with the Velcro strap.

This bag, on the inside, has a large zippered pocket on one side that goes down the full depth of the bag. This in itself could be used for anything you might keep in a purse. It also has a good-sized detachable, zippered pouch that might be used as a small purse. So if you are working and use this bag as a laptop tote, you can detach the small pouch and take it with you at lunch time containing your wallet, credit cards, etc. On the side opposite the zippered pocket, there are two pouches that might be used for a phone, glasses, or any other items you want to keep handy and not in the main compartment. For business, the main compartment is large enough for 8 1/2" x 11" folios or folders, papers, books, etc.

One of the things that I really love about this tote is that it has a zipper closure for the entire bag. Have you ever had a bag or purse sitting on the car seat next to you and have to stop quickly? The bag or purse tips and everything that is not secured or zippered in falls on the floor of the car. With the top zipper of this bag, that will never happen again. I really do love this tote bag, but for me, it is a lot more than a laptop tote. I think for some products, you need to see beyond the description to consider possible uses. This is one of those things.

title: Pay attention to your sd cards!
text:
Twister has written a great in depth review of the x5 II here and on headfi so I wont go into too many details here. The one thing I found was that the Fiio does benefit from a prolonged burn in (120 hrs or so) Out of the box the highs are rough, the bass thin and the vocals have an uncomfortable sibilance to them. Around the 40 hr burn in mark everything begins to settle down nicely. Double that and the bass starts to come thru and at around 120 everything is just optimum.
So why the three stars? Because what I find absolutely unforgivable is the high noise floor I'm experiencing through the headphone out.. Its a bit better through the line out, but there i have no control over the volume. My headphones are NAD Hp 50's and Stax portables and 90% of my music files are 24 bit or Dsd.
When connected through the coaxial out to the ami ds5, the sound is simply exceptional. way better than what my laptop running Jriver and fidelizer is capable of. One downside is that Dsd streams are converted to Pcm via the coaxial, while it does offer up native Dsd via the HP out and Line out. So as a stand alone unit feeding a good external DAC you cant go wrong. Dsd converted to 24/44 still sounds superb through the ami ds5.
Yes, as a portable device it does beat the likes of apple but that high noise floor is simply unforgivable. This is a high resolution portable player and I'm looking for that blacker than black background. Its not enough that it decodes hi res and dsd files. it needs to deliver them in audiophile quality as well. Like I said, it does whip your apple and generic music player but its not blowing my auditory mind. Yes, the highs are there, the bass is there, depth and soundstage are all there but that grey background (not black) ruins it for me.
i know my views may rub fanboys the wrong way but I stand by my findings. Maybe I have high expectations, but for 349$ I'm not prepared to lower them.

Edit 07-21-2015. i have finally narrowed down the source of the problem. it lets the Fiio x5 II off the hook- a bit. Firstly, I want to say that I am a very critical listener and what I am about to say may not be of much relevance to most people. The culprit here is actually the 128 gb micro sd cards from sandisk. I tried an otg 64 gb pen drive and I got pitch black backgrounds to the music. The same music file played through the micro sd card sounded compressed and veiled. Sony has been aware of this phenomena and has even produced an audiophile grade micro sd card. Many audiophiles report that they can hear differences between different sd cards. Forums such as headfi are rife with such comments. So should I bump the Fiio up to 4 stars? No, i'm not going to do that , for the simple reason that this is supposed to be an audiophile grade DAP and as such Fiio should have taken Sd card anomalies into consideration. Right now i'm stuck with 140$ worth of cards that i wont be using. Also defeats the purpose of having the much touted 2 sd card slots. Would I still recommend a Buy? Sure. But if you want the ultimate in hi res playback, be ready to fork out big bucks for audiophile grade cards, or do as me, use a 64 gb sandisk otg pen drive. I tried the same pen drive with an otg cable, it changed the signature of the music again! It gets pretty wild and hairy in Audiophile land!!
Edit 7-23-2015. Came across this very interesting thread on HeadFi: http://www.head-fi.org/t/639945/can-the-read-speed-of-micro-sd-effect-audio-quality
More specifically: From the design/build blog for the Altman Tera player.

""It turned out that the problem was the flash-card. While reading from the SDHC-card, every time I jumped to the FAT in order to look where the next cluster of data would be, there was a huge current surge from the supply. As the FAT has to be looked up regularly there was a very bad jitter correlation.
I learned that this was not only a problem for the one card I was using, but it is a problem inherent in all SD-cards. Whenever you have to change the reading location (i.e. jump to FAT) there will be a jerk in the supply, causing a significant and badly correlated amount of jitter.
So flash storage, just because there are no moving parts, does not mean that you will not have jitter ;-)
The mess you see below the SD-card socket on the following pic shows my attempt to smooth out the power supply of the flash card, using a simple R-C-R-C-R-C chain.

While the filter chain reduced the jitter, this was not a complete solution. I had to come up with something better ...
Then I had the idea, that if I could reduce the number of FAT reads per time, I would be able to break the jitter correlation.
Up to know I was jumping to the FAT for each and every cluster. That gave me a constant jitter frequency that was very audible also dependent on the sample-rate of the wav file.
The solution was the introduction of a continuity counter. While running through the FAT, I would count the number of clusters that are linearly allocated without fragmentation. This way I only need to jump to the FAT again when the continuous cluster chain is running out.

With the continuity counter the number of power supply jerks that are caused during each FAT read, were reduced from a couple of times per second to about 1x per minute.
This completely solved the SD-card jitter problem."

title: Great Strobe!
text:
Disclaimer: I’m not affiliated with any company and I paid for this product with my own money and for my own use.

The Godox Wistro AD600 has been a thrill in the photographic community for the last year or so, because for a quarter of the price one can get a portable studio strobe with high speed sync (HSS - more on that later), no need to be plugged to a power supply (either a wall plug or a power pack) and, in some models, the very useful TTL function (more on that bellow). Being able to get a 600 watt/second studio light anywhere is a dream for a location photographer, especially at such low prices. But, is it worth it? Does it deliver what is promised? Let’s find out!

Size: height:22 cm, width: 24.5 cm, depth:12.5 mm (8.6 x 9.65 x 4.9 in inches)

Weight: 2,70 kg (almost 6 pounds) – with battery and lamp, but with no modifier

Noise during operation: none, except if you set it to beep when recharged

This package I bought comes WITHOUT a reflector, so my measurements are all done with a bare bulb flash – I might have used one of my reflectors, but it would impact differently from what you have, so, it’s better to have apples for apples.

The manuals (to the remote controller and to the flash unit) are written both in Chinese and in English – no German version – and, contrary to the norm, the English version is very well written by a native speaker as far as I can tell.

The flash unit is made mostly of industrial durable plastic. The front of the unit where the lamp is attached is made of metal, as well as the modifier mount and the battery placement spot at the back. The LCD screen is placed on its right side, has a green background with black letters that are easy to read even in day light. On the left side of the unit is the moveable clip to lock/unlock the mount so you can fix a modifier to the unit. At the bottom, as usual, is the tripod mount (with a umbrella holder) and the locking mechanism to angulate the unit (from 90 degrees downwards to a bit more than 100 degrees upwards in a range of more than 180 degrees – all in tiny increments, because the mechanism is not locking except at certain distances) All in all, it’s a very compact and sturdy unit, given a very good impression of durability, EXCEPT for the locking mechanism that is all made of plastic (as far as I can tell) and squeaks a bit when hardly tighten. Godox should replace it with a metal one.

My unit is equipped with a Bowens mount – plenty of inexpensive modifiers on the marked. But they have it in other mounts, if you already have many modifiers and want to use them with this unit.

The AD600 has a few versions. The MANUAL one (has a M at the end of it name, as mine) and the TTL version (no letter assigned to the unit). So, if you want a BOWENS MOUNT MANUAL ONLY flash unit, you’d select the AD600 BM. If you wish the (around 30 to 40% more expensive) BOWENS MOUNT TTL AND MANUAL flash unit, you’d select the AD600 B and so on. ALL of them have HSS capabilities and all of them have VERY FAST flash durations. They also have a multistrobe function (the unit flashes many times per second), which I never use.

This strobe has a modeling lamp rated at 10w (LED). It can be used in three power steps. At step 1, it’s barely useful even in a very dark studio. At step 3, at 2 meters distance (6,6 feet), at shutter speed 1/60s and ISO 3200 will get a f/1.8 as measured by my Sekonic meter WITHOUT any modifier mounted on the strobe. Very dim light, useful if in a studio setting, but completely useless if used outdoors.

The AD600 can be adjusted in one third of a stop (EV) increments from 1/256 power to 1/1 power, equivalent to 600 watt seconds. Is it plenty? Or enough? Well, that, of course, will depend very much on what you need and the way you use the strobe. For a home studio is MORE than enough and you’ll find out you will use the unit at 1/64 or 1/32 most of the time (depending on your modifier). For a regular commercial studio, 600 watt seconds is plenty and enough with most modifiers, although you’ll find yourself using it more and more at 1/2 or 1/1 settings, which increase the recycling time. By the way, the unit DOES NOT work plugged to the wall outlet, only on battery, so no way to increase the number of shots per battery charge or to decrease the recycling times.

I’ll have a complete review video of my unit on you tube if you’d like to watch it – under “just review” in English and in Portuguese.
Some units, not mine, have also TTL capabilities. That’s very handy for those in a rush and that have not the time or the luxury to be able to take a few test shots a few times before taking the final photo. TTL means that the camera and the flash communicate (very complex stuff, better leave it alone!) and the power the strobe fires when you press the shutter is PRECISELY the amount needed to illuminate your scene. If you are familiar with Joe McNally you’ll know how TTL can make your live easier. Units with TTL capabilities are, as of now, 30 to 40% more expensive than the manual ones.

Measuring the amount of power the unit delivers with a Sekonic light meter (L-758) 2 meters away (6.6 feet) at shutter 1/200s and ISO 100 WITHOUT any modifier we have: at full power (1/1): f/16; at 1/8: f/5.6; at 1/16: f/4.5; at 1/64: f/2.2 and at 1/256: f/1.1. If you move to 1 meter distance (3.3 feet) from your subject, you’ll increase all those numbers by one stop (EV), meaning that you’d have to set your camera at f/8, at 1/200s and ISO 100 with the strobe set at 1/8th power (no modifier) to get a correct exposure. Or if you want to use your expensive f/1.4 or 1.8 lens, you’d have to use the strobe at its minimum power and position the light around 1.5 meters of your subject to get the correct exposure at those wide apertures. Very powerful strobe! Most modifiers “eat up” lots of light, especially softboxes with double diffusion, so you’d have to measure with you own modifier to get your numbers correctly, but the numbers above give you a ball park to play with.

What about color consistency (a VERY important matter that many photographers, especially beginners overlook)? I also don’t have a color meter, so I had to use the “old fashion way”… Well, I took 10 photos at each full setting (1/1, 1/2, 1/4 and so on) with the proper exposure (as measured by the Sekonic L-758) and with my color temperature on my Sony A7Rii set to “flash” with a Sony 70-200mm F4.0 lens at 200mm and then I analyzed them all in Lightroom. Godox claims that the AD600 will perform with a maximum variance of color of 200 degrees Kelvin. That’s NOT TRUE when analyzing all the photos together – from a 1/1 power to 1/256th power there was a variation of 350 degrees Kelvin (being the 1/256th visually warmer). BUT, considering that most photographers will NOT vary the power of their flash within the same sequence of photos (and, then, my friends, TTL users will suffer the most, because they can’t control that), meaning, after setting the flash to, say, 1/4th power, it will remain so for a long set of photos before changing it, then the variance was VERY GOOD INDEED. The most variance was at full power and, again, at 1/256th power (to a maximum of 100 degrees Kelvin, most of the time just 50 degrees K). For ALL the other power settings, the variance was of only 50 degrees K tops. What about tint? It varied only 1 point at 1/1, 1/32th, 1/64th and 1/128th. Impressive! Very impressive, Godox!

High speed sync (HSS) is the ability some strobes or flashes have to function with some cameras at shutter speeds ABOVE the camera’s sync speed (usually something between 1/160 to 1/250s). If the strobe doesn’t have HSS capability and you use, for instance, a shutter of 1/300s, you’ll have a BIG black bar across your frame and an uneven flash illumination of your subject. When a strobe or flash can HSS, it will fire dozens of very fast flash bursts DURING ONE SHUTTER MOVEMENT, hence illuminating all the frame and allowing the photographer to use very high shutter speeds – up to 1/8000s in the case of the AD600 WITH THE APROPRIATE REMOTE CONTROLER. This is most useful for outdoor photography when one wants to overpower the Sun and have dark environment with very well-lit subjects at the same time.

Unfortunately, I don’t have the most modern Sekonic light meter that allows to measure for HSS flashes intensity, so I’m in debt with you for that information…

Well, here it’s important to understand the difference between T.05 and T.01 flash durations. If you read about most studio strobes you’ll see that manufacturers disclose the t.05 flash durations and brag a bit about it. But the t.05 flash duration is NOT the best clue you’ll have to the motion freezing power of any flash or strobe unit, and, as expected, manufacturers try very much to “cheat” us into thinking that a flash duration of 1/1.000 (t.05) is great (and most common flash units revolve around this number). It IS NOT! With this flash duration you’d get the approximate motion freezing power of a shutter around 1/200s, which is NOT enough to freeze even a couple dancing a Waltz! If you want to freeze real action, you need a t.05 of at least 1/10,000 or 1/30,000, which most don’t have. In terms of t.01, which is the REAL DEAL, you need at least 1/1,200 or 1/5,000 of a second or more, and THAT’S A MAJOR CARACTERISTIC OF THE GODOX AD600. It has a t.01 flash duration of up to 1/10,000. Great news for those photographing children running, animals, bouncing balls, sports or dripping water! (At 1/1 power it’s flash duration T.01 is 1/220; at 1/8 is 1/2350s; 1/16 is 1/3540s; 1/64 is 1/6250s and at 1/256 is 1/10,000s!!!!!). Again, my light meter doesn’t measure flash duration (only the most modern Sekonic Light meter does so - the Sekonic L-858D ), so, I must trust the information on the flash unit itself – but on my video review I’ll have a few tests with bouncing balls and fans to be sure that Godox is telling the complete truth.

I’ll have a complete review video of my unit on you tube if you’d like to watch it – under “just review” in English and in Portuguese.

The Godox AD600 works wirelessly with a Godox X1-T controller (mentioned above) and this controller works with up to 3 groups and 32 channels in each one – so, plenty of “space” to avoid interference from other photographers or devices around you. Besides that, the X1-T works with HSS, TTL, Manual or multiflashes modes, but, unfortunately, for reasons unbeknown to me, it stops down the unit to 1/128th power at most. If you wish to set it to 1/256th power, you’ll have to do it manually.

I was able to flash the unit more than 500 times at full power before having to recharge it. Lots of juice in the 8,700mA battery! There’s a small button above the battery that shows roughly how much charged the unit still is. Except for the most avid photographer, one battery is enough, but you can buy another one if you wish to have a charged spare on hand. Important to note that even wedding photographers, known for taking up to 2,000 photos per event, will probably not need to have two batteries, because rarely they will fire the strobe at full power and I expect to squeeze up to 2,000 strobe flashes out of a single battery if used at 1/8th or 1/16th power. It takes up to 4 hours to recharge the battery depending on how much juice was left in it.

title: Great Gaming Keyboard for the Price
text:
Reviewing as a set...

Keyboard:
This is a really good keyboard for the price, it's not a mechanical keyboard and you can tell right away, however I don't think that's how it's marketed anyways. I was looking for a good all-around keyboard for light gaming, looked and felt nice, and for a good price. This definitely fits the bill. Build quality is a little better than I expected at the price point. It feels solid and the keys feel pretty good. Bear in mind this is the keyboard style with the funky return key and backslash in the middle row, which if you're not used to can be frustrating at first, but since you can see that beforehand you'll know what you're getting into and does require some getting used to. Fortunately, my work has these kind of keyboards so it wasn't a problem for me. In fact, I'm using this keyboard for this review.. If you're not used to that I really like the colors, they are vibrant without being too bright. There are several options: first, you can just have it stay a solid color and can rotate between the 3 individually(green, light blue, dark blue), you can have it pulse on one color, or have it pulse between all 3 colors. I tend to just pick one color and go with it (green being my personal favorite).

Mouse:
The mouse has a great feel to it. I like the braided cabling and the length is just right. The clicking feels good and the DPI is good enough for causal gaming and day-to-day use. I really like the colors and design. I do not believe there's a way to stay on a single color from what I have seen, but I prefer it going through all the colors anyways, looks really cool.

Mouse Pad:
It's a good size and really accommodates the bundled mouse. The mouse glides on it smoothly and I have not had a problem and I don't realize it's there (which is a good thing). However, the sharp edges on the mouse will catch on the outside stitching occasionally and this would be my only minor complaint.

Besides the minor complaint about the stitching getting caught on the mouse occasionally, this is a great casual gaming set for the price. It looks awesome with my Alienware Alpha and really completes the look. I love the colors and the overall feel. Honestly, it just looks awesome. I would highly recommend this set.

title: Great item to have around, just in case!
text:
This is one of those items that's just good to have on hand, in case of an emergency. I decided to buy it as a hurricane was approaching, but I knew it would be a good thing to keep in the house for any situation. Our power stayed on and we didn't end up needing it, but I'm still glad that I bought it. I even purchased a second one for my father a day after receiving this one!

It's small and easy to store. It's actually a little smaller than I had imagined, but that's because I wasn't paying attention to the measurements. It would, however, be good if you kept the cords with it.

One of the best things about this item though is its ability to self-charge via the hand-crank or solar power. The hand-crank could be a lot more ergonomic when you twist it, but I can deal with it if it means that I'm able to charge this thing in a pinch. I'd say that was my only complaint.

As described, it has a decent flashlight and you can even plug your phone into it for charging. I had no trouble reaching the NOAA Weather, FM, and AM stations via the antenna.

I highly recommend this item for any emergency situation.

text:
The laptop functioned fine and was quick and responsive for the evening that I had it and had all the same specs as what I ordered. However, like a lot of the other reviews, I found the display quality to be terrible. It has more light bleed than my MSRP $300 laptop, color accuracy is low, brightness is low, and the viewing angles are terrible. The overall effect is a dull, imprecise display with only one angle where you can see what's on the screen. It makes no sense to put such a poor screen on a gaming laptop, even if the GTX 1050 isn't top of the line. Count on needing to hook up an external monitor to enjoy your visuals.

A possible detractor for any potential buyer may be the red backlit keyboard AND red lettering. I wasn't expecting this to be such a pain in the neck to use, but I basically could not see the keys without leaning in. A minor annoyance if you type from memory, but I still do not know why anyone would put a red backlit keyboard on a laptop. As this is more personal preference, I haven't docked the rating for this.

While the build is not phenomenal (it's plastic), I couldn't find any obvious structural weaknesses, and for the price I thought it was really good. Still, it's not rugged and you will need to be careful with it. I ended up returning it because of the display, and though I did have to pay return shipping, the seller treated me right, so no complaints there.

title: Simply an amazing product. Ok
text:
Simply an amazing product. Ok... let's break it down...

The remote is much larger than I thought, but that makes it good so it's not lost so easily. The buttons are easy to use and it gives you all the basics.

We have our TV hung up on the wall and the outlets are down on the ground level, which means the charging cord doesn't quite reach. So a little longer charger cord would be nice (about 3-4 feet I think.)

The apps are easy to install and to navigate. The main screen make suggestions to you or lets you view your recently used apps. Then makes suggestions of shows or movies you might enjoy. As others state, it is very Prime oriented (shows you those first and has them front and center) but what do you expect from an Amazon product.

The bluetooth is a nice addition, as is the screen saver. Very adjustable. Another great feature is how it puts itself to sleep after 30 minutes of inactivity. This is great for people who fall asleep to the TV or who forget to turn off the device. Since there is not traditional "off" to the Firestick (you're supposed to unplug it) this is a good aspect to keep it from overheating and being over used.

I have a mini bluetooth keyboard with touch-pad paired up with it. It helps to navigate different apps.

The main part is how well KODI works. It is very easy to install and runs Grrreat! Feels quicker and smoother than even my laptop does; which is a pleasant but unexpected surprise.

I have read some reviews where people said it doesn't have a screen mirroring feature. This is Definitely not true. While it may be a little more clicky than Chromecast, my HTC M9 would often pause and get stuck with screen mirroring on our TV, but the screen mirroring feature for the Firestick has a little flicker to it but it does connect fast and it stays running without pausing.

Overall it's an excellent product that is super easy to use and very convenient. I plan to buy one for my other TV as well.

title: Great Sounding, High Value, Plus features for an under $50 headphones.
text:
If you are looking for a quality, nice sounding, Bluetooth headphone at entry level prices, these headphones will not disappoint you. For the money they are the best sounding headphones at the the below $50 price range. I own some higher end Bluetooth headphone and ear pods and I was looking to purchase a headphone set for my daughter who watches movies on her Ipad in the evening. These headphones will appeal to her as they are attractive (bright blue), easy to charge, easy to pair and has good battery life. To make everything better, they produce outstanding bass, midrange and high sounds from the easy to wear headphones. I tested these to make sure that the headphones were acceptable before I gave them to my daughter. Well, the T2s are more than acceptable.

Pairing the headphones are a breeze and they have pretty good range. When watching a movie, the playback is crisp and clear with the added benefit of the deep rich bass sound reproduction. If a sound track for a movie is digital, you will enjoy every sound meant to be heard by the producers. The headphones are definitely comfortable enough to watch an entire movie or use them on a cross country road trip. One of the hidden benefits is the easy to use controls on the headphone. It is easy to raise or lower the volume and just as easy to skip a soundtrack and or song. Want to listen to a song again, just hit the button and the song will repeat itself.

Please take a little time to adjust the the ear pieces to match the comfort style for head and ears. Ounce you find the magic formula, they are quite comfortable as they have a large range of adjustment.

So again for the money, this is a high value Bluetooth headphone with plenty of features and quality sound reproduction. You won't be disappointed.

title: Great machine, great value
text:
I've owned the model configured with 4GB RAM, 32GB HD, and lower resolution (1366 X 768) display for going on a month now ... and absolutely love it. It's our household's "other" computer, in addition to a desktop Mac.

Whether Chromebooks can function as "full-featured" computers might be an open question, but if you're looking for a machine to function mainly as an Internet portal that isn't weighed down with "Windows bloatware," this 15" Acer is excellent! The 3205U processor is fast, the 4GB RAM are more than adequate, set up takes just a minute or two, boot up takes just seconds, and battery life is very good (with fairly heavy use daily, I'm averaging around eight to nine hours). Once underway, it's sufficiently powerful to have no end of tabs open simultaneously, and the Chrome OS is intuitively easy to navigate.

Screen resolution (again, mine is the lower resolution model) and audio are good but not great (my hands on experience is that the Toshiba Chromebook 2 is better on those two specs ... but only those two). The keyboard and trackpad have a decent feel. Construction quality seems adequate. And it's easy to transport around the house. Points off, depending on your POV: white plastic is a little ugly.

Full-featured computer? Maybe, maybe not. Lightning quick Internet portal? Yes. This Acer Chromebook outshines Windows-based machines ... and is vastly less expensive than any comparable Apple product.

text:
I had a Pioneer receiver before purchasing this Marantz. I am enjoying the sound on the Marantz much more than on the Pioneer. The sound is full, accurate, and spacious. It's closer to the sound heard in a movie theater. The Pioneer was a 5.1 receiver with TrueHD and DTS Master capabilities, but it was not working well with HDR. I had to run the audio directly to the receiver instead of using the HDMI ports. I decided to upgrade to this newer Marantz and see how it behaves with HDR. It works great! I found out that it is Dolby Atmos and DTS:X ready, so I bought a couple of upfiring speakers. What I did not expect was how much better it sounds, even with basic 5.1 sound tracks. Marantz really brings out the fullness of sound, which I did not know I was missing with the Pioneer. Each receiver does have its own sound quality, and I'm a new fan of that "Marantz sound".

UPDATE: I am downgrading this rating to 3 stars for now because I bought this refurbished from Huppins on Amazon and they were out of refurbished, so they sent me a brand new one. Good right? Well, they never told me that they did that and as far as I knew I was warranted under the Huppins 1-year warranty for their refurbished products. The new receiver they sent is defective. The binding post where the speaker connects for the back left atmos channel is defective and quit working. I didn't learn that Huppins sent a new unit until I called to request a repair using their 1-year refurb warranty. I purchased the receiver on Huppins's refurbished page and my receipt says "Certified Refurbished", but Huppins directed me to Marantz and said my receipt clearly shows the item was brand new. NO the receipt did not. I called Huppins back because Marantz requires the receipt to approve warranty repairs and Marantz does not warrant refurbished. Huppins said they would EDIT the receipt to say "brand new" instead of "certified refurbished" and once again said I had to use Marantz and did not honor the 1 year warranty. The defect did not show up until a week after my return window lapsed. I'm going to have to pay shipping and handling to send the receiver to an authorized Marantz service center out of state, and by the time I'm finished, the receiver will have cost more than the list price for a brand new receiver. I may end up downgrading this review to one star, but the receiver does sound great when it works, and I'm still in the process of finding a way to get it fixed. I'm waiting on the edited receipt.

title: Buy the Warranty...You'll be happy you did!
text:
I bought this 4 year warranty three and a half years ago to cover my son's LG 32" TV. I usually don't buy warranties since I had a bad experience with another company's warranty.
Well, 3 1/2 years later, my son turns his TV on, hears a popping sound and the picture is black. It has sound, but no picture. I remembered I had the warranty and called to put in a claim. The gentleman I spoke with was very courteous and professional. He asked for all the information to verify the warranty, asked me for a detailed description of the problem, then talked me through trying to reset the TV. That didn't work. He immediately, tried to get me a replacement but unfortunately, there wasn't one comparable to the one I had. He then apologized and said they would, instead, refund MY PURCHASE PRICE!!! Yes...you read that correctly. I filed the claim on Wednesday and three days later, that Saturday, there was a check for the full purchase price of the TV in my mailbox. I'm Thrilled! I was going to run to a Big Box Store to grab another TV, but decided to buy another TV from Amazon and buy another 4 years warranty from Square Trade. Yes, I had to throw in a few more dollars for the same size TV, but I bought a smart TV this time.

Thank you Square Trade. A warranty you can actually be satisfied with. I definitely recommend this warranty. No hassles and it put me whole so I could purchase another TV.
