title: Light weight, fast and great value.
text:
I love this computer. I am a gadget geek I have been accused of over-researching my gadgets in the past. However, I know what I want and how I want it to work. This computer has met all my expectations.

1. It's very, very light. So light, in fact, that it's taken me a couple of weeks to get used to it. Now, I can't imagine why I carried around the beast that was my last computer.
2. Speed. I knew I wanted an i7 processor because I'm impatient. I was skeptical about this computer only having so little memory (formally known as RAM), because I'd upgraded my last computer to 32gb. However, the Solid State drive made up for it. This is my first SSD and I will likely continue to buy one from here on out.
3. Hard Drive -- again, I was a bit concerned about only 250gb of hard drive, but I've finally surrendered to the idea that I need to be fully cloud-based both at home and at work. Therefore, I don't save anything on my computer. For those skeptics out there, Carbonite.com is a reliable and cost-effect means of online backup. Check it out.
4. Screen size. I've gone from a 17-inch screen down to this 13.3 inch and I wasn't sure I'd like it, but it is plenty big for any video or movie streaming.
5. Number Keypad. This seems like a silly issue, but all my former laptops had side keypads and this one doesn't. Again, it hasn't been the issue I feared it would be.
6. Battery life. This took me a bit to adjust to what I want, but if you turn off the Bluetooth and keyboard back light, it'll hold a charge for about 5 1/2 hours.

If you're looking for a fast, reliable, light-weight, responsive laptop for work or home, this is it. I have no idea how it would handle large memory hogs like Microsoft Office, Adobe's Lightroom, Photoshop, etc. or any gaming. It handles video chat, online collaboration, and multitasking exceptionally well. Again, I do all my word processing (including excel, slideshows, presentations, etc) either through Microsoft Office Online or Google Docs.

This is a fantastic computer for the price.

Also, cheers to Amazon customer service who, when my order got lost on delivery, replaced it with this one with no problem. Have been a loyal customer for 10+ years and will continue to be one.

title: Tried to give it a chance but it failed me (broke) TWICE.
text:
Up[date 3: I've given up. Broke right after the 30 day return policy so I can't get a refund. Tried to fix it by placing my own bolts into it and the plastic plates broke right away. So basically I spent $180 on a backpack that I got to use for around 30 days. Avoid this backpack.

Update 2: Second Backpack broke in exactly the same spot. I was even trying to be extra careful with this. It just broke while walking. I really like the idea but building it with these tiny plastic pieces is a serious design flaw. I'm going to drill holes in the plastic brackets and replace the little plastic pole that holds the straps with metal bolts. Hopefully that will do the trick. I really like the backpack otherwise but... it just becomes useless when one of these little plastic pieces break... and they do seem to break easily. Like I said, this is my second attempt at using this backpack.

Update: Sooo I was loving this camera bag. I mean... it was perfect for me! But it has one major flaw: The straps at the top (that you pull to kind of lift the backpack a little) are connected by this tiny piece of plastic that... well... snapped right off as soon as I tightened it :( After that broke, the backpack hung to one side. I returned it to Amazon for a refund but.... I'm going to give this bag one more shot. I'll probably just re-enforce the upper strap brackets with some bolts. And I suggest doing the same if you're going for this bag. It's just too perfect of a bag for me not to give it another shot (minus that terrible design flaw... heh).

If you have a larger pro camera, you can still fit it in the backpack, you just have to put it on it's side (without a lens on it). I store mine without a lens anyway.

What I have in mine:
- My Nikon D800
- Battery grip
- 2 145mm lens filters + assembly kit (takes up a lot of space)
- 70mm-145mm lens adapter
- 100mm Sigma lens
- 24-70mm Nikon f/2.8 lens
- 14-24mm Nikon f/2.8 lens
- 2 70mm filters
- 3 micro-fiber cloths + rocket air-blower
- large remote shutter release with multiple attachments
- battery bank + 5 USB flashlights
- Deodorant
- Lots of different charging cables and AC-to-DC chargers
- Tripod on the side
- Tripod weight bag
- And then a bunch of smaller stuff like batteries, CF cards, usb thumb drives etc.

It doesn't have as much space as my last camera backpack but.... that backpack fell apart and didn't protect my gear as well as this one does. I LOVE the rigid, hard case for laptops (or lens filters or other flat things). That part seems like it could survive a car running over it. The larger part is still a nice, flexible but thick, padded cloth with a semi-hard plastic front.

The other thing I really love about this backpack over my last one is how quickly I can strap on and take off my heavy tripod. Just two buckles and you're good to go. They feel pretty secure too!

One thing to note is that this may not be the perfect backpack for long hiking trips. I mean, for day hikes it's perfect but if you're going to have it on for a week straight or anything, it might get uncomfortable.

title: Amazing sound & battery life
text:
I'm usually way too lazy to write reviews, but these are absolutely phenomenal. My father bought Sennheisers for about $200 and these sounded SIGNIFICANTLY better. I've had them for 3 months now and they're still all together and in good condition, just be kind them and don't throw them around and you shouldn't have problems. Used them to play basketball and found that I had only minor skipping from half court with my phone behind the basket, so the range is about 45 ft with very little skipping issues. Battery life is still excellent, I charge them about once per week with moderate use if I don't accidentally leave them on. Sound is crisp without being tinny and has well tamed and fairly punchy bass that will be great without being obnoxious. Overall, sound is excellent (coming from an audiophile). Comfort, I honestly forget, don't think I've ever had a problem wanting to take them off.

I have two complaints: 1, if you're going to be in a pretty windy area, don't use these. The noise with wind is loud and annoying because of the cups. 2, the max volume signal is pretty loud, because my music is at half volume on my phone, but just take them off your head a little when you change volume.

Overall, they're seriously amazing. Stylish, excellent sound, great range, great battery life, very few problems.

title: Poor design + LEG FELL OFF straight out of the box!
text:
[[ASIN:B00IQ7PT50 Manfrotto MT055XPRO3 055 Aluminium 3-Section Tripod with Horizontal Column (Black)]]

It's unfortunate that such an expensive tripod from a manufacturer with a high end reputation would arrive defective straight from the factory, and suffer from poor design.

ARRIVED DEFECTIVE:
I purchased this tripod brand new to go along with the Manfrotto fluid head on a film shoot I was in the middle of, to replace a cheaper, lighter tripod which had suffered some damage. The first time I took it on set, straight out of the box ONE OF THE LEGS ACTUALLY FELL OFF when I opened a clamp to adjust height. Needless to say this was quite an embarrassment to deal with, attempting to temporarily fit the leg back in, and maneuver the tripod in such a way that we could at least get our critical shots done with cast and crew waiting and watching as the leg kept dropping out every time the tripod was moved. I shudder to think how unprofessional this would appear in front of a paying corporate client, had this been a job through my production company instead of the set of my own low budget indie. It's the sort of critical equipment failure that will cost you a lost day of shooting, or worse, a lost client.

Due to the schedule constraints of our production, I attempted to fix the tripod instead of waiting for shipping back and forth to exchange it. Luckily I was able to find the right star-shaped adapter for my screwdriver and tighten down a bolt on the leg that keeps it secure. I hope it will hold up long enough to get us through filming the rest of our scenes.

LOUD, DIFFICULT-TO-GRIP CLAMPS:
If a loose bolt were the only issue, I'd still give this tripod a good rating. However, in spite of what the flashy product video would have you believe, it's bulky, cumbersome and difficult to work with on set and in close quarters. The clamp-lock system on the legs is both awkward and loud - they snap down like a metal spring onto a hollow aluminum tube (the leg) so that the noise is quite distracting and noticeable. A better design would be a quarter turn tightening mechanism with something ergonomically shaped like an oval, (in the same way that C-stands do) for a quick, quiet, and secure connection. Instead every time I adjust this tripod even a little, there's a series of BONG! BONG! BONG! sounds as the clamps spring on the hollow aluminum legs that turns heads. Not great on set, worse yet if you're trying to be inconspicuous filming a live event or wildlife. The clamps themselves are also somewhat difficult to grip, if you have nails or weak hands, or need to do a series of small adjustments it gets very annoying trying to wedge your finger under the edge to pry the clamp up to snap it back down again. A prying motion with the finger tips for releasing the clamp, as opposed to unscrewing something a quarter turn, is a terrible design oversight.

AWKWARD RISING MIDDLE SECTION:
Instead of having a spinning handle which cranks up the middle section to the desired height, as some other tripods do, this design has you loosening a screw that tightens the middle piece, and then lifting the whole thing up yourself, somehow holding it up in the desired position and re-tightening the screw. This might work when the tripod is empty, but add a heavy duty fluid head, rails, a camera, a camera monitor, a hood, a battery/batter pack, a follow focus, a long lens, a field mic, or whatever else you are using and you're not going to want to try and hoist up the weight and bulk of all that stuff with your upper body and precariously balance it in one arm as you try to tighten a screw below you. It's awkward at best, a way to get yourself injured at worst. It definitely doesn't look professional, jacking up your gear with your tripod half off the ground while you hunt for a screw to tighten.

The other issue with the middle section is it's not long enough to be practical. Even though there's an extra foot of room from the middle section piece to the ends of the collapsed legs when fully closed that the designers could have easily used the without affecting the size of the folded/stored tripod, they have instead have left us short. I wish I could get the camera to normal height without taking the time to unfold and adjust all three of the legs every time, by simply spreading out the legs and raising the middle section all the way... but instead it's always 2-12" short depending on the height of the talent. Such a shame when the middle section could have easily been made longer without effecting the overall storage dimensions of the tripod.

POOR ERGONOMICS:
In general everything that locks, adjusts and turns for the operation of this tripod is awkward or difficult to operate without good grip strength. Even if you have the strength, it becomes tiresome after a long day of shooting - which I know many of us behind the camera experience.

Overall, I expected better from Manfrotto.

title: Decent Product - Customer Support needs help
text:
I have setup over a dozen routers in my time and this one was the most frustrating.
First, I plugged in the router. No lights. Dead power supply. Used power supply from old router just to get
going. Called ASUS support figuring they would get send me a new power supply, right? No dice. I would have to return entire unit to Amazon or them and wait 3-7 business days. Got a supervisor on the line (Javhan), told me same thing. Even though router was fine, I would have to return entire package and get a new one (and go through their archaic setup once again)

Finally, logged in and yellow flashing symbol appeared indicating a firmware update was needed. No problem. Did it, router rebooted and then flashed that a firmware update was still needed. Called tech support and was told you need to manually download the firmware update from their support site when more than one update is needed. Did so, but the router locked me out. Took tech 30 minutes to get me back into router login (all the while his headset microphone kept cutting out making me repeat everything I said 3 times.)

Horrible experience...router is working now (with my old router's power adapter) and should I need to go back to use my old router, I will just spend $5 for a power adapter. Thanks for nothing ASUS support.

Update 8/31. - bought a better more expensive ASUS router (AC1900 - 68U Model) for my primary residence and had a much better experience. Much better WiFi range but not enough for a large house so bought a second one and setup Aimesh. Very good results l. Returning this one for my vacation home and getting another AC1900

Morale of the story. Don’t expect much from an older cheaper router. Spend the extra bucks and get an Aimesh one. You’ll be glad u did.

title: but can you guarantee that your drone is worth the chance they won't perform or worse yet, FAIL
text:
Please do yourself and the drone community a favor and avoid buying props from anyone other than the DJI web store or your local DJI AUTHORIZED reseller. It is the most important part of your drone and they may work, but can you guarantee that your drone is worth the chance they won't perform or worse yet, FAIL.
You as the drone pilot are responsible for the parts you put on your drone. To identify true DJI props: They NEVER EVER come in clear unmarked packages. DJI makes sure that it brands everything. You should have a BLACK cardstock label that says DJI the part number and their contact information clearly printed.
The blades should be MATTE FINISH not glossy. There is a very small DJI brand molded into the blades. You may need a magnifying glass but it is there. The hubs will be shrinkwrapped. Anyone that buys real blades knows all about picking this wrapping off. Immitations will not have this wrapping in most instances. it costs too much for them to put it on. Check the balance. Cheap knockoffs rarely are balanced.
I have not found any retailer on Amazon selling true genuine blades. Just go to DJI web store. The cost difference is minor and you know you are getting the real deal. Be safe and responsible. There are a lot of companies cashing in on drone owners and you need to know that you are the one responsible in an accident to show the FAA you have properly maintained your drone. Don't take a chance.
I am not compensated in anyway by DJI ... also Amazon is great but they cant police every product.

title: Initial review. Updated
text:
This is a prelim review of this product. I ordered the the other day and it arrived today while I was at work and I am just now opening it up to start working on it later tonight and the next day or so to get it ready to use.

Note I am using this for a weather processing workstation so I am not really looking for a regular computer. It will be headless (no keyboard and Video) after I get the initial setup and will use RealVNC to access it remotely from that point on. Some of my requirements are most likely not like some that are getting a computer for regular computer with monitor, keyboard and mouse accessing regular windows, some games etc...

So with that in mind, first impressions.

o Package was okay, not great but so far nothing is broken or missing
o Keyboard is cheap, and I haven't even taken it out of the box yet as I already have a decent spare computer to use while setting up.
o Mouse looks okay, USB laser mouse.
o The box is pretty clean, looks like some sort clay spots, not really sure but it cleaned up okay.
o Case is straight, not bent, and opens easily.
o Documentation, basically none, just a RMA 8-1/2x11" sheet with information on it.
o The computer has both a Service Tag number and a Win7Pro 64 bit tag on it.

Pros:
o It is really more of a desktop than a tower, though it has feet for both positions.
o While heavy it is a fairly small foot print and a perfect size for what I am looking for. It is not a light cheap computer

Cons:
If you plan on using this daily you will most likely want to get a better keyboard and mouse. The ones that come with this are not Lenovo parts and very basic. Other than that which for me is not really an issue everything seems okay. Will know more once I get it completely online, getting updates to the OS etc..

Will update as I get it online and eventually after it has been up and running a couple months.

I did take a few pictures but I am in a dark area so I will take more when I get some light on the subject. One is the insides of the computer which the main ad didn't show, a good look at the back ports and what the packaging looked like when I opened it. Note the box was inside another box, the one viewed is the inside box.

**UPDATE** Next day
Okay, got it all plugged and started configuring it.

Everything plugged in correctly, I even used the included keyboard (cheap but usable) and mouse, I plugged a wireless WiFi USB in so I could configure this away from where the network cable is and will move that later.

Started up without any issues, when it asked for the Windows 7 Pro key, the key was on the side of the box (part of it covered by a rub off protection square, and entered it. Worked okay.

Software already loaded, not much:
o Bullguard Anti-Virus... Not familiar with it and plan to use something else so I uninstalled it.
o Suite of Correl WordPerfect doc, spreadsheet, and whatnot, don't plan on using this as a regular computer so Uninstalled

Added:
o Chrome browser and made default
o Adblock
o MS Security Essentials
o Paid Malwarebytes
o B-folders for my security password wallet
o RealVNC for remote access to the box when I remove the keyboard and monitor.
o and of course GWX Control panel to prevent Win10 from being installed. Would make no point for the purpose of this computer and why I bought a computer with Win7pro to begin with.

It is now doing windows updates which will take it a while. It is really not that far behind but updates normally take a bit with some user interaction.

Performance is great, it is fast, quiet, not too hot. More to come after I get it moved to the gigabit switch in the network rather than the slower USB WiFi I have it on now.

**UPDATE**
Added 5th star. Unit has been flawless, only delay has been applying window updates, which required some manual intervention but the is not the boxes fault.

Fast, quiet, going to be a nice headless workstation.

To purchase the DC113A cradle go to this link: http://www.amazon.com/Netgear-AirCard-Signal-Boosting-Ethernet/dp/B00QIH1CWO
***UPDATE***

Ok, so here's the deal: The AirCard 781S is rock solid and works great as a "Mobile WiFi hotspot." So, if that's all you want to use this device for, you can stop reading and go buy it right now.

With that being said, I live out in the middle of nowhere and use this device as my sole connection to the internet...so my requirements of the device are perhaps slightly different than Netgear's target market.

THE RUB: For whatever reason, this device will only serve out 15 IP addresses at a time. Personally, I find it hard to believe this is a hardware or software limitation...we have the technology...my best guess is the limit stems not from Netgear, but rather from AT&T because they don't want people using it to connect every device in their house...but that's just what I'm going to tell you how to do :-).

So, 15 devices can connect, but #16 won't be able to connect until somebody else gets off the network. When you're out and about, using this product as designed, the family may have a few tablets / laptops...but probably not more than 15 - everyone is going to be able to connect happily. However, set this thing up in a modern household as the sole gateway to the interweb...and you'll be amazed how quickly you run out of IP addresses.

How can this limitation be circumvented? Of course, you say to yourself, just use a CAT5 cable to connect the ethernet port of the AirCard to the WAN port on a WiFi router, and let the router serve out IP addresses...oh wait...ugh...there isn't an ethernet port on the 781S :-(.

Well, most of the AirCards built by Netgear have an accessory called a cradle. The cradle provides two main benefits: 1) Larger antennas extending WiFi range, and 2) at least one ethernet port (remember this is what we need to connect a router). Except...sadly...Netgear doesn't make any cradles compatible with the 781S (if you survey Netgear's site, you'll find no shortage of cradles for AirCards...except for those AirCards designed for AT&T's network...yep, I blame AT&T).

So, what can be done? I cracked this nut by picking up Netgear's EX6200 WiFi Range Extender, which has 5 ethernet ports (remember, this is what we need to connect a router!). I am able to use the EX6200 as a bridge connecting the network as such:

AirCard 781S <--(WiFi Connection)-- EX6200 <--(CAT5 Cable)-- Router

Link to the Netgear EX6200 WiFi Range Extender: http://www.amazon.com/NETGEAR-AC1200-Power-700mW-Extender/dp/B00HQ883QW/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1424617341&sr=8-1&keywords=ex6200

This setup is far more complicated and expensive that it should be thanks to AT&T; nevertheless, it has proven to be stable. I suspect this reliabiity is owed greatly to the fact that the 781S and the EX6200 are both made by Netgear, maximizing compatibility between the two devices.

So, if you're in a similar situation to mine, you should now have all the info necessary to connect the umpteen laptops, desktops, tablets, smart thermostats, media streamers, fitness wearables, etc. in your household.

-------------------------------------------------

How to remedy the ill effects of "Double NAT":
Setting up your network as I've described above will result in a "Double NAT" situation. Basically, all of your client devices are behind two firewalls, the one that belongs to the 781S and the one that belongs to your router. As long as you're at home connecting "outbound" to the internet, there won't be any issues. However, inbound connections from the internet to computers on your network (i.e., people trying to access any servers you may be hosting) won't get routed correctly due to the double firewall situation. However, there is a work around. Basically, we need to make our router the only firewall and have inbound connections bypass the 781S's firewall.

The 781S's internal router does support the DMZ (demilitarized zone) feature. DMZ is a common feature that allows you to select one client (in our case, the router) to which all inbound traffic from the internet is forwarded. So, we want to take the WAN IP of our router and set it as the "DMZ Address." But, first we have to make sure our router's WAN IP will never change (by default, the 781S's internal router dynamically assigns a different IP to the router every time the router establishes a connection, which is not what we want to happen). Unfortunately, the 781S doesn't support DHCP reservations. So, we can't tell the 781S to reserve a specific IP address and only assign it to our router. However, this can still effectively be accomplished by assigning your router a static WAN IP just outside of the 781S's DHCP range.

First, let's check your 781S's current DHCP range:
1. On the 781S's web administration page (by default it's http://attunitepro/index.html), log in as Administrator.
2. Click "Settings" on the navigation menu on the left side.
3. Click the "Router" tab.
4. Click the "Basic" tab.
5. Scroll down to "DHCP IP Range" to check your 781S's DHCP range (the default setting is 192.168.1.20 - 192.168.1.99)

So, based on the default DHCP range, you'd want to set your router's static WAN IP to 192.168.1.100 (of course, if your 781S's DHCP range is different than the default, you'd just adjust the static WAN IP for your router accordingly to be just outside of your 781S's DHCP range).

Now that we've ensured that our router will always have the same WAN IP address, we can now assign that static WAN IP address to be in the 781S's DMZ.

To enable DMZ on the 781S:
1. On the 781S's web administration page (by default it's http://attunitepro/index.html), log in as Administrator.
2. Click "Settings" on the navigation menu on the left side.
3. Click the "Router" tab.
4. Click the "Basic" tab.
5. Scroll down to "DMZ Enabled" and select "On"
6. Just beneath that, input the router's static WAN IP in the field labeled "DMZ Address"
7. Click Submit (Submit button appears once you make a selection).

Ok, with that, you should have effectively circumvented the negative effects typically caused by a "Double NAT" situation. Technically, both firewalls still exist, so your router will still report a "Double NAT" status. However, instead of passing through the 781S's internal firewall, then the router's firewall, and finally to the client devices, inbound traffic from the internet will now be sent directly to your router's firewall and on to the client devices (point being, the 781S's firewall will get bypassed, which is what we want to happen in order to mitigate the issues commonly associated with "Double NAT" status).

title: Great Buy with HD traffic
text:
Maybe this is premature, but I have had this for a few days now and it is replacing a Garmin that was at least 7 years old. I did read the negative comments, but my experience so far has been outstanding.(I did notice that some of the comments about glare were for a 5" gps l think is actually a different model) I did some research and decided that having the convenience of HD traffic with its faster traffic updates would be something I would like to use. The HD traffic updates are wonderful and in one instance saved me a good 20 minutes with a reroute. Another time while we were stuck in traffic due to construction, it was nice to see how far we needed to travel to get past the delay. I particularly like the dual image that shows the route to take when exiting, along with what lanes to be in when approaching either an exit or split in the road. The voice command works well and is easy to use, although I found when the car was full and everyone speaking that it was necessary to speak louder than normal to get a response. I also like the way in addition to street names you are given landmarks when making the turn; turn at the light, turn at the BP gas station etc. This is much more driver friendly.

I noticed that there were a few comments about glare, and I was concerned that this might be a problem. I should say that I have tried the gps using both the windshield mount as well as the dash mount (Garmin friction mount) and did not have an issue with either display. The picture was crisp and clear. For the record I prefer the dash mount, I was worried that it would come tumbling down, but so far it has worked perfectly and it is really easy to either remove from the car or placed out of view when I leave the car.

I did a great deal of comparison shopping for this gps and realized that I did want a unit that had the HD traffic for the updates on rush hour traffic, occasional long vacation and leisure trips. This model gave me the best of both worlds; great function and a reasonable price. The 6" size is great for viewing and provides easy reading for older eyes, I really enjoy the voice command function and am looking forward to linking my cell to it for hands free calling. While it does not have the dash or rear view camera they can be added, but for me not having them was not a deal breaker. My favorite part of this model is that when you deviate from the course of the route, whether on purpose or accident, it will quickly automatically recalculate the new route - and here is the best part -- I DON'T HAVE TO LISTEN TO "RECALCULATING" over and over again.

title: Look at the pictures and judge for yourself.
text:
I wanted to like this cleaner. I have been using lenspens for years and this looked to be a product from a competitor who had studied the Lenspen and come up with a better way to do the job.

So I bought one, unboxed it and tried it out on a Leupold scope that sits on my match rifle. The pictures you see are of a 33mm lens that was already pretty much clean (I keep my scope lenses perfect), then cleaned with the Carson tool. Using the microfiber pad, I cleaned the ocular lens with the typical swirling circular motion that goes with these types of tools. Then I carried it into the kitchen and hit my very bright kitchen overhead lights. Holy cow its smudged as if the tool has oil on it. I tried it again on the objective lens and sure enough - same smudging. As you can see from the pictures the edges are clean but the center of the lens is a mess. Then I dug out a lenspen and it easily cleaned all of the gunk off that the Carson tool put on the lens.

Put simply, this tool is worthless. Sorry to see that as its construction appears sturdy whereas the Lenspen is not. But look at the pictures, and how an old Lenspen fixed the problem it caused. These results speak for themselves.

The two ocular lens pics are of the same swirls. First pic I am holding a small flashlight onto it. Second pic I used the flash on my camera. Objective lens pics I am holding a flashlight onto it with camera lens very close to scope lens.

Lastly, look around at the other 1-star reviews... Looks like I am far from the first person to describe this problem. This review just seems to be the first to show the problem on a lens.

I'm returning the product today.

edit: Whoops I went to the trouble of writing captions in the pics themselves but I got the lens names wrong. Where I say "ocular" I should have said "objective" and vice versa.

I bought this largely for the Smart TV features, especially the Spectrum App for use in the kitchen. We mostly watch that, YouTube and Netflix. title: Great idea, with room for improvement.
text: Style is what you pay for. The finish is perfect and matches my iPhone like no other but... Its a great concept with much room for improvement. First off let me say the first impression was amazing! The build quality of the box alone made me feel like I just bought a $1,000 pair of headphones. The same rigid packaging of the iPhones, clean white, an airtight vacuum when you open the box. You see a beautiful firm case that you look at and can't wait to see what's inside. Embossed with the Muzik logo, a silk bag sits inside the satin finish case, with a silver logo. Elegance at its finest. When you pull the case out of its nest inside the box you reveal the manuals, not like any other. On silky smooth cardstock in the shape of the logo. Held together with a brad of some sorts so you can spin each step into place. The instructions are simple: Charge, Power, Pair, Play & Connect. Once you connect the app will guide you through every step of how to assign the hot keys. This is where the review gets its -3 stars. Although the tagging to social media is great, the functionality isn't there yet. Maybe if you're a media giant then it makes sense, but for the average person not really. The home automation features are nice, but tend to be hit or miss. Though this could be fixed with firmware updates in the future I think they could've worked better before release. Also my headphones have started to fall apart, and I have taken great care of them. I've had to push the rubber along the head strap back into place twice although I rarely wear them. When I'm pairing them to my laptop they disconnect every 15-20 minutes. I'm using the late 2016 MacBook, so it's not a Bluetooth chip issue. So on that note I just plug in. The problem is when I went to unplug the auxiliary cable from the computer, for the first time, the sheath came unglued and came apart. I'm a photographer who is very gentile with his equipment and I'm not sure these are even the right fit for me. Frankly the build quality just doesn't live up to the price. Maybe as their order sizes get larger from the factory they can afford to improve the build quality. I wish I could return these.

So the only people giving this thing glowing reviews are people that live 10 miles or less from town and didn't need a 50 mile antenna anyway and people who work for the companies and people who are given antennas for free and told they must write a positive review. That's it because both 150 mile antennas I've had wouldn't even pick up all the channels 50 miles away pointed in any direction, let alone 150 and the now 3 anywhere from 50 to 60 mile antennas won't either. You can say "ideal conditions" and other such crap but if 5 antennas won't pick up everything they're supposed to in 2 different towns I've lived in and 2 different residences, both 2nd floor elevated places, if 5 antennas won't work, it's not me or where I'm at, it's the antennas and the criminal liars who sell them. title: Beastly hardware quality and performance
text:
This router replaced a Linksys WRT1900AC v1 I had for 2+ years. This new EA9500. The second you open the box. It feels and looks like a very premium product. Kudos to Linksys on the incredible build quality. But that is nothing new. It has always been like that with their routers. I was not even hooked up yet and I was impressed on that alone once again! Getting it setup. One word. EASY! It just does not get any simpler then this.

One thing I have liked about Linksys routers. They are so simple to setup and work with. Anyone could do it. I decided to manually set it up as I always do with my routers. Before configuring any thing. Once inside gui page. I checked for a firmware update. One was available. I let it download and after it finished. I followed up with a factory reset with in the gui. I highly advise doing this any time you do a firmware update.

Once done. I setup up each of my devices with DHCP reservations with in the routers gui. Once all devices got configured. I followed up with a reboot of the router and off I went. I have the following devices.

2 Desktops (wired)
Ooma Telo VOIP (wired)
2 iPod Touch 6th gens (5GHz wireless)
iPad Air 2 (5GHz wireless)
PS4 (2.4GHz wireless)
PS4 Pro (5GHz Wireless)
LG 65UB9300 4k tv (5GHz wireless)
Dell XPS 13 9350 (5GHz wireless)
HP Envy Printer (2.4GHz wireless)

Everything just worked. Before doing this review. I wanted to make sure it was solid. I gave it a full week hammering the network and not a single problem at all. Just does its job like it suppose to and you for get it is even there. I will say this though. I do have a couple of minor complaints. Using the factory settings. On 2.4GHz band for the channel. It had selected channel 2.

That is a bad selection. You want non over lapping channels. I manually set it to 6 and it was fine. Always use 1, 6 or 11. The other thing is the network map and dhcp listings. It can be buggy. Duplicate devices and devices showing wired instread of wireless or wireless showing as wired. I brought this to Linksys attention on their own forums. 4th post down here http://community.linksys.com/t5/Wireless-Routers/Smart-Wifi-Network-Map/td-p/1055466/page/4

I am sure Linksys will remedy this issue through future firmware updates. My other complaint. No real bandwidth monitoring. Asus, Netgear etc all have this. And what I mean. For you can see bandwidth usage in real time by device, per devices, daily, weekly and monthly usages. Linksys for some reason has not added something like that. This is their flagship router and this is a big overlook imo.

Especially with caps now a days. I imagine people would really appreciate this feature from Linksys. I would and hope its added to this EA9500 in a future firmware update. With those 2 minor complaints out of the way. The router has been great. Speed demon it is. Great stuff from Linksys. I also like the very strong warranty Linksys offers. We are talking 3 years 24/7 phone support.

The "other" guys do 1 year and 90 days phone support. It shows and tells me Linksys stands by their product and has faith in it. So in closing.

Pros
Great build quality
Easy to use and setup. Pretty sure a pet could set this up! ;)
Very fast
Reliable
Strong warranty

Cons
Network map can be buggy along with DHCP listings
2.4GHz channel selection could be better with factory settings. Maybe lock in channels 1, 6 or 11 for choices or when bouncing around if interference occurs.

With out a doubt. I can highly recommend this router to anyone with out hesitation.

I purchased this for myself for Christmas. Finally got a chance to take it out and trolled it behind my inflatable boat. It was really nice to be able to know the depth of the water wherever we trolled. That is the primary reason for the purchase. One thing I have to note is that even though we totally slayed it and caught 15 trout in 2 days the fish finder reported no fish in the lake the entire time. That's right it didn't think there were any fish in the lake at all! At no point in the two full days that we use this did it detect a single fish underwater. For that reason it lost two stars in my review. I did switch the settings around from boat mode to regular mode and the frequency back and forth with no luck. It's still never found a fish. This is a really cool thing to have and I love that it integrates with my Android phone but it's tough calling it a fish finder if it can't find fish. Just saying. Overall I am still happy with the purchase as I indicated the primary motivation was the depth finder.
On a separate note I tied two strings to the fish finder and attach them to my boat while trolling. title: Features and performance of the WRT more than overcome the retro industrial design
text:
My husband, the techie in our family tested this and here's his feedback:
The WRT1200AC (WRT) is well suited for home office (like mine) or a small business that may or may not need a dedicated firewall. I have a dedicated firewall, (old) SonicWall (SW) Appliance so my TWC modem goes into the SW with one Ethernet port to the Router, because of biz requirements.
The WRT slipped right in place of my NetGear R6300 with a MAC change on the SW. The 6300 replaced a previous Linksys EA2700, as all our phones were upgraded to SGN3's (with ac). I have several 4TB DLINK NAS boxes that have 1G+ files that I have to move around. My home office has a hard wired server and an assortment of wireless devices including phones(5), printers(3), laptops(5), NAS(4), chrome sticks (2), fire stick, set top box(3) and a couple of other mac addresses I need to track down.
The 6300 is in the middle of a single story 2600 Sq. ft. house and is somewhat range limited at the edges on g & n. The phones do fine anywhere in the house and for a good 10 feet outside the house.

As there are several detailed/quantitative reviews of the WRT on the net, I'm limiting my comments to a more qualitative review of the WRT in my environment. Phone reception is the same as the R6300. Wireless streaming to the laptops (g & n) from the NAS' is the same except at the perimeter of the house. The WRT has a stronger signal and when streaming there were no buffering lags. Again, I have no ac cards for the laptops - so g & n only.

Now here's what I really like about the WRT - I was able to hook a 2TB (WD) drive to the USB3 port and then reconfigured the drive with an eSATA adapter. Both adapters worked perfectly with WRT. I also tried a 2TB Seagate, again with no problems. I could not get an external drive to work reliably of the NetGear USB2 port. I formatted the drive in ntfs with no problems. For comparison with the NAS I did some transfers to my server eSATA port. I was able to get about 15% better performance from the WRT than from the NAS. Yea! The NAS’ are older DLINK DNS’, so that is part of the equation and the new WRT processor and USB3/eSATA was the other part – but Yippee! The expansion drive box for the WRT has USB3 & eSATA and looks to fit nicely under the WRT – Although I don’t see anyone selling that unit yet.

Internet access – The WRT should be fine, but the SW sits between TWC and the WRT for me – simplifies my many conversations with TWC!

ROS – router OS; “We” seem to be in that no man land where every vendor feels the need to do a custom web interface to their routers – I don’t like the NetGear web interface! And I don’t like the Linksys web interface either! But, the WRT processor drives the many “useless” html pages faster than the “older” NetGear or other Linksys routers I have had. And like the NetGear you can get a “useless” network map! Just what my mom and dad would enjoy – not!

Remote management – Because of the SW, I did not access the Android remote management for the WRT.

Wireless streaming - I did a 4GB file transfer from my server to the eSATA drive attached to the WRT and simultaneously streamed a 1G+ MP4 to the Chrome Stick from my laptop – WOW, no buffering on the streaming movie!

Price – mine was provided for review, BUT I’m keeping it! It seems as though the consensus is to go for the WRT1900 – better antenna price performance than the 1200 J

Oh, and one other note – I do agree with the reviewer that mentioned the WPS access should be on the front of the WRT. The NetGear’s is on the side.

Open Source – cool, but had no time to evaluate.

I will miss the warm white glow of the NetGear logo, but the Linksys panel lights are pleasing to. I thought about using the R6300 as a bridge; I thought about adding a hi-gain antenna; but at this point why waste the money and electrons (?)

Overall, the features and performance of the WRT more than overcome the retro industrial design - 4 out 5 stars

title: M3 Too Small for Most Use
text:
I have a FiiO X1 Gen 1 player and I love it. I thought the M3 would give me the same utility in a smaller, plastic box. I was wrong. As others have said, the user interface is bad - no where near as functional as the user interface on the X1. Other reviewers wrote that the buttons were too small - I agree. They are way too small. If product can be reduced in size to the point of being non functional, this is "Example A".

I do believe, that if a buyer was only looking for a portable MP3 player to use when running, hiking or working out, this is probably a fine solution so long as you are happy playing random songs from the M3. The sound is more than good enough and, as I said, it is small and very light.

If you'e looking for a unit to play organized music or playlists on a home stereo system or through some form of AUX input in your car, my advice is to spend the extra $45 and get the FiiO X1.

title: Echo is an Excellent Gizmo with Horrible Configuration Instructions and Install Menu - Over time it becomes DISAPPOINTING
text:
I changed my 5 star review to 1 star. To find out why please read the section labeled EDIT UPDATE.

I really like the Echo device, but it took me way to long to get the Echo configured because the instructions and menu's are extremely poor, to put it mildly.

THE PROBLEMS
1. First, the instruction fail to say whether the app to download is for iPhone, Android, PC or Mac.
I assumed it would be safest to use my Android smartphone, but after downloading and attempting to install I got a message which basically said -this app is incompatible the smartphone. My smarphone is compatible with every App I have downloaded. Because I hate Win8, 8.1 and 10 I still use Windows 7 which does not support "Apps", which is why I did not attempt to use my PC for downloading the "App".

2. Setup menu is also horrible, and confusing. For example for the setting of metric vs other does not really give a choice, it has an On Off button which does not appear to do anything. It certainly does not bring up an edit menu.
It should really simply have metric vs foot (units) so that you simply put a check mark to the one you want. Same for Celsius vs Fahrenheit
As a consequence I still get Celsius when I want Fahrenheit etc. This is because of an extremely useless, frustrating User Interface.

3. The Echo froze once or twice, so I had to unplug it and I had to start all over, until eventually it decided that it was fully setup.

It should have had an interface like most Routers, which you configure by browsing to the device, which brings up a menu that you configure.

If you have not setup an Echo before, you should be aware that once you run the "App" which is downloaded from the internet, you then have to disconnect from your wifi network, and instead connect to amazon-net (I don't remember the exact name) which then allows your smartphone, tablet or laptop etc. to connect your Echo (this of course means that you are no longer connected to the internet).

Other than the setup, the Echo v 2 is excellent, with wonderful text to speech conversion that is the best I have ever heard. The one thing missing is the ability to retain the very last task before it is unplugged when you take it to another location. I especially like that you can connect to any radio station, ask for any radio program (Fresh Air, Science Friday, Ted Talk, The Moth, Back Story etc. It's also great to ask about anything that is on Wikipedia. Finally, to my surprise the text to speech on Wikipedia, as well as on Kindle books is far better than I expected, far less like a robot, than what I heard in the past.

Edit UPDATE 3/1/2017: (reason why I changed my rating from 5 star to 1 star)
As others have said while the device works well at first, over time everything about the device starts growing disappointing.
Here are my reasons
1. Radio programs such as Freakonomics (via TuneIn) is no longer available
2. Radio programs that always used to be up to date Fresh Air, Science Friday, On the Media, etc. are no longer up to date. Whenever you request them you get one weeks older and they newer broadcasts are way out of date if available at all. A lot of programs available on TuneIn cannot be accessed via Echo Dot.

Echo Malfunctions:
1. Echo turns on for no apparent reasons as if someone said Alexa in the room. This problem was non existent or extremely rare for the first 2-3 months.

3. Echo does not appear to understand request nearly as well as when it was new. Sometimes re-phrasing the request for the 3rd or 4th time works, but often I we just give up. This is especially true of requesting playing Audible titles. Echo Dot often confuses Kindle text to speech version with the Audible (human / actor reading of text). With all of the "Continual Improvement" hoopla about Alexa that Amazon brags about, you would think that you could request a book title and get what you want for existing books in your Account.

4. You would think that if, while listening, you are interrupted by a phone call etc., you should be able to have Alexa, go back a page or two in the reading of your Kindle or Audible book. This function appears to be ABSENT and no matter how we tried we could not go forward or back by any amount other than by an entire Chapter. This is not Rocket Science and could easily be programmed. Pages do exist even on Kindle, it's a simple matter of assigning a "page" a standard number of words or characters.

5. Often, though not always, if you unplug Echo Dot, in order to use it in another room, it will lose information about what it was doing (what book it was reading). This should not happen and would not be difficult to prevent.

IN SUMMARY
Instead of constantly IMPROVING, Echo Dot functionality has actually declined in our experience as reported by others. This calls into question the competence of the Amazon Software Team. Sadly, like too many things in the computer world, stupidity too often overcomes common sense competence.

title: 980s Overall Experience.
text:
Do you hate options menus? Do you like graphical fidelity? Do you value performance ratings over price/performance ratios without going to extremes? Then the GTX 980 is the perfect choice for you.
It's no question that the GTX 970 has a better price/performance ratio and you'll be able to pick one up for just at 200$ less, and if your budget can't handle the increased price of the GTX 980; you're not missing all too much. Realistically from what I've seen, the GTX 980 performs about 10-20% better, which isn't enough for many to justify 200$.
Likewise, the GTX 980 is to the Titan X what the 970 is to the 980. For another 500$, twice the price of the 980, you can have a Titan X and 20-30% better performance. I, myself, opted for a dual SLI 980 build rather than a single Titan X build. SLI 980s performs a good bit better than a single Titan X and cost about 100$ more. With DirectX12 coming out soon, SLI is a smarter idea than ever due to SLI scaling. Currently, dual-GPU configs realistically only run at 160-170% the performance of a single card. DirectX12 aims to make that 200% in addition to the massive performance tweaks. With dual 980s already outperforming a single Titan X, it was a no brainer to me to go for the 980s.
For those worried about the 980 only having 4GB of VRAM (and planning to SLI), don't. DirectX12 is said to also add together VRAM instead of limit it to the maximum of one card. This means that a dual 980 build will have 8GB of usable VRAM - plenty for 1440p or 4k. At 4k, Shadows of Mordor on maximum settings with the ultra texture pack only uses 6.5GB. Shadows of Mordor is an extreme example, however, as most games don't even come close to touching 4GB, even at 4k.

All of that said, you really don't need to opt for SLI with the 980. Unless you're trying to future proof for a while or plan to play in 4k in everything that has it as an option, it's unnecessary. One single 980 very, very easily gets 60FPS at 1080p max settings. The same can be said for 1440p, you'll rarely if ever see less than 60FPS at max settings. Even at 4k, you'll generally have over 30FPS.

I'm not a fan of overclocking generally because I don't trust my own ability not to destroy it; thankfully, EVGA has one of the highest stock clocks of the 980. I can safely have an overclock done by professionals without having to worry about my warranty. Additionally, EVGA's cooler design is very well done. The ACX 2.0 design acts as an intake rather than an exhaust and seems to work very well. Only with kboost on for extended periods of time have I come close to breaking 70 Celsius (with fans set to maximum). That said, unless you're benchmarking or doing something extreme like that; you'll never, ever hear your fans. In fact, on the stock fan config, the fans won't turn on until they reach 50 degrees Celsius. On maximum, however, they are quite loud. Playing Shadows of Mordor at 4k on maximum settings, the fans are barely at half speed and still rather quiet; though I'm not the type to care about how loud fans are.

I'm very happy with my 980s and I'd recommend them to anyone with a similar budget; but for those who prefer to save 200$ or 400$ in an SLI build, the 970 is a worthy choice as well.

title: Quite a little beauty for the price
text:
[[VIDEOID:f277b18f5e8fc6d3b19a32c2d40f29bd]] Update from my original post: I have upgraded from four stars to five after having it out in the field. I found it to be very stable and solid as well as flexible for different shooting situations. Remember though that this is my light travel tripod, but I couldn't be happier for the value I got on this. I tested it against my photo buddy's light Manfrotto travel tripod (Older model) and the Q999C was lighter (his is metal) and more sturdy with less vibration. No contest.

I purchased the Q-999C on the recommendation of a friend and have to say I was very suspect of a tripod at this price, but my initial impression is very favorable. I bought it for long hikes or climbs only and it will not replace my heavy duty Manfrotto, but it weighs 7.6 pounds as opposed to this little beauty at 3.1. I've only had it a few days and haven't taken it out for a real shoot yet. I have checked it out very thoroughly in the house. The rated maximum weight is about 17.5 pounds, but I put considerably more than that on it for testing and found it held strong. The legs open and close smoothly and the ball head also moves smoothly. It has nice little extras like a ring on the tripod mount bracket screw to help tighten it to the camera. It has the ability to turn the center post around so you can mount the camera underneath for extremely low angle and macro shots. It has a spring loaded hook on the bottom of the center post for hanging your camera bag or other weights to improve stability. I personally would like it to have the ability to have both the rubber feet and metal spikes, but that is fairly minor. I go into more detail on several points in the attached video, which I hope helps you make a wise decision. Why only four stars. Because I haven't had a chance to field test it yet. After I get it out for a real shoot I'll decide if this should be upgraded or downgraded and I'll add more comments then.

title: Perfect product for my needs
text:
This is the best Bluetooth device I've ever used. It pairs easily and flawlessly with my Android phone. I mostly listen to audiobooks or music while I ride. The speakers were a perfect fit for the speaker cutouts in my Scorpion EXO T510 helmet. The wires tucked away easily under the air skirt and the mic has stayed right where I put it too. Mounting the clamp on the side was easier than I thought as well. I expected to have at least a little trouble working it between the shell and the foam, but I didn't.

HUGE props for how well the phone button activates the Android voice feature instead of some proprietary list of commands! This gives me access to tons of commands that the Sync in my F-150 doesn't offer. Plus, the jog wheel and rear button are easy to feel/use with my multi-layered leather gloves.

The FM radio is damned impressive and with the free Android app adding/changing presets is really easy. Stations come in loud and clear several counties away, but any further away it's not quite as clear as it is in a vehicle with an antenna.

I commute about 45 minutes each way to work and still only have to recharge the battery once every 3 or 4 days. On weekends I can use up a fully charged battery in a couple of day, but only if I ride 12 or 14 hours total.

I got rained on with it attached to my helmet this weekend and it kept playing radio station I was listening to without a hitch. I assumed it was water resistant, but it was good to confirm that before I "needed" it to be.

I haven't gotten to try the intercom system yet, but I'm sure it'll work. Everything else about this device is perfect.

title: Great alarm system
text:
I was looking for an alarm system but I didn't want to pay the high rate for monitoring. Simplisafe is a good alternative.
The system:
When I got the box, it said to plug the usb keychain into my computer for an automated installation. I tried that and the program wouldn't run, because its only for PC computers and some older Mac OS, not the most recent (which I have). I was able to find the instruction booklet, and a video online. The video left out some crucial information about the placement of some of the sensors, so I did have to remove some and re-stick them after reading the instruction manual. I would expect a little more from this aspect, but all in all it wasn't super difficult.
The motion sensors tell you to stick them in a corner, but the back of them is flat where the tape goes so you have to screw them into the wall if you want to get them in the corner. The manual advises you to apply them 4-5 feet off the ground, which leaves them very visible, which isn't the best looking.

Monitoring:
The monitoring was fairly easy to set up. $14.99/mo gets you the basic monitoring. When I set mine up it said I would need an alarm permit from my local police station to continue setup, and once I had this permit to call simplisafe to continue my monitoring setup. I called and the police told me it actually wasn't necessary so that was good, I called in to simplisafe (about 5-10 minutes hold time) and then the lady told me not to worry about it, I was already set up if I didn't need the permit. I also had to ask her how to get the certificate so I could submit it to my insurance company, I just had to log in to my account to get that (would have been nice to have gotten an email with the certificate to save me the step)
Once logged in, you can see all the times your system was turned on or off, which is cool. They do try to sell you the upgrade to 19.99/mo so you can get mobile alerts and whatever else, but that is par for the course. You have little prompts in the dashboard like "setup your mobile device to get alerts" and then when you click on it you get hit with the upgrade screen, pretty much like any other online service nowadays.

All in all I feel safer with the system and the price isn't bad. I really like the fact that it is modular so I can add other sensors later if I want.

title: Lasted training and racing for 5 marathons and 2 ironmans - no issues
text: As an Ironman athlete and outdoors enthusiast, I've used LifeProof waterproof cases and mounts for over 4 years. Even though I don't like paying the premium they demand, it's always worth it. I had their legacy armband as well that gripped all 4 corners of the lifeproof Fre case and it was literally bombproof. When I tried this newer sleeker design that feels less secure, I wasn't completely convinced it would hold up. Well, here I am 5 marathons, 2 ironmans and about 2,000 miles of running later and it never once fell off or became worn and loose (neither the adhesive magnet or the connection point). I also have a mount on my motorcycle handlbars and use the Quickmount to lock in my phone and ride pretty fast (with no windshield on my bike) and again, hasn't failed once. I should also add that I have the Quick mounts on both my Lifeproof waterproof case and also just a cheapo $6 pop you phone in and out of case so I have the option of clicking onto my arm or motorcycle either the solid Lifeproof case for the elements or sleeker case for nice days and at the gym. The adhesive didn't let up on either (at least 1.5 years of working out on each), so I think those that have issues likely put it on a non-smooth case surface or didn't prep the area correctly with alcohol. I've bought this for friends as a gift and they love it too. My only criticism I have is that it does rattle around a little bit vs a standard style case. If I have headphones in I can't hear it, and even when I can (i.e. during marathons) it's tolerable. Needless to say, I'm a fan and will continue using for a long time.

text:
Excellent product, very easy to use. I had installed an OTA antenna some time back and was able to pick up most stations in my living room just fine, however, in my office I was missing several stations completely. Since they all run off the same antenna and I could get some stations in my office, I found this to be odd. So, I went ahead and purchased this unit along with a "PCT Series PCTMPI1G Power Inserter for Distribution Amplifiers" and had it up and running within a few minutes. Not only was the signal much stronger in my living room, but it was good and strong for all stations in my office also. Still need to run more cables elsewhere, but I'm positive this will handle them just fine.

You might ask why I got the "Power Inserter" mentioned above? This box is very well made and weatherproof, so I located it outside under my eaves where I split off antenna signal to my different rooms. However, the power supply that comes with it is made to hook directly in to the box and be plugged in right next to it, but I didn't have a power outlet there. The power inserter allows me to insert the power right before my TV where I do have power and use the same cable to go back to this box. Normally the power alone would go into the top left input shown in the picture, which is clearly marked. When using the power inserter, the bottom left plug is clearly marked as being available for both power and antenna combined. The two work great together.

That might be my only complaint is that I was a bit cautious trying to figure out what to use. It's not clearly documented in the descriptions. I was cautious in getting a different brand power inserter for this, had a "Channel Master" version been available on Amazon I would have gone with that. With some research I felt fairly comfortable going this way though. I would have gladly spent a bit more money to get a channel master distribution amp that included the power inserter with it though!!

title: which is very good. I was curious whether it would really pick ...
text:
Somehow the word "nifty" comes to mind when thinking of this recorder. Some of that comes from its petite size: my measurements give 8.5x3.7x1.3 cm or 3.3x1.5x0.5 in, and weight 34g or 1.2 oz.

Unfortunately Amazon doesn't allow attachment of .wav files, otherwise I'd share what it records, which is very good. I was curious whether it would really pick up a lecturer in a college classroom, and from 10 feet away, it records a "public speaking" voice quite clearly.

I was able to connect this recorder to my Zen mp3 player with 3.5mm audio cables (the one provided with the recorder, and one I had on hand), and record the Zen playback with very little loss of quality.

I think I would need a special cable to record from my Nexus 5x phone. I tried connecting from its headphone jack, and got almost no audio. Then I read where some smartphones need a 3-stripe connector to interpret the signal going to a microphone jack. I won't pursue that, because putting the phone on Speaker and using the built-in mic on the recorder gives a nice clear recording. (My phone does output properly to ear buds.)

I couldn't test the telephone equipment included in the package; I don't have a landline any more.

The external lavalier mic included in the bundle did not work well, recording at about 1/4th the level of the built-in mic. Not quite inaudible, but too low to use it. The vendor said they'd send another. I'll update this if I receive it.

The USB cable has the old mini-USB plug to attach to the recorder. That provides the benefit that I now have a second cable for my Zen player, which came with a short 5" cable. This one is about 29".

The cable also serves as a data connection to your computer. I was able to rename files on the recorder, delete files from the recorder and copy files off the recorder. I was able to copy files to the recorder either by syncing within Windows Media Player, and by just drag and drop. WMP created a Music folder; I dragged to the root directory. (Two songs were provided on the root.) Playback saw both the "foldered" and the rooted files.

Battery drain is impressively slow. I deliberately let it play for a couple of hours (with a cable plugged into the headphone jack so I wouldn't have to hear it) before it showed 1/4th battery drain. Charging from a power bank was fairly fast. I also let it record overnight. It stopped at about 11.5 hours in what appears to be a battery preservation strategy, because I could wake it and saw 1/4 battery remaining, and after recharging it allowed me to start a second recording. When the second recording crossed the 12 hour mark, it still showed 1/2 battery. Then I plugged the recorder into my computer, which stopped and saved the recording. These ~12 hour recordings show (via my computer) as about 1GB each. Total capacity for the recorder shows as 7.8GB.

After Ejecting, the recorder continues to charge from the computer. You can record and playback while charging (just not while the recorder is visible to the computer as a "device".) When fully charged, the display says so.

The recorder only executes my commands while the display is lit. In other words, once the display has dimmed to power-saving mode, pressing the record (or play or any) button only wakes the display. I have to press the button a second time to get the action intended.

When playing music, the display shows the jumping histogram of volume bars. I wish it would do that when recording. (It doesn't even do it for playback of a recording.)

I tested one of the VOR settings (set under Record Type), and the recorder does pause when it hears no sound, and resumes recording when sound returns. So voice-activated recording worked.

The device has more settings than the documentation describes. But I was able to use most of its features. For instance, I found the Monitor On setting useful to compensate for the lack of volume bars when recording. And I'm impressed that you can set the timer for the display power-saver (Backlight; 0 appears to turn off the saver) and there's a sleep timer (didn't try it). But I could NOT figure out what the Record From settings did. (Tried them all, but saw no difference.)

(If only for my own future reference:) To set the date/time, use the +/- buttons on the left side to choose which cell to change, and the forward/back buttons on the right to change the values. This seems contrary to the rest of the Settings, where forward/back usually moves the cursor to choose the option. (Well, they also change values in other places. Tough call for what to do when you need to control both in one screen.)

At $20, this is quite a good value. Deducted 1 star for bad external mic and poor instruction sheet. I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

Update 8/28: I did finally receive a replacement mic. It still records at a slightly lower volume than the built-in mic, but much better than the defective original.

If you found something helpful here, don't forget that little button below.

title: Even for the price, not at all worth it--RIPPLES!!!
text:
[EDIT] Unfortunately had to drop this review to a mere 1 star rating. Why? THE RIPPLES!!! UGHHHH!!!

Out of the box there were some fairly small V shaped ripples on each side, which is fairly common for non-tensioned screens. At first, it wasn't entirely noticeable and thought I could live with it. That would've been the case had the ripples stayed as they were and hadn't gotten worse over time. Keep in mind I keep this screen down at all times, as there was no need for me to roll it up. From what I've learned, doing so could've actually let the screen flatten out further, but this was not the case with mine--the ripples got more pronounced with time as it hung there. Gaming was annoying/distracting as large areas of your field of view would distort, menus were distorted/curved rather than square, and watching 3D movies? Forget about it.

I then learned more about the alternative of tensioned screens, either fixed or built-in to a pull down system like these but with some extra tricks to keep tension. Some folks even had luck with this exact screen (or something very similar) by adding weight to the bottom. Some used lead shot to weigh down the bottom tube, others tried adding tension with bungee cords. I opted for the bungee option, and while it did make the situation better, the ripples were still more than noticeable. Adding weight/tension may help some of you guys, definitely worth a shot.

$80 may seem like a good buy, but be mindful that you definitely get what you pay for in this case. This screen is GARBAGE, easily one of the worst available today. It's cheaply made, the included hardware is crap (had to use my own for proper SAFE mounting), and most importantly your view is going to be junk due to the quality of this screen and the distortion it creates. If you're OK with ripples (trust me, no one is--you will go insane) then this is for you, but take my advice and put out a little more $$$ for your investment--get a properly tensioned screen and save yourself a huge headache. I'm replacing this with a 100" fixed screen that is only $60 more, but 100% flat and will look 10x better than these cheap pull-downs. It also includes GOOD hardware, crazy no?!

Unfortunately out $80 due to the mistake of buying this "Elite" screen, but lesson learned. Now to find someone that wants to buy my rippled screen...

title: Applephiles get a 4kTV and then buy this
text:
Our house became Apple'fied a few years ago and the Apple TV box is pretty much central to that experience. If I have any complaint it's that I had just upgraded from a 3rd generation box to the 4th when this 4k version came out. Not a big deal until we upgraded to a 4k tv soon after, and then I had NO choice but to shell out the bucks for a 4k box! There are several in depth reviews here covering all the features so I won't repeat here other than to say you will need high speed internet and make sure you are using the proper HDMI cables (HDCP 2.2, ARC, HDMI 2.0, 18Gbit, etc.). Proper HDMI cables are a must or you won't get the best 4k has to offer ie; 4kHDR or DolbyVision at 60 Hz. Our particular setup is an LG 65" LED/LCD 4kHDtv, Yamaha 4k pass through receiver and a 5.1 home theater speaker system. Peripherals include the AppleTV, Firestick and BluRay DVD player. Everything runs off high speed WiFi and everything communicates with each other perfectly. All the remotes automatically program to run each of the other devices including the Apple remote. At the end of the day 4k video is simply stunning, and I just don't see how they will improve upon it short of someday beaming signals straight to the cortex! If you're already in the Apple-verse, you know all you have to do is plug this thing in and it will set up virtually by itself. Just run the software updates and get the 4k settings where you want them. Couldn't be easier. Starting with the 4th generation box you can download apps from the App Store; many free and some paid. I don't do a lot of gaming but it has that capability. Frankly if you're here reading this then you probably already know what you want so I'll just close by saying get it. We recently cut the cord and the 4k Apple box along with an HD OTA antenna is central to that goal. We couldn't be happier.

EDIT 1: A few months have gone by and all good. Wanted to update by informing that my LG tv has some of the same apps as the Apple Box and I find they are much more stable using the Apple device. YouTubetv in particular can be wonky when using the LG app, but works perfectly on ATV. Just one more bonus point!

EDIT 2: There are a whole lot of comments under my post that seem fake to me. IDK if that's Amazon or Apple or who is responsible but it's pretty lame. Makes it seem like a scam product which of course Apple products are anything but. 2 years using this box and all good. I like it as much as when I first got it. title: If you only read B&N purchased eBooks, this is sufficient.
text:
The new case (white/copper) to the Nook GlowLight Plus is very sharp but the support and device inside falls far short of it's advertisements. My main complaint is while it advertises being compatible with library's ebook lending sites, it does not deliver this feature.

I purchased the Nook GlowLight Plus directly from B&N in early December 2015 for my mother as her previous Nook Simpletouch was not compatible with Overdrive (which many public libraries use to lend ebooks) as Nook uses Adobe Digital Editions and there were problems with the original Nook Simpletouch's compatibility. I was initially pleased to see (from the Nook Glowlight Plus' page on BN.com) that Adobe DE support had improved as the device itself stores the username & password for Adobe. Unfortunately this difference didn't correct the compatibility issue with the Simpletouch that was nearly five years old--and after two hours of troubleshooting and contacting Adobe support (who was sympathetic but had no interest in supporting the nook's compatibility issue with the Adobe DE program), there was ultimately no solution and many online forums have the same complaint from other Nook customers. The IT person at my mother's library even stated, "I've never gotten a B&N Nook to work with Overdrive."

If this were the only problem, I would have given it three stars (if an item advertises a function that it does not deliver, it will never earn a 4-star rating) but this edition doesn't deliver any of the improvements that BN advertises--the response and start-up is very slow for an e-reader and the screen is sharp but not as clear as Amazon's Kindle Paperwhite (they both have 300 dpi, the difference is likely in use of ebook format and font). My mother was also disappointed that some of the locations to controls (WiFi on/off and power button) have changed for no useful reason or been buried into menus. The in-store support policy, book sampling, and WiFi while at B&N is the same offer as previous editions--if you worked in or lived next to one of their stores, it could be very worthwhile to consider a Nook.

I decided to return the gift and will be presenting a different e-reader to my mother that I've tested and it earns 5 stars from me. I was within the rather stingy 15-day return period for the Nook Glowlight Plus but it did take 15 minutes on the phone and 3 chat sessions on BN's website to get a return label e-mailed to me.

To give this device a fair shake, the pros are:
-Good battery (as advertised, could not test)
-Good backlight
-Clear text
-Glare-free screen
-Nice case/package (claims dustproof/waterproof, could not test)
-Good boot-up experience (migrates purchased B&N ebooks automatically)
-Free WiFi and book previews while at B&N store via WiFi.

The cons are:
-Not compatible with Overdrive
-Uses a third party solution for library rentals (Adobe DE) which is not supported properly
-Library rentals would require use of a USB cable and host computer (no WiFi download for rented titles)
-Slow screen refresh, some ghosting of previous page image.
-Return/service experience was onerous.

The Nook ebook selection has not been growing as fast as other eReaders and Nook sales have dropped in recent years which affirms my decision to return this one for an e-reader that is well-supported, aligned with a more prosperous company, equally well-designed, does not use third-party licensing software, and uses WiFi to download rentals. If B&N can get their licensing technology (it should be native to consumer's B&N accounts), install a better processor, and support this device better it has the ability to regain some market share for eReaders (and the eBook sales that accompany it), but with this current offering I would advise any potential buyer to consider a different eReader.

In the bright sunny day, sometimes the cameras don't have enough WDR to clearly show the face of a person in the shadow (depending on the amount of the light reflecting to the person) when part of the image is very bright.

If a person run in the front of a camera, the camera may have a hard time to clearly capture the face of the person in moving. I'd give them a better rating if the performance of the cameras meets my expectation.

The cameras can sense the ambient light and they turn on the IR illuminators and switch the IR filter automatically in the night. The quality of the night vision isn't impressive. Additional lighting in the night would help the images.

Warning: Zmodo sPoE is not complied to the standard IEEE 802.3af PoE and don't use the power injector from other vendors to provide power to the IP cameras. Please go to Zmodo Knowledge Base FAQ to find the wiring diagram.

The setup procedure is relatively easy for me:
I have a Netgear router and I made sure the DHCP server in the router was on and UPnP was enabled before the camera system was powered on.
After power-on, use Zviewer on a PC on the same LAN to search the NVR and cameras in the LAN (LAN search). All devices should show up. Add all devices and double click the cameras to view the live images.

After I set them up, I changed the default passwords of the NVR and each camera at once since someone in the internet could hack into your NVR and cameras with the default password.
(Procedures to change passwords by Zviewer (PC version): Right-click the NVR or the cameras and select Remote Settings. Next select User Management and select Admin and click Modify User button. Enter new password.)
(After the passwords are changed, Zviewer may not be able to connect to the devices. Procedures to login the NVR and each cameras in Zviewer: Right-click the NVR or the cameras and select Edit. Enter the new password and click OK.)

To use Zviewer (PC version) to watch the live video streams outside your LAN without DDNS. You need to know 1. your internet or WAN ip address; 2. the external port numbers corresponding to the internal port 8000 of NVR and each camera (obtained from UPnP page in your router); 3. the username and the password for each devices. Run Zviewer and click Add devices. Use IP Search and manually enter the WAN IP address and the external port numbers and so on for the NVR and cameras.

If the router is power-cycled, the WAN ip address or the port numbers may not be the same and you may need to re-enter the new ones in IP Search.

Updated: 3/14/15
After about one month operation, the NVR kept showing 'Disk is not formatted' even I formatted the hard disk or I power-cycled the NVR. I am in the process to contact zmodo.com for the RMA. Down-grading the stars to 2 stars.
