title: Don't let it get too hot
text:
UPDATE (2/10/19):
I decided to give this switch another round of evaluation, to make certain it was my environment, before purchasing a much more expensive 10GBE switch. After setting this switch up, with the two 10G ports connected to different computers and one 1G port connected to my main switch, in a temperature-controlled room with a room temperature sensor placed on the wall about 2 feet from the switch, I left it running overnight. The room temperature never got above 80F, but the switch became so hot that it was unresponsive by 6am, and stayed that way until I disconnected it several hours later. Before stopping the experiment, requests/connections to the switch, and all of the devices connected directly to it, were either timing out or taking over 60 seconds to respond.

My conclusion is that these 10GBE ports run too hot for this small, passively-cooled enclosure.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
I have a NAS, that I set up to record 24/7 video, connected to a 10G port on this switch, but there are hundreds of gaps in the timeline, every day, where the recordings cut out. After a week of this, I plugged the NAS into a 1Gbps port in another switch and I have not had a single dropped second of video in days. The equipment is in a finished, air conditioned attic, but it does get to up to 95F in there during the day, and this switch gets too hot to touch. So, this may or may not be happening to others people with this switch, but, if it is, they might not notice unless their 10G port is under constant load and/or in a warm room. It is my just be my fault for putting a switch in that environment that doesn't have active cooling. Before the switch ended up there, it was used in a room I kept around 80F. I achieved amazing transfer speeds between the NAS and a PC with both connected to 10G ports on the switch.

I am not giving it a low rating because it clearly states in the documentation that the operating temperature is 32-104F. So, this is more of a warning for people looking for the cheapest/best 10G switch they can find. If you keep it nice and cool, it works great.

The image is the video recording timeline for the day I switched the NAS over to another switch I had in the same rack. I changed switches just after 11am, as you can see.

title: Nice little key tester at a reasonable price
text:
Nice little key tester at a reasonable price. The acrylic stand is solid and has a nice heft to it. While not perfect, the little faults don't take away from its score.

Yes, the keys are arranged in a completely random order, from what I can tell. Even if the keys had been arranged in some logical order, there's always a good chance that an owner will rearrange the keys anyway, so to me it's not a big deal at all.

The tester comes with black rubber o-rings installed. Some may complain about it, but it made no difference to me. After testing the switches with and without, I think I prefer the o-rings in place anyway, as the noise dampening is more prominent the harder you strike the keys.

Complaints? I think the clear keys could stand to be a bit clearer so the colors of the switches are more prominent under the caps. And I think it would have been nice if they included a little pamphlet describing the switches, but it's nothing that a quick net search doesn't sort out.

Could it be cheaper for a handful of switches and a piece of plastic? Well, sure. Can't everything be a bit cheaper? Something like this however always has very little inherent value. Once you know what switch you like, what's the point in keeping it aside from having yet another pointless desktop toy. It also would have been nice if they included a few blank spaces for future expansion for those planning on keeping this and not just passing it on to someone in need of a sampler.

title: This is so close to being an excellent headset but falls just a bit short
text:
This is so close to being an excellent headset but falls just a bit short. Prior to purchasing the Jabra headset I used a Bose Bluetooth Headset (Series 2) which I had been extremely happy with prior to the battery deteriorating after several years of heavy use. As of early 2015 the Bose was discontinued with no replacement model available, which left me to try the Jabra.

As far as features, the Jabra does several things better. The caller ID name for your contacts, for example, is spoken into the earpiece when you get an incoming call. You can then say "answer" to accept the call. The Bose headset had neither of these features. The rated battery life of the Jabra is also better, and the battery level can be checked by voice prompt.

Unfortunately in actual use the Jabra's shortcomings became glaring rather quickly. First off, the tonal quality of the earpiece is notably inferior, lacking low frequency response in particular. The range when paired with my iPhone 6s was absolutely abysmal. While the Bose could easily manage ~20 feet through a wall, the Jabra would sometimes break up while carrying the phone in my front pants pocket. The lack of volume controls on the headset was disappointing, and the tacky flashing light when the headset is in use is just unnecessary.

After several days trying to get used to the Jabra, I gave up and started the return process. While the additional features are nice, the poor performance in the core requirements of audio quality and range far outweighed the benefit of the added functions. Amazon made the return quick and painless. For the time being I've obtained another (used) Bose BT2 in hopes that it will last long enough for someone to make a headset that can combine both the features of the Jabra and the performance of the Bose.

title: Great devices which deserve better documentation and friendlier default settings
text:
I'd give this 5 stars except for the documentation and some of the default settings. I bought two, and there was only a Quick Start Guide in the boxes, no manual at all. You can find a manual online here: http://www.engeniustech.com/resources/ENS202_Manual.pdf. This manual is fairly complete, but it is not particularly helpful unless you already know what you are doing. Many terms and concepts are used without explanation, and there is no overall configuration advice for different purposes. Luckily the EnGenius tech support guy was pretty helpful, so I was able to run with what he told me and get these working in a couple of hours. It wasn't hard once I got the details right, and so far they seem to be working great.

I just wanted to extend a network (i.e., to connect two wired networks in two locations and make them appear to be one network). I suspect this is probably the most typical use of these devices. It turns out the best way, according to their tech support, is to set them up as a WDS bridge. To save you some time, if that's all you want to do, here is the recipe:

First, the devices are not configured out of the box for DHCP, so you can't just plug them into your network and expect to talk to them. You need to wire them to your computer (of course you have to wire them via the PoE gadget to provide power) and then set your computer to have an IP address on the 192.168.1.xxx network. Then you can access the internal web server at 192.168.1.1 (user: admin, password:admin). This much is explained in the Quick Start Guide.

You need to give the devices IP addresses on your local network so you can access their internal websites later. Although their tech support recommended giving them fixed IP addresses, I preferred to have them use DHCP to dynamically assign addresses on my network, as the devices are not hard to find on your router if you need to log into them. The devices at both ends of the wireless link will each need to have their own IP address. You set this up in System > IP Settings. Then you click the Accept button at the bottom of the page, AND THEN CLICK Status > Save/Reload ON THE LEFT SIDEBAR. Not knowing I had to do the latter was enough to screw me up for awhile. Once you do this you can just plug them into your network, determine their IP addresses (if you didn't give them fixed ones) and log into their internal web servers to make further changes.

If you want to set it up as a WDS bridge, all you have to do is configure both devices as WDS Bridge and then provide each device with the other device's MAC address.

To set these up as a WDS bridge, under System > Operations Mode on each device's internal web server, click the WDS radio button, then the Bridge radio button within the WDS section. Then click the Save & Apply button.

To enter the paired device's MAC address (which you can read off from Status > Main on each one's web server) go to Wireless Settings > WDS Link Settings, change the selector on the first entry from Disable to Enable and enter the paired device's MAC address. Then click on the Accept button at the bottom of the page, and then click Status > Save/Reload on the sidebar. You don't need to add a security setting on this page because the wireless link between the devices is limited to the MAC addresses you provide.

Oh one other thing: the documentation doesn't seem to mention that the second ethernet connection on the device (not the one you hook up the PoE link to) can be wired to a computer or other network device. This saved me installing yet another hub or switch near where one of the antennas was to be located.

title: Typical of Canon products, well made and precise. ...
text:
Typical of Canon products, well made and precise. Focus hits well even at 1.4 and close range. Quick also. The IS in testing does indeed help. As cameras continue to add megapixels this should help as any little shake is more noticeable. The 77mm filter is also a common size which is helpful. Some say it lacks the "magic" of the 1.2. I only see that in portraits taken from a further distance where the 1.2 is smoother. Using both I'd say you'll get more keepers with this, but on "some" shots the 1.2 just has that it factor. Also if sharpness matters this is the one compared to the 1.2. With that said...., Becareful in portraits where too much sharpness can be had (Sigma, Ziess). It really depends on the subject, texture, makeup etc. So its hard to compare exactly having shot with the Sigma it does have a sharpness edge, but I don't shoot architecture so that didn't put it over the top. Because if the Sigma is a 10 on sharpness this is a 9. The 1.2 is a 7-7.5. (it's not too soft, its just not as sharp) Though, again sharpness can be overated in certain scenarios.

Update after a few months: I'm still a fan. It's still quiet and fast and provides enough keepers even at 1.4-1.6. The look is close to the 1.2 but not quite the same. But I'd still choose this because only those that have shot both might be the only ones to be able to see the difference. It's not the sharpest but it's sharp enough. There is some fringing depending on the backlighting so be aware of that if you're shooting that way. It's not terrible but it's a bit more than I'd hoped. The IS is the real deal, maybe the most effective IS on any lens I've used. Though that could partly be because IS on an 85 has less to deal with than IS on say a 200. Looking forward to how this continues to render as cameras seem to keep increasing the MP count. If I had a 1.2 I wouldn't upgrade unless you need the speed, because the fringing upgrades and sharpness aren't probably worth it. The reason to upgrade would be the keeper rate if you shoot quickly and are missing with the 1.2 AF. If I had a choice to buy either I would buy this. The 1.2 while somewhat magical in it's rendering (if one can work it properly) has optics that are aging and I'd worry about that as newer cameras may demand more recent glass. Not that some old lenses are still usable, but the 1.2 maybe not be one of them since it's already a bit finicky on todays cameras. But if you don't mind the extra work the 1.2 is a legend.

I'm very impressed with all the features, the performance and the build quality. Excellent value for the price, and I would highly recommend this model.

title: PERFECT performance on a 10-day trip through all parts of Peru
text:
LOVE this camera!! Debated between this and the A5100 prior to a 10-day trip through all parts of Peru (from Lima, Cusco, and Iquitos - temperate, high-altitute and cold, to jungle climates). Here are my key takeaways:

- The viewfinder is a MUST and provides a better representation of the photo or video you're actually taking.
- The LCD screen is great, but will be difficult to use if you're basing a shot (in manual mode) on what you're viewing. Plus the screen is difficult to view in sunlight
- The size is perfect! Another guy on our trip was shooting with a Nikon DSLR and he continually complimented the compact size and quality
- The intelligent settings are very impressive and make it easy to quickly capture images in varied settings - though manual mode was the primary mode I shot in.
- It is durable. I hesitated to use the camera in Iquitos because it's a jungle and relatively humid (though it was "winter" with less humidity than summer), but it performed excellent. Even with some light mist, it had no issue.
- The WiFi connectivity to my iPhone was a god-send! I was able to download pictures as we wanted them, but also loved the ability to remotely "shoot" from my phone. I also purchased a mobile tripod specifically for this which came in handy for family and friend pictures - no one left out!
- Only downside? The mic does not capture audio that well, assuming due to the compact body. Regardless, we opted to use "Voice Notes" to record audio on my iPhone, then sync with the video after uploading. Honestly worked great and most people have their phone. This is not enough of a "con" to discount a high rating - external audio seems to work best anyway.
- Lastly, the kit lens worked well for most needs on this trip. Granted, I'm new and learning, but I noticed I was not able to create the favored "depth effect" for portrait shots that a different lense will produce. But, the compact size was necessary for this trip. Nothing a different lense won't fix!

Overall, cannot recommend this camera enough! This is my first time purchasing and using an advanced camera. I was able to study a few YouTube video tutorials and practice a couple days prior to our trip. I am grateful for the precious moments this camera captured and I will be buying additional lenses!

PS; yes, I captured several beautiful shots of Machu Picchu on this camera. Many friends are asking for RAW JPGs to print out as posters.

title: Sweet
text:
I bought this as a replacement for a replacement of my old Sony Dream Machine Cube that I owned for 20+ years. It was sturdy, ergonomic, and it had a wonderful radio unit. The first replacement I bought was what now passes as a Sony cube (~$20 Amazon), made in China, which is a complete piece of garbage. Ignore the positive reviews as they have been written by people who never saw a real Sony in their life. It truly stinks: cheap plastic, sharp edges, shoddy construction, crappy radio receiver, etc. I must have been mad to think that anything of the old Sony quality was available at a similar price.

Actually the old Sony Cube design now sells upwards of $100 bucks. I night have sprung for it, but I wanted to check the competition first and see if I could save some dough. $100 for a clock-radio is nuts.

The Sangean turned out to provide excellent value for the money.($35 at the time of this writing.) The manufacturing is great---sturdy, tight chassis, excellent receiver, golden light with adjustable brightness, AM-FM with Seek or pre-sets, auxiliary and headphone jacks, nap timer, easy-to-read numbers, two alarms...

The radio sound doesn't have that low-end tinny clock-radio sound. Reminds me of the table radio I had in high-school. Not content to leave well enough alone, the government has made some new AM regulations that affect the Am band sound, but the attached antenna does a great job of hiding them. (You might have reception problems way out in the boonies; otherwise it should be fine.)

The curved edges make it comfortable to cuddle up to in bed, which is one thing I alway enjoyed about the Sony. I hate using headphones when I'm going to sleep.

title: This is a really good inverter. There is one major issue
text:
This is a really good inverter. There is one major issue. This inverter has a feed back problem. If the ground wire is not hooked up this thing will pump 15v of AC power back into the batteries. Because of this I believe this inverter was meant to be used in a house or stationary place. That way you could send that feedback voltage into the earth ground.

I found a way to fix this If you want to use this in a semi like what our install was. You MUST tie the negative and the ground together. Next use the frame for the negative connection. Do not hook the negative directly to a battery. It you do it will cause your check engine light to come on and it will cause your automatic transmission to not shift out of first.

text:

I have installed the beta of iOS 11 and many of the power features involve you swiping up from the bottom of the screen and from the side. But these edges are more difficult to reach because of the framing of the case. Keep in mind, the bezels on the iPad are reduced to give the maximum amount of screen space so there's not a lot to work with. To their credit, the manufacturer did make a small cutout at the center third of each of the top and bottom bezels (when viewed in landscape mode), so it's not like you can't swipe. It's just that it's much more of a hit or miss effort each time.

I'm keeping the case. I do like it. It does look professional and I do feel that the iPad is secure and protected from minor bumps. It's stands up very well in the case. But ultimately, if you're going to use the Pro features of your iPad Pro 10.5, the case is going to cause more issues as compared to a case that has a frame that stays as close to the edges of the iPad as possible.

title: Excellent Performance Switch that Replaced a Dell PowerConnect Switch
text:
Netis? Sorry. I've never heard of them. But after purchasing and installing their ST3124G 24-port 10/10/1000 Mbps switch as the core network switch in our home office hub, I am impressed. I used the Netis switch to replace an aging, but still functional Dell PowerConnect 2716 switch. While the specified per port throughput of the Dell is he same as the Netis (1 Gbps,) the performance is radically different.

True, I haven't run and performance measurements as of yet. However, access to my network services was immediately, noticeably faster.

True, the Netis is an unmanaged switch while the Dell PowerConnect is managed. However, I've had the Dell switch installed in the network hub for nearly five years now and I can't tell you the last time I managed it--if ever. I manage our RAID 10 file server regularly. I manage our central firewall often. But manage the core network switch? Never!

I've never heard of Netis before. But after installing and using their ST3124G 24-port 10/10/1000 Mbps switch, I can promise you that I will look for their network products in the future.

title: After a lot of arguing with AT&T about the data plan (AT&T and FiLIP had very poor communication about each other product/servic
text: When I first discovered the Filip I was ecstatic!!! I felt it was an answer to my prayers.  We purchased the Filip, May 3, 2014.  After a lot of arguing with AT&T about the data plan (AT&T and FiLIP had very poor communication about each other product/service).  For the first couple days it worked great.  My son wore it it to school and the battery was still 3/4 full by the time we picked him up.  About 2 days later, the FiLIP only lasted about 3-4 hours.  I called FiLIP support, they called AT&T, apparently I was right and AT&T was wrong about the data plan and after being on the phone for hours with both companies, we finally got the FiLIP on the stand alone data plan it should have been on.  They said that should fix the issue....?  The Filip still only lasted a couple hours, so the following Saturday (one week after we bought it) we took it back to the AT&T store and exchanged it for a new one.  This FiLIP worked correctly without a huge battery drain once.  That is when we went to  San Diego to attend Comic-Con.  WiFi & mobile network coverage in downtown San Diego (especially at the convention center) is boosted due to the enormous number of attendees & the need for online access.  What we realized is that his FiLIP was CONSTANTLY searching for service back home.  We have other AT&T mobile devices and have full bars when we are at home (we live off the I-5 corridor in a very between Tacoma & Seattle.  There isn't a lack of coverage.  The internal antenna on these devices are insufficient to live up to what the device is supposed to be capable of.  How can I keep track of my child if there's no service to the device?  FiLIP support refused to take any responsibility for their poorly made device and told me that since it worked in San Diego, then there's nothing wrong with the device.  It should have been replaced under their warranty conditions.  We finally gave in and purchased a Filip 2 device in December 2014.  Guess what, the antenna had improved...(but not a whole lot).  And the spacers that were supposed to come with the FiLIP weren't there, nor did they include information that you could get them free of charge if your device did not come with one or I would have ordered them post-haste!  Consequently, my son was running at school and it flew off his wrist and the screen cracked.  I agonized over our poor experiences with the FiLIP.  After airing my grievances with Customer Service they agreed to replace the glass free of charge, I just had to send the FiLIP via trackable method and fully insured.  I paid for 2-day express delivery with insurance.  I received confirmation that they received it and followed up with them 2 days later, just to be sure and to ask how long it would take.  They said to allow 10-14 business days, they would then send me a confirmation e-mail that my FiLIP has been repaired and the shipping/tracking information.  14 business days later I contacted FiLIP support requesting the status.  They said they were "backed up with service repairs" and it was taking longer than originally anticipated.  Two weeks later I called, and was told they had no update, no way to give me an ETA and to wait for the e-mail that it was ready to ship.  Two weeks later, I follow up again and tell them if they don't give me an ETA that I was going to file a complaint with the BBB.  They quickly responded that they were escalating my request and to give them 24-72 hours to respond.  Guess what??? 72 hours and then some went by and I heard NOTHING.  I contacted them AGAIN, and they asked me for the tracking number that was used to send in my FiLIP.  Of course I didn't have that handy and my home office was in the middle of re-organization, so it took me a few days.  Finally found it, sent it to them, and I finally got a phone call.  My FiLIP was shipped back in may and delivered to my home the day I left for vacation.  The customer service rep told me to check with "other household members"....SERIOUSLY???? It was obvious it was stolen, HOWEVER, they did not require signature for the delivery.  They did not insure the delivery (even though they REQUIRED me to insure my delivery to them).  NOR DID I EVER receive the e-mail that they were shipping it.  Had they done that I could have had a neighbor keep an eye out for the package since we were going to be out of town.  They said, sorry but we have confirmation it was delivered and have no responsibility to you, however they will "escalate my complaint and I should hear back in 24-72 hours".  DO NOT PURCHASE THIS POS.  We've purchased 2 now, (over 350, plus $13 and some change every month for a device that never worked right, and then again for a device that I never had.  Poor service!!! Last year, I promoted FiLIP at Comic-Con.  With guest services AND with Max Brooks (author of World War Z).  I will now make sure everyone knows what an AWFUL device and AWFUL company this is.

title: Too scared to use
text: I really like the design/concept and so I gave two stars instead of one. I was not comfortable using it and returned it, because the lens cover or filter comes within a hair of the lens or possibly touches. The lens protrudes to the edge of the adapter and seems flush with it, so I was too scared to even try putting on either the lens cover or filter. The filter looks like the glass would be even with the edge once screwed in and thus may touch the lens. And the lens cap is not concave and also would be flush with the adapter or worse, again likely touching the lens. The adapter is snug enough that if I don't push it all the way on, then the lens is save, but that's not exactly safe protection because light pressure would push the adapter in. What I really wanted this for is using the lens naked but having a good cover for it, and also purchasing high-quality brand-name 37 mm filters. The adapter is metal and looks very good quality, and also looks nice on the camera, so I'm really disappointed to have to send it back. It only needed to protrude about a mm more. 1 mm makes a huge difference between damage and no damage to lens. The other thing is, some users said it fits too loose but the fit was perfect for my Yi 4K. If it were tighter, I would be concerned with damaging the Yi while putting on/taking off. I hope this item gets a re-design because I really would like something just like this, except safer to use with the protruding Yi lens. Also, let us save money by not including the filter. I'd prefer to buy a known brand filter, and also ND and polarizing filters, skylight filters, etc.

title: AfterShokz Trekz Titanium Open Ear Wireless bluetooth headphones. One month rating.
text:
AfterShokz Trekz Titanium Open Ear Wireless blutoothheadphones...Owned since June '17. It's July. One month so far. Like them and would buy them again. I haven't tried other bone conducting products, and cant afford to try other products. Read other reviews to understand limitaitons and perks. I bought them with full understanding. It's what I wanted ultimately. I've never liked in ear/over ear headphones (neither the feel or loss of hearing surroundings) and figured why not try these. I'm still in the self concous stage of owning these because It feels out of place for me to wear any headphones, and for other people to see me with any at all. That and the cost. But I havent bought something for me for a while.
*like the fit
*like the wireless aspect (I really hate wired anything).
*like the open ear feature
*like "on time" from full charge
*like that they ar flexible, I dont worry I'll break 'em
*like the behind-the-head, over-the-ear way you wear them. I always hated dangly wires and hair-shuffling over-the-head headphones.
*liked that canwear glasses with them.
*like that it syncs with my galaxy note 4 without problem.
*the bluetooth range: can leave my note 4 on charger upstairs and go out to back yard and hear them just fine.YMMV. my chager is in my bedrrrom wich has a wall at back of house
*Like the rubbery feel. 'Stick' to me.
*like that I can adjust them slightly where the bone-condution part touches my head and still hear (volume adjustmet aside) my stuff.
*I can quickly pull them down around my neck and they are out of the way, and secure.

Dont like:
* not much yet. but they can get uncomfortable after a while of wear, but I have the same annoyance with any headphone/earbuds/etc.
* understand the soud limitaiton. They dont bother mey though, I was listening to my podcast and musid with the phoe speakers only for a long time. its an upgrade for me either way.
*I'd like to lean back on my pillow at times. These move a bit with that, but any behind-the-head style would do that. These are actually tolerant to some of that as they are bone conducting. Also, yesterday I lifted the back-around the head band an wore them like over-head headphones and they still sat in the right spot to listen.

That is it for now. Gotta go. If I think of more to add, and have time, I will later.

title: Not ready for prime time toy.
text:
The unit I got is defective, and being replaced, but overall the unit and support of this unit is not adequate.
Overall Kenwood support has been very poor. Dozens of calls to get functions working without resolution.
Only one person actually understood the unit enough to properly troubleshoot the unit - a gentleman by the name of "J.C'" who is some sort of Kenwood liaison between consumer products and whatever.
It really does not help that the authorized dealer/installer knows nothing and has not been trained on this unit enough to know what to order in the way of cables or how to update and troubleshoot the unit.

1. AM reception is nearly nonexistent on very strong signals in my area.
2. FM is barely better.
3. Firmware updates to Bluetooth will not apply, but the main update did apply.
This results in being unable to use the MDL function ( screen mirroring plus operation of your Android smartphone ) at all as the Bluetooth firmware has to be updated in order to function.
4. The unit is hardcoded for Verizon 4G dongles only - and precisely for one of the dongles only per their support. - this means that you cannot direct connect 4G and must use a wifi hotpsot from your carrier.
5. You must have internet access ( 4g/Wifi or you cannot automatically log into the unit and must use route collector to authorize the unit.
If not - you will be constantly presented with a log in screen ).
6. Email is glacially slow to log in and load - my smartphone on the same network is hundreds of times faster.
7. No SMS - e-mail, twitter and Facebook ??
8. The phone interface is minimal, and inaccurate - battery and signal strength do not match phone.
There is no call time and YOU CANNOT transmit touch tones during a call.
9. Itunes - scrolling on playlists is not automatic so what you are playing can be off the screen.
10. The screen smudges up like crazy and becomes unusable - you need a screen protector for a 2 thousand dollar radio.
11. You have to purchase the Sirius module separately - so it's an added expense.
12. You have to buy either the android or apple cable at time of install from Kenwood - Aftermarket will not charge your phone.

This unit is a bit of a joke and in hindsight not a really good value for the money.

title: Performance as advertised!!
text: I'm a recent cord cutter.  We are upgrading from a Terk amplified indoor antenna that we picked up at a local retailer.  We could only receive 4 stations with the Terk.  Antennaweb.org said we should receive 7 channels based on our location from the stations with a medium multi-directional antenna.  The Terk would not pickup our CBS affiliate.  Did some research on the web with the vast majority of sites recommending the Mohu Leaf.  Decided to make the small investment.  Received the Mohu Leaf 50 today.  Hooked it up and after a half-hour or so of testing the antenna in various positions, I found that I could pickup 8 stations with the Mohu, including my CBS affiliate.  Checked the signal strength on the TV for each channel and it showed they were all was maxed out. Amazing performance from this product.  I even took the Mohu downstairs to our basement family room, were the Terk couldn't pickup any channels at all.  Positioned it on our only western facing window and ran the channel scan.  BOOM!!! 6 out of the 8 channels that I got upstairs!  The only channels I couldn't get were the CBS stations but this was just a quick test and I didn't try the amplifier downstairs.  That may have made the difference. Just need a second Mohu for downstairs now!  Again, couldn't be happier with the performance of this product.

text:

For the last several years, I've run dual screens (laptop monitor, and one external monitor via mini-DP to VGA adapter). Since the laptop didn't have any other ports, and my old monitors didn't have HDMI input ports, I never had occasion to try dual externals (though I have read of MANY people with the same laptop and graphics card being able to do so).

I recently got a pair of new monitors with HDMI input ports and tried to hook them up. Unfortunately, the HDMI output on the card didn't work. Researching online told me that several people with my configuration ran into this problem when they upgraded to Win 10. I don't know if that's what happened to me, or not.

What I do know is that when I bought and hooked up this external graphics interface, I can now run both external monitors. In fact, I can now run three monitors at once! The Wavlink arrived promptly, was packaged well, and was simple to hook up (simple plug & play for Win 10). For the price, this thing is a bargain.

title: BELIEVE THE HYPE!
text:
I was seriously considering Samsung's JS9500, but i've seen so many reviews about the OLED being the best looking television ever, i HAD to reconsider.
BOY am i glad i did.
I can tell you without a doubt, the hype is legit. Most content looks BETTER, with only the worst SD material losing sharpness. This was very important in justifying this purchase, since there is very little 4K or HDR content. The upscaling is better than i expected, especially with anything in 1080i or better. You can see what definition certain content is being broadcast in by clicking on the remote.
I have YET to see ANYTHING above 1080i, but i'm very impressed with how close a 1080i will come to looking like 4K when watching certain channels like the Food Network. I have YET to try anything on my Blu Ray player, but i expect it to look even better since that will be true 1080P.

Streamed 4k is fantastic, and if you actually watch a program that is 4K AND HDR, like Mozart in the Jungle, you WILL experience the holy grail.
Watching television has become exciting, as i can truly say my viewing experience has been improved dramatically.

Of course, it is NOT perfect. I haven't experienced any of the "vignetting" or color distortion some people have complained about, but i would simply chalk that up to quality control issues that come with any product. What i HAVE experienced is a pixelated blur that happens during quick motion scenes. I don't always notice it, but when i do, it's a bit annoying. I don't know what it's called, but the picture breaks up into fuzzy blocks as if there is broadcast interference.
I'm not a tech guru, and i haven't had the set calibrated. I have everything set to Standard, as the other setting are way too punchy in color.
The picture quality is the best i've ever seen, and when watching HDR content, the outdoor daylight scenes are so vibrant, it's as if you are watching through an open window.
My only other gripe is that i could have saved $1K if i had simply waited a couple of weeks. Anyway, at least more people will be able to afford this incredible piece of technology. Trust me, once you experience this television for a week, you'll NEVER think about LCD again.

title: I bought this for my new Canon 80D, but ...
text:
I bought this for my new Canon 80D, but beware.

The "Vivitar BG-E14 Battery Grip for Canon EOS 70D DSLR Camera" DOES NOT work properly with the Canon 80D, although the battery grips are sold as interchangeable between the two.

It will neither recognize Canon nor non-Canon batteries. Once installed the touch screen will prompt you to verify the authenticity of the installed batteries.

If you say yes they are Canon batteries, the camera will shut off stating that they are knock-offs. If you go ahead and state they are not Canon, they will not be recognized and the 80D will NOT see them, thus never knowing how much of a charge there is nor how much of a charge is left.

I have a 70D after-market battery grip and swapped them and the new "Vivitar BG-E14 Battery Grip for Canon EOS 70D DSLR Camera" works on the 70D and the battery grip I had on the 70D DOES work properly on the 80D.

I would observe that the software/firmware in some respects is woefully behind the Windows 10 era, an operating system that was released to the public over a year ago and to developers way before that. As a result, I have returned the camera to Amazon.

I must also observe that the Internet support of Foscam cameras in general, via your new direct sales approach, was not ready for “prime time” when Foscam broke relations with its previous sole US distributer, Foscam USA, that did have good tech support. Although, when called (the site had no internet service at the time) Foscam International’s underlying tech support personnel offered two solutions to the problem I was having: 1)use Firefox direct; and, 2)update the firmware, neither worked. While connected to my router through a NIC, direct communications with the camera with any browser option was not possible; therefore, the second solution was also impossible since one needs to use the camera’s setup app to reprogram the firmware. title: UPDATED REVIEW>  Inadequate power protection resulting in dead camera.
text:
What a piece of junk. I received this on January 4th, but didn't get around to installing it until February 13th. I went to pull up video on it today and found it wasn't working. Checked the microSD and found that the dashcam stopped working on the 15th.

All videos from the 13th are missing, though there are sporadic ".info" files from 14:13:24 to 14:33:35. I assume this is due to space management on the SD card, though I would expect the ".info" files to be removed along with the ".MP4" files. There are no files for the remainder of the 13th or at all for the 14th. This could again be space management on the SD card, though if that is the case where are the ".info" files that were previously left on the card?

The next signs of activity begin on the 15th at 08:53:01 with a video showing the next ten minutes of my car sitting in the driveway. Similar videos follow until the one that starts at 09:33:01. During this ten minute window my wife and I got in the car and when I fired the car up you hear a voice say "Power supply is disconnected." At the time I did not catch what was said or where it had come from, but now realize it was the dashcam. Since the dashcam shows no signs of life regardless what power supply I now connect it to I can only conclude that there was a surge in the electrical system while starting the car that their power supply failed to handle and the charging circuit has died. The camera then ran on its battery until exhausted at which point the camera powered down never to function again.

UPDATED: We worked with Roav who replaced the first dashcam-they are a pleasant company to work with and did their best to satisfy us however this week we found that the replacement dashcam failed because the battery had swelled. Given that this was a Li-on swelling is a serious issue. Li-on batteries are in danger of shorting and catching fire the camera represents a significant fire hazard and is unsuitable for its designated usage. Infact we had been chasing down an issue with our car dealership because we kept going out and having a dead car battery, they were unable to find an issue with the car. We now are pretty sure the problem was the dashcam since we have not had a problem since removing the camera.

title: Works better than I had imagined
text:
Incredibly happy with this purchase. Over the years I've been depending on WiFi and struggling with range and speed issues, always frustrated at not being able to get close to a wired solution. I have a 150mbps Internet package from Comcast, but with an 802.11ac 1200 wireless router from Belkin combined with an AC wifi adapter on my PC, I would often only get in the 25-50mbps range. Most recently I've been having troubles where my wireless adapter wasn't connecting on the 5GHz band.

I had been getting ready to invest in a new AC router and an AC wireless PCI card in hopes that would work better, but then these came up in a Gold Box deal and I decided it was worth a shot. In the past I've generally been skeptical of how well PowerLine networking could work (and have lived in pretty old houses where I assumed the power outlet wiring wouldn't allow for great speeds).

I'm glad I waited until this AV1200 kit came out to give this technology a shot, because I was absolutely blown away by it. I have it hooked up to the gigabit ethernet port on my otherwise mediocre Belkin wireless router, and have the other powerline adapter hooked up to my PC in a room on the other side of the house. The setup was dead simple (literally plug them both in and press the pairing button on one and then go to the other room and press the other pairing button. And the speeds were just amazing - I'm actually getting better speeds that even what my Internet package advertises (in the 165-170Mbps range, on a 150Mbps package). And dramatically better speeds and responsiveness from what I was getting on WiFi.

The value of this tech seems incredible, and I would say it's almost definitely worth giving it a shot. To have these kinds of speeds without having to wire my house for Ethernet feels like a miracle.

title: Straightforward and useful in certain situations
text:
I had an old SATA/IDE to USB 2 adapter, which does similar things to this unit. But there the comparision ends. The state of the art has greatly improved.

What do you do with this thing? You use it to access old (or new) internal SATA drives (whether spinning or SSD) without needing to install them a bay in your computer. Of course, it's not quite the same thing; the access is through a USB 3 port. It's plenty fast but obviously not native speed.

Using it is really easy. Plug in the power supply (a typical wall wart), plug in the USB cable at both ends, and then insert your hard drive. Only then, press the power button. (The instructions aren't clear about whether a hot swap is safe; I would recommend you avoid it.) Now your drive is accessible. It was truly plug and play on my Linux system and the same should be true with various Windows releases.

As mentioned above, transfer speed is fine, if not native, on USB 3. (Much slower on USB 2, of course.) My main use case is this: I replaced old SATA drives in a couple of laptops with SSDs, but sometimes I want to go back to some of the content on the old drives. With this device it's as easy as can be.

Another use case is cloning or transferring from an existing internal drive to another. You just plug the target drive into the gadget and off you go. I've done this when doing disk replacements or upgrades.

You can also possibly use it to try to rescue an old disk. The advantage is that you don't have to boot with the disk inside the machine. You can try to use the dock to mount it externally. Sometimes this works and you can quickly pull off critical files. (Alas, it doesn't always work.)

If you want the bay to be part of your installation more or less permanently, you won't lose a USB ports because there are three additional ports on the bay itself. Whoever has too many USB ports and can't use more, raise your hand.

The only thing is that if you have old old IDE drives, you can't use this (I actually do, so I'm keeping my old old adapter unit). However, the new Sabrent dock is trivially easy to use and very useful in certain situations.

title: Works well for charging Nexus 5X!  Some notes on "fast charging", superb customer service!
text:
***UPDATE - 12/7/15***
This is a late update, but I did get a chance to compare between the old and the new cables received couple weeks ago. They definitely fixed the problem as it was noticeable when I tested with a portable Anker battery and using a current measuring app on the phone (not the most accurate but I use it as to make reference measurements), the new cables did not pull max. current from the battery like the old cables did. This indicates that they did change the Rp resistor to a corrected value to ensure overcurrent conditions will not occur on the charger and cause any adverse effects, as commented in previous updates. Additionally, the same reviewer I mentioned who found non-compliant issues with a different Cable Matters cable also commented on this USB-C to USB-A cable and have also tested (with data) and confirmed that the newer cables have been corrected and fixed according to USB-C standards rev. 1.1. So for future buyers as of now who wants to charge their Nexus 5X, I highly recommend this cable!

***UPDATE - 11/19/15***
I contacted Cable Matters and have discussed the issues with the cables not being compliant to the USB-C 1.1 specification. They are aware of this issue and have since fixed the problem to meet and comply to the specification. In addition, they are sending me new replacement cables that are compliant to the specifications, all without charge! I give their customer service 5* for being prompt to fix an issue addressed, and for offering free replacement! I will definitely buy from them again!

I will update again once I get the new replacement cables to test and compare with the old.

***UPDATE - 11/10/15***
I've been reading some newer reviews and I wanted to point out some precautions if you plan to purchase these cables for charging Nexus 5X or 6P.
One reviewer (credited as a SW engineer on the Google Pixel team, review here: http://www.amazon.com/review/R3KIQ4LI5PC5JH/ref=cm_cr_rdp_perm) have pointed out that the USB3.1 Type C to Type A version of the cable by Cable Matters is not compliant to USB Type C release v1.1 and may cause damage to your charge sources (i.e. chargers, PC, hubs, etc..)
Now, I don't know if this issue also effects the USB2.0 Type C to Type A version of the cable, but I would recommend taking precautions and understanding the problem first before making a purchase, which I will remark here.

The issue that was pointed out is the fact that Cable Matters cable (USB3.1 Type C to A) did not use the correct pull-up resistor. Those of you interested in reading up the technical details, you can find the full specifications here: http://www.usb.org/developers/usbtypec/
under section 4.11. Cable Matters used 10kohm resistor, which is rated for 3.0A @ 5V, when they should really be using 56kohm for legacy connectors such as Type A or micro B (see Table 4-13 in the Type C specifications release 1.1 document). What this means is the cable will "allow" max. 3A draw from its sources. Since the other end of the cable is Type A--which is not rated for 3A--there may be potential problems if the charging sources are not also rated for 3A output (i.e. wall charger, car charger, PC USB port, USB hubs) and/or they do not have overcurrent or overcharge protection. Most, if not all, Type A chargers are rated anywhere between 500 mA to 2.4A. If the cable "allows" for 3A current to flow, it can damage the internal circuitry of those sources when connecting to a USB-C device that has the capability of sinking 3A (i.e. Chromebook Pixel, Nexus 5X,6P..etc.).

Personally, I have been using Cable Matters USB 2.0 Type C to Type A cables for well over a week using Anker 40W desktop 5-port (2.4A max. rated per USB port) charger, Monoprice 2.1A/5V wall charger, and a Dell Optiplex PC USB port for charging my Nexus 5X. So far I have not seen any issues. The Anker does have PowerIQ and safety mechanisms built-in, so it might help prevent damage if too much current is drawn. I am not sure about the hardware circuits inside the Monoprice or my Dell PC. However, I would advise anyone buying these cables to beware what chargers you have and note that it may cause damage.

***Original review***
I bought a few of these cables (3ft) specifically for charging a Nexus 5X. They work just as expected for charging. I would like to emphasize that these cables that I bought are USB-C to USB-A (USB2.0 speed), not USB 3.0 or USB 3.1. That means, if you want to transfer data, it is still limited to max. USB2.0 speeds (480Mbits/s). Besides, the Nexus 5X currently does not support USB3.1 speeds for file transferring.

These cables seem pretty well made. It's light weight and flexible. The white strain relief on both ends are made of hard plastic. The connectors on each end are not bulky.

Here are a couple things I also want to point out since some reviewers and users have asked or talked about "fast charging".
- In order to truly get the "fast charging" speed that's advertised by Google for Nexus 5X, you need to be using a USB-C to USB-C cable (Cable Matters also offer this as one of the options for about $1 more currently), not a USB-C to USB-A cable. The USB-C to USB-C cables are what support higher current exceeding beyond 2A.
- Additionally, to get the fast charge, the charger (AC adapter) must be rated for higher current output (i.e. the included charger/adapter with Nexus 5X is rated 5V, 3A = 15W)
- When charging the Nexus 5X, it will show "charging rapidly" in the lock screen when you have a high current charger, but this does not necessarily mean it's "fast charging". You can use a 2.1A charger and still see "charging rapidly" displayed on screen. But fast charging means the device can draw more current, beyond what normal USB-A buses are rated for.

So, to clarify "fast charging" is with USB-C to USB-C cables, which means you must use a charger/adapter that either has a USB-C output connector or is integrated into the adapter with a USB-C cable end. The charger must also be rated for higher current output (i.e. 3A or higher).

Now, this is not to say these cables can't charge the Nexus 5X quickly. In fact, if you have a higher current charger it can still charge very quickly, but will be a bit slower than if you used the USB-C charger that comes with the phone.

I use these cables with the Anker 40W desktop charger rated for 2.4A max per USB port, see here:
http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00GTGETFG?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o07_s00
With this, I can charge from 30% to 100% within close to an hour. I would say that within 15 minutes I can get 15-18% charge approximately (based on phone's default battery capacity indicator, with screen off and some apps running in background while idle), which is still relatively fast, and almost as fast as if I used the included charger/adapter to charge. Overall I would highly recommend getting a couple of these cables for charging if you have a USB-C phone (i.e. Nexus 5X, Nexus 6P, Oneplus Two).

If you do not have one, they sell micro usb to dc power adapters for very cheap. Then you have Bluetooth for your care for very cheap.

Summary – This was very easy to setup. I plugged the cables in and simply looked for mediabridge5 in my Bluetooth devices. No code was needed and pairing was no issue. title: Does Much More Than I Expected!
text:
Currently, I'm a researcher at a large university. Prior to purchasing the printer, I thought my needs would mainly consist of printing out 20-page academic reports (100+ per year) and creating drafts for publishing and materials for teaching. But I was wrong. More on that below! Also, to be clear, I've often been an early technology adopter (having worked with printers since the early 1980s and owned/troubleshot, both personally and professionally, since 1994). I will also come back to update this periodically if anything changes.

Replacing: Epson WF 3620 (Epson began dying a slow, painful, and costly death the same month its 1-yr warranty expired) - never again to Epson!!

I've separated this review into 4 sections: my expectations; unexpected surprise; exceeding expectations; and failing expectations.

My Expectations:
Based upon other reviewers, I became anxious about: the setup time, connectivity, color quality, and print speed. The setup time turned out to be negligible to me and met my previous setup standards. Just in case it was bad, I had the TV going in the background. I did also winced for a moment when it came to installing their somewhat alien-looking ink cartridges; and I took a deep breath when trying to connect to the internet (especially given the weird-to-me touch screen they use and the reviews that I read). But it all worked fine! In fact, I've had ZERO issues with the connectivity thus far, including using AirPrint from my iPhone (knock on wood). The slower print speed was there, but it hasn't been *too* noticeable (having already printed a few 20-page academic articles). The color quality is definitely not as crisp as the Epson (probably more comparable to an HP; Canon - 2-3x more expensive - is hard to beat there). But I also wasn't expecting to do a lot of photos or amazingly brilliant graphics with the Brother. I needed it to print: consistently and reliably! I calculate that the long term cost savings in ink ($100-$300+ per year) and the cheaper unit price relative to the higher-end models ($200+) will more than offset any *hypothetical* trips to FedEx for which I might need the higher quality vs. using a competitor's model.

Unexpected Surprise!
If you're like me, you've probably come to hate your smart phone. We use that thing for EVERYTHING!!!! Well, the biggest unexpected surprise, is that this printer can handle emailing and scanning documents to your computer or cloud account as good as, IF NOT BETTER!, than our smart phones (and I'm an iPhone user). Setting up the "Scan to Searchable PDF" and my email was easy. Previous printers would separate each page into separate attachments, but this one already knew (surprise, surprise) that I wanted it to be one file, and the quality was quite high. Among other features that I can't wait to start trying, it has Scan to Mobile, Scan to PowerPoint, Scan to Excel, and Scan to Word. In my previous department, the Scan to PDF feature (on a professional $5,000 printer!) could easily take an hour from "scan to format/edit to local save." This model scanned the document, sent it securely to my email inbox, and to where I was able to download and save it in less than 5 minutes! (Giving me the time and necessary excitement to write this review! - who gets that motivated to write these anyway?!?)

Exceeding Expectations:
Not that it should matter, but I expected a "value product" to be hard on the eyes (especially given some of the other reviews). Again, I was pleasantly surprised that it looks as sleek and contemporary as it does. Its not as bulky as the EPSON that I had, and I would add that it even makes my office space look more professional.

Failing Expectations:
None so far. Even the connectivity issues that others have talked about haven't happened for me thus far (and I make use of antivirus and double authentication). But don't worry; I'll definitely be back to take off stars if/when an issue arises.

Overall, I estimate that this machine has already saved me more than 10 hours of the ongoing headache I was having with the Epson that I'm about to chuck into the garbage (along with all the new $ ink I had purchased for it!) and never look back. That piece of mind is really priceless.

Called Amazon on 4/13 to ask why I received a refurbished model instead of a new one as it was only just over a month old. Here was their response:

Initial rep - can't help, will send you to the Kindle dept.
Kindle Dept. rep - not my area, will send you to Kindle Tech.
Kindle Tech dept. rep - It's new for the following reasons:
1. It's new.
2. It was never activated
3. It was never connected to WiFi
4. It is in a brown box (not a retail box) because it was returned.
5. It was a pre-order from the holiday season that was returned.
6. It was in a retail box but needed to be put in a refurbished box because the original box was damaged.
7. If the charger doesn't work, call us back and we'll send you a new one (it probably got damaged in shipping).
8. Open the box (FYI, I haven't opened it yet because I anticipated sending it back), start it up and let it download your content and you'll see that it is new.

Is it Amazon's policy to send refurbished items as replacements for a device that was owned for just over a month? Because that was never the answer I got. If it is, fine. I don't think that's right in this case, but if that's the policy, it's the policy.

title: Replacement Windshield Mount for Garmin Driveluxe 50LMTHD that works well
text:
I bought this as a backup mount for a Garmin Drive Luxe 50LMTHD. The mount is the same one that comes with the GPS device and it has the same magnetic mount.

The vehicle mount is in two parts. The curved magnetic-catch piece into which the GPS fits and the suction cup windshield mount. The suction cup windshield mount is the same part used with previous Garmin GPS units.

I use this adapter primarily when in another vehicle such as a rental car. In other vehicles I connect the magnetic-catch piece that holds the GPS to either the [[ASIN:B0035JL4V2 Garmin Friction Mount]] or the [[ASIN:B002OL2MU4 Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging]].

A power adapter note: This mount and the 50LMTHD use the same mini USB as in past Garmin units such as the 3790. BUT: Older power adapters will not power the 50LMTHD traffic function. Even though Garmin says the traffic antenna is built into the 50LMTHD you still need a new power adapter such as [[ASIN:B0086CTL5Y Garmin 10-24V - 2amp Vehicle Power Cable]] for the traffic to work.

title: The easiest kit ever!
text:
Time from box to picking up airplanes: Less than an hour.

Good:
- Easy to assemble. It helps to have some thin needle-nosed pliers and some tiny screwdrivers, but, in a pinch, you could assemble it with a pocket knife. Everything fits and is secure.
- Works well and worked the first time. That's always a treat!
- Tested with ForeFlight and FlyQ EFB.
- The status web page is very nice and helpful.
- With the SDR chips in the bottom slots, the USB connector of the GPS can be inserted and removed through the slot in the case. Nice when you don't need the GPS (e.g. if the iPad already has a GPS and a good signal).

Bad:
(Not really bad, but not as good as above)
- The fan is delicate and the blades are easily damaged--be careful when mounting it to the case.
- The status web page's choice of light grey and blue text on a white background is hard to read on the iPad. A higher-contrast style would be easier to read.
- The box emits some RF noise that I've picked up on a couple of receivers. Not a problem in the flight test, but I had the box in the back seat, away from the instrument panel radios and antennas.

Adaptations and observations:
(things I changed/adapted to make it work better for me)
- The only way to turn it off is to pull the micro-USB power connector. I used the short USB-A to micro USB cable that came with the battery rather than the battery's power cable to leave the micro USB connected and then pull the USB connector from the batter to avoid damaging the connector on the board.
- I added Velcro to the bottom if the case and the top of the battery to keep them together. Works well.
- The antennas like to unscrew themselves so I plan to put a rubber bushing around the connector to apply some friction to the screw terminal of the antenna and make it more resistant to unscrewing.
- Added Velcro to the GPS puck and some Velcro patches to the case to keep the puck attached when not in use.
- The flat battery (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00ZWUZG70/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o01_s02?ie=UTF8&psc=1) provides just over 4-hours of operation with the GPS puck attached and the fan running.
- I bought a high-speed SD chip (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00M55C0VU/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1) to use for the code and downloaded the image from the stratux web site. This saves a little money and I've found that the Raspberry PI runs a little better with faster chips (even though the pre-loaded chip is probably fine).
- The WiFi from the Raspberry PI-3 is pretty powerful--I wonder if some battery life could be gained by reducing the WiFi's signal. In a plane, it only has to go about 5-feet (tops). As it is, it covers my entire apartment. (Maybe I just need a bigger plane?)

title: Not bad, if you're willing to work a little bit
text:
I have used the Sony A6000 camera with all lenses mentioned here. I should first say that my copy of the 55-210mm has a de-centering problem, meaning the left side of the image is sharper than the right side. My comments on sharpness are based on getting acceptable results from the weaker side.
Good things here are light weight, reasonable size, image stabilization and low cost.
I first compared this lens to the Sony FE 28-70mm full-frame lens at the focal lengths where they overlap. I was surprised to see the 55-210mm images were just as good at 55mm and better at 70mm when examining the whole frame. Next I compared this lens to an old Minolta full-frame zoom that gives very good images. At 100mm, surprise again, no image difference between lenses. Above 100mm, however, things start to fall apart for the 55-210mm. At 135mm and 150mm, you can get acceptable edge sharpness out of this lens but you have to stop down hard, ie - f/11 or smaller. At 200mm, forget it, there is no aperture where the image is sharp.
Considering, that is not bad performance for a cheap 'kit' lens, if you're willing to work a little bit in order to use small apertures.

title: You get what you pay for
text:
Pros: The cameras are packaged well. They appear to be of good quality/construction. The video quality is much better than I expected, considering they are only $99. Night vision works well, again, much better than expected. I didn't have any issues pairing the cameras with my home WiFi network.

Cons: Detecting motion is very hit and miss. There have been times where I have walked directly in front of a camera and despite jumping up and down and waving my arms, I got zero notifications of motion activity, however, I will sometimes get a notification at 2 am because a small fly went by the camera. Recording: This is a big one. You CANNOT use any 3rd party software with these cameras. iSpy, BlueIris, ZoneMonitor, etc. You CANNOT use a 3rd party DVR/NVR. You CANNOT use any other hardware/software to intercept recordings for storing on a local PC, NAS device, Raspberry PI, etc. These cameras use proprietary firmware and networking protocols and you are forced to use only Zmodo applications/software. Based on other asked questions/reviews, Zmodo has been promising a working Cloud service since 2016 and it's still not in operation. The cameras will only record a burst of 5 photos when it detects motion. IT DOES NOT RECORD VIDEO. If you are fast enough, you will have to open the app as soon as you get a motion notification, and manually click the Record/Take photo button. There have been times where I get a delayed notification and by the time I open the app and click live view, the person/car is already gone or, sometimes I will walk through my front door and by the time it starts to record the burst of photos, it only records the door open and you have no idea who opened it. Despite the cameras being weather/water proof, the power supply included is not (not sure why they would do this), if you decide to mount these cameras outdoors like I did, you will need to purchase heat shrink tubing and electrical tape to make them as weatherproof as possible and/or purchase weatherproof extension cord covers from Home Depot or Lowe's. Sometimes the Zmodo Android App crashes during live viewing. The app could use some more tweaking and some more features.

Final Thoughts: If you want cheap cameras that provide good video, these are a good buy. I'm actually thinking about buying a few more. If you want more robust features such as a local NVR/DVR, 3rd party hardware/software support, look elsewhere.

UPDATE: My wife and I got home around the same time in two separate cars, none of the 3 cameras on the front of my house detected any motion. I think I'm going to return them.

title: A fair warning the Sony label has been "faked" in the past
text:
I had 2 failures out of 4 and decided to research. extensively......found out that the Sony label may be misleading

Here is the info from digitalfaq sponsored by VEEROTECH (a hosting site)

Discs with fake IDs (or outright counterfeits) are an annoyance to media buyers worldwide. Most fake media comes from China (and former Hong Kong), as a general rule. Fake media tends to float around Europe and Asia more than it does the USA. Fake media is normally sold in street markets, on eBay and online. Major brand name media sold in stores is probably never going to be fake.

Read more: http://www.digitalfaq.com/reviews/dvd-media.htm#ixzz3rfjpVtkc

If you go to this sight you will find very useful information on the history of blank media cd's. It will be well worth your time if you are interested in finding some more reliable media. It covers pretty much all makers, but is a bit dated. (2011). So because it is not up to date there may have been changes since. Rest assured once items get "brokered" to the lowest bidder quality gets second billing. So far the only company that has not outsourced their product is Taiyo Yuden which still is manufactured in Japan.

I thought of buying Shure SRH1540 for this thanksgiving(November 2015) but the price of Sennheiser tempted me to buy this (When I added this in my wish list it was $199 but i got this for $94.99).

AT is a closed back headphone and Sennheiser is an open back headphone. So obviously Sennheiser will leak sound. It is not suitable for listening in bed with someone next to you. AT come with three cable where as Sennheiser come with only 2 cables.

In lot of reviews I see people complaining about the chord which comes along with Sennheiser. Sennheiser has already addressed this issue. Now it comes with 2 chords. 1 shorter 1.2m chord and 3m chord. Shorter cable comes with 3.5 mm plug and 3m chord comes with 1/4 inch plug along with a 1/4 inch stereo jack to 3.5mm stereo adapter (I still like AT's
3.5mm Stereo Jack to 1/4" Stereo Plug Adapter)

Sennheiser doesn't come with a pouch but AT comes with a faux leather pouch. But it is not a big issue for me. I never used faux leather pouches. I prefer hard case.

Sennheiser HD 558

Build Quality + Durability ... = 6/10 (Ear cups won't rotate. I usually keep my AT ear cups flat while having it on my shoulder. It looks plasticy)
Comfort ............................ = 8/10 (Comfortable when compared to AT. For me Boss headphones are more comfortable than both the headphones)
Bass ............................... = 7/10 (Neutral. Not as strong as AT)
Overall Audio Quality ........ = 7/10 (Sounds better than my Koss PortaPro. They sound neutral. In layman's term it sounds as if Tremble was set to 55 and Bass 45)

Total: 28/40

Audio Technica ATH-M50x

Build Quality + Durability ... = 9/10 (Ear cups rotate. They rest nicely in my shoulder. They look sturdy and durable. Comes with 3 cable)
Comfort ............................ = 5/10 (They are not at all comfortable for me. My ears will start paining after 30 mins of listening)
Bass ............................... = 8/10 (Bass is little pronounced when compared to Sennheiser)
Overall Audio Quality ........ = 6/10 (They sound very dull and dry to my ears. In layman's term it sounds as if Tremble was set to 40 and Bass 60)

Total: 28/40

Verdict:

If comfort and superior sound quality is your main concern then go for Sennheiser.
If you can live with decent sound quality, superb build quality, little pronounced bass and can adjust strong clamping then go for AT.

Decide based on the type of genre you listen. If you listen bass heavy songs then AT is the best option. But if you are looking for over all good audio quality then go for Sennheiser.

Note: The price is fluctuating every day (Ranging from $94.99 - $249). I got mine for $94.99 (Special Edition). So closely watch the price for a weeks time before ordering.

I saw few reviews complaining about the authenticity of the special edition headphones ordered during thanksgiving (2005). But I was able to successfully verify authenticity.

title: Awesome sound and bass for the price. Sounds like its worth a lot more.
text: Sounds better than any other boombox I've ever used. The woofer in the center can put out some fancy window vibrating bass and sounds amazing. I use it regularly with my Sony Xperia z3v smartphone (huge Sony fan). The only con I've noticed is that this stereo system can make some annoying rattling noise due to the main woofer at higher volumes. The rattling can be especially noticeable when batteries are installed. Though, I recently caked the inside of the battery compartment with soft velcro to muffle the vibrations and it has helped a ton when I play the boombox with batteries. Oh, and I'd recommend using 8 rechargeable D batteries so you don't spend a fortune replacing them. My system worked fine with 1.2v 5000 mAh NiCd Sunlabz batteries and actually seemed to last longer than regular alkaline ones. And on the reviews that say this thing isn't very loud, it can be. Maxing out the volume on both your phone and the boombox can still leave you wanting more in large rooms but I attached my headphone amp to the thing and it boosted the volume by a long way making me think it's just the input that's the problem. Then again, this system might not me made to take in that much power through the aux port so I'm just hoping I doesn't blow anything. Back to the sound, it still had a good amount of bass without using the bass booster. With the bass booster and lights on, you can see the main woofer vibrating a lot even at lower volumes. The red lights make the vibrating woofer look awesome when you stand back. I get a ton of comments on the thing whenever someone comes over as well. I say comments and not compliments cause it seems around 2/3 of the crowd thinks it looks wicked awesome and the other 1/3 is more like, "meh, weird bug looking stereo." Atleast they all said it sounds great. Overall, I think it is well worth the money and hope it serves us well for the next few years.

title: Astounding camcorder with excellent still photo capabilities
text:
An astonishing example of technology like nothing I've ever seen before.

It's been forty years (!) since I first saw a video camera in high school, a big b/w camera with a backpack that contained the batteries and internals. It was impressive! Then we used a kind of mini-VHS video recorder to share kid videos with our parents maybe 15-20 years ago. Then I got an iPhone which had kind-of video capabilities. So I guess I was ripe to be blown away by this Sony FRAX53/B.

It's small and compact, like a small football. The swing-out screen is breathtakingly crisp and the internal operating system and menus are not only in color, but accompanied by clear, bright sound! I charged the battery and took a video of one of my cats. I could not believe the clarity of the image when I viewed it on the screen! The video is of such high quality that it's easy to overlook the still camera, which is remarkable. High-resolution, bright images. The "Photo" button is kind of oddly placed, it's not easy to operate it while you're holding the device with its right-side hand strap. You can also use a "Manual" mode and twist the lens to achieve custom focus. There's a 20X optical magnification which ought to satisfy anyone.

The Sony software is thorough and functional. The camcorder will transfer photos and video wirelessly if you have a fairly modern computer. I had to use a PC laptop rather than my elderly Mac. That meant using Windows 10, which led to some baffling moments trying to figure out if anything was working.

Between the Sony software and the camcorder and our WiFi setup and Windows 10 I found that the best thing to do sometimes was just WAIT. Windows would give me bad information and I would misinterpret that as an error. Ignore what Windows is telling you and be patient while the FDRAX53/B does its work.

The printed manual is basic and you'll want to spend time reviewing the online documentation. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the Sony FDRAX53/B and a "U-Stream" service to get a live stream going. There is a LOT of technology packed into this camcorder! Expect to spend some time reviewing it all. As I mentioned, Sony packed a TON of features in this device, and there's a learning curve to really understand and appreciate them all.

If you're planning a vacation or expecting a newborn child, BUY THIS CAMCORDER! You cannot take enough videos and photos of your kids when they're young, and the same goes for vacations -- this camcorder is small enough to tote with you (it does not like fog or water, though!) and the QUALITY of the images are incredible! It's not so heavy that it's going to be a burden.

The sound is very good, and there's a "gun" style microphone if you want to A) avoid wind noise B) capture audio of what you're shooting (like at a kid's soccer game) rather than local chitchat.

One thing that occurred to me while I was fiddling with the camcorder in my right hand, that being that if you were holding one of your kids in your left hand and the camcorder in your right hand and they both began to slip... which would you grab? This camcorder is THAT nice. Between the quality of the camcorder and its fantastic lens and the Sony software for image management and manipulation, this could be a major hobby in and of itself. You can easily edit, trim and combine videos with sound and add captions and text. For a consumer level product, the video and image editing suite is quite impressive. You will want a fairly modern computer, as I mentioned.

Something I come back to again and again as I figure the FDRAX53/B out is the absolute wonder of it. The small size, the quality of images, the ease of operation -- I just can't get over it. Beyond sensational and well into the realm of magical. I've never seen anything like the FDRAX53/B before.

title: NUPGRADE = EPIC FAIL!
text:
UPDATE: Sept 2017

Apparently I was a bit too hasty in posting my original review for the KDLINKS HD720. I believe a product should last longer than the overall very minimal use that this player received. It still has that “new” product
smell and the protective plastic is still adhered to the top. In all honesty, although I have owned this player for 2 years, the player itself maybe has had 36 hours total playtime. I was overly anxious to review a media player that could read from an HFS+ HDD, as I have yet to find another company that makes one.

After having this player in storage for 4 months, I connected it to my TV with a friend over. They were tired of hearing me brag about what a great player it was. Immediately after turning it on, the HD720 player display went to ‘NUPGRADE’ and locked up the screen on the TV. So I secured power and tried again, ‘NUPGRADE’ again. Needless to say, my friend was not impressed. I explained it was probably just a firmware issue or required a hard reset. I wasn’t overly concerned, as the player performed well the last time I had used it. I emailed the distributor NBOX the following day expecting a quick fix, and this was their response:

“The issue is due to the damaged circuit board, no easy to way to fix it. It can still work as USB 3.0 high speed HDD docking station if you connect it to PC. 

Do you want to upgrade this model to A400 4K model? I can give you a big trade in credit for this not working unit even you bought it over 2 years ago. We can do 80% credit for you towards the new device A400.”

I went to Amazon and clicked on all the one star product reviews concerning the HD720 player and found this NUPGRADE issue repeated over and over. I can only assume that most purchasers like myself were at first thrilled with the player and gave it great reviews but most fail to update their product review to reflect what a major disappointment the KDLINKS HD720 turned out to be.

The HD720 was stored for future use in the original packing material it came in. As I mentioned previously, the player was rarely used. The problem is I purchased the A400 earlier this year because I was impressed with their original product, and I’m sure that the cheap electronics that KDLINKS used in the HD720 were used in the A400 as well. It’s only a matter of time before that player decides to stop working. I intend to update my original review of the A400 as a cautionary tale to others to reflect this. Besides, unlike the HD720, the A400 is strictly Android based and can only read from an NTFS or FAT formatted HDD, which could pose a problem if you are a Mac user.

We all have electronic computers and players with “circuit boards” that take a beating day after day and still continue to function with no difficulty, but the HD720 media player received no hard use whatsoever, in fact, it was handled with the utmost care. I have subscriptions to NETFLIX, HULU, HBO, AMAZON PRIME, so I used this player mostly to organize my music, photos, and some obscure video files I throw in.

As far as other media players that can read from an HFS+ HDD, I cannot recommend any at this time. Personally, I have not been able to find one listed on Amazon. It hearkens back to a day when it was impossible for a Mac user to find common software available only to Windows users. If anyone can recommend a reputable media player that can read from HFS+ to me then please let me know. For Mac users there is a way around this, albeit kind’ve frustrating, what I can suggest is backing up your media files and then reformatting an external drive to NTFS. Then transferring the files from the HFS drive to the NTFS drive. This of course would require either a Windows emulator on your Mac, or purchasing an inexpensive PC laptop with a software program that can read both drives. Overall, very frustrating, but with some research, it is possible. Amazon has many media players listed that can read from an NTFS HDD. Another option is to format a drive to FAT32 or exFAT which both Macs and PC’s can read, but with a few caveats. One being file size constraints with the FAT32 (single files can’t be larger than 4GB), and exFAT being too slow.

I would be hesitant to purchase another KDLINKS media player considering the experience I have had with this one.

KDLINKS and their distributor NBOX are fully aware of the HD720 ’NUPGRADE’ issue and should either fix the problem or stop selling a defective product to trusting consumers.

Thank you.
