title: Excellent Upgrade in Computer Quality for the Price
text:
I bought this after wanting a bump in sound quality and having failed with 2 different PCI-E external sound cards. I have a pair of Micca PBX bookshelf speakers attached, and now with my new TV, I can use the optical out and run the Wii and PS3 through this D1 Amp and my good speakers! Everything sounds great! The caveat is that there's no kind of automatic input switch; meaning if you want to switch back and forth from computer USB Audio to Optical TV audio, you have to attach and detach the Optical cable. Not the worst deal you could have.

I took off a star off because I was having trouble for a little bit with some audio distortion and sync issues during playback. Tech support was responsive and worked with me to troubleshoot and diagnose the issue - mostly trying to replicate it on other machines. I forget if I was able to replicate the garbled sound on my laptop or not. My apologies. It was never constant, was the thing. I could watch one episode on Hulu, and audio would be fine. Then if I switched to audio editing in Premiere Pro or Audition, it would garble and slow overall A/V playback in an attempt to re-sync the video with the audio.

But I let my wife try it on her computer, where only headphones were an option, and she didn't have troubles. She's not an audio-nut like me, but she's leaning - and even she could tell and identify a difference in sound quality! I took it back when I got the TV so we could use the optical out for Consoles. Using the supplied [gold-plated] USB Audio cable, I plugged it into my computer, and haven't had any troubles since! Seems like not all USB cables are alike; i.e, don't try to use a printer cable on the D1, even though they are technically the same connector type...
With the included cable, there's No garbled sound; no de-synced playback. Just beautiful sound and a nice boost to my speakers! I live in a studio apartment building, so I never really get to let it explode with power - but the few times it has gotten loud, everything sounds great! [Granted that's also based on the speakers themselves, as well as their positioning in the room. An Amp/DAC is not a magic fix for "perfect audio", but it will help.]

The mids are richer without being over-powering and making the mix sound tin-y. There's nice, controlled bass. Don't expect to power a lyric-less basement party with this. But I'm pretty sure no ones buying it for that reason anyway.
I do lots of video work - both movies and my own song covers - so a balanced, studio-quality sound is needed to make adjustments later on. Don't think of it as "Flat", as in the typical iPod/phone EQ setting for Flat, which leaves no distinction between Low, Mid, and High tones. The D1 gives a professional sounding, clear mix of the entire audio spectrum. You get pronounced bass on songs that are meant to have it, but it's more controlled, like the artist/producer meant you to hear it - instead of nothing but ear-splitting reverb, like in lame car stereos you hear blasting down the road. Vocals are more clear in songs, and you'll be able to tell who on YouTube properly knows how to mix their sound and who doesn't ;)
I love listening to all my music through this thing and spotting the clear spots that sounded compressed with the onboard computer audio. You can really hear a difference in iTunes downloads [new ones, that is. I bought one that was a poor upload to iTunes, so no fix there...]

I highly recommend getting a longer replacement cable, as the included one is maybe a foot long. That said - do not just try to go to Staples and find a cable that fits. Audio transfer is much different than data.

title: Didn't know what to call these at first or how to search for them
text:
When I first made a few cables for home, I didn't know what these things were called or that you could buy them. I'd thought professionally made cables just had them molded in. Obviously, I came learn they're called strain relief boots, at which point easy enough to search for the term. Not having them is probably not a great big deal for cables that will hardly ever move once they're in. But for stuff like home entertainment gear, which somehow seems to require occasional moving about or reconfiguration, I think they're important. Because otherwise you end up with twisting and weakness in the connector ends and maybe breakage. And for a laptop station where a cable might be getting disconnected and re-connected several times a day, I think without it you just drastically increase the risk of a connector breakage/failure.

I'm using these with the following cable I got: "NavePoint Cat6 (CCA), 250ft, White, Solid Bulk Ethernet Cable, 550MHz, 23AWG 4 Pair, Unshielded Twisted Pair (UTP)" and they fit fine. They snug up easily enough and make my home made cables look just like they came from the store.

title: If I had a no stars option, I would give it that.
text:
My company and my late boss's company has sold Harman Kardon for decades, as they were a neutral sounding receiver that offered full bandwidth / full frequency range outputs in even their more affordable units. Many companies would not do this, and therefore had a truncated frequency range. Unfortunately, since the passing of Sidney Harmon, the once decent company is no longer Harman Kardon. I have talked to people in the company that have told me that the marketing department now runs it's products and the days of ultra high bandwidth receivers with decent power supplies is now over. They have replaced their former stout power supplies with digital ones containing toy-like, tiny, laughable Crown transformers. Crown was never a good company, and Harman Internation acquired them apparently as a cheaper way to build their units and make more money at the cost of quality. These cheap, lousy power supplies that cause the unit to be half it's former weight, and are much smaller make the units sound digital, tinny, thin, have a very diminished shallow bottom end, and do not sound like Harman Kardon of days past. You have to really work to get any semblance of the abundant, deep bass that you previously were able to get. Harman Kardon has also poisoned their line of Mark Levinson with these same power supplies and has received lousy reviews on those new pieces as well. Harman Kardon has also taken out their flag ship two channel integrated amplifier (HK 990) and replaced it with this lousy digital power supply garbage.

In a nut shell, the marketing executives at Harman Kardon have chosen light weight, in house gosh awful power supplies to increase profits over the legacy of a good sounding audio product and has banked on their customers not knowing the difference. I don't know about you, but I know the smell of dog poop when I smell it. And this is dog poop. Sidney Harman is most likely rolling in his grave after how much work he put into this venerable company all his life. My only hope is that enough people give them bad enough reviews and don't buy their product that they are forced to re-evaluate like they previously had to do with their failed digital receivers over 10 yrs ago and go back to making a decent product. Those were so bad that Fry's couldn't hardly give them away.

The AVR 3700 is even more of a disgrace than most of their receivers, as it's supposed to the flagship. This is basically $1000 pile of refuse that is being passed off as the best Harman Kardon has to offer. When you look inside, you will find 2 VERY SMALL crown transformers, which give the body very little shallow bass compared to units of yesteryear and give the unit a digital thin sound that is not like what Harman Kardon used to be. It's a lousy offering by a cynical company that thinks it can pass dog food onto the consumers and they will not know the difference. After being long time customers and proponents of HK, we no longer are and cannot recommend any of their receivers. We hope that we can find a company that values its customers and doesn't abuse them like Harman Kardon now does with poor products and awful customer service. The wait time is ridiculous. And you have to really work to talk to someone who isn't an East Indian and understands nothing. DO NOT BUY THIS UNIT!

title: Phiaton Chord vs Parrot Zik
text:
I bought this headset because I wanted the following features:
- noise-cancelling (my office is very noisy, and I travel very often by plane)
- Bluetooth (to avoid messing with cables)
- microphone (to use it for phone calls)
- ability to function without power (so that you can still use it as a normal headset if the battery runs out)
- comfortable (to wear it for extended periods of time, e.g. 12 hours flight!)

I used to have a Parrot Zik, so I'm comparing the Chord MS 530 to it.

Let's see how it fares for each feature.

1. Noise cancellation
It does an OK job. It's not exactly a closed headset (it doesn't cup around the ear, so there is less isolation). However, sometimes, when used purely to cancel background noise (without playing music), some weird low freq feedback loop will happen, and you will hear a kind of "WOMF-WOMF-WOMF-WOMF" which immediately becomes very uncomfortable (and makes you feel much better as soon as you remove the headset from your ears). Other reviewers mentioned this, so I'm not sure if this is a defect of my model or if all headsets have this issue. Since I often use it in planes to soften the engine noise (without music), that one is a huge showstopper.

2. Bluetooth
It works. I don't know exactly what the "dual device" thing means; if it's supposed to be "two devices connected at the same time" (e.g. my phone and my computer) then it doesn't work, though.

3. Microphone
When used as a Bluetooth headset, it did an OK job. However, I often use my headset to deliver webinars and other online presentations, and in that case, I plug it (to avoid being disconnected if the battery runs out or if I get Bluetooth issues in the middle of the presentation). As it happens, when you plug the headset, instead of using the microphones of the headset, it's using a microphone embedded in the cable. As a result, when I use the cable, I sometimes have to keep it closer to my mouth, otherwise people say that my voice is not loud enough; and I also have to be careful about not letting it brush on my shirt, because it makes annoying noises for the listeners.

4. Using it without battery
That works just fine. On that front, it is actually better than the Zik, because you can turn Bluetooth and Noise-Cancellation on and off independently. I.e. in a plane I can turn on only Noise-Cancellation if I want to; and when in a quiet environment I can turn on only Bluetooth if I want to.

5. Comfortable
In my experience, it had a tendency to fall off a bit, especially when using it in a plane. However, because of the noise cancellation issue, I have never kept it on my head for extended periods of time, so I can't really compare here. That's unfortunate because that was one of my issues with the Zik (after 4-6 hours it gets not-so-comfortable).

Other things:
- the Zik comes with an iPhone/Android app that lets you check battery level and do some (IMHO useless) customizations; to be fair, at first, I hated this app (I was wondering why they couldn't just have a simple widget showing the charge level, instead of that bloated app?) but on the Chord I have no way to check the charge level (other than a complex key sequence that I can never remember without checking the manual!) so the app is not that bad after all;
- the Zik comes with really easy controls: the right ear cover is a touchpad, so you swipe across it to adjust volume, pause, skip tracks; on the Chord, you just have one knob, and you do short presses to tweak volume, and long presses to skip tracks; I often fumbled, and also sometimes it would remain stuck in a position (e.g. when I want to lower the volume, it would remain stuck, and instead of lowering the volume it would loop back to the current track)
- the Zik has a really nice feature: it detects when you take it off, and pauses the music; sounds like something useless at first, but when you switch to something that doesn't do that, you miss it a lot (e.g. someone wants to talk to me, I have to fumble to the pause button, take off the headset, etc)
- the Chord comes with an airplane adapter, to use it in those old planes with the special dual-jack connections; that's nice, because I ended up buying one for the Zik;
- on the Chord, the micro-USB connector (for battery charge) and the jack connector are covered with little flaps, while on the Zik, there is no cover at all; the flaps might prevent dust from getting in, but in my experience, they are rather messy and frustrating when you want to plug the thing.

I haven't done a scientific test on battery life, but the Chord seems to fare better (even if it might be because I use it less since I'm less happy with it).

title: Why, Why, Why..........
text:
What a shame! B&O had the all around best (as of summer 2016) Bluetooth speaker on the market IMHO but the battery life just sucks!

OK, now for good, this is the best sounding Bluetooth speaker I have ever owned or heard. The high end sparkles with a clarity never before heard in a Bluetooth speaker. The low end is pronounced, solid and refined. There are no passive radiators, which to my ears creates a bloated artificial sounding bass. Pretty much every Bluetooth speakers has passive radiators for the low end, not this one. The A1 has a 3.5" driver and a tweeter, simple and effective.

Now, let's talk about the battery. 24hours? Really? Well that's the claim from B&O. How about reality, at volumes of 50%-75% I get about 3-4hrs, horrible for a speaker claiming to get up to 24hrs. Yea I know the fine print says (24hrs) at moderate volumes, but that is just misleading.

Another design "feature" is when the battery gets low it goes into power save mode which reduces volume to about 20%. So what's the big deal, I will just plug in a USB charger, wrong. Once it goes into power save mode (max volume 20%) even when connected to a USB charger it takes time to recharge and get out of this mode and I was not immediately able to turn the volume back up. This is a buzzkill when you are trying to provide music for your friends!

To B&O, you made a beautiful amazing sounding speaker but at the end of the day it's a wireless portable speaker, it needs to last more than several hours???

title: Wonderful little dashcam!
text:
EDIT: I should also mention that I've owned this cam since August 2016, or approximately 10 months from the time of me writing this review. Never had any issues with the cam. Some other recent reviews say the latest firmware messes with the cam. I haven't done this upgrade so can't confirm but if you do have an issue with the latest firmware simply download/install a previous, stable version (same principles for your computer).

After spending several hours researching different dash cams I wound up getting this one and don't regret it.

I love the size and shape of the cam. It's small, sleek, and streamlined and doesn't scream, "I'm a dashcam!" like so many others out there. Additionally, I don't need an LCD screen and a million buttons on the cam. What I'm seeing out my car window makes an LCD screen redundant as I know what the cam is seeing/recording already. I just need it to do a few things: Look relatively discrete, record well, and be reliable. This hits all three notes.

You can put a luggage lock on the cam to prevent people removing the SD card which is nice. Once you put a SD card in the cam automatically installs the BlackVue software onto the card for the next time you place it in your computer (the software can be used to review footage and, most importantly, tweak settings). Even if you use a new card or reformat it the cam will always re-install the software so you never have to worry about that. You can adjust the settings on this cam pretty well: Turn on/off certain voice and beep notifications, enable/disable LED lights, change it's recording sensitivities, etc.

The cam uses capacitors instead of a lithium ion battery which I also love. Capacitors have a higher heat tolerance meaning they're less likely to explode due to extreme heat (and cars can get hot in the summer) versus the lithium ions. An internal battery is used to give the cam enough juice properly "end" the current recording when you yank out the power cord otherwise that last video clip would be corrupt when trying to go back and view it.

The cord is plenty long and the cam can be swiveled on a single axis for recording height adjustments.

USE THE POWER MAGIC PRO accessory if you buy this cam/brand. The PMP allows you to record even when your car is parked. You can adjust how long you want it to record after you park (from 6 hours to infinite). What makes the PMP so special though is that it constantly checks your car's battery voltage. If you battery goes below a certain threshold the cam turns itself off to prevent it from completely draining your battery. Most other cams that offer "parking mode" recording don't do this.

All in all I love this little cam. Worth the investment. It was installed myself.

title: Great Tripod for the Price
text:
This is a great tripod for the novice to semi-pro. The included ball head is better than you get with many comparable clones. The bag is decent.

I would not say this is a portable lightweight tripod. In fact, its quiet heavy at 3.71 lbs for just the tripod and ball head. However, you are rewarded with better stability and features vs other lighter similar design clones.

The ball head on this tripod features three knobs vs just two knobs I have seen on similar clones. You have one for each degree of freedom, pitch, roll and yaw. Although, the pitch and roll knobs are not truly independent. Tightening on one does affect the other axis drag. If you want to lock it down, this one locks down very well. The yaw movement is very stiff, yet smooth. I expect it will loosen some over time. I can see you using medium weight setups with this ball head with no issues. Up to about 5 lbs will not be an issue. Above that you may be left for wanting.

This tripod is pretty sturdy up to its maximum height extension. There is some camera shake at the maximum, and its best one extension level down from that. This is not an issue for me at 5'10". Plenty of height for me even when one extension level down. On the legs I find the twist to lock to be better and work faster than the flip to lock you see on many other clones. This a personal choice. The feet are just pieces of rubber and do not have spikes or anything like that.

Overall, this is a keeper for me, even though I also own a slightly smaller and lighter clone version of this from another manufacture that works nearly the same way. This will be my out the car, in the backyard, at camp tripod. My other one will be for the back pack, on the trail, in downtown, etc. For this price, I would buy this one again.

title: Easy to setup, great to use, outstanding customer service.
text:
Couldn't be happier with this product. Performance is one step above my old wifi router. Parental controls are a snap, great tool for parents to take back control of the electronic addiction epidemic that is going through our youth these days. Set up was a breeze and management is a ridiculously easy with the smart phone app.
But the tipping point, what impressed me the most, has been the customer service. I have a network setup that I am sure is pretty unique to my case. I ran into an issue with DNS name resolution that I'd be willing to bet not even 1% of their customer base would encounter in their environments. I brought it up with Gryphon Customer Service nonetheless, and I was astonished to find out the effort they put in fixing this issue for me. They came back with prompt responses to my emails, and not from some clueless CSR following a script, but I could tell it was from the guys who actually know what the thing works. They asked the right questions for what I'm sure was trying to replicate my environment so they could replicate the bug, found what the problem was and issued a firmware update addressing it. All this in less than a week. I've never seen this kind of response from an electronics company.
I hope this product is wildly successful, and that the company reaps the fruits of their good work. Highly recommended. Five stars (and I never give 5 stars on my reviews).

title: It simply works!
text:
Got this SP 16GB RAM kit as an upgrade to my laptop. Went from 8GB to a whopping 16GB! Everything works as advertised. Did not need to tweak anything in BIOS, simply installed the sticks, booted the laptop and it began working right away. This PC3-12800 / DDR3-1600 CL11 kit runs at dual channel, and at a low voltage of 1.35V. No heat issues and it prolongs the battery life vs 1.5V sticks. It’s nice to see RAM that works as it should and doesn’t require visiting BIOS.

SP seems to be manufacturing their own memory chips / modules so they don’t reply on other vendors. That (hopefully) increases consistency and should keep prices down in comparison to the competition. What I did notice though while checking spec details in programs like CPU-Z and Speccy, their brand name is listed as “unknown”. Not sure why that is as the bigger brand names are always listed, so thought I’d point that out. On the upside the production date on my sticks said to be 8/16 (week/year), so sometime mid to end February of 2016 – very fresh!

What a nice upgrade to my Lenovo Y50-70. This RAM is a great addition to the i7, SSD & GTX 860. Now it runs smoother and faster than before. I ran a few memory stress tests and spent a total of a few hours gaming and so far it’s very stable. Hope to use it for the next few years. What’s not to like? It works great, doesn’t overheat and runs stable and efficient. The Lifetime Warranty is also a plus and provides a peace of mind. I would recommend it to anyone looking to upgrade their laptop.

title: You like sound QUALITY? Just buy this. (With yearly updates 12/09/19)
text:
At first listen, most will wonder how a company could offer a battery operated speaker with this sound quality and volume for $300. When you see and hear the smaller bluetooth speaker competitors that are in the $300 range, just go ahead and scratch your head trying to figure out why they are charging $300 for their speaker if Aiwa can produce this thing and sell it for $300.

I cheated and found the answer to that question during my research and read that Aiwa is putting all their money into better speaker components rather than spending it on marketing as most others do. No stores.....no commercials.....no glossy ads.....no big mark up.

I am however, scratching my head trying to figure out why the full list of specifications for the Exos 9 is not listed here on Amazon. It most certainly is a huge selling point. If you want the full list, go to Aiwa's home page on the internet. I'll list a few that I feel are very important that aren't listed as of the date of my review:

APTX bluetooth codec. If you want good sound, start with a good input source. Neither my phone nor my tablet have APTX, so I purchased an APTX transmitter/ receiver here on Amazon for $35. just so I would insure my Exos 9 was getting the best possible signal to begin with other than direct wire from the 3.5 mm jack input. (Brightech BTX Ultra....works great in transmit mode) You turn off your phone's bluetooth so the Aiwa won't pair with it, connect the small Brightech unit to the 3.5 mm earphone jack of your phone and boom! Instant APTX pairing with Exos 9.

The size of the 5 powered drivers......two 1" silk tweeters, two 3" neodymium midrange drivers in their own acoustically isolated chamber to lessen harmonic distortion, and a 6.5" dual voice coil woofer.

Two speaker pairing, either left and right channel stereo or both mirroring each other.

Class D bi-amplification 200 watts continuous possible output, not peak as some advertise.

This thing just flat out sings. Thumps bass, clear highs......whatever your ear's preference to dial in on the 5 band equalizer. Don't even try to compare it to any other battery operated stereo speaker. I say stereo because there are some battery mono PA systems out there that are loud, but sound quality suffers and they aren't stereo.

Go to youtube and listen to clavinetjunkie's sound comparisons. After hearing his videos, I preordered direct from Aiwa some 2 months ago and have had the speaker 5 days now and am liking it more each day. Have taken it to the community pool 3 times for low volume listening and the bass/treble even at low volume just sounds so much better than my old set-up. Makes the time under the sun and palm trees that much more enjoyable and relaxing for this Florida boy. It will also be my new best fishing buddy.

If your need doesn't require you to carry your speaker in your shirt/trouser/suit pocket or pocketbook/backpack/briefcase to be portable, this is the one. A 1980's boomer style with 2015 components and engineering with a rechargeable lithium ion battery.

A great review earlier today by Jeff right below mine pretty much covered my opinion of this fantastic bargain. Just buy it and start a party. It gets LOUD!

UPDATE 11/14/15: If you are looking for a suitable CARRYING CASE for your Exos-9, I found my 36 can soft sided cooler by AO coolers works great. (Link: [[ASIN:B00329IRJW AO Coolers Silver 36 Pack Soft Sided Fishing Cooler]]) The vinyl side version is waterproof and comes in black, blue, or silver colors. Speaker fits snug, just push down on the top of your speaker and zip her up and buckle her down. $70. and it is a great cooler when not being used to transport your speaker. Makes carrying it a lot easier in addition to offering protection.

I have found one drawback.....when people hear this speaker, they want one. I can't count how many times complete strangers have come up to me at the pool and started asking the same questions- "Where did you get it?" & "How much does it cost?" So I'm just saying....be prepared to repeat the story about how great this thing is over and over if you buy one. // End update//

6 MONTH RELIABILITY UPDATE:5/20/16:

Well, well. Here we are after 6 months of use, 3-4 times per week, 2 and 1/2 hours or so each time. Still ROCK SOLID sound and performance. I take this to the pool by car in the trunk without my soft sided cooler carrying case 3 or 4 times a week. Let's say 5 months of trips because January is cold even in Florida. That's 20 weeks worth of loading for at least 60 trips with 120 in and out of the trunk handling cycles with no problems yet. Still sounds just as good as new if not better now that the speakers are well broke in.

I charge the battery every other trip even though it doesn't need it. Have never come close to running the battery down. The speaker sits in the hot Florida sun the whole time it's playing with no issues. I don't use the control panel at all, although it works fine, as I control song selection and volume with my tablet or phone. No need to use the touch panel for me. I set the equalizer initially and then forget it.

And yes.......people are still asking me questions about the speaker when they hear it. It is that good. Worried about reliability? Not me.....

1 YEAR UPDATE 12/06/16.......

OK, so here we are after more than 1 year of fairly heavy use as described above AND (drum roll please)....nothing new to report. Sorry.

Still works as new, still sounds incredible, and still impresses anyone who hears it. So there.....you really have no reason not to buy unless you are looking for a squeaky sounding little pocket toy. They have their purpose- lightweight portability, but they are no where near in the same league as this beast when it comes to the quality of sound and the volume of sound. Period.

You know you want one. Just press the "add to cart" button. 1-2-3.....GO!!!

12/14/17.....I'm baaaaaack......
What a great pool season this year! Plenty of sunshine, plenty of tunes.

The machine has weathered the storm for yet another year with no issues whatsoever. I'm talking 90 degree heat on the pool deck, in and out of the car trunk a gazillion times, and she just keeps on PLAYING. Isn't that what you expect when you lay out 3 bills? Yep....still going strong. I don't know what else to say that I haven't already. I charge the speaker about every 3rd trip, play it for 2 1/2 hours each time and it sounds as good as new today.....over 2 years later. I transported this speaker in and out of my car trunk at least 120-130 times over the last 2 years plus with my pool schedule.

It's Christmas....treat yourself or a loved one. Listen to awesome sound wherever.

Cheers!!!! Happy Holidays everyone!!!!!

12/13/18......Just checking in.....another year of hard use and still no problems. Not too many products you can say that about after 3 years. This is one of them. Battery is STILL strong (which amazes me). These guys built a speaker to last. If I haven't broke it yet, it's solid as a rock.

12/09/19.....It's the holidays, so time for an update! Still sounds as good as new. Haven't been using it as much at the pool as past years due to buying a boat and fishing more often. Cuts into your pool time, you know? Ha! Life is good. I am amazed that I am still running the original battery with this beast with so many charge cycles under it's belt. It's nice to know I can buy a new battery if it ever does go kaput on me.

One thing I am noticing reading some of the other reviews- if you are not happy with the volume or sound quality, USE THE EQUALIZER! It makes a BIG difference in both. Listening without the equalizer in just sounds "cheap" and not as loud to me. I use the classic "v" pattern on it....gradually more bass as the frequencies get lower and more treble as they get higher with a flat midrange. It's all up to your individual ears.

It's the giving season.....buy this to give. You will be the best Santa on the planet! Merry Christmas everyone.

title: UPDATED: Shopping For Other Options
text:
UPDATE
Not loving this thing these days. I've had a lot of issues since Android 6 was released, and my Galaxy S7 barely works with the USB connection. You really have to fiddle with the connection to get audio over USB. Sometimes, it drops out and you have to disconnect and reconnect the cable. Not what I should be doing driving down the road. My steering wheel controls haven't been able to change tracks with Android 6+ on an S4, S7, G4 or a Pixel. The AAlinq and Dashlinq apps are poorly-coded garbage.

In the past, firmware updates corrected similar problems, but it's been almost a year since the last update. Tech support didn't even pretend to have a solution to these problems, nor did they seem to care. Can't recommend these anymore, feels pretty expensive now that I've experienced their level of service and support.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
Bought this directly from the manufacturer, so it came with the right harness and firmware for my '06 CR-V w/ XM. Easy to install, if you've ever replaced a car stereo you shouldn't have any problems.

I use the USB streaming feature with my Android (5.0) phone, and everything works as expected. The steering wheel controls let me change tracks in Google Music, although there is a 2-3 second delay before the next track loads up. I was pleasantly surprised by this, as the documentation led me to believe that I would only be able to control GROM's AALinQ app from the stereo. Track titles will only be displayed on the stereo if you use AALinQ or an iPhone, apparently. No big deal. My stereo displays "USB Streaming" when the adapter is active. Both the stereo wiring harness and USB/AUX cables were long enough to give me plenty of options for mounting the adapter and running the wires where I wanted them to go. I ended up mounting the box in the blank space behind my stereo, and ran the USB and AUX cables down into to the compartment below the HVAC controls. Nice and clean, and I don't have to worry about somebody breaking into my truck to steal a fancy aftermarket stereo.

I didn't buy the Bluetooth add-on, so I can't speak on that. I'd imagine it works just fine if you need that functionality.

title: Makes all the difference compared to my older unit!
text:
I bought this pre-amp to replace a 15 year old Radio Shack 15-1108 amp. That amp was originally installed on a Radio-Shack VU-190. It preformed as a great setup in both the pre digital and digital age. When I moved to a different house, the amp came with me, but the antenna stayed.

I Live in a VERY mountain filled area between NC and TN. according to tv fool and others I should receive no channels at my location. I'm at 3300 feet, and face a 4100 foot mountain range at about 1 mile from the house to the front, and 3600 foot mountains to the rear. This "Fish Bowl" makes decent TV or Radio reception difficult.
I purchased a HD-Stacker antenna, and installed it with my old amp last year with a rotor for max control over signals.

I was pleased to find that I get 11 channels, but soon found that even with the antenna pointed for max signal I would experience signal drop outs and channel freeze up most of the time on many of the channels.

The signal strength was good (ish) but I stll had reception issues.

So, a few days ago, I ordered and installed this model. I am happy to report that all the issues have disappeared, And I now have 15 to 18 channels (day vs night watching) The New amp must have either better gain, a lower noise floor, or my old amp was deteriorating. Either way I am Very pleased with this inexpensive but powerful amp.

Please note, that I actually installed my antenna and amp properly with proper grounds and static guards. It may be the difference between my install and some of the poor reviews I've seen here.

Here are some quick tips for getting good TV reception.

1st Get a bigger antenna then you think you need. There is no such thing as to much antenna!

2nd Don't skim on the wires. Get at least RG-6 or RG-6 Quad shielded wire. The better the wire, the less signal loss.

3rd. Always use a preamp that mounts at the antenna ! An in house booster is only good for diributing the signals around the house to your various TV's it will not help the signal loss that happens from your antenna to the house.

4th Keep your cable runs as short as possible. Long runs mean signal loss. Use in house boosters if needed, but try and keep your antenna to distribution box or TV as short as possible.

5th. If you can afford it get a TV antenna rotor. This is critical in deep fringe areas like mine. Being able to point your antenna at the distant transmitter makes all the difference in reception.

6th GROUND EVERYTHING!! ground the mast, the antenna, the wires, and ground it good. it helps with reception, and reduces the risk of damage to your house and equipment if there is a lightning strike. Pre-Amps are Very sensitive to static electricity and need to have a good ground setup to insure a long life.

That's it. I hope you all have the same good luck I have had with my new Radio Shack 1500526 Pre amp.

title: The worst bino by far was the Celestron 16X32
text:
I AM NOT A BINOCULAR EXPERT, BUT I KNOW NIKON CAMERAS AND LENSES OVER 20 YEARS OF BEING A NATURE PHOTOGRAPHER USING LENSES THAT COST THEN OVER $1,000. I KNOW WHAT IMAGES YOU CAN EXPECT FROM QUALITY EQUIPMENT.

I recently moved next to a golf course filled with wildlife including geese, doves, ducks, rabbits and coyotes I had an ancient pair of Zenith fully coated 7X35 binoculars, which were ok, not especially sharp, but with almost no flair or multiple images. I wanted a higher power pair and over the next month bought four: a Celestron 16X32 roof top prism bino, the Barski 10-30X50 bino, the Nikon Aculon 10-22X50, and the Skymaster 15X70. I returned the first three as defective and kept the Skymaster 15X70. Why?

The worst bino by far was the Celestron 16X32, because not only was the collimation off, but the optics were very fuzzy, and there were lots of secondary images which made them totally useless. Of course they were only $17. Amazon did a fantastic job taking them back and refunding.

Next was the Barska 10-30X50. They were fairly good in terms of clarity and double images and collimation at 10 power, but once over 20 power they were useless, so unclear that they were useless, like they had a medium fog in them. They also had a lot of secondary images around the main image.

I NOW ATTRIBUTE THE SECONDARY IMAGES TO THE UNCOATED LENSES BOUNCING LIGHT AROUND CREATING SECONDARY IMAGES THAT TAKE AWAY SHARPNESS BY KILLINGTHE ABILITY TO SEE SHARP EDGES. THE REFLECTED IMAGES WOULD NOT FOCUS DOWN TO THE CENTRAL IMAGE, LOSING LAITY AND BRIGHTNESS.

So I bought the Nikon 10-22X50 mm hoping for at least some of the clarity I find in my $400-$1,400 Nikon camera lenses, because those lenses have an "exit pupil" size large enough to cover a 35 MM film frame, which in its corners means a circle requiring crystal clarity of over 43 mm, which is far larger than the 3 mm needed at the 22 power of the Nikons, therefore less expensive sized glass, etc.

But no. The Nikon's had a higher degree of clarity than the other binos, but the lenses are not fully multicoated, and the multiple image problem was much worse than any other bino I tested. Also there was some blue color fringing on some bright sharp lines, that totally obscured the clarity at that point. The eye relief was only 8.6 mm which means you can't use eye glasses with them. When I took them out at night, I looked at a bright star, and get this---I saw 21 images. There were four light flares at 90 degree angles, and embedded in each were 5 reflected images of that central bright star!! So I sent them back to Adorma, which had to be threatened before they paid for shipping, and they still may charge me $14.95 if they don't find them defective as I did.

REMEMBER, I DON'T HAVE THE MULTIPLE IMAGE PROBLEMS WITH THE ANCIENT ZENITH FULLY MULTICOATED ZENITH 7X35 BINOS.

SO, I ORDERED THE SKYMASTER NOT EXPECTING MUCH BUT WAS PLEASANTLY SURPRISED.

These binos are bright. They are not as clear as the Nikons, but the reflected multiple image problem was the least of the four binos I bought and no noticeable color fringing, and the magnification is good enough to read a clock on the patio of a house 150 yards away. They revealed that amount of detail. I am keeping them.

But now I am aware that to get Nikon camera lens clarity in binos, you need to spend a lot more than I did on the Nikons or Skymaster. You need good quality multicoating, phase adjusted and coated prisms, perhaps ED glass, and enough robustness to not lose collimation by being bumped in shipment.

However, for the price, the Skymaster 15X70 is an excellent buy for terrestial use. Because I am nearsighted, without eyeglasses, they focus at close as 35 feet or even less, thus good for even small birds on nearby trees.

I took it out last night for a go at the sky. It beats all the others I tried hands down including the Nikons--flaring was much lower than the Nikons, and no discernible multiple images on stars.

title: Lasted six and a half months...
text:
About the only good thing about this bag is the warranty. Actually, given the option to destroy the bag in order to get the replacement you see just how little you get for your money. Yes, it holds a large computer (17" Dell Precision) but after 6.5 months of daily use the straps were at full tension limit and one strap actually stretched. Needless to say I initiated warranty replacement (actually, I wanted a refund but they wouldn't give it to me since a purchased on Amazon.) After cutting up the bag you see that they use cheap packing foam for the padding (that's why it crunches!).

Here are the talking points about this bag...

Pros:
-plenty of space
-fits a large model computer
-exterior material is good stuff (was hard to slice with a box cutter even)

Cons:
-expensive for what you get. You could put the same money or less into a different brand and have a bag that lasts many many years.
-cheap materials. Packing foam? REALLY?? My last bag had nice neoprene foam that never made a sound and was always comfortable.
-poor pocket layout and organization
-only room for one water bottle, but not a big reusable type bottle, only a cheapy
-no pocket for battery, or charger, or tablet
-big in all the wrong places
-straps don't have support strapping running throughout, which led to stretching
-chest strap attachment is useless--didn't cinch enough to make a difference
-did all that money go towards Everki labeled fabric? I'll trade that for plain orange fabric and better design/materials

Overall I think Everki is scamming people. The appearance of the bag is nice but the inner materials and actual function is pretty poor if you travel a lot and use this as a daily use bag. I've had two other bags over the last fifteen years and both were better but far cheaper than this bag. Not only do I have buyer's remorse, but I have buyer's remorse for anyone else who falls for this company's claims for a "high end bag". Look to other companies if you want a bag with some thought put into it and something that will last.

title: Excellent Motherboard, best B350 board out there!
text:
I just built my new PC afte 15 years! In between i was a dedicated console gamer until finally i decided to get back into the PC world and enjoy the higher framerates and better resolutions. After doing some homework, and based on my needs, i decided that the new AMD Ryzen 5 1600X was good for me. I wanted a machine that had some decent power and offered most bang for buck!

When looking into supporting motherboards for the Ryzen 5 i kept reading forums on Reddit and watching tons of YouTube videos by Paul's Hardware, Bitwit, Linus's Tech Tips and of course Jay'sTwoCents. Considering these guys are all pros and have what seems like the deepest pockets and sponsorships and all i couldnt really afford the best of the best system. However, when comparing this model of B350-F vs the Prime Plus vs A370, this one offered the most bang for buck and had the complete list of features i needed along with some basic RGB features included.

The Good - This variant of the b350-F motherboard is by far the best one to use, has a very easy (and pretty) bios interface - overclocking on this badboy is so easy and straightforward that you will be able to do it without even watching a YouTube video although i would recommend you watch one prior to doing anything on it. Pricing of this thing can't be beat either, i purchased this when it was for $104.99 on Amazon and had a $20 rebate from ASUS bringing it down to just $85. At that price, the amount of features this board offers, including its build quality is amazing. This board fit perfectly in my Phanteks P400 tower without feeling too tight at all. There are also a plethora of USB ports on the back including 3.0 as well. Overall quality, price and build of it is very impressive. The board also stays relatively cool and i have not experienced any spikes in temps.

The Not So Good - The only thing i disliked was that the board did not include a USB type C port. That is literally it! Everything else was perfect for my needs and booted up like a champ when i first built everything on it.

Overall - This B350-F board is the best option to get and can even save you some money. For moderate overclocking, a plethora of ports and cool RGB lighting as well as multiple points for fan and AIO connections, i would highly recommend this board. The lack of a USB Type C port is the only thing going against this board, other than that i am extremely glad with my purchase and do not regret it at all. If you're on the fence of getting this vs the A370, i would say go with this unless you are truly into water cooling and doing high Overclocking for extended periods of time. This is perfect for everything else and can handle moderate OC. Look it up on YouTube as well if you'd like to.

title: The Tips Make All the Difference
text: I recently purchased these earphones to replace a wonderful set of Klipsch headphones I unfortunately left behind at the gym. But I have Polk Audio speakers all over my home and hold the company in high respect. So I picked a pair of tips similar to those on the departed Klipsch phones. The mids and highs were nice and crisp but there was no bass at all. This didn't square with what some reviews said about the bass being punchy and, if anything, too strong and tending to distort at high volumes. So I tried another pair of tips, and another, and another. Finally,  the fourth pair of tips were a revelation. The bass came through firmly and perfectly balanced the higher registers. But now, another problem: when taking them off, the tips stayed in my ears. I tried a slightly smaller tip and, though the bass is not nearly as good, at least the tips stay on the buds. I have had many sets of earphones and never encountered a pair whose performance was so dependent on the tips. So, if your first impression is like mine -- abject disappointment -- you may simply need to try some different tips -- possibly all of them.

title: Recommended, though some things could be improved.
text:
This backpack has been my everyday carry to work and back for almost 2 years now. In that time I've come to love it, but that's not to say it doesn't have its issues.
First let's talk positive. It's very light and a great size for up to 15 inch laptops (not sure if it's specc'd for higher, but a 15 inch is the biggest I have and it works fine). I love that it has cinch straps so your stuff doesn't rattle around as you walk/run/float down the street. The pockets offer plenty of space, including the secondary main pocket (not the front most, but the pocket that has pouches for pens and such) which has plenty of room on the bottom for a small jacket (though I usually have a poncho there, and there's still plenty of room) and it doesn't get in the way of the random stuff pouches in the same pocket. The inside of the main pocket has plenty of room, and a small single pouch, a zippered pouch, a small divider lining, and a padded laptop sleeve with a velcro strap to hold the laptop in place. Also in this pocket is a USB cable that connects to a batter bank that allows you to charge your devices from the outside of your bag. The battery isn't included, and this leads me to my first negative point of this bag. As the inside layout of the bag stands, there isn't a small enough pouch to hold a battery bank securely without it turning about in the bag. I've broken a battery bank or two at the plug, so I've been apprehensive about leaving this cable plugged into the battery, thus, I haven't used the external USB plug very often. There are however, pouches that are perfect for a battery in that front storage pocket, but there's no internal pass through for the cable, which means I either don't use the USB cable, or I fashion my own way. I've recently put a small hole on the inside, to the left of the upper pockets in the main compartment which keeps the cable out of the way when I'm in searching through the main compartment, and allows me to keep the battery bank secured and plugged in without being nervous that it will break.
Another point that this backpack is lacking is in the right side pouch. This pouch has a small magnet attached strap that will hold in smaller items, but the magnet is far too strong for the weak material and leaves me feeling like it's going to rip every time I have to remove the strap. A smaller magnet, or a sturdier strap (like the cinch strap material) would go much farther.

Overall, this is a great daily backpack that I've taken to work and to school. If it had a few small tweaks I would say it's 5 stars no problem, but either way, I have no problem recommending this to friends or family.

title: Good, Modest TV with Some Weaknesses
text:
After a few months using this TV, I feel I should re-do this review.

The good:
--------------
It works well once it gets going. The image is clear (it's 1080p, whatever the pretentious reviews say, 1080p is pretty much the same everywhere), and I stream Netflix, Amazon Prime, and YouTube on it via its apps without much trouble. I also have an antenna hooked up and it pulls in many channels and has a number of built-in features that help me use broadcast. This TV also greatly simplified my home theater setup by becoming a single hub for everything I do with it, compared to my old non-smart TV.

The Bad:
--------------
-The TV doesn't seem to always play nice with my (admittedly outdated) router, requiring power cycling the router several times a week.
-Samsung support can remotely access the TV to do fixes, but the only fix they really know is to factory reset it, forcing you to go through the lengthy initial setup routine. The Netflix help desk was the one that solved the issue.
-Its browser is absolutely useless. I tried to stream the debate on CNN...it could barely load the CNN home page, after a painful process to enter the URL in the first place, then when it did start streaming it was sometimes in the background and I couldn't get it to switch the image back and forth.
-The Screen Mirroring works about one in fifty attempts (I have an S5). Its samsung-to-samsung, it *should* link up without any trouble.

The Ugly:
--------------
-A smart TV is basically a laptop with a very big screen and no keyboard (it has features to support a wireless keyboard and mouse, but I fail to see the point given its terrible browser). Presumably to save standby power, "off" turns everything off, and when you turn it on again it has to go through a bootup process of about 3-5 minutes. During this time, broadcast works fine, and you can see your apps, but you can't open any. I assume this wouldn't have been an issue if I bought a more expensive TV that advertises its processor.
-Also, it has all the makings of a DVR for broadcast (except for raw storage) but doesn't do it. I think that's a lost opportunity for Samsung, another feature but for some programming they could advertise.
-There are a lot of additional features of dubious effectiveness or use.

Like others, the only 'mod' I've made is to enable the dip switch that converts the Delete key into a BackSpace key, since I can still achieve the Delete key by hitting Fn+` which I do much much much rarer than BackSpace.

It does take some getting used to, especially for the location of the CTRL key (which I believe is at the location of where it was in the very old IBM AT PC keyboards), but for me, it's a minor consideration.

This keyboard works fine whether you use a Mac, Linux, or Windows, of which, I mostly use Mac and Linux and occasional Windows usage. At least, that's been my experience.

However, most of which are only a few episodes from programming, which require a TV subscription through your provider to continue watching. This was not advertised in the Fire Stick description, it simply states that there are over 15,000 apps and games available. It doesn't state that most of which are not full seasons (of older shows) or even multiple episodes. Some only show you one or two to entice you to purchase through a cable provider. When contacting my cable provider (Xfinity, which is only one of two in our area), they promised that their TV package would unlock networks that needed a TV subscription to view. However, the networks do not recognize Xfinity as a TV provider, so you are not able to unlock as promised. What is frustrating about this is that they require a TV subscription through a provider, you have to pay for multiple streaming services, and pay/rent in order to watch a majority of shows and movies. At this rate I might as well buy a cable subscription and continue buying DVD's from my local store. I am not seeing this as a full benefit to not having cable, as I have to have a TV provider (apparently only certain ones qualify, regardless of company promise), and subscriptions to netflix, hulu, and others in order to watch. This was very disheartening. And none of which was advertised clearly with Amazon before purchase. I don't know that I would have purchased the firestick had I known a majority of content was restricted without a variation of paid subscription.

title: Great little monitor.
text:
This monitor definitely does its job. It's lightweight, can accept nearly any power source, has an HD display and is far superior to the displays on cameras. It also maintains good picture quality when viewed at extreme angles and is very cheap. I decided to hook it up to my HDR cable box, and the picture was surprisingly good, even the little speaker was plenty loud for tv watching.

There are a few cons though. The biggest issue for me is that the display suffers from noticeable banding. I'm not sure what the bit depth of the display is, but if you're using any lens with a shallow depth of field, you'll absolutely notice banding in all out of focus areas. Banding is also quite noticeable on solid colored surfaces. The aspect ratio setting is also always reset to 16:9 after the 1:1 pixel mode is used. This is not a problem for my GH2 since it actually outputs 16:9, however for my bmpcc, I need to cycle through the options and switch it back into the "just scan" mode, a minor annoyance. There is also a 5 second splash screen that reads "Field Monitor" every time it is turned on, delaying its use. Finally, focus peaking does work, however it's not particularly effective, and it would probably be easier to simply focus by eye since the monitor is very sharp.

I find it comical that there is a USB port for firmware updates as there is no way that a firmware update will ever be released. There isn't even a website for feelworld, let alone any sort of support or firmware.

title: Compare to Thermaltake Power Suppy Cable Extensions
text:
[[ASIN:B01IA9FFIY Thermaltake Sleeve Extension Power Supply Cable Kit, Power Supply, Black & Red (AC-033-CN1NAN-A1)]]
[[ASIN:B01N5K14YM EZDIY Sleeved Cable - Cable extension for power supply with extra-sleeved 24 PIN 8PIN 6PIN 4+4 PIN - Black]]
[[ASIN:B01EGBZA1C Thermaltake CORE W200 Dual System Capable Extreme Cooling XL-ATX Computer Case CA-1F5-00F1WN-00]]

Used these to complete the very lengthy runs required on the above W200 Super Tower which still required more length after installing two sets of the Thermaltake extensions to each side of the chassis two installed systems. Notably the 16 gauge wire not-used by other extension makers is a must for high current runs of the required length for this chassis when the accessory pedestal is also used. These completed the colored Thermaltake runs just great and were the only choice that offered the same material look and texture (non-cloth) along with a compatible gauge wire. Most other makers are using lighter gauge wire so for the same reason thicker speaker cables sound better on premium loudspeakers, a heavier gauge extension is capable of more current without heating the wire to much. Obviously the price is way better than the Thermaltake product. They did not deliver with comb clips like others (a painful task but works for consolidating individual wraps), but for the price go for it.

Have used Phantek (Messy, dense weave but hard to route and look good at the same time), Thermaltake (great non-cloth alternative but ultra pricey, a couple more cables than EZ cable kits though), NZXT(cheaply made, potential fire hazard) and Bitfenix (luxurious hyper priced Euro laundry for your computer) brands on other builds for reference.

title: after losing all of my stuff to a stupid linux NAS and then everything AGAIN to another stupid ...
text:
Folks .. I've read a bunch of these reviews and I would make two quick observations: 1) Guys want to create NAS server environments in their own home with hardware that isn't rated for industrial use and most of you know what that means. 2) You buy NAS devices of questionable quality (yes you will not agree) when motherboards and other PROPRIETARY stuff fails. And then you perhaps report the hard drive as having problems -- well maybe yes and maybe no. Complain, complain.

So no, ya got me. I'm not as sophisticated as a bunch of you guys that want to tweak everything to death and complain when it doesn't work. But I will say this, after losing all of my stuff to a stupid linux NAS and then everything AGAIN to another stupid NAS (this time EMP= Yes killed me), I went back to a simple design ... local fileserver with VM, having redundant, automatic software-based drive backups to two Reds acting as RAID 1. I extend RAID 1 to an external device I lock away. My offsite device has all computer images + daily backup.

All of the individual workstations act as reverse backups to the primary system noted above. Their data saves to the file server, but if the file server goes down, files are available (with digging) upon need from each PC. We could argue about computer/network system security and most of you would be right. But I would say, my security rates pretty good for a baseline. Took me years to get to this point of thinking. I've built three systems (others) and they sleep at night. I do too.

So I've taken too much of your time to say after two years + my REDS have done very well; Reliable and error free. I will be upgrading to larger capacity because I have Plex Server needs. I will be buying REDS because they serve my simple needs, return good diagnostics.

Don't allow all the computer geeks out there trying to force enterprise performance out of retail stuff. As long as you know what you're buying and understand the purpose it was designed for, you'll do fine. I'm going back to the trough to buy more.

OH - OH ... another contributor had a very great point ... if you need more than one drive, buy them from different vendors, hopefully at the same price point. This is a learned lesson from a guy that's built a few.

Best !!

***********************************************************************

11-18-2019. Update.

After more than three years, all my 4TB "Reds" are still fully functional with -NO- file system errors. I recently built a PC for my father and his three "Reds" are also without issues. Hitachi makes a "Red" counterpart that is also a very good drive but it's not nearly as quiet as the "Red". Overall, I'm happy with either for my builds.

title: LOVE some things about it, not others (see UPDATES)
text:
I'm waiting for my straight talk specialized GSM to CDMA sim card to arrive for use on the Verizon network (yes, you can do that, according to Straight Talk technical support- it's a function of the sim card, provided the phone receives the proper bands, and this one does). So far I LOVE this thing. For one thing, it comes with my favorite ringtone, Machina, installed. For another, it works great as a phone held up to your face, just like a regular (albeit HUGE) cell phone. I determined this by recording sound with sound recorder with it held up to my face, and then listening to the playback the same way. And best of all, absolutely delighted that it works perfectly with my much-loved [[ASIN:B0087Y0I8A OPIS 60s retro handset for all modern smartphones (cream)]], which works like a dream and sounds like you're talking on a landline in your living room. It screens out extraneous noise, like in the grocery store. That way I keep the phone/tablet in my bag and just pull out the handset and talk. One minor glitch with some phones/tablets is that with the handset plugged into the headphone jack, some don't ring aloud, but even so you can place calls, or plug in the handset when the phone rings. I'll update this review after my sim card arrives, as to whether it rings with the handset plugged in, and the phablet's performance in general. But so far it's a beautiful and responsive device, and unlike my LG G-Pad, which I also love, I don't have to go through all kinds of hassles (google hangouts/voice etc) to use it as a phone.

UPDATE 1: Yes, it DOES ring with my Opis handset plugged in, yay. Note for those interested in this, one must still see the tablet to answer or place calls. What I do is keep my wide-ish bag open in the cart so I can see the tablet (also has my shopping list on it). If the phone rings I can easily answer it and pull out the handset, takes all of 3 seconds. Plus, I'm older and sometimes absent-minded, and have laid down smaller phones while looking at or bagging something- this works better for me, and if I need to step away from the cart for some reason I simply put my bag over my shoulder (second nature to me).

Regarding the sim card, I called Straight Talk to activate it and transfer my phone number from my old Straight Talk phone and sim card. It was all done automatically, without a hitch. The automated system instructed me to text APN to 611611 when the new phone became active. I did, you receive text messages you just click on to finish updating. Went from 3G to 4G and four bars (this on the Verizon network, which Straight Talk uses in my zip code). Perfect reception! I couldn't be happier. The only slight quibble I had about the phone was that the supposedly HUGE font setting was still not large enough to see without my glasses (unlike the HUGE setting on several other phones and tablets), so I downloaded the free BIG FONT app from Google Play, which lets you set any size you like. Good to go!

Finally, was able to find only one rather blah black case for the H8 when I searched on Amazon, which I ordered. Perfectly serviceable, but a boring matte black. Oddly, I found other cases on Amazon with a wider Google search, sold by Liu Shan and fulfilled by Amazon (Prime). Here are the links: [[ASIN:B07CNZNN2N Yuntab H8 Case,LiuShan PU Leather Slim Folding Stand Cover for 8.0" Yuntab H8 Android Tablet,Almond Blossom]], and [[ASIN:B07CPB9LG2 Yuntab H8 Case,LiuShan PU Leather Slim Folding Stand Cover for 8.0" Yuntab H8 Android Tablet,Red]]. There are several styles available.

In a nutshell, LOVE this tablet, perfect for my needs- I highly recommend it. It replaces my highly-regarded Irulu V3 with a 6.5" screen which was AMAZING, still going strong but the camera has stopped working after 2 1/2 years, sigh. If this Yuntab phablet malfunctions or dies I'll update my review [see below]. If you found this review helpful, please click the Helpful button. Thanks!

UPDATE 2: Three things- have no idea why, but after a month's use the sound volume decreased so I can't hear it on calls if there's any extraneous noise. I am in a new locale, but I have ample bars. I tried adding volume increasing apps, none worked. The speaker volume (and with headphones and bluetooth) is fine for media, but not for calls. So basically I can only use it as a tablet now. The second issue (after installing a new SD card, is that the combination tray for the sim card and SD card is so rinky-dink, it took me a good 10 minutes to get the sim back in (it goes in the innermost slot) along with the SD card. I have poor manual dexterity admittedly, but both kept falling through the tray- the rims to seat the cards in are so narrow as to be practically non-existent. The first time I inserted the sim card I was just lucky I guess. Issue number three is that there doesn't seem to be a "close button". Rather than swiping to get the back, minimize, and close buttons at the bottom of the screen, there is a built-in, dedicated bar at the bottom of the phone with similar legends, but pressing the one on the right doesn't bring up open apps so you can see what's open and close them individually, it just makes whatever's on the screen disappear. I downloaded a couple of apps for seeing what's running and closing whatever, the wrong apps I guess because I still couldn't tell for sure what was open, and haven't investigated further or asked someone more knowledgeable than I am. If that button IS actually closing all apps, it would be handy to have a dedicated button for that. If not, and you don't care about open apps, battery draining, memory usage etc. I guess it doesn't matter. These issues aside, I like the tablet otherwise. If I solve any of these issues I'll provide a further update.

title: Beautiful design, but some parts can be improved on
text:
I just received this laptop in the purpose of doing CAD work as a student. Overall, this laptop is a solid machine and I am quiet satisfied with my ws60. I haven't done rendering on this yet but with designing on Solidworks, I have had a pretty smooth experience with this.

Pro:
- Slim, light, and beautiful design
- The keyboard is definitely one of the best I have ever used on a laptop
- I actually like the built-in programs: True Color; Keyboard Shortcut; Nahimic etc.
- Fairly fast, just need to watch out that you don't download softwares that are meant for 32-bits computers. Doing so will result in consistent freezes of the program in your laptop
- Comes with a fashionable protective cover.
- Supports mini-displayport and thunderbolt
- Fans are quiet and work great

Con:
- Display could've been better. Although the screen is bearable and you can always connect to an external monitor, the pixels are visible and the color is a bit off (I've tried to adjust it manually but it didn't help much). With designing, a screen with a high would've been helpful.
- On/off button is too bright. It is a pretty design but I just wish that I can dim it down like the keyboard. It is right in front of the screen and can be distracting at times.
- The battery isn't great. With light use, it will last a bit more than three hours. This requires you to carry its charging cable in most occasions when going out, and this brings out the next point:
- The charging cable is bulky and heavy. When I put it in my bag, it's as if I am carrying a brick around. This is pretty contradicting to the intended "light" design of the laptop
- Since the major outputs of the fans are under the laptop, this laptop should not be placed on a bed or any soft surfaces, or else it will become extremely hot.
- Only two USB outputs. This is personal preference but I usually need one for my mouse, one for my external keyboard, and one to connect to my phone or other devices.
- The logo on the back is very easily scratched. This is my third day of usage and my logo is already scratched. I take very good care of my laptop and I always place it in the protective cover when I travel.
- The protective cover is a bit on the small side. This may be for the intend of stabilizing the laptop so it does't move around, but when I put the laptop in, the corners stick out and push onto the zipper. I am afraid that overtime, the paint on the corners will come off.

Edit:
After an year and a half of use (warranty is for one year), the overheating problem of the computer burned the graphics card which is mounted together with the motherboard with everything. I need to buy a new computer now.

title: I almost sent it back - Here's why, But a decent router in the end
text:
The TP-Link AC3200 Wireless Router is a competent pretty much "all in solution" for the average home user. It has support for older standards and most of the new ones for wireless transmission.

But here's what happened to me. The router arrived by one day Amazon delivery after my Asus router failed. The Asus had given good service for about three years. Heat finally seemed to get to it, and the power switch on the back of the router went bad. I needed a new router. Now, this isn't the first router I've had to deal with. This is probably number 8 or 10 all told. And all have suffered with the same basic flaw.

In anything other than a very simple setup, the routers just don't seem to want to recognize an IP address. That's what happened this time.
I elected to set up wired ethernet. The instructions supplied with the router are vague. Go to the website and get the full manual because if you have problems, there's a section in the very last pages devoted to troubleshooting.

I began setting up the router at 4PM (easy 30 minute job). The fun began. On a wired basis, I could not get two different computers to talk to the router. I tried the http://www.tplinkwifi.net. Repeatedly. No dice. I tried http://192.168.0.1 and a whole bunch of other addresses. No luck I rebooted the router. I reset it. I tried again and again. No luck. Reluctantly I went wireless and used the WPS button on the front. No luck. Again, on multiple machines. I finally got out an HP laptop that has Linux Mint on it, and the wireless app reported a signal, but no handshake seemed possible.
This went on till midnight. I gave up, left the router on, went to bed. Next morning, up and at it again. Maybe it was the firmware? Went to TP link and looked for new firmware. Confusing since you're not sure if you're loading the right geographical part of the world. Anyway, set up the download, ran the file, router went into an update for 40 seconds or so, and wouldn't complete the update. Not Good. Unplugged Router, unplugged computer, came back and used the paperrclip reset on the back..Now, for reasons unknown, I'm able to reach the website wirelessly. So, I tried wired. About 45 minutes later, I get the wired connection up. Works from reset to connection on all three machines now. When I say reset, I referring to the small paperclipped sized hole where you can reset the router to factory defaults.

OK, now up and running. Caution: Router wants to change the default user id and password as soon as you successfully login with admin(user name) and admin (password). Have new ones handy right away or you'll have to reset the whole thing a second time. Keep the new password and user name next to your router or if something goes wrong, you'll have to use the reset paperclip. This router has one 2Gigahertz band and two 5 Gigahertz bands. If you're in a busy area, change the default to a new channel manually. Less interference from other routers. In my setup, there was no particular difference in the working range over the signal paths between the router and the computers. All are governed by an FCC rule that limits power. The high power setting is just a little below the max the government permits.

It took this router almost 30- minutes to find an address and do a proper wired handshake when connected behind a Cisco router in the 170 IP range. It's really slow to get to a handshake so be prepared to give it time. Once inside the software, you can do the basic software setup or move on to the more advanced settings. Router power is slightly above that of the ASUS but router signal stability over the signal path is excellent. I don't even extend the antennas, but fold them flat (you may want to extend them though as a matter of good practice). The router runs well over a two story home with metal imbedded in the walls over a distance of almost 100 feet, and I run it on medium power. It runs cool. Just don't put anything on top of it. I like the button on the front far left that allows you to turn off all the blue LEDS. Great idea. WPS button gives you enough time to find a signal.

My conclusions: If you don't mind the possible hassle getting the handshake (wired or wired connection and recognition) between the router and your computer or cable modem, then it's a good purchase. I doubt there's a much better unit on the market. Amazon's price is attractive as I write this in March 2018. All routers of this type use pretty much the same basic technology and the the same internal chips. The number of antennae is a marketing gimmick. After 3-4, you've got plenty. If you need more RJ45 internal connections or more than two USB connections, then you could move up to a higher priced unit, but that would be a fairly involved setup.

The Good: Signal Transmission Reliability, Power cord long enough to avoid having th have an extension cord, adequate USB and RJ45 Connections, Lights off on the front, WPS button on the front.

The Not So Good: Difficulty logging into the router, The somewhat confusing quick setup instructions, The firmware upgrade process, The troubleshooting instructions found buried all the way in the back of the instruction book which you have to download from the website.

title: The best at the price point
text:
So I had a pair before this, and I love them so much I decided to order another pair. Now I'd like to express why I believe these headphones are the best at their price point, hands down.
I had bought my first pair literally days after they had been released, at the release price. I added them to an order from another place because I thought why not have a cheapo pair of headphones around. Well, they lasted from then up until about 3 months ago.
The sound quality is excellent, and the drivers are positioned at an angle inside of the headphones, which really, really helps with sound reproduction. They are also quite simply built with a very good quality cable, and let me tell you why.

The cable they used in these headphones is a double insulated and properly shielded cable. There is the first outer layer of the cable which we all touch, there is then an insulating layer with filtering (Ground/negative tied wire mesh traveling the entire length of the cable). Then underneath that layer there was another layer of insulation like on the outside, and then the enameled wiring. Once the cable made it's way into the headphones, there were TWO forms of stress relief. It was held in by a molded piece of rubber that was around the cable that also acted as a strain relief for moving side to side, this is the outer one you can touch. After that, it was then clamped very tightly in with a wire clamp inside the headphones, this mean the cable that led to the headphones, never broke in my time of using it, they actually had a more peculiar failure.

After the cable comes in, it is directly soldered to the speaker on that side, then another cable is introduced which then splits that one off and takes the other positive for the other ear and brings it to the other side. That cable then travels through the headband and is visible from the outside. That particular cable is what failed on mine, and because they were so cheap and I didn't have another cable that would work, I just got rid of them. However, I'm back to buy another pair as I was so incredibly impressed with how they were built when I disassembled them to attempt repairs.

Now, a lot of people might receive these and see the plastic used for the earcup swivel joints and be worried it might break. Don't be, the headband is very flexible and doesn't put too much pressure on them, they must've thought of that during production as they can be worn for hours without discomfort.

Now lets get onto the best part of these headphones: the earpads. Oh. My. God. The earpads on these headphones are done RIGHT. VERY soft yet never let the inside of the earcup touch the outer edge of your ear (unless you have big ears). The headband is also quite good, it's a standard style headband for studio monitors, the foam is great that's used in it too.

Now here's what everyone wants to know, how do they sound?:

Well, comparing to proper Tascam studio headphones, the models being TH-300X and TH-MX2 I have to say, I like them better. They do have increased bass and the highs are also accented quite a bit in these, but the reason I like them better is because when you listen to something that is properly mastered through these, they really make the music shine. You have to get to know the sound of these, use them for at least a year before you can properly master with them, as the sound is somewhat colored. However again as I said, once you know how they sound it becomes a familiar sound that's just all around enjoyable.

Now if you're also going to wonder about the durability of these headphones, I'll give you the short and sweet of it: When I threw my last pair in the garbage, you could barely see the logo on the side of the earcups, they came with me in my DJ bag and in my laptop bag, used them for gaming and in the studio. Never once could I find a fault about them.

Overall review:
Comfort - 10/10
Design - 7/10 (Standard studio monitor design they all use, no originality points here)
Durability - 7/10 Using a slightly thicker gauge of wiring would have prevented the fault in the headband, otherwise no issues.
Sound - 8/10 Due to slight coloring of the sound, however it's in a good way.

title: Good mount but not 100% compatible with my TV
text:
This came with all the necessary bolts, washer, screws, and even spacers for a curve tv. One of the problems I had is that the bolt (M5) that was for the flat tv was too short for my Samsung UN65KU6300. I had to use the longer bolts for the curve tv and cut off about an inch from it. It is advertised as working for all Samsung but this is not 100% true. It's a good thing I had a dremmel and didn't have to go to Home Depot to find the right size bolts. So if you have a Samsung UN65KU6300, just be aware of this.

And also, PLEASE DO NOT RELY ON THE LEVEL. It is not accurate as everyone had mentioned here. It's off by about 2 degrees compared to the 2 other levels I had. On a large TV that is going to be noticeable.

Another issue I had was with the locking bar. It's the length of the wall bracket so it's impossible to push the bar all the way in let alone put a lock on it. There is literally about an inch space between the wall and TV. On a smaller tv, it will probably work but definitely not on a 65. So right now I just have it about 3/4 in. So if you want to lock your larger TV, then this is not the mount you want.

On the positve:
I was able to mount it on a my wall which had 26" stud gap. The height is adjustable 2" up or down and also side ways by about 5 inches on my UN65KU6300. Sideway adjustment will be depended on your VESA mount size on your TV. Mine was pretty narrow but not sure the size. This was a good thing as the mount was not centered because of my stud locations so I was able to center my tv to the wall (mount is off the right by 3"). When adjusting height, make sure you have help on larger TV. This is as close as my TV will get to my wall and did not interfere with the small hump on the bottom rear of my tv. Installation was easy after modifying the bolts and seems to be made of strong metal. Overall I'm still happy with this mount as I was able to work around some of it's negatives and was not concerned about locking my TV. Thus the 4 star rating. Love the way my TV is so close to the wall with this mount. I will post side view pictures later today. For now I only have front view.

I strongly recommend Tekukor. The price is perfect.
