title: The future is here
text:
This is probably the best mini PC on the market right now.
* What's good:
- Price is competitive.
- i5 5th generation computer that can rest on your palm. Running 24/7 with minimal of heat issue, low power usage, great performance.
- Good display adapter with HDMI video AND audio out; Displayport output is also supported.
- 802.11ac Wifi built-in, gigabit Ethernet port.
- 4 USB 3.0 ports.
- Room for 2 DDR3L memory up to 16Gb. If you buy one bar 8Gb, install it in the lower slot. Room for 2.5" hard drive. I put Samsung SSD EVO 850 and it is perfectly fit in.
- Latest drivers are up to date on Intel's web site, supporting latest Windows 10.
* What I don't like:
- Mini HDMI instead of regular HDMI. I have to buy an adapter just to convert it back to regular (standard) HDMI. Most people are having existing standard HDMI cable at home.
- DDR3L memory only. It would be great if it also supports DDR3 which will save laptop-convert buyers some $, but this is acceptable for the benefits of its size and performance.
- This is what I hate: Product description should be clearer: (maybe just Amazon.com)
+ Model ended with RYK and RYH. Most people will overlook the differences. If RYH clearly states supporting 2.5" HDD, RYK should be states ONLY mSATA is supported to avoid wrong order. Most people who need 2.5" HDD support may just look at the price and slimmer profile of RYK and placing a wrong order because of that.
+ Product title should clearly state the generation of its processor so buyers won't place a wrong order of previous generation by just looking at the price and processor type (i3, i5, i7...)
+ Intel (or Amazon.com) delicates a whole big section of "From the manufacturer" to introduce stuffs that I think most potential buyers of NUC will just not interested at all. Where is the detail technical specification section? The spec will save buyers from unnecessary hassles. Take my case, I ordered the NUC and later on found that it only supports DDR3L, Amazon Prime Now was helpful and saved my day to put DDR3L memory order in. All items were arrived as plan within hours and I thought it should be all set. When I opened the box at night, I found that it's a mini HDMI, not standard HDMI port. Stores are all closed at the time. It sucks throwing the toy back to the box and have to wait for a darn HDMI adapter purchase tomorrow, it just ruins all the fun.

text: I bought this for my blind mother-in-law to listen to audio books on. Once I figured out how to set it up, it worked fine. There are difficulties for someone legally blind to use it. First, it is very small, which is good and bad. Second, the on/off switch doubles as a selection switch. This ends up causing many problems because what happens depends on how you use this switch. Also, it is black, no markings at all. The only way she can find it is by feel. She sometimes pushes the wrong button or pushes too long or too short on this one which means it does something she doesn't want it to do. She uses headphones (easier than earplugs) and the hole for the headphone plug is behind a door on the side. That's solved by leaving the headphones plugged in at all times. On the opposite side is the plug-in to attach the charger, also behind a door. This is pretty much impossible for her to manage. title: Basement home theater - Using Xbox One with 120" screen
text:
This is a great projector for the price! I paid $500 via the used section in amazon, which was an amazing price. It stated light scratches/scuffs but I didnt see anything wrong with it, just not in the original box. The projector was wrapped up really well in the plastic air pocket packaging stuff. The only issue I saw was the power cord was short (it was a normal power cord, not a long one that I needed). When i hooked it up the lamp life read 0 hours. I never saw anywhere on amazon the amount of hours, if any, so I assume it is in fact zero. Online reviews that give you exact settings state that the projector should be ran on eco mode in dark rooms. The lamp life on eco mode is 6000 hours.

The projector runs great. It's a little loud every once in awhile with the fan noise but I have it installed right above my couch so I knew that I might hear it sometimes. The 1080P 60hz image is amazing. It states 120hz but i'm not sure how to get to that level. The best image quality is a blu ray via my Xbox One. I also have my Tivo Romeo running the same 1080P 60hz and it isnt quite as good, I'm sure this is due to no cable channel running 1080P broadcast.

I bought a 120" 1.1 grain 16 x 9 electric screen off ebay for $109 with shipping. I've never had a high end screen so i'm not sure what to compare it to but i have had 4 or 5 projectors and this one is by far the best. My last was a Mitsubishi HD1000 and it was 720P 2500:1 contrast ratio. This Optoma has a lot more detail in the images and the contrast is better. I thought with 8 times the contrast the Optoma would blow me away, but it really didnt.

I just bought the 3D emitter and a pair of the 3D glasses and watched World War Z last night. It scared the s**t out of me more than a few times. The 3D on such a big screen is really amazing. I had an LG 55" LED 3D TV and the size really makes a difference with 3D. The emitter and glasses synced right up, no issues. The glasses are a little dark but the brightness on the projector makes up for it.

This review is getting long, sorry for that. I just wanted to give all the info i could. I know it's tough deciding on a projector with out seeing it in person. I"m $780 in with the projector, screen, longer power cable, monster HDMI cable, mount, emitter and one pair of 3D glasses. The setup is well worth it!

I went 4 out of 5 stars due to the contrast. Very dark scenes do bother me a bit. But to get any better i think you would have to spend $2000 or more on a next level projector.

title: If you want a 13" laptop capable of running the latest games then it's a great option. It's not cheap
text:
The bottom line for this laptop is that it's powerful beast in a very small package. If you want a 13" laptop capable of running the latest games then it's a great option. It's not cheap, but contains some high quality components.

Read on for a lot more detail:

OVERALL CONSTRUCTION/BUILD

My first impression on picking up this laptop is how light it is for a gaming laptop. Sure it's only 13", but I was expecting it to be feel more dense than it does at just around 4.5 pounds. The overall quality of the case is high. I would say that it's not quite as nice as the machined aluminum of a Macbook Pro, but it is light years ahead of some of the cheap plastic-feel laptops I have tried out. It definitely feels 'high quality' in your hands.

The design features a glowing blue alien logo on the outside of the screen with a few glowing blue lines on a dark grey background. If you're looking for a "professional" looking laptop then this is probably not it, but considering it's branded with an alien theme - it's a lot more subtle than it could be. Personally I like the design.

SCREEN This display on this laptop is a gorgeous 3200x1800 screen, and it looks awesome. The Amazon listing says the resolution is 2560x1440 pixels, but this is definitely incorrect - the one I got runs at 3200x1800 out of the box. The screen is bright and clear, and everyting I've tried out has looked great on it. I'm not personally a big fan of touch screens on laptops, but I tried it out for a while and everything I messed around with worked well. One reason I don't like touchscreens much is that I hate putting blemishes on my beautiful screen from oils off of my fingers, but I have to admit that even after using the touchscreen for a while there isn't really any noticible smudging at all. One minor annoyance with the touchscreen is that flicking away a bit of dust on the screen ends up opening up menus or moving my cursor. Not a knock on this specific product at all, just a personal preference.

One thing to note is that with the 3200x1800 resolution on a 13" screen, this laptop scales up content through Windows settings by default. Through "Display" -> "Make text and other items larger or smaller" the default setting puts the scale up all the way. Most programs handle this scaling well, but it's possible that you will run into one that doesn't (like thie "Alienware Product Registration" that pops up, the text is microscopic). This isn't a knock on the laptop, just the reality of running such a high resolution on a smaller screen.

KEYBOARD
The keyboard is surprisingly comfortable considering they had to cram it into a 13 inch laptop. The keys feel nice to the touch, and the space is used well. I'm especially happy to see that they found room for page up, page down, home, end, and delete keys. I use these keys often while programming, and I'm glad they're here. So far I've accidentally hit the page up/down keys a little too often, but I just need to get used to the keyboard. The palm rests are smooth and comfortable.

There are also lots of customizable keyboard backlight options if that's your thing.

TRACKPAD
The trackpad on this machine is not very good, it's the biggest negative in my experience with this product. It works alright I guess, but it's not anywhere near as smooth as the one on my Macbook Pro. Given that this is a only 13" laptop, the trackpad is a good size and fairly comfortable to use - but the texture of the pad is a little rougher than I'd like and this leads to scrolling that's just not completely smooth - the cursor tends to jump and skip a bit as you move it across the screen. Right-clicking is also a little finicky, sometimes I end up left-clicking when I intend to right-click. Gestures work fairly well with one major exception:

After setup I installed Chrome and started browsing around the web. The gesture behavior was extremely buggy in Chrome. It almost seemed completely random. Sometimes it would scroll correctly, sometimes it would snap the page to the top or bottom, it would often draw strange rectangles everywhere as I gestured. This behavior did NOT happen in Internet Explorer or Firefox, just Chrome. I tried to resolve it through driver updates but didn't have any luck. After research, it looks like the problem is with Chromium specifically, but I haven't been able to figure out a workaround. Here are two threads that have information on the topic:

https://productforums.google.com/forum/#!topic/chrome/BdaUw9boNSU
https://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=463350

As a result, I'm not able to use Chrome at all, which is a definite bummer because Chrome is my usual browser of choice. I've been using Firefox and the scrolling works very well, but I'm disappointed I can't use Chrome.

SPEAKERS
When I turned the volume all the way up on this laptop, I was honestly shocked at how loud these speakers are. It is MUCH louder than my 17" Macbook Pro. The quality is decent, it doesn't compare to a nice Sonos speaker or anything - but it's excellent for a 13" laptop. Not much bass, but boy are they loud.

GAMES
If you're buying this computer then it's highly likely that you're a gamer. I've tried it out on a bunch of different games, I'll talk about them here. The framerates are GENERAL ideas of the fps I was getting, obviously these fluctuate a lot during gameplay. I used MSI Afterburner to get the numbers.

Far Cry 4

I loaded up Far Cry 4 and it crashed immediately after launching! Bummer! I spent a while on this until I found a random forum post that said that MSI Afterburner causes Far Cry 4 to crash, and sure enough they were correct. Unfortunately that means that I don't have actual fps time data for Far Cry 4. I can tell you that it autodetected 1920x1080 on High, and this was running fairly well - but I scaled it back to Medium and the gameplay was a lot smoother. I'll stick with medium.

Fallout: New Vegas

Fallout: New Vegas autodetected 1280x720 on High quality, and it ran at a solid 60 fps. I scaled it up to 1920x1080 at Ultra quality and it ran between 40-60 fps.

Civilization V

Civilization V is a good example of what I mentioned earlier in the review: Some applications just aren't built to run at such high resolutions. Civ V autodetected 3200x1800 and the main menu was all weird, centered in between big black emptiness in the middle of the screen (Some people talkig about it here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/8930/discussions/0/864980734944032303/). The actual game worked ok though, but only ran at about 12 fps. I scaled the resolution down to 1920x1080 and it went up to about 20-22 fps. Frame rate isn't as important in an RTS as in an FPS, but there you go.

The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings

The Witcher 2 autodetected 3200x1800 at Low quality and ran at about 20 fps. I scaled it down to 1920x1080 and the framerate jumped to 35-50. I upped the quality from low to high and ended up with 22-32 frames per second. I'll also note that The Witcher 2 consistently crashed for me whenver I exited it, not sure why.

BENCHMARKS
If you're into benchmarks, I ran a few with this machine right out of the box. I didn't try to optimize these scores at all, they are just what I got with the vanilla machine:

3DMark
Sky Diver 1.0: 9209
Fire Strike 1.1: 3352

I also timed reboot, and it was just around 10 seconds. Very fast.

BATTERY

It's hard to give information about battery life because tasks vary so wildly, but I just had a battery charge last a little over 4 hours through some web browsing, video watching, and programming.

CONCLUSION

I decided to go with 5 stars for this laptop because I think for the correct customer it's an awesome product. I would have given it 4.5 stars if I could due to the lower-quality trackpad discussed above, but I don't feel it's worth taking off a full star for. I've put a lot of information in this review, and I hope it's enough to help you figure out if this is the right laptop for you. If there are any specific questions then leave them in the comments below and I will do my best to respond. I'll also be updating the review in the future as I use the laptop more and more. Best of luck making your decision!

title: Too late to return it. Threw it away.
text:
The wireless delivers good 802.11ac speeds throughout the house although 802.11n doesn't hold up at distances.

BUT the thing continually broadcasts UDP packets to 255.255.255.255. This can't be turned off, Netgear says it isn't a bug and doesn't offer any option to stop it. It's completely unnecessary. Serves no purpose whatsoever. Maybe not a real problem if you don't care about what malware is doing on your home network but I do. Monitoring network traffic is one way to prevent malware spreading from one device to another. These packets are interpreted as malicious so they clutter up and fill up monitoring logs.

The second problem is that administering the MAC address filtering (which stops unauthorized devices accessing your network even if they brute force the WPA2 key) is useless. I cannot find any way to see the list of authorized devices that are not currently connected nor any way to remove a device unless it is connected. The logic that says I must connect a device to the network that I don't want connected the network before I can stop it connecting to the network is perverse. In addition, you can only add a device to the authorized list if you disable mac address filtering first.

Both of these issues are particularly frustrating because they aren't an issue of the excellent Netgear 802.11N access point I replaced it with or the excellent Netgear 802.11G access point that came before that. It's going downhill.

Anyway, too late to return it so I threw it away and bought a different brand. That's what I thought of it.

text:

Sensor 2 (newer) batteries were each below .9 volts. Sensor 1 had a Duracell leak. (see photos) These were supposed to be good through 2025. Replaced all alkaline Duracells with new Energizer Lithium AA. I have never had a lithium battery leak. I cleaned up the corrosion with an old tooth brush and vinegar. Quick rinse, dry and a light coat of machine oil.
Tips: Use lithium batteries for less headaches and longer life. Put a small piece of tape over the screw holes to keep the mud dauber wasps from plugging them.

title: Intel processer + 2 gig of RAM = FAST
text:
I received this as a Christmas gift. I did all my research here on Amazon, and told my spouse that if he was going to buy me a laptop, this was the one I wanted. And...he got it for me. I don't think he bought it here on Amazon, though.

I have been using an 8" tablet as my primary "laptop" I have the Bluetooth mouse and keyboard & a nice case. However, it was beginning to get tiresome to write emails, or even reviews, because the keyboard was so small, I had to "hunt & peck". I will still use my tablet as our travel computer. I have a bag set up just for it, and all its accessories.

Now. About this Lenovo laptop.

It has 3 USB ports, and one of them is 3.0. Because it has an intel processer, it is even faster than my spouse's new laptop, and this Lenovo has half the RAM. 2 gig to his 4. This laptop also has "expandability"! There is a slot for a Micro SD card. (some people call it a "TIF" card) I put a 128 GB micro card in, and have everything routed to that card. The only things I have loaded on the installed 32 GB drive is the operating system & program files. Everything else is on the micro card. I really don't need more space than that, as I have everything backed up on an external hard drive.

Yes, this laptop is white. That would normally concern me, as I have a bad habit of staining anything white. Clothes, table cloths, towels, etc., are dirty and sometimes ruined as soon as I get them. However, I am really anal about my electronics. I am constantly cleaning them, and I make sure they are protected at all times. Each of my devices is in Pristine condition. Even the old ones. Therefore, I know this will remain white. It also makes it easy to spot. Who knows? Maybe there are "skins" for the outside of this laptop. Not only are skins fun, but they help protect your device.

All in all, I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a light weight (only 2.5 pounds) laptop. This may be light in weight, but it is no light-weight. It runs like the big boys. Sometimes, better.

title: The Computer that Won't Wake Up---with a faulty Trackpad and mediocre Speakers
text:
First off, it's an attractive computer. It's very lightweight, easy to carry around, and the finish is nice (although prone to getting fingerprint markings). I've had it for maybe 2 months now and I didn't have a "big" problem until today. I'm not completely familiar with this computer yet, so I didn't know that we could switch the default Sleep mode to Hibernate---which I preferred--- so whenever I closed my laptop, it automatically went into sleep mode. It used to just wake back up whenever I pressed the power button once, but this morning, I opened the lid and moved the mouse and pressed on the power button and there was just a black screen. I thought perhaps it ran out of juice, so I plugged in the charger. It charged to till the light on the side went from red to green but the screen was still black. I thought I was going to have to send it back to Asus or something, which is not ideal.

So then I pressed on the power button for a few seconds until it shut down and I powered it back up and the screen came back to life. I had to reboot it, as a few reviewers did, and then I purposely put it on sleep mode (both pressing the actual sleep function and closing the lid) to see if it'll still work, but the screen was still black, so I had to reboot both times. It's a hassle. As one reviewer suggested, I went on Settings and changed the default in the "Change what the closing lid does" from Sleep to Shut down for when I press the power button and then to Hibernate for when I press the sleep button and when I close the lid. I don't have this problem with the Hibernate function, just the sleep (for now anyway).

A few days ago I forgot to shutdown my computer and so it went to sleep for a full day and when I picked it up I noticed it was really warm at the bottom, and now I'm having this problem, so coincidence?

As for the trackpad---oh man, this was the main problem with this computer. It has a beautiful matte screen and an okay keyboard, but the trackpad could be A LOT better. There are "smart gestures" and I tried to utilize them and they work fine, but then sometimes when I'm resting my palm by the trackpad and I'm trying to scroll down a page, it misinterprets it and does something else, like maximize my screen (took me a while to get my Google Hangouts chat back to the original size).

Other than the trackpad and the sleep mode, this is a pretty solid computer. It boots up within seconds and has great graphics. It's pretty fast, though I've been living with dinosaur computers, so this is an upgrade for me. And the battery is AWESOME (I get maybe 7 hours from watching shows and movies and having multiple tabs open at once). Oh, and the speakers aren't impressive either (wish they had placed it above the keyboard or something so we could hear better). I'm debating on getting bluetooth speakers, but it's great for earphone users. Overall, I like it. I would still recommend it.

title: Powerful, articulate sound. Hip/Modern aesthetics. Some quirks w/ usability.
text:
Update 1-8-2019: Still working great! One issue I commented on in the first review has been solved. My dog chewed the first remote and Fluance kindly sent out one for free and the issue with range has disappeared. Not sure if it was a faulty remote the first time or they updated the transmitter in the new remotes so they wider reach, either way, the remote does not have any issues from all kinds of angles. Works more like an RF remote.

Original review:
I have the unit setup in the lower level of a decently large town house with bamboo floors. Just about all speaker setups I've setup struggle with the acoustics. Even the warmest sounding speaker/amplifier combos sound more on the side of bright and "echoy"...even with large area rugs. The Fluance Fi70 is no different, but I've come to appreciate it. It's really a beautiful looking piece of furniture. With the grill on, most people ask, "what is that?" I custom made a laptop stand to raise up the laptop over the touch buttons.

Even though this is a large unit (giggity) it doesn't really have the same spatial intrusiveness as a pair of large floor speakers, but still puts out an identical amount of output. It's confusing actually how Fluance sound engineers have managed to create such a large sound stage, and bass output, with such a compact (BUT HEAVY) system. Other reviewers who say ,"this unit lacks base" <-- notice they misspelled 'bass', must have it setup incorrectly, have a faulty unit, or have a terrible source connected to the unit. I run (2) 12" subwoofers in my daily driver so I am accustomed to heavy bass. Point being, the output, even when the bass is set at "0" (goes up to "8" I think) is too much. I often leave the bass at -2. The mid-range frequencies are going to take some time to get used to, some burn in period not only with the drivers, but with our ears learning to recognize and properly process the sound "the burn in period". Once some decent listening time is invested, the unit becomes alive. Mids articulate, highs are clean with plenty of sparkle. Minimal listener fatigue once broken in.

Usability:
Quirks: An effort needs to made to have the remote work within the appropriate range. As others have mentioned, the touch button features on top of the unit are not great. It takes learning and finesse to master the top buttons, but I still find myself disappointed with the lack of intuitiveness, HOWEVER, this unit is only $500, so it will not be perfect. Most guest estimate the unit is above $1,000.

title: Very nice, and a steal for the price!
text:
I saw that these are on sale ($79) and purchased them for a dedicated home theater room I'm building. The product description is not really clear enough that these are intended to be surround speakers, so if you purchased them for two-channel listening you might be disappointed. Why? Well, these are very shallow (only about 4" deep) cabinets that are made to wall mount. They have metal keyhole hangers on the back to make them easy to securely hang. Being such a small cabinet and being sealed (no port), the bass response does not go very low. It's rated down to only 100 hz, though I feel that it goes lower than that. But the speaker is very well balanced between highs and lows, and the tweeter is quite nice. To achieve tonal balance in such a tiny box, the engineers had to attenuate the tweeter, which means that the speaker has a pretty low efficiency rating. That's not necessarily a problem, you just need some power to drive it. But most home theater receivers would have adequate juice to drive this speaker as a surround.

Being used as intended in a surround application; it would typically be used with a subwoofer in the system. Having a sub to bring out the bottom end takes away any deficiencies this speaker has. It's perfectly acceptable to cross a surround speaker at 100 hz or so, so this speaker should perform nicely in such an application.

I'm listening to them now as a stereo pair, and they sound very pleasant even without a sub, though I would want one if this turned into a long term use.

Out of the box, the build quality is very nice and they are quite hefty to be so small. When I first hooked them up I was not immediately impressed. The lows sounded muddy and the highs were lacking. But even after an hour of playing, the lows have smoothed out and the tweeter has awoken. So be sure to give these guys plenty of break-in time before judging. I would suggest at least 20 hours or so. Low efficiency speakers usually need lots of play time to loosen up and sound their best.

I'll update my review once I get the home theater installed and have them playing as actual surrounds.

Good listening!

text:
As it took me quite a bit of effort to figure this out, I’ve drawn up a quick schematic of my setup. In my case, I have a [[ASIN:B00HTYBPGI Panlong Digital Optical Audio Splitter 3-Way Signal Amplifier (SPDIF / Toslink 1 In to 3 Out)]] to simultaneously send the audio stream from the TV to [[ASIN:B00F4ORTZ6 Orei DA21X Premium Optical SPDIF/Coaxial Digital to RCA L/R Analog Audio Converter with 3.5mm Jack Support Headphone/Speaker Outputs]], and a set of [[ASIN:B004M18O60 Logitech Surround Sound Speaker System Z906]]. I’m using the Orei converter to connect a wireless headset that only has 3.5mm Input. The reason for this is to be able to have the audio playing over the surround speakers, regardless of the source, but also to be able to mute the 5.1 speakers and use the wireless headset at night so that other people can sleep... It must be said that for this to be practical, you need to turn the TV volume all the way down, because otherwise you would have 2 volume adjustments: the TV and the surround speakers. But the actual volume setting of the TV itself does not affect the volume of the Digital Optical Audio Out.
Here the icing on the cake was finding a wireless headset that doesn’t “live” on the transmitter, as most do (i.e. close to the TV): I chose the [[ASIN:B00FJISZBE Sony MDRHW300K Digital Wireless Headphones]]. Like this I can have the actual headset in my bed side table (it charges via USB) and when the need arises, just mute the surround speakers and continue listening on the headset, all without having to move my lazy butt… And as the headset has its own volume adjustment, you’re all set :-)

title: 4.75 Stars
text:
Bought 2 of these, front door and back door; they install very easily. Just follow the videos within the app and you can't go wrong. We don't have a wired doorbell so we only had our phones to notify us of the doorbell and motion activity so we added a Chime to the living room to accompany the Ring for both front and back doors-works wonderfully.

The camera is pretty good, but there is a slight delay in sound when either the motion or doorbell is activated. The clarity of the picture is not very good within the first couple of seconds of activation, but after about 3 seconds, the picture clears up very well (compare pics attached). The 180 degree view is wonderful; the night vision picture is very good quality. Because our porch is sort an alcove, the lighting outside the porch is very bright, almost blinding, but based on other reviews I've read, if I get customer service to adjust this, then the picture within the porch will be darker and not as good, so I'll just keep it the way it is.

The motion sensor is VERY sensitive; more so than expected, almost to the point that it is annoying. We live on a very busy street where the curb is about 20 feet away from our porch so the total distance is about 25 feet away from the Ring; we have scaled back our proximity sensor to 20 feet and still got lots of "ghost" motion from the cars. We went back to 15 feet and got the same results, just less often. We finally scaled back down to about 5 feet and didn't get anything other than someone walking onto our porch, but by the time the sensor senses someone, they're already faced away from the camera and facing the driveway so we wouldn't be able to see their face. so because of this, we went ahead and opened our proximity back up to about 8-10 feet but have to deal with the passing cars setting off the motion sensors, even though the street is about 15-20 feet outside this zone. For this issue, I would deduct 1/4 of a star. (you can see a vehicle that activated our motion sensor in the pic attached)

If we could rate based on fractions of stars, I would give Ring 4.75 stars at this point only because of the overly sensitive motion sensor, but I'd rather it be more sensitive than not work at all!

I would definitely recommend Ring to everyone, and I actually do this all the time!!!

title: Be sure it's the size you need!
text:
This is a great bag. Even though I returned it, that was only because I couldn't get it to hold my 70-200mm f28 lens on or off my camera without it either being too tight, or giving up too much of the internal space. That was my fault though, I thought I had ordered the 450 AW, but I ordered the 350 AW by mistake. While I had it though, here were my observations....

1. It's spacious. Lot of room, every bit as roomie as the description says. The inside is pretty customizable, and a whole lot of the little dividers are included (likely more than you will be able to use), but the main ones are pretty well set where they need to be from the get go. You can rearrange them, but you could lose your quick access points if you do, at least one or two. Not always a bad thing, unless you want to be able to load multiple bodies with lenses on them, and want to be able to take them out at any given moment. The extra dividers aren't very well padded, but I don't think they need to be. They are there to keep your lenses from banging into each other, and they do that jsut fine. The main dividers, as well as the outside of the inner compartment, are very well padded.
2. MOLLE design is awesome! Not sure if it fits the bill as a true MOLLE, but it has the extra straps on the outside that you can attach things too, and it includes some pretty good ones - A water bottle pouch, an accessory bag, a tripod pouch and 2 straps. All can be placed however you want to make them work, and there is room to add more. However, according to their website, Lowepro is not currently offering these accessories on their own. Also, the tripod pouch is only big enough to fit one leg of the tripod into it, which works, but isn't as good as others I've seen.
3. The only real bad thing I have to say about this bag is the padding on the straps isn't as good as I would hope. This is why I took off a star, as I would imagine if you wore this over a stretch of time, it would get uncomfortable. I know my 450 AW does, but to be fair, the type of gear I carry in that is heavier than what is likely to be carried in the 350.
4. A side note - the all weather cover does not detach from the bag, and will make it hard to dry out if you ever need to use it. Not worth a star off, but worth a mention.

So unless you have long lenses, this bag is pretty useful overall. Here is a list of all the stuff I fit in the bag...

Canon T3i, 18-55mm, 55-250mm with hood reversed, 10-18mm wide with hood reversed, 60mm macro, 430EX II flash with diffuser and flashbender, 2 batteries and the charger, a filter case with CPLs and UVs for my three sizes of accessory mounts (58,67,77), spare lens caps, tripod tools, manuals for the camera and flash, camera strap, cleaning supplies (blower, cleaning cloths, bottle of cleaning solution; all stuffed into the accessory bag), and various other little things.

Even with all that in there, there was still room for more lenses, and maybe even another body. I didn't have a laptop to put in it to test it, so I used that as extra space to put my strap and my flashbender. With all this, I jsut couldn't get my 70-200mm lens into it, but it's not meant for that, so no worries there. If you have need to load longer lenses, especially attached to the camera, then get the 450 AW instead (I have that one now, and it does work for that). Otherwise, this would be a great bag for anyone else! I recommend.

Thanks for reading my review!

title: NOT THE PRODUCT I WAS HOPING FOR~  But thank goodness for returns and refunds!
text: I pre-ordered mine and was super excited to receive it promptly on Sept 30th, I ordered a case as well as the san disk of which I have yet to receive, no problem anyway don't need it as I'm returning my tablet. Huge disappointment to say the least, I have the second generation tablet fire HD7 and the Fire 8.9 both excellence products so I had high expectations for the newest member the fire HD 10~ first issue I encountered was the power button I had to push the button 4 times before it would fire up, then there was a problem with installation and backup, I have a lot of books and music on my original fire HD7 tablet it being my first kindle tablet I made the most of it I have to say I have never encountered any issues that couldn't be fixed and am still enjoying to this day.  the second issue with the fire HD 10 was loading, freezing, connection, and re-start issues, I have the same games on my fire HD7 and 8.9 DHX kindle when I installed the same game to the fire HD 10 I encountered loading, freezing, lost connection and re-start issues,  I had to call customer service to load my books and the tech guy of whom I had to talk to in costa rica was difficult to understand I had to keep asking him to repeat himself,  it took a very long time and I was instructed to do a hard re-set only after a few times did we manage to enable the books to download before that I couldn't open them,  I called customer service the next day and asked them to send me out another fire HD 10, I explained the issues I was encountering with the fire HD 10 and she had another sent out the very next day I thought maybe I got a dud Hey! it happens!  I needed to compare the new one which BTW was delivered in a soft brown wrapper instead of a box and the packaged was torn thank you!!  :(  I let the new fire HD 10 go through the cycle of downloads and backups which I thought went more smoothly then the first fire HD 10 that had been sent out I also fired up my fire HD7 and the 8.9HDX so I had 4 tablets going of course my first 2 gave me no problems what so ever (I knew they wouldn't)  then comparisons to all 4 in terms of loading and connection issues both fire HD10 failed to meet the standards that the new fire HD 10 claims, I'm returning both plus the case when Amazon comes to their senses and redesigns the fire HD 10 to comply with the claims  they make then I'll just leave well enough alone.  and what's with the power button? its like you need to hold it before the tablet will fire up and compared to my second generation fire HD 7 and my 8.9HDX this one failed,  sorry Amazon you'll have to do a heck of a lot better than the fire HD10 before I shell out big bucks for another dud!!  I've been a prime member for a long time and enjoy the many benefits, I'm only giving you my honest opinion.  if you revamp the fire HD10 I might give it another try but for now I have to pass,  and having customer service send out another one to help me figure out if it was just the first one being a dud or what now I know.  thank you for reading my review and to those who make the decision to buy one hope it works out better for you than it did  for me.  sorry for any miss-spelled words hope you understood what I was trying to convey.

title: They should be called dual driver on ear, but details, you know?
text: [[ASIN:B0798TVDVJ 1MORE Triple Driver Over-Ear Headphones Comfortable Foldable Earphones with Hi-Res Hi-Fi Sound, Bass Driven, Tangle-Free Detachable Cable for Smartphones/Android/PC/Tablet - Silver/Titanium]]So I was in search of a pair of cans when I traveled, but really couldn't set my mind on anything. The Bluetooth Sonys? No, too expensive for the noise canceling. (though that could come in handy for plane rides) The MX50s? Purchased those and sold them right away! Hmmmm, on ears? Triple drivers? (realistically dual drivers with a passive driver, but whatever) Sure, let's give these a chance. Oh boy I'm glad I did! Not only do they fold up nice and small for traveling, man these things are nice! The ceramic tweeter gives the highs very smooth clarity without piercing your eardrums, while the main driver only has to worry about bass and mids and it shows. For me I can just almost notice the separation between the two, kinda like a feeling more than actually hearing it, but the two drivers do blend and mix together nicely! Pretty tight and solid bass, and really clear. The sound stage is fairly wide for how small these little closed backs are so if you like to game on the road, these won't disappoint either. Very easy to drive as well. I am in love with One More now, and plan on buying something else from them in the future. Depending on what they come up with next :) I also should say that the comfort is out of this world as well! I had these on for hours a few days in a row, and only by the third day, probably 20+ hours my ears started to get a little sore. The material they use, and the padding is super soft and you don't notice them on your ears. Trust me, the thought of on ears scared me a bit. If you're washing dishes, raking outside, being productive at all your ears will sweat, but that also depends on how much work you're doing. I have about a dozen different cans, and if I'm active my ears sweat anyway so there's that I guess. Sitting for a few hours my ears got slightly damp? Not overheated, hot, or flat out sweaty, but there was a little moisture on the pads. I also love the look!

title: Great little passive heat sink, for the right build
text:
Great little heat sink.
It's designed to pull heat away from your processor passively.
So, it relies on ambient airflow though your case.

Which means it's great for a HTPC build (Quiet!), provided you buy a proper case for it.

Sadly, the manufactures spec is a little wrong.
It clams it can fit a skylak 1151 socket.
The mount pins line up, however, the bottom is perfectly square.

Which means it in fact does NOT fit into a 1151 socket, as motherboards tend to put capacitors in that space.
I am using a Asus Maximus VIII Gene Motherboard.

The company this was purchased from was very cool about refunding my money, given the add is wrong.
Thank you!

title: Otterbox Symmetry vs Speck Presidio Grip vs Pelican Protector vs Thule Atmos X3
text:
Get this case if you want a good compromise between function/style/price/protection. It's protective for drops but not too thick.

I've tried the Speck Presidio Grip and really did not like it because it hasn't been improved since the Candyshell besides being made thinner. In reality, there's very little grip, the rubber shows wear, the thin plastic piece above the lightning port is weak and flimsy just like the Speck Candyshell and will break over time, and the one I received has a bulbous back in the middle just like the Candyshell and therefore would not sit flat on a table and also would make creaking sounds with use because it just wasn't a good fit. I really did not like that case!

I've also tried the Pelican Protector which is a similar case to the Otterbox Symmetry and Speck Presidio. In terms of function/style/price protection, it's a good buy. It's protective and not too thick. The Pelican Protector and Otterbox Symmetry are about the same thickness. The Speck Presidio is perhaps a little thinner which I did not like because it was actually harder to hold. But back to the Pelican Protector, this is a perfectly good case choice. I personally prefer the Otterbox Symmetry because it's black all the way around with no gray accent color, and I also like the Otterbox Symmetry feel slightly better, but the Pelican Protector is a perfectly good case that I'd also recommend.

Lastly, the Otterbox Symmetry is the one I'll be sticking with. Buttons are responsive. It's protective but not too bulky. The plastic material is "somewhat" grippy. I've had such a hard time finding a "grippy" case that I find attractive and with good drop protection, and this one seems to fit the bill as of right now. My previous favorite case on the market for the iPhone 6 and 6s was the Thule Atmos X3, but as of September 2016 it isn't out yet and I don't see myself getting the iPhone 7 version because I don't like the redesign for the iPhone 7 which has metallic buttons and odd cutouts on the bottom near the speakers (used to just be flat across the bottom). But despite the visual design changes, I think that will also be a very good choice for people as it served me incredibly well for drops and daily use in the past while still not being too thick at all.

title: AudioEngine 5+ a Winner!
text: I purchased a set of Audioengine A5+ powered speakers on October 15th. They arrived two days later sitting on my front porch in a big box. Thank God no one ripped them off the porch while I was out having lunch. UPS just leaves stuff on your porch now. In the inner city that is very dangerous. They just shouldn't do that with a $469.00 dollar item, but that aside, I have my speakers. The speakers are packaged as described with layer after layer of cardboard, foam, fabric and plastic. The fabric is overkill if you ask me. I just don't need a tote bag for every item. What can I do with them now. It's a shame to just throw that away, but what use is it. I would have been satisfied with plastic only and a lower price. I can report the AudioEngine 5+ speakers do sound great. They can get loud and still sound clean and crisp. As reported in other reviews, the build quality is superb. I purchased the bamboo versions, and they are very nice. Not a flaw in the assembly or finish of the $70.00 dollar wood option. They are substantial and well constructed. I like the internal power supply and detachable power cord. My new speakers replaced an older Klipsch ProMedia 2.1 setup, which I was forced to retire after the subwoofer amp died. Klipsch doesn't service the amp, and the third party repair place wanted $75.00 to repair it, plus shipping and handling. To ship the woofer to them would have cost money too, so servicing a unit that was $150.00 dollars new, just didn't make sense. I thought of just replacing the unit with a new Promedia 2.1, but they are now discontinued, and I found many reports of other dead sub-woofer amps. Another promedia 2.1 was nixed!  The Audioengine 2+ is closest in spec to the promedia 2.1, but I chose to step it up a bit and got the 5+.  It is a bigger set of speakers, but the bigger power amplifier is worth it. My desktop is a bit crowded now, but I like the sound. The 5+ has better bass than the speakers I had (without a functioning sub-woofer), but I miss the deep bass of a sub. The 5+ has good flat response down to about 200Hz. That's where it falls off. There is nothing below 100hz to impress your friends, so a sub-woofer must be in your plans, down the road. I plan to save up for the audioengine S8 or Cerwin Vega, or maybe a Klipsch sub. I haven't decided. I wish audio engine packaged the amp portion of the 5+ in a box like the N22 product. I realized after setting up my new 5+ set that I no longer have a headphone jack as I did with the Klipsch Promedia 2.1.  So what is one to do? I could buy the audio engine D-1 D.A.C., but that is so expensive for just a headphone jack. Besides, then I will have three volume controls. One in the computer software, one on the DAC and one on the left speaker. How confusing!  If Audioengine would just build an N55 (hint, hint) with the 50 watt power capacity and an internal power supply, I hate the big brick power supply concept of the N22, I could have purchased a set of passive P4N speakers, and a subwoofer, had my headphone jack, and been able to mount the speakers up on the bookshelf. Audioengine should sell the right passive speaker of the 5+ as a set of passive 5" speakers. The enclosure without the power supply, as it is in the right speaker, must make for a better speaker. There is more space to resonate. I would buy that once they design the N55 amp! That would have freed up space on my desk. The 5+ speakers are not small. But they sure sound good.  One thing I wonder about, why does the 5+ speaker system have the port on the rear, where the same basic designed P4N speakers have the port on the front?  Is the port better on the front or rear?  The endless rotation of the volume control of the 5+ is a problem. I realize this concept is common for digital volume controls as you find in cars and other modern equipment. It is necessary with the use of a remote control. However, you never know where the volume is set.  I would prefer a digital readout of level instead of a power light. The power lamp could just relate to volume. Bright is loud, dim is low. Off could be dim / blinking. One last comment. Why is there no bamboo option for the S8 subwoofer? I wish I could buy a matching sub-woofer for my fabulous 5+'s. Bottom line, you will be happy with a set of audioengine 5+ speakers.

title: 5 Gbps network connection and drag-and-drop?  Yes please!  BSODs, hard-freezes, and other shenanigans?  Uh, no...
text:
To clarify what this product actually does:
A) Creates a network connection between two PCs over USB 3.0. This. Is. Awesome! (when it works)
B) Also allows the ability to control the other PC's keyboard and mouse input from a single keyboard/mouse in a KVM-ish/LogMeIn-ish way by moving the mouse cursor to the right of the host PC. Files can also be dragged and dropped between PCs (also pretty cool), and doesn't seem to actually use the TCP/IP connection established in A) above (or at least it doesn't show any network activity in Task Manager when transferring files through the drag-and-drop method).

The reason I'm deducting two stars is because of driver instability. I've had the driver Blue-Screen Windows 8.1 and hard-freeze Windows 7 multiple times. This could be from USB 3.0 power draw--when I used USB 3.0 powered hubs on both PCs, things were a lot more stable.

Transferring files using Method B) only exacerbates the instability--this is when you're most likely to get a BSOD or hard freeze. To reduce the chance of instability, use Method A) and transfer through a file share.

As for actual speeds? Well you're really only going to see the benefit if you're not bottlenecked by anything else (like mechanical storage).

I would recommend this cable only if you want the convenience of drag and drop, have additional USB 3.0 hubs to offset power issues, and are okay with the occasional BSOD or hard freeze. If you're buying this for super-high speed file transfers, you better have SSDs. Otherwise just stick to Gigabit Ethernet.

j5create: If you want a more positive review, fix your drivers and/or this product's power draw! Better yet, add a Y-cable to one or both ends to help with power issues!

UPDATE: 7/2/2015: I tried Method A to do Hyper-V VM live migrations between two servers that have USB 3.0 cards in them. Transfer speed hovers between 1.1 and 1.4 Gbps, which is nice! The important part is that it's STABLE!

I thought about adding a star to the review, but since this product is advertised to do Method B, and it still has BSODs, disconnects, etc. with that, I'm keeping it at 3 stars.

I took the stock ones off and got a set of 9dbi antenna's to replace them with. my neighbor that is about 90 feet up the street, can get a signal from me, and that is through 2 houses too. I am not saying a great signal, but a signal that connects is still a signal. that is with the new 9dbi antennas.. I did not check with the stock ones. It does not have annoying lights on the front, or really bright ones either, like a lot of devices seen to have these days. they lights that are on the front are easy to see, but also easy to ignore too.

The complaints that I do have with it is more in the software then on how good it works. These are some features that some other brands have had that this one does not. It requires a password, but no user name.. so that drops security to get into it in half right there. If you dont have to much to worry about, when it comes to people getting into the setup on yours, like if you have WEP or whatever security enabled, this will be less of an issue, but if you leave yours open, then this might be more of an issue.

What I do is set mine up for mac filtering, add the mac addresses of the devises I want to be able to connect, and then select, only let the devices in the mac address list to be able to connect wireless. This is one place that I dont like the setup. Even though it is easy to get into it to add them, there is no place to distinguish one device from the next. So say for example, you have a cell phone, and loose the cell phone, or break it, and have to get another, you may want to remove the mac listing from the list.. but how do you do it if you dont remember which mac address was for that device? or say you have a child, and you want them to get off the net, and they dont listen, or try to sneak on when grounded. Well, if you knew which mac address was theirs, you could just click to disable that one device.. but not having and description box for each mac make it harder to keep track of what device is for what mac address.

Next is there is no reboot. Granted, you really should not need to reboot it very often, but if for some reason you do want to, you have to manually pull the power plug to do it. I have had others that had a reboot feature in the software. There is no status up time on it either. If you wanted to see how long it has been on for some reason, you can not. This comes into play, say, it something starts glitching, and you want to see if the device and been rebooted, or rebooted itself for some reason, or... if you can see the up time, then you would know, but that is a small feature that is left out of the software. there is also no info about connections either. If someone has been connected to the router, there is no way to tell how much they have been on it, how much data they have downloaded, or anything else. the only thing that they have about any connection use, is they will tell you how much time left you have on your IP lease. which can tell you how long ago it was that you connected to the router. and there is the info on that page too, that tells what your computer name is. No other info is there for you to get any other info about you though. Like I said, very limited on information. My last router, i could tell how much a certain computer has used the internet, how much data was downloaded by them, and much more. this one just seems to lack all the details about things. Oh yea, and that DCHP info, about who has a lease on an IP address.. well that is under local network, not the wireless tab too.

In case you are wondering, there are times where I will leave my wireless open for neighbors that do not have internet. and when i do, as long as they dont abuse the privilege, I may leave it that way for a time. But, if I see that someone is constantly thrashing my network, it would be nice to know who is doing it. just by simply being able to see how much data they have used, I can tell who did it. There are other things too, so that is just one example. so yes, these features can come in handy too. Like I said, they just did not seem to think about putting in most features that are not needed features. I guess they consider those other features, a luxury.

All of the main, basic features are there though, like changing the speed that anyone can connect to it at, WEP, WPA, WPA2, etc security, the tons of little things that most people never touch, the ability of blocking both times, and services, or even URL's. Like I said, the basic stuff that most people dont use.

yea, i know, this is only wireless G, but for me, that is more then enough. Right now, I only have 20 meg down, and when time warner upgrades their service in my area, My plan will go up to 100 meg down, but when it comes down to it, for basic use, unless you are doing high end gaming, or doing things like torrents wirelessly, you really dont need faster then a 54meg connection to the internet. so it is not really a big deal. Even things like streaming services like netflix, only uses something like 4 meg down at best. at least that is the best setting that I can get that is available to me. that means you could have 10 people streaming video's at the same time, and still have much room to spare. Like I said, most average people do not need more then 54 meg down.

Setup was very easy, and you can do it, even from a factory hard reset, without any disks too. Just simply connect your computer to the router through an ethernet cord, go to your web browser, and type in the IP address of the router in the web browser, and make any changes. No need to use install software, so if you loose the install disk, it is not a big deal. There is descriptions for all the setting built right in, so no need to look things up, or look for manuals if you are trying to figure out what a setting does.. It is right there on the side. If it is not, then there is a "more" link that you can click that will open another web page for you to view that info in.

As for the antenna's, if you want to remove them, there is a plastic cap over the base of the antenna. Straighten the antenna for easier grip, then grab that plastic base, and just turn like you would a nut.. It will unscrew off, and if the antenna does not come off with it, then just unscrew the antenna too.

Overall, this is a good router, and seems well made. i hope it lasts me for years to come too. I just wish that it had more info about things. So would I recommend it.. yes.. as long as its limitations do not bother you. so far, it has been a good reliable little router.

--------------------------------------------------

Update.

I have found a little more info about this that I did not realize. First, you always hear that wireless G is up to 54Mb speeds, but what they do not advertise is this. First, that 54 is both way communication. So that means, you max out at 27Mb up, and 27Mb down. On top of that, that 27 is total, not just info. Meaning, overhead, security info, etc, is included in that 27. It is not just data. So the data speed will be closer to around 21 Mb speeds. and that is on a good connection. This is more then fine for someone with a low internet speed, someone just surfing the net, etc. But if you get 50Mb down internet speeds, don't expect to get the full use of it on this router. Mine started glitching out, so I just upgraded to an N router as I also upgraded my internet speeds too. Just don't forget, if you do upgrade your modem in aspects of higher speeds, you will also need to make sure that you have a wireless N adapter in your device too, or it will not improve your speeds any.

title: I love these headphones and would have given them a 5 ...
text:
I love these headphones and would have given them a 5 star rating except for one major flaw. The battery reporting is seriously flawed. I have been testing the battery life and it starts out OK with "Battery High" then it drops to "Battery Medium" and stays there for a while, the problem is it doesn't report "Battery Low" at all - it goes straight to "Battery VERY Low". For example I went to the gym this morning - at 8am I turned on the headset and it reported "Battery Medium" - at 8:16am it reported "Battery Life VERY low", 2 minutes later it shutdown. That's less than 20 minutes from Medium to Shutdown!

Battery High - reports this when about 80-100% power remaining 12-15 hours left
Battery Medium - reports this from about 1%-79% power remaining - 20 minutes to 9 hours remaining
Battery Very Low - reports this from 0-1% power remaining with about 0-10 minutes remaining

It's not that it doesn't have good battery life, the problem is that you should get a low battery warning with 1-2 hours of time left so you could finish whatever you're doing before it needs charging. But when you turn the unit on and it reports "Battery Life Medium" you don't know if you have 9 hours or 9 minutes left before shutdown.

title: Solid, Reliable Dual Camera in One Package
text:
I purchased and received this dash cam along with the suggested SD card bundle within the last week. Used it a little bit over the last couple of days and was satisfied with the results so far. The dual cameras in one integrated package is what made me purchase this item. The visual quality is not quite what I had hoped for but there's always going to be a trade off between how wide the view is and how detailed the images are, especially away from the center of the image. This dash-camera strikes a reasonable balance. I was able to read the license plates of vehicles in front of me in my lane on the roadway from both day and night video but it was difficult (not possible) to read license plates from cars further from the center of the image.

I've also used the TimaCam app (iOS version) that works with this dash-cam and it is adequate. I was disappointed that the app is not fully integrated into the other major apps on my phone, so it takes a couple of extra steps to download videos to the Camera Roll or connect to the cam's internal Wi-Fi network. Not a big deal and both of these features are available but it takes 2-3 extra steps to do them. I did like that all of the major settings for the dash-cam can be changed from within the app. That was easier for me than using the interface on the dash-cam.

Things I liked:
+ Dual cameras in one package
+ 4K available in single-camera mode
+ Good picture quality in day and adequate at night
+ Reliable operation
+ Multiple mounting options included in the box (came in handy when I installed the first mount pointing the wrong direction...)
+ Good audio quality
+ Position/Direction of both camera lenses can be adjusted without dismounting the unit
+ The battery seems adequate
+ All major cam system settings can be modified from the app (at least on iOS)
+ The Wi-Fi password is displayed on the screen when Wi-Fi mode starts so you don't have to worry about losing/forgetting it

Things that could be improved:
- The symbols on the buttons don't seem to be very intuitive. I have to look at the manual each time I want to do something (till I get more practice)
- The app integration is not as strong as it could be on iOS
- The "feel" of the plastic housing and buttons does not seem very durable (wouldn't take a drop on a hard surface well). As far as normal use I don't see this being an issue as you don't really need to use the buttons to operate the device.
- The screen always turns on automatically when the device powers on. A setting to keep the screen off by default and only use the status lights to know the device is recording would be nice. This would be helpful because in my region it is against the law to have an electronic screen mounted
- Addition of some type of security feature to prevent unauthorized playback, access to video if the device is lost/stolen/seized

title: Compact, functional, useful.
text:
I got this too use as a bench power supply for small electronics projects. These projects don't require a precision instrument, so this tiny unit fills the bill perfectly.

The case is a little tricky to assemble. The six pieces plus two buttons have to be aligned correctly with tabs inserted and then held together with two screws. If you have trouble getting the pieces to stay together, some painter's tape will work to keep things in place until you get the screws in.

One of the buttons was too large to fit through the hole in the case. I was able to file it down to fit in a couple of minutes.

I used a 19 volt power supply from an old laptop. I cut the barrel connector off, stripped the wires and tinned the ends with a soldering iron. They were a bit too thick to fit in the connectors, but crimping them with pliers fixed the problem.

As can be seen in the photos, the output voltage runs a bit higher than indicated on the screen. This is inconsequential for my projects, but if necessary, you can hook the power supply up to a meter and adjust to offset to the exact voltage.

Great product, at an excellent price. Just for grins I added a photo of the computer power supply and adapter this unit replaces. At about 5% of the size and weight, my workbench is much happier.

title: Best you can do for the price
text:
It was this or plugging an OPPO into my 11 year old unit or a soundbar. Wanted to buy at Amazon, like their service, but when I walked into another store it was 349$!!!.
Could not believe it. Can't pass that up, cheaper than open box, even after tax. Sorry Amazon, but I'm poor.
Anyway this is a nice little piece of kit, original MSRP was around 600$, and its about that good, but a few words about the problems first.
The USB played my 500gb drive well, then just quit, still plays other stuff, don't want to do the reset just yet.
Design flaws, some not unique to Onkyo.
Two Component inouts, both are worthless, as they only pass 480i and 5 something or other, the pic is as good as composite, so why bother?
How about a detachable power cord instead? Or better amps? And a zone two line out, also worthless.
If it was a pre out, great, hook up an amp to the front two channels, for music. But its a LINE OUT, like the tape out on older receivers, supposed to be used to run
a signal to another "zone", so just how far can you run a line signal? twenty feet? thirty?
More expense that could have been spent elsewhere, especially since there's' a powered zone two, apart from all of the other channels.
And AM\FM tuners were already a joke, how long before they figure out that the great streaming on this unit will pick up everything with better sound anyway?
And now the good.
Great surround receiver, and good for listening in a non critical fashion. Being of audiophile pretensions, this is not for serious audio, but not what its built for.
The clock radio amps in this thing have an audible distortion rate, but that's not real world, just don't put it in too large a room.
And since you can't put an amp on it, I would strongly suggest you do what's called "BI-AMPING", that is if your speakers allow it..
Ever since the industry has insisted on cramming seven or more amps (one amp split up into seven with a distribution scheme) I have made use of this feature, and where it might run outta steam with one amp on each front channel, sounds a lot better with two running each one.
You have to say goodbye to the latest gimmick from Dolby labs, but trust me, you can live without it, with bi-amping this unit works well without much strain.
The networking is where it shines, I ran cat cable to it, and my computer, and my new BLU ray, and I run it from my tablet with Wi-Fi.
If you get the APP, I suggest the Integra version, it has this classy brushed metal look to it. Between it and my Panny app I can run my Bluray,
my DVD recorder, my old DVD AUDIO player that passes for a reference CD player, and my Panasonic 55".
The remote works well for a remote that uses codes, but there is no record or eject buttons.
No macros either, of course, but the only macro I used was one that turns on my TV and receiver, and if you hit the "tv power" button " that is what happens, so I'm covered there.
Minor but important things, computer video fits the screen perfect, DSD from my SACD discs is close to amazing, switching between inputs is whisper quite..
I was going to try to make my eleven year old Integra work, but glad its my preamp in my audio system now, this little unit was well worth the
initial price point of six hundred bucks, at the price its going for, its a steal, the surround sound is great, its use as a media hub is pretty much seamless, and ready for 4K, just get an audio system for music if that's your thing, but at moderate to semi loud levels this thing sounds really good.
Don't know about quality of build yet, but I have had two Integra's, Onkyo's best , one lasted eleven years and still going strong, one lasted three years when the HDMI board fried. So so far its fifty fifty with Onkyo products.
Fingers crossed.
Big wide smile.

title: Built well
text:
I have both this (10.1") and Tontec's 7" displays. My reviews for both are similar because an important component of these units is the video driver board. Both use the same video driver board (details below).

This is a very well built unit. I had purchased several different OEM video solutions for an in-car navigation system that I built. This unit had the best connectors out of the bunch.

This works perfectly with a Raspberry Pi, Beaglebone, or other DIY systems that use either an AV, HDMI, or VGA ports. I've tested it on Ubuntu 12 and Ubuntu 14 systems. The resolution is automatically set to 1280x800 (16:10). Strangely, the OS "recognizes" this as a 'Liyama North America' 17" screen. The screen resolution and ratios are perfect. Rotation using Ubuntu's screen settings (for example, to portrait mode) also works well.

The screen quality is good. The driver board automatically switches from HDMI input to AV input when that source has a signal. (For example, when using a rear-view camera in your car.) The specs are provided by the seller in the link which is very appreciated. My only wish is that it had audio output from the HDMI signal, but this isn't enough to rate it any less than 5-stars.

One minor gripe about this display compared with its 7" counterpart is the orientation of the connector jack on the back of the display. The 7" display's jack faced inwards, allowing to easily hide the wires behind the screen. On this display, the jack faces outwards at the bottom of the display. This causes the wires to slightly protrude from the bottom. This isn't a problem if your project doesn't need an absolutely flush edge, or if you have space behind a bevel to hide the wires. Hopefully, this is an easy fix.

If using for a backup camera application, run a +12V line from the car's reverse taillights to the ACC pin on the board. (Look at the back of the board to find which pin is the ACC pin. It is the pin closest to the edge of the board near the AV input jack.) This will automatically switch the board from any of the other inputs (e.g. HDMI) to the AV2 input where the backup camera is plugged, whenever the car is put into reverse.

Also, if you are going to use this in a car, I would suggest running electric tape over the connector on the back of the display. Although it is built and connected well, it is a good idea to re-inforce it just in case you hit those potholes.

The infrared remote control mimics the functions available on the button board. The buttons are as follows:
S1 = Power, S2=Menu/Select, S3=Down, S4=Up, S5=Video Source Select

This size display is perfect for DIY makers working on custom projects. I would love to see a touchscreen overlay for this sized screen since I think it is perfect for touch applications such as a DIY tablet, home automation/security, OEM equipment console, etc.

The video driver board is also known as PCB800099. It was hard to find information on this board, especially how to get the reverse camera working automatically. So, here are some useful links for this board:

Firmware: http://www.elecrealm.com/down/upload/20131119/1384860772.rar
Software for upgrading the firmware: http://www.elecrealm.com/down/upload/20131117/1384673829.rar
Specification: http://www.elecrealm.com/down/html/?47.html
User guide: http://www.elecrealm.com/down/html/?40.html

title: Disappointed.
text:
Pros: Looks great and feels well-made. Was shipped quickly and in sufficient packaging.

Cons: Loses around 90% of reception compared to the OEM antenna.

Conclusion: Buy a taller antenna instead, unless you only want to listen to a few stations.

Long explanation: Bought this little antenna for our Sienna after the stock one came off in an automatic car wash. (Oops) I couldn't find a cheap OEM replacement, but after reading the many positive reviews about the stubby antenna, I decided to go for it. That was a mistake.

It was really easy to install this thing; it just screwed right in. However, I noticed very little difference between using the antenna and the reception without any antenna. In fact, I noticed no difference at all. However, as soon as I touch it with my hand, a station that was only static before cleans right up and I can enjoy the music. Basically, the person riding in the passenger seat would need to roll down the window and hold the antenna while driving around.

Although the antenna doesn't pick up any of my favorite stations, it does pick up a few stations with very tall or close towers. But those stations already came in, even without using an antenna.

I'm not sure why I thought this purchase would be a good idea. The height of an antenna has a huge impact on its reception. Don't make the same mistake I did. Buy a taller antenna.

title: Not Your Average USB Charger
text:
I am a computer reseller and I purchased this Smart Charger at the recommendation of a colleague.

Here's the story: If you have multiple items (such as Smartphones, Tablets, smart watches, etc.) this is a very interesting device. Most tablets (and some iPhones and new Samsung phones, I think) require at least 2A (amps) to get the device(s) charged in a reasonable time. Other Smartphones and watches require only 1-1.5A. As a result, it's important to use the correct charger for each device.

JideTech's Smart Charger solves the problem and eliminates the guesswork: Simply plug in your USB cable into ANY of the 4 ports and this device will automatically detect and choose the correct amperage for charging. AND, you can charge up to 4 devices at once. For "techies" (OK, "guilty as charged"), that solves the problem of trying to find enough outlets for nightly charges. I was suspicious about the "auto detect" feature, but my Android Tablet charged as fast or faster than it did with the factory-included charger and my LG Phone and smartwatch never overheated, so I know that the correct amperage was chosen.

The Smart Charger also includes a 2-outlet power strip with 1700 joules of surge protection. The outlets worked well (and the specifications boast that you can use them even for heavy-duty appliances), but, fortunately, I haven't experienced any electrical events that required the protection... I have no reason to believe that the surge protection won't work exactly as expected. And, while I'm not sure that most people here in the U.S. will benefit from it, both outlets support all types of plugs (including European, Great Britain, etc.). I hope the look of the outlets doesn't confuse people who are unfamiliar with the different plug types. Each outlet can handle one 2 or 3-prong U.S. plug.

OK, it's not perfect: The included instructions suffer from translation issues... but you won't need much in the way of instructions. Just turn the switch to on (the LED glows blue) and you're good to go.

The price is pretty good. I've seen lower-priced items, but they are the type that mount on a wall outlet. I liked that this unit had a power cord, but that's just a personal preference. Also, I haven't seen many that had more than 2 USB ports. The 4 "smart" ports give this unit an advantage. This device can sit on a desk or table and will offer both USB charging and 2 surge-protected electrical outlets. Nice! Finally, the casing feels very strong and durable, though, admittedly, I've only been using it for a few days.

I think most people will be happy with this device. I'll be recommending to my customers.

title: Very Good From A Seasoned Pro Editor
text:
I bought it to replace the HD Cinema Display monitor that I've used for years because I'm working in 4K. I edit on Priemiere and Avid, sometimes FCP, and in Premiere needed playback for 4K that wouldn't stutter and would be truer to resolution. Problem is I still occasionally do get some stutter but that could be my video cards (2015 MacBook Pro Retina 16 gb, AMD Radeon R9 M370X 2048 MB), plus seem to get it more working in longer sequences which is often a memory issue. I have used the same monitor at a workplace setting operating on a late model MacPro and don't experience all the same playback issues in Premiere but can't say that it's been 100% frame accurate.

For most uses though, this is a serious step up from an HD monitor. In Avid, where 4K is not so great anyway, I am very happy with the display of my timeline - so much crisper I don't need glasses (haha!). Would definitely recommend to anyone looking for a 4K monitor, though wouldn't want this as my "final" monitor in any kind of online situation as I'd need a truer non stutters playback, and color grade, professional monitor.

title: In Attic Antenna that Delivers
text:
We live in the north DFW area which is about 25 to 30 miles from most of the major television towers in our area. We were looking to cut the cord and had been researching antennas. I didn't really want to have something mounted on the outside because I didn't want the hassle of trying to manage it when it's two stories up if I ever had to adjust it so I was specifically looking for something that would work in my attic. We came across this and it seemed to have pretty good reviews. We hooked it up and couldn't be happier. We got all of our local stations with ease. The only one that gave any issue was WFAA which only gave me two bars out of three according to my TV. It's still a crystal clear picture and through a couple of heavy storms now, no degradation of signal. It comes with a power adapter which works well. We have split the signal to three televisions and none have experienced any type of issue with signal quality. The area in our attic in which we had to mount it in order to pick up all the stations didn't leave any room for the included mounting hardware. This was not a problem. The antenna is fairly light. Just some small eye hooks and some nylon string and I mounted it to the roof of the attic.

If you're looking to cut the cord and wanting a quality antenna. I highly recommend this beauty.

title: Buzzing and connectivity render these, sadly, useless.
text:
I have been purchasing from Amazon since 2011, and rarely write reviews. I do, however, read reviews very thoroughly before purchasing a product, so I feel compelled to leave a note here, if only to help others avoid throwing away a hard-earned $250.

I should note that I own several Bose speakers, wired headphones, noise-cancelling headphones, etc.., indeed the company is my go-to for audio systems, and I have thus far been very happy with their products.

I use this particular product occasionally, perhaps 1-2 times every week or two on average, with intervals of sometimes weeks between use. I use them only at home when my family is asleep and I am trying not to disturb anyone. I do not use them in a gym setting, or any other setting which would be considered a ‘rough’ environment.

While the sound quality, fit, and comfort (as well as styling, in my opinion) are far superior to other brands, the negative issues I’ve found with this product outweigh the benefits, and render it unworthy of a Bose reputation.

Connectivity issues are a common problem with all devices of this sort, but what I find absolutely infuriating of late is an exceedingly loud and persistent (even after the signaling music is turned off) electronic buzzing that screams out of the left ear bud. This is continuous, random, and does not stop. That is, I cannot even power off the ear bud to stop it. Placing it in the charger does not stop it. Nothing stops it save letting the ear bud run down it’s charge then recharging it. A few quick searches Google shows this to be not a rare issue with other users.

As of today (1/4/2018) Bose offers no updates or fixes for this.

For a $250 item, and even with forgiveness for the somewhat common connection issues, this issue renders this item useless, and frustratingly so.

I would recommend avoiding purchase of this product until an update, software or firmware, is established.

*I should note that I purchased these via Best Buy several months ago, prior to seeing the reviews on Amazon, much to my chagrin.

title: Only works with HDDs. SSDs do not work. SSD uses too much power.
text:
Number 1 lesson learned with this expansion boards is that it will not work reliably with a solid state drive (SSD) due to SSD requiring too much power.

I first started my assembly of the board and Pi expecting to use a spare SSD, but I had problems the entire time. Sometimes the drive would show up, most times it wouldn't. When it did connect, the Pi would run for an hour, then the entire system would freeze and require a power cycle. I have a 5V 4A power supply which is what is recommended, but the combination would never work. I was ready to return the item, then I saw the amount of power the SSD used compared to the regular hard drive. I have a Seagate 1TB 2.5 inch SSD and it uses 1.6A! The spare WD 500GB 2.5 inch HHD uses only 0.7A.

After installing the HHD, the system has never had an issue and has run for a week with no problems. Keep this in mind as you are planning to build your media server or other such Pi project.
