title: Flawed Design for People Who Sweat
text:
First one lasted nearly 6 months. Fitbit sent me a replacement. It lasted 6 days. Fitbit sent me another replacement. It lasted 3 days. I've given up. The contacts for recharging are exposed and if you sweat much, it shorts them out and the battery instantly discharges, which means it can't keep track of your steps until you recharge it. Since the unit does not take a standard USB cable to discharge it, you can simply recharge it anywhere unless you carry the special cable with you.
Also, the unit is not waterproof at all, so sweat creeps in the recharging opening and ruins the display. It is an absolutely terrible design for a product that is to be used to encourage exercise--if you sweat, it ruins it. Recharging is a hassle because it does not take a standard USB cable and you have to recharge about every six days, if the unit does not randomly discharge. I had a Garmin before this and it was at least 10 times better.
I will say that Fitbit customer service has been excellent and they have promptly sent me replacements. Unfortunately, their product is terrible. I won't be buying anymore Fitbit products for a long time.

title: The Okay-ist .mp3 Player To Date.
text:
... but isn't it supposed to be a Hi-Res player?

The Review:

On paper, this player looks fantastic. 2 Micro SD card slots (A great idea and executed well, actually.), Wifi for streaming, bluetooth support for cars and sound systems. Plus it meets the Japanese defined High Resolution standard adopted in 2014. It's why I purchased it. However, after a few days, I can assure you that this is merely only an OK player.

Positives:

It supports 2 Micro SD cards, which currently - as of this review - means a support of 400GB of extra space in addition to the 32GB native to the device. Not too shabby. I need that space for my music and audiobook collections.

It does have bluetooth compatible with my 2011 Elantra and bluetooth speaker at home, which is great for audio mobility, if not enjoyment.

Wifi seems to work well, but I don't have a subscription to a streaming service, but it was able to download android apps, including a WAV music player I had purchased years ago for a phone. (That was to simply play the music, mind you.) Nice.

Controls on the side are extremely easy to use and the volume control is extraordinarily sensitive to pressure allowing swift volume change.

Settings allow for control over whether volume can be adjusted with screen off, control over music on one of the home screen and the ability to force the player into "play the damn music, and only the music" mode (my words) are some of the benefits of the adapted Android operating system.

MQA support (available through update). I have no experience with MQA at this time. No comment on function or quality of this service, look elsewhere, please.

The Cons and their Explanation

Now, it CAN play lossless files and states that the playback meets the standard for Hi Resolution audio. When compared to the other players I have used (Fiio X5, X3II and X5II, AK100II and iBasso DX80) this has the second worst sound, only to a massively defective DX80. That's after the software update that fixed an issue similar to the one the DX80 exhibited, which was a clicking sound.(iBasso updates did not solve this, plus it had other issues on top of that.) So, that's not a good starting point. As for the quality of the music, I would hand this device to someone who wanted to debunk High Resolution audio for an example. It doesn't produce sound noticeably better than that which I get through my phone. Everything is better through the other non-iBasso players above. (Also, don't think I have something against iBasso, I don't, I just got a bad player.) Why do I say this? It lacked richness. I spent a while comparing Pink Floyd's "Us and Them" between this and the Fiio X5II. Noticeable difference on same headphones. The XDP-100R is just missing a little bit of everything on the range of frequency that makes it feel flat at similar volume levels. Mediocre sound at best.

Second issue is that WAV files pose a relatively catastrophic problem for the player. Can you guess my preferred audio format? Yep! An update allowed for folder support, but not the ability to play through the folder. Boo! Also had issues with playing the track on command. It was hit or miss, with about a 70/30 split in favor of hit. Still. those times of silence as you expect music to start are annoying, particularly when driving. Also had issues with hiccuping audio through both bluetooth and headphone. This included hiccups in the "play the damn music and only the music" mode as well. Seriously a negative to have a moment of unexpected silence in the middle of a song.

Third issue is the ease of which the player has it's play button hit when you are not expecting it. In my pocket, I would need to find a way to protect the XDP-100R here from stopping or starting playback because the raised button allowed for anything to trigger it. Same for the back and forward buttons.

Fourth issue is the speaker. There's a freaking speaker in this thing. WHY? For the love of all that is good and holy, WHY IS THERE A SPEAKER IN THE PLAYER? Completely unnecessary. Particularly from a hi-res device. Might expect it out of an iPod Touch, where it's more of a multimedia device, but seriously, that's not this. Also, if we were to start comparing this to an iPod Touch, I'd just have to state, for the record, that the only advantage this has over it is the capacity for storage. Let's not go there, shall we?

Last Issue: Bumpers. Seriously Stupid. I had to remove the top bumper just to fit in my headphone jack. It's a 1/4 in and I have an 1/8 in adapter. Did not fit with the bumper. At least it's removable.

Conclusion:

Pound for pound, this device has promise. No, really. It does. Micro SD card support for high capacity and bluetooth were my primary motives for purchasing this device. Sure, maybe I'll want MQA support in the future once I experience it. That's not today. For what the Pioneer XDP-100R is, it's ok. Just does not do anything really well and needs support to become a more polished player. This seems like a device released before the software developers had gone to beta and has such bugs that they're playing catch-up. The fact that it didn't come with folder playback support from the box is telling: when they said it supported WAV, they forgot that it does not contain ID3 tags. They had to push an update for that, and it didn't install immediately. I installed the several year old program so that I could listen to my precious WAV files by album, rather than the first tract of every album I have ever ripped. Bah. If they ever fix all the problems with the software, then we've got a pretty ok mp3 player.

Should You Buy This?

Um. No. It's too much hassle. Maybe if the software is fixed. But then there will be another player around. In the meantime, I can think of noone I can recommend this to, even hypothetically.

Final Thoughts:

It's a great first step for Pioneer. I think they need the failure of this device to make the next step as a company. Naturally, that company is Onkyo, who purchased Pioneer a while ago. Knowing why this device isn't great should help them develop a next generation that sounds much more professional and can allow the brand name to gain some relevance in the future. If, for some reason, this is the company's final shot at greatness, I salute you, because it was a great, though doomed, idea.

title: Great way to build or upgrade a home or office network.
text:
Setup was relatively straightforward.

The are 3 modes to choose from:
Router, bridge, wireless ISP - Share wireless connection through ethernet (Wireless ethernet bridge). I configured it to act as a router.

My home network uses a FIOS connection into a Verizon router, and is made up of four Apple Airports of varying ages (though not the newest models) in strategic parts of the house to provide maximum coverage and performance.

I replaced one Airport - an Airport Extreme Dual Band 5th Generation, which supports the older 802.11N protocol - with the Alfa AC1200. I used a wired connection to the main Airport, and from there a wired connection to the Verizon router.

I set it up so I would have two wireless networks going at the same time, making it easier to do accurate A/B testing.

I tried a variety of devices including a MacBook Pro Retina laptop, an iPad Pro and several iPhones.

First off, I can say that the Alfa “feels” substantially faster across all devices. Websites loaded considerably quicker, and files downloaded up to 50% faster.

The biggest difference, naturally, was with devices equipped with the new 802.11AC protocol. Speeds increased up to 400% using the Alfa with the newer iPad and iPhones. The laptop only has an N connection, so the difference was not as great, but still ran to as much as 50% faster.

I also found the Alfa to provide greater coverage with more a stable signal than the Airport it replaced. Areas in the house in which coverage has been spotty or weak now have a clear, fast, reliable connection.

The Alfa High-Power Gigabit AC1200 Router is a great way to upgrade a home or office LAN without breaking your budget. Setup was smooth, and the speed increase was impressive, particularly on newer devices.

I will try to provide an update as I continue to put it through its paces.

For the record, I was provided a unit for review.

title: Absolutely the best alternative to wired gigabit Ethernet
text:
After struggling with powerline network adapters that never work as advertised and a hodgepodge of wi-fi extenders that never provide the reliability or range as advertised, I've finally found a solution: Actiontec Bonded MoCA 2.0 adapters. With a stupid-easy installation, they provide speeds every bit as fast as a wired Ethernet connection. And the best part - they're reliable. I haven't experienced any connection hiccups or interference issues that plague powerline network adapters.

If you have an older home and don't want to spend the money to wire Cat6 Ethernet, this is the next-best solution. I haven't tested LAN speeds, but my service provider guarantees 200 mbit and, sure enough, in my basement that is only connected through MoCA, I'm seeing the full 200 mbit on Ookla Speedtest.

I've installed a second pair (actually three) in a large, old rambler. To blanket the house in wi-fi, install these modules at opposite ends of the house and add a wi-fi access point (which you can get for about $20 a pop, or repurpose an old router).

Installation is easy - just follow the clear instructions and, once connected, the modules act like a wired connection. No software setup or reconfiguration necessary.

The only downside: the modules do create cable clutter. Coaxial cables are by their very nature tough to tidy up, and they do require separate power. Add more cable clutter if you're going to be adding access points. A small price to pay for incredible performance where wired Ethernet isn't possible or affordable.

title: Simply stunning sound. Can't do better for double the $$$!
text:

You simply cannot go wrong. I have heard a lot of the speakers in this size and range and the RC-70s take a back seat to none. I like Energy bookshelf speakers a lot, and have owned a couple pairs. There are pro audio reviews online comparing these to $5,000 pairs of speakers, favorably.

The tweeters (subtle, highly accurate, clear but not horn-y or overly bright) and mids are dramatically good, the bass is solid, clean, and full. I do have a subwoofer but the bass of the RC-70s is clean, deep and plenty beefy on the speakers alone. They do seem to have a break-in period, which I originally doubted even exists, but which many people observe and which Energy mentions in their literature.

They just get better and better. Best decision I have ever made regarding speakers.

*Edited: with additional time, I am even more in love with these! They never fatigue your ears, they just open up and sound amazing. All music is good. Well-recorded, good sources will shine. All genres too. So glad to join the Cult Of Energy! Consider me a fanboy. Buy with utmost confidence.
Google the SoundStage review, and the Sound & Vision review, of these speakers...so, so, good.

title: They're comfortable, anyway.
text:
Saw these a few days ago on Amazon's Daily Deals and couldn't believe the reviews and markdown. I even searched around for other reviews, and despite some prospective purchasers asking how they compare to "Beats" --Dre's horrendous marketing ploy-- I figured they were worth a shot. Just received them and tested them out with a few tracks, but before I get to the cons, let me highlight the pros.

First off, these are undoubtedly some of the most comfortable headphones I have ever tried. Seriously. The padding fits snuggly and comfortably around the ear with just enough pressure to keep them snug without giving you a headache. They excellently muffle out your surroundings as well and provide a pure, quiet environment for most any audiophile. Secondly, the audio quality pumping out of these headphones is phenomenal. The treble and mids are crisp. And I mean crisp. Bite into a Lays. On a diet? Fair enough. Find a ripe Fuji apple. It's crisper than that. These things absolutely fit the HiFi requirement, and you'd expect mostly that at a $100 price tag. At $25, they're a steal.

What's missing? The bass. It's isn't there. I've had a pair of $20 Sennheiser 202's for six years, and they still kick these Sentey's out of the water. Albeit, these Sentey's do have superior clarity in the mids and highs, but the experience is destroyed by the muddled, lackluster lows. They lack that certain "punch" you expect when the bassline kicks in, or if you're using them for gaming, when a .308 goes off in your ear. On that note, I'd still be comfortable using these as earmuffs at a range.

Either way, these headphones lack half the experience you're looking for, no matter how comfortable they may fit, nor how crisp those mids and highs.

title: Pretty good sound/build, but have some usability issues.
text:
Have this headset since 2 months back (used a Logitech H800 before this). I use it for work and some occasional gaming. I'd say overall it is a good headset, but slightly pricey given shortcomings. (honestly I'd give it a 3.5 rating). If they were to fix the quircks I'd give it 5 stars.

Pros:
> Overall build & comfort is good.
> Battery duration is very good as well - so you don't need to recharge that often.
> Folds up nicely for say a laptop bag
> The sound is good & the noice cancelling is pretty good too (my first noice cancelling headset, so not really able to compared on that aspect - can only state that it's a good noise reduction whilst on an airplane)
> You can connect to two seperate devices (say phone and laptop), there's a caveat (ses in the cons).
> If it's not connected to anything it'll shut off after appx 10 mins / ie powersaving feature.
> Comes with a smartphone app (me having a Windows Phone - impressed they made one for that too).
> Good Bluetooth range.

Cons:
1) Cannot use noice cancelling w/o using a 3.5mm cable. Unfortunately the design is poor if you want to use Noice Cancelling only (say if you want to use it on an airplane) since bluetooth cannot be turned off on the headset. The workaround ( ) is to attack the line-in cable that comes with the headset (my guess is that this disables Bluetooth). If you don't have the cable with you.. the headset (and noice cancelling) turns off after 10 mins due to the powersaving feature.
2) Cannot charge it whilst speaking. Albeit the battery time is very good mini USB port hidden behind the wishbone shaped arms that hold the speakers/earmuffs with the effect you cannot wear the heatset and have have a USB Cable attached.
3) Sensitive touchplate/lack of tactile feedback. Since there's no tactile feedback when you use the buttons (to turn up/down volume, receive call and similar) you might accidentically start/stop music instead of turning volume up/down.
4) The mute button, is too small. Using it frequently for business calls where being able mute/unmute quickly is desirable.
5) When it's connected to two devices, sound is bad :-S. Example if you're playing a game on the computer (use a PC) and use the headphones, then the sound is poor if somebody calls on the mobile phone. I'm not sure if this is an issue with the Bluetooth standard or the headphones. Net result I only connect one device at the time (shame).
5.1) in Windows it shows up as two seperate devices one being "SHB9850NC hands-free" and SHB9850NC Stereo", which adds a slight usability issue as there's two devices when controlling the volume. Example if you call in on say a Skype call then the taskbar in Windows might only show the 'stereo' volume control - whilst the audio come through the 'hands-free' part.. ie you can turn the volume up and down w/o any effect. My guess is that it's how they allow it to be connected to two devices at the same time. Suspect the design idea was that you listen to music from one device (ie 'stereo') and then take a call from say a smartphone (the 'hands-free' device).

Hope this helps someone else.

text:
I purchased this to support a [[ASIN:B00ND1KHY2 Mackie Mix Series Mix12FX -Watt 12-Channel Mixer]], which it easily does. What impressed me the most is the construction. I had been using a music stand with the tray perpendicular to the ground and it worked, but was not nearly as stable as this stand. Moreover, I looked at a few other brands, but most were cheaply made.

Here are a few things that set this one apart: first, the clamping mechanisms are quick release type and not the cheesy knobs that every other stand I tried employs. Second, if you are considering this for a truly heavy device like a projector the pins for the support pole guarantee that it will be supported. Frankly, the pins are probably never going to be needed because the main release mechanisms hold firmly.

Dimensions are:
Tray: 15 9/16 x 10 7/8 inches with lips along the widths top and bottom.

I do 3D character/creature animation in Autodesk Maya so the extra muscle here is most welcome. One thing to note is that this CPU did not work right after dropping it into my motherboard. It was necessary to clear the CMOS memory and boot with the default settings that motherboard automatically detected and applied. Since doing that, my machine has been rock solid in terms of stability and dramatically faster across gaming and 3D content creation.

title: Beautiful case, with a few quirks.
text:
[[VIDEOID:13f7966d54ad4bc5afc5bf7c4f902494]] Picked this up because I wanted tempered glass, but the 460 was just too small for my liking. I've got 2 HDD's and an SSD from an old rig in the back, all of them stay cool (about 30C for the HDDS). The 3 fans on front work great off a splitter and are very quiet at low speed. Adding rear fan and 2 top fans (currently I have Enermax TB Silence red LED fans that look great in the case) and the case cools nicely. My 7600K OC'd to 4.6GHz sits at about 25 degrees with the trusty 212 EVO, and I've never seen it go above 50. There is A LOT of airflow out the back, the case is very open and at idle nearly silent thanks to the glass.

Things I like: Beautiful! Doesn't really show fingerprints/dust as much as I thought it would. Fingerprints wipe right off, unlike the aluminum CM Cosmos it replaced. Fans look nice even though they aren't the HD versions (which honestly are too expensive). Good variety of colors/light effects. Glass on all sides to show off your rig, and fans diffuse noise from fans. Cools well with additional fans. Lit front logo and PSU logo are a nice touch!

Things I don't like: Took me a long time to get the wiring right so it would fit behind the metal shroud on the rear and look neat. Expect to think out wiring and take your time. The fan wiring is a bit sloppy from the factory. Also, Corsair really could have included at least a non-LED fan for the rear at this price point. The CPU shroud - it's too short, and it's open so you see right into it. I ended up taking a piece of black foam from packaging I had and cutting to fit the front. The front logo and PSU logo have separate SATA plugs for power - they really could have been combined into one. Folks might have trouble with top radiators depending on their motherboards. Also, there should be a channel in the PSU shroud to hide wiring across the bottom of the motherboard. I solved this issue by using slightly longer offsets and running the cables behind the mobo.

Finally - Corsair kind of missed the mark in one critical area - the fans and logos should be able to be controlled with the CUE software via USB header!

Despite that and the other (relatively minor imo) shortcomings I still give it 5 stars simply because it's so gorgeous. And, unlike InWin cases it has actual airflow and keeps your components cool.

title: If you understand how this product works before you buy it, you’ll be pleased with the results
text:
There are three things you need to know about the Pavlok:

(1) The Pavlok does what it says it does: it breaks habits if you use it properly, which is very easy to do.

(2) The habit-breaking regimen is manually self-administered. (There is no device that can tell when you are about to eat ice cream.) There are a number of people who seem to buy this product expecting it to somehow have cognitive awareness. This false hope seems to ruin it for some people but there’s no reason to be upset by this. Just buy it knowing that you have to shock yourself. Arguably this is BETTER because the entire time you’re breaking the habit you’ll train conscious awareness and choice. There is an argument that this is just an expensive version of wearing a rubber band and snapping it when you do something you don’t want to do. This is true except the reconditioning is stronger with the Pavlok, and it’s much harder to forget that you’re wearing it. Believe me, when you’re giving yourself electric shocks, you’ll be thinking about the habit constantly. Is that worth $200? I felt it was.

(3) There is no such thing as magic. The original impetus to do the habit will always exist. Refined sugar will always be addictive, for example. The Pavlok just removes the habituality associated with these behaviors. So, don’t expect to lose all desire to do something. Just know that you will be totally conscious in your choices, which means you’ll have a MUCH easier time not doing whatever you don’t want to do.

I’ve had the Pavlok for 3 weeks now and have used it to break two habits. I’ve also gifted them to my whole family.

title: This is a nice little HDMI switch box with some truly useful features
text:
This is a nice little HDMI switch box with some truly useful features. It's probably worthy of a five star review, but it's sometimes hampered by the fact that it's an HDMI switch box.

What I mean by that, is that there's may not be a product out there that and deal with all the hand-shake issues brought on by the various components in the chain if equipment.This one will occasionally not switch automatically and I need to use the remote control and manually switch it. Sometimes my projector will not recognize the new component that got switched on, so the process needs to be repeated. Not sure if this is the fault of the switcher, the projector, or the flaky HDMI standard.

I find this particularly useful switching between my PS3 and PS4. I have a pair of Skullcandy PLYR 1 7.1 headphones that I share between the PS3 and PS4. The switcher is capable of stripping the Dolby Digital audio from HDMI. It then sends this to an optical output that goes to the decoder box of the headphones. So when I switch between the PS3 and PS4 HDMI outputs, it also switches the output going to the optical out.

title: Great little device. but one major flaw for a small subset of users : USB MIDI is broken.
text:
This is a great device for the price, but not without flaws.

I still give it a 5 star review because, as with many of the video reviews out there, I've found it to be a really useful 2-in-1 to have around for games, taking notes, web operations etc. I make much more use out of the built-in pen than I thought I would, and the screen is simply superb.
There is, however one oversight with their build of chromeos that will be insignificant to 90% of users, but a showstopper for the few people who want to plug in external MIDI devices for music production.

PROS:
Display : almost unusable for text at its native resolution, the display has a very wide viewing angle, good black levels ( to my eye ) and is very bright.
Stylus pen : really handy, especially at hi-resolutions. Art programs are fun
2-in-1 : At less than 2.5lb, feasible to use in tablet mode. Tent, vertical and other modes are handy.
keyboard : decent travel, small backspace button, but you get used to that pretty quickly
Android on-board : some issues with some applications, but overall a good experience.
Snappy performance: Not driven this too hard but performs well for regular use.
CONS:
- speakers are pretty meh, but I guess that's to be expected; I don't use it to listen to anything
- Bluetooth connectivity seems iffy .. they might have not implemented everything perfectly
- USB MIDI Does Not Work, period. I've spent a lot of email and phone time with them to convince them to check this out, but Chromeos does support MIDI over USB and the samsung engineers dropped the ball on this one. I've verified MIDI initializes and works on other chromeOS devices, but this one looks like it's missing the drivers or they simply didn't build in the midi libraries. MIDI fails to get past initialization on this device. I escalated the issue as far as I could and eventually convinced the support person to try to get the bug in front of an engineer, but we'll have to wait and see if they fix it. If they do, and make the 14 of us who actually want to use it for midi happy , I'll update this review.

OK UPDATE ( 5/17/17 ) : still no fix for midi; samsung cs dropped the ticket, as far as I can tell. Still love the chromebook for other tasks, but I'm dropping a star cos they didn't build the os to spec... and I'm in a petty mood.

title: If it's good enough for the military than it's good enough for me
text:
Updated 516/2016

Recently I received a comment that the statement Military Tested is untrue as the military don't use iPads. I'm glad to tell you after a lot of research I found indeed that the military DOES USE IPADS ! Every service branch has been using them sinc 2013 when the Pentagon approved the iPad and iOS 6 as it was proven safe. It can't be used to connect to the military network. The iPad is also used by Homeland Security, the FBI, the DEA, the US Marshal Service and many police agencies world wide. The military test is the standard test used by the military to prove the items being protected can withstand dropping from the minimum height of 48 inches on multiple dropping from different angles. So I stick with my statement. If it's good enough for the military it's good enough for me.

Sorry Amazon but this time I went with a different seller as you were our of stock. I hope this can be reviewed anyway. These cases are tough to find anywhere. Even UAG were out of stock but they did give me a seller who just received a larger shipment. They weren't sure if they had any left as it is a large retailer and online store. A quick call to the local retail store and I guess it was an amusing request because all I got from the polite sales rep was a chuckle. He had them on his shelf for all of one day. Honestly he only received 2 of each color from his warehouse. He told me to place one on order and he would call when it arrived but couldn't give any delivery date. He was also kind enough to check his web site to find that they had some in stock but I would have to order online. Since I do have an account with this company and the app on my iPad I took a shot. Low and behold they had 3 and only in black. Black was exactly what I wanted so I placed the order and waited for confirmation. Within 20 minutes I got an E-mail confirming the order with free 3 day delivery. Once again sorry Amazon. The case arrived on the day promised in a shipping box big enough to hold at least 5 cases and wrapped in enough air filled little bags to float the Titanic. I think someone was having a bit of fun or they ran out of the regular boxes.

The case itself is nothing short of amazing. The material is of some type of material resembling rubber but stiffer. I was surprised about the weight as it is very light. Now UAG claims the case is designed for military use and I assume that means it's pretty rugged. It's a simple procedure placing the iPad in the case and took a few seconds. It only goes on one way. Once on every opening is precise. All 4 speakers cutouts line up, the camera cutout is perfect, the volume controls right where they are supposed to be and easily maneuverable with my fat fingers, earphones jack and charge cord opening and on off switch aligned exactly. As for the camera protruding that's been taken care of and the case does lay flat. There is an attached loop for the Apple Pencil which is convenient and the magnetic clasp is very secure. The case can be separated so the Apple keyboard can be attached. There's a few ways to adjust the case for viewing and flipping the cover over for hand holding is very easy. Because the case cradles the iPad very securely I'm not sure if there is enough space to place any kind of screen protector and still have it fit properly. I'm pretty sure anyone owning this case will have some peace of mind knowing that their iPad is well protected and easier to hold. The case is probably the most expensive out there now other than some fancy leather ones but it's worth every penny.

title: Very Capable Tri-Band Radio
text:
The UV-5RX3 is a very capable tri-band addition to the well known UV-5R lineup. Having the convenience of the 1.25M band rolled into the typical 2M & 70cm configuration at such an affordable price point should make this radio the new 'standard' for the UV-5R family with amateur/HAM operators.

I found the UV-5RX3 to be simple to program using CHIRP software with my existing UV-5R cable. No driver issues...no read/write issues, etc. I actually used an existing file from my UV-5R, edited out a handful of seldom used frequencies, plugged in the several active 1.25M pairs for my area, and was up and running in less than 10 minutes from opening the box. It's really convenient that the accessories between the variants of the UV-5R are interchangeable. Battery life is very good. RX performance is typical 'good but not great' I've experienced with the existing UV-5R family--that's not a demerit--I'm simply saying it does the job and does it well but isn't going to be as sensitive as a $300 HT, which nobody should expect anyway. TX performance is very good across all three bands. The 1.25M TX power is full power on this radio, not a reduced output that several other tri-bands offer.

The only suggestion I would have would be for Baofeng/Radioddity to include a single tri-band antenna instead of the 2M/70cm dual band and a separate 1.25M antenna. I chose to add the Radioddity RD-301 tri-band antenna to the UV-5RX3 which now allows me to switch between any of the three bands without changing antennas and makes this a great carry along radio for everyday use.

text: Despite my misgivings (and a lot of questionable reviews about this type of product) i went ahead and purchased this odd motorized device to see if i could use it to transfer about 30 old VHS-C tapes to my Mac.  I was using an old borrowed VHS and had some problems initially with the video not showing up and then the quality being lousy.  With all the variables it took a while for me to figure things out.  Turns out I had to try a couple of video capture devices before i found one that worked well (elgato video capture on amazon) and then i had to watch a few Youtube videos and figure out how to clean the VCR heads (made a BIG difference).  And also had to watch a youtube video to make sure i was loading the VHS-C tape correctly.  But after all of that, this adapter turns out to work very well.  Trick is to make sure there is no slack in the tape (manually turn tape to tighten) before you insert it into the VCR.  Hit rewind to make sure tape is rewound and tight. I've had zero problems playing the tapes.  I did have to clean the heads a second time because apparently the tapes were funky (or i didn't get them properly cleaned the first time)  But the adapter has worked like a champ.  Highly recommend it if you are one of those folks that went down the VHS-C path.  Enjoy.

title: So far so good
text:
I need the widest lens I can get without barreling like mad. I bought the first lens used for $300 (same model but older) but it did not communicate with my Nikon D5100 so I returned it. For another $100 I got a one new, properly tuned and with the full warranty. I was unsure as to whether buying another one was a good idea but the price point is very attractive, especially considering I don't need to spend much on a lens right now. Tamron or Tokina glass is at least another $100-200 and the Nikon is twice the price. None of them match the wide spec this one has, and I don't really need anything much tighter than this lens offers. Preliminary shots impressed me. It focuses properly and although there is some distortion at wide, it's not terrible and quite fixable with PS Elements. I plan to use it for my fledgling real estate photography sideline.

Update: Significant distortion is apparent at wide focal length and aperture and requires correction. However, many realtors want me to use a 10mm lens so this is it and it still beats using a cell phone by a long shot.

Another Update: I suppose this is Photo 101 but if you shoot on a level, straight-ahead axis (that is, avoiding up or down tilting), results are very acceptable and distortion is minimized. In some instances the up/down tilt distortion actually improves things by exaggerating the field of view.

Good lens for the dough.

title: A great machine at a good price
text:
This Dell Inspiron 15" laptop was purchased about 2 weeks ago (mid-Nov 2015) after my other laptop died (mostly- graphic card fail). Previous laptop was a Dell 1520 with 1 hdd (7200rpm- replaced a few times), m8600gt card, 5gb ram (upgraded from 2gb) and a bunch of other details.

I was looking at other brands and even some options at XoticPC. They offer numerous versions and upgrades, which is great, but can easily double or triple your budget in a build if one isn't careful lol . Anyway, back to the prebuilt -

This was ready to go out of the box. Battery was mostly full.

Runs quiet with the ssd vs the 7200rpm drive I used to have and that part is cooler as well.

Battery - as noted is was near full charge and ran for a number of hours before it got down to low levels. At this time I plugged in the 130w charger (brick). No response. Actually an error stating that this wasn't recognized and not charging. huh?? Everything was in order, no cracks, dents, etc... I plugged in my older 90w from other computer, same error but it charged. ... Well, skip some time for research, talk with dell rep and update. It's working It seems that has happened with other units. There is a bios update that addresses that. I didn't flash this machine, yet. I did have to push the end in the computer and held it there for a few seconds after I did some update and all errors went away. I mention this in case others have a similar issue. My concern for the future is that the connector on my previous computer got loose after a few years. The connector on this 130w charger seems to have a thicker and stronger sheathing. Hopefully the insides are better as well.

Touchpad - meh. This is why I took off 1 star, that and some other "nickel-and-dime" issues. The problem I am having is some "coasting" of the cursor and pausing (or intermittent movement). Add to that, the buttons are underneath the touchpad. This does add to some cool features but try to click on some tab and the cursor moves. I would prefer dedicated buttons like many other units have. I have looked for adjustments, thinking maybe the sensitivity could be lowered. I have adjusted the speed to where I'm comfortable with. ... This touchpad is larger (a plus) and there are many cool features and gestures that can be customized (a big plus), but the core of moving cursor around and have it stop on a tab or slider and this thing just coasts off. So I'm finding myself often micro adjusting the cursor, which I've never done on other units. I think some setting where one could turn off the pad on the area above the 'buttons' might be an answer. Meanwhile - workaround - use a mouse and all of the above problems go away. ... Technique(?) perhaps, and maybe this touchpad is just supersensitive to my movements, so when I think I've stopped moving it keeps moving to edge of finger tip(?) . Still, I'd prefer dedicated buttons.

Keypad - it's OK. The keys feel fine and are quieter than my other unit, but the other unit was better to type on and more comfortable. True, nothing beats a good keyboard and most laptops aren't known for that. The frame of the 1520 was curved down on the edge - where the wrists are - and this one is a corner. It just feels like poor posture. I'm using it now to type this review. Is this a big deal?, probably not. If I was going to be consistently writing I might consider a wrist pad or something. One big Plus - in the whole time of typing, not once has the cursor jumped around, unlike the other unit. This in part due to placement of touchpad to keyboard and adjusting settings.

Backlit Keys - This option has been around for a while. It's standard here. White light in color and brightness is adjustable, 3 settings ( On, Off, middle). They do fade out or on, so that's cool

Speakers - a little better than what I had. Any music or movies I would plug in to stereo, headphones, or work radio. Let's be fair here, some others have complained, but there's not much room in a laptop for a great sound system and for the price, it's good.

Monitor - I got the FHD 1920x1068 res. There is a 4k touchscreen option. While movies and some apps would benefit, others not so much. Battery life may be shortened and expect the screen to be constantly full of smudges. I have a tablet and smart phone, although they have screen protectors on them. Overall, I'm pleased. Again, I know there are better, brighter screens out there. I have not used a calibration tool here (recommended for working on photos or videos).

Memory - 8 gb. Take note, those interested in expanding. There are 2 memory slots, only 1 is filled with an 8gb, as compared to 2 4gb. So adding on doesn't require selling parts online. What's in it is Hynix DDR3L (note the 'L', it's also marked inside next to memory). I just bought an 8gb stick from Kingston - ( KTD-L3CL-8g for those interested). This will not take DDR4 mem. You can get that in other gaming units, but expect to may more. I'm pleased.

SSD storage- This is great. It's cool, quiet, and faster than previous 7200rpm drive (which is faster than 5400rpm). Also take note - this is in mSata slot, thus freeing the hd bay for a 2nd drive, be it another ssd or disk. I was able to add a 1tb hybrid 5400rpm from another computer last night. It took, basically plug & play. I adjusted partitions and did a format, then moved photos and such over. Yes, I realize that it adds to weight (slightly) and noise (low) and may be a drain to battery (not sure how much). Yes, I'm at risk of losing lots of data if computer goes swimming or something. That's why and external drive or 2 is a great idea. Also, I do have the option of removing it and storing it, if the need arises

Graphic card - I'm not a real gamer. If I was, there are better units with much faster processors and dual cards. For that matter, get a desktop version. You get more room, better cooling, better components, etc... Still, some apps perform smoother and there is the occasional game. Some reviews have mentioned that they could have added the 970 or 980. Perhaps, but keep in mind they use more energy and run warmer and cost more. There is a 965 that has better performance and is more in line with the 960. Whatever, this unit is above average and can hold it's own and then some and for under $800, that's hard to beat. Plus, from a company perspective, they order in large batches and they are 'hard-wired' in. Hence pre-builds. That's partly why they may direct customers to their gaming units, which have the better components and such.

Weight - This is lighter than the 1520 with 12cell battery, heavier than the Kindle Fire, and is very light compared to some tools I carry around. My take - we are talking about a few pounds total and ounces of differences between other 15" laptops. Lift some weights or carry some cameras with large lenses and all of a sudden this laptop seems like air LoL. If that's a concern, then do without the 2nd drive, graphic card and consider a 13" or a tablet. Actually, if bulk is a problem, then I'd do what I could with my smart phone (sorry, but my Kindle seems slow even though I like it)

One minor irritant with Microsoft Edge (windows) is that they reset to minimum size after a video is played or a reboot. I've installed Chrome and that seems to be stable in that respect. I tend to open lots of tabs when reading news articles, Edge seems multiple times better than IE ever was, hence I used Chrome, but Chrome tends to suck up memory when multiple tabs are open. Edge is slightly better so far. This computer is notably faster when scrolling through sites than old one, even on a slow network. For office, I installed LibreOffice. It's open source, some friends use it in their business. I'm a newbie with this, but just thought I'd mention it.

Wireless- Works, sort of... There have been a few times, when it appears connected, but isn't. Phone and tablet are on. Check settings, turn off/on wireless and it's good, but slow. Plug in with cable and all is fine. I've read some, and others have mentioned similar in reviews. Might do an update soon, I've been busy... Older one could get weak signals in back rooms, this one detects them, but... yah, that's it.

Since I bought this, the price dropped $40. Amazon adjusted. That basically paid for extra memory. :) I ordered on a Saturday and it was delivered end of next Tuesday (2 business days). Short of going to some big box store and getting one off the shelf, this was faster than other places that would take a week or so.

All in all, I'm pleased with this setup, save for those kinks. It had the core of what I was looking for -- a 15" monitor, ssd with room for a 2nd drive, graphic card that wasn't a room heater, enough memory, and fast processor (newer intel i5 or i7). It met this at a good price.

title: Best Thunderbolt 3 dock for the price!
text:
This thing is basically a $50 Thunderbolt 3 dock for your laptop. I have the 2016 14" Razer Blade which is thunderbolt 3 compatible, so it works amazingly smooth running a 4k monitor 1Gbps internet speed and a USB 3.0 dock out of one port. If you have seen other docks out there you will pay $200 - $300 for them which is ridiculous. This is a no-brainer.

I only have two complaints about this product, but I won't reduce rating since it isn't major and I am thankful to Cable Matters that they compete with the ridiculous dock manufacturers out there charging 5x as much for essentially the same device. For $50 this is a bargain.

1) I wish the USB-C cable was a little longer. I use a laptop riser for work and with the laptop sitting above my desktop it bends down and puts pressure on the USB-C port on my laptop. It still works fine, but being that my laptop is new I don't want to have that tension on the port since I will be using this laptop and the Cable Matters USB-C dock daily. I want the cable to fit straight in without bending and this is especially hard when you have an HDMI cable, Ethernet cable, and USB cable plugged into the dock so the dock gets heavy. I ended up using some Velcro to hold the dock to my monitor with the USB-C cable sticking out since my laptop sits right next to it and it works fine. It fits in straight with no tension, It would be easier if the cable was at least a foot long.

2) I can't completely diagnose this problem since I barely moved from my Apple 2015 15" Retina MacBook Pro to the 2016 Razer Blade, but my 4K monitor will sometimes crash if I let my laptop go to sleep with the dock plugged in. I have to unplug the monitor and plug it back in for it to work again. I don't know if this is my laptop or the USB-C dock. I do suspect the USB-C dock to be the problem more than the laptop since the monitor has always worked fine with my old laptop and anything else I plugged into it.

Regardless these problems are minor and this is a good buy. I wanted a dock for my old MacBook pro, but Thunderbolt 2 docks are super expensive and they don't have the bandwidth necessary to do everything I need it to with 1 port. With this Thunderbolt 3 dock I can do so much with 1 port for so much cheaper than any other brand. 5-stars!

title: battery arrived with a jammed pin
text:
Item took awhile to arrive, when It arrived I went to set it up but the battery kept disconnecting

the battery would instantly disconnect after inserting it
I tried turning the device on its side, inserting the battery, battery connects, turn device upright, disconnects

after closer inspection I noticed that the - pin on the battery was jammed into the battery...brand new device and it had an issue

I REALLY didn't feel like having to RMA a brand new device and having to wait for it to ship to and from support taking at least a month..
I just got over having to RMA my Atomos Shogun and it took over two months to get back, maybe APC is faster, maybe not, I have no idea, the device is big and heavy, no idea, didn't feel like going through the headache of RMA

I grabbed a medium sized safety pin, bent the needle into a hook, fished it down into the batter pins and tugged the pin back up into position
reinserting the battery just jammed the pin again so I fished the pin back out, used the needle nose pliers to bend the pin
reinserting the battery a second time showed success

i removed the battery and confirmed the pin was no longer jammed

now the device works fine
i would like to think this was a special case and this doesn't happen often..i'll be purchasing more in the future but this event keeps me from giving a 5 star.

title: Your search for your next ex-car stereo can stop here!
text:
Previously to switching to PIONEER I had a variety of DUAL car stereos. The first noticeable improvement in the Pioneer is the sound shaping. The Pioneer has an excellent sounding EQ plus a 3 way variable Loudness and a multi-level Bass Boost. Three stages of tone contour will help just about anyone get a good sound in their vehicle. Once tuned in the Pioneer FHX820BS really shows off it's excellence. The MP3 player is not grainy and noisy (compared again to the Dual .) I put 20,000 songs on a 32Mb USB Micro Stick and in less than 30 seconds the music player is off to the races. In the past few years Pioneer has developed a MIXTRAX feature that allows the user to specify a track length of 1-3 minutes at the end of which the deck will attempt to genre/beat/timbre match-up the next track. If you have the Mix Cut Effects turned on then the player will cross-fade with some interesting (and some obscure) DJ type mixovers. While a novelty at worst, at best it's a fun way to keep the music going non-stop. Just don't be too surprised if you've got a variety of music and you have a raging "Disturbed" track filter-shift into a limp "Taylor Swift" pop-noodle.
The buttons, functions and menus are easy to navigate although a brightly lit day will wash out the readability. The manual speaks of a LINK mode that would allow you to lock down playback on a single artist, album or genre of music. This is a great feature but ONLY is available if the playback source is an iPOD. Too bad... it would be great if it could do this from a standard ID tagged MP3 music library loaded on a USB device.
The 820BS and it's siblings allow a cool integration with your Pandora account but you must purchase a CUSTOM USB CABLE (CD-IU52 iPod®/iPhone® Lightning to USB Interface Cable) or (CD-MU200 - Android Interface Cable ). I ordered one from BIG CHOPSTICKS and although it may come with some delicious Orange sauce I won't have it for a few postal weeks so I can't really review the Pandora features at this time.
The FM Radio (is it a SUPERTUNER?) I can't say but the spec of 11 dBf (0.8 μV/75Ω) is very respectable and Pioneer after-all 'pioneered' great car stereo FM reception so I give it a big 'Greatful-Dead-Truckin' style thumbs up. Again, it blows the doors off what I've experienced in this price range.
With all that you'd probably expect a gleaming report on the hands-free Bluetooth calling.... sorry can't do it. It's just another kind of strange sounding two-way VOIP like device that requires clever yet difficult external Mic mounting and a "All Windows Up - AC/HEATER Fan on low Mode' environment to really have any kind of intimate phone conversation ...especially one that requires the exchange of credit card information.
Haven't tried the BT streaming but will report on that when the USB cable arrives.
Other oddities.. Three sets of RCA preamp outs on the backside! An ill-conceived Steering Wheel wireless remote option (CD-SR100 Steering Wheel Remote) but I seriously doubt anyone will ever buy one until OVERSTOCK, MEH., or WOOT breaks the ice. And the many colors of illumination - MUCH APPRECIATED TRULY!
I can't give it 5 stars... it'd just serve to raise my future alimony when I replace it.

title: Good for movies and podcasts, subpar for music
text:
PROS:

If i'm listening to a podcast or watching a movie, the sound on these is pretty decent. Voices are clear and it's easy to listen to the speaker. These headphones are marketed as tangle-free, and I did indeed find that it was incredibly difficult to tangle the wires. This is a really nice feature as untangling headphones is a nuisance and usually leads to damage over time. I also liked that the headphones came with multiple bud sizes and found they fit easily in my ear (pretty rare for me).

CONS:

When I'm listening to music, the sound on these buds is consistently muddled and tinny with faint, but noticeable background graininess, regardless of the genre of music. Mid range notes are congested and base notes are non-existent. Honestly, the music sounds as though it's being plated on a phonograph from the 50s. I get that these buds are by no means high end and are just intended to be tossed in a briefcase or pocket for on the go listening, but even with those expectations, they still miss the mark.

OVERALL:

Overall, I'm not too impressed. These are ok if you'll mainly be listening to movies, podcasts, or the like. But if you want to listen to music, I can't recommend these.

Disclaimer:
I bought this product with my own money at a discounted price in exchange for an honest review. I roll my eyes when I see other "sponsored" reviews because they are often excessively glowing, are discordant with the reviews by non-sponsored customers, and lack depth. I don't want to be that reviewer, so I make a point of telling it as it is. If a product is great, I'll tell you; if its subpar, I'll tell you that too. If you found this review helpful, I'd appreciate it if you gave it a thumbs up because I try to be as thorough as possible and it's nice to know my work helped someone.

title: Do your homework to make sure this is right for you - it has lots of problems that are not really discussed in reviews.
text:
The concept of an ultrawide screen sounds good in theory, but in practice it has issues, and this monitor specifically misses the target.

PROS:
- great screen real estate, you can put three documents side by side in full screen.

- higher line resolution than normal HD - 1440p vs. 1080p meaning you get crisper images IF the application supports it

- LGs dual controller app is great - it allows you to control two machines (or more) with the same keyboard and mouse so if you have a laptop and desktop you can hook both up to the monitor and use one set for both which is convenient

- the screen splitter app is very useful. It allows you to essentially set different screen 'zones' similar to the snap feature in windows in which you drag your application and it will automatically resize to fill out that zone. There are many different combinations of zones to choose from to match whatever your needs might be.

- 34" is very wide... almost too wide. You'll want a high DPI mouse to cover the real estate efficiently, otherwise you'll waste time searching for the pointer and refocusing your attention from one side to the other.

- very good built in speakers and audio controls - I haven't felt the need one time to add external speakers which is a very nice touch since the display port or hdmi cable will carry the sound and video in one without the need for additional wiring.

CONS:
- I hate to say it, but LG screwed the pooch on this monitor - there is HORRIBLE backlight bleed in the corners of the screen. When you boot up the corners as far in as 4 inches on both left hand corners of my screen are ORANGE, not black. That is unacceptable for a monitor of this price, and that is the primary reason I am returning this monitor.

- Another MAJOR problem. With a windows desktop at least, if you put your computer to sleep, sometimes when you turn the computer back on, the monitor doesn't come back on with the system. Using the joystick control to turn the monitor off and on doesn't work either. I have to actually unplug the power cord from the back and plug it back in to get the monitor to respond. This is the extremely annoying when the first thing you do when you start working is fix your monitor.

- in order to change between your ports (display port to either HDMI 1 or 2) you have to go through a super annoying set of menu screens because all of the controls are inside an on screen display menu controlled by a little joystick in the center of the bottom front of the monitor. Changing inputs takes no less than 4-5 joystick actions and 3 different menu screens which are not exactly snappy in their response time. This is a particular problem when you are using PBP from two inputs or switch between inputs often for gaming consoles or other devices. Additionally, the picture by picture feature which is fantastic in its own right, requires a lot of time to configure in the on screen menus using that joystick because it does not automatically detect what inputs have signals coming in. IF my laptop is on HDMI 1 and my desktop is on the display port, the desktop MUST me the master window b/c that is the only way it is usable in PBP which is annoying, and the second screen does not know whether a signal is coming from HDMI 1 or 2, so if you want to do PBP for two devices you have to go into the menu and spend a couple of solid minutes screwing around with it trying to get it to pick up the signals properly. They really should have added a simple input selection button in addition to the joystick to make this monitor more functional.

- Programs do NOT scale properly from 1080p to 1440p resolutions. They are designed to work in 16:9 format, and this screen is 21:9. While in theory that's great, if the application doesn't have a native resolution setting to match 1440p, then what you get is one of three things:
1. The app will fill in the gaps around the native resolution with black or gray bars to the left and/or right of your app wasting your real estate;
2. The display or your GPU will stretch the window from its original resolution to fit the whole screen which distorts the images and makes them look 'fatter' than they should; or
3. You will get the original resolution which only fills about 1/4-1/3 of your screen.
Since there are very very few applications, including most games that support 1440p, this is a major problem.

- if you don't have a very powerful GPU, don't bother. Most GPUs don't have display port connections, which is the only way to run this screen at 60hz (true for many high resolution monitors, not just this one) otherwise it runs at 30hz which will cause eye strain after a while. Even if you have a display port, if it's not display port 1.2 it won't run at 60hz.

VERDICT:
- if you work in video editing, animation, or other professional areas like this, and you only use your monitor using one input for most of the time and you need lots of screen real estate and have a very high end workstation, then this screen may serve your needs well, although it's still not 4k resolution which is the standard moving forward for video so 1440p may not cut it.

- if you're looking for a gaming monitor get a 4K Ultra HD monitor for this reason - no consoles support 4K yet, and because they run at 1080p, if you want your games to scale properly you need a screen that runs at a multiple of 1080p native resolution. Because 4K runs at 3840x2160, a 1920x1080 Full HD signal will simply scale up to fit the whole screen.

- there's a lot of talk about curved monitors. I'll be honest, that was one of the biggest selling points for me on this screen because I thought it would be more impactful on my viewing experience. Take my advice, don't let that be a big factor for you. After about 30 seconds of using it you dont' even notice the curve any more its so slight. The only part that's really curved is the back which you don't see. The front curve is probably 1 degree or something very very low. Neat concept, but until the curves are larger it won't really be a big deal. UNLESS you are using multiple displays and you want to set up a batman lair type surround video screen, then by all means get curved displays.

For full disclosure, I have decided to replace this monitor with the BenQ BL3201PH CAD Monitor - it only has 2" less screen space, is 4K UHD, the screen rotates to portrait mode changing layout automatically, and it has an external dedicated control button to switch between the incredible array of design settings that are available for CAD, animation, etc. without having to use some tiny joystick and tediously work through menus. The stand also swivels, where the LG doesn't, and it has the same type of height and pivot adjustments. It's worth a comparison if you're about to drop close to a thousand bucks on a screen. The price is comparable.

text:
Easily the best TV available today (except for its more expensive siblings). The 65B6P has the same panel and outstanding picture quality as the G6P ($8k) and E6P ($6k), the only things you lose are 3D capabilities, the soundbar (is anyone really going to use a soundbar on a TV this expensive?), and the panel on glass design. The 2016 OLEDs are a substantial improvement over 2015. Color range has been expanded, judder issues have been eliminated, the grays are superior, max brightness has been enhanced, the smart TV processor is faster, and Dolby Vision support has been added. It is easily worth the extra $1k or so you will pay over the 2015 models. The only downsides to this TV is the cost and the fact it will ruin every other TV for you. Grade is a small company from BROOKLYN, NY... They started out 75 or so years ago making needles for phonograph players. All their products are excellent. text:
I have many of the same problems other people here have. I don't know why people give this 5 stars while seeing the same problems as me.
List of issues on a 2012 Audi A4 using a iPhone 6 Plus running iOS 8.2.

1. I need to disable the car's blue tooth. Otherwise, I will hear skips when playing music through Apple's Music App.
2. The MMI will show the music information reliably only when using the car's interface (MMI) to control the music. Changing music on the phone causes the MMI to become confused. It won't show the current song playing and it will eventually go back to playing your first playlist. If you don't have any playlists the first song in your catalog will be played.
3. The unit doesn't reliably continue playing the last song. Example: play a song, turn off the car, leave, and then come back. Sometimes the last song played is continued. Most of the time the first song in your playlist is played. If you don't have any playlists then the first song in your catalog is played.

Sometimes, the unit does work correctly. That's what really bothers me. Sometimes changing the song on the phone will update the MMI correctly. Considering the issues I can't recommend this at the given price. It is too expensive considering it only works correctly some of the time. Unfortunately, I don't see anything available that is guaranteed to be better.

title: Excellent quality 5-port Ethernet switch with a great warranty and ...
text: Excellent quality 5-port Ethernet switch with a great warranty and repair policy.  I originally purchased this as a mistake not noticing it was a 10/100 or "fast" Ethernet with only 100 Mb/s speed.  I decided to keep it since a $10 rebate was being offered by Netgear.  I also thought it could easily be used for my entertainment devices - TV, DVD and Audio receiver since all of those devices have 100 Mb/s Ethernet ports.  Using this switch between those 3 devices and the router has improved the efficiency of this segment of my network.  Constant re-transmitting of packets due to packet collision errors is a thing of the past with this unit installed.  The only complaint I have isn't about the device at all.  I found it disturbing that Netgear would NOT honor their mail-in $10 rebate.  They denied it saying only 1 rebate per household.  Since I submitted their mail-in rebate for the gigabit switch (GS105NA 5-port), they would not honor the rebate for this switch.  Not good.  I would understand if I purchased two identical switches but that was not the case.  I purchased two different models and each of them had a mail-in $10 rebate offered.  I have used Netgear products for many years now and have always found them to be a very good company to work with.  But in this particular rebate issue, I feel they are not treating me fairly at all.  Their wording in the small print "one rebate per household" should only apply to the same item and not include a different item being purchased by a person in that household.  Basically, I paid the same for this item that I did for their gigabit switch I mentioned above.  If I would have known it would work out this way, I would have cancelled the order for this item.  I found a good use for it with my home theater devices so the "pain" is reduced.  It would be nice though if Netgear customer service contacted me and made good on their rebate especially since I have spent hundreds of dollars on their products over the last few years.  I don't expect that to happen at all.

title: This Thing Is AWESOME!
text:
I live in an old NYC Apartment Building with a bunch of other tenants with wi-fi. Needless to say, although my 2G had decent range, the range on my 5G suffered tremendously.

(Basically, if my router was out of site, I had no real access to 5G.)

In my bedroom, not only was 5G inaccessible, but the slower 2G was unacceptable (and unstable).

So... I purchased this, followed the WPS instructions 2x (twice), as per instructions (for those operating a dual band router).

The instructions are simple:

1st, plug in and power on the extender near the router (and give it a minute to 'warm up').

2nd, press the WPS button on the extender (it will blink repeatedly).

3rd, press (and in my case, hold) the WPS button on the router (which blinked as well, on the router).

4th, wait for the WPS LED on the extender to turn solid green (which indicates a connection (1st, to the 2G).

***Repeating steps 2-4 will link a second connection to 5G (if you have a dual-band router).

5th, unplug the extender, and place/plug it midway between the router and the device(s) which will access it (which in my case was near the entrance of my bedroom).

Lastly... Search for the extender's SSID --- ending in '_EXT'.

Since I wanted to extend and obtain access to 5G, I searched for the '...5G_EXT', typed in the same password used to access my roter's wi-fi, and VIOLA! I now have access to 5G in my bedroom, all bars MAXED!

Since my devices aren't accessing the 5G from the router directly, there is some (theoretical) loss in speed (which I do not notice).

One thing for sure, however, is the internet speed in my bedroom is now MUCH faster (and more reliable) since I can now tap into the 5G speeds which I couldn't access before the extender.

Thus, "Mission Accomplished!"

The directions are so simple, I think a lot of people over-complicate it. I almost did.

They said to repeat the steps to link a second connection to 5G; that's what I did.

Maybe someday I'll try to configure it for other security measures I've read other reviewers mentioned...

But for now... No more 2G for me! ...and that has made ALL the difference 😉👍

(Btw... I am using the 1200 model.)

Hope this helps.

title: Unstable with Win 10 and no option to downgrade
text:
I needed an upgrade to my aging Toshiba laptop. This computer seemed to check all the boxes, latest Intel processor, SSD C drive and standard 1T D drive, 17" display and 16G of memory.

It arrived with Windows 10 Home. I have not been a fan of Windows 10 and frankly, have been avoiding it for some time now. But, with no drivers available for Windows 7 for this laptop I was stuck.

Right off the bat, the problems started. First, when it would sit idle and go into hibernate mode, it would never come out. No amount of button pushing could wake it up. So, power cycle it to get it back and immediately disable hibernate mode.

I purchased a license for Windows 10 Pro and upgraded the laptop. For a while it seemed like it was working fine but there were still occasional lockups.

Finally, while I was away for the long weekend after the 4th of July the OS updated itself (it seems nearly impossible to stop that from happening with Win 10) and the computer became totally unstable. If would get to the login screen but soon after would black screen with a spinning mouse cursor. Sometimes you could log in and start working, but invariably the black screen would return causing you to potentially lose work. After much googling and trying to solve this issue the configuration got corrupted and it would no longer boot...not even to Safe Mode. I was unwilling to spend hours or days trying to recover this and get it to a stable point again. Nobody should have to do that.

At this point I had had it with this thing. I needed a fast, reliable machine for work and this wasn't it. Fortunately, I was still within the 30 day window to return it, so I packed it up and sent it back.

Too bad, really. When I was younger I would always use ASUS motherboards in the computers I built. But unfortunately, the combination of Win 10 and this computer was a match made in hell.

title: A magnificent scope at a very reasonable price... don't waste your money on cheaper items, they will NOT perform like this one.
text:
We were given a cheap $50 microscope kit for our daughters. They were so excited to receive it and play... to be suddenly dashed into frustration and sadness when the images through the microscope were so blurry as to be useless. Seeing their enthusiasm remaining to play with the plastic toy even though it could never do what they hoped, we decided to obtain a real microscope to connect to our computer to foster their love of exploration and science.

This microscope is AMAZING. The images that came from it on the same slide that the previous $50 scope saw as blurry somethings were suddenly in sharp focus with amazing detail! Took about a minute to figure out how to operate the optics, zooming around until we were actually focussed on our slide instead of through the slide into the light source. Then pure beauty.

The feel of it is hefty and quality. The control knobs (coarse and fine scale) for zoom and pan are magnificent and lab-grade. Installing the software was flawless and instantly started working the moment we ran it. I have no complaints, as I will be using this exclusively for broadcasting what we're seeing up on a large monitor so all can see.

Ignore the users that complain about a lack of manual. The company sends a white paper that contains the weblink to download a thorough manual, and emailed me after the transaction to ensure I got the link.

I cannot be happier. I feel like I just saved my daughters' interests in science and microscopy singlehandedly through this purchase.

Spend the money, and enjoy the quality. You won't regret it.

title: Best Bang for Your Buck Laptop
text:
Coming from a $2000 gaming desktop and a MacBook pro, I didn't know what to expect from a chromebook other than what I have read online. I was looking for a replacement for my MacBook, but I didn't want or need to spend so much money on a laptop that I would mainly be doing web browsing on (I can use my desktop for anything that requires real muscle). All I have to say is that this is definitely 'The Little Laptop That Could'. I usually have pretty high expectations for my devices being in the IT field, but wow has this thing surpassed my expectations. It is quick and snappy and handles most tasks without even breaking a sweat. For web browsing, this is all the laptop you need. I am heavily invested in google services (google drive, gmail, google photos, google play music, etc.) so this works perfectly, but I would say that if you are not a big google user, especially if you don't use google drive or gmail, a chromebook might not be the best laptop for you. What makes this laptop even better though is the ability to use android apps, so for some light photoshop or lightroom work, I can use the android app which works flawlessly. The display on this thing is second to none, and the keyboard, while small, feels just like my macbook. The two biggest gripes that people have (the small keyboard and the lack of keyboard back lighting), are over exaggerated and I have never had a problem with them.

Pros:
- amazing screen
- ChromeOS is a pleasure to work with
- keyboard & trackpad are excellent
- build quality is better than $1000+ windows/mac laptops
- battery life is awesome
- integration with google services is seamless
- very easy to use for both novices and professionals
- touch screen and stylus are a good bonus

Cons:
- OP1 chipset can stutter sometimes, if you'll be doing HEAVY work on Chrome you might want to go with a chromebook with an m3 processor or better

Overall: This is the best money I have spent on a tech product in a long time. If I find continued success with ChromeOS I might permanently migrate to it
