title: reliable brand, good value for money...
text:
There is not much to say about this external hard drive. I bought it for using as a Time machine backup device in my macbook pro. For that purpose it works okay. I needed to reformat it for mac for that purpose but before that I tried it on my pc and it is ready to go with no need for reformatting or setting up

The USB 3.0 capability is a plus (but it is also backward compatible with USB2.0 as well). I have seen a data transfer rate of upto 80.6 mb/sec and an average of 70-75mb/sec while transferring a 2.2gb video file into the drive. When I transferred the same file from the drive back to my laptop the maximum transfer rate was 101mb/sec and the average was 80-90mb/sec. Of course these values depend on the file as well but I measured similar values with different files so I can say it is consistently fast..

It comes with an approximately 18.5 inches long transfer cable and through this cable it transfers both data and power. Other than that it does not offer a case or anything else. The device has limited warranty but, to me it is very difficult to make a warranty claim for an external hard drive since the warranty only covers none user mediated errors and most drives do fail either due to dropping or not safely removing neither of which are covered by this limited warranty. However, This hard drive is UL certified and that is a plus in terms of electrical safety (yet it does not guarantee it won't ever fail).

WD is a reliable brand in external hard drive market and in addition to this 1gb WD element, I also have a WD passport ultra which I use for backing up my PC. The main difference between these two exactly same size (3.2 X 4.3X 0.5 inches) devices is that the ultra comes with the full version of the WDsmartware software which automatically backs up the PC when the device is connected. This cheaper model has only the trial version of that software but honestly, if you are buying it for mac's you don't ever need it anyways (time machine does the same thing for free).

Currently (april 2015) this is one of the cheapest (among well known brands) 1tb device in amazon market place so I can easily recommend this as a backup drive to whoever is looking for one...

title: Another nice effort from AMD
text:
A nice APU if you have "realistic" expectations about what it is and isn't. It IS a great APU that has enough built in graphic power to power a day to day work, web, email machine and be able to do some "moderate" gaming at lower resolutions and FPS. I ISN'T a high power gaming platform! It will be hit or miss what games and resolutions you will be able to play. Trial and error plus reviews will tell you what works with this APU. I can tell you that this chip really needs the fastest RAM speeds for full performance. IMO 2133 MHz or faster DIMMS. Overall I like where AMD is going with their APU's so we should see even better stuff down the road. For now though the 7850K is the boss.

I used this APU in a new build for my daily driver. Used a Fractal Define R4 case, ASUS A88X-PRO motherboard, ADATA XPG V1.0 OC Series 16GB DDR3 2133MHZ memory. I didn't use the stock cooler that came with the chip, I installed a CoolerMaster Hyper 212 evo due to the fact that this is a 95 watt chip and tends to run a bit hotter. My uses are primarily web, streaming HD content, email, light video editing, and recording music. The APU delivers everything I need for that. Easily driving my HP 25bw and 23bw monitors at native resolution.

Machine booted up perfectly first time and has run stable with a fresh install of Win 8.1. I was able to use the auto overclocking feature on the ASUS A88X to get an overclock of 4558.0 MHz on the CPU and 960.0 MHz on the GPU with the system remaining stable. IMO If you're looking for an APU build you can't go wrong with this chip.

title: My new A4 (and why I picked it instead of the A6)
text:
Like many people looking at this A4 speaker, I debated many months between the A4 & the A6. I ultimately decided upon the A4 for a simple reason - Amazon dropped the price a bunch and I couldn't pass it up! It was stuck at $250 for months and finally dropped to $165 for a day. I don't remember if it was a deal of the day or not, but I snagged it during that brief drop.

Now, for the CSI A4 speaker itself. My old center was from a Polk HTIB (Home Theater in a Box) set and the A4 is a big upgrade from that and rounds out my speaker set (PSW505 sub & RTI A5 fronts) nicely. I should have replaced the center speaker earlier, but didn't - there's just something about a sub-woofer that I've never been able to resist! I use my system for low to moderate volume music, movies, and TV watching. The most immediately noticeable change is that dialog in movies is much more balanced. I no longer have to increase the volume during talking scenes and scramble to lower it during action scenes. What a great change!

Another factor between the A6 & A4 - the A6 is a good bit bigger than the A4 based on the product documentation and the A4 isn't small. It's 3-4x bigger than my old center. I measured my shelving and knew i had a good bit of work for the A6, but if I went with the A4 I could just raise my TV on its stand. It arrived and the A4 just barely fit even after raising the TV. I'm glad I didn't go with the A6 and have to deal with the extra hassle of drilling holes, filing metal, etc. to raise my TV enough for the A6 to fit!

Should I have spent the extra bucks and gone with the A6? I'll never know. I'm very satisfied with the A4 and don't see a reason any time soon to replace it.

title: Nice speaker in this catagory
text:
This speaker can be fickle. I've listened to it next to my Bose Soundlink Mini ll [[ASIN:B00WK47UZC Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker II (Pearl)]] and depending on what I'm listening to it can lag behind or crush the Bose.

We put on Paul Hardcastle a wonderful contemporary and crossover jazz artist whose tracks often feature a strong bass line. Once we turned up the sound to fill up the room this little speaker gets pretty muddy and you lose some of the midrange and the highs were almost undetectable. The separation just fell apart. Lowering the volume helped a some, but the bass just overpowered the mix.

Next, I put on Robin Trower, Joe Satrianni and this tube of sound beat the Bose hands down. Filled the room with sound while the Bose just muted the sound from these artists across the span of bandwidths specific to the songs I listened to and the Bose was unimpressive.

I tried some Christmas jazz. Louis Armstrong playing Cool Yule, Bing Crosby singing White Christmas...and the sound was very nice from either of the two speakers.

To summarize, neither of these corners the small speaker sound market. The Bose is far more portable and feature rich. But lacks sound dynamics in certain music environments and at higher volume. It isn't a room filling speaker from my observations.

The Samsung can be an exceptional value but can lose separation of the low/mid/high ranges as you increase the volume in some music applications as described above, but can outperform the Bose in others. It can fill the room with rich balanced sound in some music genres, but not all.

If you can afford it...get both. Listen to the Bose on the beach, camping, and out on your deck. Listen to the Samsung in your reading room, bedroom or anywhere you have a power source and want a smaller personal speaker with rich sound potential.

title: A unique high-tech blast from the past
text:
This is a cameras that is perfect for some but not something that everyone will find useful. The ideal user is someone who wants a simple to use digital camera that has the ability to instantly print the photo without dealing with a PC or conventional printer. This does a pretty good job of accomplishing that goal. But, if you’re looking for a more advanced point and shoot with lots of image features, this may not be your best option.

The camera itself feels very solid, but lacks a key digital camera feature: a view screen. At first glance may seem to be a major omission. But, this camera is designed to be a high-tech replacement for the old-style Polaroid instant cameras by instantly (well, relatively instantly) printing the photo on Zink paper. Note that the paper needs to be purchased separately, and is pretty much an essential component for using the camera. While you can store photos on an SD card, the camera is really designed to be used with the Zink paper.

Usage is very straightforward – it’s about as point and shoot as you can get. That’s great for those who don’t want to fiddle with any settings, but it does put some constraints on image quality. I’ve had about 20% of my photos so far turn out less than ideal due to improper focus, poor white balance, poor resolution and/or incorrect color registration. That’s my major complaint with this camera – the paper is costly, and when you have to toss (or at least not really like) one in five photos, the cost can add up.

The images are small – the paper is only 2 by 3 inches. On the plus side it has a peel and stick backing, so you can use the photos as “post-its” very easily. Again, this is keeping with the intent of the camera, so I won’t downgrade the rating due to the small photo size.

Other negatives for me is that the battery is not user-replaceable. I’ve had too many electronic products with built-in batteries that had to be trashed since the internal battery no longer held a charge. I’m also not fond of the lens cap. It’s very easy to take off (it’s held in place by magnets) but there’s no attachment to the camera, so it’s very easy to misplace.

But this does score well with regard to ease of use and fun. As a test of ease of use I handed this to my Mom who is technically challenged, to say the least. She had no problems snapping photos and loved having the image print right there. She’s never liked using a digital camera in the past due to difficulty using it and dealing with image files. This was right up her ally.

While I’ll drop the rating to 4 stars due to the image quality issues that can crop up, overall this is a unique camera. It’s not right for everyone, but if you’re looking to revisit the days of the Polaroid instant camera while staying in the digital world, this is well worth considering.

title: M.2 Drive Cooling
text:
UPDATE: 01/28/19 This product is still ticking and keeps the ssd cool no matter the demand placed on it. Glad it has held up for this length of time.

This M.2 pcie card is listed for use with the Samsung line of nvme SSD's, BUT, this works right out of the box with a MyDigital BPX 80 nvme SSD. No drivers needed.

I had tried another pcie card without a fan that did work, but it did not reduce the temperatures of the drive during use. I almost decided on a pcie card with dual fans to reduce temps, just fans and not an interface for the M.2 drive. The fan only card would have been mounted directly below the M.2 drive where it was located on the motherboard. I am glad I chose to take a chance with this card even though there was no indication that it would work with any other drives than were mentioned.

This M.2 drive is the system drive and works just as if it were mounted directly to the motherboard, Z170 chipset. The temperatures have dropped by 13C when idle and 17C when under a heavy load. At the high end it previously ran as high as 90C when under a heavy load. With this card installed in the pcie slot and the fan pulling upwards, the drive's temperature maxed out at 73C. You can locate the fan to either side of the card for the flow you desire. The fan is quite small but does a good job with zero noise. The adjustment knob screws counter clockwise for increased speed, I twisted to full and left it at that. The card has large open areas for air flow.

The item shipped without the case bracket attached, long one only, and the fan was attached by one screw only. There were plenty of screws for the installation of the fan, M.2 drive and case bracket. The fan has 4 standoffs w/screws and there was one extra screw to mount the fan to the standoffs. There is also a screw kit for attaching the M.2 drive to the card and it includes a small phillip screw driver.

So far, so good. If it holds up over time it will be money well spent.

title: Well worth the money and probably more.
text:
I have a small studio. I don't need lighting to light up a stage or a stadium. I do, however, periodically do charity photo sessions like Breakfast with Santa for free. What I need is cost effective and reliable. With that in mind, I decided to invest in some strobe lights. Keeping flashes synced and changing batteries all day was too painful. Having to get people in place for each shot, gives me a few seconds between each shutter release (or a lot more), so instant refresh is also not an issue.

The price range on strobes is outrageous. While there may be "reasons" to spend the extra money, a good photographer knows how to adjust and doesn't need to waste the extra money. So I chose to try out the low price NEEWER units (I've had great experiences with their shutter releases and off camera remotes). Great decision. Work right out of the box. The modeling light lets me see the setup before I ever release a shutter, and the issues of sleeping flash units and dead batteries is gone. Add a portable battery jumper with AC outlet from my local Harbor Freight hardware store for under $100, and I have portable lighting anywhere.

title: Perfect, but you need to know an install trick; AND successfully cloned from smaller AND from RAID 0 paired drive
text:
Quite nice. The included 2014 True Image (linked) software included took two attempts to clone 930 gigs from a 1.5 tb to the 1 gig Crucial. The first time I downloaded the True Image software to the old disk and cloned it including the downloaded TI software. This appeared to clone my HP disk properly and I could boot -- but then I found that I could not get access to Windows profiles and any personal data. After researching the problem, I saw that someone had posted a potential solution deep in the bowels of the Internet. I re-cloned, but this time I made a boot CD from True Image and then deleted the True Image software off of the c drive. When I booted into the boot CD this allowed me to clone the c drive without the True Image software itself. For some unknown reason this worked perfectly and the new Crucial now gives complete access and no problems at all. Perfect.
And so I bought another 500 gig and put on another computer (Dell 8300). Again, used 2014 True Image included with the new disk. Used the exact same procedure. However, the Dell 8300 originally had two Seagate 1TB drives paired in a RAID 0 config (this makes it look like one drive). On the net, people said cloning from paired RAID 0 disks could not be done. However, the cloning DID work and the single new Crucial 500 gig successfully took the place of the two Seagate 1TB drives. (I would add that the amount of data on this computer was only about 100 gig, so I wasn't also trying to do something that was near the storage limit of the Crucial.)

title: Setup problems? Can't log in? Read this!
text: When you plug this extender into an Ethernet socket you have to go to www.asusrouter.com (it has a built in web server) to change your password. Things went south immediately at this point as once I changed it I could never log back in. I reset it several times with no luck. So I took it to my office and it worked perfectly there. Hmm. Back home again it was back to the same problem. Then I realized what the issue was - my existing ASUS RTN66R was the device responding to www.asusrouter.com - not the new N900 Extender - so no wonder it would not accept the new password I was entering as I use a different password for the router. WELL ASUS - THAT IS DUMB! Most of us will buy this to extend an ASUS ROUTER so you need to give this a DIFFERENT default hostname!! With that knowledge, I turned off my router while I logged onto the extender and set the new password - success. Once logged in, I turned my router back on and then waited for it to boot back up and then connected the new extender to my wireless network. Now it works perfectly. Luckily I am the Chief Technology Officer and Sr. VP of an IT firm so I was able to troubleshoot the problem and know what to do. But many less savvy consumers may not. Shame on you ASUS!

title: Superb travel/walk around zoom lens
text:
I purchased this lens from Amazon to go with my D7200. I have mostly been an FX user the last 4 years and currently also own a D750 and D800. My interest in going back to the DX camera and lenses started with using the D7200 as a way to get extra reach for my telephoto lenses such as the Nikkor 80-400mm VR and the newest Nikkor 300mmF4 VR.

I was enjoying how well the D7200 worked with these lenses but I no longer had any wide angle "walk around lens" to use with this camera.

I did have the Nikkor 24-120mmF4 VR and the 24-85mmF3.5/5.6 VR but those lenses are best suited for the FX format.

I purchased the 16-80mmF2.8/4 VR on a whim. Having previously owned the 16-85 version, I hoped that this lens would have the improvements necessary to make it a "keeper".

After a few days of testing and comparisons, I must admit that I will definitely keep this lens!

My first test was to compare the 16-80 on my D7200 to the 24-120 on my D750. This is an easy test to do as the equivalent zoom ranges and apertures are the same (except for the ability of the 16-80 to go to F2.8).

The result of this test amazed me. The 16-80 was sharper at all apertures from F4 through F16. It did not matter what focal length I was at. In addition, the 16-80 was better at contrast. Dark areas were darker, yet had more detail. A side benefit was the lack of any vignetting when a filter was attached to the 16-80 lens. This is not the case with the 24-120, when at 24mm focal length.

I then compared the 16-80 (set to 34mm on my D7200) with the Nikkor 50mF1.8 mounted on my D750. Again, I was surprised that the 16-80 actually looked better at all apertures but F4, where the 50mm was slightly better in the extreme corners. Again, contrast was noticeably better on the 16-80. This was the first time any lens I owned outperformed this 50mm prime.

I also own the Nikkor 20mmF1.8. Testing this lens directly with the 16-80 on my D7200 did show the superior performance of the 20mm lens, but the differences went away by F8. Both these lenses show the excellent contrast that comes with Nikon's latest coatings.

The Nikkor 16-80mmF2.8/4 VR is slightly lighter than the 16-85 but otherwise about the same size. The focus speed seems similar to the 24-120, and the VR seems to work as advertised.

At 80mm, I compared the 16-80 to my Nikkor 70-200F4 VR. The first test was done with the 16-80 on the D7200 (set for 80mm) and the 70-200 on the D750 (set to 120mm). The result of this test was almost a dead heat with maybe a slight edge to the 70-200.

I did a second test where both lenses were mounted on the D7200 (at 80mm). In this test the 70-200 clearly won. This is not surprising in that the FX format puts real demands on the corner performance of FX lenses whereas the DX format does not. in addition, the D750 has an anti-alias filter. The D7200 does not, allowing for better overall resolution if the lens can pull it off.(and the 70-200 certainly can!)

I would go on a hike with the 16-80 on a D7200 and feel confident that I would get as good or better photos than if I carried the 24-120 with the D750. In low light, or the need to have limited DOF, I might want the FX combo, but for most scenery shots, I want maximum DOF and high ISO's are generally not needed. Do remember that DX cameras have 1.5 times greater DOF than FX.

This lens is pricey. If I could not afford it, I would be temped by the Sigma 17-70mmF2.8/4. It looks to have similar performance overall.

The only caveat, is the distortion. At 16mm, this lens has lots of barrel distortion. Strangely, it goes away by 19mm and quickly becomes pincushion all the way to 80mm. Most zooms seem similar in this regard. Just beware that you will want to correct for this distortion if buildings or ocean etc. are predominant in your images.

I have not really tested this lens wide open at F2.8. It looked really good, but I just don't go there much, as I am mostly doing scenery shots rather than people shots, where one often wants to isolate the subject from the background. I can tell you this. Looking through the viewfinder one notices that the image is bright! That is an advantage of 2.8F worth noting.

All in all, it is great to see such lenses come onto the market. The latest 24mp sensors are very demanding. This lens will hold up to those kind of sensors.

title: A Converter That Actually Works with a Mac!
text:
I had some 8mm cassette tapes made with a 20 year old Sharp Camcorder, which I wanted to convert to digital format on my computer. The camcorder has only one outlet for a cable connection. I ordered a video converter that was priced around $100 on Amazon, and it was supposed to work with either Windows or Mac computers. I have two iMac computers. I could not get that converter to work on either one and ended up returning it. Later I ordered this Vidbox for Mac. Although there are other converters, somewhat cheaper, that are supposed to work with either Windows or Macs, I was willing to pay a bit more for one that was designed just for Macs. And it works!

The instructions are fairly easy to understand and set up was easy. You first download the driver, either from the enclosed CD or from the internet. Since I have a CD reader with my Mac, I used it. Be aware that during the registration process, you might get a message saying you are not connected to the internet. Just ignore it and proceed.

I did run into a problem connecting the converter to my camcorder. The cables that come with the converter will not connect into a single outlet, but rather require a three pronged RCA connection. I tried using another cable that converts a one prong connection to a three prong cable, but this would not work. Then I tried the cable that came with my camcorder, which has one prong at one end and two (white and yellow) at the other. This one did work! Of course it carries only one sound channel to the computer, but my camcorder only had one sound channel anyway, so no problem.

My tapes are about two hours long, so it takes two hours to convert them. But again, this is no problem, as you can proceed to use your computer for other things while the conversion process is taking place. The only problem here that I ran into was that I had trouble locating where the files were stored on my computer. I didn't pay enough attention to where it was putting them when converting. But I finally found them. This converter does not provide tools for editing your videos, so you have to use iMovie (included on most Mac computers) to do this. I'm in the process of trying to edit some of mine (cutting out blank spaces, joining two segments together, etc.), but that's another story not related to this converter.

Overall I am very pleased. I haven't tried using this converter for VCR tapes yet, but I assume it will work just as well with them. If not, I'll later edit this review accordingly.

title: Doesn't work all the time...  Update: now it does!!
text:
This was very easy to install. It comes with an adapter that uses the cigarette lighter plug. But that would leave a wire hanging down from the windshield. I don't think the power wire is long enough to run around the edge of the windshield, unless you had a very small car with a very small windshield. Instead I spent the extra money on this:
[[ASIN:B00MH4ZVHO Dash Camera Vehicle Hard Wire Kit - Mini USB Compatible with G1w / G1w-C / G1WH / GT680W / Mini 0801 / Mobius Action Spy Tec Camera and More | Car DVR Camera Recorder Dashboard Dashcam | Black Box Video Recorder |]]
and this:
[[ASIN:B001QRSBW0 Pico 0956PT 10 Amp ATM Mini Blade Fuse Add-A-Circuit Fuse Holder]]
The hardwire kit will work with this camera. The Add-A-Circuit should be vehicle dependent...so be sure you get the one that matches the fuses in your car. The one I posted here should work a lot of cars, but you should double check. It's much easier than just jamming the power wire into the fuse box like I used to do.

Anyway, with those parts the install was easy. The camera itself seems to work great. I haven't had to go back and use the footage yet...but I've checked the card a few times and it's recording fine. BTW, as other reviews mention, get the 32GB card max.

The settings out of the box are fine...I didn't change much. But the manual is actually very good (nice surprise) and it's easy to change anything you want.

I had been thinking of getting this for a while, but never pulled the trigger. I was riding in a car the other day and it was struck by a guy driving recklessly. Fortunatley it wasn't my car, and I wasn't driving (and no one was hurt), but I remember thinking that if there was a dash cam installed, the issue of who was at fault would be much more simple. I pulled the trigger that night, got the camera in 2 days, and was up and running a couple hours after that. Worth it for the peace of mind.

**Update 4-18-16**
I've been periodically checking the SD card and the recordings are sporadic. It will record for 5 min, then it stops and doesn't start a new recording. Sometimes it does, sometimes it doesn't. Also, the other day I saw someone driving crazy on the highway, I hit the red button to save the file, but when I got home, it wasn't saved. So, it only records sometimes...which is definitely NOT OK for something like this. The point is to have a recording when you need it. With this unit I have no confidence that it's recording.

Maybe my unit went bad? At this point I would not buy again.

**Update 7/9/17**
I kept this unit going until I sold the car recently. Here is what I found over the past year. The type of SD card you use seems to matter. I don't recall what SD card I was using initially, but something about it was not compatible with the unit. I cheaper card seemed to work much better. The biggest issue is that cold temps prevented my unit from working. The unit won't turn on until the temp inside the car is warm enough. I don't know what the unit has inside for power (battery), but whatever it is, doesn't seem to work when it's cold. So the first 15-20 min of each drive is not captured until the unit warms up...in the winter only. Aside from that, it seemed to work OK. I'd still keep my 2 star rating. In my new vehicle, I'll look around a bit before installing this again.

**Update 1/21/2020**
Rexing has been contacting me about some of the negative issues I had with my unit and sent me a new unit to replace my old one. This unit is an updated version and seems to work better than my original unit did. No problems with the recordings or power like I had before. It's a good unit and I'd recommend it for sure. Form factor is the same as the previous version, which is good. Some units look big and clunky, like a go pro stuck on your dash. This fits nicely behind your rear view mirror and is not visible at all. Good unit.

title: Good for UHF - but make sure you don't need VHF-low
text:
This antenna works well for UHF and the higher part of the VHF spectrum.

However, if you need to pick up VHF-low band channels - those which actually broadcast on 2-6 - you will have issues.

I am about 30 miles from the broadcast towers of the Philadelphia market. Philly is one of the TV markets which has a major network still broadcasting on a VHF low-band channel (WPVI - ABC channel 6). CBS and NBC still market their 'old' channel numbers (3 and 10) but are actually broadcasting in UHF.

This antenna receives the UHF channels quite well, as well as a VHF-high channel (12) without issues. But I can't get ABC.

title: I bought 3 Digital Picture Frames and compared their features
text:

The first thing I notice is that the Spiro Goods Digital Frame has a carbon fiber finish. Nix and Tenker are just generic plastic frame fronts. This makes a huge difference.

Secondly, let’s talk resolution. Spiro’s resolution is 1080p, compared to the other two at 720p. This is a massive upgrade as well.

The entire purpose of these Digital Frames is to display media in high quality, so Spiro’s Frame wins the most important feature.

Thirdly, the memory in Nix is only 8gb, where as in Spiro is 16gb. This means you can store DOU-BLE the media files on Spiro’s Digital Frame.

In terms of ease of set-up, they are both equally extremely easy.

However, you can play media right away directly from Spiro’s remote (which has more features than the Nix remote also).

My favorite frame from this comparison is the Spiro Digital Frame. And I didn’t even mention all the features it has here.

text:
I bought this backpack about 2 months ago when there were no photos of it, so I took a lot of pictures the day it arrived so I could contribute some. The backpack was just the style and size I was looking for, although admittedly not the material I was expecting. It's a bit more shiny / synthetic than I thought it would be, although I didn't mind it in the end. It does make a bit of a scratchy sound against my jacket when I walk, but nothing too noticeable.

Despite the material, it fits all my belongings for college perfectly: my 13" macbook pro 2015 fits nicely in the laptop pocket, my water bottle and umbrella fit well in the side pockets, and there are sooo many lovely pockets for all my other things. It is def waterproof--my laptop has stayed nice and dry, even without an umbrella. I love the style of it, and the luggage strap is unbeatable for me, since I fly frequently.

The biggest thing I was looking for was a backpack that wouldn't swallow me up (I'm a 5'0 petite girl), and this backpack looks just right on me. It looks slim, but can also hold a lot if you need it to. And so far, with 2 months of daily use, nothing's broken! So durability for me has been great.

The USB charging port is also handy when I'm in a pinch--sometimes I just plug it into my laptop.

Overall, I love this backpack a lot, and it's been a worthwhile purchase!

title: Small but mighty
text:
What a breath of fresh air. I have been using a Sony VAIO VPCCW 17 FX for years now, and the wear and tear is pretty evident. Files take ages to load, the cooling fan only seems to work about half the time, and the screen intermittently turns black. Needless to say, I was in the market for a long-overdue upgrade. I considered just getting a tablet but realized having a laptop is much more suited to my tasks. I definitely didn't need something too tech heavy, as I'm not a gamer, but simply wanted speed, efficiency, and a good quality screen.

The Dell notebook hit almost every mark. The size is absolutely perfect, not too heavy not to light but feels sturdy and well built. The screen is one of the best I've ever seen, boasting super high res HD, and even though it's smaller than my previous laptop, the screen feels easier to look at.

This is my first experience with Windows 8, which took a little adjusting coming from Windows 7. I'm still on the fence as to whether or not I like the new operating system, but I can say it's very smooth very quick and seems aptly matched for this notebook.

Coming from an Intel Core 2 Duo 2.2GHz processor to the 4th generation i5 is a night and day difference. Everything from web browsing, file loading, and startup time are so much faster.

The 500 GB hard drive is perfect for me as I store most of my files on the cloud anyway. I'm sure this laptop would perform even better with the smaller solid-state drive, but given the cost increase this would impose, the factory hard drive is apt.

An optical drive would be nice, but as of yet I have not had a need for one. The USB 3.0 ports cover most of my file sharing and software installing needs, and I can always get an external optical drive if need be.

My favorite feature has to be the touchscreen itself. The screen is very responsive, ultrafast and in many ways much easier than using a mouse. I now hate having to go back to my desktop and optical mouse.

Overall there are very few things I dislike about the Dell Inspiron notebook tablet convertible. To truly be more competitive, I think Dell could drop the price a bit, but even so it's still a great investment.

title: NOT worth it! Expandable is a joke and can't even download books from the Cloud without jumping!!!!
text:
VERY DISAPPOINTING! Not a Kindle standard device as I am used to! I have upgraded each and every time a Kindle has been released and this is the 1st that I will be returning due to false advertising (expandable storage is a joke) and extremely poor performance. This is my 1st poor review on anything kindle and I've had not only all the devices but currently run Fire TV and TV Stick in my home. Sad to see quality of product is going down as they grow. I've already purchased my daughter a 10 for Christmas and now I'm going to have to check that one out tomorrow and hope it is a problem with the 8's. I'm not holding out much hope and am guessing it'll be returned too!

DEVICE ISSUES:

As I was downloading books from my cloud (to match up with my currently owned device) the unit continued to recycle/refresh itself. Every minute or two it would "twitch" and blank out. Then it would pop back up to the book home screen NOT my library, where I was. My previous generation HDX was doing this more often which is a big reason as to why I rushed to purchase this new one (and was really happy that the timing was perfect for my old one to be crashing as I'm usually "lucky" enough to have a new release shortly after I've just replaced my device.) Now if this device can't even handle downloading books from my Amazon Cloud library on day one, how is it going to hold up after a month of use? VERY DISAPPOINTING! I wasn't even about to try running a movie on the device as a test, it couldn't handle downloading a book!!!! Very worried about my daughter's 10 being able to do any better!

But my biggest disappointment was the "expandable" storage. Now, if you want the storage for Music, Movies and Photos this may be a great feature for you. Unfortunately I mainly use mine as an e-reader and document device. The expandable storage therefore becomes useless to me. And the 1st time these restrictions were mentioned was when I turned on the device and was working on inserting the expandable card. Ridiculous! This was stated NO WHERE until I turned on the unit. Now don't I feel stupid for purchasing a useless piece of equipment. Not inspiring my continued loyalty with that little shocker Amazon!!!!

So, sad to say I will be doing my return as soon as this review is completed. My hopes for this device was that it was advanced in technology and a revolutionary "expandable" unit! Missed the boat on this one Amazon because it has failed miserably. I will stick with my previous generation HDX and cross my fingers that you get back to what I've known Amazon for: great products, great quality, up front information and great customer service. I'm sorry to say I think Amazon has lost it's way!

If this will be your first kindle unit, I'd recommend a previous generation device until they get their act together. I always recommend Kindles as they've been fabulous and everyone in our family has one! Don't judge all kindles by this miserable excuse for a device! The others have far surpassed my expectations and I would put my hard earned $$$ into one of those. They are well worth their prices! I wouldn't use this one over my HDX if it was FREE!!!

The factory speaker is nothing but a piece of paper hooked to a large plastic mount.
When you consider the steps to install these:
1) Drill out the factory rivets to remove the original speakers.
2) Rifle around the garage or take a trip to the hardware store for nuts and bolts that will fit in the now drilled out holes in the doors.
3) Mount the new speakers to these mounts making your own holes with a drill or self tapping screws that may have just required a second trip to the hardware store.
I could have taken a razor knife and cut out the paper from the factory mount and I would have had a slightly more heavy duty piece of plastic already riveted to the door that fit the new 6.5" speaker perfectly. The same drill or self tapping screws could have fastened the new speakers to the factory speakers in the same manner and the final product would have been a more secure mount. This was in a 09 Yaris. It had the cheapest factory speaker I have ever witnessed. If they had a magnet, it was no bigger than a dime, so it's possible other Toyota's will be different.

title: That solution angles the camera too far down and sounds like a recipe for disaster to me
text:
I purchased this wireless camera system for my 26 ft. travel trailer. I read many of the reviews that talked about the difficulty mounting the camera on the back (vertical) wall of a travel trailer or 5th wheel. The reviews noted that the camera mount does not allow enough room for the antenna to be attached when mounted vertically. I now understand what they were talking about. The camera mount is designed and engineered to attach to the roof (horizontal) of a vehicle - not on the back wall (vertical) of an RV. The bracket simply does not allow enough room for the antenna to be attached to the camera when you try to mount it on a vertical wall. You can make more room for the antenna by attaching the camera with only one screw on a side. That solution angles the camera too far down and sounds like a recipe for disaster to me.

To fix this issue, I bought a 4x4" outdoor plastic electric box and modified it. I took the front lid off and cut away 3 of it's sides making an "L" shaped shelf (4" long and wide and about 2" high). This allows the camera to be mounted away from the back of the wall and giving the antenna room to be attached and swivel freely. After some black spray paint to make it look professional, it was easy to mount my "shelf" to the back wall of the RV and then attach the bracket and then the camera.

I got a good signal and the picture quality of the camera was nice. Remember the monitor has a plastic protective covering that needs to be removed to get a good view.

If it wasn't for the mounting issue, I would have given this product 5 stars. Considering the price of this system, it would be nice if 4Ucam had included a separate bracket for mounting the camera vertically. There certainly have been enough reviews to warrant a review of the bracket design.

I too like many others fell in love with the idea of the Echo Show. I already had a slew of other Amazon devices that I was extremely happy with. Many devices. Five Amazon Fire TV's, two Echo Shows, three Echo Dots, and several different Kindles over the years. Hell, I even had a Fire phone at one time. The new Show units were not at a price point I was willing to pay but Amazon offered a discount of $-100.00 when purchasing two. As such I decided to bite the bullet and ordered two Echo Show units on the day that they were announced.

Like most shipments from Amazon the units arrived pretty quickly. I rushed home on my lunch break to check them out knowing they had arrived. The two separate display boxes were not properly packaged into the larger shipment box which caused one of the boxes to take some major damage. The unit itself was however undamaged.

I opened both units and plugged them both in the kitchen. I was thoroughly impressed with the design. I ordered the black units. Very modern, sleek, and a small enough form factor and yet still be viable as a screen. They were so cool, shiny, and new!

I quickly and easily connected them to wifi and updated the firmware. The interface was simple and as always using Alexa was a cinch. Over the next few days my teenage daughter and I had loads of laughs and other fun continuing our normal Alexa antics. The original excitement and fun continued for a few weeks and I tied more and more into home automation using Alexa. Then the newness wore off and the bad started to really show. Things I had not really noticed prior to owning an Echo Show but that I have realized are mostly just an Alexa plague. The Echo Show device I was so excited about, the now backbone to my home automation, and fairly invested in, had became the Echo NoShow.

To save time read the following paragraph and advice when thinking about a purchase. Otherwise feel free to read below for more detailed information regarding the Amazon Echo Show.

All-in-all the Echo Show is much like a blind date that never arrived or a blind date that arrived and pretended you weren't there. Aka the NoShow. The device had much promise and in fact promised a lot. In the end the device fails to meet those promises and is lacking in so many ways. The Show and built-in Alexa are flawed and have more downfalls than positive features. The good news is that Amazon can address most of these issues with a single firmware update and a complete redesign to their smartphone app and UI for the Show. Hopefully this happens sooner rather than later and prior to Echo Show 2. Until then keep your money and stick with your Echo or Dot, or even purchase a different home device. Both of my Show units are now merely over priced clocks. One in the kitchen and one in the bedroom.

I should note that I am a fairly tech savvy person before I note the good, bad, and the ugly.

Good things
- Small intelligent design: Still manages good sound and a decent display.
- Simple installation and setup: Up and running in less than five minutes.
- Amazon account synchronization: Anything and Everything Amazon with only a single sign-on.
- Alexa: A name we all know and are familiar with. Also. Litterally the only woman ever to sometimes listen to me. Who can't love that, right?
- Simple UI (User Interface): Navigation is a cinch with the voice control through Alexa and the touch screen.
- Easily connects to most other "smart" items: A simple search to find items using the Alexa app on your smart phone. Usually. Even allows IFTT.
- Calling and Video Calling: This feature is great especially with the device to device calls within your own account.
- Development: Amazon has been quick to encourage everyone to become involved with developing on the Alexa platform. Even as an end user you can setup an account and create your own Alexa skills.

Bad things
- UI (User Interface): Severely lacking options. Almost too many to name but I'll try. No real customization. You cannot easily add or remove cards from the display. Cards are basically information tidbits that display on the screen like a slideshow of sorts. Most if not all changes need to be completed via the Alexa app which is a whole other disappointment. All in all the display is limited to displaying the time, weather, Alexa tips, and some "news" tidbits. Things that should be simple are overly difficult or impossible. Alexa "Play Strangers to Ourselves by Modest Mouse." Simple enough. Alexa responds "playing the album Strangers to Oursleves by Modesf Mouse." The album begins playing and if available lyrics are displayed as well. Something missing however is the ability to see a list of songs on the album and choose songs from that list. Something easily accomplished on your phone. The same can be said for Amazon Prime video. The premise of being in the kitchen and watching the latest episode of your favorite show while you prepare a meal seems appealing. It would even be great if only it were so simple. Browsing videos is a joke as you are limited to scrolling to the right only and inquiry results are severely limited. In fact most interactions on screen scroll left to right only.
- Alexa: Alexa is still somewhat young in the AI assistant space and has much to learn from other more advanced AI such as Microsoft's Cortana. Simple questions are often answered with "I don't have an answer for that." or a simple pause and beep as if she didn't hear you in the first place. Fun interactions with Alexa are quickly worn out as too many things are repeated over and over. This is even the case for things where Alexa has several responses, yet gives the same response back to back daily. Often times throughout the day Alexa will randomly think she was called for when nothing remotely close to "Alexa" was uttered. Sometimes just a simple beep and a wait to hear what you want and sometimes she responds to things you haven't asked. Sometimes this is funny especially if she says something odd like "The Unicorn is a mythical creature, etc." when never summoned in the first place. For the most part these often unnecessary interruptions to normal conversation or a television show are a complete nuisance. At the same time Alexa often does not answer when beckoned and doesn't comprehend questions or statements, replying back nonsense. Voice training does not seem to help this downfall either. Alexa's ability to hear you from across the room is still somewhat true, at least until you try to call for her when music is playing, at which point even screaming "Alexa" from five feet away does nothing.
- Cards and Skills: First and foremost. Anything news or weather related is limited to being a Flash Brief skill. That's fine. Label it what you will. However making a person listen to a ton of information they don't specifically ask for is ridiculous. To hear news I shouldn't have to first listen to the weather. To hear "on this day" I shouldn't have to listen to the news or weather. Skills in general are weak and lackluster. This really isn't the fault of Amazon but still it's the platform. Amazon is definitely to blame for the 5000000000 completely worthless skills in the repo though. With no form of testing or approval methods for garbage available for addition to your library you could easily scroll through available skills for hours and find nothing of value.
- Loss of internet connectivity: Basically renders your device as useless even when trying to access your own devices.
- Loss of YouTube: This was a MAJOR blow. Not having access or the support of Google services is one thing but losing YouTube which was a major selling point is another. Even if Amazon plans to launch their own cloud video program it would take them decades to come close to branding as well as YouTube. This is also true for the lack of social media interaction.
- Device to device: The lack of device synchronization. Voice training does not carry over via your account and must be completed on each device. Not that voice training helps. Pickup resume or multi-device support of any kind is nonexistent. The ability to start a song or show in one room and have it paused and continued in another or the ability to play a song or show on all devices at once is missing.
- Shopping: Shopping is basically limited to Alexa show me your deals and those deals are limited to a handful of items which are 10/10 times trash. This is crazy to me because I know Amazon has the best algorithm there is for matching product to a person. On the website I can browse 1000 pages of deals and add filters to what's displayed. Thus showing me items I may actually have interest in buying. Alexa however limits deal items to pet products or over priced random crap. After ten days of asking Alexa to see her deals I learned that it wasn't going to change. Shopping in general is lame as well unless you have something you wish to reorder or if you know the exact item you want.
Lists: Not having the ability to create custom lists to interact with. You are limited to a todo list and a shopping list. That is all. You also have to say Alexa every time you want to add something. Viewing the list is only possible on your phone as asking Alexa about your list only involves Alexa reading everything back to you.
Dashwand integration: This is somewhat only to do with the dashwand but also somewhat the Echo Show as these devices could work great together. They however don't work together at all. In an ideal world I could ask Alexa to start a shopping list and add items that I scan from with my dashwand. Then when I was finished I could say that I was through adding. The dashwand however only scans and adds to your Amazon shopping cart. Let's face facts. We all probably buy tons of stuff from Amazon but are still left purchasing items in our local communities as well. Whether by choice or in my case out of necessity as I do not live in an area remotely near an Amazon distribution center.
- Commute times: Even knowing your work and home addresses aren't enough for Alexa to accurately give time to leave alerts or good approximations when asking Alexa how long it would take to get anywhere.

title: Very Fast and Well Worth the Very Low Price
text:
A surprisingly good tablet. The extra RAM makes all the difference. This tablet runs very smoothly and is very fast. The bump from 1 GB RAM to 1.5 GB RAM has freed the quad core processors from extra duty. Yes, the 1.3 GHz processors are not the same as the 1.5 GHz processors of previous models, but they are newer and have tested at faster speeds. My Fire HD 6 is not nearly as quick as this new HD 8.

Some may wonder if the 189 ppi screen resolution is sufficient. It is. Movies, videos and even SlingTV looks good on this screen. You won't be disappointed. In fact, you will be pleasantly surprised.

The tablet is thin, light and easy to hold. I bought the blue one and it's beautiful.

The new OS isn't out yet, but when it arrives Alexa will be on the tablet. No doubt other improvements will be included in the upgrade. The OS has been optimized very well.

The reading experience continues to improve. You can let the tablet read the book to you, flip through and view many pages without losing your place, use the X-Ray feature for a quick lookup of the characters or view pictures in the book. If you have a large Amazon book library this tablet is much better than using the Kindle app on a competing Android or iOS device.

$89 is a ridiculously low price for a tablet that is much better than last year's $149 tablet. If you want a fast, inexpensive tablet there really is no other choice but the Fire HD 8.

title: Fits the Arlo Pro 2 perfectly by itself, just replace  the tightening wheel with a simple 1/4 inch nut if using USB power cord.
text: These wall mounts are an excellent value at three for $12, and do hold the Arlo Pro 2 Cameras very securely.  You can use them wireless right out of the box , as well as with a USB Power cord. The only difficulty you may encounter with these 3-packs is that the Take-UP  Wheel to tighten it extra secure is too wide for using it with a power cord. That has nothing to do with the mounts, it is because ARLO placed the screw base very close to the power receptacle (see photo). You would run into that with any other third party base.  ARLO's base resolved this by using a small threaded tightener (see photo). Many people simply removed the tightening wheel and first screwed the camera all the way in, then did the final adjustment with the main tightening ears, but I simply removed the Take-Up Wheel and replaced it with a  simple 20 cent stainless steel 1/4 inch coarse thread #20, which is the thread of the Arlo unit (not fine thread). I have attached photos of the Mount with its WHEEL, a photo of the tightening wheel and my replacement nut, and a pic of the factory ARLO mount with its thin tightening nut.  For me it was no problem at all buying a simple nut so I could attach a USB Cable, but for some people that might be a bit of a hassle. It would be GREAT if a thin threaded tightening nut could be included in these packages. I  plan to buy 3 more so I have additional security points around the home.

title: Get if you don't mind spending extra
text:
**Updated 7/19/15**
Verdict: Still a 5* product. I would encourage anyone with the budget to get these headphones without hesitation. I decided to run my headphones through some rigorous testing (again I reiterate I am not a sound engineer or in the music business, but I love listening to music). I used spotify with the extreme (320 bit rate) setting that comes with the premium membership as my benchmark to get the best streaming quality available to me. All my music is served via streaming services or digitally via itunes. I tested my Grado RS2e against my new Bowers & Wilkins P7, Beats Pro, AudioTechnica, AKGs and Shure headphones. I played several types of music genres, including classical, opera, pop, techno, hip hop, jazz, etc. And time and again these headphones beat out all the rest or came in a close second. I did this test accompanied by my friend who is a trained musician to get a real musician's perspective. And she agreed with me. These headphones can't be beat. If you can only afford one headphone and don't need it for commuting or use at the office (since these are open back headphones and can disturb others) then go for it. You will elevate your music consumption to a whole new level.

The sound is mind blowing. Clean, clear and rich. You can pick each instrument out while listening to music. I have many headphones that are on any top headphone review you can find out there and these have topped them all. I love music and I spend good money to enjoy the experience, including my sonos system at home. But when I want to listen to music without disturbing anyone else these are my go to headphones. I am not a sound engineer and can't explain why these work so well but they do and you have to experience them yourself.

title: Yamaha does it again
text:
The Cherry on top of my Home Theater Sunday

I had a HK home theater receiver from 12 years ago that died. Over the last year, I first upgraded my speakers, then bought a new Sony BD player last month, and this month I got this Yamaha receiver at a great model year end close out price. I have had the receiver for 16 days and am getting acquainted with its powers and performance. I was hoping that it would have plenty of power for my Polk Audio RTI A5s, CSI A6 and RTI A1 surrounds. And it does! No need to add an external amp to drive the front left and right A5 speakers. Loud for movies is -35 db and for music -37 to -40 db. I may, in the future, add front presence/Atmos speakers, but I am very happy with good old 5.1 surround.

HDMI switching is fast and without any problems. So far, I'm very happy with the receiver. The set-up was easy. The complaints against the remote seem to be overblown. The remote is easy to use and to cycle thru the different audio settings and to switch from HDMI 1 (BD player), HDMI 2 (cable TV) and my analog audio input from my computer. My A5s like the power provided for 2 channel and sound very dynamic, balanced and detailed. This is my second Yamaha and I am fast becoming a devoted fan. The reviews I read about the higher tier Aventage receivers praised the very excellent sound quality and they are spot on. With new movies, I find myself being as interested in the dynamic, surround sound movie sound tracks as I am with the visuals.

title: Good Performance in a Small Package
text:
This review is from: ASUS M580VD-EB76 15.6" Intel Core i7 7th Gen 7700HQ (2.80 GHz) NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 16 GB DDR4 Memory 256 GB SSD 1 TB HDD Windows 10 Home 64-Bit Gaming Laptop

Pros: Background: I bought this to replace my aging 5 year old (Bulky/Heavy) MSI laptop with a 660M. Set up was relatively fast and I got most of my files and settings set up in around 2 hours on and off once Windows 10 was done downloading and installing updates. Onto the physical bits:

-The computer is extremely thin and light like the product description suggests. Build quality is quite good and the plastic bottom could have fooled me for how solid it feels. I could go on for days how much nicer using this laptop is than my old MSI.

-Speakers are a mixed bag in that at proper (i.e. lower) volumes they sound super clean and wonderfully full especially when voices and speech are concerned. I'd say they are better than they are worse so long as you adjust the volume to suit whatever you are listening to, as they tend to distort easily on higher settings. By far the best laptop speakers I've heard under the right conditions.

-The specs for this computer looked good on paper and play good in practice (so far). Boot up from fully shut down takes around 5-8 seconds to the login screen which is faster than my desktop. The 1050 inside is able to play last gen titles well like Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin and so on at full HD with no issues. I haven't tried pushing it with more demanding titles so that might be updated later on.

-Wireless is extremely fast with no latency or issues.

Cons: -Keyboard is kind of squishy if you "really" push down on the keys with a small amount of flex on the surrounding area being depressed but unless you like to smash the keys when you type it's perfectly serviceable with decent feedback.

-Screen has sweet spots and the viewing angle can wash out colors quickly if you aren't looking at it dead on. Not a deal breaker but noticeable.

-Fan noise is noticeable when running benchmarks, but I guess that was expected. Could be worse.

-Battery life is not amazing but it charges quickly.

-Stuck with the 1050 instead of a 1050 ti or 1060 variant, couldn't find a higher spec'd GPU on the Vivobook line, which is a shame as I'd have gladly paid a bit extra for some more power.

-Some bloatware from ASUS but nothing that couldn't be removed with minimal effort.

Other Thoughts: -I would recommend this model if you are looking for a very professional looking laptop for work with the ability to stretch its legs and do some decent gaming on the side. I primarily got this for travel and for its form factor/styling, as it doesn't scream "WOW LOOK AT ME I AM A GAMER LOOK AT ME" like most competing models seem to flaunt with horrible aesthetics. For $999 (at the time of this review) and the performance/form factor this laptop is in a very specific segment that I wasn't able to find anywhere else for the relative cost, especially with it having a 7700HQ and 256 SSD AND 16 Gigs of ram AND the 4 Gig 1050.

-My only concern with this product was heat from the GPU and if the design could cope. Will update when I have more results. Dark Souls II didn't push the GPU too hard from what I could gather.

title: Fast, easy to set up.
text:
Setup: no software needed. When I connected an ethernet cable from a PC to the router it automatically detected the cable modem. A window appeared and said I can type in the SSID and password of the previous router. I did, and and all devices connected without having to reconfigure anything, Within 5 minutes the old router was swapped out and the new Belkin had taken over without any issues.

I spent another 5 minutes setting up the self-healing so that twice a week at 3:30 am the router resets itself. This has been going on now for 3 days and there have been no problems.

SPEED
My internet plan has a maximum speed of 104mbs so I knew the top speed possible.
The previous router was a "g" router, this one is an "n+".
The speed increase has been noticeable, about 50% faster with no dropped connections.

wired connection speed: 96 mbs with a CAT5e cable. Perhaps a CAT6 cable would allow the full 104 mbs
wireless connection speed 61 mbs (20 feet away, same floor level as router)
54 mbs (40 feet away, one floor level below router)

Theoretically, this modem has a speed up to 450 Mbps which is faster than what my ISP offers. I chose this router over faster models because I knew that 104mbs is the fastest I have. There was no point in paying for a speed I could not attain.

title: For theater experience avoid it for TV shows its great
text:
You must be reading this review to know whether to buy this projector or not.
You should know from whom this review is coming from... so you can decide better. This review is for budget projector for Full HD movies under 800 USD.

-I am someone (and this review is for) who is videoholic, watches movies 80% of the time, rest is Youtube/TV Shows/PS4.
-I don't like any movie which is less than 1080p. Picture and audio quality must be on top for me to watch any movie.
-I have owned BENQ HT1075 (big brother of w1070 and younger to HT2050A), so when it died i was looking for new projector.
-I projected EPSON on the off-white wall 140 inches screen from 14 feet (same as with BENQ)
-I was impressed and more than happy with Benq (except it needed bulb replacement after couple of years and it costs much)

I had shortlisted BENQ HT2050, 2550 (4K) and EPSON 2150. And finally decided and bought EPSON 2150.

Why would someone very happy with BENQ, buy EPSON instead of another new model of BENQ?
-Wanted to experience something different.
-EPSON have placed this projector under HOME CINEMA category, hence i assumed its made mainly for movies.
-I think EPSON is far bigger brand than BENQ
-Amazon positive reviews and some site like PC Mag amateurishly saying its great.
-Better 3D quality. 3D's basic issue is darkness, so i agreed to the reviews that said it has better 3D due to higher lumens.
- Low cost bulb and More bulb life compared to BENQ
- Lumens not only for white, impressively it has color lumens
- All the bells and whistle like Frame Interpolation and many more.

My experience:
EPSON 2150 have every feature you dream for except picture quality. Picture that is washed out images. However, I wanted to keep this projector for all the great features it have, we (family) tried to like it, but even my 11 yr old boy said why it is not sharp as our previous projector. His fortnite (PS4 game) also was not as good BENQ.
You feel like you are watching movie on HBO or any TV channel not in theater. 3D was again disappointment (I bought and used 3ACTIVE 3D glasses for this projector).
Whereas my wife said this projector is OK (because she doesn't bother for quality, she is more into TV shows)

So if you into movies and would want theater like picture quality and sharpness avoid this and go for DLP, if you are more into TV shows, sports... this is great projector.

Why 3 stars out of 5...
+3 for all the great features it have, like great color, good night scenes, features...
-1.5 EPSON misleading customers by using terms as HOME CINEMA, 60000:1 contrast ratio etc.
-0.5 Shipping: Mine was international shipping and Shipping was good but return had issues that i could not return. When i processed return, the return label had cost 800 USD whereas i bought it for 699 USD. And for any items value 800 and more have to pay much extra (unlucky me), so i could not return. Fortunately I was able to sell it with facing 200 USD loss.

I have learned higher lumens doesn't mean better sharpness / picture quality, its just more brighter. On the contrary, its the drawback to have higher lumens for movies. LCD technology must have limits and to compensate that all the features have been provided.
I know i will have some cons while buying DLP projector like bulb cost, light leaking etc but i cant compromise on not having theater at home and just having a 140 inch TV.

Bottom line: If you are looking for budget projector for movies and if you are first time projector buyer or experienced one, note that EPSON 2150 is not HOME CINEMA projector as the name suggest, it JUST a bigger TV in your room, giving washed out pictures thou colors are great in this projector, think how much you will watch blu rays... if its more than 50%, don't buy this, if its less than 50% this is a great projector.

Also i don't find any difference in BENQ and EPSON in ambient light, both gets washed out similarly. I dont know what so much fuss about ambient light viewing with EPSON.

I have ordered BENQ HT2050A and it will be arriving soon. I will write review on that too.

Please leave comments if you have any query.

text: A great tablet! I've been using this tablet on medibang and krita for a few weeks now and i am really enjoying my time with it! The 6 express keys, though you do have to press down a bit to get it to register (same with the pen shortcut buttons) are a great way to get your workflow going without having to reach out for a keyboard. The red dial is also a great addition, being that this tablet doesn't have any touch features, doing things like rotating the canvas, zooming in and out and adjusting the brush size on the fly feel really quick and easy, this way my left hand is focused on those tasks while my right hand is mostly focused on drawing. The drivers are great and work well on windows 10. The feature to map different shortcuts depending on what program i'm on is extremely useful, and the transition between programs is absolutely seamless. One think i do however recommend in regards to the drivers is to add an ability to have a mouse click + a shortcut mapped to the same button, i also use allot of 3D programs and i do feel a bit limited in that regards, especially since it only has 6 shortcut buttons, the added ability to have a click and key mapped to 1 button as opposed to having two separate shortcut buttons just to do 1 task would greatly  increase workflow and free up some shortcut buttons for other tasks i may need. However this is only a small nitpick i have in regards to 3D programs and when it comes to 2D drawing, i have no problems whatsoever. Overall a great tablet for it's price; I would defiantly recommend this to anyone in a heartbeat, good job xp-pen!

title: Good lens with not-so-good accessories
text:
The Opteka LR 1300 HD Super Telephoto Zoom Lens is not so much a zoom lens as it is a zoomable lens. It does no zooming of its own but the user is allowed to twist and pull it out to a longer focal length. I bought this because it was advertised as being "for Sony Alpha E-Mount A7r, A7s ..." <and other Sony E-Mount cameras>, and the price at just over $200 seemed almost too good.

Well, the lens itself is not exactly "for" an E-Mount camera. It is actually a T-Mount with a bunch of finely threaded turns which fit onto a two-inch long T-Mount to E-Mount adapter tube. Opteka does NOT provide a cap to cover the E-Mount end of the adapter.

The good news is that this comes with a very nice bag to hold the lens. The bad news is, the bag is too short to hold the lens with the T-Mount adapter. The combination sticks out of the bag by two inches. The bag also does not fit the Lens plus the 2X teleconverter plus the T-Mount Adapter. The combination sticks out over four inches from the end of the bag.

The good news is the lens itself looks very clean and clear. The bad news is, the 2X teleconverter has spots all over its lens on both sides, including inside where it cannot be cleaned. This makes the teleconverter useless for High Definition photography --- So say goodbye to 1200 to 2600 zoom. We're left with the 650 to 1300mm basic lens. Or, you can just buy another 2X teleconverter on Amazon for $26 and hope you get a clean one.

The good news is that the lens has a tripod adapter. This is really a requirement since the lens is far to long for hand-held shooting. The bad news is that while the tripod mount plate is screwed into two rings surrounding the lens, only the back ring is tight to the lens, leaving about a .2 mm gap between the lens and the front ring. This allows the camera attached to the back of the lens/adapter to wobble around about a quarter inch every time you touch the camera. Which makes it impossible to snap a clear picture as both the back and front of the lens wobble up to a quarter inch every time the shutter is pressed. Without a 2 second shutter delay in the camera, the lens itself would be useless. Yes, you'll have to use a few straight pins (or toothpicks to avoid scratches) to shim the loose ring if you want the lens to be less wobbly. But you'll probably need to use a time delay shutter release or a remote, to prevent vibration anyway.

The instructions say to use the teeny-tiny allen wrench to loosen the screws in the adapter so you can turn the words to an upright position, so when you attach the camera it will be (somewhat) level. But you shouldn't bother. After screwing the adapter snug to the lens, tighten the little screws and never loosen them again, they have a tendency to strip. You can just twist the whole tube in front of the adapter to get the camera upright. The camera will get twisted off of level every time you push/pull the zoom tube anyway.

Yeah, in retrospect, the price was too good for perfection. Hopefully, one of these days I'll be able to get a really sharp picture at 1300mm.

title: Great Tool For Repairing Old Cameras
text:
This is a great tool for repairing old cameras. Without this tool I had a hard time removing the lens elements from an old Canonet 28 but this spanner wrench made it super simple.

It comes with four hand-adjustable screws to hold the pieces at any desired length, as well as 4 tool adjustable ones that can be tightened even more with the included hex key. This tool can also be configured in several ways.

The two halves can be arranged to not only curve outward, but also to curve inward. This was especially useful since it allowed the tool to fit into the lens without scraping the sides, and is ultimately the reason why I chose this curved model over the straight one.

The tool is all metal and very sturdy. The hand-adjustable screws are enough to hold it together rock solid at the desired width.

When a lot of pressure/torque is required to unscrew a ring on the lens, I found that it was best to wear thick work gloves. Otherwise the tool's edges would dig into my hand, making it uncomfortable to use.

Overall this is a great tool at a great price and I am very satisfied. I wouldn't be able to repair old cameras without it.

title: Works well
text:
I bought this to replace a Channelmaster Flatenna, which cost $10 shipped from Channelmaster (now $19) and $10 + shipping ordered here. The Flatenna does as good of a job as the more expensive flat rectangular antennas that I tried, but it isn't very good on low VHF (channels 2 through 6), which a few stations still use. When a station in my area that dual-broadcasts on UHF 47 and VHF 4 began having issues with its UHF band, I bought this antenna. It picks up the VHF band of that station, and it also picks up every other station in my area that other indoor antennas get. It should be noted that the transmitter of the low-VHF station is only a few miles away; other transmitters vary between 15 and 35 miles away. This does not pick up stations that are 60 miles away (nor is it advertised to), even with the amplifier.

The one downside is the amplifier. It did not improve reception on any stations, and it distorted a few due to over-amplification. The problem with the amplifier is that the antenna is useless if the amplifier is connected but not plugged into a power source (USB, outlet, etc.). Because of this, if you need to switch from a station that needs the amplifier to one that is distorted when it's plugged in, you have to swap the entire amplifier out, meaning unscrewing and screwing in cables. I therefore recommend that you buy just the antenna itself, and if you need an amplifier for harder-to-reach stations, buy one with a toggle switch that turns it on and off but still allows the antenna to work if the amplifier is toggled off.

Overall, this is an excellent antenna that does work for me on a low VHF station with a nearby transmitter, and it works on stations on the UHF band with transmitters up to 35 miles away. I don't recommend the amplifier at this time.

I had to go to the store to drop it off, and they pointed out to me that I was still being charged for a rental even though I didn't have one. Then you receive an email receipt for your return, then call billing for the charge to be removed. The router itself has pretty basic wireless capabilities, so I suggest buying a newer N or AC type router to take advantage of maximum speeds on newer devices. title: Notes after 4 months.
text:
Have this for four months now. Bought this to supplement Voigtlander 35mm 1.2 for when I need autofocus such as when shooting moving objects or video. Sharpness wise, the two lenses are right up there in terms of resolution, color and sharpess. I believe Voigtlander has a prettier bokeh rendering with a slight faux "leica halo" when wide open that the f2 can't achieve. There is notable distortion with both lenses. It's not worth fixing most of the time with the Voigtlander. And, it's very easy to fix with lens profile with the Sony.

I also have the 21mm converter. Great attachment for the 28mm lens. Easy to attach and detach, and fairly well built for the price. Picture is softer with the adapter, but, amazingly enough, the distortion is lower. At the same time, distortion is harder to fix if you want it distortion free.

I use this lens on both my A7II and NEX3N. They are just as sharp on both cameras. With the 21mm adapter, the NEX3N is sharper.

My opinion, I can't justify getting the 35mm FE when you can get this lens. IMO, it's better in every way even if they were the same price.

title: I REALLY wanted to like this mp3 player
text:
Update: 4/21

More problems
1. On 2nd/3rd run through, full charge to empty, I'm not getting anywhere NEAR the advertised battery life. Seemed to drop to 1/2 of the first time I charged it!
2. When you're playing the last song in a folder, pushing the button to move to the next song actually moves you backwards to the previous album. How did they not catch this in testing? Even moves to a different artist entirely. Whatever was the first song in the last folder. That's not what "forward" means.
3. Very upset to find out that I have been unable to detect and link up to my new bluetooth earbuds, which my Phone finds immediately.
These: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0798FXWSN

Too many problems to keep this player. I hope I'm still eligible for a refund, I don't want a replacement.

I REALLY wanted to like this mp3 player, but poor design decisions/bugs made that impossible. I selected this player after days of looking at everything on the market now, reading countless reviews here and professional ones. So many others had 10% negative reviews and 1/10 is just too high of a failure rate for me.

I'm about 90% sure I'm going to return it as it's just a step backward from what I had before, and that's really strange considering they don't even make my old players anymore. How did they not look at what was out there, and improve on that, instead of re-inventing the wheel with something worse?

I've owned two dedicated players before this and used them countless times for years each, both from iAudio. A really only HD-based unit (still works), and the J3.
I loved the J3, but got it wet, and you can't get it repaired anymore, or even buy it.

This unit is about the same width and height as the J3, but twice as thick for some reason I can't understand.

I'll start with the cons because that's what I care about in a review.

1) The corners of the unit are very sharp, like another reviewer mentioned. It doesn't feel good in your hand at all, unlike the J3 did. This doesn't seem like a big deal, but it literally hurts each time I use it, and I have rough hands.
2) The colors for text, blue? What were they thinking? It's almost unreadable. You can only change the background color.
3) The jog wheel, well, it's just stupid. If you have a lot of folders on your memory card like I do, you're gonna be rotating your thumb around this thing for quite a while before you get to the folder you want. The J3 gave you a touchscreen with a scroll bar for immediate access to what you were looking for. I would MUCH rather have a d-pad for music selection, or a touch-screen.
4) For some reason, twice now, and this was a deal-breaker of course, is that the unit only recognized about 10-15 folders, out of 150-200. So, why bother if you can't even play 90% of your music? I tried again now, and it worked. No idea what changed.

Pros:
1) Sound quality seems good
2) UI is better than the J3, which is pretty much awful. Minimal menus, simple to master.

I'd avoid this player, to be honest. If it was $50, it would be OK, but it's not worth $140, not with this many flaws.

title: I really love this camera
text:
I really love this camera. I came from a Nikon D52000 DSLR setup in search of a small point and shoot. (Got tired of carrying all the lenses and fuss associated with the DSLR.) I wanted a camera with large sensor and the best pictures for a point and shoot - smaller camera model. My search came down to the same three cameras time and time again. A Sony A6000, the Canon Powershot G7X and this camera. I instantly ruled out the powershot based on lack of tilt screen and view finder as these are a must for me.

Went with the Sony A6000 as the specs were the best among the cameras. In terms of specs, this camera offers a ton more features - quality - speed - focus points - etc... This came with the standard power zoom 16-50mm. I took indoor and outdoor pictures and either the lens was defective or the pictures were simply that poor - disappointing. Non zoomed, the pictures look nice and not bad. But if you zoom, the edges in my opinion were soft and were not crisp at all. (Again, I thought I was being too critical and expecting too much from a non full size DSLR as the one I owned.) I then had to see if it was a lens issue and tried a 30mm Sigma Prime Lens. The difference was night and day in terms of quality. The images were crisp and just entirely better. Downfall though, if you use a prime, you lose the zoom and the small A6000 is then getting not so small and portable anymore. (Heading back towards the full DSLR type of setup.)

Then there is this camera. Easy to use - navigate and the Zeiss lens it uses is incredibly sharp and great at all zoom levels the camera has to offer. Comparing this to the A6000 with kit lens was pretty clear. This camera outperformed and provided higher quality images hands down.

So overall, while I did not get to test the Canonpowershot G7X, this camera is the winner.

I have also learned through the camera buying process that while a camera may have tons of features such as the A6000 making it seem hands down better than all others, it may not be if it is used with a sub par or kit lens. So if you are in the market to buy simple camera and not invest in lenses, this is the winner. If you want to buy a smaller camera and plan to invest in high quality lenses, the A6000 is your winner. To me, this is a perfect carry everywhere do all amazing picture quality and build camera.
