title: Great quality in a little package
text:
I searched long an hard for quite some time before finally choosing these speakers. I wanted/needed a decent set of small desktop speakers to bring into the office to quietly listen to music while I worked. My criteria were:
- Needed to look plain and simple
- Simple connectivity to avoid wire clutter
- Small footprint
- Sound quality needed to be worth the price

The bass response on these little things is actually quite good for their size. I'd actually classify the bass as boomy and overwhelms the mids, and to a certain extent the highs as well. Because of this the vocals can sometimes be recessed, but its very subtle and I don't recognize it unless I am specifically looking for it (even less so at lower volumes). I had to set an equalizer to level it out, but if you prefer heavy bass you'll be pleasantly surprised.

Despite these criticisms, the sound quality is fantastic for such a little package. They are able to project a fairly decent level of sound when cranked. The highs are clearly presented yet do not overwhelm, the mids are strong and clear, and the bass is better than expected. Overall, I am very happy with my purchase, albeit a little more pricey than I originally anticipated for a set of work-space speakers. Great quality in a little package.

title: Cheaply made, DON'T BUY!!!
text:
This review is for the Powerbeats 2 In-Ear Bluetooth Headphones, I'm posting under Powerbeats 3 because the issue I've had with the headphones doesn't concern the battery(the primary difference between Powerbeats 2 and Powerbeats 3)

My 15 yo daughter bought her first pair about 20 months ago. She loved them, they're light and have good sound. The absolute best feature is the over the ear clip that secures the headphone in the ear. Great feature if you're working out.

I ended up buying a pair about 14 months ago so I wouldn't have to continue to borrow hers. About 7 months later, after my daughter had hers a little more than a year, the right in ear headphone broke where it bends at an angle to fit in the ear. I assumed she was irresponsible in taking care of them. I glued them back together with crazy glue however, I have to re-glue them every couple of weeks.

6 - 7 months after my daughter's headphones broke, the volume control pad fell of my headphones. Without it, obviously I couldn't control the volume, whatever level I had the headphones at when the pad fell off was the volume I was stuck with. I decided to make due, 2 months later the in-ear piece broke in the exact same way my daughter's did!

Well, I got "lucky" and won a pair at a raffle... Within a month AGAIN THE IN EAR PIECE BROKE ON THE 3RD PAIR!!!

I will never buy another pair, if I win a pair, I'll give them to someone else or trade with someone.

Cheap, poorly made and now that I bought a different brand I don't think they really sound any better than any other in ear headphone similarly priced. (not mentioning the other brand name because I'm not trying to persuade anyone to buy the brand I have now, trying to DISSUADE anyone from buying Powerbeats In-Ear)

title: Awesome Desktop with Solid Specs For a Phenomenal Price!!!
text:
I bought my XPS 8900 2506BLK from Costco in March 2016. I was able to buy it for a PHENOMENAL price since Costco was selling it for $799 and I had a Costco coupon good for $120 so I was able to buy my XPS 8900 for just $680. $680 with these specs is pretty fricken unreal! Also Costco has a great 90 day return policy for electronics plus they also give you another year of warranty for free for a total of 2 years.

My XPS 8900 came with these main specs out of the box:

Intel i7 6700 3.4 ghz
16gb DDR4
1 TB hard drive - My XPS 8900 from Costco came with this 1TB HDD: http://www.amazon.com/dp/B008KXFEZK/ref=wl_it_dp_o_pC_nS_ttl?_encoding=UTF8&colid=2HND0BE6VP47I&coliid=I3LLQW2MHFXBI7&psc=1
GeForce GTX 745 4gb DDR3
6 USB 3 ports
4 USB 2 ports
460 Watt PSU
Windows 10 Home 64bit

Now the computer with the stock specs is quite good right out of the box and is capable of doing everything really well. I immediately noticed how much faster this computer is with the new i7 Skylake compared to my older computer running a i5 4th gen. As I'm writing this review I have 56 browser windows open, downloading a handful of movies and TV shows, running VLC, got Microsoft office open and I am editing photos in Photoshop and my CPU usage is just 2%.

The one area where this computer maybe lacking to some is in the GPU. The GeForce GTX 745 (3DMark GPU Score 3140) is at best a mid range card that's on the low end of the mid range. Now for me this card is more than enough for my computing needs since I'm just a casual gamer and not a hardcore gamer. But I do a lot of photo and video editing and the GTX 745 has been stellar in that regard as far as I'm concerned.

I would highly recommend this XPS 8900 to anyone who is looking for a powerful yet reasonably priced all around workhorse of a computer that can and is more than willing to do more intensive tasks when called upon without even flinching. I expect this computer and especially the i7 6700 to be able to hold up well for at least the next 3-5 years without having to worry about it becoming too outdated by the time I'm in the market for another desktop.

SIDENOTE: I've had the XPS 8900 for about a month and a good friend of mine had some extra parts lying around and he helped me upgrade my computer for free. Well, I did trade some stereo stuff for the 128gb SSD and 1 TB hard drive but I got the GeForce GTX 760 (3DMark GPU Score 8680) and 550 Watt PSU for free since I gave him back my stock GeForce GTX 745 and the stock 460 Watt PSU.

title: Good entry level amp
text:
This is a good quality amp for the price. I would consider it entry level. It is above the cheap Boss, Pyramid, etc but below Diamond, JL Audio, CDT, Focal, ID, etc. Sound quality is excellent and I have it pushing a set of CTX65CS components in the front doors. The amp is rated for 150 watts rms for 2 channels at 4 ohms or can be ran down to 2 ohms at 225w each. You can also bridge it to run 450w at 4 ohms for one channel.
150w x 2 rms at 4 ohms
225w x 2 rms at 2 ohms
450w x 1 rms at 4 ohms

Based on the output and features I would recommend using it for a set of components, small 8 inch quality sub, or cheap 10 or 12 inch medium sub.

Look at yours speaker specs and ensure the rms rating of the speaker(s) matches or is less than the amp. If you use an amp that has an rms output less than the rating of the speakers you will induce distortion, hard on the amp, and possibly damage the speakers if you run loud with distortion. If you use an amp that can put out more then the speakers you adjust the gains on the amp down to reach maximum volume before distortion. I always recommend over-amp vs under-amp and adjust gains to your volume, eq or distortion limit.

There is no fan so mount where air can flow across it to prevent overheating. It comes with speaker level inputs, low pass filter, bass boost, and adjustable low pass freq. Best practice is to use pre-amp outputs from the sub, turn bass boost off, turn low pass filter off, and eq everything from your headunit (if possible, almost all aftermarket headunits can).

I also run the little brother GM-A3602 amp which is the same version amp at lower rms rating. No problems with either amp and I recommend them.

title: This phone works.
text:
We have metal buildings and concrete block buildings on 3 acres. This phone does what no other cordless phone has been able to do. Allow us to talk in every building on our property!! It is wonderful to know, no matter where we are, we can answer the phone. As a business this is critical. The phone lines for all but one building became damaged and replacing them was too expensive so we've tried different versions of several phone systems (Panasonic and AT&T to name two) and the EnGenius Technologies FreeStyl 2 is the only one to work. The others were pure static, even when we would stand outside. I know the En Genius phones seem expensive, but when you add up all the cost of all the phones we tried that didn't work, we spent more than the EnGenius Technologies FreeStyl 2 and 5 handsets we bought.

So why only 4 stars. Well, these phones are not perfect. The volume simply isn't loud enough for my husband. Even at full "6" (the highest it goes), he can barely hear it. And when he switches to speaker phone it frequently starts breaking up. For me, it is really hard to get my ear centered over the speaker. And I don't like how the CID works. It is cumbersome to go through the process unless you want to delete all. All of these issues were something we couldn't know until we tried the phones. And we will put up with it because they work.

I would probably have overlooked the flaws if this phone offered call blocking. For some reason, I can't get this phone to recognize the call block feature offered by my phone company either. No deduction of stars because I knew it didn't call block, although I didn't know it wouldn't recognize the phone companies feature either.

All in all, if you have lots of buildings, spread over a large lot, this phone should work for you! We will never go back.

title: Huge, sturdy backpack for gaming needs, but a little pricey
text:
I own an Acer Helios 300, which is a 15.6" gaming laptop. When I put the laptop, power supply, a lap desk, and an XBox One-style together, all the gear weighs 10 pounds while gear plus bag weighs 13.5 pounds. So, doing the math, this is a large, heavy duty backpack at around 3.5 pounds.

This backpack provides a nice means of transporting laptop gear on family trips. The laptop itself fits into a large sleeve near the back of the pack. The sleeve, oddly, is kind of curved, and leaves headroom above the laptop open. But it doesn't slide around, since it is snug on the sides. I put my thin plastic lap desk into the slot with the laptop and it all fits fine. I imagine I could put one or two more thin devices like tablets or 2-in-1's, as well. I see no reason a 17 inch laptop would not fit easily into the same space, which would probably reduce that curved headroom. I've included a picture of the interior which shows the curve of the laptop sleeve (as well as my items snugly inside).

Below the main compartment is a front pocket that was shown in product pictures as storage for power bricks and cords. I use it for this purpose, and it seems reinforced enough not to bend or crush. It sits in front of the laptop itself so it not weighed down upon by it. The other major areas of storage are two large side pockets, which seem about the right size for controllers or disc cases, a medium flat front pocket which seems best suited to flash drives, hard drives, and other media, and two front zippers which could accommodate flat items like cards or manuals.

The top is a large, relatively stiff piece that zips over it all, maintaining the basic shape of the pack. Which is to say, this pack doesn't really shrink down if you press on the outside of it or try to stuff it into a compartment. The top piece has a heavy duty handle which is very convenient for times in which you might not want it on your back.

The back straps and the back of the pack are covered in a sort of ventilating mesh which is both soft and allows for some air flow. The straps are wide and do not chafe after some time carrying (I am about 6 feet tall, FYI, and can't speak to a smaller or larger person). There is a small strap-joining clip for additional stability if need be.

All in all, this is a very nice pack for gaming on the go. I feel very confident in the construction of it, its stitching and zipper quality, and its ability to keep things safe, and there is an absolute plethora of storage areas, which I doubt I will ever use. If anything, I might try to add clothes, books, and other devices into the bag for trips.

The only real knock on this bag to my mind is price. It seems like you're paying a significant premium just to have the Predator logo on the back (which is nicely understated, thank goodness). title: Great FUN Tablet for Entertainment...BUT!
text:
The Fire 7" is a wonderful little tablet FOR ENTERTAINMENT, watching movies, listening to music, and reading books.

PROS:
1. Excellent performance in spite of its little CPU and 1 GB of RAM. In fact, the Fire 7's hardware specifications are superior to the Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 that sells for a higher price. (CAVEAT. Performance is fine IF you use it for entertainment-only; IF you don't overload it with too many apps; and, IF you don't try to multi-task with business apps.)
2. Very nice picture-quality for watching movies.
3. Very simple to use. Even my 89-year grandma is able to use the Fire 7 (after she rejected a Samsung Tab S as being too complicated). Indeed, Fire's Android LITE is perfect for beginners to learn how to use the Android operating system. And, honestly, the stripped-down Fire Android is best for most 'home' users. (I don't hear 'Honey, what do I do know?' as often.)
4. Does a fine job of surfing the web and viewing email.
5. The Fire 7 doubles as a perfect remote control for a Roku device or Roku TV.
5. For $50, there is NO better deal anywhere for a new 7" tablet.

CONS: NO Cons IF USED FOR WHAT IT WAS DESIGNED TO DO (but see the LIMITATIONS section below for explanation).
*** Also, I don't view the advertisement on the Lock Screen as a 'con'...because BIG DEAL about the ad...it goes away as soon as you go to Home screen. And if the Lock-Screen ad keeps the price down while maintaining the excellent quality, I say I love the ad!

LIMITATIONS:
*** The Fire 7 is NOT a Samsung Note 10.1 edition 2014 with a mega-horsepower CPU, 3 GB of RAM, and a full-blown Android OS. So, don't expect the Fire 7 to be a rocketship.
*** The Fire 7 is NOT a good tablet for business purposes. Its performance is not up to what's needed to run business apps in a multi-tasking environment. (Yeah, sure, you can surf the web and review your email...but don't think you can surf, do email, write invoices, and etc without serious stutter.)
*** Amazon kind of limits you on various Google Apps for Business...and that kills it for business use (in my case).
*** The Fire 7 is not a device that you'd want to root, custom ROM-itize, overclock, or otherwise tweak. Don't try to customize it into something it wasn't meant to be.
*** The Amazon Fire version of Android is NOT Android KitKat, Lollipop, or Marshmellow. 'Fire' is just a fun LITE version of Android. So, don't expect a full-featured Android experience with Amazon Fire (but, actually, that's a good thing for most users, especially Android beginners).

VERDICT: For $50, there is NO better ENTERTAINMENT tablet for the kids, mom, and grandma.

TIP: Give your FAMILY this inexpensive FIRE tablet. They will be very happy. That way you save money to buy yourself a real kick-azz tablet, like the Note 10.1 ed. 2014 (or Tab S2), which can be tricked out to run like a Ferrari. He, he, he...that's what I did!

title: Great case, just a few flaws.
text:
Review of ZOGU iPad case:
Shopping for an iPad Pro case was extremely daunting. There are so many different cases that range from less than $10 into the hundreds! This case is a great middle ground (bought at ~$50). I had the Apple Pencil and wanted a case that would be able to hold the pencil but also not be too bulky and have a fairly minimalist design. Nothing too flashy. Here are some basic categories that I have broken this review down into to detail my 4/5 rating.

Build Quality:
Overall this case has great build quality. The velcro doesn't feel cheap like I thought it would and the pencil holder is made of a tight piece of flexable material that doesn't seem to wear down easily. Both the outside and inside materials seem stylish, sturdy, and functional.

Stand:
The case works great as a stand with the use of vecro to allow unlimited viewing angles. Sometimes when you set up the stand the velcro can become misalligned which requires readjustment but that's a fairly minor issue. The front of the case may feel a bit unsteady or weighted toward the front if on an edge but for lap use and table use it works great.

Reading:
Overall, the case works great for reading at any orientation. I have noticed that you need to position a certain flap inward when folding into a comfortable position so the velcro doesn't attatch (or to make it attatch if you want keep the case secure rather than keeping it easy to fold up).

Pencil Holder:
Very secure and useful for keeping track of your pencil while not in use. There is one kind of major issue with this pencil holder which is why I will take a star off of this device, the pencil covers up the headphone jack. the main problem with stylus storage on any case is what to cover up? There isn't that much space on the edges of the device that is undesignated so you are going to have to choose what you want to cover. All things considered, the audio jack is the overall least important thing to cover while in storage but it is still annoying.

title: best in class
text:
I am using this unconventionally to mount my TV above the bay window in my living room. I could not find anything else as fully featured that would allow the TV to drop BELOW the center of the mount. This is really important because I only have a little over a foot of clearance between the top of my window and the ceiling.

Pros:
The mount is sturdy, has good range, is easy to adjust up and down, and was extremely easy to put together. Slick accomodations for a bottom sound-bar is nice.

Cons:
The angle of panning is weak. It is very expensive. It is fairly heavy, by itself.

WARNING:
If you are using this mount for a similar purpose as me, you need to know that you have to open the lowering arm BEFORE you mount it to the wall bracket. It took a lot of strength to pull the thing away from it's neutral position in order to put a lock in it in order to keep it open so it can be safely mounted. This is a two person job, it requires lots of strength, and it is definitely not meant to be opened without first being mounted to the wall. Also note that even with this lock, the top of the arm will rise just a little above the wall mount bracket.

Room for improvement:
Please, please, please make this easier to open without being mounted. The resistence is turned pretty much all the way up out of the box. Wider pan and tilt angles would make this mount literally the best mount available. Also it would be real nice to be have the ability to adjust the vertical stop so you can set the maximum height.

While this mount is expensive, it is definitely worth the money. I imagine it would be even nicer if I were using it for the intended above-mantle purpose, but just keep in mind the difficulties of following in my footsteps if you choose to buy it for that purpose.

title: This device is revolutionary
text:
[[VIDEOID:1fd544c8f1abc374863fbb41199f132b]] [[VIDEOID:37afde6beb67cd0d95c2c237a2853746]] [[VIDEOID:97345731bde79c0e615bfb783837157]] [[VIDEOID:82540562fb13b30dddf39d2534324224]] [[VIDEOID:2ef0a2e5b8cb410a34b1587a71421121]] So I am one of the first people to have the device as I pre-ordered from their first batch on their website. This product has so far been amazing to me. I plan on being as thorough and honest in this review.

My first impression when I got the item was wow this is huge. It's a (not entirely huge) speaker. It's light and made of plastic. Each side of the device has 3 outlets (1 for each channel, 6 total). The first thing you have to do is install an app. I used Google Play because I have Android, I cannot comment on the IOS version.

Initial setup:

So the initial setup is a little bit touchy. It took me a minute to figure out how to set it up but it's actually very similar to devices of this kind. You open the app, create an account, log in, and start the setup for your TapTap. It will tell you to connect to the access point of the device. I have 2 wireless networks, one that is 5Ghz and one that is the standard wireless frequency. This device does not support 5Ghz. When adding the device, after you connect it, you need to make sure you connect to the network that the device is connected to. If you do not and connect to a network with a different name, such as Wifi-5Ghz instead of Wifi, it will give you an error. I had trouble recovering from that mess up, however, I reset the device and went through initial setup again and was good to go.

Programming:
So it's easy to get started as they included a large collection of instrumental Christmas songs. You just add the songs you want to the TapTap and hit play. It will start playing and you can adjust the volume, select different songs, tell it to repeat, shuffle, etc. I think actually adding a song and programming it required a bit of a learning curve, however, I did notice they have a tutorial video here: [...]

I honestly just hooked it up to my Christmas tree lights on 1 channel and started playing one of the several default songs included right when I unpacked it. It's extremely easy to get going right off the bat. Obviously, this was not the intended reason I bought it. So I started building a setup on my patio using all 6 different channels. EDIT: I reuploaded a video with sound of my fully setup light show.

I have also been in contact with the company and I feel that they are very loyal to their customers. Looking at their other product line they have a good background in technology. I am so excited to see this device evolve.

The bottom line is. Christmas light shows used to be something only certain people could do, they would take hours (even days or months) and lots of money to create. Asante just created a device that brings this into the hands of everyday people. This is something that every home should have! It just brings more joy to Christmas.

Also, be aware that the green connector is tiny and good 14 or 16 ga stranded wire won't simply plug right in. Even if you cut some of the strands off, the heavier wire has a tendency to pull the connectors apart.

title: I didn't think I'd like this but I'm really happy with it.
text:
Color me impressed. For what many call a ‘clone’ this tablet really is impressing me. It has everything you need to get it started and some extras the competition should be including. You get TWO pens, and the battery lasts up to a week before it needs to be recharged, a pen-stand for that has 8 replacement nibs hidden away. You get a metal stand included, this sounds like “well duh you do” but sadly the competition isn’t including one and they want you to pay $100 for a plastic wonky one, also you get a tablet glove! That thing that makes your hand glide on tablets vs sticking to them.

I honestly got this because I got teased by a lot of my friends and fellow comic artists for working on such a small tablet, my Surface Pro 4. So I had some store credit and decided to try this out while it was on sale. I was really nervous about it as I’m always hearing “There’s a trade off with the clone tablets”. Sure, maybe if you’re expecting a luxury tablet that’s got a metal chassis or whatever but this tablet has a glass screen, a ton of extras and feels sturdy.

I worked on a piece for a while, trying to get comfortable with it and it’s impressive to say the least. I don’t think the parallax (distance between the pen & screen) is bad, way better than my old Wacom 12WX…as is the color accuracy. I’ve worked on the Surface Pro 4 for a while which has very minimal parallax and I honestly didn’t have much trouble on here with the Huion tablet. Also there’s no hot spot on the face of the tablet, you know that spot where your hand would stick to or just start to get sweaty, none of that here.

The pressure range of 8k is really good and I noticed it was higher than my Surface Pro 4’s 1k pressure range. That said I’m not so blown away that I feel the SP4’s pen is bad or unusable but there’s a difference. You have a solid range of control that’s to be certain but I think past a certain number you’re less and less likely to notice. Must be said, some may be turned away by the plastic pen on the glass screen (there is a textured screen protector but we’ll get to that and why it’s bad with my tips) and I’m fairly spoiled with my Surface’s pen tips giving me a range of 4 different feels as this only comes with 1 type of 8 nibs, smooth and plastic.

There are speakers in the unit, I haven’t tested them but I honestly haven’t seen a good set of speakers in a monitor/TV since the ol’ CRT days where they could fit larger drivers in there. I can’t give my 2 cents on that since I haven’t tried them but, this is an artist tablet and I’m focusing on that.

I tested it with Clip Studio Paint EX and I’m including a pic of the workspace & the piece I finished so you can suss out how it can work. I did one doodle before it and then straight to this from being used to my Surface Pro 4 so I didn’t have much of a learning curve to get on with this. I had no compatibility issues and had it working with the software instantly. Messed a bit with Photoshop and the pressure seems to work straight away. I don’t use photoshop much for the art end so I can’t say fully how well it works but when I made some brush strokes they worked fine enough.

As far as negatives, well the monitor is large and a bit heavier than you’d expect with a lot of modern ones really slimming them down. This monitor is a fat one, and the stand really makes the footprint of this device pretty big on your desk. This with the stand isn’t going to strain your muscles to move it about but I don’t think you’ll have this on your lap while you’re sat back in the chair either. The pen I’ve heard feels cheap, I’d say it feels very light and there’s no rubber like on the wacom ones so that might be where that feeling comes from. The screen protector that’s supposed to add a texture is worthless and really isn’t worth having on…When you use it, a rainbow effect appears as you’re wearing into it and it makes the tablet unusable. You simply can’t see what is going on under it, so stick with the glass, your plastic pen won’t hurt it but make sure you’re not wearing a watch or whatever.
The other thing is there’s no eraser on the pen’s butt, there’s two buttons which are programmable but it’s something you’ll either have to learn to live with or adapt if you’re gonna grab this.

Overall, if you’re looking for a tablet where you can work right on screen this is an excellent one to have pro or hobbyist alike. If you’re just starting out it has everything you need, especially for the cost. I’ve worked on Wacom products for years and the Surface Pro 2 and 4 for ages as well and this tablet impressed me. Thing to keep in mind, this is not a luxury tablet, it’s not ultra thin and light and it’s not made of an aluminum chassis, but it’s well built and I feel is worth the asking price. Especially considering I’ve spent far more on Wacom with their 12WX and was underwhelmed.

Here’s some tips for setting the thing up since the youtube reviewers I’ve watched missed some things:

-You need to calibrate the colors out of the box. Once you do the colors are really nice and the 1080P works nicely on this size monitor.

-I would say remove the textured screen protector. Because the screen is glass your not going to do much harm to it with a plastic nib. I have a Surface Pro 4 which I’ve worked on for 2 years and without a screen protector. After all that time there’s no damage I can see on it. The screen protector on this thing has a texture to it to make it more like working on paper. The problem is it’s useless and ruins the experience, The colors are ruined with it because of the matte texture and as you use it, a rainbow effect appears as you use it. It’s really bad and isn’t something I think is worth the texture effect. I was genuinely struggling seeing my linework on the monitor till I removed it and it’s vastly better.

-What the youtubers got wrong: They say the stand gets stuck on the cables, this really caught me as odd as the stand has a massive hole in it for you to put the cables through so it makes it impossible to put the stand on the cables in any way.

-Be sure to NOT install the drivers off the CD, you’d be wasting your time. Go to the huion website and download the fully up to date drivers there.

-There are no express keys, honestly I’m so used to a keyboard that this didn’t even register till I saw others complaining about it.

-No touch interaction, this IS what got me since I’ve been working on a Surface Pro 4 using 2 fingers to rotate and zoom. That’s simply not here. Which is a shame but, something I’m getting used to again.

-Wash the glass screen, there’s some form of residue that makes the pen kinda drag against it, but after a microfiber cloth+water wash over the glass it’s super smooth and nice.

-Make sure you uninstall all other tablet drivers before using this.

My tablet history: (Unknown name brand), Wacom Graphire 2 & 3, Intous 2, Wacom 12WX, Surface Pro 2 w/ Wacom Bamboo Feel, Surface Pro 4, Huion GT-191

And hey, if you have any questions or want me to clarify something feel free to leave a comment and ask and I’ll answer as best I can.

Update: After about 2 weeks or so of not charging the pen and tons and tons of use it finally needed charging. Didn't expect that!

-Mike G

title: Disappointing
text:
As much as I wanted to love this monitor based off the specs, I just can't live with the major flaw in the sampleI received.

About 1 cm from the bezel on every side of the screen there is a noticeably darker area where the contrast is much lower than the rest of the screen. I tested with multiple sources and connections, all showed the same results. Its as if this 35 in monitor has a 34 inch backlight. The much less expensive Acer ED7 34 inch curved monitor I am testing against does not display this problem.

Additionally the height adjustment of the included stand is very limited in range and does not swivel, which the ED7 does. The bottom bezel is much thicker than the sides or top, taking a bit away from the near bezel-free look.

One of the main reasons I purchased this monitor is the HDR feature. My HDR10 4K Samsung TV is quite stunning with HDR source material so being an video/audio enthusiast I wanted this feature for a computer monitor I spend so much time with. I knew going on that this monitor does not have a high contrast ratio needed for HDR nor does it have local dimming zones needed to truly create the effect. Nevertheless the visual impact of HDR material is noticeable and impressive on this monitor.

However the black box 1 cm from the edge of the bezel surrounding this screen kills it for me. Just too noticeable and jarring. As a sanity check I had my wife sit and look at the monitor with me and she also noticed it immediately as well, and she's not normally one to notice these sort of things that I nitpick at in TVs/monitors.

Will be returning this to Amazon.

If anyone has a suggestion for a freesync 35 inch UWQHD curved monitor with at least 100 Hz refresh rate and HDR compatibility please let me know!

title: good keyboard -- but maybe *not* "Plug & Play"
text:
Really like this logitech K400 plus -- once I got it working. Should preface by saying I bought a "Used" unit from a vendor here on Amazon, which came in a fairly beat-up, taped up box -- but keyboard looked fine. First I couldn't find the USB receiver -- not in the battery compartment (tho two 'AA's were in place), not in a notch or pocket anywhere on keyboard, not in the bag -- oh wait ! There it is, tucked in a notch in the rim of the box (DOH !). Plugged into my Linux Xubuntu htpc -- "lsusb" showed it right away, & "sudo lshw -C input" identified the receiver's USB id, vendor Logitech, & showed usbhid driver had been loaded. Switched on the keyboard -- and nothing. Multiple battery swaps, reboots, different USB ports later -- still nothing. Next I tried on my Win 10 laptop -- similar deal. Receiver recognized right away, drivers linstalled, Device Manager shows it ready & working -- but no input from keyboard.
I was ready to ask for Return/Refund -- but first I wanted to know. I pulled the screws & popped keyboard apart to see if the switch was damaged or possibly a lead from battery contacts was broken -- all looked good, so back together. I was headed to Amazon.com (on an old Win 7 laptop) to start RETURN process, when a little more research turned up "Logitech Unifying Software" -- downloaded & ran it & BOOM -- that did the trick. Apparently, my "Used" K400 Plus had lost it's Pairing with the USB dongle (or maybe the original had been replaced & not Paired ?) -- at any rate, the keyboard, touchpad, volume/media buttons all work fine now, on both Windows & Xubuntu (haven't tried Android yet, but sure that would work too -- the Receiver & Keyboard are storing their Pairing now).
Very happy with this purchase now -- but in my "Used" case, the only documentation I got was the back of the box (which makes a point of "Plug & Play" ease), & a pictograph QuickStart guide, that shows basically the same. Add a further frustration -- whether it's Windows 10, or it's Edge Browser, (or maybe just some security settings in my particular Edge Browser), I kept getting hung up in the "Support / Downloads" section of Logitech's official website. It took Win 7 & Chrome browser for me to get to & download the "Logitech Unifying Software" that made Pairing/Re-Pairing possible

title: Buyer Beware, get assurances first...
text:
Buyer beware,

Something fishy is gong on with this so called "protection plan". Some are saying that coverage starts at time of item shipping, which does match what product listing says, but then one person mentioned that it starts as soon as you buy it.

Now easy fix would be to cancel, if you already purchased, then wait till close to release date of dot gen 2, then reorder purchase protection. Problem solved.

However,

I pre-ordered the 6 pack of dots for my home, and i want some questions answered about the "protection" I'm gonna be paying for. I asked specific and targeted questions in the question section. I asked about types of coverage and if the plan only caters to "one" dot, not multiple. I took the time to read all the fine print of their service agreement as well.

Now,

Lo, and behold (but not shocked at all) all questions were just removed from the page. I have never seen that happen before. Was it square trade? Was it Amazon? Its just too fishy. The questions section, albeit dumb and redundant at times, proves very helpful when you have a specific question. The guy who said the strange thing about the time the coverage starts had asked a question there too, of which it is now erased, gone. Leads me to believe something fishy is going on with this "protection plan".

Now, im not saying don't get it to cover your brand new dot, just be careful and get some real assurances before you give these people more of your hard earned money after spending a few bucks already on the dot. $5 bucks is cheap enough for a year of coverage, but that coverage better not be fishy...

That's all I'm saying.

Be careful out there guys, and enjoy your new dots when they arrive. I cant wait for mines!

P.S. Update: 10/09/16

So I figured this mess out. Amazon already offers a 90 day warranty on the echo dot. DON'T purchase any coverage until you are near your 90 day mark with amazon. Then, you can buy a 1 year policy with square trade for 5 bucks. That way, you get 1 year + the original 3 months of coverage. Even square trade tells you if it gets damaged in the 90 day period after receiving, they will refer you to Amazon. Why give them any cash earlier, and lose 3 whole months of coverage?

Also, if you buy say, 2 or more ehco dots, just buy like two 1 year policies for 5 bucks each instead of one 2 year policy for 10 bucks. That way, you can claim for both if needed. Each individual policy covers up to 3 claims.

Heheh....square trade is gonna be pissed....But people should be informed. I'm tired of companies taking advantage of people who don't know better. Also, if i could read and figure stuff out, please try for yourself too. That is all folks.

title: It's a great case
text: It's a good looking case. The color is a nice chocolate brown and it fits my Surface Pro 4 perfectly. One thing I wasn't expecting was how much heavier my surface would be after putting the case on. It's not extremely heavy (my 15 inch laptop is a little heavier) but it now feels like I'm carrying around a thin hardback textbook. Your pen won't be able to clip onto the side anymore, so you'll have to use the pen holder on the case for it. The ports and controls are still easy to get to and you can still attach you keyboard at an angle with this case on (I'm actually typing this on my surface). You won't be able to use the kickstand anymore; however, the case gives you the same angle flexibility as the kickstand. I'd still be very careful about dropping the surface even with the case on. The top corners are still exposed and the case itself has no type of rubber bumpers anywhere on it to dampen the impact.  If you're looking for something that looks professional, doesn't take away from the Surface experience and will protect your device if you accidentally bump into something, this is the case for you. If you need a case you can beat up and drop all the time (or that's child-proof) and not have to worry about breaking your Surface, this may not be a good fit. Overall, I'm happy with my purchase. I travel with my Surface Pro 4 all the time and this gives it a little more protection.

title: ASUS Z170 has BIOS problem
text: I've build 4-5 computers over the past 4-5 years using ASUS MBs because I found them to be reliable.  Unfortunately, the Z170-AR seems to be the exception.  Specifically, the BIOS on the board does not retain some settings when I shut down the computer.  I am using a Samsung 512Gb 950 pro as the primary "C" drive, so I changed a setting in the BIOS from "SATA Express" to "M.2" to take full advantage of the 950 Pros features, as Samsung and ASUS recommend.  However, the next time I powered up the computer and checked the BIOS, I found the BIOS had not retained the "m.2" setting and had reverted to the "SATA express" setting.  This happened every time I shut the computer down.  I would have to change the BIOS setting every time I power up the computer if I want to take full advantage of the 950 pro, not something I want to or should need to do.  Contacted ASUS support, which suggested changing the Motherboard battery.  I did but that made no difference at all.  Still had the problem.  In addition, I'm using DRAM rated at 2666MHz, and the BIOS shows two different frequency speeds for the DRAM in two different places.  So I am not sure at what speed the DRAM is actually running.  Not sure if I want to go through the RMA process with ASUS, or if I'll try another Motherboard brand.

title: Fantastic Head-unit Offering Substantial Upgrades Over Last Year's Model
text:
I am a DIY, and have never worked in car audio. I self-installed all of my car radios and speakers. I purchased this unit at Best Buy (price matched amazon for $517) and installed it myself in my 2010 Toyota Tundra.

The DDX9073S has a large, beautiful screen that is very responsive to your touch. This year’s model features a re-written OS in linux which results in a buttery smooth experience. Kenwood upgraded its USB 2.0 port to 1.5 amps, allowing for a quicker charge. One of the big additions this year is the Equalizer which now has 13 bands (as compared last year’s 5) and FLAC file support. The product comes with a clip microphone that you can hardwire for hands free calling and a hardwired GPS antenna to give you better signal than your phone.

TLDR: From Kenwood’s site:
6.95 inch Wide VGA Color LCD Display with LED Backlight
Clear Resistive Panel
Motorized 7 Step Tilt Angle Adjust
Touch Panel Control, Variable Key Illumination
50W x 4 RMS
Built-in HD Radio
HDMI / MHL Connection with Optional Cable
Android Rapid Charge
Bluetooth 3.0 Built-in (Hands-Free Profile / Audio Profile(A2DP) / AVRCP1.5 / SPP)
iDataLink support
Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
Dual Phone Connection
Wireless Music Browsing (AVRCP 1.5)
Sirius XM Ready

The unit features has the following features:

Linux based OS: The system has no lag and is buttery smooth. I find the home screen to be the most useful screen of all. It displays information and cover art for any source you are playing (e.g. Bluetooth, carplay, HD radio, Pandora, etc.) In most cases, I found the home screen to be more aesthetically pleasing than in the apps or modules themselves, plus the music visualizer is very neat to look at. There are so many audio settings that it would take forever to cover. The ones that stand out are speaker size/type/height settings for EQ; seat position sound; and Separate HPF for front/rear. All of this means that the sound you will get out of this will undoubtedly sound much better than a comparable model Pioneer head unit.

6.95” Clear Resistive touch screen: It is not a capacitive screen, but do not be alarm because I found that it was very responsive to my touch. It is a TFT screen with an 800x480 resolution. The downside to the screen is it is a bit of a fingerprint magnet and does reflect a lot of light in the daytime. This is the reason for minus one star. Nighttime viewing was clear and bright. I turned the backlight down to minimum and could still see the screen clearly.

CD/DVD playback: Note you must connect the parking brake wire to a wire in your vehicle that shows speed in order to display video on the screen. Some people have connected this wire to a vehicle ground or body panel to get video all the time, but note it is illegal in most cases and unsafe to watch video while driving.

HD radio: provides crystal clear audio, provides song information, and even album cover art on some stations. This was one of the main reasons I purchased a new radio.

2 RCA Video Inputs (Rear View Camera w/Parking Guide Line & Front View Camera): You will need to purchase a good quality, waterproof camera and run RCA to the back of the head unit, power from the brake lights to the camera, and connect the reverse wire from the head unit to a reverse wire on your vehicle.

Screen Mirroring (Android only): You must first download Kenwood's Smartphone Control App to get running.

HDMI/MHL: I used this feature for iOS device screen mirroring. Note you will need to attach an HDMI cable (must have a skinny connector) and purchase the Apple Lightning AV adapter https://www.amazon.com/Apple-Lightning-Digital-Adapter-MD826AM/dp/B009WHV3BM. There is a cover plate on the back of the unit that must be removed to access the HDMI port. Also the cover can be reinstalled to secure the HDMI cable in place. When using this setup, the image will appear very light and most apps that only support portrait mode, will be unreadable on the screen. None of this is a fault of the unit however. Tip: if you are not getting video, hit the button with four squares on it, as the unit may be displaying a blank backup camera screen.

Bluetooth Built-in (Hands-Free Profile / Audio Profile(A2DP) / AVRCP1.5 / SPP). This unit will support two phone connected at the same time. It has on screen prompts that allow you to toggle back and forth.

Android Auto: Reviews are mixed on this. Some of the problems include album art not displaying. Again not a fault of the Kenwood.

CarPlay: I have found Apple’s interface to be buggy and of minimal use. The main issue is there is a lack of support from most app developers. Aside of Apple’s apps you will find Pandora, iHeart Radio, and Audible, but that is about it. Sometime’s the CarPlay apps will not respond until you unplug and re-plug in your phone. Apple Maps is currently the only CarPlay mapping software that can be used. If you minimize the maps on your phone, the map will disappear off the Kenwood. All of this is no fault of Kenwood. Useful features of CarPlay are: Siri’s ability to read iMessages to you and allow you to respond with your voice and hand’s free calling. If you don’t like CarPlay I recommend using the HDMI/MHL interface to use your google apps.

iDataLink Support: If you purchase a Maestro RR and a matching vehicle harness you will be able to integrate factory vehicle features such as Satellite Radio, USB Media Player, Bluetooth hands-free and music streaming. However, the coolest feature is the ability to display vehicle information on the home screen such as doors open, TPMS tire pressure, climate control, and performance. In the menu system you can dive deeper and get check engine light details, setup gauges to performance information and much more.

Please click yes if you found my review helpful. 

padding in the headband. However, I did not experience
any discomfort during use.

Biggest surprise was the cord they used on these headphones.
Talk about being thick! Mini-jack plug is equally built
tough.

Only complaint I have is padded ear cups get warm very
quickly from my body heat.

So what made me give 5 stars? I tested this product
using iPhone 6. Sound quality for these headphones is surprisingly good for
this price range. It's got the highs (treble) and lows (bass) without hint of any distortion.
To me, sound quality was excellent. I even checked with my second device, Google Nexus 9
tablet.

I've recently written reviews for other Panasonic headphones, and they cost twice
as much as this pair but this one beats all of them when it comes to sound quality.
I love this headset!

I needed a range extender to boost signal from my router situated in a bedroom out to a living room that is roughly 35-40 feet away, I was getting 1 to 2 bars on my devices and was having difficulty streaming video and music. I followed the set up instructions (which were very easy) and located an area that had good connectivity to my wireless router (as dictated by the range extender), however I was a little surprised that I had to place it about 15 feet away from the router for it to connect properly, any further away it would not connect.

This range extender only succeeded in boosting the signal strength so that It appears I have a strong connection and get full bars on devices, however it does not reliably provide a consistent internet connection in that it still cannot stream any media. I tested out the streaming media on two different devices, first connecting to the range extender while in the living room then connecting to the wireless router directly while in the bedroom, the range extender failed to provide a stable connection while connecting to the router worked perfectly so I am confident the performance of my router and Internet bandwidth are not the problem.

Also I have had to reboot the range extender every 2 days, it seems to only be reliable in taking a dive in signal strength that only recovers after rebooting. Have been using this range extender for a couple weeks now to give it a fair chance but I'm pretty disappointed by its lack of performance.

title: Excellent desktop replacement with a gorgeous screen!
text:
This Toshiba Satellite is a fantastic, sub-$1000 computer. It hits all the right notes and should be considered by anyone looking for a responsive desktop replacement machine.

PROS
• SCREEN: First and foremost, the screen is absolutely gorgeous. As a design professional, I rely on color and clarity to make critical decisions in my work and I spend my days staring at monitors and laptop screens from all the big, computer makers. This is by FAR the best screen I've looked at on a laptop (and that includes Macs). I can't believe how crisp text is: Web pages practically sing.
• FAST: This system is optimized for Windows 10 and it shows. I've found nary a delay over the week that I've used it.
• KEYBOARD: The haptics of the Satellite's keyboard are spot on. While the full-size keyboard does mean that, on my lap, my right arm is stretched a bit further across my body than I'd like, it's not a problem on tabletops. The keys are perfectly spaced and the keyboard is quiet.
• PORTS: While many computer makers are moving away from ports as they release laptops, Toshiba took the opposite tack. If you have something you need to plug into your laptop, there are plenty of options. When I first fired up the machine, I was delighted to find a rare, built-in Ethernet port. I used it to quickly download Windows 10 Pro and install it on my machine. With three USB ports, and SD card slot, Ethernet, HDMI, and even a media drive (!), you're set to up- and download your content (which I find I'm doing a lot, because I love this screen!).
• QUIET: This machine is made for media and, as a result, it runs quietly. I've taxed it by playing games (even streamed from my Xbox--a new feature of Windows 10), watching Netflix, and playing music at full volume while working on graphics files and it handles all of that without sounding like it's about to take off and launch into outer space.
• TRACKPAD: The trackpad has a nice surface that adds just a bit of friction to enhance accuracy. Overall I've found it to be responsive, though I prefer to use a [[ASIN:B009CP4PIW Microsoft Arc Touch Mouse - Black]] (which shines on this system).

CONS
• BUILD QUALITY: The build quality of the Satellite line is more of a light-weight, consumer friendly style. I find it's perfect for moving from room to room in my house, but I'd be a bit concerned if my needs involved heavy movement (e.g., in and out of a backpack and shuttled around a campus). The battery, which sits at the back of the machine where I typically pick it up, has a bit more play than I'd like. Toshiba was definitely making some decisions to keep this thing light in the face of all of it's features and size. As a result, it's not a rugged laptop like say a Macbook or Thinkpad.
• ERGONOMICS: As mentioned before, the full-size keyboard makes for an awkward hand position when using this machine on your lap. In addition, there's a distinct edge at the seam where the metal keyboard surface meets the plastic body of the computer. I find this irritates my arms with extended use (yes, I know I shouldn't be resting my arms on the computer).
• BATTERY LIFE: So far the battery life on this laptop is not that great. I suspect it's draining due to the high-quality screen, as it seems to only last about 4 hours when only doing light-weight activities like browsing or responding to email. Hopefully a patch from Toshiba is in the works.

All in all, the cons don't outweigh the pros with this machine. I'm incredibly happy with it. Since I got it, my elder Macbook Air and iMac have been collecting dust because I can't resist the siren song of the Satellite's gorgeous screen.

title: Recommend the System
text: It has been 8 months since I installed the system.  Rock solid is the best I can describe it.  I had  small problems installing the cameras because they were not designed for concrete installations where the cable can't be hidden inside the sheet rock.  The solution, install the aluminum base to the roof (don't use Tapcon screws, the heads are too big and will interfere rolling up the cables), drill a hole to the side 1/2" knockout, insert the cat 6 cable and  punch the RJ45 Keystone Jack.  With this done, you will need to carefully roll up the long cables of the cameras letting almost no room for male and female plugs.  Changing the IP address of each camera is not big deal but having a small knowledge in internet access protocols will be very helpful.  Night vision quality is acceptable even in complete darkness. The hard disk can record 7 days with no problems.  The mobile app for iPhone is very easy to use.  The verdict: Recommend it and do it yourself if you have previous experience with these systems, otherwise pay for it.

title: The buckle is a one-hand clip which means practical jokers or thieves could easily unbuckle the strap from behind you
text: This latest iteration is a 1 step forward, 2 steps back.  The buckle is a one-hand clip which means practical jokers or thieves could easily unbuckle the strap from behind you.  A thick zip tie will solve this in my case, as would some gaff or duct tape since most of us won't be unbuckling this very often, if at all.  The other questionable pieces are the 2 moveable bumper locks.  The previous version would unlock and slide easily in both directions, making one-hand adjustments quick and smooth.  On this version, the spring-loaded clips require tension if you have a smaller camera, meaning two hands are needed to put each lock in place.  This isn't a big deal but does slow you down in some situations.  Other than that, the strap holds nicely in place and I like the new locking carabiner design - it feels like a tighter lock and the flanged lock/screw are a nice touch.  Otherwise, love these straps and use them on both my cameras.

title: Make sure it works with your phone
text:
This product ended up being a disappointment for me. I had an older phone, a Galaxy S3 Mini, that I used it with. It worked pretty well with that phone and I probably would have given it three or four stars. The only real problem was that when connected a feedback noise came through the speakers. It was kind of like little beeps or chirps and didn't happen consistently. I figured out how to stop that by putting my phone in airplane mode. That was annoying, but not damning.

I upgraded to a Galaxy S6 and hoped that the feedback problem would go away. It didn't, and other performance issues started cropping up. The phone has this dumb feature where it warns when the volume is over half capacity when headphones are plugged in. That means that the alarm won't make noise if you have it turned up too loud until you tell the phone it's okay. I would have thought there would be a way for the Hale apps to disable that stupid safety feature. Then I got a software upgrade from AT&T, and now the alarm doesn't take the phone out of sleep mode to wake me up. Basically, my wife's alarm would go off and I'd start to wonder why mine hadn't. I'd wake my phone up and the alarm would go off. I'm not a software designer, but I think that's backwards. It's obvious to me that the people behind this product don't keep their software up to date.

Really, there were a lot of cool features with the product. The sound was very good and I'll probably keep it to listen to music on. Having a button to dismiss/snooze was very nice while it worked. The alarm app itself was pretty good. There were some features I wish it had, but it was as feature-rich as many other alarm apps that I've seen. If you have a phone that you know will work with this, I do recommend it. On Hale's website there's a list of confirmed devices. Don't do like I did and hope that your phone will work if it's not on that list.

title: A Great FM DX Performer for the Summer of 2018
text: This radio is great for the summer of 2018, the reason why I am saying that is that this radio is very small, small enough to fit inside your front pocket of the shorts you are wearing outside.  The HD radio reception is great, and it's very sensitive to pick up DX signals, and weak part 15, low power FM, and weak FM translator signals, and the selectivity is great as well.  I am able to take this radio with me, and listen to my favorite HD radio broadcasts while I out sitting outside waiting to board my city bus.  I have taken this radio out during a hot day, and it survives high temperatures, especially the high humidity we get here in Southeastern, Virginia.  I would recommend this radio for your travel, vacation spots, and for BBQ's and also for hanging around in a park somewhere.  Now for the AM radio reception, this radio does great picking up distant AM stations, local, semi local AM stations, and also traveller information stations. It's also good picking up strong local HD digital AM stations.  You can use this with a tunable AM loop antenna to pull in more distant AM stations.  The only thing that this radio is missing is Bluetooth, and AUX and Shortwave and Longwave with SSB would be nice for this radio maybe in the next model.  Also it's great on battery life, it's been a while me replacing the AA batteries.  Also it comes with a quiet switching mode AC adapter, so be sure that when you plug it in that it's away from the radio receiver like down on the floor away from the radio.

title: Lots of bells and whistle for Windows 10, doesn't work with Windows 7
text:
Using this motherboard is like using a small Lear Jet to drive a mile down the road. It will get you there, but there are so many extra buttons and switches you have to push, just to get it going, it can be very intimidating. And.. it's like having a brand new instrument panel, full of buried and confusing menu items that are set to use engines from 2018, but yours are from 2014 and... the instruments just don't see them.
right off the bat this mobo wouldn't "see" any of my SATA drives. Neither the HDD or the SDD. I DID see my BluRay reader/writer. but moving a drive there again, wouldn't be seen. Then it WOULD be seen, but not able to be boot from.
Turns out, this mobo is set from the factory to automatically use Intel's Optane memory. And if it doesn't see it, nada. You have to dig in, find the right menu (sub, sub, menu) choice and turn it to SATA AHCI.
I was finally able to get it to boot from a Windows 10 SSD, but it wouldn't boot from a Windows 7 SSD.
I gave it 3 stars because of the fact that it DID start up with Windows 10.
Could NOT get it to work with Windows 7! Windows would start 3 seconds later, reboot. Same thing if I tried "Safe Mode" it would load basic drivers for a few seconds, hang, and reboot.
I was able to get it to boot from, and use a UEFI Windows 10 Recovery DVD. But, after 4 hours of futzing this POS I couldn't get it to use either a Windows "Recovery" DVD or a Windows 7 "Installation" DVD. Several different DVDs, in fact. I could get it to boot to the DVD initial menu of choosing a US layout Keyboard, but at that point, the USB locked up. Neither mouse, nor keyboard were recognized. Changing USB menu options in the BIOS (UEFI) would either make the lights on the keyboard/mouse go out as soon as the DVD loaded, OR.. would leave the lights on, but made both the keyboard and mouse unresponsive. There were lights on, but nooobody home.

It also would not recognize my RAM, DDR4 3200. It recognized it as 2133. Now, that could be because my CPU, and Intel Core-i9700k was only clocked at 3.6GHz (natively). Or that I had to go into the submenus and figure out how to "overclock" it to the correct speed. I've never, ever had this problem with RAM. I buy a speed, plug it in, and it's seen as it's supposed to be. Whether DDR2 or DDR3, 4200, 6400, 12800, 1600, whatever, the mobo automatically picked the correct speed.

I think if you have Windows 10 (Maybe Windows H8 (that's pronounced HATE), you *might* get this to work. It has some menu choices for either Windows 8/10 or "other OS". Changing this made no difference.
In addition to having Windows 10, if you also have a love of digging into and trying to figure out cryptic motherboard choices, overclocks and lots of non-intuitive submenus.. then this is the mobo for you.
Not for me. I'm sending it back.
No, I would not recommend it UNLESS you have Windows 10, a LOVE of tiny sub, sub, sub menu choices and lots and LOTS of time. Not hours, but days or weeks!

text:
This machine is snappy, the 6th gen i3 processor is plenty for a Chromebook. The keyboard and touchpad are both good and the glass top attracts fingerprints but they wipe off easily. USB type C is going to become more and more common, so it's great that this device charges via a USB C port. This device can now run Android apps, which opens up a lot of possibilities. Games like Hearthstone work surprisingly well.

The speakers are adequate, but once a week or so I'll hear a little static on top of whatever audio is playing. If I pause the audio for a second and restart it, the static is gone. It's minor and uncommon but it makes me wonder about the quality of the speakers.

Finally, the 1366 x 768 display is only okay. It's matte, so you don't get a lot of glare, and brightness seems good to me. The contrast is a little lacking though, and the viewing angles aren't great. The display isn't really a distraction to me and I use this laptop everyday, but don't expect it to be great.

Overall this is a machine with great performance, Android app support, a good touchpad and keyboard, an okay screen and a great price. Overall I'm very happy with it.

title: Pop goes the weasel
text:
Wired this up to a factory ford head unit that supplies low level outputs. I have the unit set to RCA input with no filtering. I have a 12v power on wire that comes on when the doors open (The ford factory amp turn on is only 6v). I have the cables inside a shielded sheath, so it is done correctly. The amp gets the ground from the same ground point as the head unit. All connections are soldered or using OEM-type connectors.

When the unit gets power, with the car off, there is a faint noise from the speaker. Also a "pop" when you turn it on. That was at a gain of 50%. I turned it down all the way, which was enough for me, yet I still get the pop (Although it is quieter). Afterwards, the unit sounds great and puts out plenty of power for the factory drivers. But still, the pop isn't good for the speakers, and Alpine should be ashamed for the pop.

If you research it online, you will find lots of people with the same problem, using different installs, so it's not just because I'm using a factory head unit. It was a pain to install, so I'm not going to return it, but if I had known about it, I would have got something else.

These headphones had great construction and great sound. That said, they are not worth the MSRP $500.

The foam pads feel really nice. They are the best quality I have seen on a pair of headphones. That said, their stiffness didn't allow them to form a tight seal around my ears, causing that disorienting feeling mentioned earlier.

Choosing between these and the Bose QC35, I'd go with the Bose. They're cheaper, feel just as good on my head, and the sound is still great. The noise cancellation is a level above, and the signal doesn't crap out when walking through the city. I will say, however, that the Bose do not seem to have to same robust construction as the Momentum 2.0. The Momentum band is metal vs the plastic on the Bose.

Overall, great headphones. But realistically, not worth the money. There are much better cans out there for the price.

title: Fast, light, powerful and good looking.
text:
This is a fantastic laptop. I've been using a MacBook Air for a while and when it fell to the ground and the screen was shattered, I felt paying $450 for a new screen was a ripoff. After lots of researching, I settled for this UX305, buying the 8GB RAM, Core i5 and 256GB SSD version. My comparison will be directly to my experience with the MacBook Air.

1) Performance: if you buy the Core i5 version (cost me $750 from Amazon, just $50 more than the anemic Core M version) you get a 5200U processor, which is very similar to what you get on a 2015 MacBook Air. This is the Broadwell architecture from 2015, which in itself is little more than a 14nm reduction of the 2014 Haswell architecture, which was 20nm. When the fabrication process of the CPU is reduced (20 to 14 nanometers), you automatically get power benefits, giving you the option of achieving better battery life with the same performance as last year, or more performance at the same battery life as the previous year. Over the past few weeks that I've owned the UX305, I regularly have Word, Excel, Acrobat Pro and Edge/Chrome open with ~10 tabs active. This doesn't fully load the 8GB RAM and the performance remains fluid. I even tried playing 4K videos on YouTube and they played flawlessly, no stutter. So, performance, for office work - and light gaming, think Trine 2 on high settings and 720p resolution - is flawless.

2) Weight: the MacBook Air is 2.97 pounds, whereas the UX305 is 2.6 pounds. If you find the Air portable, the UX305 is even more so. I didn't think I'd notice those .3 pounds, but it actually makes a big, big difference. I "forget" my UX305 is in my work bag, whereas I was very conscious that the Air was in it.

3) Design: pretty much a MacBook Air ripoff. The frame of the laptop is actually a bit thinner and narrower than the Air, so you get a similar experience on an overall smaller (by a hair) machine. The aluminum build feels great and is sturdy - no flex that I notice, but I'm not bending it on purpose as those tests make no sense.

The keyboard doesn't feel as excellent in quality as the Air, but then again, the UX305 is literally half the price of the equivalent Air. Still, I'm typing on it right now, and it's been perfectly fine for the past few weeks. There is enough key travel to be comfortable and keys are well spaced. The only drawback is the lack of keyboard backlight, but if you don't type in dark places, this is a non-issue. (I've heard people complain about the power button position on top of the backspace key: guess what, it's literally the same as the Air, yet nobody ever complained about that in the Apple machine. That's bias for you. It was never a problem for Apple, yet somehow it "is a problem" in the Asus for some reviewers. News flash: it wasn't a problem in the Air, and it's not a problem in the Asus. It's literally the same.)

The screen is insane. A 13.3" 1080p IPS matte panel - compare that to the Air's pathetic 900p TFT display. The matte panel is welcome as I have yet to see a single reflection on the screen: it is pristinely clear. Windows 10 defaults to a 150% scaling which I think makes everything look like fisher price toys. I toned it back down to %125 and things look perfect, super sharp too. Color calibration is a bit cool - makes the screen seem a bit brighter - and after calibrating with my Spyder5Express - which I wholeheartedly recommend - it looks even better. A bit dimmer than factory default, for sure, but still bright enough for using outside under sunlight.

The audio quality is better than I expected. I had read plenty reviews that said the audio sucks and it's quite tinny. Maybe that's a problem with the Core M version, but on this i5 honestly it sounds fine. If anything, it's not tinny at all, it has a decent "body" or "volume", it reminds me of the Surface Pro 3, so I wouldn't call it bad at all. Of course, don't expect amazing bass, you have to be realistic here, but it's perfectly fine sound quality. I would say though, the MacBook Air definitely had better sound. Not insanely better, but it felt as better quality reproduction (not sure how to explain it). Then again, remember: the UX305 costs half what the Air does.

4) Battery - I've used it for 2 working days straight (not constantly on) on a battery charge. On a more regular workday, it lasts through the day, usually around 9 hours. That's pretty much all I need. The Air gives you easily 3-4h more battery life on equivalent workloads, but the UX305 gets me through the day comfortably and that's all I need.

So, in conclusion, this UX305 is in essence a faster, lighter, more powerful version of the i5 MacBook Air, but it is Windows based, made by Asus and it'll cost you half the price. If you want such a machine for office work and light gaming/browsing/video viewing, go for it. It's excellent.

title: VERY unhappy with the product quality and features... I would skip this version or return it if you already ordered it
text:
Update 08-JAN-2018: I increased my review to 2 stars after following the fix posted by another reviewer. I had to remove my PlayStation account from Bungie so that this piece of kit could see my PC account for Destiny 2. The device is still lacking in every other area... It could have been so much more if they'd just made it a standalone Echo device with special features....

Original Review Below:

It is aesthetically pleasing, sadly it has some design flaws that significantly detract from my ability to enjoy the product as is...

1. This is a glorified speaker and not a very high quality one at that...
2. There is NO MIC? If you want to speak to it, do it through your Amazon Echo device or the App on your phone. At this price point it is 2x the current cost of an Amazon Echo Dot. Why didn't they simply license it and make it a full blown Echo (with a mic of course)? The current price for the features provided makes for a regrettable purchase. I honestly THOUGHT this was simply an Echo Dot with a different plastic trim kit, a few LEDs and a custom voice... THAT would have been doable at this price point and made for a device that is usable for a lot more than it does now.
3. The plastic feels cheap. If this is ever dropped on a hard surface, I would expect a busted device as the plastic is not pliable enough to absorb the impact.
4. The speaker sounds cheap and there is NO volume adjustment. The speaker on my Echo Dot sounds better at half the price.
5. The Installation Process is rife with issues. Do an Internet search and you will see no shortage of posts on problems with linking Accounts. You cannot have more than a single platform linked with bungee. I have my PS4 account for Destiny on PSN and play Destin 2 on my PC via Battle.net and the Ghost device would act as though it was activated but would be unable to do anything with my character like equip a weapon, change loadout, etc... I had to unlink my PS4 account from Bungee and re-do the setup for the Ghost when my Battle.net account was the only one linked.
That resolved the issue... That is simply unacceptable. I have to give up my PS4 PSN account link in Bungee so that I can use this device in Destiny 2.
6. The ghost stands on 2 points that have a very small flattened area for the 'feet'. Any bump and it tips over. Bump the computer desk it sits on with the chair? It falls over. Close the drawer on the desk, it falls over. Sit your drink on the coaster next to it, the Ghost falls over. How hard it is to provide a design that actually stands up as it should?
7. The power cable is REQUIRED for it to work. The power cable provided is VERY short. It barely reaches from desk height to the power strip on the floor... barely. If are power cable is required to even use the device, why not provide a cable that is long enough to provide some flexibility on where you plug it in. The cable is far shorter than my Echo Dot cable, yet it uses the same power brick. Meh.
8. My Echo is the only thing that plays audio back in the voice of the Ghost. This problem is also rampant among consumers. It took 3 setup attempts and the solution has not yet been found. I believe if I reset it to factory and repeat the entire setup process now that I've followed the account link fix listed in item # 5 on this list, it 'might' work, but I'm not holding out much hope at this point.
9. No comments or statement from the manufacturer on the issues people are having on the forums at Activision, Bungee, Battle.net, etc... At least say SOMETHING... as it is the consumer is forced to use a 'hobbled' product or simply return it.
10. Free Alexa skill, BUT you need an Amazon Echo device to use this one. That adds even more $$$ should you not have one already. I assumed incorrectly on this shortcoming when I pre-ordered the device. I simply assumed at this price point it would be just be an Echo device with a fancy outfit.. NOPE. That mistake is on me.

Instead of a multi-use device you get a cheap plastic "Ghost" with 4 single color LED light, a flashing center light, a crappy speaker, no support, poor instructions, ridiculously short power cable, no integrated mic and ZERO functionality outside of Destiny 2. On the bright side you will get some exercise from picking the Ghost up and balancing it upright repeatedly. I have resorted to just leaving it sideways.

title: Works Perfectly; Fantastic Buy
text:
I bought this to use with a Raspberry Pi. However, I tested it with a few other things, just to play around with it. It works fantastically. So far, I have not been able to find a case that I like for it yet, so you will see in the photos, I temporarily used the box it came in to make an enclosure for both it, and my rPi. It's actually pretty nice, and convenient to use this way (for now).

I love using this thing constantly. It works perfectly for my needs.

So, on most of the things I plugged it into, the resolution worked without a problem. However, as you can see in the pictures, Raspberian does not automatically work well with it. You have to do a few things first. First off, when I first plugged it into my rPi, it actually just flickered on and off randomly, so it didn't seem to be getting enough power. The touchscreen will not work, when it is not plugged into the rPi, so you want to fix this, and get it working properly, instead of using an external power source.

You can find the config.txt documentation here:
[...]

If you don't want to look through all of the documentation, or just need help, here is what I did:
-Connected the screen to an external power supply temporarily, and used a regular mouse/keyboard
-Opened 'Terminal' and entered the following:
sudo nano /boot/config.txt

Using the arrow keys, I scrolled to the bottom, and typed in:
# Config - Kuman 7" Touchscreen
hdmi_cvt 800 480 60 6 0 0 0
hdmi_group=2
hdmi_mode=1
hdmi_mode=87
max_usb_current=1

-To exit and save the file:
Press 'Ctrl-X' then 'Y' then 'Enter'

-To reboot type:
sudo shutdown -r now

-Plug the usb power cord into your rPi.
The screen will flicker with colors as it comes on, then once it gets to the desktop, everything should be fitting perfectly, not flickering, and the touchscreen will work.

I received this product at a discount, with the agreement that I would provide a proper review, purely off my experience with it.
No agreement was given, on a positive or negative review and I was not compensated, past the initial discount, for reviewing it.
I myself depend entirely on reviews, before purchasing new items, so please, [...]!

title: my experience has been good with these routers on a single network
text:
I bought 2 of these from Amazon when they were full price, before the comment-kazi storm.

In terms of real world performance, from a verified purchaser, my experience has been good with these routers on a single network, using the 2nd router in range extender / wireless access point mode. Setup was easy per the Medialink user manual.

My house is an L shaped brick rambler over full basement with open rafters, so I was able to install one router in each end of the house, each sitting on top of a beam, such that they were under the hardwood flooring of the main floor. I had tried to make one router work at first by placing it centrally, but brick homes, with old plaster and wire walls with a behemoth of a sandstone fireplace isn't conducive to wireless, hence the need for a 2nd router.

Connected to the main router was the cable modem, cable to the 2nd router, a Cisco VOIP device, a NAS drive, and an 8 port switch to which was connected a Windows7 PC (running 24x7) and pair of Silicondust HD Homerun digital tuners that powered my Snapstream BeyondTV PVR setup. The 2nd router connected a pair of old non-wireless printers stuffed in the coat closet.

The network served 4 Windows 7 wireless desktops, 4 Kindles, 3 Roku devices, 2 laptops, a netbook, and guests, without issue of any kind. I routinely backed up all the PCs with Macrium Reflect Free to a notebook USB drive and then transferred the file to the NAS server, accessed internet from every capable device, watched live TV with the Silicondust software from EVERY PC and streamed recorded TV from the NAS server with VLC player and the Mega CODEC pack. I used Newsbin6 to access and download programs from Usenet binary archives, which were reassembled from PAR files over the network to the NAS server, flawlessly.

In the 2 years (give or take) that I used this setup, I had to reboot the routers just 3 or 4 times. I upgraded the firmware twice as best I can recall.

These routers, at the current pricing level, are an excellent bargain for a wireless N router. In a brick home like mine (described above), I'd put the range at about 35' radius.

Regarding the negative reviews, well, most were part of the comment-kazi storm and had more to do with an internet 'social media' attack campaign than it had to do with the quality and operation / functionality of the product.

Yeah, I paid a premium price for these, but then, I've gotten excellent service from them and that, as far as I am concerned, is the real value. Putting that in perspective, these 2 routers replaced a dying and trouble prone Linksys G and an Asus N router that locks up when I access the admin pages. It got old, fast with those 2 routers - having to do a pushbutton/factory reset and reconfigure them from the ground up every time they decided to lock up. That you'll just have to take my word on, I guess, since they were purchased elsewhere.
