title: Best Splitter/Amp for large house installations! You can't go wrong!
text:
After doing a lot of research on amplifiers/splitters for large Coax installations, I found this to be the best. In fact it looks like Comcast (My local cable provider) uses both the PPC 5-port and 9-port models for large X1 installations. I spent the past weekend installing this in place of a standalone amplifier and passive 5-way splitter (which wasn't working very well). Everything is working amazing now! Prior to the installation (which included running all new RG6 Quad Shielded Coax) I was only able to achieve a maximum of 90mbps down on a good day. Now I'm hitting 120mbps. You can't go wrong with this splitter/amp! It's also MOCA compatible, so if you have an X1 Entertainment system, you're covered! The new RG6Q I ran probably had more to do with my cable internet performance increase since there was a noticeable decrease in line noise and an increase in signal integrity to the modem (Both Downstream and Upstream). However without the Amplifier portion of this splitter, the attenuation from the sheer length of Coax and the number of set-top boxes (HD Receivers) I have in the house would have degraded the signal to the modem (More ports/splitters = More Loss per port). To a point where the modem would have dropped it's connection to Comcast and possibly even the HD boxes/X1 DVR would have seen connectivity issues. The house I networked is fairly large, about 2500sq/ft, two story, 5 bedroom. This made some of the coax runs very lengthy, using a passive splitter for this many rooms/devices simply would not have worked.

PROs:
- 9 port Splitter Amp. (0 loss/0 gain)
- Low Cost.
- Easy setup/installation.
- Includes passive port for VOIP or DATA modems (In the event you lose power to amp).

CONs:
- NONE!

For those that are curious. My current house installation is setup as follows:
PPC-EVO (P1) - X1 DVR in Family Room [20ft run, P1 recommended for DVR or Master video units]
PPC-EVO (P2) - X1 HD Box Bedroom#3 [~75ft run, P1-4 recommended for longest runs]
PPC-EVO (P3) - Bedroom#4 (Future use, 75ohm terminated) [~75ft run]
PPC-EVO (P4) - NON-HD Digital Receiver (Kitchen Cabinet TV) [~80ft run]
PPC-EVO (P5) - X1 HD Box Bedroom#5 [~35ft run, P5-8 recommended for shortest runs]
PPC-EVO (P6) - Bedroom#1 (Future use, 75ohm terminated) [~40ft run]
PPC-EVO (P7) - Bedroom#2 (Future use, 75ohm terminated) [~50ft run]
PPC-EVO (P8) - NULL
PPC-EVO (Passive -3.5db) - Motorola Surfboard Cable Modem [~65ft run]

I'm getting +2dbmV downstream on the modem, which is much higher than I expected when using the passive -3.5db port, but well within the modem's "happy place."

title: Refrigerator For Your AVR!
text:
Best small investment I've made yet for my home theater, hands down!

I was waiting on AC Infinity to hopefully make an S10 or T10 front exhaust system since the rear exhaust wouldn't work for me with my media rack not having an open rear cabinet and didn't want the top exhaust because I wanted to stack my BD player on top of exhaust system due to space constraints in my media rack and I saw on their website at the end of last year that they were coming soon and I kept an eye out on Amazon for them to be released and both systems went on sale within days apart and I couldn't wait to get my hands on the T10 and ordered it as soon as it was available.

This thing is incredible and does an awesome job keeping my Onkyo TX-RZ720 nice and cool. I love the digital display and felt that was worth the upgrade price over the S10. Being able to see the exact current temp of my AVR is extremely useful, I also like temp and fan speed settings along with the ability to set an alarm if your unit goes over a certain temp so you know to shut off your AVR if need be so it doesn't overheat.

I have the unit set on smart mode with a max temp setting of 87 degrees F for max fan speed to engage on that setting it starts the fan on low speed at 77 degrees F and for the past week my AVR hasn't gone over 80 degrees F and usually stays around 78 degrees F while still on the lowest fan setting and that's with driving the AVR pretty hard and in use for over 5 hours at a time.

As a reference, I wanted to test the temp probe and see how hot my AVR was getting without cooling and didn't engage the fans and ran my AVR for 6 hours the day I got this and it showed my AVR hovering at about 94 degrees F. Shut down the AVR and went to bed and the next day engaged the fans on smart mode and the temp has been holding steady at 78 degrees F after 5 hours of use. Very Impressed!

The fan is also extremely quiet, I can't really hear that it's running but the display tells me that it is and I can also feel the air coming out of the front exhaust vents.

Trust me, if you want to prolong the life of your AVR, grab one of these exhaust systems, either the S or T models and whatever exhaust application works for your (front, rear or top). The T has a few more bells and whistles than the S and I don't regret the extra $20 for these upgrades but either way, protect your AVR as overheating is one of the reasons amps or HDMI boards go out prematurely and with how much AVR's cost, especially higher end ones, there's no reason not to protect your investment but that's just me :)

title: Recording video requires paid subscription - per camera!
text:
Dropcam comes out of the box with live video watching only. And you cannot record it to a computer in your home. You must pay $99 per year PER CAMERA if you want to be able to replay any video. Unless you pay this fee you will be telling the officers that you have no recorded video of the crime, even though you had cameras in your home.

It gets worse: Even if you pay the fee, if you go on an extended vacation and return to find your home robbed, you still will have to tell the officers that you have no recorded video of the crime because Dropcam automatically deletes all your videos after 7 days. You have to pay $299 per year PER CAMERA if you want Dropcam to give you access to your own video longer than a week.

And to top it off: starting a subscription does not retroactively give you access to video recordings. If you had no subscription before the cameras captured something important, like a home invasion, you're screwed.

Who is the real burglar here?

title: I bough this router because my old one was garbage; it was legitimately dropping the signal due to ...
text:
People complain a lot about this router. They forget that electronic appliances, especially wireless ones, are bound by the laws of physics. As in, if you install it poorly, have obstructions in the way, have it on the wrong settings, it will not work!

I get some people have legitimate complaints. I get some of them are lemons, I have sympathy for you. But for many of you who are having issues with dropped signals, you need to look into some of the settings. As an avid pc gamer, I bough this router because my old one was garbage; it was legitimately dropping the signal due to its age. I got the Netgear N600 and I had the SAME issue. Every game, it would disconnect for a few seconds.

I went into the settings, and changed the capped data transfer rate, and changed the channel from like...153, to 3. It solved everything. It works perfectly. In my opinion it's one of the best bang-for-your-buck dual band wireless router/modem combos you can buy.

title: Great Buy
text: I bought this bundle for my 9-year-old son who is an avid reader. This kindle does not have a light like the Paperwhite, but that is fine for a 9-year-old child who can see just fine. It is not too dark for him to read. If he wants to read in bed at night, he uses a small book light.  I bought myself the Kindle Paperwhite because I now use reading glasses and need more light to read. I also do a lot of reading before bed in my low lit bedroom. Otherwise, I would have bought this bundle for myself too. I did add the Kindle Free Time reading setting for my son because he likes to keep track of how much he is reading each day. His teacher requires him to turn in a reading log weekly. With the app this just makes it so much easier because it automatically does it. Once he outgrows the "Free time" it can be turned off. The content in the kids free time store is not that important to us since we borrow a lot of e-books from the library. I think in previous generations when the "free time" app was turned on, you could not borrow books from the library. That is not the case now. We have no problem downloading books from the library. I will say it takes a few steps to accomplish this. I have to search the library on my laptop first. Check the e-book out from the library. Have the book sent to my Amazon account. Then go to Amazon and tell it which kindle to send the e-book to. Once it arrives in the right kindle, you need to download it onto the kindle. More steps than I would like, but not enough that it keeps me from borrowing books. Overall, this has been a great buy for us. My son takes his kindle everywhere. If you think you need some lighting to see better, go with the Kindle Paperwhite. Otherwise, this one is just fine.

title: Good Portable Speaker That's Easy To Operate And Sounds Clear And Punchy With More Bass But It's Not Overdone
text:
This Sony speaker sounds clear and punchy, and it provides overall good sound quality for its small size. It's uber portable so it can be used anywhere in the house or on the go. This speaker has a rubbery exterior and is water resistant, so it seems quite durable and perfect for outdoor activities like hanging by the pool. I pair it with my iPhone or iPad and use it in different locations in the house as a speakerphone or as a speaker for listening to music or video I'm streaming. This Sony speaker pairs easily with my Apple devices (hold down on power a couple seconds and select it in your Bluetooth settings) and maintains a steady connection.

I've maxed out the volume to see how it sounds, and it's plenty powerful for me and sounds pretty good at higher volumes. The features aren't a lot different than a couple good portable speakers I've owned for years, though it definitely has more bass (but not too much for me), plus I like the capability of using two speakers together for stereo sound. The color looks like orange red to me instead of a true red, and the control markings don't really contrast with the color. So the controls are a strain for me to see, but it's not a big deal as there are so few controls. This is an easy speaker to use, has a good battery life, seems durable and sounds good especially for those who like extra bass as this is more bassy than my other small speakers. Recommended.

title: Get this TV NOW!! You WON'T regret it!! Amazing picture!! Best bang for your buck!!
text:
I wanted to upgrade my 50" Vizio E Series (2013 model) to a larger sized set. At first, I purchased a 60" "more expensive" brand that I just wasn't impressed with (especially for the price tag: $1,500.00). Returned the $1,500.00 set after having it for only 3 days and seeing a TON of motion blur, and the "upscaling" that the 4k was supposed to offer wasn't that impressive at all. I liked the built-in browser the set had, but it wasn't enough to justify the amount of money I had spent on it. When I went to upgrade, I thought I'd splurge and try out a 4K UHD set, because that's what's trending now.

After returning the "more expensive brand" TV I originally bought, I thought I'd go back to Vizio for not only the value, but the fact that I could get a 65" screen for hundreds of dollars less (and better picture!), and also because my previous 50" E Series never did me wrong! I loved it, but I just wanted a bigger screen. Had it just over a year, never had a problem. Yes, it's more simplistic than some other brands, and yes, it is only 1080P, and I'm aware Vizio makes the M Series, or the P Series, and now, even the R Series, which all offer 4k, but my main focus was on SIZE. I just wanted a BIGGER TV.

At first, I was going to go with the 60" Vizio E Series set, because to me, going from 50" to 60" is quite the difference. But then I did some research and found that the 65"-70" E Series sets offer the 6 (vs the 4) core processor, and a the higher "240HZ" refresh rate (which is really 120HZ, but still better than the 60HZ that the "more expensive brand" had, hence all the motion blur I noticed).
I've had this set now for over a month and I will say, I LOVE it! I'm EXTREMELY happy with my decision to stick with 1080P (for now), and to have gotten the size I did. Some TV snobs might say Vizio's aren't anything special, but I've now had 2 sets from them, and have never had a problem, and have always really enjoyed the picture the sets produce. The technology has definitely been improved. My previous set would lag a little bit sometimes upon starting up the APPS, and I don't know if it's because of the faster processor or what that the 65"-70" E series models have that affect this; but the APPS all launch VERY quickly, the set starts up very quickly, and the initial set-up is a breeze and if you have WiFi, you'll be connected to it within minutes after turning the TV on out of the box and going through the set-up process.
I have both Hulu PLUS and Netflix, and I've yet to experience ANY problems streaming anything on either of those two APPS. I've also used the Yahoo! APP, since the 6th season of "Community" was on it, and that never gave me a problem either.
I also have a PS4 connected to the TV for gaming, and this TV is AMAZING in that category as well! All around, it's an excellent value, especially for the size and all the features you get.

The design of the TV is nice and modern looking. All black, which I love! Minimalistic, clean, and sharp looking. I don't have my set mounted to the wall, I use the legs and have it on a stand. The ONLY draw-back I could see, is it IS mandatory to have a WIDE enough stand to place the set on, because the of the legs being quite far apart. Luckily for me, I already had a wide enough stand, so this wasn't an issue for me.
Eventually, when the content is there, I'll definitely get a 4K set, and it'll most likely be a Vizio, because you just can't beat the value! I have the 5.1 sound system to accompany the set (which is an AMAZING sound system!), and that's also another product from them that I'm extremely happy with. No, it isn't a Bose, but whatever. To me, the sound is incredible, and to be honest, the only other minor thing that could be improved with this TV is the sound it comes with itself. But how much sound quality can you really expect from ANY flat screen TV out there? Regardless of the brand, all sets now are so thin, there's not really a whole lot of room to house amazing speakers in any of these TV's now. But I think most people are pairing their sets (especially larger TV's) with some sort of alternative sound system nowadays anyway.

This has been a much longer review than I expected to write, but I really can't say enough positive things about this TV. I'm in LOVE, and 100% satisfied with my purchase. But if you're considering getting this TV, DON'T HESITATE! GO FOR IT!! You won't regret it!! I know I've only had it for a month, so time will tell how long it lasts me, but I'm counting on at LEAST a few years, until I'm ready to upgrade again.

I should also note that I have it on for at least 16 hours/day EVERY day for the month I've had it. When my wife and I go to work, the set needs to be on for our one dog who has separation anxiety. Having the TV on puts him at ease. And like I said, not one problem. Not a glitch, not a problem streaming, everything has been PERFECT!! My previous E-Series (2013 model) would sometimes freeze up while streaming Netflix, but I haven't had that problem once since getting this set. Both Netflix and Hulu movies/series/etc. all load rapidly and NEVER stop to "buffer". Netflix has 1080P resolution, and Hulu has 720P, and the picture from Hulu still looks AMAZING.

I'm already excited to get my next VIZIO set with the 4K, and this one will either be used as our bedroom TV, or media room TV. My wife is sick of hearing about the TV talk, but I can't help it, I'm in LOVE!! haha.

I really hope this review helps some people during their hunt for their next set. If you're not ready to invest in the 4K, but want a big screen, and a fantastic picture, and also offers smart capabilities, along with a great gaming experience, LOOK NO FURTHER! And DEFINITELY go for the 65"-70" for the more advanced technology! The 65" - 70" has the faster processor (which actually is a very noticeable upgrade with how fast everything loads), and also comes with true 120HZ, so there's hardly any motion blur. There really is a distinct difference between 60HZ and 120HZ.

title: With Tagg this was the best tracker I've tried, now under Whistle completely useless!
text:
We upgraded to this tracker after several years with Tagg. I was agreeably suprised at the improvements in battery life, tracking and general design. It seemed that Tagg had worked out some kinks and I was happy and confident in my dogs safety.
In fact, it worked flawlessly until Tuesday October 6, when were forced (literally) to "upgrade" to Whistle. Then it became a completely useless collar attachment. Oh, I can post pics of my dog on social media now, but am unable to locate her, track her, or even monitor her activity. Hate to point this out to you Whistle, but those are the exact reasons I purchased this product!
Customer support is terrible. I'm not saying they're rude cause they are very nice, but it took 6 days, 5 emails, and 4 phone calls to get someone to authorize a replacement for me. And who knows if that one will work since it's clearly not for many others?
My questions:
Why remove critical features from a potentially life-saving device? Why focus on pet social media instead? And why not admit you made a huge mistake and roll back to Tagg (something that was working!) until you actually get this working?
Buyer beware, this may work in the future, but right not, it's totally inoperable for anything other than social media.

title: Powerful, Sexy, but runs hot.
text:
I got the 1080 with optane version and just set it up last night, so far so good.

I have it hooked up to a 27" Dell 2k monitor with G-Sync. A monitor with G-Sync is an absolute must for this graphics card, and currently the one I got is on sale at bestbuy and is the cheapest on the market.

Only tested two games so far:

Arma 3 on ULTRA settings, was hovering at around 80 fps. Pretty good for a terribly optimized game.
League of Legends (never looked so good lol) at max settings peaked at the beginning of the game at over 500 fps, and hovered in the mid 200's to 300's for the majority of the match.

Some pros so far:
>The case looks even better in person, and you can customize the lights. Hands down best looking AW case I've seen, some of them can look really ridiculous.
>Powerful. If it can handle a game as terribly optimized as Arma 3 on ULTRA, it can handle anything.
>Alienware Command Center is definitely a neat tool to monitor your thermals, and manually adjust your fan profiles.
>Although I haven't done it yet, it's very easy to take it apart to get at the internals. I've seen videos of people doing it, and it requires no tools; just pop off the side and push a lever and you're looking at the motherboard.

Only con I've noticed so far:
>Thermals. Seeing as this Amazon config is *NOT* running liquid cooling, you need to manually adjust the fan profiles to actually make a difference. They don't do too much at default settings. They are super loud, and it makes me a little nervous. I personally will be looking at liquid cooling options very soon.

The verdict so far is that it's a fantastic beast of a machine. I will update this review as I spend more time with it and notice any more pros/cons.

title: Sound quality unbeatable until you double the cost!
text:
I cannot say enough good things about these speakers. I auditioned many speakers, and could not find better sounding units for the money. Are there better sounding speakers? Absolutely there are. But you have to spend at least double to beat them. If you are looking for audiophile sound quality without breaking the bank these are your speaker.

The highs are bright and crisp without much coloration and no harshness. They play incredibly deep, and hit harder than you can imagine. The bass is controlled, punchy, and full but never gets boomy. They reproduce sound faithfully and are fairly efficient. That last bit are their biggest downfall. They are so faithful that they make poor sources sound poor. It truly is garbage in garbage out. A lot of speakers color the sound with resonances. These do not (which is good). If you bring someone over to show off, make sure you use a high quality source (Blu-ray, CD, high bitrate audio).

You will not be disappointed!

title: Does its job for bright telescopes.
text:
It's pretty simple: it acts like "moonglasses" so the moon isn't so bright. I use this on my Meade 20mm and my Orion 28mm Expanse eyepieces and it's a perfect fit. With my 8" Dobsonian reflector and these two wide angle eyepieces, the moon looks amazing...and painfully bright. Without the filter, when you are done looking at the moon, you'll be stuck with a ghost image in your vision as you're trying to observe other, much-less-bright things. With the brightness comes a loss of details, especially the details of craters such as Tycho. I don't know if it was me or the filter, but I did see a tiny drop on sharpness, but the improved contrast is worth it. It's still very sharp, though!

13% transmission is a substantial darkening, so if you have a smaller scope (100mm or 4 inches is what I'm seeing in my research), go with a 25% transmission, which will allow in much more light while still reducing the brightness to a comfortable level.

You probably won't need this for a crescent moon, but certainly when it gets to Gibbous and Full phases, you'll need it to make it comfortable to view. I might be getting another one so I won't have to keep switching it back and forth between eyepieces.

title: MORE DATA POINTS
text:
I ordered three [3] of these boomCANs and plan on ordering more for gifts and personal use. Each boomCAN package contains two [2] devices; the speaker and the cerberus-like three-headed cable (USB/miniUSB/3.5mm jack). I tested all six devices. Here are my results:
One of three cables was bad.
Were you to receive a bad cable the results would be what you see in the 1 or 2 star reviews; eg the cable doesn't work, or sometimes works, or makes poor connections, causing weak to sporadic sound. If you have the spare parts lying around all you need is USB male to miniUSB male (for charging), 3.5mm male to 3.5mm male (for connecting it to your device). Both of which are less than a dollar if you look in the right places.
The sound quality, volume and frequency response is quite impressive for such tiny speakers.
These speakers can also be daisy chained together using the cable provided (if it works right). There is no drop or gain in volume across all the speakers.
I will be probably be ordering 9 more of these for future gifts. Unfortunately I will have to open every single one to make sure it works as I do not trust the manufacturer's quality control. However, if the next batch have better statistics, I will update this review.

If you found this review helpful please make note of it.

title: Wasn't the best option for Korea
text:
I bought these to use while traveling in South Korea, and they worked, but the one problem I had was that while this plug adapter definitely fits into the outlet, it wasn't a secure fit and was easy to knock it loose. Very frustrating to wake up in the morning to find out that your phone wasn't charging all night because the plug had partially come out.

The issue I found is that contrary to what is listed on the seller's description, the majority of the outlets in Korea were the F-type plug (picture attached to this review) which has a bit of a recess before the plugs go in, which is designed to keep the plug from coming loose. Unfortunately, this C-type adapter doesn't fit flush into the plug, and with just the tips of the plug in the outlet, it's prone to come loose.

If you're planning on using these in Korea, I would highly recommend the F-type adapter.

So, it got returned. I was a little apprehensive to spend $80 on a new router, but this time around everything was great. I opted for this AC1200 router instead of a top of the line N900 or N600 router. I couldn't be happier with my choice. My N devices connect at faster speeds and I can now get 15-20 mb/s way in the back of my apartment where I couldn't even get a connection before. The iPad, which uses AC wireless is amazing. It can max out my 60 mbit internet connection.  I have not had to reboot it a single time. I love this router, and as someone who works in IT, I would recommend it to all my friends and family. If you don't need USB 3.0 for the purpose of backing up to a hard drive, and you aren't copying large files between multiple PCs, I don't think you can beat this router.

title: Music Production/ Mixing without needing an amp.
text:
Good is a relative term. I've auditioned quite a few headphones. I own a few different cans: Audio Technica M50 (original), Sennheiser HD280 & HD600.. and the Sony 7520. I'll keep this short. They're the truest cans i've heard that don't require an amp. I produce and mix music (and learning to master). In the industry, we don't need extra bass or anything colorful. The process demands a neutral and honest presentation. Other than the HD600's (paired with an O2 amp), these are my goto speakers when an amp isn't convenient. Most really great reference headphones require an additional amp (other than a phone or notebook) to drive them. However, as far as closed back, low impedance cans go, these are the ones you want.

Without going into full depth about soundstage, articulation, warmth, fatigue or frequency response.. If you're in music, don't want open back cans that need an amp, GET THESE, especially if you're traveling with a MBP. The bass is little soft and mids are slightly recessed (vs. HD600). Of course we mix and test through many mediums: headphones, monitors, computers, car stereo etc. These won't let you down. When I'm on the go and need to hear a project, I bring the Sonys. When I'm gonna be in a noisy environment, and just consuming media.. i bring the Bose QC35 with me.

I've spent years reading reviews and auditioning audio equipment from home stereo, to studio, to car stereo. I'm not rich, but I'm extremely anal about A/V tech equipment. I need the best (without having to rob a bank).

Don't second guess. BUY THEM. I got mine on Craigslist for a super steal, but I'd definitely pay Amazon retail for these, if i had to.

I tried to find out more about the company and this bag but they seem to be a start up in Turkey with an unfinished website. I can't find any reviews elsewhere or ones that specifically talk about durability after a few months use. The design of the bag is great, but we all know what really matters is that it lasts more than 3 months with normal use. Check back here in Nov for an update.

title: This Samsung monitor is fantastic but not without it’s faults.
text:
For reference, I tested both monitors with a few different computers and tablets:

Microsoft Surface Pro 4
Samsung Spin 9
Macbook 12
Alienware X51

I am also going to compare it to the Dell U3415W which I have been using for the past several months.This has the most "curved” of all monitors I’ve seen. It claims “1500R”

The packaging, as usual, was top notch. Everything was easy to find and safely stowed. It came with the following:
• Monitor
• Power supply
• Manuals
• CD/DVD
• HDMI cable
• Display port cable
• Display port adapter (works with some Macs and PC’s that don’t have a full size port)

Pros:
• Amazing screen for video and photographs
• Comes with all the adapters and cables you need (enough for me to make quick changes between computers)
• AMD Freesync is amazing. (I have a monitor with NVidia Gsync and I literally could not tell the difference)
• Quantum Dot Display- slightly better blacks but I have this on my TV and it doesn’t do miracles
• Personal Preference but I love the gloss white back panel
• Panel movement was nice and easy. Moving it up and down and tilting was smooth. So many require pressure and then jerk so it’s hard to adjust- not this one.

Cons:
• I hate the round base. It sticks out 4 inches forward from the bottom of the screen. Due to its shape, you wouldn’t want to put anything on top of it.
• Worse angles than my Dell U3415W. The Samsung is a VA (Vertical Aligned) monitor vs the Dell, which is an IPS (In-Plane Switching) thus held the image noticeably better than an angle which may or may not be important to you. VA monitors typically provide better 'blacks' and better images in darker environments.
• Not so much a con but I have to say that, for the price, the image quality was not noticeably better than my Dell. I watched some QHD movie trailers on YouTube side by side with the U3415W and did not see any better colors or differentials other than speed which is where the Samsung excelled.

One thing- I was never able to bring it to its recommended resolution after multiple tries- close but no cigar.

All in all, a solid achievement from Samsung. A graphic artist or heavy gamer might have other opinions but for the average user, it’s definitely a good choice.

title: The largest and fastest drive you can get for an XBOX360.
text:
I bought this drive to use with my XBOX 360. Using HDDHACKR 1.40 I successfully modified the drive and was also able to recover the original XBOX emulator from my old drive. Once I set everything up, which took about 15 minutes total. The drive was instantly recognized by the Xbox, which gave me 460 GB after formatting. After that i transferred 200 GB of data to it from my old 250 GB drive with an XBOX transfer cable. The drive does get warm inside the Xbox. However this can be remedied with an inter-cooler to lower the ambient temperature, or you can just do what I did and leave the drive door off of the Xbox and lay it flat so the heat can rise and escape.

To any of the people out there that say there is no real difference in getting a 7200 rpm drive, you are crazy. The loading times for all games and apps decreased dramatically. It used to take about 30-45 seconds to go from loading screen to action in Halo 4 now the loading screen cant even finish before i'm in the game. GTA 5 used to take over 2 minutes to get into single player from the Rockstar logo. Now it takes about 1:00-1:15 to get into single player. Destiny load times were cut in half. On average i would say it has cut loading times by ten to fifty percent it just depends on the game. So if you want 500 GB of the fastest loading storage for your XBOX 360, then I recommend this drive 100%.

title: Amazing video camera, no alias and moire with filter
text:
I have owned the 5D Mark ii, 5D Mark iii, and now the 6D. Honestly, the 5D Mark iii doesn't have enough advantages to pay that much more money for it. All you get is slightly better weather sealing and more auto focus points. But the 6D has more auto focus points than the 5D Mark ii. The ISO performance is better than the 5D Mark iii even. The center focus point is faster and more accurate in low light than the 5D Mark iii. You can focus and recompose, you really don't need all those focus points. When you're not in low light, the focus points on the sides still work great if you don't want to move your camera too much while recomposing.

Now with video, it was unusable when I purchased it. The alias and moire is extreme. However, I bought a VAF-6D filter that goes over the sensor of the camera. With the filter it won't alias or moire no matter how hard you try and it also filters out high hard frequencies. The 3rd party filter seems to be better than the filter built into the 5D Mark iii. When I compare the footage from both cameras, as I have owned both, with the filter in the 6D, it seems to be sharper and the 5D Mark iii is softer. I do notice the slight difference in ISO performance, 6D seems to be better.

The 6D is very light and I mostly use it with the 24-70 2.8 ii, which is lighter than the original 24-70 2.8 that I had with my Canon 5D Mark iii. This fits in my hands perfectly. I wouldn't add a battery grip to it, I did that for a while and the ergonomics are just so much better without the grip and it's so much lighter. Also, with third party grips things can go bad. For example, ONE battery, rather OEM or off brand last a very long time in the 6D for photography and video. 30 minutes of video takes a battery down to about 80%. With my battery grip, with two batteries, it took one down to 76% and the other to 96% with 30 minutes of video in the same test environment. The reason I did the test is because I noticed how quickly the battery drained even with OEM batteries. Turns out it was the grip. It was either draining my batteries faster or the contacts of the grip were communicating to my camera that the batteries had less life in them than they actually did.

If you're not gonna shoot RAW video and want to shoot continuous I would choose the 6D with the VAF-6D filter over the 5D Mark iii. Also, glass makes the biggest difference. More so in photos than in video. I'd skip the kit that has the 24-105 f/4. Even though it's an L series lens, for photography it's VERY soft, tons of CA. Go with the Sigma 24-105 F/4 or Canon 24-70 f/4. But if you can afford it, the 24-70 2.8 ii is the most amazing lens I've used and I keep it on the camera 99% of the time.

My music is on a 128gb thumb drive. I like a lot of different music, so I put music in genre specific folders (i.e 80's New Wave, Punk, etc), and want to random play within those, rather that the whole collection, but that feature is lost if you allow it to create a data base, so you have to see it ask every single time you you turn it on, and just ignore it, even though you don't want to do it.

Over all, it's pretty nice, yet irritating at the same time. I assume all similar Pioneer units have the same stupid tendencies.

title: I have owned an Aria for a couple of years ...
text: I have owned an Aria for a couple of years now, upon purchasing it I was excited that it would sync with my Fitbit app which would allow all of my fitness information to be in one spot.  The scale worked well, for the most part, however, the flaws I saw were the inconsistency in an accurate weight (sometimes a pound weight difference within multiple simultaneous weighings) and it was never consistent with how to weigh (step on, weight would show OR step on, step off, thinking, weight). A couple of months ago I did the update to my Aria.  I continuously got the V39 error message, step off, step on, thinking and then nothing. I tried replacing the batteries, made sure that the connections were cleaned (as I had seen on the FitBit support feed), checking for updates, etc.  I also tried many of the tips that moderators suggested in response to numerous others having the same issue.  The scale would turn on with nobody on it and killed another set of batteries within a few days.  Now it will not turn on at all (despite fresh batteries) and when I called FitBit to ask for assistance they said that there is nothing they can do and tried to offer me the exact same pricing as Amazon on a new one.  I am very surprised at the lack of acknowledgment that an update is causing so many issues and many scales to be turned into oversized bricks.  I am going to go back to the inexpensive versions of scales that are out on the market - I just do not think the price point is worth it with a total lack of customer service and a quality product that will last.

title: Sophisticated Receiver
text:
I bought this factory refurbished from a seller that sells through Amazon. Since they are across town I just drove over and bought it direct from them.

I previously had a Denon X2000 which was fine until it started resetting itself twice a day. It appears one of the amp channels was going, as the wiring was fine. Given that it was just over 2 years old I was frustrated but rather than go down the endless repair route (there is not a repair center within 150 miles of where I live) I decided to get a new one. But for this, I might well have bought a X2200W.

I looked around at reviews and thought I would try a Yamaha. My setup is currently 5.1 with front heights, I will probably convert this to 5.1.2 to support Atmos fully.

I looked at the 850 and 1050, as they both support 7,2 channels. They are, in reality, fairly similar.

Only 3 of the 850's HDMI ports support 4K/ HDCP2.2 but it seems unlikely in the near to mid future that many people will have even that number of 4K inputs. The 1050 would appear to have a better power supply - it weighs 8lb more and it does have better DACs. In addition the 850 will not have DTS:X, if that matters.

One point to note is that the 1050 is deeper than the 850 and people with a fixed length shelf (or a closed back) should check out if it fits.

Setting it up is fairly easy. Plug everything in the back and run YPAO (Yamaha equivalent to Audessy). That worked well but it misplaced the sub woofer - which I corrected manually .

These receivers certainly have plenty of sound options! By the time you multiply the number of channels by the number of options it can be a little overwhelming. Yamaha tries to control this by the existence of 'Scenes'. These group an input with a set of options, the 850 has 4 and the 1050 has 12. You could use these to have say 3 different Xbox modes, Music, Game and Film with different DSP and active speaker options.

I use this with a Logitech 650 controller. You could activate a scene as one of the commands it issues on changing function.

Generally the sound is very good and there is more than enough power to drive the speakers I have (ELACs) to levels that the family will tolerate.

Hopefully it will last longer than the Denon.

title: The best you can get at $800
text:
I am a college student majoring in Software Engineering, who enjoys gaming and creating digital artwork.
I've owned the Dell inspiron 7559 for about a week now.
I have an i5 processor, 256GB SSD, 4GB of Ram, and the NVIDIA gtx960m with 4GB of vRam. I paid $800 +tax on Amazon.

PROS
The laptop has run well with only a couple of stutters. Opening programs is fast and snappy. The screen is nice a bright, although I don't use it outside so I can't judge there. The 15.6 inches is a plus for me since I often have a text editor and another web page open while programming. The sound is okay. It's not the best, but it gets the job done. I've only played Portal 2, Fallout 4 and Life is Strange on this device. All run well, but the 7559 can definitely play more graphic intensive games. Just look it up on YouTube.

CONS
This laptop is heavy. As a college student I've got to move around a lot so carrying this isn't fun. However, this was never advertise as ultra-portable. Just keep in mind that if you want to use this in college you'll most likely be carrying other things and this by itself is about 5lb. Secondly, the light from the charger is INCREDIBLY bright, especially in my small dorm room when the lights are off. The track pad isn't the most responsive when using multi-finger gesture, but I use a mouse often so it doesn't bother me too much.

Conclusion
If your on a budget and want to game on a portable machine, get it. It works great, looks good, and it's budget friendly. My only suggestion would be to buy another source of storage. title: fantastic video resolution, easy to use, useless driver assist features
text:
I've been using a BlackVue (older model from about 4 years ago) and it had been flawless so far. But for our second car I decided to go with this Papago mainly because I really liked the ultra high resolution of this model. It's a 21:9 ratio sensor and gives you a really wide sharp picture with its 2K resolution and a 145 degree lens. Even though it has no GPS function like my old BlackVue, I don't think I will miss it.

I tried out the Driver Safety features and they were annoying, especially the Stop and Go feature which tells you to proceed forward you wait too long after the light turns green and the driver ahead pulls forward. As for headlight warning and driver fatigue reminders, I can do that fine thank you. My car already has tons of nannies so I didn't need even more beeping going on.

Anyway, the main reason you buy this is its resolution, video is crisp and at least as good as my old BlackVue in low light. I use a 32GB card and it gives me at least 4 hours of footage which is good to record a week of driving (before it starts to auto delete the older files)

The only mount this comes with is a suction cup mount. I really wish it came with an adhesive mount that allowed me to stick the device higher onto the top of my windshield where there is a dot matrix pattern on the glass (the suction cup won't stick to that). So the device is a bit lower than I'd like. I never liked suction cups because they eventually degrade and fall off. I added an extra tether to the device with a NiteIze gear tie just in case the cup lets go. You can detach the device from the cup mount by sliding it sideways but I wonder how many times I can do that before I break the whole mount (putting force on it)

The power cable was more than long enough to run the cord around the edge of my windshield and down below my glove box in my sedan, so I don't think most people will run into problems.

The menus are pretty simple once you play with them for a few minutes. I do like the fact that it can auto record for a fixed time after the power is disconnected due to its internal battery.

Startup time is fast, although there is a mandatory annoying chime when the device is turned on

All in all I like the unit. It does need a different mount option and a way to disable the power on/off chime.

title: Remote Does Not Work, Rendering Product Useless to Me
text:
My 1-star rating may not apply to most of you who use "Scroll-Lock" keyboards, or who have no need of remote switching between computers. Since I am crippled and bed-ridden, I definitely do need remote switching, otherwise the KVM switch is useless to me. Add to that fact I don't use moribund keyboards with "Scroll-Lock," the "hot-key" way of switching computers. Such a keyboard is depressing, an anathema to progress, harking back to the dismal days of DOS and obsolete-ville. I have not seen a keyboard with "Scroll-Lock" for decades. Then add to that, that I took every precaution before buying this KVM switch that the remote control would work, so maybe you can understand why I give it the solo "Hate it" star of shame, standing up all by itself like a single medial digit from the knuckle of my hand.

You try not to be "helpless" when you can't move around and walk, but the thing that really makes you feel useless, is when you need a little ramp for your wheelchair, and you are presented with an impassable stair-step, or you search far and wide for a remote control KVM switch that will solve your non-ambulatory problem, and it's all a big hoax.

Please, someone prove me wrong in my suspicion that none of the remotes for any of these KVM switches works. I tried using two different brand-new CR2032 batteries, and there was no power to the remote with either one. It was dead as a doornail. It was no more than a dummy prop, like a phaser handgun on Star Trek.

Even if the remote control had gotten power, what on earth would it have done? It has 21 buttons on it with all sorts of important-looking icons on each -- to perform one push-button function: switch computer. This task comprises only one button on the KVM switch itself.

No literature about the remote comes with the product. If it worked, would not the vendor tell us which one of those 21 keys to press in order to switch computers, and what to do with the other 20? Can you type, "S-U-C-K-E-R?"

title: Great Laptop if you Remove the Bloat
text:
Background: I needed a new laptop after my Lenovo Thinkpad kind of fell apart, after around 4 years though so that is understandable.
There are many good things about this laptop. There are few bad.
Negatives:
-The one thing you will notice is the bloat when you first receive it. Reading the reviews, I thought it was all exaggeration but it isn't, it is full of bloat. It took me around 3 hours to get rid of it all and install everything I wanted. Once it is all gone, it runs smooth and fast. The first thing you should install is Malwarebytes though. After running Malwarebytes, it found 94 threats. Run that immediately and get rid of superfish.
-The keys stick as well. It is not a big deal while typing, but if you play some games, which I will talk about, it can get irritating. You really have to press hard while typing for it to be accurate. Not the best for people who are comfortable with a more sensitive laptop.
-The function keys are on the same keys as the volume, refresh, brightness, etc., keys but I think that is how most laptops do it now. I just wish differently.
With all of these, I took off one star as one can be fixed, and two just take getting comfortable with.

Positives:
-The price for what you are getting. The bloat really lowers the price on this, which is actually good for someone like me, a part time worker/college student who knows how to remove bloat easily. A8 is great and for this price, you can't beat it.
-Casual gaming is great with this laptop. Triple A games will not run on this laptop. On the other hand; Terraria, Team Fortress 2, Minecraft, and a plethora of great indie games run perfectly. No lag at all, nearly a consistent 60 fps, with settings on high in TF2 which is not what I was expecting. It runs games like LoL pretty well and Smite all right. Some lag, unresponsiveness, and a few crashes every once in awhile but not unplayable. As I said before, the keys stick a bit. For example, in TF2, sometimes when I try rocket jumping, I don't jump. You really have to have your hand centered on the space bar and give it a firm push.

The webcam, speakers, track pad, and screen are all decent for this price as well. No negatives or positives for these.

Overall, it is a great laptop for the price. If you are comfortable with removing bloatware and are looking for a nice laptop at a great price, this is it. If you are not comfortable removing bloatware, I would find someone who is to do it for you or find another laptop. It could make your laptop severely slow if not taken care of.

With the 4” clamp, the [[ASIN:B00JI6NCCK Height-Adjustable Standing Desk - VARIDESK Pro Plus 36 - Black]] could not go down all of the way, but I was ok with that. This weekend I drilled a hole in the top portion of the desk and attached the mount using the 4” grommet. Now the stand up desk is fully adjustable.

When I ordered the mount, I didn’t realize that the 4” grommet would work for passing it through a desk with a hole in it. I think that is helpful feature for those of you that have a desk where you cannot clamp and don’t want to drill a hole.

The monitor mount is more stable than setting a monitor on top of a stand. One of my old monitors did not have the VESA mount, so I left it on the stand. The old monitor would wobble and the new monitor would barely move.

I really like that it is fully adjustable! I have two 24” monitors on it. I have offset the monitor mount to fit my desk configuration. It has allowed me to have the left monitor arm fully extended and then the right one it adjusted to be next to it. The included wrenches allow me to adjust the tension of the arms.

I will try to add pictures with the new monitors on it. [Update - Added final photos]

title: but awesome! So when I bought a new iPod touch
text:
I had an Otterbox on my iPhone 3 for 5 years. It was a little bulky, but awesome!
So when I bought a new iPod touch, I knew I wanted an Otterbox again.
This Otterbox is similar in that it's two plastic pieces that latch together, with a silicone piece that goes over top.

It's a bad thing because I take my case on/off frequently (to put inside an armband), and the plastic feels easy to break. My last Otterbox was practically impossible to break. The silicone is nice and soft, yet has some texture to it so it's easy to grip.

It was not as responsive as I like - had to push down to hard. The good thing is the screen protector is SUPER easy to take off. Another thing I had read in the reviews is that the case is hard to get off. That's not true, if you know what you're doing. I can open this in seconds. Pop the top latch, then pop the sides. I've been opening Otterbox cases for years, but even for first timers, it should not take "7 to 8 minutes"

title: Simple, but just what I wanted.
text:
I've been using this watch for a little over a week now, and I love it. For me, it's a perfect fit. I wanted something that I could receive notifications discretely with, but I've always hated the idea of a standard smartwatch. I don't want to charge my watch every night. I don't want a paperweight on my wrist when I don't charge my watch. I don't need a fitness tracker and a bunch of other useless bloat. And also, I hate the way most smartwatches look. LCD screens strapped to my wrist don't appeal to me. But this watch defies all of the things that I hated about other wearables. The battery life is fairly good lasting about 4 days with my current usage. The watch is stylish and accepts a normal 22mm strap (I'm currently using a nato). It's a little bulky, but no more than G-Shock is. The styling is classic, and when the smart parts of the watch finally die, you still have a normal watch until you get time to charge it back up.

As for the functions of the watch, it serves its one purpose well. Notifications are prompt, repeat themselves once, and can easily be ignored if you tap on the watch. Every app I've tried works well, and it gets information across its tiny screen well. The app used to control the watch seems fairly good and has a decent UI. A little more functionality would be nice though, but I only have minor complaints. Music controls and the ability to answer calls from the watch wouldn't be a bad addition.

The only complaints I have with this product are the missing functionalities I mentioned and not being waterproof. I've had no issues while wearing this in the rain or snow, and I wash my hands constantly at work without any issues, but I'm still cautious about any kind of submersion with the device. Overall, I'm satisfied and don't see any reason to buy anything more. If you just want a simple, stylish watch that recieves notifications, this is the one to buy.

title: Almost like an Otterbox Defender, but on the HTC 10 the curved back is very slippery.......could slide off a surface easily.
text:
Given that Otterbox reportedly is not going to make a case for the HTC 10, this is the next best thing. I like it so far, except for one issue, which is important to me.

The HTC 10 has a convex curved back, so this case back curves outward in the center to fit it. The rubber around the edges makes it pretty easy to grip with dry fingers and hands such as mine. But the hard plastic in the center, being curved outward, is the only contact on whatever surface you place your phone using this case, if you lay it on its back. So unlike the full rubber outer enclosure Otterbox uses, this will very easily slide across any hard or slippery surfaces such as desks, tables, countertops, etc. There is much more danger of accidentally sliding over the edge and falling to the floor than with the fully rubberized outer case. I would like to see Supcase make a version where the entire outer side of this case is rubberized.

title: The Glow gives good sound
text:
It's been a month with this amazing little amp. I've since replaced the stock opamp with a MUSES02 and the stock tubes with many different ones, and have settled on the Voskhod 6ZH1P-EV. All I can say is WOW! The amp with the stock opamp and tubes sounded great. But with the upgrades, it's out of this world. Seriously.

Below are my earlier reviews that I've made since the purchase.

First night impressions:
Pros
-It's got that glow! Don't underestimate the glow. Probably biasing my impressions, but here goes anyway.
-Clear and clean. Crisp highs and mid range is very smooth. Alison Krauss & Union Station Live sounds as good as I've heard. No hiss or distracting noises. Just crisp and clean sound. Voice sounds great.
-3D imaging? Amber Rubarth "Hold On"; voice is front and center, first time hearing height in this track. Some instruments sound like they're floating above others. Not distracting at all, just a very neat effect.
-Bass is present with stock tubes. KDrew "Bullseye" is a killer track if you like dub. Bass sounds thick, if a bit smeared sounding. I was afraid the stock tubes would be thin sounding, it isn't. But it leads to a con...
Cons
-Bass is a little smudgy or loose sounding. It's the first night with these stock tubes and I understand it takes 20 or so hours before tubes get comfy in their new homes and sing.
-Piano sound isn't quite right. Smudgy bass makes the lower registers sound blurred.
-BRIGHT LED. It's blue and it's bright. Should be a soothing green or white. Such a contrast to the glow. I should put tape over it.

Two weeks later:
Pros
-Trying new tubes is fun! They glow and improve / alter the sound.
-Bass is MUCH improved. Rolling tubes, I'm a believer.
-Smooth smooth smooth!
-Overall an EXCELLENT amp.
Cons
-BRIGHT LED. Still haven't put tape over it.

text:
My story is similar to the review from January 30, 2016. I plugged in my NEW unit and the display said 82% battery. ok fine it'll charge that sucker up. Keep in mind I *never* had anything plugged into the UPS as of yet. It will take me some time to get all my computers sorted out and move things around so this was simply getting it up and making sure it worked. Each day I looked at the display it said a lower % of battery charge. hmmm ok. I thought that was weird but figured nothing was plugged into it so maybe it's in some sort of discharge cycle. Yesterday morning I was awakened at 3am by several beeps and a long beep and then the beep stopped. I didn't figure out till later that it was this PR1500LCD unit that did it. I have the network expansion card plugged into it and looked at what it said. It kept saying that the battery was not installed (????) and that the battery was old. It said battery was at 0%. I figured out what was going on is it doesn't seem to know it is plugged in and the entire time it was working off battery. With it at 0% battery I'd turn it on and a couple of minutes later it turns itself off. Soooooo there is some sort of internal problem with it. It's too late for me to return it (or else I would) so I had to call up tech support. I'm having to wait 24-48 hours for a UPS prepaid label to be emailed to me and then have to send it out and the guy said they'd send me a brand new unit since mine is so new. I figure that's the LEAST they can do. This thing about broke my back trying to get it off the floor and drag it through my house and get it into the box. yeah I'm a bit pissed. Who knows when I'll get the new one.

I'll update when it's all settled.

title: The Reason It's Not a Five-Star GoPro Pole
text:
The GoScope BOOST is a solid design. The telescoping/locking mechanism is stellar; there are no screws and it feels super sturdy! The pole itself is lightweight but feels strong like bull! The aluminum-magnesium alloy feels really dependable! The grip feels like the handlebars to a bike; it's a tough rubber that gives you a great grip. If your grip fails you, there's a quality wrist strap that's included. This is a great overall product, but it's not perfect in my eyes and let me tell you why. It's great for selfie shots, but if I want to aim the GoPro in a forward direction I would have to remount the GoPro; the mount is limited to about 130 degrees with the waterproof housing. I would have liked the mount to allow for more than 180-degree-rotation like my other pole, the GoPole. I will upload pictures to show you what I'm talking about. So for this reason, I did not give the GoScope BOOST 5 stars. It was almost a deal breaker for me. Fortunately I semi-solved my problem by adding a three-way pivot arm (included with GoPro camera) so that I am able to swivel the GoPro around for forward shots on the fly. I say "semi-solved" because it doesn't give a complete 270-degree pivot but it allows about 225 degrees which is a lot better than the insignificant 130 degrees. I also like that the there are dual mounts for the GoPro; not because I would like to mount 2 GoPros at the same time, but because it stabilizes the GoPro when I set it down. Who carries around multiple GoPros anyway!? So other than that one gripe, the GoScope is a quality product.

I have owned a GoPro for about 1 year. I typically use it for traveling. I have been using the GoPole for a little under a year and just recently picked up the GoScope BOOST. I just used the GoScope on a recent trip to the San Diego Safari Zoo and this was when I realized the difficulties in shooting selfies and then quickly wanting to shoot forward. I have not taken the GoScope under water so I don't know how it will do in the ocean, but the GoPole would allow water to seep in the pole. Well I hope this review helps.

Upon receiving the item I set everything up, and the headset wouldn't pair with the base. After a number of attempts, different USB ports, powercycling, and the like it finally paired...then the microphone wouldn't work.

Wearing the headphones for an extended period of time has caused a bit of discomfort as well, it's a bit tight on the ears. This may change over time, and the headset seems to be the best option for a business headset for my home office, so I'm getting an exchange to see if a replacement will function properly.

UPDATE: Amazon shipped me a replacement and it's functioning, I still have not heard back from Logitech support and it's been 10 days since their last response at this point.

As some others have mentioned, the audio quality is not very good. I'm primarily using the headset for Skype calls during work, so I don't need audiophile quality sound, but voices aren't as clear as they were even on the H800 I had, definitely not as good as the G330, and the microphone recording quality is average at best.

That being said, the Skype integration doesn't always work properly with the base station flashing like there's an incoming call all the time, at times, and muting the call using a keybind/mute icon on the window doesn't activate the mute indicator on the headset on every occasion, as it should.

I'll save up and grab one of the Sennheisers next time, I think, it's just not the premium quality product you'd expect. Outside of range, which is great.

title: My 2nd Seiki TV and this TV is definitely not 1080 resolution
text:
This is my second Seiki TV. I bought the white bezeled 24 inch model 3 years ago and it has been a fine little TV but I needed a bigger size for my bedroom. That 24 inch model was definitely 1080 as I doubled the use of that TV as a computer monitor.

[[ASIN:B00IB179FE Seiki SE24FE01-W 24-Inch 1080p 60Hz LED TV (2014 Model)]]

This one, the SE32HY is absolutely not 1080. It states on the box that it is 720p (1368 by 768) and I connected it to my computer with a high end Nvidia graphics card and ran all sorts of tests and it shows up as 720p. My Nvidia card can force this TV into higher resolution but it looks poor as its image is interpolated up through the graphics card software.

Those who hook up a Roku or Fire stick even if it says 1080 that is the native resolution of that streaming device. If you put any 1080 source into the TV the Seiki automatically converts it to 720p as that is the total number of pixels of the resolution of the LED panel which is fixed at manufacture time.

That being said this is a very nice TV even at 720p and I just watched the Super Bowl on it and it was a great picture. I use antenna only and get great reception on this TV's ATSC tuner. However, it is not QAM certified.

My last Seiki was a white TV and I wanted another white one but Seiki seems to have discontinued that color. This TV has a black bezel. Seiki, please bring back white!

Putting the feet on the bottom of this TV is a grueling experience but a magnetic tipped Phillips screwdriver is a big help and this only has to be done once.

But the best reason for me to buy another Seiki is that this is one of the few TV manufacturers these days that has a headphone jack out. This allows me to connect an inexpensive set of computer speakers and get very good sound out of the TV. The remote can raise or lower the output to the speakers and mute when necessary. Yes, this TV also has optical audio out jack but those speakers are expensive so the headphone jack works great for me.

I hope this TV lasts as long as my last Seiki which was flawless in the time I used it and still works great. It's now in my kitchen.

For the price and quality I can recommend this TV to others.

title: Excellent quality and functionality
text:
I purchased this at a discount so I could provide this unbiased review.
INITIAL REVIEW: March 12, 2016:
I'm reviewing this after installing it today, I will update my review after a few weeks of usage as well.
[U1]: UPDATE1: March 16, 2016
[U2]: UPDATE2: March 21, 2016 - updated to 5 stars as all the quirks I've mentioned before, seem to work out perfectly.
NOTE (not good not bad): SD Card is not supplied, and is required for actual capture of video / images.

The Good:
Good quality packaging.
Good build quality.
All supplied items are of good quality.
Self installation is easy enough, if you understand how to pass wiring across your car (if you are unsure check a few YouTube videos, and you'll be an expert).
Rear view camera switches into focus when in reverse. This is accomplished by hooking up the supplied cable to the reverse-rear-taillight.
Installation should take about 15-20 minutes, and for most cars would not require special tools.
Supplied cables are of adequate length.
System is battery powered, which is charged by a mini-USB connector. This is good, because in case of a malfunction in the electrical system (maybe due to an accident), the camera can continue to function and record.
Has a microphone. Good for recording when giving a statement to a police officer.
[U1] Found out today that display does have an option to auto switch off, minimum time is 30s.

The less than Good:
No installation instructions, you need to rely on your own knowledge and technical skills, or ask an auto-audio tech to do it for you.
System comes preset to Chinese, took me a few trial-and-error clicks and shutdown/restart cycles until I switched to English.
Power supply utilizes a 'lighter' power outlet, while it is a mini-USB connector. I would have preferred it would be a plain USB cable, and the power supply be a USB charger (maybe even with an additional slot).

Not decided yet if good or not:
Mirror has a blue tint, and is darker than regular rear view mirror. While different, might be a positive point, as it will reduce glare from cars in the rear-view.

Overall impressive product, the location of the screen is on the right side of the mirror, which makes sense to me, as it keeps most of the rear view visible, even when the screen is on.

I was lucky to get the chance to review this, as I was looking for a camera solution, and this provides me a great baseline, as I've never installed one of these before.

The quality of the image/video is quite good, the wide 120° angle camera captures almost everything visible from the front of the car.

I will update the review after I get more experience with the product.

title: A Few Issues
text:
Purchased this desk to use while in bed, or on the sofa in front of the TV. I was excited to receive the tray, but disappointed once I started putting it together. The table is sturdy when set up, and easy to set up and fold down. Overall, it’s a nice looking desk. However, the one I received has a few issues:

1) The drawer frame that the drawer slides in is too wide, so the drawer falls off the desk. If I mess with it to get it exactly centered between the slides, it will stay. But as soon as the drawer is bumped, or I try to open it, it simply falls off the desk.
2) The wood is a bit rough on several of the edges. It’s nothing that a couple passes with a fine grit sandpaper won’t fix, but I would be concerned about snagging clothing before its sanded.
3) The piece of wood that stops a laptop from sliding off the tray when tilted is split down the entire length.

Also worth mentioning is that the fabric glued on the flat surface on the side of the tilting portion of the desk is a faux leather. It looks nice, and will help keep things like glasses or phones from sliding off. But it’s much too sticky to be used as a mouse pad as advertised. Not a big deal as it’s easy to just lay a mouse pad over the top of it.

Overall, I can sand the edges no problem, and even look past the split in the stopper. But given that the drawer is non-functional, I will be returning the desk.

UPDATE: The seller was very responsive to my feedback and sent me a replacement desk right away. The replacement was better quality, and the drawer works properly. Overall we are very happy with the desks. Upgrading my rating to 5 stars.

title: Good for a Sunday drive, or to get you lost.  Took me thru a farmers field today.
text: Review by Stan.  I bought this 2/2/15.  Have been using it about 5 days a week since then- almost 3 months.  This is my second Garmin Nuvi.  The old one just died after several years, so I ordered and received this Nuvi on time, if not early.  Very pleased with the shipper.  My old one would choose a very logical rout, following main roads close to the turn offs, then secondary roads.  This one, even though I have set it up several different ways, will follow the main highway for a while, and then take me off some back road and at times almost a complete circle around the address I want to get to, as if it’s purposely taking me on a long ride.  Even choosing fastest time on the options is no help.  I can skip a couple turns it tells me to take, and save many minutes on its estimated time.  At one point it took me pretty directly to work, then in the last blocks went almost 270 degrees (3/4 of a circle) around the office before finally zeroing in.  Another time from work to home it took me a mile out of the way, to go one block.  Seems Garmin has been paid off by the gas companies to increase the rout mileage so you use more gas, since my last model.  Also, the unit does not have the option for fewer turns, or ecoRout, or a save gas rout option.  The only way I have found to make it go more direct is to punch in some “via” points along the most direct route.  Google takes a much better rout, as does MapQuest, so this is clearly Gamins’ doing. I do hope the airplane G1000 and G500 glass cockpits do not behave this badly.  Poor pilots if they do.  I am very disappointed, even with the newest maps and updates installed; it takes me way out of the way to known locations. I buy these for out of town trips; what’s it going to do when I get to Denver, or Salt Lake City, or Dallas and try to go to an address I have not been to before?  Take me on a meandering drive like I’m out for a Sunday ride?  Come on Garmin, get a software fix for this. Also, it’s not just mine, a friends new one does the same thing, and my wifes now that I updated the maps.  The following link shows this has gone on since 2009.  http://forums.gpsreview.net/discussion/13967/why-does-the-nuvi-keep-trying-to-take-me-on-back-roads/p16  .  I will try a Tom Tom next time, as I am afraid to use this in a city I don’t know.  And that’s precisely why most of us buy these.

title: Very well built, easy setup, works SOMETIMES but only as a non-gaming router.
text:
So far, not so good. I am an IT Consultant and have been for 20 years and I am an avid ASUS fan, but wow, the ROG Rapture GT-AC5300 is aggravating to say the least at this point.

I couldn't possibly count the number of wireless access points, routers, extenders and other devices i've configured over the years, certainly more than 500, probably more than 1000. Some are awesome, others are a little tricky but work fine once you find their sweet spot, others just don't seem to want to show up for work at random moments. My experience so far is that the latter is the case with the GT-AC5300.

Unboxing:
It is a formidable looking and feeling wireless router, big, heavy and it makes me want to run from its spidery legs =] but i kind of liked that. Very solid, feels like it is made well with solid materials and would be able to disperse heat with no problem at all.

Initial Setup:
Pretty painless, attach the antennae, plug it in to our comcast business connection, get power to it, let it boot up and break out my laptop to connect to the standard default wireless networks that magically appear. No problem
Connected to the admin UI, most folks complain about the ugly ROG interface, meh, i don't care much either way, a UI is a UI at this point to me, its all a matter of finding what needs to be done and doing it. So i won't go into all that too much, only to say that i like the initial screen of network stats screen., not necessarily the look (who cares), but the data.. me likey data.. Anyway, i'm in the admin UI, I go thru the initial standard setup that anyone who should be considering this router would be very familiar with (translation: if you are looking at a router like this, you should be very familiar with the ins and outs of how to setup wifi by now, not like its hard) and within 10 minutes or less i'm up and running with my 2g, 5gx2 internal and guest wifi networks. There is a firmware update, so i go ahead and do that as well. All is well, Cool, just as it should be. I leave it at that for the night because i have other things to do and it seems to be working ok. IPS, Game Boost, QOS and GPN (WTFast) are all in their default disabled state.

If i didn't want to use the router for anything more than a standard $125 router could handle i suppose i would be writing a 4 star review.. umm.. but i spent a LOT more than that and for a reason..

Later the next day, i go in and enable Game IPS (the GT-AC5300's implementation of Trend Micros security), Adaptive QOS, Game Boost and WTFast.. woot! game on baby! well.. sorta.. i mean its JUST diablo 3 for crying out loud.. which i've been playing for years off various other wireless routers just fine... but as i'm sure you can tell.. Hell hath no fury as a necromancer routed thru a GT-AC5300! i noticed a little bit of load time issues right away, but thought nothing of it, maybe my computer was just slow today (please.. please God.. let it just be my computer slow today.. ok???) once i get in game and start up a grift, i get about 3 minutes in and i lag out, ping goes from 65ms (already very slow for me) to well over 1000ms.. then 2000ms.. 3000ms.. you know where this is going.. connection dropped..

I am in the middle of "trying everything" on this router, but i'm frustrated as you can imagine. even disabling everything and making the router the equivalent of a $400 version of a $125 router, d3 gets massive lag spikes and disconnects.. this is hardlined into the 5300 or via wireless. if i wifi directly into my old wireless router d3 plays fine.

I am sad to say, that at this point my professional opinion as an IT professional with 20+ year experience specifically with network hardware and infrastructure. This router isn't ready. Either there is a manufacturing issue, where some routers have a problem and i got one of those, or there is a firmware issue or its just plain bad. i'll continue my experiments today and post anything useful i might learn.

**Updated 7/2/17 1pm PST**
I've downloaded the latest firmware, which as mentioned above i already installed via the admin UI, and installed it again directly from file. then did a factory reset to clear all the settings. Resetup with the same exactly settings, enabling Game IPS but leaving QOS, WTFast and Game Boost disabled, and so far so good. i've run about a dozen grifts fine, although my in game latency is averaging about 70ms which is a bit slow for me. it isn't lagging out at least and all webpages are loading so far.

**Updated 7/2/17 4:45pm PST **
Sadly one problem fixed and another pops up.. I run a plex media server at home and while my wireless devices previously streamed at full file size original no problem before with many simultaneous streams. Now i can't even get a single stream to play without constant buffering. Even with a very small originating filesize of barely 1mbps. i've turned Game IPS (trend micro) off, hoping that would help but no. I also went into the advanced troubleshooting page to see if the showed anything of value and noticed that it doesn't reflect the proper wireless network names, it retained the default network names and shows no data whats so ever. /facepalm

**Updated 7/2/17 5pm PST**
ANOTHER manual power cycle of the router and it updated the advanced troubleshooting page to show the right SSID's. it is at least temporarily streaming video as well too. Let's see if it maintains.

**Updated 7/3/17 10:20am PST**
I am noticing that the router will work great for a short time after a restart, which makes it very difficult and much more time consuming to troubleshoot if a change actually has a positive effect or if its just a reboot "honeymoon phase" for the router. Lots of issues last night for my wireless devices, the kids had trouble streaming youtube and pandora and even just getting page loads on snapchat and instagram. Restart the router and it works for 30 minutes or an hour or 3. Same thing going on this morning. Definitely not good.

**Updated 7/20/17 1:30pm PST**
After an extreme amount of testing, tweaking and retesting.. i've found a configuration that at least for my particular router works great. Albeit, with less than fully advertised functionality. First thing i did was download the current firmware(3.0.0.4.382_12184, signature v2.022) directly from asus and manually patch the router (again, this version was already applied to the router, but i did it again, this time manually (choose file), NOT via the automatic "check" button. per a forum recommendation). After trial and error here is my basic configuration that has worked GREAT for the last 2 weeks:
Game IPS - ON (all 3)
Game Boost - OFF (on caused issues)
Game Private Network - OFF (on caused issues)
Wifi Radar - remember to STOP data collection when you are done in here or it will cause issues
VPN - OFF (haven't tried it yet)
Traffic Analyzer - On or Off is fine, i have mine on

title: Picture Quality is just MEH. I expected better.
text:
Picture quality is kind of MEH when using it, but if you need to output to a larger screen from your iPhone or iPad this is pretty much your best/only option.

Apparently, unless I am mistaken, the adapter doesn't carry a native 1080p signal, and the optimal resolution for mirroring from your device is actually 1600x900. When the signal is showing on your 1080p TV/monitor, it is up-converted so it can show artifacts that are common with streaming and uncompressing video data. This has been known since 2013. Apple knew that the quality could be better, but they thought that this was "good enough" to sell. This adapter has firmware stored in RAM so that updates could be given with iOS updates. As far as I can tell in my cursory google search, no formal update has been done for this.

This can explain why the picture quality is so "off" when I am trying to mirror from my iPad Air 2 to my 1080p TV. Or....it just sucks.

It gets really finicky with different apps. Everything can kind of change with a mistaken hit to the home button and does not always change back when you re-enter the app. I use this with the native Apple app on iOS as well as AVPlayerHD from the app store.

Again, it gets the job done if you need it. As a big Apple fan, I just really did not expect this adapter to be so finicky and "ghetto." I would love to say that I use this a lot, but because of its finickiness and MEH quality, I just end up using my Macbook to output to projectors/TVs instead.

Lastly, YES YOU CAN OUTPUT TO YOUR TV FROM YOUR APPLE DEVICE AND STILL CHARGE YOUR APPLE DEVICE AT THE SAME TIME USING THIS ADAPTER. The adapter plugs into your device's lightning port on one end and has a HDMI port and ANOTHER lightning port on the other end, so you can charge.

title: Smoked immediately!
text:
Powered it on after double checking connections were correct and used 3 wire power cord for it. I immediately started hearing distinctive AC hum noise from a stereo that was plugged in nearby, but was not connected directly to this power supply ... strange! I then measured a 9v potential between neutral and ground, which is NOT SAFE. I should have stopped there, but continued getting it ready to try out. I measured output voltage, and adjusted it to 13.8 volts DC then connected a 12 volt short-wave radio to the DC output. The radio came on, but produced static noise that never happens when it's running on a 12v car battery, and within 2 seconds I heard a loud pop that came from this power supply and then smelled that distinct burnt electronics odor. The power supply then dropped to 7 volts on output with the tiny 0.4 amp load from the radio. After removing the radio connection from the power supply, the voltage jumped back up to 13.8 volts.

Obviously this thing is defective and unsafe for any use.

I'm sending it back for refund. Based on other reviews here, I don't think I'll try another low-cost power supply. They all look the same from different vendors, so I'm guessing they're all made in the same factory and just get different branding.
