title: VERY DISAPPOINTING
text:
I have had other similar speakers on bikes before with mixed results. Nothing will ever be as satisfying as a full factory installed sound system however, you pay dearly for that as well.

I have had these on the bike about 2 weeks now and spent one full day riding and another short ride running errands. I didn't install right away because I was trying to decide where/how to locate the amp. I wanted to put inside a waterproof plastic box and mount under the rack on back of sissy bar however I decided not to go that way because I was afraid of overheating. I tested a day with it up front under the steering neck area attached to frame however the supplied silicone cover for ports was gone within the first mile and since it is not rated as waterproof and this cover was now gone I decided for a temporary location inside saddlebag. The bag it is in is basically empty so it had a lot of room and air around the AMP however after an 90 minutes of riding I went to turn it off and it was super hot to touch. I turned it off, went to lunch and an hour later came out turned on and had to pair it to my phone again to be able to stream music :-(

The first ride after install I had to jump start bike but I thought it was because I had things on for extended period of time when installing and tweaking. Later throughout the day no issue bike started right up but each time I had to pair phone to the AMP again. It would show in list but would not connect and I had to delete device and pair again. Then it was fine until I turned the power off again :-(

about 10 days after last ride I went to start bike to run a few errands and it was dead. I didn't have time to jump so I took car. 3 days later I went out to jump and ride to work and it is so dead it wont even take a jump start. Took battery to be tested and it was at 4 volts. Charging overnight tonight to try and test tomorrow and see if battery is toast or not.

The sound was ok from the speakers. I mean I didn't expect super high end just wanted to be able to hear without distortion and when I would keep phone volume no higher then 3/4 I could get AMP up loud enough to hear at 75 MPH and not have distorted sound. That said having to pair the device every time I turn on bike is not going to work for me. I can not speak to lifespan pf speakers I see many had single speakers die but I have only been able to ride one day with them so not enough time to say if they will last.

Between running battery down in just a few days even when off, not being able to stay paired properly after a power down and how hot the unit runs I am overall not happy with these and I am going to look into return/exchange and see if I can have better luck with another brand.

title: Needs Ability to Play Through Internal Speaker When Audio Jack is in Use
text:
I am an Echo owner and bought the dot in order to not only expand Alexa's coverage area, but mainly to take advantage of the audio-out jack feature that is absent on the Echo. I'm not going to fill this review with everything I like about these units; instead, I'm going to zero in on the one (in my opinion) major flaw of the Dot that caused me to knock off a star in an otherwise 5-star product.

The main reason for me wanting the Dot was due to the audio-out jack which would allow me to attach the device to my whole-house audio system and pump the audio output into multiple rooms in the house. The problem lies in the fact that once something is plugged into the audio jack of the Dot, the built-in speaker no longer functions at all.

There are two problems with this situation. One is that if I don't have the audio system turned on in the room with the Dot, I cannot hear any responses from Alexa, since she talks via the audio jack only. (This is especially a problem to me, since I use Alexa to turn on that same audio system.) The other problem is that, if someone is listening to the music that is streaming from the Dot in another room, they will be interrupted with Alexa's responses anytime someone talks to her in the main room. The latter is not that big of a deal, and actually may be useful in some situations; however, the former is a deal-breaker.

What I would like to see is that, when something is plugged into the audio jack, only streamed music is fed to that device, while feedback from Alexa remains to be played via the built-in speaker. Of course, not everyone would want it this way, so this would need to be a user adjustable setting in the Alexa app. Another setting would be to chose whether Alexa feedback plays via just the internal speaker, or to the audio jack also.

I'm not sure how the jack is wired internally -- I fear that the disconnection from the internal speaker might be a hard connections within the jack itself (as opposed to software directing the output to the separate sound devices; internal speaker, or audio jack). If it is not switched via the hardware, then this could easily be just a firmware update, so I'm not giving up hope just yet.

Hopefully Amazon sees this reviews and considers this change in further hardware/software updates of the Dot. I am guessing there are many others out there like me, for whatever reason, that would welcome these options. If you do share my view on this feature, please add a comment and/or like this review -- maybe that will bring enough attention to get this into the hands of Amazon's R&D department.

title: Awesome for Movies - LG has a lot to improve however
text:
This is my first projector and I like it a lot - I don’t love it, but I also do not regret making the purchase and I will not return it. I’d like to note that I’m very critical in my review of electronics. This comes from a lot of knowledge on the subject. I’m also very hard to impress - Keep that in mind as you read my review.

I reviewed and researched my life away before finally pulling the trigger on the PF1500. I reviewed every comparable BenQ, Epson and Optoma for over two months - Reviewing projectorcentral.com reviews and every YouTube video under the sun. I narrowed things down to the BenQ 3050, BenQ 1085st and the PF1500. I eliminated the Epson 2040 completely because I decided 3LCD wasn’t for me - I’ve read way too much about how the darks just aren’t dark…They’re more so washed out. Some factors that drove me to the PF1500 were: The LED bulb, every single type of input in the world, built in HD tuner, bluetooth, size, tripod mountable and the brand name, LG.

Let’s start with the Cons; there are a lot of them that LG needs to fix.

Con #1 - Being this is my first projector, I really didn’t know how Keystone correction worked - Well, it’s horrible. What is does, if you don’t already know, or think you know, is correctly proportion the image WITHIN the projected viewing window. This is beyond annoying because you will still see the outer areas of the projected window. I thought it would work by correcting the size of the image it was throwing; my bad. I keep this feature turned off and I don't think this is something LG can fix. This is where the tripod mount has been a lifesaver. I’m able to correctly position this projector anywhere. Had I purchased the BenQ I wouldn't know where to place it.

Con #2 - LG should be sued for false advertisement and flat out lying! Their app store doesn’t have most of the apps pictured as standard on the LG PF1500 website and even on the PF1500 box. How can you market your product with the most popular apps out there and not include them? Hulu and Amazon, the two I really wanted, are not available at all. Worse, their app store is terrible!!! You have to give them your credit card information to begin, which I did, hoping Hulu and Amazon would then be unlocked, but that was’t the case. You can also forget about HBO GO. Logging into LG’s app website shows you a lot of apps, but they are all unavailable for the PF1500. To remedy, I purchased a Roku HDMI stick, which I love! It popped right on the back and I plugged the power into one of the two USB outlets on the projector. The fact LG pictures key apps and doesn’t offer them was not only misleading, but is also one of the reasons I went with this projector, thinking I would have everything I need built in…But I needed to spend an additional $40 on the Roku.

Con #3 - The fan on Minimum energy savings (brightest) setting is LOUD! What doesn’t make sense to me is that when you change it to Medium the noise is almost eliminated and the brightness only slightly dims and barely affects the image, making you wonder why it’s so loud on Minimum. Even with my Bose bluetooth speaker connected and the volume turned up, you can still hear the stinking fan. After several hours on Minimum the projector is not even hot, so I don’t know why the fan is blasting. Hopefully they can fix with a software update.

Con #4 - If the projector is unplugged for more than a few hours all of your picture settings will go away! It will remember your zip code, Wi-Fi network and other details. But it won’t remember the most important thing…The thing you spent hours tweaking…Your picture settings! Poof! They’re gone! So you’ll want to take pictures of them. Considering this is marketed as a portable projector, one that likely isn’t going to be plugged in for its entire life, that doesn’t make any sense to me. Hopefully they can fix with a software update.

Con #4 - This was purchased brand new and LG’s packaging is not secure! It was not tightly held as I believe they intended. Basically, it was kinda bouncing around in the box. I was a bit ticked off to see that when I opened the box. The box was not opened…It was brand new. This is simply poor packaging.

Con #5 - The picture setting comes defaulted to 16:9 mode. If you don’t think that’s a big deal, allow me to explain. 16:9 mode will trim the image to fully display a picture. So you’ll need to change this setting to Just Scan, which will display the image according to its source. I list this as a con because most people will not know this and it may be very frustrating and hard to figure out as you’re left wondering why your movie doesn’t look right. Just Scan.

Con #6 - Xbox One looks awesome, but gameplay is unplayable! Pretty much, you can’t play video games using this projector. I am not a hardcore gamer, so if you are you’ll be even more upset than I am. Playing Forza, the driving game, I found the need to turn the car what feels like a half-second in advance of turns due to the lag - Crashing a lot! This is horribly slow video processing on LG’s part and definitely something that should’ve been at the top of their list during the product's design phase. LG has unfortunately eliminated an entire population of potential buyers - Gamers. If you are considering this purchase for video games I would recommend that you stay away - You just can’t play video games on this projector.

Con #7 - No lens cap. Yes, no lens cap. Every projector in the world comes with some form of lens projection; however, this projector does not. Having no lens cap makes storing this in a secure location a little more worrisome. The lens is such an important component of the projector. I’m left confused, as are other buyers, with LG’s decision to disregard protection of the most important part of the unit - The lens.

Con #8 - There is a 1 inch black border around the entire screen. It's so noticeable and it's very annoying! It's most annoying when you're watching a movie that's shot in true cinema wide-screen and you otherwise would never notice the true proportion of the screen...But the border will help you remember. LG you have got to fix this one. I've seen a number of reviews that complained about this and I will never understand why the projector went into production like this.

Pros

Pro #1 - The picture is great! Really the whole point, right? I’m projecting the picture onto a light beige wall and I’m blown away at how perfect everything looked out of the box. I made some tweaks, and it looks stunning! I’m also able to watch it with the blinds open, lights on, etc. Obviously, the picture will fade a bit, but not much at all. The brightness is bright and when it’s completely dark you’ll be blown away at the detail and colors. I threw the lego movie on and was blown away with the 1080p detail, colors, sharpness, etc. I have it set to Minimum energy savings, Contrast at 100, Brightness at 50, Sharpness at 25, Color at 70 - Yes, 70 - Makes the colors pop! Dynamic Contrast - High, Dynamic Color - High, Color Gamut - High, Super Resolution - High, Black Tones - High and all noise filters, etc, are set to Auto.

Pro #2 - No rainbow effect. Other DLP projectors use a spinning rainbow wheel. This projector has a green, blue and red LED light source that is used with a Texas Instruments pico-class DLP chip. I do not believe it’s possible for this projector to have the rainbow effect - In fact, I read a review on projectorcentral.com and I believe they stated the same. Fast moving scenes are no problem!

Pro #3 - The bluetooth DOES work with non-LG devices. I’ve read some reviews where others state it only works with LG devices, and I think they’re simply confused in the menu system. There are options in the menu to hook up LG’s bluetooth devices, but there are also separate options to connect any other bluetooth device. I easily hooked up by Bose speaker via bluetooth and it works great! Bluetooth has an inherent delay, so I don’t use the bluetooth option any longer, but instead use a wire connected to the headphone out into the Bose speaker.

Pro #4 - There are no Audio/Video sync delays, as I read elsewhere. However, if you believe there is LG has controls to modify the sync in the menu system.

Pro #5 - Turns on/off just as quickly as your television. I mention this because any other non-LED projector will not. This is due to the type of bulb.

Pro #6 - I put some movies on a 32GB USB stick, connected it and the projector played them without any issue. Awesome!

Pro #7 - Built in HD tuner. You are able to plug in an antenna or a coax cable. I’ll probably watch some sports in the garage with this.

Pro #8 - LED bulbs. This is one of the main reason I decided to go with the PF1500. I didn’t want the hassle of bulb replacement. I also didn’t want to deal with image quality degrading over time with a bulb. All bulb projectors will have a large percentage of their brightness go away in the first 1,000 hour, and that is NOT the case with LED. I’ll replace this projector before I’ll ever have to worry about the LEDs.

Pro #9 - Two internal 3W stereo speakers. Not awesome sound, but good enough. I wasn’t expecting this to sound like my Bose, but it’s nice to have and does the job, especially for news or sports.

Pro #10 - Size. This projector is small and light.

Pro #11 - You can plug anything into this projector - Anything! HDMI, USB, Component, A/V, Coax, it has a ton of wireless input options, etc. This unit is very flexible!

Overall, I’m very happy with the projector and I love watching movies on it - It’s my weekend stress relief. Depending on LG’s next model I’ll probably upgrade, but for now this is one of my favorite new purchases and it’s getting a lot of use…Mostly by my 4 year old :) If I was going to place this in a fixed location for a movie theater I'd likely go with the BenQ 3050 over this, but portability was a big need for me.

title: Not an easy decision, but happy with this choice
text:
In December 2015, I bought a nicer Philips voice recorder to record college lectures and make voice memos. It was used just a few times, and then put up for a while as I entered classes that did not allow recording. More recently, I pulled it out of hibernation and found that the unit was no longer functioning. How was this possible? The unit was safely stored away! Vowing not to buy another Philips, I looked into both Olympus and Sony. In my case, Sony won me over with the smaller size. As a medical coding student, I am already hauling enough books to stock a library. The smaller the better for me.

With a bit of research, I found that Sony has five models on the market, three of which I was considering due to features and high reviews: ICD-PX333, ICD-PX440, and ICD-UX533. Initially, I purchased the ICD-PX333 from my local Best Buy. That model was returned just the next day. It wasn't that anything was wrong with the device, but navigating the menu was difficult and playback sound was insufficient. Furthermore, the instructions consisted of a mere Quick Start Guide that also mentioned a non-existent case/pouch.

Next I looked into the remaining two Sony recorders on my list. Though I wanted very much to appreciate the features of the ICD-UX533, I suspected that I would not care for that device either. Though the higher-end unit does recharge the battery, the actual battery life is much less before the unit requires a charge. Other things I did not care for on the ICD-UX533 included rear speaker placement and glossy finish that would likely be a fingerprint magnet.

So the ICD-PX440 won in the end. It came in the mail yesterday. Its instructions were slightly more sufficient than the previous model, and written in English as well as a variety of foreign languages. Thankfully, I can figure the unit out just enough to begin navigating the menu to use the unit. For others of you who are wondering which unit to buy, the ICD-PX440 playback quality is worlds better than the PX33. I believe that this unit will probably suit my needs the best out of Sony's line-up.

UPDATE: The speech recognition (VOC) does not appear to be functioning on the model that I was sent. It could be a user problem, but I likely have one with an issue. I will try exchanging the unit and update again with the results.

title: Perfect speakers for small living room. Flat, neutral, accurate sound across all frequencies.
text:
I've used Audioengine A5s on my desktop computer for the last 4 years and have absolutely loved them for gaming, media, and music composition and mastering. When it came time to get speakers for my living room setup, I knew I wanted to use Audioengine products again.

I tried the Audioengine passive P4s first, but those are more for desktop computing and the speakers weren't able to fill my living room with clear sound at louder volumes. So I upgraded to the HDP6s and I have been blown away. Like the A5s, they have the same crisp neutral sound that I was looking for, but they are even flatter than the A5s (a good thing in my opinion), probably due to the fact that the A5s built-in amp is not intended to be totally flat. But I paired these HDP6s with a Yamaha AV receiver and the result is phenomenal. You may want to pair them with a subwoofer, but I honestly don't feel the need to. I haven't even needed to adjust the EQ on my receiver.

I would not recommend using these on a desktop setup. They're too big and they're not really meant to be listened to right up close. They work great on either side of a TV in a small to medium sized living room. If you don't have an AV receiver or amplifier, consider buying the HD6s that these are based off of, which come with their own amplification built into one of the speakers.

One suggestion: Let the speakers break in! Like with my A5s, I was originally kind of disappointed when I fired these speakers up for the first time. But after a few hours of listening at loud volume, the speakers had a chance to get broken in a bit and the sound just became phenomenal. I had a big stupid grin on my face the entire first night I spent listening to music. Highly recommend!

title: Flakier than a box of corn flakes.
text:
I have 300Mbps cable Internet service at my home, with Wi-Fi coverage from a current-model router which lets me realize between a high of 230 Mbps and a low of 50 Mbps over Wi-Fi, depending on where in the home I stand, and on how many walls and floors are between my devices and the Wi-Fi router. I bought this Wi-Fi extender to even out that service by boosting the signal in those portions of the home which are ill-served by my router's coverage; I received it today. I'm a retired software engineer. The Linksys extender is plugged into an outlet four feet off the ground, and right in the middle of the green "sweet spot," as reported by the admin interface. I wish that I could report that this product has made my access to the network better, but it hasn't.

This device is completely flaky. I have just thrown away four hours of my life trying to get it to work correctly, including two calls to Linksys tech support. (But not, however, including the time I'm spending to write this review.) I have been through the initial setup procedure FIVE TIMES, three of them going step by step with a Linksys T.S. person on the other end of the phone. Sometimes, after a setup, nothing at all worked, and I had to push a toothpick into the reset hole yet again. Sometimes, the device broadcasts an SSID, but has no connection to the internet. Sometimes when it has gotten an IP address from the router, and therefore allows access to the Internet, I get data rates which are somewhat better than I get by simply using the SSID broadcast by my router, but sometimes I'll see rates of under 10 Mbps, or an entire loss of the network.

The HTTP-based admin interface will serve pages sometimes, but won't even be reachable at others. (That is, sometimes port 80 is reported as open by a port scan of the extender device, but sometimes it's not on the list.) Sometimes I'll click on a link and get a placeholder page, although the page I came from will continue to be served. Sometimes a refresh of the page I'm currently looking at yields a placeholder page. Sometimes the admin interface claims that the extender device hasn't been set up yet, even though I'm using it to connect to the Internet, and that connection is supplying the very page which is telling me that the extender is not accessible. The T.S. support response to every weirdness was to suggest that I do a hard reset on the device and go through the setup procedure again — a sequence which is not, apparently, guaranteed to result in a working device. Using a somewhat lighter hammer, I've power-cycled the device about 10 times in 4 hours to get back enough functionality to continue to debug the thing.

There had been a firmware update since the unit was manufactured. During one of the random times during which the admin interface had decided to work, I downloaded and installed the update, after which the device stopped working. A call to T.S. revealed that the damn thing needs to go through a hard reset and the entire setup procedure again after EVERY firmware update. It would seem to me that a few words of NVRAM and a checksum might have been spared to allow the extender to remember what its purpose in life is.

I think that if I need more bandwidth when my laptop is at a place in the home where I'm getting 50 Mbps, the right technological solution is to pick it up and walk in into the living room, where I'll consistently get between 160 and 200 Mbps. That's technology which works 10 times out of 10, instead of 2 times out of 10.

My advice is to HOLD the speaker by the middle (silver) section to avoid pushing controls you don't want. In my opinion, it is worth twice the $22.00 I paid for it. I don't have time to be part of the R&D team. If that's the case I'd be better off with ADT or Xfinity security monitoring.

At this point these cameras are useless to me as a security/monitoring device. A novelty at best...and that is when they work consistently.

title: Great product!
text:
After having time with this security system I have come away very happy. The NVR and cameras paired quickly and the cameras work as described! My only issue is with the phone app. Though you can view what the alarm triggered, getting to that area takes a little navigation. When you open the app, you should see the images of your camera with a universal play icon on top of it. Below that image, are several icons. One of the icons is a cloud and if you click it, it takes you to a screen which you have to select the hard drive over the cloud. Once this is done, you will see camera 1. If you try to select the other cameras, you will only see the recording from camera 1. The only way I can find to change the cameras is as follows: 1. You have to make the camera 1 recording full screen, 2. Once in full screen, you have to press the menu icon located on the upper right and you will see 1-4 display appear, to the right of the screen, 3. At this time you can now circulate between the different cameras and their recordings. If there is a better way, please let me know, otherwise I would suggest to update the app so it is more user friendly. Possibly allowing you to tap on the camera that notified you of the alarm and directly taking you to that feed.

I previously had the Arlo system and I have to say that the quality of the video is on par with that system. No more buying batteries!!!

Having installed the system there are several thing that need to be taken into account. The power supply is short. When you buy this system, you might want to survey your property first, to determine how far away your receptacles will be. I had to buy 3, 12 volt power extensions for my setup. As you read above, you will need power. You can call an electrician to wire your house for this system. However, I bought a converter that screwed into one of the two flood light sockets on both sides of my house. Works like a dream and costs me somewhere around $7-$8.

title: A Mash-up of Good and Bad …
text:
When I think of Honeywell, I think of hi-tech, military-grade and precision. While the HONEYWELL SMART HOME SECURITY CAMERA BASE STATION seems to exhibit these traits, it is also hindered by them.

WHAT IT IS

The HOME SECURITY BASE STATION is a ~7” tall cylindrical camera that serves as a hub/base for adding other products/features. While the emphasis for this product is expansion that provides coverage for an entire house, it can be used as a single/standalone security camera. This device is compatible with Amazon and Google smart devices.

FEATURES

- The cylinder is comprised of three sections: the lower section is for visual alerts, the large middle section is a speaker and the top section houses the camera/lens.

- The 147 degree wide-angle camera lens records videos in 1080P HD with audio.

- The audio is two way and can work with Amazon Alexa for voice commands
.
- There is a Honeywell app that allows users to control and customize the base as wells as view and save videos recorded by the camera.

- The system can be set up as a simple camera or a security system that detects motion, recognizes faces and features an alarm.

HOW IT PERFORMS

The set-up is relatively simple and typical … download the smartphone app and connect to your network. The instructions “manual” is a folded sheet of paper that provides limited information, especially considering the device’s capability and complexity. Unfortunately, my experience with the HOME SECURITY BASE STATION was based on trial and error. The support for this device is limited and what is severely missing is a comprehensive manual that clearly details every aspect of the device. The app is where I had to discover most features and even the app has issues.

While the setup is simple, figuring out how to interpret and control the base stations is a pain. I simply moved the device after setting it up and the alarm was triggered. On the plus side, the alarm’s piercing shriek is certainly effective, but turning it off was a problem that wasn’t solved by disconnecting the power source. It took almost 30 minutes to find out how to silence the alarm and if burying the device under pillows/blankets and closing the bedroom door had not worked, the base station would have been in pieces on the street (yes, it was THAT bad).
The instructions indicate the top of the base station has a “button” which controls several things, but it’s a touch pad that offers no indication of when it’s been engaged. Then there are the color-coded lights that emanate from the base … blue/red/green/white … figuring out (and remembering) what those stand for is not so easy (a red light accompanies the alarm as well as indicates the system is not online). Occasionally, the device delivers an unexpected notification that comes across as a wakeup chime or hum … while this is not unpleasant (it is actually soothing), I still have no idea what it means. The base set also reacts to any command given to Alexa (flashing blue light and a subtle audible tone).

The app is essential, and it serves as the best way to control this beast. This is where you will discover the additional features and expansion capability of the base station, such as facial recognition, camera modes, motion detection settings, etc. Discovering these functions is a trial-and-error process as well; I was receiving HUNDREDS of email notifications of motion detection before I figured out how to stop the deluge and only then could I take steps necessary to control the motion detection aspects of the camera. The camera records when motion is detected, so if your phone will start accumulating a lot of videos in short order if you haven’t made the right setting.

Unfortunately, some of the most interesting/promising features of the base station will require a subscription for service. For example, the facial recognition is certainly a neat feature that involves a process in which the camera learns facial features … you are allowed two faces for free and must subscribe to add more. In other words, you will pay for the bells and whistles.

As frustrated as I was with so many aspects of this device, the basic function of wide-angle coverage of a room is outstanding and the video quality is superb. Once I adjusted to the nuances of the base station, mainly setting the motion detection parameters and putting a halt to the notifications, I’ve enjoyed using it. It is a hi-tech device with a lot of potential but too little information on how to operate the thing. Many of problems I experienced could have been prevented had Honeywell simply provided a more thoughtful and thorough user manual. The HONEYWELL SMART HOME SECURITY BASE STATION has a lot of potential, but for now, I’m a little hesitant to consider expanding or subscribing.

title: Buyer Be Informed
text: I have recently acquired three Gskyer telescopes. While there are some differences they all have similarities.. Out of the three this one is the best because of the 90mm aperture. This allows a bit more light to enter the telescope then the other two that I have. First of all to be fair I am an amateur. But I do a lot of high-end photography so I know a bit about lenses. I rely on reviews especially from products I know little about. When looking at the reviews for all of the Gskyer telescopes the first thing I noticed were the large amount of suspicious five-star reviews. This speaks volumes to the integrity of a company. As my headline implies I am unsure what this company's definition of "German technology" is other than two words used to increase sales and trust in their product. My definition of German technology must differ from the Gskyer definition. There is little of this telescope that I would consider anywhere near the quality level of German technology. So already before even telling you about this product it has lost two stars. The price range and configuration of this telescope clearly puts it in the amateur category. The assembly instructions are incredibly poor. You get a sheet of paper filled with small photographs that tell you nothing on how to assemble this telescope. Nor do you get any instructions on how to adjust settings or how to use it. There is no carrying case for the multiple eyepieces you will receive and there is no case for the entire telescope. The lenses themselves are of the lowest quality and on this telescope any planet you try to observe will give very disappointing results. It is just fair for looking at the moon or seeing distant terrestrial objects like birds. Trying to fine-tune adjustments Is a very frustrating process. All of the fittings are loose and need constant attention. Again, this is not something that would be tolerated in German technology. If you are interested in astronomy you will be better off saving for a better telescope from a more reputable company that does not make false claims or pad their reviews. I am only giving this two stars instead of one because the telescope is usable and does work, although frustratingly, to look at the moon. If you like the price and you do not mind warped and imprecise fittings in this telescope might be a good place to start.

title: Excellent entry in to the pro tablet world
text:
Like many others searching for a large drawing tablet, Wacom Cintiq is a name that has been known for a long time and was the first place I went to read reviews and begin to make the most informed choice I could about my tablet purchase. For that reason, while this is a review of the MVP22U(V3) +RH, I think it’s important to keep in mind other options that will face many large tablet buyers.

Wacom is considered an industry standard and up until recently, there really haven’t been major competitors to enter the market. Fueled by artists like Ray Frenden who aim to provide working and aspiring artists unbiased reviews and comparisons that aren’t based on the appeal of a name, rather the quality and value of the product, I was inspired to dig a little deeper in my own search for a digital drawing solution.

There were a few factors that were important to me in my search:

Customer service:
One common thread through many of the reviews I read about Wacom was lousy customer support, from outright denial of commonly known issues to long wait times on repairs and hard to reach customer service.

The first time I read about Yiynova was a comment about how fast and caring their customer support was. In the US, Yiynova shipping and support is run through Panda City, the name of the seller that you’ll see here on Amazon.

I can already say in my experiences contacting Panda City that they are fast and helpful. I’ve heard that when it comes to product issues and support they are excellent, and fortunately I have had no issues yet with my tablet. That being said, for many of us, buying a tablet is a big expenditure, and there is comfort in knowing that if things go wrong that you have a safety net.

Quality:
I was impressed with the quality of my MVP22U(V3)+RH before it even got pugged in. The unit was well packed and arrived safely. When I pulled it out of the box the bubble sleeve they used fit tightly and felt really solid. The many included accessories (multiple connecting cables to suit PC or Mac, drawing glove, the comfortable P2X pen) were well labeled and organized.

After plugging in the unit and giving it a spin (I use it both now as a second monitor and also for drawing with Clip/Manga Studio), I can safely say that I have been impressed across the board with the stability, build quality, and responsiveness of the included pen.

For being a 22 inch monitor the footprint is quite small, and the built in stand is extremely easy to adjust without moving from a seated working position. This means when creativity strikes the time from being upright as a second monitor, to a much lower angle comfortable to drawing takes all of about 5 seconds. Even better is that I’ve found the stand to be solid no matter the angle, which is great because I tend to have a pretty heavy hand when I draw.

The glass is easy to clean and I have no issues with the smoothness of it. I know myself well enough to know that any non-glass screen would leave me paranoid about making permanent marks and scratches. I’ve heard of many Cintiq users buying protective films and there was something that bugged me about spending $2,000 or more on a tablet and still needing to buy the appropriate cables and a protective film. So far after many hours of use the glass on the Yiynova is smooth, solid, and showing no signs of wear.

My one issue is with the included remote that uses suction cups to place on the screen. While I appreciate that it can be placed anywhere for convenience, when I do suction it to the screen it often falls of. Maybe someone knows a trick to get it on tight. I have started setting the remote on my desk in front of the screen and it has been working fine there.

Value:
This is wear the Yiynova really shines. When paying half of the price of a comparable tablet from Wacom, I would totally expect for their to be sacrifices. For some people that have used any tablet for any length of time, there may be sacrifices - different button mapping, less buttons, etc., but for me everything that I need and expect for a smooth workflow is here. I tend to be a very practical buyer, buying what I think I need and not spending money on what I don’t, but the difference in price here is so extreme for a product that is so comparable (and in my opinion preferable in some ways) that the value in this product goes beyond my feeling of making a good purchase, and makes me feel proud to support a company that backing up a great product with responsive customer service at a phenomenal price.

All this to say, this doesn’t feel like a budget tablet. This feels like a solid, thoughtfully designed product that is offered at an excellent price. Getting innovation out to their customers seems to be a goal of Yiynova, as seen by the relatively short product cycles of their last few tablets. The feedback they receive seems to be directly reflected in their releases. The remote is an example of this. While this monitor is similar to their previous version, the hotkeys were at the top of the monitor and many comments were made about that being an inconvenient location. Their solution was to let the user decide where their buttons were more comfortably placed. While I do have the small gripe about the strength of the suction cups, I appreciate that Yiynova hears their customers and tries to adjust quickly.

Summary:
If you’re looking for a large drawing tablet and you have $1000 to spend, this is a phenomenal choice that should keep you happy for a long time to come. If you have $2000 to spend, consider buying this tablet and saving your other $1000. The jump in cost for a well known name just doesn’t seem worth it. Everyone has their own set of criteria and will buy what’s best for them, but I’d give this tablet a good hard look if you’re in the market. I’m looking forward to using my Yiynova for a long time to come and feel good about supporting a company that respects and values their customers.

title: Good Value For The Price
text:
The first thing to understand about these tweeters is that they are inexpensive; for twenty bucks you get a big, bright sound that may or may not appeal to the individual listener. I have a pair of KEF C85 speakers that are in remarkable shape, except for the Uni-Q tweeters. The tweeters were filled with ferro-fluid, which dried out over the years and left the tweeters essentially dead. Since these tweeters are no longer manufactured (and positioned in the middle of the midrange driver), I wanted to see what I could get mounting a set of tweeters on top of the speaker cabinets. The TW28 fit the bill perfectly and at little cost. The TW28s did indeed bring the KEFs back to life. The highs returned, opening up the soundstage and making the speakers listenable. Unfortunately, the overall sound, to my ear, was harsh, brittle, piercing at times, and, ultimately, tiresome. None of this surprised me. Like I said, the TW28s are cheap, not bad, just cheap. They pointed me in the right direction. I purchased a set of Fountek NEOCD 1.0 Ribbon tweeters (as I write this, on sale here at Amazon for $45 each). These are modest but well-made ribbons that produce clean high frequencies. The KEFs sound good again, though that sound is undoubtedly different from the original factory configuration.
I think the TW28s have a genuine appeal, depending on a given set of considerations, and are certainly worth $21. I'm not sorry I bought them.

title: Excellent size, build quality, nice screen and good keyboard but Bluetooth audio is a maybe.
text:
IMPORTANT FORTH UPDATE ADDED:

A few initial Asus Chromebook flip observations: The device arrived far ahead of the initial projected two week delivery date and in pristine condition. The 'manual' admonished customers to charge eight hours before using with battery power only and my exploration of the flip or pseudo tablet mode was painfully delayed. The all metal body looks great and build quality is impressive.

Because it is a Chrome OS device, it instantly updated and was up and running with all my apps within five minutes of powering on. The screen is bright, crisp and equal to my now orphaned Asus Windows RT tablet and aging iPad Mini. The keyboard is comfortable and responsive, audio is surprisingly good, both online and offline videos play without stutter. The track-pad and touchscreen are responsive. The glass appears to have a coating that makes it more difficult to slide my fingers across the screen. This is particularly noticeable when I compare the subjective feeling of interacting with my Acer 720P, Windows and iPad tablets. I notice more delay and less fluid scrolling when interacting with sites like Facebook. The stutter in page scrolling is noticeable but certainly not sluggish enough to detract from an overall excellent surfing experience. I would like to know if anyone else has noted similar issues.

When in the flip-mode, the added thickness of the keyboard and combined weight makes for a less than ideal tablet experience. I've only begun to test pairing with my Bluetooth audio devices but have already noticed some disconcerting issues with sound and pairing when using my LG 700 headset and DKnight BT speaker. In both cases pairing took longer than usual and I noticed micro interruptions in streaming audio. The computer has updated at least three times since I began using it and will continue to test Bluetooth audio with follow up posts to this review.

I suspect that my growing preference for Chrome OS devices, size, weight, excellent display, portability, hybrid / flip construction and build quality of the Acer C100 will ensure my dependence on my iPad Mini continues to decrease. title: Bad WiFi Direct
text: The Roku Streaming Stick + worked OK, but soon after installing it, other WiFi devices began to get kicked off the network.  I noticed in the android WiFI analyzer app that someone had brought up a WiFi access point on the same channel as mine. :(  It was also transmitting at a higher power than mine.  I soon realized that it was the Roku stick's WiFi Direct connection to its remote.  I tried changing my WAP to a different channel, but the Roku followed it there.  I tried changing from 2.4 to 5Ghz, but it also followed my access point to the new frequency/channel.  I reached out to Roku tech support, and they suggested that I change channels on my WAP...which I'd already done.  I informed them that I'd already been down that rabbit hole and they said to try a free HDMI extender?  The stick was on a 3 foot extender already.  Roku used to have an option in the firmware to try to correct this issue, but they've removed it.  I would have given 2 or 3 stars if they'd been more helpful.  But as it is, I must highly discourage anyone from purchasing this product until they fix the WiFi design/firmware.  I hope they do fix it.  If not, I'd probably go for an older Roku model with an infrared remote.

title: USB-C is not the same as Thunderbolt 3
text:
The picture is good. The monitor ports (USB-C, DP, HDMI) are difficult to get to once the monitor is on its stand. The on-screen display is insanely ugly with incredibly blocky text and graphics. It really cheapens the feel of the monitor.

USB-C is not Thunderbolt 3. This means you cannot use an Apple Thunderbolt 2 to Thunderbolt 3 adapter to connect a TB2-equipped MacBook to this display. A DP cable (mini DisplayPort to DisplayPort) works for these older MacBooks. I agree with @Gamut's review recommending DP with older Macs. With HDMI, the Mac selects a BT.709 ICC profile, even though the monitor is still set at its default sRGB, and for scaling you get a choice of tiny or very large text. You have much finer control of scale with DP. Of course DP doesn't connect the USB hub. You will have to use the included USB-A to USB-C cable to connect the on board USB hub to a USB port on the MacBook.

@Gamut also wrote that the 4th USB (A) port is for charging only. While the User Guide is silent on why this port has different, yellow, coloring, it is not for charging only. I have connected a USB drive and my MBP sees and can read it. I suspect the yellow indicates it is the port to use for fast charging.

The instructions in the User Guide for installing the Lenovo config/driver files on Windows 10 are incorrect and do not match the Settings/Control Panel in Windows 10 Fall Creators Edition. I had to invoke the Device Manager directly. Furthermore the instructions for updating the driver once you've got into the Device Manager are also incorrect.

title: Great Quality And Design
text:
Wow. This quality and design of this strap clearly exceeded my expectations on my Fuji x-T10. The "give" of the neoprene shoulder pad provides incredible comfort. The QD loop easily attached to the camera lug. Love the fact that the loop itself is woven nylon, and won't cause any dings or scratches to the camera body (ditto for the wider nylon carry strap or the hard nylon quick disconnects).

This strap has a modular design, comprised of 5 distinct sections held together by quick disconnects ("QD"s - this allows the strap to be easily removed intentionally (e.g when using the camera on a tripod). As many reviewers have noted, the QD's aren't prone to accidental openings that could result in camera drops. If you really want a belt and suspenders approach, the larger QD's can be further protected from accidental openings by using simple Velcro strips (Op/Tech sells them but they're just strips of Velcro One Wrap you can make yourself). The strap design also allows for simple, easy adjustment of length and carry position against the body, without having to remove it. For each side, just hold the upper (larger) larger QD clip and slide it up or down to change its length

Op/Tech's modular approach also offers another benefit- just buy another set of QD loops and you're able to switch the strap between multiple non-dSLR cameras. And if one section gets damaged, etc., you can replace that part only (but given the low cost of the entire strap, savings vs a totally new strap may be pretty minimal).

One caveat - as the strap ages or experiences frequent use, be sure you have a plan to regularly inspect the "QD loop" (where it attaches to the camera lug) for any signs of wear.

title: First EVGA Power Supply....AND MY LAST!
text:
At first I was impressed with the overall build quality. I installed in a new Ryzen/B350 system, and while the motherboard did power on, none of the fans would turn, nor would the video card power up. Long story short, after nearly 4 hours of troubleshooting (the most maddening part), and power tests, I found that this unit was not supplying the correct voltages to the motherboard.

Further investigation uncovered that the EVGA power supplies have "compatibility issues" with a number of systems, and a number of those instances I found were the Ryzen/B350 systems.
In order to get my new system up and running, I install an OLD XFX 550 Watt power supply, and everything worked perfectly....but I'm right on the borderline of having enough power for the system, and wasted the majority of a day tracking down the issue(s).
This was my first purchase of an EVGA power supply, and it was the last! There is no excuse for a power supply of a 750watt rating to supply less then the correct voltages to power a system, nor have "compatibility issue" with ANY CPU/Chipset.
It's being returned for a refund, and I will give Corsair a try.

I tried to ditch the included 1 terabtye 7200 RPM hard drive and swap it for my 1 terabyte solid state drive, but encountered a stripped screw. I just kept the original hard drive in and put my solid state drive in the second hard drive slot, and then I disabled the original one in BIOS settings.

PROS: NVIDIA 970 mobile version can process 4K at 60hz and 1080p at 120hz

Modest battery life 2.5 hours gaming 4 hours casual use on "Balanced Mode"
G-SYNC makes a huge difference in gaming quality.
Can support virtual reality headsets.
Expanding the RAM can be done easily by popping off the lid.
There's 2 hard drive slots!
Trackpad disabled itself when the mouse is plugged in.
The left click and right click buttons feel so much better than the touchscreen ASUS laptops and most other new brands.

NOT SO GOOD:
It's huge and heavy. If weight is a concern just get a Macbook.
Keyboard layout... The letters do not feel as natural to type on as my Sony Vaio
DVD drive (seriously, it's 2016 why is that even there?!)
Optical hard drive disc that it comes with are outdated (again, it's 2016)
GTX980M is a little bit more powerful. If you are rich just go for it but for me it was not worth the extra $500. Honestly, if you really need a GTX980M you should just get the desktop GTX 980 for full computing power to do whatever gaming/editing you need.
Conclusion: Ditch the optical hard drive and go with the solid state. Hoping this stays "futureproof" until 2019 or 2020. My Sony desktop from 2010 can barely handle anything today. Will update when I test some 4K games.

UPDATE March 3, 2016: Started to fall apart after three months. Speakers made horrible crackling sound even on mute. Keyboard backlight randomly turns off. And seriously, 4th generation Intel chipset? Most 2015-2016 models are 6th generation. Battery life is barely two hours. 4K video/gaming support @ 60hz is almost impossible with the GTX970 but 1080p @ 120hz looks great. If you need real 4K support, get a desktop because it won't happen with a laptop anytime soon.

title: I am very happy with the speed improvement
text:
This is the cheapest SSD I could find in terms of cost per GB. So, my expectation was not very high. I was just looking something to speed up my 7 year old Dell E6520 (already had 8 G of RAM). But, was I surprised. After copying disk image to the new SSD, everything now only takes a fraction the time it used to. It used to take 1-1/2 minutes to boot up Windows 10, it now takes about 20 seconds. All the applications now take less than 1/3 the time it used to take. There were no major issues cloning or installing the SSD in my PC. Everything was straight forward. I am very happy with this.
Update: After using this for a few months, I decided to take 2 stars away. My reason? Shortly after my initial review, I started having bootup issues. Every few days, my laptop would take a few reboots to come up. One day, it just refused to boot at all, Neither restore point or recovery disk could revive it. Luckily, I had saved an image when I started having boot up issues. At that time, I discovered that the SSD was not completed seated in the slot. Turned, this SSD is a teeny bit shorter than my normal 2.5 hard drive. I have the Dell Latitude 6520 which the the drive is inserted from the side of the laptop and secured with the 4 screws at the bottom. When the screws holes are lined up with the laptop, the SSD does not go all the way in. as I pushed the SSD all the way in, i would no long put the screws in. So now, I just left it unscrewed. and just tried not to move the laptop too much. The Dell E6520 is a very heavy laptop, I am using like a desktop anyway, so that is not an issue for me.
Depending on how the SSD is installed in your computer, this may or may not be an issue, I wanted to point this out in case anyone has a similar laptop.

title: Good for BEGINNERS wanting something cheap
text:
I am a professional photographer and we typically do photo shoots outdoors so we don't have a studio. That being said, there are times when we do shoot indoors, and having a backdrop can be helpful. Photography backdrops are expensive, so I was very hesitant to try one that is extremely cheap. I read reviews and some people loved them, some hated them. Only a few had decent photo quality of photos if they did upload pictures. I decided to give it a shot.
I received the item in a tiny package. The background was folded as small as it could be. I unfolded it and it was completely wrinkled. The material is thin and stiff. I have been trying to figure out how to describe it, and it reminds me of a tarp because it is stiff and doesn't have much motion to it. For example, it's extremely difficult to roll, it tends to just cave in on itself.
I had read that it comes wrinkled so I took out the iron and ironed it out. I actually just used the iron on a low setting directly on the back of the material. I tried it with the towel on top but it didn't work for me. Most of the wrinkles came out but some are stuck in there. Nothing a little photoshop can't fix I guess. There were a few spots where the color had rubbed off on the background, but it could be because my package came damaged. The spots were minimal so I didn't feel the need to return it. When photographed they weren't visible.

The background has a very short section for the floor. The difficulty here is getting the client far enough away from the background so that it can have a nice blur and create depth. I had to pull my client in front of the background so I could create that depth. As far as how it photographed, it photographed great! The colors were rich and it didn't look fake. I had to edit out some of the folds though.
Overall if you are a beginning photographer this item would be a good place to start. That being said, I would only get these if you do have a studio where you can leave he backdrops hanging. Trying to roll them to store them somewhere just isn't possible due to the material and is quite the pain. If they can be stored hanging it would be great. If you are a professional, you get what you pay for, and I wouldn't use these even if I did have a studio, simply because the "floor" section is much too short. It needs at least another 2 ft. For a beginner I think these are a decent start.

title: It is also better than it's stablemate (H110i GTX made by Asetek - ...
text:
Overall, it is a decent all-in-one cooling solution. It is also better than it's stablemate (H110i GTX made by Asetek - the H110i GT is made by CoolIT). Here is a Quote from the Corsair forums:

"The firmware differences are huge and even Corsair admit "Asetek hardware is...silly".
1. CoolIT H110iGT has two and H100i + H80i have four fan controllers, all Asetek only have one.
2. CoolIT can use any temperature source, Asetek can only use the Cooler Temperature.
3. CoolIT firmware can be updated, Asetek can't
4. CoolIT lights have far more functionality than the Asetek .
5. CoolIT reports the pump speed to CPU_FAN, Asetek reports a fan speed."

I also prefer the hose connections on the CPU block used with H110i GT. You can get better temps and lower noise levels with a well put together custom water cooling loop, but you will spend more and it requires much greater knowledge and time to do right. The H110i GT can be installed by just about anyone.

There is one issue with this product and that is the Corsair Link software. It has some bugs in it and for those using the latest Windows 10 updates, it will endlessly send pop-ups telling you that a new device has been found and a restart is required. Getting rid of this requires manually editing the Windows Registry: http://forum.corsair.com/forums/showthread.php?p=822047. Corsair has been slow in fixes and updates for this software, so expect the issue to continue until they get an update out.

The unit is unbearably loud if you crank the fans up or use the performance profile, but if you use the quiet profile, or tinker with your own custom profile, it can be made to operate pretty quietly while still keeping temperatures low. In summary, despite the software issue, this probably the best all in one water cooling product currently available. I prefer this to hanging the considerable weight of a large heat sink and fan off the CPU area of a motherboard. If they do a decent update to Corsair Link, I would give the H110i GT 5 stars.

title: Just buy it, critics be damned!
text:
____________________________________________Disclaimer______________________________________________________
First let me say that I purchased this item from amazon and was in no way compensated by this company for this review. I have had dealings with their customer support and it is for that reason that even with the short coming of this item, they have received a 5 star rating.
___________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Ok, so I have seen some of the criticisms of this stand/holder and they range from complaints about the plastic to the stiffness, and or bounciness of this item.
First: yes, it has plastic, if you don't want plastic, find another product that is going to cost you much more and provide none of the flexibility of this product.
Second: Is the flexible part stiff and hard to shape... yes... but if it were not so then it would sag every time you used it.
Third: is it bouncy... yes.. what do you expect? it is an ADJUSTABLE arm that can be put into most any shape withing reason. How it is that people would expect anything different is beyond comprehension.
Fourth: Does it break... yes... anything will break if you apply to much force or in the case of this stand, at the base where the clamp is. This apparently is not common sense so people need to be told to not be overly aggressive with something at its weakest point.

Rant over!
I have had it for a couple of months now and here is my take on it, It is a nice item to have and once I played with it for a bit I found a shape (spiral) that best suited my use. It is a bit springy which makes touch screen a bit of a pain but it also allows us to use it in unconventional places where a normal stand type would not work. I originally purchased it for my iPad, unfortunately, the clamp is not deep enough to hold my iPad [ http://a.co/d/6SAqD3G ] in its protective case [ http://a.co/d/4vSKCrf ] because in the back of the case is a hand strap and kickstand. I then decided to see if it would work for my wife's Surface pro, and it did, so it currently resides on the headboard of our bed on my wife's side where she mounts the surface pro so she can watch videos with here headphones on instead of turning on the TV. The weight of the surface pro is not an issue and there is no sag. I shaped the arm into a spiral shape and pressed the rings closely together to minimize the springiness of it. While not perfect, it works extremely well, all my wife does is hold one corner of the tablet while using the touch screen with the other. I eventually got a follow up message from this company in regards to the item and whether or not I am happy with it. I explained the issue with my ipad case but that my wife uses it for her surface pro. They quickly got back to me and offered to take the item back for a full refund since it did not meet my needs. Now for those that complain about this product, I have only one question, did you contact customer support? I understand that there are going to be problem units, but I also know that people will complain just to complain. I wholly support putting information out about a bad product and have done so on occasion myself but I always add that the issue I had is based on one unit that I received and may not reflect the product as a whole. I have no complaints about this product or this company, I have purchased two products from them and have yet to see any of the issues others have complained about. Maybe i'm lucky but I think that it has more to do with managing expectations and not abusing the products. I highly recommend this product for two reasons, first, it is actually a very good product that is durable as long as you are not heavy handed when using it. Two, they have taken a page out of the amazon customer service handbook and made it better. Their customer service is amazingly responsive, professional and courteous. I would and will buy from this company again because I know that if the product is not up to my standards then they are willing to make things right within reason. A big thumbs up for a very cool product and the amazing customer service rep Kevin that deserves a raise for dealing with a difficult person like me. I hope this review helped

Oh yeah, one last thing, the clip (that holds your table or phone depending on which one you get) uses a very strong spring which is needed to hold things in place. It is made of plastic which keeps the weight down and keeps the arm from sagging, this plastic will eventually break if you allow it to snap shut when you remove you phone or tablet. If you don't want it to break then use a little common sense and don't allow it to snap closed, that should be a no brainer but from looking at some of the reviews, apparently it needs to be said out loud.

title: They came very nicely and securely packaged-a good beginning
text: I bought these without being able to sample them anywhere and with very little review information to be found.  They came very nicely and securely packaged-a good beginning!  After setting them up and playing them for a while-I decided to compare them to other speakers I own--these included Bose, Yamaha, JBL, Sony and infinity.  The sonys were the lowest priced and the JBLs the most expensive-(2 different type of JBLs tested a 3 way system and a pair of towers)..These aren't actually recommended as front speakers but they actually outperform all the others, at least to my hearing.  Besides music, I ran different tones through the speakers and again, these speakers were the clearest at reproducing the tones at all frequencies.  They are roughly the same size as Bose 201s (wider than they are tall).  All speakers were 8 ohms driven by an 80 watt Onkyo receiver.  It did seem like the Fluance speakers needed slighty more power to produce the same volume as the others--not a significant difference, but still a difference.  (It could be the material used in the speakers--I can't say for sure)  Anyway, bottom line is great sound at a fairly reasonable price.  Crossover is at 3600 hz--I noticed no problems with that.  Bass is fine for my listening pleasure, but for those who like to shake the windows a subwoofer would be needed.  Really no complaints of any kind and I think they make excellent main speakers and for the price I doubt anyone could find better.  A difference from other speakers I've owned or own the grills are held to the speaker by magnets instead of the typical push in connectors--it's nice, but be careful when moving the speakers,  they tend to slip free.  Brackets are attached to the rear of the speakers for wall mounting, I haven't done that yet, but it would appear to be a simple and solid setup which I'm sure I'll get to eventually.  Decided to add an edit--the speakers I compared the fluances to are considerably older-some (yamaha) are over 25 years old and the infinitys and jbls are about 25 years old--the bose and sonys are within the last 10 years

title: I wanted to like these KEF's but!!
text:
I wanted to like these KEF's but I did not at all. Not sure if I was spoiled coming from my current setup of speakers with a dedicated DAC (Oppo HA-1) with my Adam Audio ARTist 5 speakers. I also have been tested speakers for a new computer build using a MATRIX Mini-i Pro DAC started with Genelec 8020C Active Two-Way 4" Studio Monitor, and then the Kef's X300A by them self, along with some Genelec 8020C Active Two-Way 4" Studio Monitors. And I must say the KEF's sounded the worst out of all speakers. I really wanted to like them I think they look the best out of the bunch, but other then the large size like my Adam's ARTist 5 speakers. They come off very bright with no mid-range and a boomy bass that's trying to hard. Now I watched many YouTube video's on the Kef's X300A and watching the video I noticed the FRONT midrange/woofer section move's allot to all types of music in the review's, but for some reason mine very rarely moved which made the the speakers come across very bright sounding. So I thought maybe I am have a driver issue so I used my new laptop no audio drivers on it same issue, I even used my friends computer to try one last time same problem. I decided to let the speakers break in for a week with the same outcome. So I decided to send them back and went with the Genelec 8020C Active Two-Way 4" Studio Monitors. They come in half the size of the Kef's X300A and put out 10 times the clear neutral sound. And yes they were $300 more but worth every penny, along with my Adam speakers. I also sent back the Senal speakers which are copy's from the Genelecs at half the price but had too much distortion.
I am not done with KEF I will be building a living room listening setup and plan on trying the Kef LS50's which seem very popular I just hope I do not have the same bad luck like I did with the X300A speakers.

title: Amazing little speaker with one slight drawback
text:
After looking at a bunch of the obviously fake reviews for this product I was definitely a little skeptical. Every review was 5 stars and written in broken english. Anyway, I figured at that price I could give it a shot. It is a great little speaker with very easy to use functionality and helpful features. The speaker itself is very small and compact but the sound quality is unbelievable for something it's size. The form factor is great as well. It has a smooth almost soft feel to it but it still feels very sturdy. I've only taken it in the shower so I can't speak to the full waterproof-ness of the device but it works great in the shower. Takes calls easily with no complaints from the other end and sounds perfect. One of the cooler features is the color changing lights. It has 3 options: steady single blue light, multi-colored spinning/changing lights that somewhat respond to the music itself, and a multi-colored steady state. 2 options for connecting: bluetooth or aux in (comes with headphone to headphone input cable). My only complaint, and the only thing keeping this from getting 5 stars is that there are no skip or pause buttons. This makes it so even if your phone isn't close to you you are stuck with whatever song is playing. This sounds minor but with a waterproof bluetooth speaker that is huge as you could concievably take this little guy into the pool with you and lounge, not worrying about getting your phone wet. It would literally be perfect if they added one more button to skip songs so you wouldn't have to go grab your phone every time. Overall a great little speaker though.

Pros:
+great sound quality
+easy to use
+beautiful color changing lights
+compact

Cons
-no ability to skip songs from the speaker itself

title: Higher resistance than expected
text:
What's good: It's inexpensive, it's shielded, it's easy to strip work work with.

What's bad: I tested the resistance of the conductors (which appeared to be copper) and I noticed that I'm getting significantly higher resistance (4.8 Ohms per 100 ft) than I would have expected for 22 guage pure copper (1.6 Ohms per 100 ft). It turns out the conductors are Copper-Clad Aluminum. This is why the cable is so inexpensive!

Also, after doing a relatively gentle 50' run with this cable, I found one of the conductors was bad. Aluminum isn't as forgiving as copper when it comes to bending and pulling.

Giving two stars for not mentioning this up-front in the description.

title: Professional product...for everyone.
text:
Top quality and craftsmanship. Let's face it...when we think of Chinese or India for products, we think of cheap quality...not this time. With my 40yrs in the film industry working small to large budget films, I've worked with top quality equipment.  All my follow focuses through the years have been $2500 FF made in Germany considered the best.  My budget these days don't allow for that.  I have tried several FF from Amazon only to be amazed at the lack of quality and steadiness.  I got this unit and right away, the crank is as high a quality as my $2500 FF.  Although I don't need a gear belt, it two was the best I've seen.  It tightened easily and secured fast.  My amazement was when I lifted the unit itself out of the box.  Solid, heavy, precise quality.  It mounts firm and easily...without having to disassemble the rig to slide it on the rails. This is important when you have to change from operator side to Focus Puller side of the camera rig. It moves onto the gears with a smooth and precise motion and locks firm.  The focus gear is smooth and the double hard stops are quality.  If you've never used hard stops, you have to use them to see how much easier it makes racking a shot.

Notice in the photos that one is the $2500 FF and the other is FilmCity...both can change their gear side but only the FilmCity has hard stops and quick rail mount.

To sum it up...this unit is a quality machined aluminum device worth far more than it sells for.  The truth is I'm selling my $2500 FF and using the money to replace all my FF with these units.

Once again FilmCty(Cinecity) comes through with top quality that satisfied even the toughest of critic's as myself.

Get yourself a good whip such as the one I reviewed, and you're set to go.

R.G.
IAWFilmWorks

text:
If I could rate this a -5 I would. Not only is this a horrible product that lasted just two months before the backlight went out, Toshiba has the worst customer service of any major manufacturer I've had the displeasure of wasting my money on.

The picture is great in 4k mode (when it was working), fair in 1080p mode with strange shades of gray/black. After 2 months it simply stopped displaying a picture. A call to tech support lead to a warranty repair being scheduled for what was thought to be a main-board replacement. About a week later I got a call from the tech who quickly determined that the issue was a back-light malfunction. I called Toshiba again and was told that it would take a month for the part to ship but that someone would call me.

On the day that the new part was to ship I got a call from Toshiba saying that the part had been delayed and that they would suggest to the order desk that I receive a replacement. I got a call the following week (today) saying that Toshiba was discontinuing this model because they could no longer get parts for it and offered me two choices: 1- refund minus a pro-rated charge for the time I had the TV (4 months, nearly 2 of which were spent waiting for repair) or 2 - Accept a refurbished downgrade model (65L7350) with a 90-day warranty.

I will not soon buy another Toshiba product and I advise the same.

title: Great Upgrade At A Reasonable Price - 2 HDMI Ports!
text:
Over the years, my ol' trusty EVGA GTX 560 has been through many hours of gameplay, however, it was time for an upgrade. I'm a gamer, but not the type of gamer that dedicates his life to games. I'm not a streamer, just your casual gamer who likes to play a couple hours every other day. Planetside 2, Just Survive, and a few others really. A lot of newer games came out that I really wanted to play, but needed an update (PUBG) .. so after months of deliberation, I made my purchase.

To be honest, I'm not very knowledgeable on video cards and didn't know what I was looking for. My last one was an EVGA, so, maybe I'd get another one of those.. right? Doing my research, I settled on the EVGA GTX 1050ti or the 1060 6gb. They both looked great, however, what led me to the ASUS GTX 1060 6gb is the dual HDMI ports. The specs compared strongly with the ECGA 1060 6gb and knew it was time to pull the trigger on the higher end card over the 1050ti. All my friends kept pushing me to get a 1080 or a 1080ti.. but the prices are just insane. As I said, I'm a casual gamer, not someone who was looking to drop $800 on a card!

I got it in and installed it in about 10 minutes (remember to take the protective cover off the PCI chip at the bottom.. duh!) and the driver installed automatically and I was up and running. My computer is quieter than before with my older card and Just Survive and other games run incredible. Really happy and love the dual HDMI ports!

title: The keyboard is half great, half abysmal
text:
I've only had the Chi for a couple of days but it has exceeded my expectations. There are a number of criticisms I read pre-purchase that concerned me about the Chi that turned out to be dead on accurate. The keyboard is half great, half abysmal. The track pad really does suck. It's too small and inaccurate. The Chi is difficult to open because of the keyboard. I'm going to get a stylus when they're available so I can use it as a pry bay to open the sucker. On the other hand it's great to type on, it feels very natural. The magnet attachment system works like gangbusters, it's a nice design touch. One final criticism about the keyboard, it is very sharp and pointy and digs into your palm if you overuse the arrow keys while surfing. My palm is red and a little sore, I'm not going to burst into tears or anything but it is an annoyance. I solved the problem by purchasing a bluetooth mouse. Generally I've gone through life mouseless, they've really improved in the 5 years I've totally ignored them.

The computer itself is truly awesome. I've been playing tablet roulette the past six months and nothing has satisfied me. I've tried out the Dell Venue 8 (too small), Dell Venue 11 (poor for internet browsing, re-sizing) Galaxy Note Pro 12.2 (too android :), and the Dell XPS 18 (too big). None of them fit the bill. I do a lot of mobile work in my car and paired with the ikross tablet holder the Chi is a godsend. I can now get quite a bit of work done on the road and I'm not overloaded with hardware up front. Any of you ever use a laptop desk? They suck something awful. They bounce around and can distract you from the road. This combination is the best setup I ever had.

The battery life is fine with the sig edition, I'm averaging 8 hours without a charge. I brought a power inverter with me just in case but it was unneeded. It's not the best battery ever but it's good enough. The aspect ratio isn't a problem like some have suggested. The screen is AOK and doesn't have any back light bleeding issues, It's perfect in every way. Reading in portrait mode is truly awesome, it's like having a super kindle.I'm not concerned with the lone micro USB port, I'll work around it. Tomorrow I'm going to figure out how to switch my old Windows Office 2007 disc over, it will be a little challenge but easily beatable, probably:).

The keyboard bundled with the Chi means very little to me. It's not important. The actual chi is well worth purchasing, at $599 it's the bargain of the year. Very odd reviews out there for this little beast that succeeds on every level. I would certainly buy this one again. When the prices drop I may even upgrade to the swanky high priced version. The $599 was just too good of a deal to pass up.

title: Great tool for anyones arsenal
text: I received this item as scheduled new in box.  The converter work great with SATA HDD/SSD drives.  I also bought it for a spare internal 3.5 Blu-Ray DVD drive I have laying around and it works.  However there is a fly in the ointment.  If you unplug it then plug it back in it will not see the DVD drive.  Apparently, it now thinks the DVD drive is a HDD and shows an unknown disk drive in Windows Disk Management and Device Manager now shows my Blu-ray drive under "Disk drives" instead of DVD/CD-ROM drives, where it was before unplugging.  Only restarting the computer will sort this out.  This will happen every time you unplug the DVD drive without restarting the computer; thus the 4 star rating.  This is not an issue with HDD/SSD.  FYI, I am using Windows 10 Home v.1511 and no longer have Win 7 to try this out on.  So, I do not know if this issue is a Win 10 only thing.  None the less, the product does work and is a good portable tool for my needs, and relatively inexpensive.  With that said, I think they are charging too much for the IDE adapter.  I guess that is due to low volume since most drives now are SATA.  There are other products out there that will do both SATA/IDE but not 3.5 DVD burners.  These units are usually only 5 volts and you need 12 volts for 3.5 DVD burners.

title: WAVLINK not ready for prime time
text:
Well my experience was not stellar- Great box and cool look: 1 star. Performance: No stars. Straight out of the box it was hooked up, recognized by the Win 10 OS on this Surface Pro 4, (as it should be for current products). Plugged in the dongle for the wireless mouse and nothing, waited....., nothing. (It was literally only 10 inches away on the desk). So I started moving it towards the hub. Erratic movements started at 5 inches, full control ability was achieved at 3 inches! Well, I don't know about you, but in this age of cool electronic gadgets I expect that I should be able to have full use of my peripherals as I would without the hub, -10 to 15 feet at least, but only 3 inches!?
So this hub interferes with the wireless signal therefore the performance is well below sub-par which is a deal breaker. What other areas will I find this unit lacking performance if such a basic need is not fulfilled? As an IT semi-pro, I would stay away from WAVLINK products since they seem to not have the current needs of the computing public in mind when they release obviously sub-par products.
