title: Fine for a touch of decorative lighting, but not recommended for its advertised use
text:
I was skeptical, but I installed these on the back of my TV to see if they made watching it in the dark more comfortable. Many of the color settings are too bright and distracting and make the viewing less pleasant. A soft violet color was the best and in that case I’d only say that it was not terribly distracting, I don’t think it helped with eye strain or anything like that. And certainly anything other than a steady light/color was just silly for that use. The fade/chase patterns just compete with whatever you’re trying to watch.

But that was as expected. I figured I would mostly want to use these as decorative lights and that’s what I do. They are powered via a USB port and I wanted to leave them behind the TV just for a pleasant glow when I wasn’t watching anything, but unfortunately my TV’s USB port is only powered when the TV is powered on—i.e. exactly when I didn’t want to use them.

The lights come with a remote control that let you set different colors and patterns. It’s a good idea but hard to use. I’ve found that the lights aren’t great at reading the commands from the remote and I often have to hit a button several times for it to take. It is an IR remote (like for TVs) and there is an IR sensor hanging off a wire on the LED strip. You have to make sure that has line-of-sight to the remote. There are several light-changing modes you can choose from, but they are preprogrammed colors/brightnesses. In other words, you can’t use the 3-color fade mode to fade between colors of your choosing, it just fades between red, green, and blue. I found the color combos a tad on the conspicuous side—I like this sort of lighting to be soft and subtle—so the patterns are useless to me.  It does remember the last color/brightness setting it was on, though, so I’ve set it to a color and brightness I like and never use the remote at all now.

Overall, it’s fine as some decorative lighting to stick in a small area. You really want them behind an object and the light to bounce off the wall so you get a softer glow out of them. Looking at the LEDs directly is a bit unsightly. The remote and the functions it controls are clunky-to-useless and the idea of using to improve your TV viewing experience is nonsense. The fact that you can power it via USB could be convenient if you have a port nearby that is on when you need it. If not, you can just plug it into a USB charger port too.

title: Holds My New Samsung C27HG70 with Ease!
text:
I bought this stand to mount my new Samsung C27HG70 monitor too. The stand that comes stock with the monitor has an enormous adjustable arm on the back of it, which would have bumped into the wall behind my desk and caused me to have to move the monitor closer to me, and it would have been too close to my eyes.

Now, I do want to start the review by stating that this stand came to me missing the mounting screws used to assemble it. I was able to get it safely put together using the screws that came with my new Samsung monitor, but I honestly was a little agitated that there were no screws in the box like the instructions said there should have been.

That said, Pixio was quick to fix this. I contacted them here on Amazon and explained the situation to them, and they were more than happy to mail me a bag of screws, free of charge. They came in rather quickly too, and everything is as it should be now!

So, what do I think about this monitor stand? Well, I love it. It's amazing, and it holds my new monitor up with ease. The height is completely adjustable, the base is very sturdy, everything swivels as it's supposed to, etc. It's a little off-putting that the stand seems to weigh more than the monitor itself does, but I guess that's a good thing, since it's a sign of how sturdy it is!

If there was one thing I could change about this monitor, it would probably be the footprint of it; it's pretty large. I've been able to get around that by getting clever with the positioning, but at one point I did find that my mouse cable kept getting snagged on the foot of the stand. I actually fixed that by very loosely affixing a cable tie to the foot and feeding the mouse cable through it, which allows it to stay in a certain position and move freely, without getting snagged. Other than that, I have no complaints!

All in all, I love this stand. It does exactly what I wanted it to, and I'm very pleased with it!

In more detail:
(1) Sound quality in their passive mode is excellent. I tested them for several weeks with a range of music from contemporary jazz (Gregory Porter, Carmen Lundy), metal (Metallica, Type O Negative), shoegaze (My Bloody Valentine), post-punk (XTC), etc. I would not go so far as to say that these headphones were "revelatory," but I definitely enjoyed hearing a lot of musical nuance that I have not enjoyed in most of the mobile headphones that I've used for the past several years. Instruments and voices are clear, and different performers can be clearly heard and separated on the virtual soundstage. Imaging is remarkably good.
(2) Passive noise reduction is "pretty good." Most of the time - e.g., sitting in an office, studying, even walking around the city - you probably won't "need" to turn the active system on.
(3) Active noise reduction (in the "plane" mode) does color the music a little. However, it is extremely powerful - I can stand on a sidewalk under the "el" platform in downtown Chicago and enjoy listening without cranking the volume all the way up. If B&W forced me to use active noise reduction all the time, I don't think I'd recommend these headphones at this price. But of course you can use the app to toggle it (or configure its strength) at will, which is great because it leaves it to the user to decide whether background noise or sonic fidelity is more important.
(4) Other active noise reduction modes ("office" and "city") try to balance noise reduction with sound amplification so that you don't get sneaked up on by a person or car, for example. I don't think very highly of those modes, they don't do much for me in my usual use scenarios. more of a distraction than anything else.
(5) These headphones work great with audiobooks (Audible). Obviously, a set of multi-hundred dollar headphones would be overkill if your primary use is going to be audiobooks, but I am mentioning it because the active noise reduction is VERY effective with audiobooks. Tremendous sound isolation without cranking up the volume or distorting the voices noticeably.
(6) Battery charges last forever. Easily more than a week even using the headphones 2-3 hours per day.
(7) Some people complain that they interfere with glasses. I suppose that's a comment one could make about any circumaural headphones, but I don't have a serious problem wearing reading glasses while using them. A little manual adjustment of the cans and/or the glasses is all it takes.

I'm sort of a headphone junkie, and have owned or tested dozens of models made by the usual suspects including B&W, Bose, Sennheiser, Klipsch, Etymotic, Apple, and Ultimate Ears, along with a variety of lesser-known/regarded brands. When I'm listening at home, I generally use a set of wired, open-air Sennheiser circumaural headphones, but when mobile I've almost exclusively used in-canal earphones. Their portability, easy-packing, and the inherent passive sound isolation of in-canal silicone tips is hard to beat. Yes I've tried a couple of models of the perennially popular Bose headphones (and passed one of them to my wife, who uses it exclusively as her main set), but I never loved them. These B&W's are the first set of portable headphones that I've personally tried which combine comfort, isolation, and good sound in such a great package.

title: LOVE! Dewy Finish and Great for All Skin Types
text:
I purchased this because I've seen KathleenLights and Jaclyn Hill rave about it on Youtube and although they have dry skin and I have oily/combo skin, it worked for me! It took me FOREVER to pick the shade that would best match my skin since this isn't available in the United States, so I just looked up a lot of different swatches and tried to make the best possible choice. I chose "beige fonce" which is basically a darker beige shade, and it matched my skin tone perfectly! So surprised because I honestly thought I had picked the wrong color. I'm a light-medium skin tone, more on the medium side right now since it's summer, with neutral undertones and this foundation was the most perfect match.

I was a little disappointed in the size of the foundation, but a little goes a long way and I've barely made a noticeable dent in this foundation since I got it, which is great. It smells like fruits inside the container, but it doesn't transfer when you apply it to your skin. Didn't break me out or irritate my skin either, and I can have sensitive skin to certain things at times.

I would suggest applying this with a beauty blender or some sort of blending sponge for smooth application, and it'll make your foundation look like your skin. I used a Real Techniques blending sponge and it worked out perfectly. I have dry skin around my lips and it did cling to that a little bit, so I suggest moisturizing before applying this. But this did not settle into my fine lines nor did it look cakey on my face. My mom said she couldn't even tell I was wearing foundation! This is definitely light coverage, and it can be buildable to medium coverage. I have redness on my cheeks (rosacea) and this did not completely hide the redness, but did tone it down enough for me personally.

A lot of people have complained about the longevity of this foundation in reviews I've seen or read, but I think you just have to use a good primer, apply with a blending sponge, and set your face with a good powder. I had no issues with this foundation rubbing off or fading throughout the course of the night (and I'm in the always-humid weather of Florida). When I got home, everything was still in place (I used the Marc Jacobs coconut primer and the NYX HD translucent powder to set my face).

Overall, I highly recommend this foundation for any skin type. I think it works great and leaves a slightly dewy finish that you can mattify with a matte setting spray or powder for those of you who are oilier. Shipping was quick, no issues with that. I will suggest to watch the price of this as it does fluctuate a lot. I had seen this in fall of 2015 going for around $30, and I bought it for less than $20 in May. So if the price seems like too much, just wait it out. The biggest issue you'll have is guessing your shade, so look up swatches of the different shades and see which one would best match you. That's my best advice. But great foundation and so cheap, wish it was available in stores in America!

title: Fantastic fit and favorite pair yet
text:
This is my third pair of Bluetooth Sony earbuds that I have used primarily for running/exercising/walking with and each time Sony has made iterative improvements to its design to the point that these are the absolute best yet. These things will not fall out of your ears, period. The set I had before (MDRAS600BT) were also very good at this, though they did not feel nearly as secure as these do - the way they fit you can tell they are absolutely not going anywhere. They filter out a decent bit of noise as well which is a bonus when at the gym or running/walking near busier areas. The battery life is absolutely outstanding - I'll usually use them 2-3 times for an hour or two at a time and then charge them and don't have any issues.

They are not kidding that these are heavy on the bass - sometimes almost too much for my liking since I came from the MDRAS600BT and before that the MDRAS800BT, which had the tendency to have a slightly more neutral sound to them. However, even though these have heavy bass they have outstanding clarity to them - songs that are lighter on bass still sound fantastic, and if you are like me and prefer less bass you can always play around with an equalizer to get them sounding to your liking. The bottom line is these have great potential and bass is as advertised.

It's easy to look at what's available for $20-30 on Amazon and write these off. I understand the design might also be a turn-off for some, but i've come to prefer it for the ability to quickly change a song, pause your music and adjust the volume without reaching for your phone. The bottom line is these are well worth spending the extra money for great build quality, battery life, access to music controls, and most importantly fit and clear sound.

title: Super simple control circuit for DOS, Windows, Linux, or Macs - great for sprinklers or resetting low pwr Appliances.
text: It arrived in an outer sealed consumer shelf ziplock bag, and inside an inner silver static protection bag. A mini cdrom was included with the drivers and software on it.The design dates from 2013 and has the more reliable USB to Serial converter chip CH340 on it, since FTDI released drivers that bricked Third party clones of their chip.. rendering the entire FTDI market suspect.. you never know if you have a 'safe' USB to Serial chip or are one step away from being bricked by a Windows Driver update with the official FTDI driver. The instructions are unfortunately in Chinese, and some of the file names are also in unicode which breaks up on display in many English operating systems. There are two chips these days the CH340 and the CH341 (the more advanced) they have several modes of operation, but this implementation is as a simple Relay over a USB port connection, Windows will install the driver on XP, W7, W8, W10 and produce a COM port, which any terminal software can then address and send commands. The command strings are well known and similar to old fashioned modem commands. Which say On/Off to throw the relay. The three terminals are NC, C, NO for normally closed, common and normally open. Throwing the switch relay with a command from software enables make or break of an electrical circuit using the relay and a switch. There are also programs for MSDOS, Linux and MacOSX which will recognize the USB device as a HID and spawn a serial port which can be controlled with the same commands.. so its close to universal. These can be sourced at lower cost but then you must pay extra for shipping and find the software for yourself online.. which is not easy since it is scattered. This was a very convenient way to find a USB relay controller at a very low price with software. The amperage ratings and voltages are also fairly broad at 10 A and 30v DC and up to 250v AC but i would be cautious about inductive feedback spikes upstream if you use this as a switch, the relay is housed in a small blue plastic block which can't disappate much heat.. and is certainly not anti-spark rated.. be sure to full understand the implications of disconnecting a large current flow, or the arcing that might occur in an upstream circuit when cutting a high voltage circuit.. in other words.. don't use this to switch a Horizontal Flyback Transformer, Van De Graff Generator.. or F.lux Capacitor!

title: Unique speaker boosts volume on your phone or laptop with decent sound quality. No muss, no fuss.
text: Finally! Hats off to Leadsound for being the first company to make a quality version of this type of mini-speaker (there's a super cheopo speaker of this type (white and t-shaped) that's been on the market for years and it is totally useless). By "this type," I mean a tiny speaker that has no cords and connects directly to a laptop or phone by simply plugging it into the head phone jack -- it basically becomes an extension of the laptop or phone. It's true, that you're not going to host a rave with this thing or even totally "rock out" in your living room, but considering it's size, it delivers a decent sound for situations where you need a super portable, super simple speaker. I use it for two things: 1) boosting the volume on my laptop. Even at full volume, the speakers on my lap top are weak. Sometimes while listening to a video, I find myself straining to hear. This solves the problem -- I started by buying one to make sure it worked well (and it does -- way better than I expected). Now I bought a second one and I simply roatate them -- one is charging while I'm using the other. I just swap them out about once a day. 2) I use this for listening to audiobooks and podcasts while doing the dishes -- it boosts the volume of the phone enough so I can hear the audio over the running water. So you might ask, "Why not use a mini-bluetooth speaker" -- those have their place, and I have used them in the past for both of the applications I described -- but bluetooth is notoriously "fussy" (at least for me). Every so often the bluetooth cuts out or won't connect without repairing, etc. I've also used mini-speakers that connect via a cord, but that is not as clean and simple a solution as this speaker -- with this little guy, you just plug him in and "bam" he works and you can carry you phone with you while you listen! A couple other notes -- one reviewer mentioned a short battery life. I feel for him, but that hasn't been my experience -- maybe I listen on a lower volume. I haven't actually "clocked" the battery life, but it seems to go at least several hours -- long enough for my purposes. Another reviewer mentioned that if there is no input for a few minutes you have to turn it back on. That's how I use it so the batteries last longer. But if you don't like that, you can override the "battery-save" mode, by pushing and holding the on button for several seconds when you turn it on. This speaker has a real quaility feel -- as soon as you pick it up, you can tell it's well made. I especially like the on/off button which is a big push button that basically covers the whole bottom of the unit -- it has a super cool, quality feel. You might think this seems a little pricey for such a small speaker, but it's definitely worth it. This would also make a unique gift to anyone who listens to audiobooks or who travels a lot and would like a tiny speaker to use in their hotel room just to give them a little better sound and volume than their phone alone.

title: Outstanding Fitness In-Ear Buds
text:
Over the last couple of years I’ve bought and tried several sets of wired lightweight portable headphones, Bluetooth headphones, Bluetooth bone-induction headphones, wired in ear monitors, Bluetooth in ear monitors, and inexpensive wireless Bluetooth in ear monitors for use while working out but nothing that I liked using in that role well enough to keep using them for workouts. Some of them sounded awful, some sounded really good, some even sounded phenomenal, but the good ones either were either uncomfortable, inconvenient (the wired sets), fragile, or kept falling off or out of my ears.

I’d just about given up on good quality workout tunes when Amazon asked me to try out Jabra’s Elite Sport True Wireless Waterproof Fitness & Running Earbuds. The Jabra’s were a very pleasant surprise. No, they aren’t the smallest truly wireless Bluetooth in ear monitors but they are by far the best sounding that I’ve tried. No, they aren’t what audiophiles refer to as “critical listening” headphones, headphones that they’d spend hours and hours using to soak up every detail and nuance from the music, but they still sound really-really good. The sound is like what you’d expect from closed back wired headphones, that is the music sounds like it’s inside your head with plenty of power behind it. As you would expect at this price point, the highs are all there and crystal clear, mids are well balanced and do justice to the vocals, and as long as you select tight but comfortable inserts from the included options, all the bass that you’d expect is there in spades. In-ear-monitors depend on a good seal between the in-ear inserts and your ear canal to reproduce good solid bass and these do a fine job of it. As a bonus, the fit of the insert combined with the shape of the Jabra Elites means that they do not fall out even while running. In fact, if fitted properly, they take some effort to remove from your ears.

The Jabra Elite Sports are dedicated workout headphone and not only do they stay in your ears, but for safety reasons they allow you to hear what’s going on around you. If you are looking for total isolation these aren’t the buds for you. Personally, I think it’s pretty important to be able to hear traffic noises while running. As a smartphone headset they also provide a pretty decent microphone for phone conversations.

So far so good, however there is one feature that I did not like. As workout devices the Jabra Sport Elites include a biomonitoring function. When used in conjunction with Jabra’s Android workout apps (2 apps working together) they monitor your heart rate. I found the application to be badly written. It’s a pain to setup unless you were born in 1987 (changing years is a sloooooooooow one month at a time chore) and it nags while in use. I own a good fitness band and for now its job is safe. This is the one and only reason that I’m taking off a star and if they fix it and they can have their 5th star. They sound great and battery life is plenty long enough to last through any workout or run that I can survive. The bottom line is that as fitness headphones/in-ear-monitors I love these things!

text: I ordered a 6-pack of these items back in September 2016 to be gifts for family and friends at Christmas, and a couple for myself.  Up until January 20, 2017 I had no problem with my devices.  But on that day one went unresponsive and the blue light would spin for a few seconds, then go out, then light up again and start spinning.  It continued this cycle non-stop for hours.  I attempted to reset the device a few times with no success.  Finally I unregistered the device from my Alexa app at which point I could go through setup again on the device.  Got it setup again and was playing music through it again.  I asked Alexa to pause while I went and run some errands.  Upon returning, the device was spinning the blue circle again.  I called Amazon customer help, who then connected me to tech support for the echo.  The tech looked up my account and said I only had 1 day left on my warranty.  For this device they are allowing me to send it back to be checked out and either repaired or replaced.  I asked about the other devices, which a couple are still unopened and not registered, but the tech said that the warranty will expire on them all at the same time.  So, if any of the unregistered, never been used, devices have problems, they are essentially $50 bricks.  Beware that the warranty begins the day that you place the order on these from Amazon.  I like the Echo Dot (actually love it) but the fact that the warranty is ending before a few of the devices have even been registered really irritates me.

I am a professional photographer with 20 years in the business. I bought this based on the favorable reviews and used the case this summer (2015) in Hawaii. I checked for leaks like instructed. Used in a pool for about 15 minutes. All was good. Then I went snorkeling for about an hour in which time a very small hole in the case had the time to leak in enough water to destroy my camera.

I treat my equipment very well. This camera was in "excellent" condition. This included the case since I knew I was going to be relying on it to protect my camera and lens. Yes, I could have bought a professional housing, but I was doing this for fun and hope to get some stock images during my vacation.

This is what the company said (in summary) when I finally got their report back from South Korea. They determined after doing their test that the leak was my fault. One reason was given that my camera was too big and that I should have been using their bigger case. Silly. The 5D Mark II had almost too much room! The second reason is more reasonable. The very small hole they found was close to the top of the lens tube. Not on a seam. Again, I treat my equipment very well and looked after this case before using. So, if it was me and not a hole made during the making of and packing into the original box. Then this case is so fragile that it does not stand up to normal (even kid glove) use.

title: Easily Fix Bent Pins in the Belkin Compact Flash Card Reader
text:
I have the Belkin FCR-H53 multi-card reader, but these instructions will probably work for similar models.

The FCR-H53 reader is fast and convenient. It reads and writes at USB 3.0 speeds, and can deal with more than one card at a time (for example, transfer files from an SD card to a CF card)., which not all readers can do.

I use my reader exclusively for compact flash cards and SD cards—mostly for compact flash.

The big problem, which many people comment on, is that the pins inside the compact flash slot are easily bent, which can render that slot useless. The pins are quite long (in order to penetrate the sockets in the cf card), they're thin, and the insertion slot in the reader is not shaped precisely enough to keep the card perfectly positioned as it is inserted. The result is bent pins. Note that some CF cards have beveled pin sockets, which help direct the pins into the hole, while others have just sharp-edged holes that are more demanding of a precisely aligned insertion.

The attached image shows how to open the case (a very simple operation) and how to straighten the pins.

Even if your Belkin reader does not have bent pins, you might do well to follow the instructions to keep the case open, so that you can visually ensure the card is inserted exactly right every time. This may sound tedious, but it's not. It will take you only 2-3 seconds extra when inserting the card, and you'll have a fast, useful, moderately priced reader that should last many years.

title: Small learning curve, amazing quality, LOTS of fun!
text:
I'm not sure I could more clearly love this camera. I purchased this camera after looking for an excuse to buy a nice camera for a long time. When the opportunity arrived for me to teach our school yearbook class, it was time for me to learn how to take good photos. There are plenty of comprehensive reviews on here... so I will just addressed why I pulled the trigger on this purchase, and why I'm so happy with it.

For starters, I FIRMLY believe this camera is the best bang for your buck you can possibly get in DSLR or mirrorless at the time of this review. In fact, I've noticed the price just dropped this month. Like many of you reading this, I've spent COUNTLESS hours doing research to be sure this big purchase was the right one. I knew I'd use the camera semi-professionally, and needed it to meet criteria that allowed it to be effective in low light and take rapid shots to capture the action of the kids I work with. The a6000 was the clear winner despite a suggestion from a family member who has a cheaper model Sony mirrorless. After comparing the two... I'm FIRMLY convinced I made the perfect decision for me.

I use this camera primarily to take pictures of the kids at our school, and that includes our middle school sports program. At 11 shots per second... I don't miss a beat. I've caught some incredible photos of our kids, and the parents and school community are buzzing about the awesome impact these cool photos have on our ability to create a buzz around campus. One of the parents on campus is a professional photographer, and when she was taking photos next to me at our annual winter concert she looked at my photos and was stunned that I was not only getting photos on par with the quality of her pro DSLR setup, but that some of the low-light photos even came out BETTER.

I'm using nothing so far besides the kit lens and 50-210mm lense. Though I plan to upgrade to a strong fixed lens soon.

Quick heads up... the Wasabi battery pack isn't just important, it's ESSENTIAL. This camera sucks battery like crazy, but you should be able to go three to four hours of HEAVY shooting on 2 or 3 batteries. With that said, the Wasabi batteries also have a larger capacity than the Sony batteries, so I use them more often anyways.

The only other minor gripe I have about the camera is the sensor that detects your eye at the viewfinder (and shuts off the LCD display) is crazy sensitive. But that's super minor compared to what feels to me like the best big dollar purchase I may have ever made.

Get a good book to teach you this camera, spend a small amount of time on it, and you won't believe the quality photos you get out of it.

title: dsr250 - port forwarding and static route not working
text:
I have been using a dlink dir825 (with latest dlink firmware) as the gateway to my home lan, sitting between my ISP gateway and my lan. The dir 825 worked perfectly, except it could not do static routing on the lan (it is limited to static on the wan). I purchased the dsr-250 so I could do static lan routing.

My home lan uses only dlink products ( 16 ip cameras, 3 wireless AC routers in addition to the dir825, 2 additional dir825 with dd-wrt providing vpn service, and dlink switches.) I run a Linux server with DNS and web servers. I have considerable experience with this technology, especially dlink products.

After installing the latest firmware 2.11_ww (mine was hardware ver A3 - it was not easy finding firmware for the A3 on the dlink web site), I programmed the dsr-250 in a manner just as the dir825 was programmed, making changes for the router interface differences. I use extensive port forwarding for the cameras and the dns & web servers, as well as a couple VPN servers and clients.) It is a little complex, but not extreme.

Once I placed the dsr250 in service with all of the settings matching the dir825 (I did not add the static routing at first), the unit worked correctly except for port forwarding. The "standard services" ftp and dns worked perfectly. However the standard http service did not work reliably. When I booted the dsr250 the http (access from outside the home) would work for a few minutes, then it would quit working till re-booted. It would then do the same thing - work a few minutes and then stop (this problem only occurred when connecting to http from outside the home.)

None of custom services I programmed (primarily for IP cameras, and vpn access) would work. They never worked. I programmed these like I have done on other dlink products and like I did on the ISP gateway. I also compared my settings to the dlink web instructions for port forwarding, as well as other instructions I found on the internet. My settings matched every reference I lookup at. It just did not work. I tried several variations on the settings and nothing worked. Without changing any settings, I hooked the dir825 gateway back up and removed the dsr250, and everything worked immediately, just as it should. Clearly a dsr250 issue.

I then tried setting up 1 lan static route. When I first set it up, it worked immediately. After the first dsr250 re-boot it never worked again. I tried several things including removing and re-entering the static route. It never worked again.

I worked on this for 3 days straight - about 30 hours. I tried hard resets, re-flashing firmware, followed by hard resets, reloading saved config files. Nothing would fix the forwarding or static route.

It would be well to mention that when I accessed the dsr250 web page using ie11 (windows 10) the web page certificate was not valid, so I had to override the exception every time I accessed the dsr250. Not a big deal, but not good.

I think the firmware on this product is not ready for prime time. It is not robust, and I think it is buggy based on my observations, especially the http port forwarding and static routing.

I still need a device that does lan static routing.

Given the size of the driver and the weight of the speaker this lack of volume is very hard to understand. This is a great speaker if you are going to listen to it at your desk while you are sitting at your desk next to the speaker or if you normally listen to speakers at low volume.  Another negative, as mentioned earlier, given the great weight of the speaker it is not very portable.  This is not a speaker you are going to throw in your travel bag for the weekend, you will need another bag for the speaker.  I wish I could give this a better rating as I really like Polk as a manufacturer, but I was disappointed by the compromises present in the design of this model.

title: Easy setup with one quirk
text:
Kind of a pain to set up with my modem but it's NOT the ERX's fault. I bought a Netgear CM1000 modem because it works with Comcast and does not have the faulty Intel puma Chip, it has a Broadcom. When setting up the ERX it didn't want to grab an IP from the CM1000. To get a successful connection I did the following
1) Plug PC into ETH0
2) Configure PC for the following:
a) static IP 192.168.1.10
b) subnet 255.255.255.0
c) default gateway 192.168.1.1
d) dns empty
3) navigate to 192.168.1.1 in a browser
4) go to wizards page on right
5) Select WAN+2LAN2 on left and configure for ETH0, DHCP, One LAN, created new user and password
6) Save settings and reboot the router
7) Plug PC into ETH1 while router is rebooting
8) Plug modem into ETH0 while router is rebooting
9) Set PC back to DHCP, automatic IP address
10) Let ERX boot back up and reconnect, sometimes I had to disable and re enable LAN connection in windows 10 in order to connect back to 192.168.1.1
11) If you have internet then great, in my case I did not
12) The fix for me was to reboot the modem, left unplugged for 3-4min. Quick 20 second reboots didn't work for some reason.
13) After about 1 minute the modem booted up and the ERX automatically grabbed the external IP
14) Internet!

As far as performance, with the ERX and a 2x Ubiquiti UAP AC PRO I'm pulling down 250mbps over WiFi, no saturation. Pretty happy so far

I'm at a loss to explain why these cans get such rave reviews. They have almost no high end. There's no "air" in them to give a sense of space to instruments and to fill out the tone of individual instruments. They leave out a big chunk of auditory information. If you listen to live recordings where you're used to hearing a bit of natural echo or reverb from the venue, you're not going to hear those cues through the ATH-M50x's. They make live recordings sound almost like they were recorded direct into the mixing board because so much of the top end is rolled off. The bass is pretty prominent but not especially tight. Whatever style of music you enjoy, I just don't see how the sound signature of these things could be particularly enjoyable to anyone. I don't get it.

If you like to hear soundstage and upper end detail, then I'd recommend avoiding these. If you want booming bass and don't care too much about anything else, then these will work just fine.

title: On My Second Unit - First one lasted over 3 years = Same Issues as Others Killed the First = H20
text:
As stated in my headline: I purchased my first 50002 unit approximately 3 year ago. I had my mechanic install the system.
The first unit worked awesome. I've give it 5 stars out of 5 stars. It functioned flawlessly (going on when the truck was put into reverse + VERY clear picture with super detail & definition. It looked and worked (at least to me) = just as good as any factory back-up camera on a brand new truck.

So, after 3 + years, the first camera started working intermittently (that can be a first sign or red flag of moisture issues being present).

I did some reading (on here) about what others were experiencing with water getting into it.

So I ordered another (my second) 50002 camera.
When it came, I simply un-plugged the old panel with the old camera and removed it from the license plate area. I plugged in the new one and = sure enough, all was working again in 5 minutes.

I opened up the old one (panel) and it looked just like the other pictures on here, with water in it, and rusted and corroded PC board electronics (including a capacitor that was completely rusted off and fell out when I removed the back panel cover).

THIS TIME = With the new panel and cover, I siliconed everything (where the wiring goes in, and along all the seams. IT IS VERY VERY IMPORTANT THAT YOU DO THIS = Seal the panel completely !!!!!
(Another step may be to also spray a liquid sealer over the entire panel exterior).

ALSO = When you are installing the license plate onto the panel, and then all of it onto the license plate area, the wires coming out of the camera panel will move around at the base where they come into the panel (even if you have pre-siliconed them). So you will need to re-apply more silicone during the new license plate location install process (make sure you do this thoroughly around any wires going into the panel).

I really like this camera and this system. Again, I give it 5 out of 5 stars for its operation, but my rating here is 4 out of 5 stars because of this design flaw. So make sure that you do these sealing modifications and you will be very happy with it.

title: Good Hub for Media, Half-Baked Home Automation Support.
text:
It's a good hub, and serves admirably replacing the functions of my old Harmony Link, but not much else. I'm a bit bitter that it is necessary, however. The Harmony Link has been working fine for years, and then a software update to the mobile app basically obsoleted the thing for no reason. I stuck with the old app for a while, and decided to make the jump because of SmartThings integration for home automation.

The new app is much cleaner, and seems to run faster as well. I also really appreciate the incorporation of a bluetooth radio, which works fantastically with my Fire TV. Prior to the upgrade, I had to use a clunky USB IR Receiver to bridge the gap, and this is way better.

However, the reason I made the switch was for the home automation integration, and it's definitely half-baked. I was able to get Harmony to control my SmartThings devices, but not the other way around, even though that's an advertised feature. After a bit of research and some emails to tech support, it appears that the issue is definitely on Logitech's side.

Furthermore, what you can actually do with the HA stuff is very limited: You can control your devices manually in the Harmony app, which really accomplishes nothing, since you can do that from the HA system's app. Also, you can add commands to the start up and shut down sequences of activities, which sounds great, but is really limited.

Here's what you CANNOT do: You can't add a shortcut button for any HA item to the remote for an activity. For instance, I can't add a button to dim the lights to my "Watch a Movie" activity. In order to do that, I must exit the activity, go the the "Devices" menu, select the each light I want to change individually, open the menu for that light, and manually dim it, then go on to the next one, before returning to the "Activity" menu to press play. Also, macros do not work with HA devices. I thought it would be really cool if the lights would automatically dim when I press "Play" and brighten when I press "Pause." This functionality is only a few lines of code away from being a reality, but it's IMPOSSIBLE to do with the current software. I confirmed this with Harmony support.

I'm really hopeful that these issues all get hammered out, since I don't have any complaints that can't be fixed with a software update. However, given Logitech's history, I'm a bit concerned that they'll just release a new hub with this functionality completed and phase mine out in a year or two. They advertise SmartThings support on the box. Support it.

title: Not Getting 5.1 Surround? It's a selection confirmation problem...read on.
text:
I've had this unit for 9 months now and while I'm not one to write reviews I do believe in helping others when I can. That said, I happened to run into a help me post on another site and realized after some investigation that as great as this sound bar is, like most products it has flaws, convoluted steps and outright disastrous "workings" that make it prone to easy connection mistakes.

One such issue that I've read many complaints and issues with is getting a surround sound connection with devices/apps/media players, not limited to but including Netflix, PS3/ PS4, Amazon Fire, etc... There at times seems to be infinite connections and ways to connect devices, I'm lucky enough that I tinker to no end. All that said, every manual will give you several straight forward connection choices and regardless of which you choose (barring equipment and cable failures) they should all work if not at least one will work. Here's the thing, this particular Vizio soundbar has what I consider a deceptive and fatal error when it comes to surround; an error that stems from bad or rather sloppy implementation of an otherwise straight forward set up.

First the remote as I'm sure you've read leaves a lot to be desired and could at the least be back lit and offer some form of beep (adjustable on/off) to confirm whatever setting you've just changed. Secondly, no onscreen visual cues only makes the beep more necessary. Yes the visual cues with lights is a simple and fantastic method of confirming a choice but as you will see is deceptive as hell. Third, it has an odd way of confirming choices you've selected through the remote and on thru the soundbar itself.

So what's the issue? Well, as other reviewers have mentioned more subtly in their reviews, their is a selection on the remote to turn SURROUND ON/OFF. As with all selections turning this on / off will engage or disengage your 5.1 surround on every medium and device (Netflix, PS3, etc) . No matter how you've connected your device, this little trigger controls your access to surround greatness. Some have implied that it's a line of sight issue(that the ON trigger actually takes place) when changing the Surround ON/OFF; I do agree line of sight is important however it's also a mftr. programming/false confirmation of the change. Please let me explain. I only emphasize the utter importance of this "ON/OFF confirmation" to point out it's glearing flaw. A top reviewer also points out how upon almost returning their bar he stumbled upon the Surround ON/OFF not correctly switching to the desired selection. Of course he is dead right, but a small detail that I did not read elsewhere is that it's not so much a line of sight issue or that the switch to ON/OFF is not correctly taking place. It is in fact that the switch from OFF to ON(or even vice-versa) requires at least 2 pushes on the arrow button to properly register. Yes 2+ full pushes to ensure the change from ON/OFF et al. With that, I would add that the line of sight doesn't seem to change that at all in terms of false or missed signal registers; of course line of sight will guarantee that all your selections are registered to begin with.

For the record this confirmation (middle 4 lights) seems to apply to the selection of all settings.. surround being the most obvious because you can literally hear whether it's been engaged to on or not. Other settings are just not as obvious.

So what happens is.. when you switch the surround OFF, the top and bottom 4 lights signify it's OFF. Once the lights fade or If you leave that setting and come back to it, pushing the setting to ON will give you another set of 4 top and bottom lights with the SURROUND ON showing on the display which leads you to believe the SURROUND ON has been activated..IT HAS NOT. The activation has only taken place when the MIDDLE 4 lights show very brightly. The 4 top and bottom lights initially show which can be deceptive. To reiterate, this false confirmation of SURROUND ON seems to happen only if you leave the setting after turning the surround off. If you stay in the surround setting toggling between off and on, this doesn't seem to be the case. The ON/OFF will toggle correctly. This only seems to occur after you've left the selection screen and go back to change the setting to ON (or OFF) for that matter.

So again, just because the remote is showing SURROUND ON, does not mean it is in fact on. Push the selector right again (2+ pushes might be necessary) to get those middle center lights confirmation to show. The display on the remote will not change from SURROUND ON (assuming you pushed the arrow once already to change the selection), but the 5.1 surround will in fact be engaged with this small yet stupid extra confirmation step. This kind of unintentional error or rather, programmed deception I'm sure has caused countless returns and customer service calls with complaints of non-functioning Surround units. This may also apply to any other Vizio bars that require similar steps and this remote.

So the 4 bottom / top lights showing appears to be purposeful as a means of showing the remote is engaged with the box, with the top and bottom 4 lights showing a rudimentary connection with the remote. But the display showing a setting that is "ON", when it is in fact still OFF, that's a whole other misleading programming issue by itself. Remote law (yes this is probably real somewhere in the internet) dictates "When I press to change a setting to ON the remote and the lights will come on, and the display/visual setting updates to "ON". That should confirm the setting is ON, I shouldn't have to push the same setting change again to get a whole other set of lights to show, which then make the actual change, all the while the display stays exactly as it was showing already "ON".

Hope I explained that correctly and didn't confuse anyone further. In an attempt to explain the smaller yet important aspects of this "error"? I hope I was able to help and not over-share less pertinent information that seemed important at the time.

Hope this helped!

title: Disappointing.
text:
I have been looking forward to earbuds like these for quite a while. I have wanted the comfort of earbuds coupled with the convenience of bluetooth, and when I saw these I was pretty excited. Then I got them, and now I'm pretty disappointed.

First, the positives. They are comfortable. I have a pair of Skullcandy bluetooth headphones, and they're great, but they aren't earbuds, and they get hot on my head. These are much cooler, and more comfortable, They're more comfortable than my other wired headphones, including my favorite Panasonic LUXE earbuds (RP-HJX21M-K) earbuds. So there's a point in their favor.

But the sound is what is important in headphones and earbuds, and the NuForce earbuds don't quite deliver. As other reviewers have mentioned, the bass is virtually nonexistent. Coomparing them with my Skullcandy headphones showed me a BIG difference, with the headphones winning out over the earbuds. Factor in that the headphones are only $42 right now, and you'll see where my disappointment starts.

Then I compared them to my other earbuds. The LUXE earbuds blew them out of the water -- FAR superior sound quality. In fact, I had to go to a pair of $16 Altec Lansing earbuds to find similar sound quality to these headphones. VERY disappointing. I've tried them with an Android phone and an Ipad -- same results, same comparisons.

I'll wear these while mowing the lawn, or walking/hiking/disc golfing. They are good for exercise because they're light and comfortable. But for daily use? I've got other, FAR superior headphones that I'll be using. I'm not an audiophile, I'm not that picky, but there's a difference between these and my other earbuds that should NOT be there given the price, and isn't really because they're bluetooth. Three stars is kind of generous for these, but I can't do half stars.

text:
I purchased this AVR to replace a Denon from 2007. The main reasons for the upgrades were this receiver's ability to pass through 4K video, and its integrated HEOS system. I plugged a Cat5 cable directly into the unit, for speed and reliability. The GUI (graphical user interface) is vastly improved over the prior receiver, with the whole process only taking about 15 minutes, including a three-point audio calibration. Simple, and easy. At first, I was using a 2-year old 25-foot long HDMI cable with my new projector and the 4300H, and it would simply not pass any signal through to the projector (No Signal message). After replacing the cable with a shorter (20-foot), new cable, I've had no problems with the image being passed through. I absolutely love being able to run HEOS off my tablet or phone, and the ability to sync multiple zones. I would highly recommend an all-in-one remote to operate even moderately complex systems. Sound is awesome. Highly recommended.

EDIT: I've been using this AVR for a few years, and mostly love it. I have two other HEOS speakers at home. The HEOS app for iOS is buggy, at best. The three HEOS devices (AVR, two stand-alone speakers) don't always show up. HEOS is often unable to play music. If there's a software update, you'll have to wait to play music until it installs. I don't h ave experience with Sonos or other streaming speakers other than Yamaha. If they would fix the HEOS problems, then I could unabashedly give this 5 stars.

title: Pleasantly Surprised
text:
I've been doing some renovating, and haven't had much time to experiment with this projector, but the limited time I have had with it has been excellent. Bonus for the fact that after a visit, my brother was convinced to buy one, with no persuading of my own.(He uses it regularly, and has thoroughly enjoyed the purchase so far.)

The Image:

The image this thing provides is nice, large, and clear. I've tried everything on it, games, anime, TV, and movies. They all looks great, and will definitely provide an exciting experience if it's your first step into projecting.(Up until this review, I had been projecting on the wall, which is a cool slate color, and still got great results)

The Sound:

Yes, this projector is a little noisy. For any gamers reading this, think the original Xbox 360. For non-gamers, if you focus on the sound, it'll bother you, but otherwise it'll just fade into the background. In terms of audio output, I can't say. I have an external setup.

Potentially Bad News:

If you want to hook this up to your computer you may be out of luck. My laptop just has VGA, and that's the one thing that doesn't seem to work. I'm not sure how nicely a converter will work, but that may be my only option.

Final Thoughts:

If you're just getting into projecting this is a solid purchase. If you're getting this expecting the quality of a $500+ projector, you're probably going to be disappointed.

Bonus Info:

When I first took this out and turned it on, the image was blurry. I very delicately tried twisting the lens, but nothing happened. I referenced the manual, which isn't that great, and tried to work my way around the menus. I've seen other people comment about this, and not get any answers so i was beginning to think I got a defect. If this happens to you, just twist the lens. It's a little stiff.

Update: 4/25/16

It still works amazingly (for the most part). I use it almost daily, and haven't experienced anything too bad. I've been using it without the sound bar for a while, and the audio is surprisingly good. Doesn't beat an external setup, but better than I imagined.

The Issue:

Occasionally, the projector is unresponsive. Press the power button on the remote? No response. The button on the projector? Nope. If you leave it as is it may take awhile. But if you switch of the power and unplug it, the plug it back in and try powering it up, it usually cranks up in a few minutes. It's only happened a few times, so I'm not that torn up about it, but it's a little obnoxious.

title: Poorly designed leg extension/retraction causing constant problems...Manfrotto needs to do some serious re-designing...
text:
This is my second Manfrotto tripod, and I don't like having to say this, but I am extremely disappointed with this product. For an expensive (for me) tripod, the internal sliding mechanism for extending/retracting the legs is pathetic. I was out shooting the milky way in the middle of the night in the deserts of southern Baja about one month after receiving this product. One of the legs would not slide back in. It was sticking, and after a bit of jiggling it finally retracted. I changed locations and went to set up the tripod, and the same leg was very difficult to extend, and then came completely out. Luckily it was very quiet and I heard something land on the ground near my feet. I found two small pieces of plastic that had fallen out of the cylinder.

See attached photos.

I finally figured out that the two little plastic pieces set into two small recessed holes on each side of the leg, then the leg inserts with the groove created by the two pieces of plastic aligning with a slight metal lip inside the leg. Now this is a recurring problem. The plastic pieces will not stay in their little holes while sliding in/out, the leg sticks, I have to dis-assemble it, put the little plastic pieces back in their little holes and put it back together. This occurs almost every shoot. The other two legs also are sticky, but I am extremely careful with them (I shouldn't have to be) hoping to avoid the same problem happening with them.

As I said, I am currently in Mexico doing volunteer work and photography for a sea turtle rescue organization in the middle of nowhere...Not conducive to returning what I thought would be a "bullet proof" tripod from a respected manufacturer. By the time I get back to civilization, it will be too late to return this...!

title: Monster performance, damsel looks
text:
First of all I've been using a Desktop for the last 2 years so when I decided to buy I laptop I didn't want a downgrade on performance. Normally I would make a build of a computer with the price that a laptop would cost to balance out how each component measured. The build I did was as expensive as the laptop and the big difference was the processor which was overclock-able. This is by far of the best if not the best ratio of a laptop against a desktop. Needless to say I've loved this laptop, the benchmarks are great and the jump from a 60hz monitor to a 144hz one is massive.

Pros
- Absolutely mad performance. Will run most, if not all games on max settings at 60fps or more.
- The laptop is gorgeous. The design is very clean, and subtle. You'll be able to bring this to a Starbucks and no one will notice it is a gaming laptop.
- No MLG 420 red all over the place like most earlier Asus gaming laptops models.
- PCIExpress is on the 99th percentile of storage right now, with some tweaks the laptop will boot up in less than 5 seconds.
- Webcam, speakers and track pad are all very good (Even though you are never probably using them).
- Connectivity is on point, the A/C outlet is on a comfortable spot and there is ample adapters for a mouse, headphones and more.

Cons
- The material will get marks when used for more than a couple of minutes as your body temperature will make the material "foggy".
- A lot of bloatware that is difficult to get rid of, like most laptops have but I took a good 2 hours making sure everything was off the computer.
- Battery is sub-par with other gaming laptops (that are not running a 144hz screen).
- Fans WILL get loud. When pushing the laptop to its limits on intense games the fans will go ballistic, but this is something good as you know your CPU and GPU are being kept cold. If you are using headphones or earplugs the noise is barely noticeable though.

Recomendations
- Buy a cooling pad for long cpu/gpu intensive tasks sessions and try to keep your room dust free.
- Buy a backpack for laptops and buy a sleeve on top of that. The laptop feels delicate around the edges.

title: I've tried 'em all and this one is my favorite
text:
Over the last 2 years I have tried probably a dozen different Slimport adapters with a couple Nexus 4's and a Nexus 5. I've tried the cheapest adapters I could find (about $6) to some of the more expensive ones. I have even tried the Analogix "official" one that is $29. All of them suffer from one of two problems:

1. The audio and video cuts in and out. I see this a lot if the phone is switching from 3g to LTE to no service and vice versa.
2. A short in one of the wires. Eventually the adapters either stop charging the device or no longer display video. Sometimes twisting the cable a little will get it working again. Complete failure is inevitable at this point.

So far this Accell adapter has been the most reliable and consistent of all that I have tried (knock on wood). I do not know why it is so difficult to make a good Slimport adapter, but Accell seems to have got it right. I have this permanently hooked up to a Nexus 5 that I use for a few hours a week and it has worked flawlessly. I turn on the monitor and there is the display of the Nexus 5. Every single time. It doesn't work that way with the other adapters I've tried.

title: The New Reference Line delivers
text:
At the time of this review, I've had these speakers for 6 months and they are very good! Klipsch speakers are known for their efficiency, like all their speakers they are not power hungry so you won't need an amp to push these at all. These NEW Reference Line speakers (not to be confused with the New Reference Premiere) are replacing the Klipsch Icon and Synergy Line. Some say that the only thing that was done to these speakers was painting the cones copper like the previous Reference Line, which is so not the case! Not only was the horn tweeter upgraded delivering a wider sound stage, but the crossover was updated as well. The dual 8" woofers are still IMG, but the copper was spun tighter for better mid/bass response. The only reason I didn't give these speakers 5 stars is because I finally was able to hear the RP-260F/280F and the sound clarity and stage is much better! However these speakers hold their own very well and sound better than both the Icon and Synergy Line. They are available at Best Buy and Hhgreg and are the only Klipsch speakers available in store, as the others are only available online. Do not judge these speakers based on what they sound like in the store as the environment and setting is no where close to ideal.

The clarity of these speakers sound just as good at low volume as it does at high volume, especially after you've broken them in. I have them hooked up to a Denon X2100w. I really pushed these speakers, the highs are warm and not as bright as the previous models they are replacing, giving them a more clean and natural sound. The mids sound lush when it should be and does not dominate the rest of the sound. I have my low end "bass" going to a JL Audio E112 sub, which I shut off to test the speakers. If you don't own a sub the 8" drivers can hold their own very well no worries, though movies like Tron: Legacy at high volumes will have you looking to purchase a sub (JL Audio,SVS,HSU). I doubt you'd want to damage the drivers before their time but lets face it, you won't be playing these that loud without a sub! Gaming on the PS4 is much more immersive and now I can establish what direction sounds are coming from without the use of headphones. Blu-ray movies sound very clear, distinct and life-like in size, scale and weight, nothing is missing. Music is crisp, clean and detailed giving your ears the bliss they crave. These speakers won't disappoint you. The Klipsch R-28F are great for anyone wanting a mid range home theater, your getting a truly quality speaker!

title: Amazing balance of features for travel and amateur photography
text:
I purchased this camera after an incredible amount of research on many, many different cameras. I was looking for a large sensor camera anything above the 1" RX100's/G7x II/G5X while still maintaining a reasonably small size so the the camera would be travel friendly. Therefore, I limited myself to mirrorless cameras. I was also looking for the camera to have a number of features which I did not want to compromise on, which I will explain shortly. Like many of you reading this review, the Sony A6000 was definitely a contender for me. However, its lack of touchscreen to select focus points killed it for me. I do know there are various other ways to select focus, but me as well as others that would be using this camera are just too used to touch focus due to smartphone cameras. Additionally, I did play around with that camera and the menu system was not as intuitive as it was on Panasonic.Other contenders were the Olympus cameras, mainly the OMD E M5/M1/M10, as well

Going back to the GX85, it has ALL the features I would want in a larger sensor camera: compact size, a nice large articulating touch screen, a very respectable sensor size, electronic viewfinder, popup flash for the rare times its needed, a good selection of lenses, multiple dials to control settings, panorama mode, FIVE AXIS STABILIZATION!!! (combined with the in-body and lens stabilzations) and other filter/fun modes along with the traditional programmable settings.

I just got back from a trip to Alaska with this camera and I am very pleased with the shots. The camera functioned perfectly. I was happy with the quick on time, helping me capture many moments I would've missed on slower cameras. The stabilization in the camera BLEW me away. This was previously the advantage Olympus had over Panasonic, but with this camera, as long as you have an OIS lens to complement the in-body stabilzation, the stabilization is AMAZING. I was on a speedboat on a lake and I could clearly see how stable the image was in the viewfinder based compared to the choppy environment I was in. Truly amazing. The user interface was very very friendly. After an excursion, I was showing my group shots of a far off bear that I took. I was pleasantly surprised to find that one dial moved picture to picture and the other dial was zooming in. On top of that, after zooming in on a picture in playback mode, I could move to the next picture and the camera would stay zoomed in on that same area. Wow!! The camera focuses VERY quickly and takes the photo instantaneously.

That being said, a few tiny issues I had with the camera: Buttons are slightly small and difficult to press at first, but I quickly became used to pressing the buttons. My lens (12-60mm Panasonic) was splash and dust-proof, and there were moments I wished the camera body was as well, so I could have that extra sense of security around waterfalls etc. The touchscreen comes out a bit and articulates up and down, but not around to face forward for a selfie mode. I never thought I'd care about this, but I found myself wishing for it when I was kayaking and it was hard for anyone else to take photos of me. The forward facing screen would've helped frame the shots better. Finally, looking at the photos, it looks like many of my panorama photos have jagged edges/color variations throughout. It may be me not having a steady hand, but my panorama's with my iphone and A6000 I used to have did not have this issue. Could be fixed with a software update. All of these gripes are tiny and not enough to drop a star, especially compared to the other choices out there, which have major issues/missing features.

There are MANY features I didn't even get to try, such as the 4k video picture mode, to get photos before and after you press the shutter or something like that, as well as the ability to find the correct focus AFTER taking the shot. I'm truly impressed by the number of features Panasonic has crammed into this small camera. With other camera's, the smaller it gets, the more features that are lost. This was a camera that had everything I was looking for in a form factor slightly bigger than many point-and-shoot cameras.

title: Things to know before you buy
text:
My review for the Samsung QN65Q9FNAF
I spent weeks researching the best TV and I decided to purchase the top of the line: Samsung QLED -QN65Q9FNAF.
I have been around electronics all my life; I was a supervisor at a University’s audio visual department for 24 years; after having this TV for 2 weeks I can only give it a 3 star rating based on the following:

PICTURE:
The 65” picture is very, very good however it did not blow me away like I thought a Qled top of the line TV would.

SETUP AND OPERATION:
Setting up this TV is very confusing and basic operation is confusing; the TV does not come with a user manual so you must go on line to download it, I printed all 171 pages just to find out that it does not 7fully explain what you are doing when you follow the instructions. It shows you where certain settings are but that’s it, if you have several choices it does not tell you what each one does and trying to add other devices such as a DVD player and to make it recognize the device so confusing I had to call Samsung Technical Support to take control of the TV so they could set the TV to recognize the device.

REMOTE CONTROL:
The remote control is touted by Samsung as the only “ONE” remote that you will ever need for everything, well this is simply not true; the remote is small with about 10 function buttons on it, which is supposed to control your cable box and all devices connected to the TV, in order for it to control the cable box you must press a series of buttons on the remote and then select from the on screen menu, wow about ten steps , whereas on the cable box remote you have to only press one button! Needless to say I rather use the cable box remote control. In addition the Samsung remote cannot select certain functions for your Cable box, DVD player and I can’t find anywhere to control the Amazon Fire TV. I have a Harmony One remote that will not completely work with the Samsung QN65Q9FNAF. So now I am using 4 remote controls whereas I use to use only the Harmony One with my old TV.

AUDIO:
The built in speakers on this TV are absolutely TERRIBLE! Even when you find out how to make certain sound settings, it does not improve the audio. For a $4,000.00 television I expect quality audio from the TV speakers, not something tinny that sounds like a cheap speaker on an old transistor radio. I decided to hookup my old auxiliary amplifier receiver, which would not work; after talking with the amp’s manufacture (Sony) and Samsung Support (talked between the two support teams for 5 hours, it was then determine that the audio amp receiver system was incompatible with the Samsung TV. I decided to purchase a Yamaha sound bar, I could not get the new sound bar to work with the TV so I called Yamaha support, the tech. was very knowledgeable and even downloaded a copy of the Samsung QN65Q9FNAF manual to help with trying to get the sound bar to work with the TV he spent an hour on the phone with me trying to figure out how to make the TV recognized the sound bar, after trying various settings the TV still would not recognized the sound bar, he finally gave up and said I would have to call Samsung; the Samsung technical support took remote control of the TV and change a setting which made the TV recognize the sound bar, the settings he performed appears nowhere in the Samsung QN65Q9FNAF manual or online.

Samsung Support:
Samsung support for me was excellent, and I have spoken to a dozen or more support people, I like the fact that they can remotely take over the TV to find and resolve the problem.

I hope this review will help people with their decision on what TV to purchase.

title: Good quality sound without breaking the bank.
text:
Very good base sound from this unit that you can feel. I use it with my Samsung UN65HU8550 UHD 4K Smart TV. Hookup was easy using an Amazon brand TOSLINK fiber optic cable from the TV to the subwoofer unit. The remote control is a huge plus and I keep it next to my TV's remote control. I also have an AppleTV connected to its other optical input. The sound is very clean. Each pair of satellite speakers are adjustable relative to the others in the system both from the control unit and the remote control unit. You can, for example, increase/decrease the base, center channel, front left and right channels and rear channels independently relative to the rest. There is a general volume control that increases all channels. It has DSP settings for non-dolby digital source sources. It handles DTS-HD and AC3 5.1 and 2.0 perfectly. Actor dialog coming in from the center channel speakers are very clear. The sound is very strong without distortion. If you would like a great sounding surround sound system without having to spend lots of money on a separate 5.1 receiver and speakers, this system might be for you. I would recommend it for a small to the medium-sized livingroom.

I purchased this system when there was a sale on Amazon and during that time it was an exceptional value. My only wish would have been the speaker wires not to be black, but white, so they would be less noticeable on the walls. But I plan on replacing the wire soon. I also wished the rear speaker wire length were a few feet longer, but I will remedy that when I replace the speaker wires. Other than those two minor mentions, I really like the system.

I also found these mounting brackets perfectly suited to this speaker system. VideoSecu Universal Satellite Speaker Mounts / Brackets for Walls and Ceilings (White,Black Available) http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B002WNAFSU?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o09_s00

UPDATE 07/22/2019 ==================================================
I have owned this system for four years today and I am just as happy with them as I was in 2015. Recently I moved into a new home and had to take down the speakers from the wall. Since then I learned from researching the net that you get a better surround sound experience by having the speakers at ear level instead up high. Plus I didn't want to put holes in the new walls using the old mounting brackets that I mentioned earlier in this review. I found an excellent high-quality alternative using speaker stands that are perfectly compatible with the Z906 speakers. I purchased two pairs of Atlantic Adjustable Height Speaker Stands - Set of 2 Holds Satellite Speakers, Adjustable Stand Height from 27 to 48 inch, Heavy Duty Powder Coated Aluminum with Wire Management PN77305018 in Black https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B000289DC6/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

I can certainly appreciate the difference having the speakers at ear level and I highly recommend these stands because they are made from both cast iron and steel poles. I also would like to offer a tip to new users of the Z906 speakers. If you are installing them for the first time, the Logitech Z906 controller has a built-in pink test. No need to download a pink 5.1 audio test file off the web. When the system is on, simply hold down the [INPUT] button for 5 seconds and then let go. The controller will go into test mode by generating a tone in sequential order for all five channels in this order, Left Front, Center, Right Front, Right Rear, Left Rear, and Subwoofer. This will help guide you to make sure your rear surround sounds are wired correctly. Perhaps I overlooked this trick in the manual five years ago, but it really helped me a lot when I had to reinstall this system in my new living room. I hope that trick helps you too.

This is our third Kindle. We had the original, the Fire HD and now, the Paperwhite.

I thought the original was the greatest reading device ever made. The paperwhite is in itself a fantastic reading device as well but I really do miss the text-to-speech and Audible intergration. Being able to listen to my books during my commute and then have my kindle know exatly where the audio left off so that I can resume at that spot was a fantastic feature that I will sorely miss.

That being said: I can understand Amazon's more focused approach here in wanting the Kindle to be the ultimate reading device with less bloat and overhead to distract from that goal.

I do love the new device and reading on it is so much easier on your eyes than with other tablets. The touch controls are also smmoth and responsive with the rare hichup on illustrated pages.

Still... I gotta dock it 1 star for the missing text-to-speech. Audible I can live without... But the text to speech loss hurts.

title: A pathetic joke!
text: We bought this DVD player after the battery on our learning disabled adult son's 8-year-old Sony DVP-FX810 swelled up and popped the case apart. We had gotten the old Sony player for camping so he could watch movies in our trailer, and it worked great until recently. Last week we went camping nearby and assumed that we could just plug the Sylvania player into the 12 volt power in the trailer and turn it on. Not only would it not turn on, it would also not charge on 12 volt current (as the Sony would). I drove back into town and charged it, and while it charged I read the pidgen Chinese-English manual. It does not explicitly state that the player will not charge on 12 volt, but does say to attach the 110 volt power cord when charging. After charging the player back up I took it back up to the mountains, plugged it into the 12 volt, and it played for about 5 hours, then went dead - no movies the rest of the weekend (much to the disappointment of our son). After coming home I charged it on 110 volt current again and plugged it back into the trailer 12 volt power. I played one movie over and over with the sound off, and it again went dead in about 5 hours. My question - why the hell does the thing even have a 12 volt cord or plug if it won't charge on 12 volt, and why doesn't the battery at least STAY charged when it's plugged into 12 volt current??? It isn't even usable for a 10 hour road trip in a car. Other comments: the unit rattles when running, and the speakers are so wimpy you can barely hear it when sitting directly in front of it. The four most commonly used functions - PLAY/STOP and VOLUME +/VOLUME - are combined into two buttons, in spite of the fact that there are 10 buttons on it. Preposterously, there is a remote for a player you can't hear from 6 feet away. Unfortunately we waited too long to try out the player, and the return policy lapsed before we discovered what a piece of junk it is. Wish I'd read the other comments on this product before we bought it. I'll soon be buying a used Sony DVP-FX810 on eBay.

title: Great home camera hardware -- Software needs help
text:
For the money, I am very pleased with this product. I bought the 1080p, 8 camera set with the 3 TB NVR.

Pros:
- Good picture quality
- Wide view angle
- Lots of IR LEDs for good night vision
- Decent motion detection, including "mapping" sections of the view to ignore for motion
- Pre-configured cameras, which means plug them in and they detect the NVR -- no extra work for user!
- Good cable/power cord length so no extensions were needed (at least not for me).
- Physical quality of camera and housing is very nice.

Cons:
- Documentation is minimal and doesn't offer enough explanation of how to configure features. If you're fairly technical/handy, you can figure it out.
- E-mail interface is considered not-trusted by Google, so notification delivery is hit or miss.
- Recommended remote client (phone) is very poor. You can make it work, but it is amateurish at best compared to others.
- Viewing multiple cameras at once on remote client rarely works. Single camera at a time is usually okay.
- No ability to playback NVR via remote client. You can view live feed, but that's it.

Other:
- NVR software is Okay, but needs serious polish from a usability perspective. Things just aren't organized very well.
- Needs to support one of the OpenSource home automation projects. The hardware is great, the software isn't. Supporting OpenSource home automation projects would bring much needed improvements in the software which right now is the worst part of this product.

title: Measure your subs first! (And not just mounting depth!)
text:
It fits perfectly under the rear seats of my '12 F150 SuperCrew. However! The speaker terminal cups are in the way of the subwoofer mounting rings. I get that you can't foresee every possible design, bit darn man....just some simple forethought that "gee maybe I shouldn't mount this terminal cup 1 3/4 inches from where the giant speaker is going to mount" would be nice. I made it work but I had to rotate the sub mounting tabs around and now 1/4 inch of tab overhangs from the front face of the box.

Now, in all fairness, the box is well built otherwise and does fit very nicely overall. It sounds quite nice with my 2 10" Kenwood Excelons being driven by 1000w mono amp.

Really is a good product and I do like it, just that one simple fix and it would be a great box. There's so much room...they really could have mounted those terminal cups anywhere else. Frankly I'm shocked they thought this was a good idea.

I'd recommend this product, just make sure your subs fit (and not just the mounting depth).

title: Hard Drive failed - Still 5 Stars - Customer service is amazing.
text:
I purchased this drive about 13 months ago on Amazon (with protection package). I am a professional photographer working on a 13" laptop often doing so on a plane. The idea of a drive I could use while being crammed on a plane wirelessly was ideal. From streaming movies to working n files the drive worked as expected and was secure on network. The user interface was a little clunky and not terribly impressive but I didn't care - it worked

Fast forward to Jan 15th 2015. My computer (for whatever reason) froze while the drive was plugged in. No big deal, restart, right? When I did so the drive was locked up and inaccessible. Crap. I have some backups but the last thing I wanted to do was deal with another issue and data recovery. UGHH

Thats when I first experienced real customer service. (I know how stupid that sounds) But truth be told, as soon as I got off of Seagate's clunky website and called someone, I spoke with a real person within 5 minutes. This person was a native english speaking person, who seriously sounded like she was having a decent day and was happy to talk to me. What??

Long story short, I had not activated my "protection plan" and Seagate helped me thru the steps. Within an hour of my failure I had spoke with 2 reps, who were both VERY helpful. They helped confirm my protection plan (purchased thru amazon) and sent me a shipping label to get my data recovered. Instead of $500, it was $0.

2 days after the ordeal I sent out my drive and within 10 business days my data was returned to me on a new drive.

As a freelancer my life is constantly being occupied with small tasks that take up time and drive me crazy. Seagate made what was one of my worst fears into one of the easiest transactions I've done in years. I own several WD drives which have never had problems but moving forward and having interacted with Seagate customer service, I will only be buying Seagate drives from now on.
