title: Great watch, but make sure to verify your TOPO maps version installed
text:
I love this watch - though my review is based on only three days of use and I've sadly had to return it. The seller I purchased from (OE USA) sent me the version with EU topo maps and not the US topo maps as advertised in the description. I called them and they said the EU version was sent by mistake. I have returned it to them, they received it today, and they are sending me the US version of the watch. They were very helpful fixing the situation. There is no marking on the box to indicate that you have an EU version - you won't know until you go in and check the watch settings and see which TOPO maps were loaded. Make sure to check the map version right away just in case there is a limited return window on the product.

I have been a Microsoft Band user since the first generation and I loved all of the data the band collected as well as the integration with my phone (yeah, I'm in the minority as a Windows Phone user). I love the look and feel of the watch, but I miss seeing all of the data on the inside of my wrist while I am running instead of having to turn my arm over and look at the top of my wrist. I was concerned that the heart rate data wouldn't be as good if I wore it on the inside of my wrist so I wore it on the outside. When I get the replacement I will experiment with it on the inside of my wrist and update my review. I also really like that it doesn't have a touchscreen. I live in Georgia and after a run on a humid day, the condensation on the glass of my Microsoft Band made it VERY difficult to navigate any of the functions, and I usually didn't have a dry spot on my sweat-soaked shirt to wipe it off so I would struggle with it for a few minutes. With the buttons on the Fenix 5x, I can easily start/stop a workout with no issues in the humidity.

I was very pleased with how customizable the screens are on the Fenix 5x watch as well as the data that is pushed to Garmin Connect. During the three runs I took while I had it, I also used the Endomondo app on my phone just to compare distances and they were fairly similar, though the watch always showed less mileage than the Endomondo app on my phone showed. The difference was negligible to me so it wasn't a big deal.

I was able to get everything (mostly) working with my Windows Phone. The only functionality that was really lacking was the ability to switch songs from the watch - the only thing I could do was start and stop the music. If you are having issues getting things working with your Windows Phone (I'm using a Lumia 950XL) I highly recommend downloading Garmin Express to your PC/Mac and syncing once through the computer. I think some firmware updates were installed to the watch when I used Garmin Express that then got everything working as expected with my phone (with the exception of the music widget) on both the watch and the phone. I did (briefly) also pair my watch with Garmin Connect on my iPhone 7 and my Surface Book and it worked fine with both of those devices, too.

I really wanted to test out the mapping functionality, but if you get the watch that is not preloaded with the TOPO maps for your region, you only get some pretty high-level maps. I couldn't even see any of the streets near me on the maps - it was just the major state and interstate highways in the Atlanta area. I considered just keeping the watch and buying the US TOPO maps from the Garmin store separately, but the cost of the maps was too prohibitive, and they should have come with the watch anyway because that is what I was paying for when I bought the watch.

I also like the haptic feedback for notifications and alarms. Having a vibrating alarm allows me to wake up in the early mornings without waking up my spouse.

I used the metronome feature on two of my runs and my feelings are mixed. The first time, it really helped me pick up the pace and I ran a faster time compared to the previous day. The second run with the metronome I completely ignored it because I was running a really tough course and there was no way I could keep up. I think this is a feature that I'll use based on the course and what I'm trying to accomplish. You can set the tempo, how you want it to alert you (tone, vibration, or both), and how frequently it should alert you (every beat, once every 4 beats, etc.).

I can't wait for the exchange to be processed so I can start using it again.

title: If you like your audio to cut out in each ear randomly ...
text:
If you like your audio to cut out in each ear randomly every couple of seconds, these headphones are for you. I bought these after owning a pair of airpods, and to be clear I was not expecting that level of sound quality (they come nowhere close at all) but I'll say the audio quality is up there with a 30$ pair from 2012 perhaps, maybe the older LG Tone models. My experiment was to see if any of the more "budget" brands had caught up to Apple/Bose/etc in some features, it was a disaster.

I have to wonder if their marketing is doctored because these are HUGE and easily twice the size of airpods, but in the photos they don't look nearly as bad! If you look at the amazon user photos, THIS is representative of what you'll look like wearing them, the marketing photos are either doctored or use smaller (likely non-functional) versions.

The controls work, although they were designed by an idiot, and I've owned a few cheap chinese "lg-tone" knockoffs, when the power on/power off buttons are different for some reason? The manual states otherwise but functionally it's different. When the left pod disconnects (it's the secondary and is reliable as securing a hammock with dental floss) you'll lose access to those functions provided by that pod which are the next/prev track functions. Think you can just power cycle the left to get it back to it's typically fluctuating in-and-out state? NO DICE, power the whole thing off and on again and pray for it to say "connected" (which isn't connected to your phone, it's connected to the other pod, there's no indication if it's connected to your phone other than to use your phone to find out. The standard BS you'll read in the troubleshooting section of the manual will tell you to "ensure nothing is blocking the signal" (oh geez, my PANTS are too much for these headphones, or maybe my HEAD is too big) or that to keep them within 38 feet, helpful.

Other annoyances:

You'll have to consider the fact I own a pair of airpods and have been somewhat spoiled, so some of this is probably fine for people who enjoy this non-sense.

- pods do not turn off when placed in their case/dock, and they stay connected and play audio, therefore you can run into a situation where you keep audio playing and effectively drain the dock. You MUST make sure that you've turned them off.

- taking out one ear does not stop the other pod from playing.

- the buttons on each ear are very cheap, they have a little "spring" to them but not much very much, they have few audio cues that you've actually pressed the button either, very fun.

- they only charge in the dock when put in ONE way, but nothing stops you from mistakenly putting them in the WRONG way.

- it takes a lot of effort to pull the headphones out of the case/dock, enough that you will probably wreck them (eventually at least) as I've already damaged the screening over one of the pods just pulling them out.

title: Incredible battery life, good sound quality, intuitive controls, lightweight and comfortable
text:
I have owned dozens of Bluetooth headsets in the past 10+ years. Many of them have been a complete waste of money. The saying you get what you pay for does not always seem to apply in this electronics category. I received these headphones as a gift from my amazon wish list Christmas 2015 and they have been phenomenal.

The sound quality is very good, though as at least one other reviewer mentioned, they do not go very deeply into the ear canal, so they do not isolate sound the way other in-ear headphones do, but this is by design as they are intended for outdoor use where it's important to be able to hear your surroundings. Once in a while, in noisy environments, people can hear background noise, but I use them much more for music than phone, but having the phone features is imperative too as I don't want to have to carry another device. I can often overcome this nuisance by simply speaking a little louder.

The battery life is excellent compared with many other bluetooth headsets I've used. I seem to be able to listen to music on them for hours and hours before they get below half power. I only think I've had the battery die once and it was because the power button had been pressed inadvertently in my bag. That is probably my only complaint about them is that the power button protrudes slightly so it can get pressed in stowage, inside a bag. I do wish there was a slightly recessed button.

Controls are really well thought out, aside from the protruding power button, as mentioned above. All of the phone/power controls are on the right ear and music controls (volume, play/pause, track advance) on the left ear. Once you get used to that, it becomes second nature to operate them. I do also like that the power button is exclusively dedicated to turning the power on/off. Many headsets employ a multi-function button which includes the power on/off, so if you hold that multi-function button for too long to access Siri, or similar function, you accidentally are turning it off, which can be frustrating. Since the power button only controls power and pairing, you don't have to worry about making that mistake. The power and the volume buttons also have a slightly different tactical feel, that's very subtle, but when you learn it, easy enough to distinguish right from left without having to look at them, which is nice in the dark.

I find these headphones to be super lightweight and very comfortable. I often forget I'm wearing them. I pair them with my Mac and my iPhone and they work great with both, though it can be a little clunky to switch back and forth between phone and computer. I've had the battery last all day playing music while at work, which is surprising. And I never get the uncomfortable ear strain that I get with many other headsets or headphones.

I have run in the rain and as a test, I have even showered with them on to ensure they're truly waterproof. No issues except that sometime moisture gets between ear and headphones making some wet splotchy sounds while wearing them. This only really happened in the shower, not in the rain.

I'd recommend these to anyone who wants a great headset for outdoor activity or exercising.

Has anyone figured out some kind of cover to put over the right ear piece to prevent the power button from getting pressed inadvertently inside a bag?

title: Received half a product, went through hell dealing with Celestron
text:
I had ordered this to arrive just in time to see Uranus at opposition on 10/19. When the packages arrived that day, I opened them to find that I was sent just the CGX-L mount. So, disappointed that I missed opposition, I called the seller and requested the rest of my product (the OTA) be sent to me.

After the call, I went back to assemble and check out the mount to find that it was missing one of the screws to fasten the mount to the tripod. Whatever, I'll just request one be sent over with the OTA. I continue assembling it to find that it seems like the rod up which you slide the lens holder/base plate is staggered. Only one of the tripod legs are flush with the plate, and turning the nut under the plate any further filled the room with the screech of grinding metal. Now, I'm upset that not only am I missing something, now my 140lb mount may have to be returned for being defective.

Frustrated, I call Celestron support at 3:30pm shortly after assembling the mount (they close at 4pm). After waiting 5-10min to get on the line, I'm greeted by an angry agent who says (to the best of my memory, something like) "COME ON man, really? It's almost 4 o'clock!" Stunned, I assured him that if he was angry, he was nowhere near as angry as me. We continued the conversation about requesting the screw, with him giving me an angry tone almost the entire time. The conversation switched over to why my mount seemed defective. At this point, his tone lightened up a bit, and he said that it sounds like something he's dealt with in his own experience, and that the legs just have to be really pulled to get in place. That remains to be seen, because I've tried moving those legs every which way and nothing brings the rod straight enough to come closer to having the plate flush with the legs. We hang up, and I'm furious about the call I just had and the fact that I'm even having to deal with this in the first place.

A few days go by and I see the mount/ota combo I bought in an AdSense ad and notice something different. I realize that this setup comes with two counterweights, and my mount came with one, as the mount does when purchased alone. Immediately I dreaded having to call these people back, but got on the phone. Thankfully I was greeted by a much more pleasant agent who helped a great deal with arranging the weight be delivered asap, and offered to ask the engineers about the issue regarding the mount rod alignment. So, I sent over pictures and am awaiting the response to see if I'll have to deal with repackaging and returning a 40lb tripod, or (hopefully not) the entire mount.

Given that this thing cost over $6000, you would think an issue as blatant as sending only half of a product (a product weighing 200lb total) would be obvious. I'm going to do my best to avoid Celestron in the future, only as a last resort when no other brand or store will do. I'm waiting to receive the item to give any more stars, because only being blown away by its quality will I give anything more than 1 star. The way they handled the second call regarding the screw and mount was absolutely unacceptable, and I'm DEEPLY regretting not driving the 2-3hrs it would take to get it from the nearest dealer.

And I won't be using my telescope for another week, assuming nothing else goes wrong from here on out. I'll include pictures of the mount defects if they are confirmed to be defects by the product engineers.

title: Love it for travel!!! (Still!!!!)
text:
Great little tripod - folds down to nothing and easily attaches to my backpack. I have had this tripod for a year now - purchased it on Amazon as part of a bundle (LensPen, blower, etc). It has held up and has "traversed" the US with me - from Yosemite to DC.

First - this is not my regular tripod - I use it only for travel because of its size and weight. I took a $100 gamble and it paid off. It can easily support a DSLR with a 200mm 2.8 lens without ball head creep. Only thing (as said in another review) is hold your camera when loosening the ball head friction knob - it will flop-over rather quickly - no matter what camera/lens combo you are using.

Something else I found - the 10 pound limit is "The Limit". I had a camera mounted and added weight to the hook - it was close to 11 pounds (my backpack being the weight) and the legs started to retract. I removed a couple items from the bag and reset the legs - not a problem. The ball head was stable. Later, I weighed the camera and bag - that is how I got the 11 pound mark. With the same items removed (as previously) - was around 9 pounds. Someone did their factory testing.

Another item - with the center column fully extended - it is a little shaky (I never use the column - even with my main tripod - I find a long column a hindrance more than an assistant.

All of that being said - why five stars? It is just that reliable for me.

I am planning to take this tripod with me on a few trips this year and have no reservations about it - fantastic bang-for-the-buck - excellent for travel. If it were lost/stolen/damaged - I would definitely get another one.

Update---I have now had this tripod for 3 1/2 years. My camera and lenses have been upgraded (heavier), The tripod has been across the US a few times so it has quite a few scars from airports, slot canyons, rock walls, drops... It is still my go-to for travels when my full-sized tripod can't go with me. There is no wear on the leg locks or ballhead. When I lock the legs, they stay locked. Same with the ballhead...no looseness in any of the joints of the tripod. Yes - I have had to re-tighten the hex screws where the legs attach to the spider but - that is to be expected with as much use as this tripod has received.

I would definitely recommend this tripod for the traveler and would still - if it was lost/stolen/damaged get a new one asap.

title: Recent AV review- 1 Feb. from an original backer
text:
Disclaimer: This is my first extensive Amazon review. After backing this project from day one and seeing the wide range of comments on the AV, I wanted to give a more recent review from my initial experience as a backer, my expectations as a backer and my current very positive outlook for the product.

Comments on Crowd Source Funded Projects (how this one started):
I thought this was important to point out, since some of the reviewers are commenting on the AV at various stages of its early release and the delays to get theirs. As someone who has been an active member of crowd funded projects for a while. I have seen the best, the worst and everything in between. What some people tend to forget is they are voluntarily helping someone with an idea realize a dream. Many of the "companies" are small startups with very limited resources and are trying to work with manufacturing companies in Asia for the first time. Having been an Engineer for 30+ years, very few products go from engineering build to manufacturing success according to a business plan in the first try. This is very much an iterative process, where mis-steps are costly when products are highly differentiated and complex. My guidance is to set your expectations appropriately. If patience and tolerance are not your strengths, wait for it to show up in your favorite box store, with a display item that you can play with. If you want to be first and love gadgets than jump in and enjoy the ride.

The AuraVisor early days:
Yes (IMHO) it was a somewhat bumpy ride to get to a very positive point. First of all the DA team is genuinely helpful and more than willing to communicate in a professional and timely manner to help their customers enjoy the product. My first unit did not live up to my expectations for charging times and battery life. The support team without question replaced the unit and with the most recent firmware update (2.00.015) meets my expectations and provides real enjoyment for a now released product.

Using the onscreen keyboard:
The latest firmware has addressed the clipping and drifting issues that some folks experienced early on.
The Bluetooth game controller allows me to use the virtual mouse to locate (using the built in head tracker) the virtual keys and select them with the A button. The X button will back you up with in the application, the round black button on the left of the controller will back you up to the previous menu.

Originally there were a few bugs in the early firmware, making it a challenge to enter login info. One thing that worked fine for me was the use of a iPazzPort Wireless Mini Handheld Bluetooth Keyboard, it bonded fine and continues to work with the latest firmware release. I did try one other bluetooth keyboard that I had (Brookstone iPad keyboard) which did not work. My guess is given that this is an android based device, there were probably driver issues, which I do not find surprising.

Audio:
I personally use wired Bose noise cancelling headphones, and have not yet tried any wireless options. For me the Bose plug into the top of the AV
and they sound great. The hanging wire does not bother me.

The optical adjustments:
Intra Pupil Distance adjustment is very nice, and works well for me.
My eyes have very different prescriptions, so the focus adjust for me is pretty much opposite extremes. While it is not perfect, for this price point I am impressed that I can manage without my glasses. While showing this to family and friends who are dependent on their glasses due to age, they were able to keep them on and enjoy it. However it was a very tight fit and not comfortable for long viewing. But in fairness it really depends on the frames, shape of ones face etc.

Comfort:
For me the strap rides a bit low on the inner top of my ears. They are adjustable in three places (left, right and top) so your mileage will very.
I had no issue watching 2 hours of video with only minor adjustments at various times to relieve pressure points. I do not find the weight or the nose piece to be an issue.

What we did with it:
Google Play account, Discovery VR, Jaunt, YouTube, Amazon Video etc.
Loaded several videos on the micro SD card, when we did not have internet access.
Sorry I am not a big game player, so no useful data to share. Others have reported success with RiftCat and VRidge for teathered video input.

The unit is completely self contained and for me that is the greatness of it. I recently charged it up and took it to visit friends and family, many of whom had not experience any type of VR system previously. Their reaction to 360 degree video was priceless, particularly for those who were a generation older. This simply would not have been so easy with a PC based VR solution.

Rating Explanation:
Initially I give the AV 4 stars. however, with every firmware release it keeps getting more refined.
I than gave them back the 5th star for a total rating of 5 for customer support. In my opinion their customer support team exceeded my expectations. Mr Talbot himself emailed me from the UK to make sure I was happy as a follow up to their customer support team.

Hope this helps someone make an informed decision.

text: My wife and I have an office each on either side of a family room. The router is in my office. She complained that, at times, she lost connection to the Internet or to our peer-to-peer network. So, I decided to purchase this Netgear EX2700-100PAS. It was not as easy as "plug and play." I followed all the instructions given in the manual. However, the device failed to connect automatically to the router that was right next to it, as it was supposed to. The manual said that, if it fails to connect, one should try it with the Netgear Installation Assistant on p.10. There, you are supposed to launch your browser and go to www.mywifiext.net. When I tried doing that, I ended up on a third party search engine that had nothing to do with Netgear. After several unsuccessful attempts, I clicked on the Chat option and waited for someone to come on. No one did. After about 10 minutes, I decided to call the number shown on the Netgear page. A recorded voice came up that said: "The person you are trying to reach is not available." Then, all of a sudden, a Chat person came up. I explained the problem and she said an expert would call me back within 2 minutes. When I looked at the Chat window, it said: "You have been banned" (which makes one feel good)! About 15 minutes later, a fellow (with the proverbial Indian accent) called. Most of the explanations he gave me went over my head, not so much because of the accent but because it had to do with Firewall stuff with which I am not knowledgeable. He gained remote access to my desktop and found that, apparently, there were many devices that had nothing to do with me (over 600 of them) and that these were added through ad pages, etc. He said we should (1) secure the network; (2) reconfigure the Extender from the scratch; (3) remove the infections from the network; (4) assign secure IP addresses to each device; and (5) provide some anti-hacking tools to remove hackers. The Extender set-up and the clean-up would be done at no cost since I was a first-time user. However, the rest of the work (i.e., firewall network) would be done at the following subscription prices:  (1) $99.99/6 months; (2) $149.99/1 year; and (3) $249.99/3 years. I needed to resolve this problem, so I chose one year. He fixed everything remotely and the Extender finally worked. After I received a copy of the bill, I noticed that I dealt with a subcontractor of Netgear called Computer Services TX, based in Round Rock, Texas, although the fellow who helped me could be anywhere. By the way, he was very nice, polite, and seemed very knowledgeable. The wireless network connection on my wife's computer went from 2 bars to 3 (not a great improvement) after the successful installation of the the Extender. So, I have to give 2 stars to Netgear (instead of 1) because the Extender is working after all. I really disliked my experience following their directives in the manual, contacting them online, and trying to talk to them on the phone. All this needs A LOT of improvement. Last but not least, the final result (gaining 1 bar of strength on my wife's computer) was not was I was hoping for. So, the cost of all this was not $27.99 as advertised but really $177.98! If it had not been for the subcontractor's help, the Extender would have never worked. I believe that Netgear itself should offer to support their product for free and help with its installation.

title: OK for my usage. Maybe not for yours.
text:
I was searching for a device specifically for Amazon Prime Video streaming for my 1080p TV. I already have a 3rd gen Apple TV for other streaming. I thought about buying a 4K streamer for future compatibility, but given that most 4K TVs come with smart TV functions, I decided to go for cheaper models. I first bought a 2015 FireTV stick, but the incompatibility with my IR-only (old but trusted) Harmony 550 frustrated me so I returned it. I then bought a Roku Express on the day it was released. The Harmony database did not contain the codes for the Express yet, but all Roku 2 codes work fine. I have used this for about a week and, for my specific usage, I am happy with the fact that now I can watch Amazon Prime Videos without looking for another remote. For your information, if this is your first time registering at Roku and you don't like giving away your credit card information, there is a way. Google with "roku nocc".

For the general usage, though, I have some reservations. Firstly, the Express is definitely not a speed monster. By casual comparisons, its Netflix loading is slower than that of my 3rd gen Apple TV. Secondly, the included remote is very weak. I placed my Express next to my AV prepro/receiver, which is ~5 feet left to my TV. The distance between the Express and my viewing position is ~10 feet, and I made sure that the Express' face is fully in sight. Still, I absolutely need to swing my arm to target the face for the included remote to work (and this still fails sometimes). In contrast, my Harmony 550 works with the Express even if it is pointing toward the TV. Thirdly, the Amazon app on Roku uses a poorly organized interface. If I didn't care about the IR compatibility, my choice would be the Fire Stick and its crisper and quicker RF remote.

title: A handsome streaming device that sounds good, but a flawed app and $$ price tag are nagging issues
text:
The B&O Beoplay M5 fills a small to medium space with a much bigger soundstage than expected without cluttering up a table. It needs to sit out in the open to be able to project sound rather than placed in a bookshelf where it cannot really perform as designed. Once you set it up, simply press down on the Beoplay M5's nicely machined aluminum top to control the music's volume or to pause it. I do not have a second one, but this is also how you cannot one M5 to another.

B&O describes its sound as omnidirectional, and that's accurate. I found, however, that I actually had to learn to listen to the Beoplay as I come from that old school of folks who like to have true stereo coming from a pair of speakers. That is the most satisfying sound for me. But the Beoplay has its place. It allows you to fill a porch, a sitting room, or a kitchen with quality sounding music. The music does flow around you, and, conversely you do not have to find the perfect spot. I think my point is simply that devices such as this one have their place, and once I dispensed with my conditioning, I liked the way it sounds.

Certainly, the M5 is handsome. It does not call undue attention to itself, and it holds up well to scrutiny. It has character without being ugly, I have seen (and heard) many ugly speakers and streaming devices, and the M5 is near the top for aesthetics.

But Houston, we have a problem, perhaps a lethal one, perhaps not. After a month I cannot get the streaming to work. I've tried installing and reinstalling various permutations of the B&O streaming app on my two-year-old smart phone and my Samsung Galaxy tablet that is several years old. None work. So I not able to access or use all of the purported features of the M5 supported by the app. Nothing on the B&O website has helped so far, though I admit I have only invested about an hour into solving the problem. But why should I need to spend time troubleshooting a streaming device that costs this much. I'm going to try again and will change my rating if I can find a satisfactory solution.

Meanwhile, I can still use Bluetooth or plug directly into base of the unit to listen to music. I can move it around easily and even take it one the road without much trouble to ensure I have a way to connect to music when I travel.

The price should give you pause. Check out the competition before you decide. I like the way the M5 sounds and I that it recedes into the background. Hope some of this review proves helpful .

title: Awesome noise-cancelling for plane rides! YES!
text:
I'll start of by saying that I am not an audiophile- just a regular gal who likes to listen to music! So, I can't speak to the sound quality- just to the noise-cancelling feature.

I bought these to take with me on airplanes, as I do quite a bit of travel but haven't yet mastered the skill of reading on moving vehicles. Let me just say- these are INCREDIBLE! When I first used them with the noise-cancelling (which you have to do manually by moving a switch), I almost cried. They do SUCH a good job of cancelling noise- I was no longer bothered by the humming sound of the engine and could really enjoy my music/ movies. I used to use just regular, cheap-o headphones on planes, but always had to crank up the volume just to *barely* hear my music. Now, I can listen at a normal, non-ear damaging volume! Yay! Like other reviewers have mentioned- these do not cancel ALL noise. I could still hear random bursts of noise (like, the flight attendant talking on the loud speaker), but that's not a big deal.

As far as comfort goes, I found these to be quite comfortable. I get headaches with any stress on my head (wearing glasses, wearing my hair in a ponytail for too long), but these gave me no problems. My ears were mildly relieved when I took them off, but they were never too tight that I had to take a break from them.

Overall, these are really nice! They ARE expensive- that's why you should put them on your birthday or holiday wishlist. Get to it!

title: Cost-Cutting at the Consumer's Expense
text:
After using the QC15 for five years--and as a Million Miler they served me extraordinarily well--for some reason I felt it was time for an "upgrade." I replaced the ear pads on the 15's--which, given their overall condition rendered them "brand new" (I take care of my stuff)--and gifted them to my daughter. I then ordered the QuietComfort 25.

After two weeks of use, including a week on a long overseas trip, my brief observations and impressions of the QC25 are as follows:
- Pro: The case is very attractive and slightly more compact than the QC15, with a nifty holder for the airplane adapter a spare battery.
- Pro: The zipper construction is clean and sturdy, and probably will provide years of use without problem.
- Pro: The battery seems to last about the same amount of time as it did on the QC15, but when the battery goes dead you can still hear your music.
- Pro: Folding the headphones to fit into the compact case is easy, and the hinges work without binding.
- Pro: They sound as good, if not modestly better, than the QC15. (Non-HiFi but good enough for Road Warrior use.)
- Pro: The noise reduction seems comparable to the QC15.
- Pro: The inline pause/start and volume control works great with my iPod and iPad.
- Pro: They are comfortable, but...
- Con: They are not as comfortable for long wear (8+ hours) as the QC15. I can't explain why, they just aren't.
- Con: Without any input and the cable disconnected--i.e., just using them to cancel outside noise--there is a slight background hiss that I never experienced with the QC15.
- Con: The QC25 "feels cheaper" than the QC15. I can't explain why, particularly given the construction of both is plastic.
- Con: From the very first use, when jiggling the cable I experienced a "dirty connection" clicking in the headphones. After two weeks of use this went completely bad, leaving me without audio, and and the device jack (opposite the end that plugs into the headphone) appears to be broken below the plastic housing.

Additional Comments
In my opinion, the overall cheaper feel to these phones and the problem with the cable is a margin-preservation effort (a.k.a. cost-cutting). The cable connector design in particular is clearly inferior to the that of the QC15. I've attached a photo that shows the difference, which can be summed up with two points: (1) The QC25's more rigid connector stress-relief sheath, coupled with the 90-degree connector structure, puts more stress on the connector itself than the non-90 degree angle and more flexible stress-relief sheath of the QC15. (2) The connector base of the QC25 is "on the cheap" compared to the robust connector base of the QC15.

Sorry, Bose, but I'm sending these back. Cutting corners will bite you every time.

Perhaps my daughter will let me borrow her QC15's....

title: Toshiba III is my last...
text:
This is my third Toshiba. I loved both my Toshiba 1, and Toshiba 2. I lost BOTH in an accident when both were in car. I was under pressure to buy fast, and Staples had this on sale $650... It was my first Windows 10. And the infuriating "learning" curve from the good OS, Win 7, to, Win 10, yet another idiotic fix to something not broken, was the focus...Thus, agree:
"windows 10... proved to be a lot of work to get this computer set up and remove all the crappy software it comes with (windows 10 related)"

I hate windows 10, and attention upon getting started, was that and circumnavigating the bloat of software, and it's insistence to use Edge for searches, (oh the entire thing is stupid...) So the above and all that go along, and the install of my licensed software, all back ups on Toshiba 2 gone...Well, once I tried to get up and going, the quirks I dismissed in the baptism of fire, like those you mention, became understood as part of the mess. For one, the jumping cursor issue is infuriating. If it doesn't randomly select areas of text with or without knowing, deleting or causing go back edits, it simply jumps off the window you're typing in. I'm not always looking at what's typing on screen, but at my notes, from which I type... So I'm typing away, getting good stuff fleshed out from my source notes, and voila, at a pause, there's like a few phrases maybe, of the thinking on screen, the rest... well the cursor took a f---ing leap 3 paragraphs ago. Ridiculous. I now have to stop to review every few seconds (I type 75 wpm, so it is REALLY a very bad quirk...)
But gotta add two other BIG let downs:
It's 1-slow and 2- the screen display sucks!

Slow:
I thought as an i7, it would be faster than my Satellite i3, and as fast as my i7 was, but as it turns out, it isn't faster than the i3 and IS SLOWER than my older i7 (may they rest in loyal peace...) And now I may understand better why, from reading one of the reviews below this one. Here is an excerpt: " i7-5500u only has two cores: its performance is probably equivalent to the older generation i3 dual core processor. Noticeably worse than older i-7 quad core...."

I feel betrayed by Staples store tech for not pointing out the distinction re processor cores. I'm no tech savant, and really, after the guy determined the HDs in both my Toshibas had been damaged in the crash, and cost of replacing HD etc on older machines.... well, time for a new Toshiba. I said I needed one as fast as the last i7 I bought there (in fact, I've purchased 4 laptops from same place... And the guy sells me this i7- and I've been baffled as to why it's so slow compared to my other... And now I see why. And no excuse as he just finished checking HD on my 'old' i7quad, so when I said, as fast as... it was, "as fast as the one you have right there in front of you.... So, I'll be going back for a chat. Granted that's about the tech... but upon presenting the S55 C5274, it IS qualified as an i7, and an average buyer isn't going to know to ASK , "So, oh, I understand you're now making your processors in a new line that, though to the average Joe buyer, an i7 means what they know it to mean... THAT'S not necessarily true now... So, can you please specify, if the components of THIS, as an i7, are what I know them to be?" What the h-ll? So, Staples guy aside, it does seem pretty slick for Toshiba to qualify a newer machine, with upgrades, as an i7, when, they've developed another line with inferior components as an i7. Not all buyers are so flipping knowledgeable- And really, to that degree of detail? Maybe I'm wrong- maybe nobody has a right to buy what they think they're buying from name and past buys, and whine, because, really, it's my fault because I don't read PC Magazine or PC Pro, don't know how to rebuild a laptop, am not brave enough (or stupid enough) to install a new HD on my own, and think an i7 processor means what it meant last time I bought a Toshiba i7... Silly me.

As to the screen:
Friend was looking over a document on screen with me, and said, "This is so blurry. it's giving me a headache". I was almost relieved, bc prior, I wasn't sure if I needed glasses or wtf. Watching shows on Amazon and CouchTuner reveals such bad image, compared to my last 2 Toshibas. Washed out color, clarity is so bad that I can barely read the icons when just sitting back in my chair, with external keyboard. I have tried adjustments in display options (color/gamma) for the screen still s--*. This Screen can't be pushed.

I did set display preferences for large text,- menu, address, icons... anything in any app that can be enhanced... Bold/Large....Done what I can, short of using laptop in that weird Assistance Contrast mode.... But there things for which nothing can be done with a crap screen. Example: delineation within folder windows for adjusting side bar widths is almost invisible. So, say 'preview' is open in a folder, and you want to adjust it... wider... less wide... trying to find the delineation between the main folder window, and that preview window, requires moving your cursor around until it responds to having found the division line, because the delineation line is TOTALLY invisible (due also, to the idiotic change in Win 10 redesigned folder interface... hairline thin, light light gray... what the heck is THAT about?) Anywho... it's that, coupled with s--* screen, that makes this a purchase I really regret.

So beyond that pesky problem of really bad 'visibility', if you do anything where image matters to you, on monitor, or monitor to output..... even just basic photo editing, this will drive you bonkers. I'm not using mine to display work, but if I still did, it would look like crap. Granted, this is not meant for that, it's a general use pc. But in general use, most people do basic edits on photos, make cards, family or work or whatever newsletters, graphs..etc, w color graphics and photo inserts, but if you care about your display,matching your print, forget about it, because calibrating your monitor and printer, and syncing color profiles, won't matter here, as the screen color doesn't exist in output.

Yeah, if it bugs me, why didn't I make sure first? Well, I addressed that, not in full, but I should have gotten point across.
So, having covered it for all potential buyers, I hope, I, personally, would not buy this computer again, or if I'd seen the future. I would not even buy it for 1/2 the price. As it is, I'm stuck with it have lost $980... with tax and warranty... OH about the warranty:
I did buy a warranty for $200 full coverage... in any kind of failure or accident... Even if I spilled a gallon of milk on it, dropped it from the second floor, accident... failure.... it's all covered. But........I can't return if for not being the machine I was to have been sold, nor because it's not a very good machine, especially for the money. Oh, and on the note of Toshiba customer care- It is true, they have plummeted from what they were. All around, this IS my last Toshiba.

title: NOT TRUE OUTPUT POWER/ Frequency
text:
As a long time electronics tech please note the following:
Product does work as advertised-BUT note does not provide a true sine wave output (wall power at 60 Herz. There during the recent power outages in Virginia I ran the UPS with my SMART TV which only uses a 100 watts, two laptops and several small LED desk lights Phone/radio charger. IT will mess up your SmartTV.
I do not use/connect the TV to the Internet and use over the air TV signals except for software updates The TV is a real power saver trying to reduce your electric bills vs the older plasma or picture tube TVs.
The issue is when you purchase a UPS make certain you buy a True sine wave 60Hz one if you live in the US (same as what you get from your wall outlet) if you you run a desktop computer, new TV, you may have a problem. In my case despite numerous customer help from my TV Mfg, the software is corrupted despite new downloads. The time and TV programs programming does not match and is always an hour off.
If you are only using it for lights radio , chargers or other light loads you are good it go.
Also note tech support also says if the load is less then 40 watts or so the display will not show the actual load, only the battery display
Also note although Cyber Power is listed on the WEB as made in Taiwan and as delivered shows made in China.

title: Muscians: Finally Low Latency good enough for Instrument Audio!
text:
I recommend that you purchase both TROND units, and have them talk to each other directly. You will be wire-free!

I am very excited to report that two Bluetooth Low Latency Trond units are working together with very low latency good enough for playing live music! I play my EWI4000s (Electronic Wind Instrument) and send audio from Trond's BT-DUO S Transmitter to Trond's BT-RX S Receiver which is plugged into my Roland KC-110 amplifier. I experience no noticeable delay until I am about 20 feet away. Even then it is slight and playable.

I had previously purchased a Taotronics TT-BA07 receiver (which is supposed to be very low 40ms latency also). Unfortunately it does not perform as claimed and adds about 300 milliseconds delay. It is unplayable.

I purchased Trond’s BT-RX S and got the same delay so I contacted Trond. The Trond BT-DUO S transmitter unit was provided to me as a free sample for testing purposes, to see if the 30-40ms latency was achievable with the Trond receiver unit which I had purchased. Gary from Trond was clear that they did not claim that it would be good enough for live performance by musicians, but I explained that 40ms would be sufficient for my personal practice. I was hopeful this could work because I have the Korg MicroKEY Air-37 and the Yamaha MD-BT01 and both work with my iPad and iPhone with no noticeable latency. The one caveat is that these are passing CC Midi, not audio via BlueTooth, so the volume of data may be much less.

I am so excited that BlueTooth Audio via Tronds units has worked well enough that I will use them for informal performances. I am now wire-free for both midi (via Yamaha) and audio thanks to Trond!
Please see my pictures.

title: Does not autoadvance the preview pictures. Forces you to continually click multiple times in the gallery to see your newest pix
text:
I have been looking for a better solution than the eyefi card for previewing images on my ipad or google tablets. The weye-feye appears as an access point which can be connected to from PC, Android or IOS and on the latter two, allow remote control of the camera's functions in much the same way as CamRanger but at 1/2 the cost.

https://xsories.com/weye-feye-orange

They make 2 version of this. The regular version described above, and an "S" version which only includes the gallery functions (i.e. no remote-control).

I bought the regular version with remote control even though I don't currently have a use for it. The unit seems to be more rugged and better protected as well as smaller than the camranger and has 2x the range if you believe the specs.

The way it works is that you plug your camera into the USB port on the weye-feye and you connect wirelessly to the weye-feye from your iPad, iPhone, android device or windows PC.

On ios/android you have a pretty complete set of remote control functions including live view, selection of most camera parameters, focus point selection, etc.

On windows, you just get file transfer to the folder of your choice.

On ios/android you do not get file transfer but the host app on your device is able to peak into the camera's file system to view files stored on your camera's flash card.

Contrary to the whining on amazon.com, connecting up to the weye-feye was very simple and easy.

For me - interested primarily in previewing images - the big #FAIL in the android and ios app is the inability to autoadvance the picture. You have to manually refresh the image list every time a new picture is taken. With the eyefi card, on android , pc and ios, I can be in the gallery and looking at a full screen picture of the latest image I have taken and every time I take a new picture, it auto-updates and shows the new picture full screen. With the weye-feye, I have to go over to the tablet and manually refresh and open the latest picture each time. This is no good in the studio or in the field IMO and it seems like an easy problem to solve but 3 separate attempts at contacting their support yielded nothing.

If you are using a windows computer, you can have the weye-feye app auto-transfer the files to your computer and using lightroom's file monitoring function, lightroom *will* auto-update to the latest file you have transfered. However, I do not want to take my notebook computer out in the field for shoots. I guess if you have a surface pro and are running the full version of lightroom on it you could have the best of both worlds.

I also contacted shuttersnitch - who's software i use on my ipad with my eyefi card - but it seems that they are not particularly interested in supporting weye-feye (or camranger for that matter).

I have not had a chance to investigate whether the camranger apps for ios or andoid can do the auto-update of the gallery photos. Maybe someone else can comment on that?

Anyway, for me and the fact that I'm not particularly interested in the remote control aspect, the weye-feye and the lack of support have me inclined to return the unit. Maybe a future software update will fix the problem. If so, i would buy this again.

title: Great system for the money
text:
I had been searching for a good quality HD front camera and an HD rear camera and this unit fits the bill. The package came with plenty of cabling and even a 16g card so I could use the product as soon as I finished installation. I've had the product for two weeks and so far, I'm very happy with it.
The over-the mirror unit is heavy but hopefully a sign of a well-built system. The system is fairly intuitive and easy to start up, especially with the directions.
In terms of features, I immediately upgraded the memory to a superfast 128g card by Lexar who has a lifetime warranty on the card. Avoid Samsung and Sandisk cards because dash cams eat them over time. (Samsung publicly discourages their use in dash cams.) Now, I have plenty of recording space for both front and rear videos. The picture quality and (internal) sound quality of the recording are excellent and something I know will be critical if I'm involved in an accident.
The KD Links people are really awesome. They were helpful with pre-purchase questions and video samples from a R100 unit. I couldn't find much other than good reviews for KD Links other dash cams so I asked the support team some questions about the unit. They answered me by the next morning - even on Thanksgiving Day.
My car is a diesel so I need to heat the glow plugs a bit before I start my car. I think this messes with the unit's start up protocol which starts as soon as my 12v plug receives power, or seven seconds before I start the car. On occasion, I need to start the camera manually but its no big deal. You press one button. However, I'm confident that if my car were gas powered, there wouldn't be any issues.
I've not been in any accidents so I cant make any statements on the unit's ability to automatically save video after sensing a crash. However, having a high-cap micro SD card assures me that I'll have the video.
The best feature of this unit is it's stealth. Other modular cameras stick out and are easily visible so they can be a theft target. This unit envelops the mirror so it's hard to spot it unless you are looking for it there. The rear cameral mounts quickly with high-quality, high-tack 3M transfer tape to the top of the rear window so it's also hard to spot. Another nice feature is the main power cord. While it resides permanently in your cigarette lighter outlet, the plug itself contains a USB port so you don't lose the ability to charge a phone or tablet.
My only complaint is the proximity sensor is overly sensitive and warns me of being too close to vehicles in front of me unnecessarily. I don't think I really need this so I'll be turning it off.
Ultimately, the dual HD picture quality and prior great reviews of other KD Links dash cams is what convinced me to purchase this unit. As of today, I'm glad I did. Thanks!

title: Perfect for extending your Oculus Rift sensors at USB 3.0 speeds!
text:
Works great with the Oculus Rift sensors, I've been using these for about 2-3 weeks now and have had no problems, everything is recognized as USB 3.0 and the room scale is working perfectly.

I think some of the negative reviews saying this is only recognized as 2.0 are blaming the problem on the wrong thing. Your computer's USB controller can only handle so many devices, regardless of how much power your PSU pumps out, regardless of how many ports your computer has, the fact is USB controllers have limited bandwidth and there's nothing you can do about it.

The best way to test if you are maxing out your controller's bandwidth is to unplug every USB device except your mouse, keyboard, and Oculus Rift then re-run the sensor setup, if you have no issues then you know the problem is that you have too much stuff connected to it, in this case the solution for that is not a new cable but rather an additional USB expansion card

title: Perfect for planets.
text:
I purchased this telescope for planetary and lunar viewing. It's not the just light collector for DSOs but managed to capture some of the brighter Messier objects.

For an intermediate telescope the Omni XLT 102 is the perfect balance of power and portability. I live in a major US city so light pollution restricts what I can see in the night sky. But planets turn out amazingly in this scope. I made out the red spot on Jupiter once and you can easily see the Cassini division in Saturn. The focuser is adjustable, allowing for better control. However the focuser is greasy and lacks a fine tune knob.

Chromatic aberration is not too much of an issue. The coating on the lens is ample but is not what you expect on refractors $800+. Jupiter has a distinct blue halo around it and Saturn has some green hue but this does not ruin the viewing experience at all. Seeing the chromatic aberration is more of an observation than a complaint.

The focal length of the scope is phenomenal and really one of the best features. It allows for better magnification especially with planets. I would recommend at least a 2X Barlow and a 10mm eyepiece to really capture planetary detail such as the Cassini division.

The mount is sturdy and not too shaky. Only when you focus does the image shake for a brief moment. I believe you can attach a motor drive on this mount too, so for astrophotography this is a great semi-portable, semi-powerful telescope.

You won't see amazing images that bigger telescopes like 10" Dobs get, but if you're looking for a somewhat portable telescope that's still good enough to make you gasp. This is the baby for you!

PROs:
Sturdy tripod
Solid EQ mount, with option for polar alignment scope
Nice coating on the lens
Not too heavy (For me. I guess, it is larger than most refractors you see)
Easy to set up (less than 5 minutes)
AMAZING FOCAL LENGTH f/9.8
Easily magnify up to 200x

CONs:
Greasy focuser
Tripod legs could extend longer
EQ mount is not very fluid when balancing
Slow motion knobs can be longer

title: SIMPLY ONE OF THE BEST HEADPHONES ON THE MARKET
text:
I felt compelled to write a review about these headphones since there were just 9 reviews that averaged to a 4 star rating. This Focal Classic is clearly underrated. To give you a background, my in-ear headphones of choice is the $1,000 Shure 846s. For over-the-ear headphones, I auditioned all types of headphones including, among others, B&W P7, Bose, Beats Pro, Audio-Technica ATH-M50, Audio-Technica ATH-M50, Sennheiser Momentum, Philips Fidelio X1, Parrot Zik 2.0, and others.

As we ALL KNOW, sound preference and what we each think sounds "good" or "great" is so subjective. Therefore, I will tell you that I tend to prefer a "U" shape spectrum on the sounds scale with very, crisp sparkly trebles, and very prominent deep, tight, powerful bass. I enjoy listening to as large of a sound spectrum as possible, while hearing the realistic details of every instrument, every grain of every violin string, and to notice every intricate detail of background instruments as possible, while feeling like the vocalist is performing within feet of me. I listen to every genre of music from movie scores, trance, house, R&B, Hawaiian reggae, pop, classical, hard rock, rap, and yes, even some limited country.

That being said, despite not personally being very familiar with Focal as a headphone brand, but rather having some distant familiarity with Focal as a speaker maker, admittedly I was hesitant to admit that these were going to be "the ones" that I would keep. But one headphone audition after the next, while each time comparing them to the Focal Classic, the Focal remained the undisputed Champion, defeating every reputable-brand headphones maker and model after the the other.

The detail that is heard through the Focals will leave you with a "Wow" moment. You will rediscover music that you've listedned for years and hear new details. The stage presentation is wide and distinct, while each instrument and detail, from my perspective, is no less than incredible. The trebles are crystal clear and bright, while the bass is powerful with great depth. Most headphones cannot accomplish both. One tends to drown out the other. With the Focals, none of the brilliance is lost. I was simply amazed. I have probably owned and tested over 3-4 dozen over the ear headphones in my adult lifetime, and the same with in ear headphones. If you told me these headphones cost $1,000, I would believe it. They are that good. And NO, I did not receive these free to review like many reviewers receive free gear from companies. I paid for these on my own, choosing these over MANY others.

Those who know me say I am extremely musical and with an excellent ear for music and detail. I am extremely picky with the gear that I listen to music. Simply put, you will NOT be disappointed, and in fact, will have the "WOW!" factor. I am confident of this. Therefore, to quickly give it a rating on a 10 scale, based on MY personal preference of sound quality:

OVERALL SOUND: 10/10
BASS: 10/10
MID: 10/10
TREBLE: 10/10
SOUNDSTAGE: 10/10
DETAILS/SEPARATION: 9.5/10

CONSTRUCTION/BUILD QUALITY: 9/10
COMFORT: 8.5/10
DO YOU NEED A HEADPHONES AMP? I SAY NO.

Pros:
-8 core powerhouse

-Overclockable

Cons:
-Heat, so plan on spending extra for a cooler if overclocking.

title: Um, WOW
text:
I had the XB950BT, but found the sound slightly muffled and the BASS BOOST feature overdone and not usable (WAY over-exaggerated the bass), so I ended up returning those (last year).

Let's get one thing out of the way, if you're buying these, you're not looking for a "balanced, even sound", you want something that sounds good & will rattle your brain.

Enter the Sony XB950N1...

SOUND & APP
Sound is quite good even with the "bass effect" off. Highs are smooth (vs. a little sharp with the Beats Studio), mids are full & rich, and lows are not boomy, rather, solid & deep. The Sony Headphone Connect App further allows you to customize the bass, so if you actually want to decrease the bass from out-of-the-box levels, you can (negative 1-10), or if you want more, you can increase on a scale from 1-10. For me, +3 is enough to strike the right balance of hard-hitting bass and musicality. The soundstage is surprisingly good for this type of closed-back headphone. Overall, it's a fun headphone that also sounds really good.

ANC
On par with the Sony 100ABN (which I also have), except there is a bit less white noise. Not as good as Bose or the Sony 1000X, but definitely in the 2nd tier of ANC systems out there. Very capable and effective.

MIC
Works great. One of the issues the XB950BT mic had, was the poor range (100 Hz - 4,000 Hz), however, the mic on these have literally 2x the vocal range (50 Hz - 8,000 Hz) and meet the HD Voice specification. My voice sounds very clear when using as a headset.

BUILD
The plastic is a nice rough matte finish and is of a higher grade than the XB950BT & XB950B1. The headphones feel solid and the adjustment slider clicks are nice & even (both sides respond equally). The headphones also fold like the Beats Studio, so you can fit them in a smaller case if you want to (they only come with a bag, so you may want to buy a 3rd party hardcase). The buttons have a nice response and the overall fabrication is high-end and fits nicely & smoothly together.

OVERALL
Even at suggested retail of $249, these are a good buy, and in fact, have a bit more features than most others in this mid-premium range.

title: Great potential...
text: For about 1/4 the price of Sonos, you can have wireless mid-Fi around your home. The Caskeid (pronounced kas-kade) technology truly locks every speaker in sync! (when it works...) Let's be realistic: none of today's WiFi speakers provide truly high-fidelity, but then we've compromised for so long with mp3/aac content, any step up from Bluetooth sounds great! The Jongo T2, S3, and siblings sound pretty good! And a price that let's you place two in stereo, you get a great sound field at a bargain (compared to others like Sonos or Bluesound.) If you're placing just a few here and there, this is a decent system and is improving by leaps and bounds every quarter via automatically downloaded software updates. Like any new system, there remain kinks to work out. Among them: be prepared for quirks with Pure Connect app designed to direct the speakers to online or local content. And be prepared to deploy a dedicated access point channel strictly for Jongo WiFi traffic when deploying more than about 6 units. I found that until I set up a dedicated dual-core WiFi router just for Jongo, I could not get the 10 units in my house to sync consistently. And using the (very clever) Bluetooth input, I could never *maintain* sync on more than about 4 units. I have no doubt that Pure (Imagination/Caskeid) will solve these problems. For now, I've put my Jongo plans on hold till these kinks are ironed out, instead deploying a (much smaller, more expensive) Sonos system. I really look forward to seeing Pure address these problems and returning to their solution. I think it's the better value, but just has a few shortcomings in large systems that must be solved.

title: "Dell Premier Sleeve S" fulfilled as 460-BBRZ by Amazon.com LLC is suspect
text:
I received this "Dell Premier Sleeve S" yesterday, which was "Sold by: Amazon.com LLC" per my Order Details. I didn't suspect anything until I looked at the tag that was attached to the item itself.

Recently we've been seeing more of these "authentication tags" which have holographic strips and direct you to go to a website and type in a number on the card. The site/landing page itself is suspect (it's not a Dell site) and it's completely in Chinese with a company at the bottom I do not recognize. I didn't enter the code into the site from the tag because: A) I don't know which field it is since I can't read Chinese, B) upon closer inspection of the tag, the holograph looks faked and the traditional Dell "font" doesn't look genuine, and C) other observations expanded below.

Comparing the item itself, the wrapping as it was packed within the box, and the (possibly imitation) Dell box it came in, none of the model, product/part, or other numbers matches with what it here on this Amazon listing. No label, tag, or other text in what I received says 460-BBRZ anywhere. Further, I went to Dell's website and found their manufacturer part no., which again, is nowhere to be found in the product I received.

Overall, it looks legitimate if you didn't dive into details. Another observation is that I'm a long-time Dell product user, and I don't want to go as far as to say this is a flimsy product, but it just doesn't seem to be built like all other Dell products and accessories.

Additional note 1: The "Dell P/N" printed on the box and stitched into the bag does not match any P/Ns on Dell's official website.

text:
So far so good! Been using only 30 minutes though, lol.

Word of advice on initial setup, as i just went through this and wanna help anyone who runs into the same issue.

I bought this cable to connect a Windows 10 laptop to a Cisco 3750G Switch. The process was simple.
-Connect cable to usb (2.0) on laptop and console port on switch
-Go into device manager, find the cable (mine was listed under "other"), update the driver (which will move the device from other to its proper category)

Here's where i ran into trouble. Once i did both of the above steps, i still could not console into the switch using putty. No clue as to why. Turns out, for whatever reason, the newly updated device driver defaults to COM3 (instead of COM1, which is what putty expects). So change COM1 to COM3 in the putty serial connection tab, open, and boom, should be in.

Great cable.

title: Great product with some flaws
text:
I did not buy the item on Amazon and did not get paid by anyone for this review.

I supported the Nura on kickstarter campaign. The headphone took 1-2 years behind expected delivery date to arrive. I would almost forget that I had ordered this headphone if they had not been consistent with the updates. With kickstarter product, communication and updates are key to success. It shows how commitment and transparent the company is to their products and their investors/customers. Nura has scored good on this part. Let's move on to the product itself.

Pros:
- Nice package with plenty of accessories
- I really like the case, very sturdy, very modern, a bit big but not obnoxiously obstructing. The case even has a small magnet box/pocket in which you can store your choice of charger or connection cable. This is very smart!!! Normal headphone gives you a leather/plastic bag to store your headphone with no place to store your charger/connection cable. Therefore, you either will lose the cable when storing somewhere else or stumbling and dropping it as you taking the headphone out of the bag. With Nura, you can simply take the headphone out and keep the cable there until you need it. Sweet and smart solution.
- Quality of the headphone is great for the price. Possibly on par with some high end headphone out there. Metal headband with soft cushion gives the feeling of sturdy and comfy. The earpieces and earbuds are soft. The on/off app button feels solid. The charging cable feels solid. The magnet charging system is quite nice. As you put the charging cable in, it disappears in the headphones with a smooth gap and very pleasing to the eye.
- Sound is great. You can definitely hear the difference with the app activated. The sound has a bit more dimension, a bit more bass, and slightly clearer. The difference would be more evident with high quality music or classical/concert music.
- Headphone automatically turns on as you put it on and welcomes you with your name. This is a nice little touch which gives you the feeling of special/luxury item.
- Due to the auto on/off, the headphone battery seems pretty good. I notice an average of 2-3 days of use with ~2-4 hrs of use per day. When the battery is low, the headphone will literally tell you.
- App on phone is fairly simple to use and easy to set up. No issue sync between phone and headphones.
- Bluetooth range is good. I do not measure exact but it can hear fine roughly 10-15 meters apart from my phone.
- Decent passive noise cancelling due to the well-pad cushions that hug your ears.

Cons:
- Case and headphone are a bit bulky. Not too much of an issue but I could appreciate a bit of compact especially if you plan to put it in a suitcase. The case fits better with big backpack for students than office worker trying to keep a nice pair of headphone for daily train committing.
- The headphone, although comfortable at first, starts to hurt my ear after ~2 hrs wearing it straight. This is probably due to the earbuds and the weight of the headphone. I am usually able to wear my headphone for a bit more than that ~4 hrs. Earbuds tends to hurt my ear around 2 hrs.
- The sound when the app is off can sometimes sound better depend on the type of music or sound you try to hear. This brings a question about the usability of the app. It seems to me like a preset equalizer but instead of being able to customize yourself, you kind of stuck with this manufacturer preset.
- The individual hearing test on the app is not very obvious. I can hardly see the difference between my wife's test and mine. The sound we hear are somewhat similar (when the app is on) as well from what I pick up. This brings up the question: is it really individualized?
- The app is too simple with not much customization settings and functions. Hopefully we can get some updates soon with more functions we can play with.
- No active noise cancelling. For a retail price of $399, I would like to see some noise cancelling in there.
- No way to see how much battery you have left on the headphone or the app (at least not to my knowledge at this point). I wish they could have some sort of light indicator on the headphone which blinks at 20% or 10% battery or shows different color at different battery level. I also wish they have battery level notification on their phone app so we don't have to open the app to check it. We could just receive the notification as the headphone juice is running low.

Overall, I think this is a solid device. At a price I paid of $179, this is an awesome product. I think if the price is below $400, it is a great product to consider. It is currently on amazon. With amazon service, I think it is worth the try.

title: I wanted to get a feel for what it is like flying a quadcopter before spending more money on one
text:
This review is for the Parrot Mambo only.

First, you don't need to register this with the FAA. The minimum weight where registration is required is 0.55 lb (8.8 oz). This lightweight guy weighs 2.4 oz with battery, but without any accessories, way below the limit. The entire package it came in weighs under 12 oz.

I bought a small quadcopter before, one that's in the $30 range. I wanted to get a feel for what it is like flying a quadcopter before spending more money on one. The first time I launched it, it crashed into the ceiling. The second time I launched it, it crashed into a wall. No matter how carefully I adjusted the trim, it could never cancel out the drift. I'm sure there are people who can do wonders with it, but I'm not one of them. After a while, I could fly it around for a couple of minutes without crashing into anything, but I would need to move it at a crawl.

So what does an extra $70 get me? A bunch of sensors, I guess. The most obvious is a small camera and what looks like an ultrasound transducer, presumably for measuring the distance to the ground. I assume there's also a bunch of accelerometers and other sensors to check its position while in flight. Whatever they have included, I can say they work, and they work very well.

Together with the quadcopter and battery (3.7V 550 mAh), you get a thick manual (don't get too excited - there's only 11 pages of information in there, but it is in 8 different languages), the grabber, the shooter (and a small pack of plastic pellets), some decals, and a short microUSB cable. There's also a plastic clip thing that I haven't figured out what to use it for - it can attach to the top of the Mambo. What you don't get: controls (you use your Bluetooth smartphone for this - or buy the Flypad for an extra $40), spare propellers, external charger, spare batteries, a high power USB charger - things that you will very likely want if you intend to fly this for more than a few minutes a day. The shooter can only hold up to 6 BBs, and there's not a lot of force behind it, so don't get too excited at the idea of flying around strafing your friends / siblings / kids. They're standard 6mm plastic BBs widely available.

If you're getting this as a Christmas gift and intend to play with it after opening, definitely open up the package, recharge the battery, install the app, and update the firmware before wrapping it up. You do not want to give this to someone, then have them find out that they need to wait 18 minutes while the firmware is updated before they can fly it. Charging the battery also takes up to 30 minutes with a 2.1A charger according to the manual. It comes with a partial charge, but you will want to fully charge it before flying. I tried plugging it into my computer to charge, and it doesn't appear to even start charging. Plugging it into a cell phone charger did the trick.

The app itself is fairly easy to use. The left pad controls altitude and rotation. Right pad makes it move forward and back. You can leave the hulls (bumpers) attached, or you can remove them - the app will ask you what's your configuration. Because there are no spare propellers, I recommend leaving them attached for the first couple of flights unless you're an experienced quadcopter pilot. The app has many customization parameters - you can limit the speed, altitude, etc. while you're getting some experience flying it. There are also some pre-programmed stunts that it can perform. I highly recommend doing that outdoors unless you have a high ceiling. Don't ask :)

To start flying, place it on a flat surface (so that its sensors can calibrate), connect to it, then either press "take off", or launch from your hand. To launch from your hand, tap the top button, which will start the propellers spinning at low power, then lightly toss it in the air. Marvel at how it maintains its position in the air on its own instead of careening all over the room threatening everyone nearby.

Due to its light weight, a light breeze will cause it to sway and drift somewhat, but even then it manage to maintain its position fairly well.

What's not widely advertised, and perhaps for obvious reason, is that the Mambo has a built-in camera. It is, however, a rather low resolution camera, and can only take rather grainy snapshots and no video. Transferring the photos to the phone takes a few seconds each. The first time I tried that it wouldn't connect to download the photos, but exiting the app and relaunching it fixed that. I'm not sure what's the internal storage capacity of the Mambo, but with its limited usefulness I don't see myself exceeding it.

It would be nice if it comes with a simple video camera instead of the grabber and shooter accessories. $100 may not seem too expensive, but do consider the additions - Flypad, batteries, propellers - can easily double that. But it is definitely easier to fly than the cheaper quadcopters.

title: 1.88mmH2O static pressure at 22.5dBA with great flow rate. Fantastic!
text:
I first purchased 4 of these in mid-2013 for a push-pull configuration for my 240 water cooled radiator. They were $8 a piece when I ordered them, but at $15-20 each they're still a great purchase! Not only are they still going strong after heavy use a year and a half later, but they're performance is just as good as new. I've since then purchased six of these, and for the foreseeable future I'm not sure that will change. Here's why:

- PWM! I have a break-out board that controls all of my fans, and PWM is the most efficient way to do that, especially when you have multiple fans running at a time.
- 1.88mmH2O static pressure with 51 CFM at 22.5 dBA at 1800RPM. Basically they maintain high static pressure and airflow but are very quiet! These specs are very similar to most Noctua's which are twice the price, and are ten times as ugly!
- Quality fluid bearings.
- On all the fans I received the exhaust side has 92mm fan spacing holes. This is awesome if you mounted the fans to a rad (Which these are perfect for) and want to mount the exhaust to another part of the case with different sizing. This added flexibility is very much appreciated!
- The white color that I got them in is very clean and professional, and hasn't faded in the slightest. It also matches most other white computer components very well.

When at idle at 700ish RPM, they are dead silent, and for most basic computing that's when they operate anyway. But when you put on your headphones and start up a game, they're going to keep your components cool and not sound like the jet engine many fans are known for!

The only possible down-side to these fans is the lack of any LED ports; a non-issue for me as I prefer a totally dark room when I compute, but this is still a consideration for those looking to light their computers.

The length of the cable, to me, is actually way too long, but for most people that is probably a good thing as it will allow you to place these in multiple locations without extensions, which I've experienced with Ya-Li, Cooler Master and Corsair Fans.

Bottom line: I recommend these to anyone.

title: Close to the original, but not quite there.
text:
I chose to buy this hood over the genuine Fujifilm version for one reason: price. That said, if you are looking for the best hood possible for your 35mm or 23mm f/2, or if you have used the Fuji version, this may not satisfy.

The differences between the two hoods are subtle, but they are there, and for me, they’re enough that I returned this item after comparing it to the Fuji. I’d had the Fuji hood for my 35mm before, and it saved the life of my lens from a nasty fall — so of course, I have a high opinion of that hood. (I also simply don’t like how these “Fujicrons" look without the hood.)

Namely, the Fuji hood is made from a thicker, heavier aluminium, and that’s obvious when you hold the two in hand — I actually ordered the Fuji after I got this in the mail, and felt that it was lighter than I remembered my Fuji being. The JJC hood is also a slightly lighter black than the Fuji, making it match not quite as well on my X-Pro2. The two are nearly identical in size and shape, but the JJC is a little taller (maybe a couple of millimetres), and the angle of the hood is not quite as severe as that of the Fuji. I tried the best I could in the photos to show these differences.

Overall, this is a great product if what you want is to protect your lens from damage (and flare), and the cheap plastic hood that comes in the box isn’t cutting the mustard for you. But if what you want is the quality of the genuine Fujifilm hood, this will get you only, I’d say, 80% there — which isn’t enough for some of us.

I will be sticking to the genuine article from now on.
