title: Most negative review i have ever submitted.
text:
DO NOT buy these speakers unless you want to be forced to rely exclusively on a mobile device (phone or tablet) with (yet another!) required app to control and manage them conveniently. A mobile device app would be convenient as a secondary means of control and management, but it should NOT be the only means! Only a portion of my music library resides on my mobile devices. My ENTIRE music library resides on my PC (in both Apple and Windows media player formats) so of COURSE I would want to control my speakers from my PC! Never mind. I apparently can't stream my music library to the speakers from my PC anyway! How lame! Of course I would not need the app to control the speakers if I only take them down off the shelf, which is situated too high to see or operate the control buttons on the top of the speaker, after first disconnecting the power cable which is routed between the shelf and the wall behind for appearance sake. No, wait! You can't adjust them if they aren't plugged in! So now i can't put the speakers where I want them, unless I climb up on a step stool. Of course Bluetooth is an option that could solve some of these issues - but it is an option that is unacceptable because it degrades sound quality and reduces the speaker's effective wireless range of operation. If I would have wanted cheap, inferior Bluetooth speakers I would not have purchased Wifi speakers! It seems that these design flaws and limitations are built into Wifi speakers in general, not just this particular manufacturer. These just happen to be the speakers I purchased, and I am not happy with wireless speakers that i can't place where I want, listen to what I want, control with my PC, and use to play my PC music library without a smart phone app..No speaker sounds good enough to make up for these limitations IMHO. I will impose a "cooling off" period on myself before returning them. I really wanted these to work for me.
UPDATE: The smartphone app required to control the features and functions of these speakers does not work on my Samsung Galaxy smartphone. That particular issue may well not apply to most who purchase this speaker. And, if like many people, you are happy with the sound of mp3 or other compressed files on your smartphone or ipod nano and bluetooth connectivity, you will be happy with these. I have two of these I wanted to set up in stereo, and switch inputs easily between my TV, my ipod classic and my PC library. With a fubar phone app I am forced to change inputs manually which is a royal inconvenience - as I explained in detail above. To my ears sound quality of a pair of these working in stereo is comparable to something like a Bose 2.1 system - not fine dining sound-wise - but just OK as in "I'm hungry so MacDonald's will be OK" sort of way. If you are like most people (and thank God not like me) you should be pleased with them.

Early Impressions:
I was excited to get this product and it arrived early! However, I am not sure if I will keep it. Here are the reasons:
1) Not Acceptable: The product is shipped without a charger! It has an automobile power cable and it comes with a very short USB cable. However, the device does not allow charging from any USB power source (You can operate it, but not charge it). You need to BUY SEPARATELY a charger. Otherwise, you are limited to charging the device with a car, engine running, and the device off. If the device is running, charging takes forever.
2) I have completed the setup and linking with my iPhone. The process is not for the faint of heart. The most complicated part was finding the "right" Garmin app at the Appstore. You must type exactly "garmin smartphone link". Even then, the store gives you various Garmin and 3rd party apps. I installed Garmin Connect, as it was the first thing that looked right. It took me a while to find the correct product: Garmin Smart Link! Garmin's documentation, not shipped but down-loadable as a PDF, was not much of a help. They use a lot of trademarked product names and jargon that all sound the same, but are not the right one. No phone support was readily available, you need to find the right support page and search.
3) The product looks slick and the screen is bright and easy to read. However, the power connector attaches vertical to the surface at the back center of the device. You can not install it flush with the dashboard or any other surface. The connector would have been much better placed at the edge of the device, providing more flexible installation options.
4) I will post more if I manage to charge the device and take it for a drive.

title: Adds to Echo Spot's Visibility By Raising and Tilting It
text:
This stand is designed to fit the Echo Spot and the Echo Spot ([[ASIN:B073SQYXTW Echo Spot - Black]]) only. It comes in black or white to match the Spot and it magnetically attaches to the bottom of the Spot.

It does two things: it raises the Spot 1 1/2" and it allows the Spot to tilt back and forth.

Is this a necessary addition to the Spot? It depends on what your needs are.

I purchased the Spot to act as a clock radio on my bedside table. The table has a rim around it and without the stand, I would have trouble seeing much of the Spot's screen while I lie in bed. Tilting the Spot back and forth also enhances the visibility of the screen and reduces glare.

The attachment is magnetic. The Spot sits firmly on the stand. I've found that it's best to lift the Spot and stand together. If you lift just the Spot, the stand (which has a non-skid base) sometimes will stay put and the Spot separates from it and will be in your hand.

The non-skid base on the stand keeps things firmly in place. With the Spot on top, nothing is moving around unintentionally.

If you are unsure if you require the stand, purchase the Spot first [[ASIN:B073SRJD46 Echo Spot - White]] and if you think a stand will enhance its visibility, you can always purchase it later.

My only 'gripe' is that the port for the lightning cable has no leeway making it a requirement that the cable used does not have any excess bulk (there are some 3rd party lightning accessories and chargers that are a no-go with this case on that work fine with other cases). On the flip-side, this is not so much a negative as it means that there is additional material protecting the underside of the iPhone.

The only reason I can't give this five stars is because I find myself once a week where the corner near the headphone jack pops off while in my pocket. The case slips back on securely and I have no issues afterwards, but this may be due to the pants / shorts I am wearing and how the iPhone sits in my pocket. title: Very sturdy and accurate
text:
Very sturdy and accurate. Tracks beautifully! First trackball I've tried where I didn't need to adjust to it in that respect. Because the ball is held in place by something other than gravity, it does work well at a 45-50 degree angle. I really wanted to be able to keep this one, but it's just too big for my hand (6.5 inches) and hard to click. It was hard to find a position where I could comfortably rest my wrist and hand while using it. I tried using various cloths to use as a rest but with the trackball at an angle, the ball was just too high to find a good position without interfering with the right click button (I mouse left-handed).

I could have probably found a way around that issue eventually, but my biggest problem was actually the buttons. I'm not sure if it's normal or if it was just this unit, but the bottom half of the mouse buttons was much harder to click than the top half. Since my thumbs are where most of my pain is, it made left clicking with my thumb pretty painful after only a couple of hours at work. The top half of the buttons was easier (not as easy as the Logitech Trackman Marble, but easier than the bottom half), but I was having a lot of trouble clicking with my forefinger without moving the ball. And it was also a little uncomfortable to reach the button due to my smaller fingers.

The scroll wheel was also too far away for me and I found it hard to scroll one "click" at a time. If I had kept this mouse, I would have probably switched the mouse control panel from scrolling "screens" to scrolling "lines". I didn't bother using their software CD; I just downloaded X-Mouse button control from the internet. I didn't try using the third button. I really wish they made a smaller version of this trackball. I loved the idea of adding the extra buttons as well. I would definitely recommend this trackball, but only for people with larger hands than mine. Or at least people who don’t have RSI in their thumbs.

title: Very impressive bass reponse
text:
These earbuds are on the edge of current headphone technology and as such, many of its shortcomings will be forgiven in this review because of this, and I'll explain why. These headphones can best be described as the CIA plugs you see on many movies and TV shows. Once you place these in your ear comfortably, you will forget that they are even there. It is a very strange experience the first time, but afterwards you'll wonder why you dealt with headphones that were any larger.

Wireless Connectivity
In my opinion, this is one of the most important aspects of a wireless pair of ear buds. After you take these ear buds out of the package, you sync them one time with your phone and they always connect, every time there after. These ear buds feature a heartbeat sensor which also can detect when you place the buds in your ear. Simply place the bud in your ear and a soft voice will give you a confirmation "Connected," each and every time you put them in your ears. It's impressive after the first few days after getting used to connecting Bluetooth headphones sporadically.

Sound Quality
People will certainly argue with this perspective, but I personally believe these headphones rival the loudness and bass of the Powerbeats Wireless earbuds. After owning those particular earbuds for over a year and a half, these earbuds do not have any compromise in sound at a reasonable volume.

*They are very impressive when you turn your head the first hear the clear bass and turn your head to realize there is no headphones visible on either side of your head. It's a neat experience.

Battery Life
The third most important aspect of these headphones, and as I have mentioned before, these are at the forefront of headphone technology. From experience these headphones can last 1 to 1/5 hours on a charge streaming, and around 3 hours with pre-loaded music. For most work-out applications these headphones meet expectations. The sense of freedom when you first wear these headphones in the gym is unmatched.

Pros:
Fits perfectly for working out
Awesome design with functional touch controls
Comparable sound to Powerbeats
4GB of on-board memory on each earbud

Cons
Limited battery life for some uses
Price

title: Awesome system, easy to install
text:
I had a 10 year old, wired alarm system, no longer monitored, and when it recently decided to start beeping at me every night at 11:45 with no way to make it stop, I had to replace it. Since my needs are pretty simple, I didn't want to get involved with the big companies, I looked into 2GIG as a possible replacement. It looked like I could use their [[ASIN:B005LX15LO 2gig TAKE Switch Wireless Takeover Module]] to use all of the existing wired contacts and put that to work for me in the new wireless system.

Before I made the decision, I went to the 2GIG site and called Linear, to see if I could use this system strictly to have it beep for zone openings if I desired. I spoke to a very pleasant and helpful employee, who informed me that while the system is designed to be installed by dealers, yes, it should be possible to install it and use it in that way. So I bought this control panel and the takeover module, and today I installed them.

I started by checking out some YouTube videos on installation and programming for the system, which were very helpful. There's one that's about an hour long that's a full training session on the entire system. This control panel has a touch screen, and the system is easy to configure. I will say, the video walk through I found made it super easy, but the same information is available to read.

My system is 6 zones (you can have up to eight on one panel, plus you can link panels to create additional zones, if you so desire). This system allows for two wired zones in addition to the wireless ones.

You can choose from a variety of chimes and/or voice info when a zone is opened, which is handy in certain situations. There are people in my home who are at risk for wandering due to medical conditions, so knowing which zone has been opened by choosing to include voice with the chime makes it easier for me to know where to look, in case someone is leaving when he or she shouldn't be. That was actually a problem for me with the old system, which only had a chime and I had to run around the house to figure out which door or window had been opened--so I consider this a huge benefit!

I was worried it might not be loud enough, but alerts from the control panel can be easily heard through my mostly open, one story home. When I tested the alarm when armed, the alarm was quite loud, so it will definitely wake me up if a zone is opened during the night.

There are several companies that can monitor this alarm system if you wish, or you can choose to disable call outs. That's handy if you just want to be notified of zone openings, or to arm the system at night to wake you if there's a problem. (Naturally, if you disable that feature, it won't help much if your alarm goes off with no one home, and if you ARE home, you have to call 911 on your own...but if you're on a budget and your primary concern is wandering, it's a way to monitor entry and egress without paying a monthly fee.)

I installed both the takeover module and control panel in about 5 hours, maybe less. That includes the time it took to program and test the system completely, and bearing in mind I've never worked with an alarm system before, so I'm very much a beginner and had to go slowly with the old wiring. During that time, I did have to run out to the store for some wire...they don't include wire to connect the control panel to the plug-in transformer, so be prepared! It's easy to do, but wire is helpful.

One of the really cool things that excites me about this system is its flexibility, and the fact I can add more features going forward, including home automation. I'm looking forward to trying some of them out in the future.

All in all, 2GIG provides a relatively inexpensive way to take over existing systems like mine, or set up a home security and automation system a bit at a time for those on a budget. So far, I'm very pleased.

title: Careful, R6700v2. Terrific router when it works but Netgear support is shareholder-centric (not customer).
text:
ROUTER: Excellent when it works and it has done so with little to no hiccups for about a year now. It is most definitely the R6700v2 that I received and that means MediaTek chip, not Broadcom so there is no custom hardware to load on it. I dealt with that ok and the stock Web UI is easy enough to learn and work with. I wasn't doing anything fancy with it anyway, just device connectivity, gaming and movie streaming. The router was purchased in April of 2017 and the warranty is close to expiring (2 weeks away). It has started having issues with the 5Ghz radio and not broadcasting SSID/dropping connections. This got progressively worse and worse until the 5Ghz radio has stopped working altogether. Troubleshot it with all available information and called support in the end.

SUPPORT/WARRANTY: I started the painful quest of getting support and an RMA from Netgear not expecting much. My expectations are quite low calling into level 1 support usually anyway, everyone knows you have to be patient and work through it with the person on the other end whose job it is to listed to people complain all day. The gentleman was kind and polite though he asked me to repeat my name and email 4 times in a row. I explained the situation and he understood that the troubleshooting options were now exhausted so we moved on to the next step and this is where things got ridiculous. You see netgear will provide you with free, "good" support for 90 days after your purchase. The gentleman said my options were to either purchase 1yr of premium support @ ~$120 or 2yrs @ ~$200. They will then be able to work with you to issue an RMA request if it's found that it's a warranty issue, at which point they'll refund your money back. I politely declined and explained to the fellow that for that kind of money i can just buy a new router and there's nothing compelling me to buy Netgear again since I saw their idea of customer service. He did not budge and I finally asked to speak with a supervisor. Supervisor was too busy assisting customers so my man hooked it up with and RMA as a one time favor to me and I am set to receive a new router sometime in the future. At least the RMA process was decent enough. Either you pay nothing and send your unit in (you pay for shipping) and they send you a replacement out, pay 15-20 to get a replacement and a return label for your broken one or pay 20-30 to get an overnight replacement and a return label. I get it, businesses are built to make money but this just didn't seem like a good way to do it. My advice, if you have to go the RMA route, is to just be polite, persistent and don't pay for the premium support just to get the privilege of getting a warranty replacement.

TL;DR - Great, trouble-free router when working with no custom firmware options. Netgear support needs lots of patience and persistence.

title: Have used this for many years in several locations
text:
This is my old reliable antenna; I've purchased two others in the past. It says a lot about a product when the design remains unchanged over the years. Mine is hooked up to a converter box with a twelve year old Panasonic tv and the hi-def broadcasts look great. I get all of my local over-the-air channels plus PBS.

To get the best results place it near a window and point it in the direction of your local broadcast tower. Also find a spot where it won't get knocked over because the rabbit ears are delicate and break easily. I occasionally have to reposition it if extremely windy weather interferes with the signal. title: ASUS service and support are lacking for Z170 Deluxe motherboard
text:
I purchased the ASUS Z170 Deluxe motherboard in November of 2015. The board ran quite well for 6 months when it failed outright in April, 2016. My system was a Windows 10 home brew with an i7-6700K CPU, 16 GB G. Skills TridentZ 3200Htz DDR4 RAM, 256GB AHCI Samsung SM-951 M.2 PCIe 3.0 x 4 SSD, 2 WDC-WD10EZEX 1 TB drives in RAID 1, and EVGA GeForce GTX 960 Video Card. They are all premium parts; not the best of their brand, but all brand name parts.

When the failure occurred, ASUS refused to replace the board with a new unit and offered me an advanced exchange where they sent me the replacement board while I returned the defective board. Of course, they charged my credit card $320 until my original board was returned. I had the new board within 3 days and it failed after only 20 minutes in my system. I went back to ASUS support and this time they refused an advance replacement and I had to ship the new board in for repair. This took 2 weeks and when I received the repaired board back, it failed in less than a single day of operation.

This procedure went on for 3 more exchanges where I had to ship the board back and wait 2 weeks to receive the supposedly repaired board. Each time a board was received by me, it exhibited different problems that caused total failure. After 4 exchanges, I threatened ASUS with going to court for a refund, but I finally agreed to accept a fifth repair. When the fifth exchange failed, I told them I was definitely taking them to court, but they offered yet another, sixth return. I outright refused return #6 and filed the papers for small claims court here in New Jersey. When a court date was set up for early September, 2016, ASUS agreed to a refund of $480.00 for the board, my shipping costs, and my filing fees for the court case. The failures left me without use of my system for more than 4 months and, in August, 2016, I purchased an ASRock Z170 OC Formula with my refund. Excluding minor Windows 10 issues, the ASRock board has run superbly.

The ASUS Z170 Deluxe board looks to me to be the most feature rich Z170 board on the market, but I will never purchase another ASUS product, especially a motherboard. This fiasco went on for 4 months where ASUS could not give me a functional motherboard or effectively repair the motherboard I returned to their service organization. Their outrageous refusal to agree to a refund after 6 failures was totally unacceptable. The board ran exceptionally well for 6 months and I don’t know what happened after that.

If you purchase an ASUS motherboard, you have to take into consideration that their philosophy is “No Refunds” and that their engineering resources may be lacking. My first ASUS motherboard, a P8Z77-V Pro had to be exchanged twice in the first year, but it is running quite well today after 4 years. When I bought the Z170 Deluxe, I figured I would not run into a similar problem, but I was dead wrong. The experience with the Z170 board was much worse.

Service and support are intangibles that are very often overlooked when purchasing a motherboard or computer peripherals. Don’t make the mistakes I did.

Update -- March 3, 2018

The ASRock Z170 OC formula ran perfectly for a year and would still be going, but I've upgraded to a new i7-8700k 6-core CPU and an ASRock Z370 Professional Gaming K6 motherboard and the system is running superbly. I figured 6 cores was worth the upgrade even though the Z170 OC Formula board was only a year old, I will still not purchase another ASUS product and doubt if I will ever change my mind on that issue.

title: A well made MLC NAND SATA3 SSD with great compatibility and quality.
text:
I've been using SATA3 SSDs for years. Those include the Plextor M6 Pro / Plextor M6S / Samsung 850 Pro / Samsung 860 Pro and Transcend SSD 360S. Among them, Plextor M6 Pro and M6S were the first ones for me and they have been impressive, although I had to replace my first M6 Pro due to initial recognition failure. After replacement the Plextor SSDs seemed to work flawlessly. Recently I'm using Samsung 850 Pro and 860 Pro at my workplace and on my laptop. They have been working flawlessly without any kind of event until now. Recently I purchased Transcend 360S and installed it onto my old laptop with SATA2 interface. Initially it seemed to work nice but after less than a week of use, my old laptop occasionally freezes up and I had to wait for more than tens of seconds to work with it again. And it was my first experience in which I regretted my purchase of SSD.

I think Samsung SSDs are one of those having the greatest compatibility to various systems and quality and durability. As I do not want to get disappointed as time goes on, I may go further with those Samsung SATA3 SSDs. Compatibility? Its just Okay for Samsung. A lot of reviewers protested they are compatible with various systems they have / Reliability? There are a great number of people that say they purchase only Samsung SATA SSDs. / Speed? While speed is always next to reliability for me, my test result was best with Samsung SSDs, followed by Plextor MLC SSDs. / Price? Recently the prices for Samsung SSDs are decreasing suddenly and significantly. And I think the price itself may mean nothing unless the SSDs are compatible, reliable and fast enough.

I'm thinking of purchasing a number of Samsung 860 Pro SSDs to store my music and movie files and as frequent backing drive. I think it is also good for Samsung to let the customers know whether they are buying an MLC NAND SSD or a TLC one, while there are a number of brands who does not give important information about their product to the customers. What else to say??

title: Once this was a 5 star router, until connectivity problems surfaced
text:
A month or two go, I would have written a FIVE star review. But just recently, I have connectivity issues. I was using independent 2G and 5G Wi-Fi endpoints, but consolidated them under a single name and password. When they were separate, everything was fine.

I started having the internet drop off after a while. My suspicion was that this started after I tried using Disney Circle - Netgear pushes this subscription service for parental control. I tried it, but dropped it when there were connection problems. I removed it and since reset the device back to factory settings.

Since then, smart home devices are no longer getting to the Internet. Phones received browser messages that the Internet was down. We only use streaming TV services, and those were working. I knew it was a Wi-Fi connectivity issue. Oddly, my laptop was connecting fine. Until it started dropping as well.

It just seems like a few devices were being dropped, then all of them were being dropped.

Searches on the Netgear site tell you to reset the router to factory settings -- which I did to no avail. I combined the wireless networks under a single SSID and password. But that worked only when you got on the 5G connection. Upgrading the router firmware did not correct the issue either. What's more - people were adamant that the newer firmware made the problems worse. I cannot conclude or disprove this.

All I know is that we have had this router for a while and it suddenly started indiscriminately dropping devices from the network.

I cannot recommend this router until Netgear can get their firmware issues in order.

title: The Silverstone Argon heatsinks are the best heatsinks you can buy in the sub $50 range
text:
The Silverstone Argon heatsinks are the best heatsinks you can buy in the sub $50 range, and I'd even recommend them over the Noctua and other brand heatsinks which sell for much more. Now, why would you pay an extra 20 dollars for the Argon AR03 version vs the Hyper 212? The Hyper 212 design is terrible, as in the base to attach the heatsink to the motherboard is terrible. I can't tell you how many times I've had to remove and reapply TIM to a cpu because the heatsink kept sliding around and messing up because of the design of the Hyper 212, trying to screw it into the motherboard with the flimsy x-bar. With the Argon AR03, you just attach the base, put on the TIM, then stick on the heatsink, then put the bar over the heatsink, then screw in two screws - all of which can be done without sliding the heatsink everywhere.

I recommend any of these Silverstone Argon heatsinks, primarily because the base design uses the much superior screw in bar.

I did remove one star however, the fan that it comes with is terrible. Buying almost any 4 pin fan will put out more CFM and cool your heatsink faster.

title: So this is what a flagship portable headphone sounds like...
text: I got this headphone used in "like new" amazon condition. Proud owner of the Sennheiser Momentum, AKG Q701, Denon AHD 600, Beyerdynamic Custom One Pros, Audiotechnica ATH M50, and Grado RS2i. I just happened to have just enough money from saving and decided to go for one of my dream headphones. I definitely never imagined that one day I would even think of going to the 1000 dollar plus territory. I was initially deciding on either the T5P 2nd gens, the Fostex TH900 mk2, Audeze LCD XC, Final Design Sonorous VI, or MrSpeakers Ether C since I have friends who owner a few of these and others were auditioned in a store. I settled with the T5P since it had the best isolation of the others and was most comfortable. Those who tested These headphones claim that they are also good at every genre, so it was a no brainer for me. I can't imagine going portable with the Fostex being that they don't feel as solid or durable. Not to mention that they leak. LCD XC is honestly very detailed but has a very small soundstage for that price and even compared to the T5P for significantly less. It's also unbearably uncomfortable being hands down the heaviest headphones I've ever worn (LCD 3 is a close 2nd obviously). I didn't find enough info on the Final Design Sonorous VI (they do look sexy) and no one I know owns them. I almost bought the Ether C but they are harder to drive and don't feel as comfortable to wear long term. The winner is T5P 2nd gen! The sound quality and accuracy of the Ether C is worth boasting over all the other headphones for sure, but needless to say, it ain't that much of an improvement over the T5P. Not enough to justify the much higher price tag. If Ether C is a 10/10 closed back headphone, I will gladly give T5P a 9.5/10. That good and worlds better than all of my other headphones. I was surprised that it was more detailed than my Grado RS2i and had a bigger soundstage than my AKG Q701. The bass was so full of extension and punchy when the recording called for it. I heard the 1st T5P had a treble overload. They definitely have treble, but it is soothing and wasnt buried behind the bass and mids. These headphones feel like an open headphone and I can't recommend them enough.

title: Great for tunes while swimming laps
text:
I recently began swimming laps for exercise. I have always listened to music when working out and was frustrated by the need to leave my usual earbuds in my gym bag while in the pool. This MP3 player solves that problem.

At first I thought waterproof bluetooth earbuds would be the best choice for me but it turns out bluetooth doesn't transmit well under water. I gave this MP3 player a try and am very happy with it. The sound quality from it while in the water is not as good as what you'd get from high quality non-waterproof earbuds but it is still pretty good- amazing considering The MP3 player pops out of the back of the headband and then plugs into a USB port to be loaded. Loading it with music just required dragging and dropping the songs I wanted onto the icon for the MP3 player. I swim 45-60 minutes per day, 5-6 days/week and have gone 2-3 weeks without charging this. I've never had the battery die on it so I don't know how many hours of play you could get out of it before needing to charge it.

I have a fairly big head but this fits comfortably. It does not interfere with the straps for my goggles and controlling it while wearing it is easy as the volume, pause/play, and rewind/fast forward buttons are intuitively placed. The earbuds do get a bit warm in your ears while using this, but not uncomfortably so. The wire from the headband to the earbuds does seem somewhat fragile, so I am careful about never pulling the headband off my head by the wires or pulling the earbuds out of my ears by the wires. I know others reviewing this have found those wires to be a failure point. I'll update this review if that is ever an issue for me.

title: "Scream at me until my ears bleed."
text:
These Sony headphones are used in recording studios all over the world and are the industry standard for studio monitoring. This must mean they are the best headphones ever, right? Wrong. It depends on what you are using them for. Yes, they are very revealing and you hear every detail, and that is why they are used in production. However, in order to achieve that level of transparency and clarity, they have an EXTREME treble response, and as such, makes them too fatiguing for enjoyable home listening. Listening to an album in these is like being screamed at for an hour, directly in your ears, by someone with the most shrill and irritating voice you've ever heard. Don't get me wrong. They do sound amazing, as for being able to hear every detail, and I went back and forth over whether to keep or return them, but after listening to them all day and constantly adjusting the volume, I decided it's just not worth it. While I do prefer headphones that reveal every detail, these don't do so in a way that is pleasing to listen to. I own a pair of Sennheiser HD 595's and they are very bright, revealing phones, but they are open backed and non fatiguing. If I put my hands over the openings, however, they sound more shrill like these Sonys. I have come to the conclusion that Sony has made the sound of these headphones too bright for a closed back headphone. All that treble trapped in a closed headphone is just painful to listen to.
For studio monitor, audiophile quality headphones for home listening, I would suggest instead the Sennheiser HD 280 Pro for the same price as the Sonys. I had purchased the Sennheisers first, then exchanged for the Sonys after being told they were better and listening to them in the store. I thought they were better upon first listening, but after listening at home for a longer period of time, I realized how harsh the highs really are. I returned them again and went back to my original purchase of the Sennheiser HD 280 Pro. The Sennheisers offer great clarity and transparency, but do so in a more relaxed presentation that is easier on the ears. They also have better bass, but are well balanced overall. NOTE: To anyone thinking I may have gotten a fake pair, they were purchased brand new at Guitar Center, so highly unlikely.

title: Worked for Two Weeks, Then Nothing But Trouble
text: I purchased this router as an upgrade to our home network because our previous router didn't have the WAN-LAN throughput necessary for us to fully utilize the speed of our cable Internet connection. What a mistake this router was – I should have listened to the negative reviews here. It froze on me during the initial setup, but then worked fine after that for about two weeks. Then, my cat stepped on the power switch to the surge protector that this router was plugged into, turning off the power. I saw it happen, rebooted everything, and then started dealing with the router freezing up after a few minutes, which could only be resolved by a reboot. I spent several hours troubleshooting this, and never getting a connection to work for more than about 10 minutes. I was able to trace the problem to the router, as the modem was working fine, as was everything else on our network. I filed a warranty claim and Amazon sent me a replacement overnight. I got that one set up, and it worked, but it did seem like web pages were slow to load. The next morning, I was back to constant drops and freezes of the Internet connection when it was plugged into this router, which were not happening if our cable modem was connected directly to a computer, or to our wireless router, which normally just operates as a Wi-Fi access point. I gave up, returned the second unit, and ordered an equivalent D-Link model instead. And, that model worked right out of the box, has been trouble-free so far, and is MUCH faster. I've had good luck with Netgear products before, especially from their ProSAFE line, but this router is just too unreliable.

title: We have some unfortunate neighbors that really like to steal things
text:
This sensor almost does what it's supposed to do- sense vehicles and people that might come up our rural, private driveway. We have some unfortunate neighbors that really like to steal things, so this sensor has actually alerted us to someone coming up our driveway one evening, up to no good. We were able to chase him off before he broke into our vehicle, so I'm grateful for that.
However- only one sensor will ever work. We've followed the instruction booklet, looked online, tried everything to get both to work at the same time but they simply will not work. One of the sensors is literally sitting on my desk right now. The red light goes off, on both, but the alarm will not sound. And which one works will change, which is annoying when it's time to change batteries.
About that alarm- holy crap, what an annoying sound. It has two volumes, ear piercing and not quite so ear piercing. To maximize how well it works we have it in the window sill that faces the sensor mounted about 50 feet away and is in clear "site". I'd say it works about 80% of the time, but for those 20% times when it doesn't work you can walk right beside the sensor, jump up and down in front of it, and it won't sound. The little red light usually comes on, but not every time. (We actually plan to cover the red light, it defeats the hope that we can respond to someone coming up the drive before they know they've been detected.
Annoyingly, it also alarms if sunlight filters through the trees at 6:30am on a summer morning, if a cat or possum creeps up the drive (but only at night), or if leaves are falling on dry autumn days. Oh, we live in the woods... this happens a lot. It's really annoying.
We'll keep it and continue to use it but I can't say I would recommend this to everyone.

title: From a Theta m15 and Giroptic 360cam owner.
text:
Fantastic upgrade from the Ricoh Theta m15, and WAY BETTER overall than the 360cam from Giroptic.

My first experience with 360 photos was an old mirror attachment (SurroundPhoto) that connected to a normal camera. You would shoot images with the camera pointing up, and software would convert the round image in to a panorama. Those images had limited up/down viewing (they could not look directly up or down at all), and the setup was fragile and bulky.

When I learned of the Giroptic 360cam Kickstarter back in 2014, I signed up. They did not even come close to making their original delivery date of November 2014 -- I received my unit in summer of 2016! During the time I was waiting, I found out about the Ricoh Theta m15 (the second model). I bought one, and thought it was great, but the image quality was not great, and it did not have good low-light capability.

When the Theta S was announced, I sold my m15 and went to order the new model. Unfortunately, it was back ordered for months (I should have checked that before selling my m15). While I was waiting, my 360cam finally arrived. The Theta has spoiled me with how fast it was, and how convienient (it easily fits in a pocket). The 360cam was bulky and had such a large base, you could not look directly down (it would put a circular graphic at the bottom of the image). It was also painfully slow -- taking almost a minute just to turn on, and nearly as long to switch from photo to video mode. After a week of using it, I sold it and used the money to buy a Theta S.

The Theta S is everything the m15 was, but better. Better pictures in daylight, and much better pictures in low light. The controls are improved -- you can toggle between video and photo mode with a dedicated button (the earlier models required you to hold down a button while powering up). The power, WiFi and mode buttons are very simple. The only thing you need to remember is how to enable the new self-timer mode (that requires holding down WiFi while powering up).

The camera can be customized (self timer duration, etc.) using a mobile app. I have used the iOS app on my iPad and an old iPhone. The Theta can act like a WiFi base, and you connect your phone to it then run the app. You can trigger the camera via the phone, or toggle modes and adjust settings. You can also get a live preview of what the camera is seeing - very useful.

I was able to take about 350 pictures once day, and a short video (a few minutes lone) on a single batter charge. The next day, I took 100-200 more photos, and a 10+ minute video, and still have plenty of battery left. And, I never had to download to free up memory. The internal memory is more than enough for tons of photos.

I expect doing nothing but video shooting and using WiFi would fill up memory and run down batteries much faster ;-)

The only negative I have seen is an annoying red spot that appears in images taken in sunlight. From reading posts online, this is a defect of how the lenses work -- though I never noticed this with the m15. The spot is in different locations, too, so unless you use the video preview on a phone, I don't know if you can do anything to control where it will be when taking a photo in bright light.

Overall, I love this device. It's super easy to use, and you can share photos to Facebook and they play back in 360. You can also upload to the Theta website (public searchable, or unlisted to only those you give the link to can see it). There are also free plug ins for websites to let visitors view these photos. I use one of them on my Wordpress blog site.

I wish Ricoh had included a belt strap on the camera case like the m15 came with. I liked being able to carry it on my belt rather than have to carry a pouch or camera bag with me.

I will update this review with more details if my opinions change after using it for a few more months.

title: So far, so good. Better quality than HP.
text:
Great product so far! I've had this printer for about a week and so far I'm very impressed. I had a lot of printers over the years and all of them have been HP. After destroying my old HP printer by putting off brand ink in it (their ink and new ink refill program are really expensive), I decided to try a Brother. I print a decent volume of items, but usually in batches, so I may not print much for a few months, then print a couple hundred pages in a couple days. With the HP auto refill program it just didn't make sense for my ink usage. I decided to try this Brother because it includes 2400 pages of black and 1200 pages of color worth of ink.
My first impressions of this device out of the box is how can it be this small? I've gotten used to the HP Officejet 8000 series, which is at least more than double the size of the Brother. I have a small home office, so the space is much appreciated. The build quality also seems to be a little better than the HP printers. There is not as much paper storage in the tray, but there's plenty for me. The print quality is great for what I have printed so far. Document with text look good and crisp, even in fast mode. I also tried to print an edgeless 4x6 and it turned out great.
Scanning on this printer is easy and painless. I was amazed at the speed the ADF scans, especially compared to my old HP. The included PageManager software is even pretty helpful, which is uncommon in my experience for printer software. Scan quality is good, I haven't tested it with images though.
I had no issues setting it up with OS X, which impressed me. I always had problems with HP printers (especially the scanner function) connecting to my Macs.
So, we will see how long this printer last, I'm hoping that the ink will last me over a year, maybe even two. I wish that I would have had one of these in college, I would go through the 2400 pages in a semester.

title: Jingle Bells
text:
The first thing I noticed when I unpacked this backpack was the jingly jangly noise made by the zipper pulls. This was annoying, but I could have tolerated it if the other features were not wanting.

The interior laptop pocket is not well padded, and is not well separated from other items in the same inner compartment. I much prefer a pack that has a dedicated laptop compartment; this one has a pocket with a retaining strap within the main comparment. This is the main reason for the existence of this type of backpack, and so I found it inadequate and returned it, despite its other desirable features.

Despite this, there were several features that I liked about this backpack:
The contrastingly-colored lining makes it easier to find things.
The multiple mesh zippered pockets provide a good storage space with easy access for small accessories like USB adapters, memory cards, flash drives and such.
The "garage" on the bottom of the pack is a great storage space for power supplies and bulkier items that you don't want to just throw in the bottom of the bag.
The backpack appears to be well constructed, and is relatively inexpensive compared to similar high quality packs.

One other issue I had is that the tablet compartment is too small to hold my 12 inch iPad, but I knew that in advance; almost none of the laptop backpacks that I've looked at can handle the largest iPad (the Incase Icon that I bought has the same issue), so I didn't hold that out as a negative feature against this eBags pack.

title: What Hifi product of the year is my new ear buds of a lifetime. The Sony mdr-ex650 is sensational.
text: Simply the best in ear headphones I've used. The upgrade from budget in ears are beyond my expectations. I'm a big music lover of all genres from opera to hip hop to heavy metal and electronic music. I did fairly extensive research before settling on these sony. It was what hifi's product of the year 2014. So i decided to take the chance on them. I was a bit skeptical at first since the magazine rated it so highly, especially for the price. Hearing and listening is so subjective but I knew what I wanted my in ears to sound like, no too clinical and sanitized but rather dynamic and lively. From the moment I played he first song it blew me away! Skeptic no more. What hifi stated that these sonys can handle anything you throw at them and they were right. Super tight bass and clear open mids and highs. I like to listen to my music extremely loud and for the first time ever I've found headphones that forces me to turn down the volume on some songs. Some reviews I've read says the bass is not that strong, well to my ears they are awesome on my hip hop and dance tunes. I've had these for about three weeks now and even though they aren't even burned in yet they still sound amazing. These are worth trying out if you want an upgrade from stock mp3 ear buds that come with an ipod etc. I did critical listening using my headphone out from my behringer mixer, headphone out from a technics home theatre reciever, an ipod shuffle and nano, my studio software output from my desktop. They all sounded incredible. Then I decided to pair theses earbuds to a fiio 6 portable headphone amp, the sony earbuds sound went to a whole new level! I cannot even begin to tell you how much better a great product to begin with sounded even more incredible. Lastly I upgraded the ear tips to the comply t200 isolation tips and sound leakage and isolation was even better. These sony paired with my fiio e6 and the comply tips takes my modest mobile music enjoyment well past my expectations given my whole set up cost less than $120. But even if it cost double that it would still be an unbelievable deal. An ipod shuffle, fiio e6 has changed the way I think about music on the go forever, working out at my gym has never been more inspiring. The sony is incredible, paired with the fiio e6, they are absolutely awe inspiring. And for about $70 for the sony, $30 for the fiio, $15 for the comply t200 tips Id give 6 or 7 star rating if I could. I love my sennheiser momentum over ear headphones but I really love my sony ex650. The icing on the cake is the brass finish is beautiful, I have the gray/black ones and I'll be buying the gold brass ones soon.

title: I only buy an AV system every 15 years so this had to be a good one. It is!
text:
4 stars compared to systems at any price. 5 if you are talking this price point...

I only buy an AV system about once every 15 years so I wanted this one to be future proof and a good value. It's replacing an early 2000's Yamaha 7.1 surround system set up in a 6.1 configuration. Speakers are Paradigm Atoms (5 each), an Energy center, 8" hand me down Infinity subwoofer, all set in the corner of the family room (diagonal configuration) with a Samsung 54" HD TV. After re-foaming and gluing the Paradigms one too many times, it's just time to take the plunge. Faithful servants to retire to the office.

My previous audio system is an old analog Yamaha CR620 receiver, Pioneer towers, Bose 301 book shelfs and direct drive Pioneer PL-518 turn table which I bought new in 1977, kept restored and now use to listen to mostly vinyl records in the garage. (There was a Sony 5.1 system somewhere in the middle but it was pretty much crap)

In this search I was at a loss as to where to start. I had to educate myself which brought me up to speed on Atmos and DTS:X, two new immersive audio standards. Onkyo, Pioneer, Klipsch and Yamaha came up as ahead of the trend. I was intrigued with what I read about Andrew Jones' work at Pioneer and CNET's reviews had me sold on the SP-BS22A group...until I researched further and found the ELAC's buried in CNET and other audiophile reviews. Andrew's encore at ELAC was vastly improved over the Pioneers. A Yamaha receiver was always the top choice just because I'm impressed with everything they make (except speakers). The Debut was touted as ground breaking. I really liked what I read about the Uni-Fi series but not the premium price. I was fortunate enough to find a high end integrator locally who demo'd the F5 and I was sold on the Debut series.

I set the new ELAC system up in the basement at work to break them in as a 5.1.4 system that will wind up at home eventually. The entire system is comprised of a pair of F5's in front, B5 surrounds, C5 front center (on back order), S10EQ sub, and 2 pairs of Atmos A4 speakers. All attached to a Yamaha A3050 receiver with a Samsung 3D/4K (UBD-K8500) blu ray player. Temporary components include an old 780p Sony LCD TV and a Cambridge Newton center channel while the C5 is on back order.

The "shop" is all concrete walls and floors with galvanized steel covered concrete ceiling. Essentially, a bunker by construction. The system is between two parallel I-beams (front to back) in the ceiling which focuses the sound stage within a 10Wx15Lx10H boundary. (The actual floor width of the space is 60 ft.) The B5's are sitting on a pair of solid Pangea LS300 stands that I intend to fill with sand or buckshot at home. The acoustics in this space really works, especially with the fire proofing on the ceiling and I-beams. There is also a throw rug and soft furniture to absorb reverb. It is not echo-y at all.

Visually the whole system just looks "all together". The Atmos A4 speakers fit perfectly flush in all dimensions on top of the F5 and B5 speakers. Unlike the F6/B6 and Uni-Fi models which make the A4’s look like an add-on. I imagine the next iteration of this speaker system will have the A4 integrated in the same housing, like the Pioneers. (I couldn’t wait for that evolution.) The vinyl finish of the ELACs is not glossy which resists fingerprints. It’s a high quality vinyl that looks too similar to a vinyl record album be coincidental. Nice touch in my opinion. The face of the Yamaha receiver is simple and subdued with all controls hidden behind a flip down panel. The real business is happening in the back of the receiver. There’s a lot going on back there. Every connection you could want and more.

As break in time has increased, the sound from the speakers is definitely "relaxing" and getting better each day. The S10EQ sub really completes the sound range. You just can't beat the extra bass you get from the sub with the cross over set at 120 hz and sonic deep dives down to 28 hz. I have not used Yamaha's YPAO system to tune the sound to the room yet but I'm anxious to do it once the C5 arrives in the next couple of weeks.

I've ordered a few movies with the Atmos and DTS:X immersive audio. So far it's just an outstanding upgrade over standard surround sound. The overhead imaging truly needs to be experienced. In an early street fight in The Expendables 3, there's a scene where Mel Gibson is shooting one of the team with a rifle from above, in a helicopter. The ceiling space between the I beams could have actually been the blades of the chopper itself! The tinkling of glass just engulfs you from all angles. Bass is clear with ooomph when called on but not overwhelming. You feel the whump whump whump of the chopper blades in your bones. Music is simply fabulous. I prefer the 9 ch stereo setting the most but the various sound stages are fun to play with. They work really well for Fleetwood Mac (Amsterdam theater) but not so for Pink Floyd which needs an immersive stage. I've only been streaming music from iCloud and Pandora but hope to put some CD's in the player soon.

I'll update this review as parts come in and it moves to the family room next month.

title: Who the Hell is David Cooper?
text:
Periodically, Alexa will pipe up (unprovoked), and say "Now connected to David Cooper's computer!". I do not know David Cooper, but I live in a building with 78 condo units in it, so I think it's safe to assume he must be close by.

The first time she did this at 3am I sprinted naked through the house to unplug her and left her that way for months. When I finally couldn't stand not making my grocery shopping list while cooking dinner any longer, I plugged her back in. Within less than a day, she was back in bed with David Cooper.

This time, I tried a tentative "Alexa - DISconnect from David Cooper's computer?". "OK!" she replied, "disconnecting from David Cooper's computer." Problem solved! But no, the very next day... "Now connected to David Cooper's computer!", which has now evolved into a daily tango of Alexa cozying up to Mr. Cooper and me reprimanding her back down again.

Yesterday I heard voices of someone talking in the hall outside of my unit, but eventually noticed they seemed to be standing right outside my door and not moving, so I turned off the music at my work station to listen, only to realize that it was just one man's voice, and it was coming from Alexa! It was very poor sound quality and I couldn't make out what was being said, so I stood up and walked towards Alexa and as soon as I got near, the audio sputtered briefly, then cut out entirely.

I can only assume that this was David Cooper, however I am unsure as to whether Alexa is spying on me for him, or him for me. I plan to continue to investigate this situation and figure it out, but in the meantime I'm giving the Echo Dot 3 stars because really I just use it for my grocery list, it tries to play my Spotify but cuts out in the middle of songs, someone at one of my parties once jokingly said "Alexa order me a Rolex" and she actually ordered one, and obviously because it appears to have gained sentience and communicating with other devices around my building.

title: With MAC, DO NOT USE THE PLANTRONICS SOFTWARE
text:
All Right, Qemo Savi:

5 stars for dictation (speech to text) in a Mac.
3 stars for not working at all if you follow Plantronics instructions & download their (Hub) software to your Mac.
? stars for working with a PA system in an auditorium.

To make a long story short, IMHO this mic will not work with a MAC if you download the (Hub) software from plantronics. But if you just plug & play, it will work very well once you set the sound controls in Systems Preferences, particularly it works well with the Speech dictation system of Yosemite.

I think its range (headset to dongle) is claimed to be 300 feet. Thus it might be tried as a headset mic for a PA system in an auditorium. I have been trying this. You hook the dongle to your Macbook Pro and route the input mic sound to go to the Mac output sound (input monitoring). But how do you do that? I tried 3 ways:

1) I downloaded a little freebie program called LineIn which lets you do "pass through" (input monitoring). The result was only a slight latency between input & output with a little canyon sound on the voice -- not too bad.
2) Use QuickTime set for audio recording (don't push the record button unless you want to record), push up the virtual volume slider.
The results are similar to that with LineIn, but a little more latency. so I prefer 1.
3) Use GarageBand set for input monitoring? I tried that & went round with 2 tech advisers from Apple with no success. Using older versions of GarageBand, I got the input monitoring, but the output sounded like high-pitched Donald Duck / Chipmunks with hoarseness.

I ran the audio out the earphones jack of the MacBook, out to an ampifier.
It sounded better when I used USB output via a Peavey DAC ($50) box which has XLR outputs.

The drawback seems to be that as you increase the distance (range) between headset & receiver dongle, the quality of the sound decreases. Thus, one probably needs to keep the MacBook with attached receiver dongle within 15 feet. So then you would attach the Peavey DAC via XLR cables to your PA sound system.

My history with this headset is as follows:

First I downloaded the software from Plantronics into the first computer, a MacBook Pro ( ~2013) with Yosemite, which I run in clamshell mode (lid shut) connected via (the mini display port via HDMI adapter to an external monitor. But after following instructions & calling Plantronics tech support, the unit would neither produce audible sound nor would its microphone deliver sound to my computer. The Plantronics tech after working with me told me to return the item as defective.

Then I tried the unit in other macs that I own without using the Platronics software, and it worked. But my iMac 5K Retina (late 2014), the built in microphone is good enough so that you don't need an external microphone for speech dictation.

I think that Plantronics needs to get its software and/or its documentation right for Macs. The brochure with the headset doesn't even mention Mac.

As to using this for Public Address mic, I like the claimed long range & the fact that it has no wire to transmitter box (to wear on you belt). I am still playing with this concept. But if you count the cost of your Mac computer, it is cheaper to buy a system (perhaps the Gem Sound GMX62) dedicated to PA system use.

I am not using this for games.

title: The AT-300 is the answer here because the power source is not inside, but outside on the converter plug.
text: Since previous AT-163 models I owned had failures, possibly due to the internal power source going bad, they sent me this AT-300 as a replacement.  I have 1 remaining AT-163 they also replaced that still works since it's rarely plugged in.  Now I will leave these both unplugged or plugged into a surge protector with an on/off switch, switched off when not in use to avoid power source failures.  Just plug in and use; the memory keeps all your scanned channels and settings.  The AT-300 is the answer here because the power source is not inside, but outside on the converter plug (outputs 5 volts at 1500 mA), so if that goes bad, the whole unit won't be junk, just replace that part.  This model also does have the onscreen TV display of the actual channel (say 6-1 see pictures); note that on the box it displays the channel number using a zero in lieu of a dash, thus 0601 (6-1) or 1201 (12-1) but becomes the clock time display when the box is off.  Also has a built in antenna amplifier, and both a signal strength and signal quality meter for when fine tuning in the antenna direction!  The tuner is a good tuner that really pulls in the stations, although that's more dependent on the antenna you use and your location/direction to the TV broadcast transmission towers.  Supports connecting up to a 2 TB USB hard drive (Limit) or a USB thumb drive for recording stuff and playing back, including any pictures, other movie formats (such as AVI, mpg,vob, & dat), and music (mp3 & acc) that's on your drive.  We really like this one!  Hopefully this will last too.

title: Great watch and possibly the best out there!
text:
After owning the 1st generation Apple Watch for a couple of years, I decided it was time to upgrade to the new one. Though I don't swim, I do run once in a while and wanted the option of tracking my run with GPS without having to take my iPhone. I also liked the cool band that is great for breathability.

Pros:
- Much faster than 1st generation
- Integrated GPS
- Waterproof (though I used my other one in the shower all the time with no issues)
- Really bright display
- Great looking band (perfect for running and breathability)
- Improved battery life (I was able to get two days of use instead of only one)
- Quick glances at texts, emails, and other notifications
- You can store local music from Apple Music and listen through bluetooth headphones
- Great for swimming

Cons:
- Same design as 1st generation
- Heart rate monitor still not very accurate (just average)
- Most of the apps are not very useful on the watch

Conclusion:
Should I buy the Nike+ edition?: If you are planning on getting a Series 2 Apple Watch, then there is no reason why you shouldn't get the Nike+ edition instead of the regular one since they are the same price. The Nike+ edition comes with a nicer band (that as of this moment Apple does not sell by itself) and you get some exclusive Nike+ watch faces.

Should I upgrade?: It's faster, it has GPS, and it has a cool new band but unless you are an Apple fan or exercise a lot (running and swimming mostly), then this is probably not worth the upgrade. If you really need a new watch, I would recommend taking a look at the cheaper Series 1 Apple Watch which is basically the same as the first generation but with the faster processor of the Series 2...or waiting for the 3rd generation which should feature a new design.

title: A very good choice for your media room
text:
Early in 2015, I decided to upgrade my Denon AVR-1911 receiver. That Denon had served me very well for over 5 years, but it was time to get a receiver that supported 4K and HDMI 2.2, with latest bells and whistles.

Studied all competing models, including Denon, Sony, Yamaha, Marantz. Made several visits to big box retailers like Best Buy and local pro-audio shops to compare models. Finally decided on this Onkyo.
Boy, am I happy! No, Ecstatic is the right word.

Connected this unit up with no effort. I take that back; the biggest effort was lifting this big boy into place.
He weighs a whopping 34 lb! Finished the AccuEQ setup, was prompted to remove the mic and off we went.

A few notes of caution:

title: Incredible camera
text: This camera can only be described as INCREDIBLE.  My wife and I both had its predecessor, the SX50 -- which we thought was a remarkable camera -- and she literally wore hers out, prompting purchase of this newer version as a replacement..  With the 35-mm-equivalent of 21 mm wide angle, zooming out 65 x with the glass optics to 1365mm, and add a 4x digital zoom -- this camera REALLY reaches out there.  The array of controls should satisfy any purists, but we usually just shoot in Program mode.  For pure point and shoot, there is an intelligent program which makes all the decisions for you.  Image stabilization makes hand-held shots at the extremes of the telephoto possible and routinely superbly sharp.  Macro photos to a couple of inches from the lens brings tiny flowers to fill the view screen.  Battery life is amazing, we usually get 200+ photos before the battery indicator suggests a recharge.  Burst mode allows a series of photos of fast-moving subjects such as wildlife, and the response to the shutter button is only a fraction of a second.  I'd like a wider range of aperture options -- but in all candor I rarely need more than the camera can provide.  Having spent a lifetime (65 years) in photography, wearing out Olympus OM1 and Nikon and Canon  35 mm cameras with full (heavy) array of lenses, and working our way through 4 previous generations of digital cameras, this camera truly is the best of the best.  Cost is more than a snapshot camera, but if you want a snapshot camera you don't want all this camera's capability.  If you want to take National Geographic quality photos, and have to do it on a budget, look at this camera!  For the price of under $500 the camera is truly INCREDIBLE.  And no, I got no discount or other "perq" for writing this glowing comment.  The camera EARNED it.

title: Awesome vertical lines and nearly zero barrel distortion! Great lens for the price!
text: I am a real estate photographer and I was looking for a new wide angle lens for my Canon 7D with crop sensor. I usually shoot with a 6D that has a full frame sensor. All my lenses for my 6D are L series pro lenses but when you use them on a crop sensor body you loose 1.4x of mm focal length. So I was using an L series 17-40mm on my 6D. When I put it on my 7D, it is no longer 17mm which is what I need. It now becomes a 23mm lens and just not wide enough. I searched and found the 10-18mm Sigma for $400 here on Amazon. Had great reviews and a solid lens so I purchased it. I took it out on my 1st shoot and crap! It had soooo much barrel distortion! The walls were titling and when I leveled it forward/backward and up/down it bowed... there was a massive fish eye effect and would mean massive photoshop processing time on each photo which is not good. I didn't even use it for a full shoot. I sent it back and found this one which equates to apprx 18-25mm on my crop sensor. It had great reviews and one was from another real estate photographer who said she got great results with this lens. So I bought this one. I took it out on 2 shoots and WOW! It has nearly ZERO barrel distortion! When I use the balance level on camera each shot the results are amazing! Even my $900 L series lens can even compare to the solid straight lines from any angle I got from this lens. The sharpness is pretty darn nice too. Overall this lens is a 5 star for sure. The price is way cheaper then other lens costing 2x the price. The extra bundled items are very awesome to be included especially at this low price. I've used Altura products in the past and they are decent quality. It came with a nice lens bag, UV filter, ND4 filter, and a polarizer filter! Also included was 2 microfiber clothes and a full cleaning kit. If your looking for a good deal on a wide angle for a crop sensor that wont break your wallet then look no more. Now I wont say its better than my 17-40mm L series when attached to my 6D full frame for landscapes but for the crop sensor its awesome.

title: Let me start by saying the cameras provide great quality image and sound
text:
I purchased 3 of these Canary cameras along with the Canary All-in-One and the outdoor version. Let me start by saying the cameras provide great quality image and sound. Unfortunately Canary is subpar for what my needs are. As I said I purchased a total of 5 cameras with the intention of adding more. I set up the first 4 and to my surprise Canary does not let you add a 5th camera unless you pay them $10 a month!!! I don’t know who Canary thinks they are kidding, but these are just WiFi cameras. Oh, if you want to use the two-way talk feature, guess what…you have to pay them the $10 a month. My kids WiFi baby monitors cost me $200 for 2 pan/tilt cameras, a monitor, the ability to view it through WiFi on my phone along with two way talk. Add it’s all for free! Now the video quality is a little less, but then again its free and I can move the cameras.

I travel a lot for work and wanted these so I could check in on my kids while they are with the nanny. My nanny knows I have the cameras, but I’d rather her not know when I’m looking in. The problem is that all these cameras emit a bright white light (see pictures) when you open the app to view a camera. Talked to Canary about this and they don’t offer a way to disable these lights. You can put electrical tape over the lights, but when you’re spending this much for a camera how hard is it to build this into the software?

Now for my interaction with customer service. I tried to find a number on Canary’s website to discuss all this, but the best you’ll get is an email address or you can text them. Yes, because people love to text about technical issues! After spending 25 minutes of back and forth texting about why I couldn’t add the additional camera the person on the other end finally realized the reason and hence you have to pay monthly if you want these features. But told me I could set up another account/location for another 4 cameras. If I can do that why not just let us add additional cameras for free and make it easier on the customer?

Overall, good quality camera if you only want 4 or less and don’t mind the lack of two-way talking. Or you don’t mind paying $10 a month, plus the high cost of the cameras. For me I’m going to send the cameras back and get a different brand. Customer service is lacking and there are better cameras for the money in my opinion.

title: After 2 months of use I can recommend Arlo
text:
While I did not purchase the set of 4 Arlo Pro cameras from Amazon, I did thoroughly read the reviews both on Amazon and Best Buy websites. I was wary due to some of the negative reviews but decided to give it a go. It's now 2 months since the cameras were installed outside of my home - I wanted to allow time for a more accurate review. The cameras are incredibly easy to install - wireless means no drilling for running cables. The Arlo app easily lets you frame the camera including an option to rotate the image in the event the camera is hanging upside down. I purchased two additional articulating mounts because I was unable to position the camera the way I wanted with the magnetic mount. One of the magnetic mounts is in a tree and it has held pretty well - except for the time a squirrel bumped the camera and repositioned it!

I read many reviews about how sensitive the cameras were and would record continuously when there was no movement in the frame. This initially happened with one of my cameras, but it turns out a juniper tree needed to be trimmed and the camera repositioned. Since then, no problems. Another concern was battery life. Arlo claims 4-6 months - two months in now, my cameras are at 55% from that initial charge and set to the Optimized video setting. The quality of the image is fairly good at this setting. I was sure to position the camera so it isn't triggered by any car passing by. The camera's sensitivity to motion is only about 7-10 ft in front of the camera. Arlo' ability to store videos in the cloud for one week is perfect. If it is an important video you can download it to your computer. You are also able to text or email the video.

Arlo was attractive to me for its wireless capabilities and the fact that there is no monthly fee, like there is with Nest. I'm very pleased with the purchase and would recommend it to someone else.

title: Exceeded my expectations!
text:
I recently purchased this to replace a 3 year old 720TVL Lorex system. Overall I have been very impressed with ZMODO and have found a lot of advantages over Lorex

PROs

Cameras - The ZMODO cameras are solid metal and very rugged. I am impressed! My previous Lorex cameras were plastic. One drop on the ground from ladder height pretty much destroys a plastic camera. Even driving a screw to hard on the flange will cause problems.

LED status lights - I like that ZMODO included led status lights on the back of the NVR for each RJ45 connector. It makes installation much easier as I could tell from the blink pattern that a camera was communicating. Nice touch and also unexpected on a low cost system.

User Interface - I found the ZMODO user interface to be more intuitive than the Lorex UI. Using the mouse scroll wheel to adjust the time bar on playback works well and its easy to zoom into the time slot you want to look at.

Remote Connectivity - The app and remote connectivity worked the first time. No complicated port setup was required like the Lorex system.

Warranty Response - Immediately sent me a new camera because one had an IR problem. The new camera arrived within a week and everything works great.

Price - You really can't beat the price for this system, especially if you are ok with installing your own WD purple hardrive.

CONs

Camera - I had one camera that had an IR problem at night. (but quickly replaced by ZMODO) Hopefully I will have good reliability on the these cameras. In the 3 years with the Lorex cameras I had a 40% failure rate. Yes they honored the first couple of failure under warranty after losing two more cameras post warranty I gave up.

Cables - You have to be really careful with these cables. I pretested everything before installation so all cables were good out of the box. Unfortunately I ended up damaging two cables, probably from my poor aim with a staple gun but I really couldn't find the damage so it could have been a kink Note to others - use cable staples that you screw or nail in and be careful with tight bends.

Overall I can honestly say that this ZMODO system exceeded my expectations. I haven't enabled some of the more advanced features like motion detection or alert emails, but so far in basic mode this system works well.
