title: If it only worked as advertised!
text:
This isn't my first go around with TrackR. I had purchased the original TrackR and was was disappointed with its performance. Ever hopeful, or gullible, I purchased a few TrackR Bravos, on the belief the second version must be improved... I was wrong. Let me share my experience with three of the devices claims.

1.) Item Ringer - This seems like it's a great feature, super useful to find a misplaced possession, problem is that it's unreliable. I have 8 Bravos, and one arrived with a dead battery, the other 7 were tested by me by placing them in clear sight, about 3 feet (1 yard) from my phone, a Galaxy Note 4 and I tried to "ring" each one. The result was very intermittent. Sometimes a Bravo would ring, other times not. The real world implication is if I were frantically searching for my keys, relying on the "ring" feature, I may walk by my keys because the ringer didn't go off.
2.) Phone Finder - This feature also was intermittent, although for whatever reason seemed to work better. I could see the real world use of this feature when I am out and about and misplace my phone. I do have "find my phone" though Google and Lookout, but if you're out, without your phone, that would help much. Unfortunately, this feature is intermittent.
3.) The crowd source GPS hasn't worked yet. I've given one away as a test, and it has not moved on the map.The only update is when my phone gets close to it. I understand the crowd source GPS concept, but it doesn't seem to work in my area (Northeast Ohio)

Bottom line, I love the idea, I tried the product and based on my out of the package experience, I can't recommend the device. It's performance is too unreliable, whether it's the phone, the battery, sunspots, whatever, the device just doesn't live up to ts billing.

title: Receives stations as just well as my old GE Superadio II.  It's smaller though, and can't match the full sound of the big GE.
text:
I disliked that it took 2 tries to get a good one. The first radio I received would "hang" about every third power up, ignoring all buttons and requiring a battery removal to unlock it. Amazon was helpful though, and sent a replacement immediately.
Second try was the charm. I just set this radio up side by side with my GE Superadio II. I ran thru both the AM band and FM band on both of them. The HDR-16 pulled in every single station that the older GE did (and that's a lot of stations). I would have to call the reception a dead tie. Where one struggled, the other struggled. I own the Superadio II and III, as well as a Panasonic RF-2800. As a tuner, this radio definitely holds its own. To be fair, the Superadio II still beat this new one for sound quality. The two 2.75" speakers on the Sangean just couldn't quite match the 5" main speaker and 1.5" tweeter on the old GE Superadio II. Still, the HDR-16 weighs just 2.5 lbs. to the Superadio's 6.5 lbs, so it is certainly more portable, plus you get stereo output.. The rubber feet have good grip, so pushing the buttons doesn't send it sliding. I have software version 38, and the changes in and out of HD are about as graceful as they can be. The FM HD stations tune and lock in 3 seconds or so. AM HD is a different animal, as HD struggles with the weaker signals. Right now I have 6 AM stations indicating HD signal, but only the local one locks into HD mode. It is still just late afternoon though, so the noise levels are high, and the signal strengths are low. The non-HD quality is still excellent though. Oh, and the included AC power adapter is not giving me any added noise on the weak AM stations. It's about perfect, with no need to go to batteries to gain any noise margin. The recorder output gives a nice clean output without regard to your listening volume setting, and the tone controls do nothing to the recorder output. The headphone outputs do use the volume and tone controls, and with good headphones the sound is quite awesome. It really shows how good the tuner is. Some Koss PortaPros were plenty to really let the audio output shine. I tried the Aux input as well. I fed in professional quality audio, and it came out about as expected from two 2.75" speakers. It was clean, amplified well, but wasn't overly impressive. The trade-off for portability and light weight was the lesser sound from the smaller speakers. The tone controls work fine but can't turn this into Hi-Fi sound. If you want that, use a good set of headphones, or connect the recorder output to your home stereo.

title: RinoGear Polymer Film Screen Protectors - Good Value for the Money
text:
I installed these screen protectors on TomTom Spark 3 and TomTom Adventure Fitness Watches. I have also used this manufacturers screen protectors on the Fitbit Charge/Charge HR Fitness Bands. Based on the experience with the Fitbit Charge bands, the screen protectors do prevent scratches to the display and are abrasion resistant with some cut resistance but the protectors are prone to lifting at the edges and do not protect the screen face from damage when impacted with sharp objects or larger rocks. In my opinion, these screen protectors are worth the money to be able to keep the fitness watch looking good and the ability to replace the protector easily at low cost is a plus.

Pros:
- Screen protector is relatively easy to put on with no defects if the directions are followed.
- All the necessary items (except soap and water) are included in the package along with clear instructions on how to install the screen protectors without defects.
- 6 screen protectors are included in the package so you have multiple tries to learn how to install the screen protector correctly.
- Relatively low cost for the screen protector.
- Ability to use the same screen protector on the TomTom Spark, TomTom Spark 3, and TomTom Adventure GPS Fitness Watches.

Cons:
- Screen protectors will lift at the edges when the protectors are exposed and not protected by the bezel of the fitness watch/band.
- The soft screen protector film and thicker adhesive allows the screen protector to be deformed during application and use such that visual defects can be created.
- The polymer film screen protector does not offer as much impact protection or scratch resistance as tempered glass screen protectors against impacts.

Having used the RinoGear screen protectors on several Fitbit fitness bands for a couple years, we have a reasonable amount of experience and know the plusses and minuses of these protectors. They are good for protecting the display screens from everyday wear and tear or scratches that the polymer screens are prone to having. These screen protectors will also refresh a display that has already been scratched, making it look good. The RinoGear screen protectors are worth the cost for that alone. If you do a lot of trail running through the brush, run obstacle races/courses, or work out in a gym with free weights and hit your fitness band/watch against equipment, the screen protector does not protect as good as a harder tempered glass/gorilla glass screen protector would. Currently, the tempered glass screen protectors are many times more expensive than these RinoGear polymer film protectors so it is a tradeoff of cost vs. amount of protection.

The biggest negative of these polymer film screen protectors is that the edge of the film gets lifted during normal wear/use because the film is flexible. When this happens, the protective film is either pulled up and unsightly or pulled off completely. Both these conditions require that the remaining film and adhesive be removed from the display and a new screen protector be installed. The TomTom Spark/Spark 3 Fitness Watches have small bezels which leave the edge of the RinoGear screen protector exposed and prone to lifting. The TomTom Adventure GPS Fitness Watch has a raised bezel which protects the screen protector and display. That should allow the screen protector to last much longer without lifting.

Other reviewers state that these RinoGear screen protectors are not clear. After years of using these on several different types of fitness monitors, I have never noticed the screen protector obscuring the display when the screen protector is new. After extended use or, when the screen protector is lifted, scratching and lifting can make the display difficult to see. At that point the screen protector should be replaced.

These RinoGear screen protectors have a lifetime warranty but I have never attempted to seek replacements (I just bought another set) since the cost was so low. the Fitbit Charge fitness monitors break before the packs of screen protectors so I do not know whether RinoGear honors their lifetime warranty. Hopefully these TomTom Spark 3 and Adventurer Fitness Watches will last long enough to find out.

title: Did you turn it off and on again?
text:
There's clearly something wrong with this series of routers. Within my first few days of owning it, I kept have issues downloading files/updates ultimately resulting in them failing and restarting, failing and restarting. The strange thing is, I would never see the connection drop in windows and there was no issue with the download speed and the logs don't indicate any issues. I would have to reboot the router in order to stabilize my connection again. This would only fix it temporarily. It seemed like this occurred after prolonged periods of streaming media or gaming. Potential memory issue? With my experience as a network technician my troubleshooting was proven ineffective. With my adjustments I pretty much disabled everything I didn't need, including the wireless radio and just used the LAN ports. I will say the only positive about this router is the UI is pretty simple to navigate. Overall, if you search forums or other reviews on here you'll notice a vast majority of reviewers all say they have constantly power cycle this router in order to fix connection problems.

I gave up out of frustration after a week of constant failed downloads and bought a Unifi EdgeRouter. However, I only recommend this router to advanced users familiar with static ips, vlans, subnets and using a CLI.

title: Best. Tablet. Ever.
text:
This is a phenomenal device.

I bought this to serve as a gaming / media device for an ailing iPad 5/Air. This is not an iPad killer, but it is killer!

The unit has a good heft to it, but is not overly heavy. It's to be expected due to that battery/speaker bar. It feels comfortable in your hands in portrait orientation reading, and the Yoga stand works great for desktop and lap usage. The wall hanging mode is great for cooking in the kitchen.

The speaker is pretty solid. Obviously not powerful on bass, but respectable. Better than any little speaker, but will hold up to a reasonably sized portable speaker.

The battery life seems decent. My son plays a lot of games, but the battery seems to hold out well.

The projector is pretty awesome, though hardly the selling point for me (wanted the bigger / better tech specs). It works well in a dark room, coupled with the speakers. The focusing is cool, and the image correction for angle is pretty impressive.

I bought a 128 GB SanDisk microSD card and now have 192 GB of storage. All the content for me! I recommend you doing the same.

There are a lot of complaints about the interface and bloatware... but honestly, this is Android, you don't use the default launcher (ever use a Samsung device... *shudder*). Install Google Now if you are Google focused; OneDrive and Arrow Launcher if you are Microsoft focused. If you are Apple focused you will not be happy without an iPad. The file manager, camera app and gallery apps are fine. Being able to have Kindle content, Microsoft content and Google content on one device is great.

All in all, I'm very happy with the device. If you are concerned about taking a gamble (I was), don't. It's a great multi-purpose tablet and device, saves you the need to bring a lot of accessories and will impress people, tech geeks and normals alike.

Go Lenovo!

title: Generally a very good piece of technology, with a few notable quirks and limitations ...
text:
The Garmin DriveAssist 50LMT is a solid piece of technology that functions as a combination GPS, dash camera and a driver assistance (ADAS) system. That said, it does have a few important limitations that you should be aware of.

Here's a summary of the positives and negatives pertaining to this device:

Positives:

1) Price and value: I paid $99 for a refurbished unit, and at this price, I think it's a fantastic value. Although, at the original $299 asking price, I'm not sure I would have purchased it.
2) The unit is well made, and simple to set up.
3) The GPS provides clear, simple voice directions, the screen is bright and easy to follow (though of very low resolution for 2018).
4) The dashcam video is generally pretty good quality; although it gets somewhat marginal at night because of the small size of the lens.
5) The ADAS features really do work: the forward collision, lane departure warning and moving traffic warnings function as described. The unit also warns you of speed limit changes, red light cameras and when you are driving the wrong way (though see below on that last point).
6) You can operate the unit by voice command in addition to pressing options on the screen.

Negatives:

1) The GPS sometimes makes mistakes and is missing some locations (e.g. it didn't know about a CVS pharmacy in Savannah, GA even though that business has been there for years). It also told me I was driving the wrong way down a street at one point (even though I wasn't) and took me on a mile long "side trip" rather than telling me to execute a perfectly legal U turn.
2) The unit takes quite awhile to calculate routes.
3) The battery life is really short (less than 30 minutes): this unit is only designed to function plugged into your car.
4) Some major US cities (like Savannah, GA) have no traffic antennas, so you won't be able to get live traffic updates.
5) The ADAS system gives false positives sometimes, especially if the sensitivity is set to "high".
6) At night time, and in the rain, the ADAS system really doesn't work reliably (even though this is arguably, when you might need it most).
7) The supplied suction cup mount really doesn't hold very well.

All-in-all, I recommend this unit.

Based on my readings of other reviews, most ADAS systems in stand alone dashcams are completely useless, whereas while this system makes the occasional mistake, but it actually does work (in some ways it works BETTER than the system in my $60K BMW ... that system warns SO late that metal is already crumpling by the time the alarms go off! I'm exaggerating, but only slightly). The GPS works fine, but honestly, no better than the free Google Maps app on my smart phone. The dash camera records in full HD quality, and during the day the video looks fine, but because the lens and sensor are so small, in marginal light it looks worse than the video from some $50 stand alone dashcam units.

If you ONLY need a dashcam or ONLY need a GPS, you probably shouldn't buy the Garmin DriveAssist; however, if you want both of these functions in one machine, and you're curious about "smart" driver assistance / collision avoidance systems, and you want to test one out for very little money, I think you'll be happy with your purchase.

title: Great for first time builders
text:
This case is actually very sleek, and much larger than I had anticipated. I'm a new PC builder and this admittedly had to be the best case to start off with in doing so. Even though the glossy finish smudges easily it is easily cleaned after with a cloth, or sometimes just dissipates on its own. The black matte top also does not smudge at all.

The stock fans on this case are sufficient for cooling, just because of how much extra space I have. The dust filters however could use some refinement. Their plastic finish makes frequent cleaning a necessity; even if it is easily done. It also has great clearance on the bottom so your power supply can suck in a sufficient amount of air.

There's some SSD slots pre-built into the case, and enough hard drive holdings to safely say future expansions will be a breeze. This also applies to the amount of room you get in its width to install a beefier heatsink for overclockers, as well as the clearance you get with OR without a radiator for liquid cooling for your gpu. This thing is a monster, really.

The thumb screws on the back are also a treat, but you'll need to loosen them with a screwdriver the first time opening the side panels. Accessibility on this case (especially for the price) is great. It's overall a very high quality case and feels much more premium than the price point hints at.

title: THE Game-Changer, iPhone Becomes Mobile News Trough. (IOS 9.2 Update Needed)
text:
Amazing. Today, this Lightning SD card reader became a game-changer where I work.
Having an iPhone 5S, I had just downloaded the IOS 9.2 update, necessary for the iPhone to recognize JPEGs on an SD card. Yesterday was my first day with the card reader, and it was odd that I had taken a few images with my [[ASIN:B00KOUIBZW Panasonic Lumix DMC-FZ1000 4K, Point and Shoot Camera with Leica Lens 16X Zoom (Black)]] (16GB Promaster Class 10 card used).

Today we had breaking news; a mistrial in the case of officer William Porter in the death of Freddie Gray. We all scrambled to different areas of the city; mine was at Pennsylvania/North Aves, where the unrest centered in April. After capturing a few images with the FZ1K, I pulled the SD card out, plugged it into the reader, then plugged the reader into the Lightning port of the iPhone. A white screen popped up, revealing thumbnails of all the images I had taken.

"WOW." From that point on, any time I had a decent image to send, I would swap SD cards between my camera and the iPhone, store the selects onto the phone, use the "Photos" app to prep the image, speech-to-text to attach a caption, spell-check, then send to the editors. This kept going on all afternoon, sending files of the peace at the intersection, people leaving the DSS office (which was closed in reaction to the mistrial), people milling about, a woman sitting beneath a mural, a man talking about his reaction. The reader attached, plus a few pics that were sent moments after they were captured, are added here.

With today's events, we can't sit somewhere, remove a laptop and transfer, edit, caption, fire up a WiFi hotspot, and send images or video. We need to travel light. Pairing the iPhone and Lightning SD reader with my Lumix FZ1000 gives me freedom to move, shoot, send, and help my business update much faster, hours earlier than other shooters could do at the same location. It turns your iPhone into a mobile imaging and video trough. As quickly as you upload, it gets devoured by my organization. I feel safer and more confident in getting updates sent regularly and quickly.

title: Not bad when u get one that works.
text:
Latest update: I'm on my second unit. The transducer had to been bad on the first one. This one seems to working fairly well. These Fish finder are pretty neat when they work. The biggest problem I'm seeing it the soft screen that scratches up even with a fine coasta cleaning cloth and it fogs up. But other then that it's fair enough for a front mount fish finder on a small boat, even a kayak just don't get it wet or it's done for. Buy a cover to keep over it when not in use.

First review: Ummm... Well... It's okay. Using it as my bow mounted fish finder, on my smaller Jon boat, looks good on a ram mount. I don't think the transducer is working on my trolling motor. It works great one min, then the next it goes froms 3ft to 300ft then 0ft. The temp seems to be spot on and has pretty clear read out it sees the fish just fine and sees the bottom and everything on it just fine didn't have any prob there. Only prob Is..., it's not keeping depth really well but... Like I said before maybe because it's transducer is on a trolling motor mount, and maybe it was the shallow grassy area I was floating around in. Maybe! I'm going to give it a full season before I judge to harshly. So far it's just okay. Not happy it's not keeping depth. Oh it's depth alarm, starts at 3ft. I'm on a small boat that can float in a foot of water. Would like to be able to set it at 1ft. But that's not a option. ALSO!!! OMG!! Do NOT!! Even touch the screen!!!! I got some water spots on the screen along with lint. So using my clean cotton tshirt i was wearing, to wiped the screen and it left scratches and swirl marks !! BAD!!! Swirl Marks!! Absolutely ridiculous!!! Can't even see the screen for the swirl marks. I don't know if I can deal with this.

Update: I've contacted Humminbird about the units depth problems. They where not very helpful! They wanted to put the blame on how I had it hooked from the trolling motors power supply. So I got a small 12v humminbird battery and that didn't help anything! They wanted to blame how I had it setup so while on the phone with them out on the lake they walked me thru all the settings, that didn't help! They blamed how it was mounted on my trolling motor on there own trolling motor mount, might I add!! So I rear mounted it! Didn't help! They blamed me for having more then one Humminbird fishfinder running at one time!!! So... I unplugged the other console unit! And guess what!!! Yea, that didn't fix it either!!! Does Kevin VanDam go thru this BS??! He has TWO units running at once! I guess that's why he has the 2,000 dollar units running on his boats. Anyway it's on it's way back I'm going to try another NEW Unit! If I get the same problems I'm going to get a refund and I'm going to Lowrance!!! About over the Bird!

title: Not Anywhere Near As Good As I Was Expecting
text:
Amazon had a daily deal on some computer accessories and I had been thinking about replacing my D-Link wireless PCI card for an 802.11ac card. So the timing seemed good. The D-Link was installed for years in 2 different computers. Even though the card was rated at 300Mbps, I was only getting 150Mbps. That is one of the reasons that prompted me to go with something new.

After having this installed in my HP Envy system for about a month, I was ready to return it. Unfortunately, I didn't realize I was 2 days past the return deadline. So now I am stuck with this piece of junk.

Throughout the month that this has been installed in my PC, my network connection drops frequently. I will be surfing various sites and all of a sudden, the pages freeze and/or I'll get an error page cannot be displayed. In my house I have 4 desktop PCs, 1 laptop, 2 all-in-ones, 3 iPhones, kindles, game consoles, etc. None of the other devices experience the issues I have had since I installed this lousy TP-Link card.

I mainly got this card for the 5GHz (802.11ac) connectivity because I thought I would get better throughput considering I have so many 2.4GHz (802.11g/n) devices. But Windows 8.1 shows about 40% of the signal strength for the 5GHz Wi-Fi versus the 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. Using my phone and the Wi-Fi analyzer app, signal strength of the 2.4GHz and 5GHz signals are practically identical. But for whatever reason the TP-Link card doesn't get the same signal.

I was hoping to get close to 1Gbps speeds with this and my router. I am getting 450 Mbps, but my guess is that is really closer to 300 Mbps. So it wasn't much of an upgrade to my D-Link 300 Mbps card that never dropped my connection. Certainly not worth the $70.

I am really frustrated with this card and more exasperated that I am stuck with this thing because of the lame return policy. Maybe by chance, this unit is defective and that is why I get so many drops and low signal for 5GHz. I'll try my luck with TP-Link support. Hopefully they aren't as evasive as Amazon is with trying to find a phone number to call and talk to someone. The one time I actually want to return something.....

So it has been quite some time since I got a replacement card from TP-Link. However, this junky card is still frequently dropping connections. It's dropped 3 times in 10 minutes on my this morning which drove me back to vent in my review. The is the T9E card. I recently rebuilt my system with a clean copy of Windows 10 Home (x64). So I know that it's not likely that there is some software causing the issue. Maybe this card has some specific issue with the HP Envy PC I have. Obviously, there are plenty of folks that are happy with the card.

When I was working with TP-Link support on the issue, they recommended me to use google to try and find a newer driver from the chip maker. What??? You want me to go to the internet and get a driver that TP-Link hasn't even tested and you want me to search around for it. At lease send me a link to the chip maker's drivers.

I am fed up with this card. I will be putting the slower, but reliable D-Link card back in this weekend. I can say with certainty that this is my first and last TP-Link product.

title: Used it to freeze the wart off my thumb, successfully!!!
text:
I had the wart on the pad of my thumb for years, otc stuff did nothing. It eventually grew larger and other smaller warts started to pop up on same thumb.
I went to the doc, he put something on it (not freeze it). I ended up with painful blisters on half of my thumb for weeks, it literally stuck out like a sore thumb bc I couldn't even bend it or touch it.
The blister pelt off and the wart came back tenfold. Imagine half of your thumb, palm side, infected with wart. What was a 1 mm wide wart became a freaking 1 cm wide pad of wart.
I was so pissed. Not only the doc didn't fix it, it got worse, and I got billed the whole visit charge bc insurance didn't deem it medically necessary. So I bought the can to try freezing it myself bc otc freeze stuff didn't work before and I wasn't going to go back to that doctor.
I used it every other night, I wrapped the whole thumb with roll bandage to keep it contained, last thing I want is for it to spread. Wash hand thoroughly when changing bandage every night.
After a week the edges of the pad came off and I kept trimming it as it pelt. After 2 weeks, the last piece came off today.
Would recommend to anyone suffering those warts for a cheap and relatively pain free removal.

title: Great Receiver! Loving it so far!  App controller is well done, however, setup, sound modes, and remote seem a little confusing.
text:
I have only had this receiver set up for a few days, and I will update as needed. I will write a "quick" review for the 1st paragraph, and go into some detail in the 2nd. :)

I am upgrading from an older Sony "All in One" surround sound/DVD system, which might explain my pro and con things a little bit. Overall, this is a very nice receiver, and I absolutely love it. It does everything i need, and then some. I recommend it if its in the price range your looking for. Yamaha doesn't usually disappoint.

*Quick: There are some amazing features, such as 4k support, Multicast, AirPlay, WiFi/Network & Bluetooth connectivity, YPAO (which is the Mic Calibration program) as well as a pretty awesome app that controls the system. I am using the App on an iPad, and love it. The receiver has a "quality" feel overall, with tons of connections, including and extra HDMI and USB on the front. The picture and sound quality is great. I do feel that the setup process was a little complicated. There are just SOOOO many types of "Sound Modes". The remote is also a little nutty, tons and tons of buttons. But once you get this setup, you can leave it alone, which does make it worth it in my opinion.

*Little more: If you have been following the Surround Sound Scene, and stayed educated to the old and new formats over the years, you will be fine using this system. If your like me, and have some general knowledge, you might get a little overwhelmed with what you can pick from for sound modes, and what they will do, and Yamaha doesn't go into great detail, because its not their technology (meaning they don't develop Dolby or DTS), they just support it in their systems. So finding out exactly which Sound Mode does what is hard to find through Yamaha. You'd have to go to Dolby, or DTS's websites to learn more about it, or do what I did, and just start switching the modes around until its what you like... I know, real technical, right? lol. However, I will "complain" about the ease of use, which is why i knocked off 1 star. I would definitely say this is not an "Out of the box ready", user friendly type system. You will definitely need to set some time aside to set up everything. I would absolutely recommend using the Yamaha A/V Controller app, which I'm using on an iPad, and it makes it much easier to control. I will say that this is a perfect system for someone who has the knowledge of all the different types of Surround Sound Formats, or for a "secondary" surround sound system set up, again, because you would have the knowledge. however, don't be afraid to learn something about these technologies, because this receiver is a great way to have a nice home theater.

I consider myself to be and "Advanced Amateur" Audiophile. I've been working with audio equipment for 20+ years. Just never dove full into it. I would gladly get a 2nd one of these if i needed it, and would recommend it to anyone looking for a decent surround sound receiver.

title: No different than the others, but no worse either.
text:
Before starting my review, you should know two things:

1) Omoton sent me a sample of this keyboard to give my honest opinion of
2) This keyboard is a mass-produced, re-branded wireless keyboard. I have used four of these, each from different "manufacturers" and each one has been the exact same. My coworker just ordered one from another brand here on Amazon, and except for the sticker they are identical down to the very last fraction of an inch in size.

Why do I mention the latter? Because really when choosing these keyboards, the only things you should look for are price and warranty length. The price on this keyboard is competitive, but I can't find anything about the warranty length.

For use with my Macbook Pro and Mac Pro computers, I find the keyboard to be pretty decent overall. Note that it does not have a dedicated escape key, instead it has a home key in its place. By pressing "Fn" and the home button, it will work as an escape key. A pain, but at least it can be done. The key mechanism is decent enough, and although the keyboard is louder than my macbook pro's keyboard, it's quieter than my old Apple Pro keyboard (the white one) so that's a plus. Battery life is excellent - I can go two weeks of daily and extensive use before needing to put new batteries in.

So why not 5 stars? A couple of reasons:

1) The command key sticks a little on the Omoton. I have to press hard for it to register.
2) Sometimes (and this happens on all of these keyboards) the release of a key won't register, making a letter repeaaaaaat six or seven times.
3) It disconnects every now and then for a few seconds, which my Apple wireless keyboard never did.

Overall, not bad for the price, that's for sure. Has some quirks that I have experienced with all of these keyboards regardless of branding. A cheap and handy keyboard for my macbook pro and mac pro. It's no Apple wireless keyboard, but at a quarter or less of the price, you shouldn't expect it to be.

When I put the CDs into this Sony I could not believe the quality of sound, and the clarity of the sung words, regardless of whether I played softly or loudly. I also like the idea that I can transfer/record music (or whatever) from a CD to a Thumb drive and, play music stored on a thumb drive. I also like the size of the unit; I thought it was going to be about 50 percent larger, but I like the smaller size. Couldn't be more satisfied.

UPDATE - 3-31-2017: I tutor groups of students in singing and I like it that I can pause the CD to discuss ideas/techniques used in a song, and continue from where I paused. I can also record via another technique (not this unit), put it into my computer, move it to Windows Media Player, burn it onto a CD, and finally play the students' singing back to them via this boom box--using that pause button to help them understand what they're doing right and wrong. I also discovered that I can hook this box up to the school auditorium's wall speaker system via a suitable cable. A real boon!

UPDATE - 7-13-2017: Something can always happen; so I bought a second/backup of this model a short time ago so I'll know I'll always have the quality.

title: Works like it is supposed to.
text:
Got it for my cellphone (iPhone 4S) since I can't reposition my router. The kitchen is between my room and the router, which makes for bad signal due to interference from the appliances. My car also happens to be directly below my room, so getting wifi for starting navigation was also a goal. Room is probably about 40ft from router.

Positioned it across from the kitchen, so it could directly receive/send to both router and my room without going through the kitchen. Got a much stronger signal with it. From the car, I took two snapshots of speed tests comparing the main router to the extended network. Here they are for reference.

Setup was easy enough. My router doesn't have the WPS feature so I can't say how well that works. The web interface (just connect to it as if it were your router wifi in order to access it) was simple and worked just fine.

Things to keep in mind: out of the usual b/g/n for the 2.4GHz frequency, this uses ONLY the g broadcast. Reading also tells me that he antennae send signal PERPENDICULAR to the direction they point, so imagine a circle radiating out from your antenna point and position accordingly.

For the price, the more tech savvy (and less space-limited) might consider just buying another router. Not difficult to find a $20 router that has dedicated routing (as opposed to gateway'ing, where your router ALSO acts as a go between from your computer to the modem) as an option in the manufacturer's firmware, or one of the 3rd party firmware upgrades like DD-WRT.

So far, no issues whatsoever with the performance.

title: Works great, easy to instal, high quality. UPDATE - Stopped working after 5 months
text:
Update, as of January 31, 2019. I received the door lock on September 5, 2018. Although I did say I was skeptical If you read the original post I gave it a great review with 5 stars. I should have gone with my initial intuition. The lock worked great until a few nights ago when I went out my back sliding glass door to take the trash out. I then took the trash cans to the front curb and as usual, I come in through the front door. Everything worked the same except I did not hear the motor engaging the door handle, so the handle just moves freely while the latch stays locked. Lucky I left the sliding glass door open or I would have been locked out of my house.

The key does work when the motors fail, and the handle on the inside is always fixed to the latch. You can still use the lock as long as you always have the key. The door is always locked from the outside and unlocked from the inside. I have a Schlage electronic deadbolt above it and I have had that for over 5 years and it has never failed. I have read some of the other stories on here and I am lucky I did not have to call a locksmith. It could have been a much worse situation. I have also noticed that the reviews and customer ratings are getting worse. It did work great for 5 months. I see quite a few from the last 5 months all saying the lock failed. I do remember some mention of motor failure when I was comparing, but there is always a chance of any product failing and other companies had worse or no review. I have to be honest and say that everything else worked and still works perfectly. The card reader, fingerprint scanner, keypad, voice prompts, digital readout. All still working, but no motor to unlock it. I think the product idea is still new with the fingerprint and card reader. I would wait till a bigger and well-known company has one and will back it. I doubt I will try to contact the manufacturer, the stories on here don't sound encouraging. This lock could have great potential, just make sure you have a hide-a-key somewhere if you want to take a gamble and buy it. Happy shopping.

Mark I

Original post - "I was skeptical when I first ordered this. It did look and sound too good for the price. I have used electronic locks for 10 years at my house. I have gone through many brands, some better than others. I have seen technology change and this is by far the best. It does everything for home and business security. Great if you need to give a one-time use code to a friend. Has 3 different user levels with up to 300 different users. It keeps a log of all the user and the time and date they entered.

Fingerprint scanner works great, with the option for a passcode, card entry, and even a metal key can be used. It also has a place to supply power from outside if the batteries die and you need temporary power to get in. The handles reverse and the top LCD is backlit and easy to read. The keypad is illuminated in a nice blue and even does lighted patterns for different responses. It has a nice voice guided prompt for entry that can also be muted. A perfect lock that does everything I can imagine and looks and feels high quality.

Mark I"

title: works, but needs lots of improvements especially in speed, connectivity, and mobile access
text:
I was looking for a personal cloud storage, so I could have all my data with me all the time. This does that, but only partially. First of all, setting up is not as simple as I would have liked. Let me say it is not hard to set up, just not as straight forward. Accessing it from the local network is fairly easy, usually with no major issues however as many users mention it is slow. Copying files to it over the local network does not exceeded the 3.5-4Mb/s ever and depending on the file size it can get much slower. This is one of the major drawbacks, cause this also translates onto the remote accessing from outside the local network which makes it painfully slow, almost useless. The other major drawback is that if you don't have a stable local network and your router gets turned off, some times the IP of it would change and you will have to reconfigure it.
Now, software wise, there are a couple of software that you'll have to download to access it (although you can also access it without any software throught the windows explorer from the local network). The backup tool from seagate never worked for me as I wasn't able to detect the drive. The other important software you'll need to get is S-drive which basically allows you to access the drive from the local network as well as the internet, creating a drive access on your windows explorer as it was another drive. Now for this you'll need to create a seagate account and link this drive to it. This works just fine most of the times, but I had trouble to reconnect after my router was rebooted once.
finally the mobile access/backup is painfully slow too, again pretty much useless. it has two apps that do completely different things, one that allows to backup everything in your phone to the drive (works fairly well, although you have to log in into the drive manually every time!!!!!) and the other app is to access the content in the drive which is just plain crap when you access over the internet, as it does not allow you to see your private folders and you can only access public ones which pretty much defeat the purpose of the drive.

title: Could have been a Great 5 Start product except.....
text:
I had really high hopes for this product. It seems to be the only HD video device that will capture to .mp4 files on SD cards.

Sadly there are two problems. First: Support is effectively non existent. I emailed AGPtek® with a question about the availability of firmware updates mentioned in the documentation that came with the device. (No URL was given for the download though). Their response was a request for "a copy of my order confirmation", so I sent them a screenshot of my Amazon order history. Their response to that was to resend the same stock request for "a copy of my order confirmation". ...so that seems to be the extent of their "support".

The second problem is that the device only supports SD cards and USB sticks formatted a FAT32. This imposes an absolute file size limit of 2.1GB.
Even a 60 minute recording at 720p60 is larger than that. 1080p recordings are even larger. Supporting ExFAT would have solved that problem nicely.

UPDATE: I should have posted a work-around for the split file issue. It's actually fairly easy to fix with ffmpeg as long as you're comfortable on the command line.

First we convert the .mp4 files int mpeg-2 transport streams:

Encode_16.mp4 -b:v 2.5M -bsf:v h264_mp4toannexb -f mpegts A.ts
Encode_16_1.mp4 -b:v 2.5M -bsf:v h264_mp4toannexb -f mpegts B.ts

(The -b:v 2.5M parameter sets the bitrate of the .ts files to 2.5 Mbits/sec. You can play with that number to trade off quality for file size, but you can't improve the quality over that of the original by increasing the bitrate).

Then we concatenate the .ts files and output the result to an mp4 file:

ffmpeg -i "concat:A.ts|B.ts" -c copy result.mp4

If I ever discover a link to the firmware update download I'll post another update.

UPDATE 2: It appears that I misread the 3.5pt type on the meager little documentation slip. (I believe it saving trees, but this is a bit too much... at least provide a link to a readable web page or PDF download).

When I scanned it and blew it up to a readable size it appears that the firmware they mentioned was firmware for the PS4, not the firmware for the Game Capture box itself. While that means that successfully contacting customer support probably wouldn't have yielded any results, it doesn't excuse their complete evasion any actual contact from customers.

title: A great value and must buy for audio fans in cars without Bluetooth.
text:
First of all, I want to say, for the current list price (At time of this review, $12.99) this product is a bargain. If the only thing it did successfully was play clear music through the car stereo via Bluetooth connection, I would find it worth it's price. That being said, it does also allow for Bluetooth calling through your car stereo, a feature that is, perhaps, a little less effective (more on that later) but still functional and an added value for older cars, or cars with failing Bluetooth systems.

I have to say I haven't used an FM transmitter since my 1985 Chrysler LeBaron, and I am always amazed by how few people know these exist. To put it plainly, if your car has no Bluetooth capability, this is how you can stream audio files (like radio, phone calls, MP3s) from any Bluetooth capable device (MP3 players, tablets, smartphones.)

You can indeed set it up straight out of the (minimal) packaging- but I had 'duh' moment when I realized I couldn't have the transmitter paired to my Bluetooth device AND change the transmission frequency/station at the same time. The default is 87.5FM, and my car does not read below 87.7. It took me a while to realize I had to un-pair my phone and the transmitter to use the buttons to toggle the station pre-set. If paired the buttons will only make or decline calls, change the frequency volume, and switch through tracks.

To help adjust the clarity of the unit you can range the transmission volume/frequency down and up 1-30. Find a clarity that is sharp, then adjust the volumne on your car stereo directly to the desired listening volume.

The LCD display on the front is very easy to read in just about every lighting situation, even direct with the moon roof back, and there are a few simple features that add bonus functionality to the device such as the ability to angle it at any direction (to fit within your car's console/dash) configuration, and dual USB ports so that you can still charge from the cigarette lighter port while using the transmitter. As far as making 'hands free' calls, yes you can talk through the stereo system, thanks to a mic receiver on the front of the device, but you will have to fumble with the small buttons on the end to accept or end the call.

I have had a few accidental hangups (Whoops) because the buttons are so small and so close. In addition, my cigarette lighter is located very low on the passenger's side and the mic picks up a decent amount of interference. It is usable in a pinch (an important call comes in while driving and streaming music) but I wouldn't choose to use it as a Bluetooth call device in any other scenario.

Again, this was easy to set up and use out of the package (instruction included but not needed in the end,) and works great as an FM transmitter. I love listening to my Amazon Prime library while cruising around town- it's so nice not to have to listen to commercials on the radio anymore. Even better, the clarity is sometimes sharper than the local radio station! I received this product at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. [...].

title: Pray to the gods you never need TCL warranty support...
text: I must be one of the unfortunate ones. Thankfully there's Amazon's customer service 'cause TCL's is dismal. Buyer beware if you need to contact TCL support. I bought the unit just under a month ago. It worked fine for two weeks. After two weeks, it would turn on and appear okay, but after a few minutes you'd hear a hum/buzz that would get louder over a few minutes, then the video would go blank. Audio still worked, but no video and no pressing of any mouse buttons would bring it back. Unplugging and immediately replugging wouldn't help either. But unplugging for an hour and turning it on worked, only the problem would happen again. It was sort of like something tried to warm up and when it did, it just died. I tried all factory reset options... tried reseting via the button on the side. The sound before the video went out was from the back of the unit, not the speakers and was unaffected by speaker volume. I initially tried to replace it with Amazon but they were out of stock so I started a return process (since you only have 30 days on devices like this). With the return started just in case, I reached out to TCL. They are slow. The send duplicate emails. They take days to reply. They do not communicate well. Despite sending the serial number and proof of purchase, they wanted a picture of the serial number and a video of the problem (hard to upload a 3 minute video from a phone when their website limits uploads to 10Mb). After 10 days of back and forth and with only 3 days left to return it to Amazon, they finally called me. They wanted to send out a tech in another 7-10 days to repair it. If the tech couldn't repair it, then they wanted to send a tech with a replacement after that (another 1-2 weeks). I offered to give them my CC to secure it and asked to ship a replacement and I would return the old one, but they said they cannot do that. I work and can't wait for a tech to come to my home to do a repair for hours and possibly have to return again. Plus it would be another week to three weeks before I'd have a working TV... which would be too late to return it to Amazon and would now be an item with used, replacement parts in it... this for something I'd had less than a month. I've seen some good reviews for these and some bad ones. I understand tech fails. But its the TCL technical support that really failed here. In the end, I saw Amazon had these in stock again... so I cancelled the return, and redid it as an exchange. New TV will be here in 48 hours and I have 30 days to return the bad one to Amazon. No waiting 7-10 days for a tech... and 1-2 weeks for a new unit if repairs can't be done. I just put the bad one into the replacement ones box and drop it off at UPS. Thank you Amazon for having such great customer service. TCL... I will never deal with you again.

title: Good Machine at a Great Price
text:
I bought this netbook because my kids' school assigns so much internet and computer-based homework that we needed a second laptop. It works fine for its intended purpose (homework for elementary and middle school aged kids), but I would not want this to be my personal laptop.

The Bad:
The matte screen is not good for watching videos/movies/streaming, and I definitely would not want to try to edit photos on this machine. The keyboard is unpleasant to type on (the keys are awkwardly shaped and sticky, so it takes a little concentration and banging, which I'm not used to needing to do), and the trackpad and buttons are the pits.

The Good
Price: As a basic internet-based word processor/research tool, this fits the bill just fine, and the price for a reliable machine is hard to beat.
Good looks: This is a pretty little machine, and certainly doesn't look like my clunky workaholic Lenovo T-series.
Zippy: Internet searches are fast and smooth on our home WiFi. Despite the less-than-stellar screen, streaming video is no problem for this machine (as long as you don't mind the matte surface and poor resolution).
Versatile: I like that we are able to use Microsoft Office products and Adobe on this machine, as well as Google-based documents.
Expandable storage: I'm not a fan of cloud-based storage; I just don't trust it. So I like that I was able to add a 128 GB SD card to the card slot and there are plenty of USB ports that allow me to plug in flash drives and external hard-drives for additional versatility.

Tl;dr This netbook won't replace my work-horse pro laptop as my go-to, but it is a good little machine that worked right out of the box. It's expandable storage and the ability to use Microsoft Office products make it a really good deal at under $200.

title: Great in quality for any Photographer on a budget!
text:
[[VIDEOID:7f791da5fd9945a27fba666eede874c9]] Inside the Black carrying case are the contents which are each in their own separate box. (If you plan on using this for a portable studio, it is wise that you do not discard the boxes as it does not fit right without them. It will also protect the equipment during travel.
Inside will include
a set of instructions (which are quite frankly not the best at understanding)
2x light stands
2x lighting lamps (each has 5 bulbs to one head, each with their own power switch.)
2x power cords
2x soft boxes
10x Florescent bulbs (5500k which is equal to day light) (these could be changed to whatever you color temp you desire just use the correct wattage)

Set up:
Set up was relatively easy with everything. The soft boxes prove to be a bit of a pain as you will see in the video included. But once you put the first together it's pretty simple.
The lighting is extremely bright which is perfect for photography or videography. The Constant light helps any photographer in knowing exactly how the lighting will frame the subject before they push the trigger.
My two concern is that I felt that the lighting stands were not sturdy enough to hold the weight of the lighting heads, the bulbs and the softbox. I suppose it could be settled with a weighted sand bag or something but I had some sturdier light stands that I could use in the meantime and now am using the ones in this kit for the single lighting. Also the plastic where you attach the headlamp to the light stand felt a bit too fragile. With the weight of the lights and box, it seemed to tilt at times.
Overall I am extremely happy with this product. For the price and the quality it is an extremely well made product this can be stationary or moved. (though that would mean you'd have to tear down and re make the softboxes and I'd rather not do that again... )
I received the Emart Continuous Lighting Studio Kit at a discount for my personal view of this product. Any opinions expressed in this review as well as the video are solely that of my own.

title: Looks Great, Sound Has Improved Since the Initial Release Date
text:
***Update 11/4/17: I wish I hadn't raised my review to 5 stars yesterday, because I got the firmware update that other reviewers have commented on last night on 2 of my 3 new Echoes (version 592452420), and I'd like to be able to bump it up another star now that I have. These speakers sound great for their size, better than the original Echo. And they are definitely a great speaker at the $99 price point (and an even better deal if you get them cheaper). It's unfortunate that these speakers didn't ship with this version of the software. It would have saved Amazon a lot of returns. I'm glad I had faith that Amazon would fix it, because they certainly did.

***Update 11/3/17: raising my review to 5 stars from 3. The more I listen to the new Echo, the more I like the sound when playing music (perhaps my ears are just getting habituated to them? Perhaps, but the sound really does seem to be richer than when they came out of the box). These speakers sound is just very different than the first generation. As you can see from reviews so far, those of us who had the first generation Echo have been unusually harsh, while those who are just buying this Echo as their first full Echo product generally love it. I think it’s all about expectations.

—-
11/2/17: I purchased the three-pack of the All-new Echo because I wanted to grow my family of Echo products now that Amazon allows for multi-room audio syncing, which already included 3 of the original Echoes as well as an Echo Dot that I have hooked up to the Klipsch 2.1 Promedia speakers via a line-in connection.

I think my impression of the new version of the Echo is in line with some reviews I've read online from some of the tech magazines, which is that the audio quality seems to be a step down from the original Echo rather than an improvement. The instrumental parts of a song get muddied together while the vocals get pushed forward a bit too much, and the bass is much weaker than it is with the original Echo. However, the size and looks of this speaker is a huge improvement over the original Echo (and it actually makes me much more aware of how ugly the grill on the original Echo really is [unfortunately, this had to be preserved on the non-cloth shells of the new Echo).

That said, I noticed that the more I listened to one of the new speakers over a few hours, I started to notice that I was appreciating the sounds more. I'm not sure if my ear was just habituating to the speaker or if the speaker has a bit of a break-in period. But, when I went back to one of the other new speakers that hasn't been used much, I still noted a difference.

I will also say that when I bought my first original Echo, I was likewise not very happy with the sound (and I had similar complaints). Yet, over time, the speaker seemed to sound better, and I eventually decided to buy two more on Prime Day last year. I think that Amazon regularly updates the software on their products, and I believe that they tweaked some of the EQ on the original Echo to make it sound better (however, I can't find any documentation to back that up; I have found the latest Tap update specifically says it was partially made to improve the bass on that speaker).

Overall, I'd probably give this four stars if the "improved" sound hadn't been so hyped, only to see that they sound worse to me. I'm still impressed by Alexa and the ease with which I can play pretty much any music I want just by asking for it via Amazon Music Unlimited. I also love the multi-room audio feature. I'd love to see the ability to pair two speakers in a stereo mode, but just being able to sync them at all is pretty great for now. I also love the fact that Amazon appears committed to adding useful features, such as the ability to make voice calls with a simple voice prompt, which I've really appreciated when I'm trying to take care of my 8-month old.

I will update my review as I use these speakers more, particularly if I notice any improvement in audio quality.

title: Fake reviews and defected dash camera
text:
[[VIDEOID:303c09924bb76a6c20959305e568b2d6]] [[VIDEOID:55d92f47cba06ff91d83fa1dd98b3de4]] [[VIDEOID:94dd47245589e21f676cb97cae8cb9ff]] [[VIDEOID:ce6d4fe3abc0f67c4a77a0b64f478fc8]] [[VIDEOID:c7ff9381deea212cdd74058e6756dee1]] [New Update: Reviewed on 10/9/2015]
So I finally decided to give it a shoot. I purchased Napoer's highest model: Black-A505 [Revise: it's actually Black-A101, my bad.] dash cam for $53.99 on 9/25/15, and the package arrived on 9/28/15. Yes, it has been sitting on my desk for almost two weeks. I was too busy with school works, but I finally managed to open the box and play with it today.

Just like many reviewers have mentioned, the User's Manual basically just tells you how to power it on/off. I am usually good with electronics, so I proceed with confidence. I went through all menus and settings for the three modes (record, photo, and gallery), and had almost figure out everything about this model. THEN THE SYSTEM DECIDED TO CRASH ON ME. The screen frozen, discolored and shown weird pattern as if it got smashed. I've tried pressing all 7 buttons and none of them work. So I had to proceed with resetting the system by poking reset button with a needle. After the system got back on, it starting to restart itself repeatedly and it just wouldn’t stop. So I had to unplug it and let the battery die out.

All of these dramas happened on Day 1 right out of the box, so what do you expect me to say about Napoer’s dash cam? One word: disappointed! Additionally, I observed about a 50% increase in fake reviews on this product listing since my last review on 9/10/15.

So…I’ll let you be the judge.

[Reviewed on 9/10/2015]==============================================
First of all, I have not purchase this dash cam yet, this item catches my attention due to its low price and 5 stars review.

What stops me from buying is I smelled something fishy about all these 5 stars review. So I collected some data.

Out of the 13 reviews, 12 of them are "verified owner" who only has ONE 5 stars review on their profile, which all happened to be on this same line of products during the period of 9/2 ~ 9/10.

Review Date / Name: 9/2 Alexander, 9/2 Helen, 9/2 Serena, 9/2 Keith, 9/7 Karen, 9/7 Tiffany, 9/7 .Roberson, 9/8 Annette J. McQueen, 9/8 Patricia, 9/8 Jean, 9/8 Lynne, and 9/10 April.

What a coincident, right?

Until Amazon can makes a change and do something about fraud prevention on the reviewing system. We can only look after each other, and identify fraud on our own. Please make sure you study the reviews before your purchase, and look at reviewer's profile to make sure they are "real" people.

title: The 11e Celeron-powered series works really well for us
text:
As pointed out in a comment, there are several models/generations of this laptop, so to avoid confusion let me make clear that the model I have has slightly different specs, but the differences will be minor for most purposes.

We've looked around, and this laptop series blows other options at this price point (I got the $269 Woot deal ealier this year) out of the water in most aspects. You can find this as various item listings, so watch out you don't pay too much. There's also a non-touchscreen version, which should be cheaper. Used it for around a half year now and it works great.

Good: fast mobile Celeron processor, and although I can definitely tell it's not as smooth as the i5 and i7 systems I have with "heavy" web content, it's more than snappy enough for what we intend to use it for (browsing, Office, light work tasks). 4GB RAM has been doing well, and it's upgradable to 8GB if you need. The 128GB SSD keeps things from bogging down, and you can use the SD card slot to easily and cheaply add 256GB (or you could use the USB3 slot also). The keyboard is very nice, with actual raised keys and good tactile feel. Screen and sound quality are very nice. Networking is AC dual band, Bluetooth, and it even has an ethernet port. It's sturdy and doesn't seem like it would damage too easily.

Less good: relatively low screen resolution and size. Although it would have been more costly, a 12" or 13" screen with smaller bezel would be the thing that made this a "six star" laptop. It's also a bit heavy for its size, but that's what you get if you want something not so flimsy (it's slightly over 3.5 lbs - the 5 lbs for the listing is the including box and power supply). Did I mention the screen is small?

It does not come with a lot of bloatware preinstalled. You get the usual so-many month subscription to McAfee, which luckily is easy to remove. It also has various rather useless Lenovo applications, and you can tell it's a super-standard build: even though the laptop has an SSD, it comes with an "active protection" agent meant for HDDs turned on. I find it pretty easy with modern Windows to remove/disable these things.

Added a picture of the insides: the RAM (only one slot, but it's upgradeable to 8 gig!), SSD, and battery are all replaceable.

title: This is the one that you're looking for.
text:
This is just what you want if you're looking to wall mount your big screen TV. I've been using this type of mount for years. And, hear me, this is important...this unit comes assembled. Just take it out of the box and it's ready to mount. No assembly required.

The good. It's well made. It can be mounted by one person...if you are experienced. It articulates easily and over a range that exceeds the mount I'm using now. All the parts are there...

The bad...nothing.

Just remember to predrill your studs before you try driving the lag bolts that are used to secure the mount to the wall. And, you should use the outermost holes on the mount...they're 16" apart and that coinsides with the distance between stud centers.

A word of caution...if mounting to drywall, you should always find the studs, and then this mount should be screwed to the wall studs. Your TV might not seem as if it weighs much, but it can creat a lot of force when it's pulled away from the wall, and unsupported drywall will not handle the forces generated by moving and adjusting your TV over and over.

Just my observations. Buy one.

text:
This made a wonderful gift for my girlfriend who has really gotten into digital photography. It is simple to use and the image quality is very good. This aspect ratio makes more sense than the wide screen versions since it matches the native aspect ratio of your typical digital camera.

I really wish this had a Ken-Burns slide show effect which is an option in some computer photo programs like iPhoto. Perhaps that is expecting too much for this type of simple device. While it does come with a small variety of slide transition effects, it lacks the most basic effect of all, a dissolve from one image to the next. The unit does do a nice fade in and fade out when waking up and going to sleep, so I don't understand why no dissolve effect. The transition effects it does have are all highly animated and rapid transitions. To me they are annoying, so we just use the plain old "hard-cut" transition. There is a wide range of timer intervals for the pace of the slide show.

We keep ours in the dining room where we can see it while we are eating. A perfect location for us. The motion sensor works well at detecting when we enter the room. But if we sit too still at the table, it will get bored and go to sleep. We end up waving our arms in the air, as if we don't care, to wake it up.

title: Works out-of-the-box on Windows 10: no need to install external drivers!
text:
I purchased this unit because my old USB to RS-232 adapter did not work on Windows 10. The reason for this is that the PL-2303 chip used in most of these devices is created by Prolific, and in an attempt to combat the rampant counterfeit clones, Prolific started to add some features to their chips which the standard drivers on Windows 10 (and 8) now look for. If that feature cannot be found, the driver assumes it is dealing with a counterfeit unit and refuses to work, with Windows Device Manager showing a Prolific USB-to-Serial Comm Port device with a yellow mark, indicating error 10.

Very old units, based on the PL-2303 H, HXA and XA chips, unfortunately got caught in the crossfire, as they simply lack the verification feature that was added to combat counterfeiting. This is the reason my very old unit (of 10+ year) refused to work. While this was annoying, I understand Prolific’s desire to combat unscrupulous 3rd parties selling counterfeit chips, claiming to be originals, down to the stamp on the chip. As such I opted to find a new adapter that was based on current chip versions and ended up purchasing this unit.

When it arrived (in a nice-looking retail box), I was a little weary that it mentioned drivers being available for download, as this is how vendors using counterfeit units may try to get around the standard Windows 10 drivers not working: they offer a replacement driver, possibly based on the older Prolific one that lacked the counterfeit check. Fortunately, my worry was quickly put at easy when hooked up the adapter, as it was instantaneously recognized as a valid device. I ran Prolific’s utility to check the chip version (PL2303_CheckChipVersion_v1006.exe), as it confirmed the Sabrent USB 2.0 to Serial adapter was equipped with a genuine PL-2303 TA chip. Happy joy!

Now for those complaining this unit is “wrong” because it has nuts and not screws: you may be forgetting that this adapter is replacing the DB-9 RS-232 port that used to exist on a computer. Those looked just the same as this adapter, as you were expected to put a male-female serial cable between your PC and the device you were hooking it up to, and those cables has the screws needed to secure both ends. While replacing the nuts with screws may be convenient for those serial devices close enough to the computer that they could plug the adapter straight into it, doing so would make it impossible to securely hook up a configuration with a standard serial cable. An option could be for Sabrent to make the screws removable, which would be the best of both worlds, but their existing design is in no way wrong.

text:
[[VIDEOID:2271603282e467cc7dd2d0b79f91c4f5]] First Impressions....

The fan issue that I had from the get go has only gotten worse. title: Works, had some occasional issues setting up.  But now I know how to get around them.  4/5 works, but not the best.
text:
Here is my review of the Sabrent 4-Port USB 3.0 Hub and 5V/2.5A power adapter [[ASIN:B00TPMEOYM Sabrent 4-Port USB 3.0 Hub with Individual Power Switches and LEDs included 5V/2.5A power adapter (HB-UMP3)]]:

My laptop has only 2 usb3.0 ports, and I have a plethora of devices that I have to plug in. Ethernet to usb, external hard drive, mouse, flash drives. And I really needed something to fit my needs. I found many devices that I thought would fit my needs, some looked tad nice than this one (with brushed aluminum and sleeker designs), but this was the best one I could find that had a power adapter. One main concern I had was powering my external hard drive. I didn't want it to run on low power, which can damage the drive. And having multiple devices plugged into one port doesn't supply them all with the right amount of power. So this one it is!

I received the item from my residence hall's front desk (go college!). Prime 2 day shipping worked like a breeze (unlike last time...). As soon as i received the box, i turned it on its side to carry it with one hand: and I could feel the contents of the box shift and smack the bottom of the box. My heart sank. I bought this with the UTechSmart Uranus mouse (review here: ). Opening returning to my room I opened it and found that they had only but bubble wrap between the two items, and not around the two items. What idiot packed my box?!?!?! I was hoping nothing would be DOA because of shipping.

The actual box for this was fairly nice. Sleek black cardboard, well wrapped parts. Came with the hub and attached usb cord and a nice long power adapter. I opened it up and plugged it in! I decided to try all my items one at a time. First the Ethernet. Plugged it in and... nothing. Tried different ports, tried turning on and off the buttons. Nothing. Unplugged the hub, replugged, and still nothing. Losing hope I unplugged everything, replugged, and it worked?! After further testing with various devices, I think I believe it is this. If you unplug without ejecting the hub, my CPU doesn't like it and has issues reconnecting the devices later. So after a small heart attack it works.

Pros:

power adapter (5'8")
4 USB3.0 ports
buttons to turn items on and off
works well with all my various devices
speed seems to be doing fine as well

Cons:

Only comes in blue
LEDs only light up the bottom half of the buttons
ports are super tight, all devices have to be forced in and out
USB cord is a tad short. Would have liked to see a few more inches on it
Bit finicky with disconnecting and reconnecting

Overall:

Has lots of pros and cons. Cons are a few things that I can work around, so I am happy it works. For 16$ it’s not bad. Will edit if something comes up later. Due to the issues I've had, only 4/5 stars for the product. If I could give amazon a separate rating, it would probably be 2/5 stars. (one star up from my last shipment)

title: Reliability and warranty issues, plus other problems
text:
The Cougar 700M has some good features, but I am writing this review because of the problems that I encountered with the first mouse product that I have purchased from this company. I am not a big fan of the "Transformer' appearance of the mouse, and that is not why I bought it in the first place. I wanted a mouse with high precision that had good placement on the buttons. In general I like the button layout on the 770M, and the feel of the mouse in your hand is good. I don't like the deep grooved surfaces on the left and right sides, they do not need to be that textured, and they tend to pick up dust and other debris over time. They are also hard to clean because the grooves are relatively deep and very narrow. The braided cord also tends to pick up dust and lint over time. The software is good, and gives you lots of control over the mouse setup. You get 4 settings for different dpi/sensitivities.

Now for the problems. After about 5 weeks of normal use (no dropping or other issues that might have affected reliability) the left mouse button started performing "double clicks" when only a single click had been made. At first I did not pay too much attention, but it began to happen more frequently, often while working on a spreadsheet or when selecting files from a folder. So rather than selecting a file or folder, the file or folder would open. I would go to select a cell in the spreadsheet, and instead it would go into text editing mode while I was trying to do a "Ctrl-C" to copy the contents of the cell. As this happened more and more, the mouse became less and less usable, and very frustrating.

I began testing the left mouse button extensively to see how often the double click problem happened. I would go across a row of folders on the desktop and single click on each one to see if the folder was selected, or opened. Sometimes I could go for dozens and dozens of clicks before a folder opened, sometimes it would happen in the first 10 clicks. The company claims that the "Omron microswitches" are rated for 5 million clicks, so it is curious that my 700M started having switch problems after barely more than a month. When it became obvious that the problem was not going away, I contacted the company (The HEC Group) to request an RMA to have the mouse replaced under warranty. The first reply was swift and decisive:

"Hello
As Amazon is not one of our authorized resellers, please process returns with Amazon.
Thank you
HEC GROUP USA
rma@hecgroupusa.com"

I wrote back to explain that the 30 day return period was over and that I needed to process the RMA through them. Again, I got a swift reply:

"When purchasing on Amazon, if that particular ad for the item states " Sold by MALABS, fulfilled by Amazon" then warranty service can be processed by HEC as MALABS is one of our authorized reseller.
Unfortunately, that is how the rules work as there are many individuals and small stores out there that sell through Amazon, and we cannot authenticate the nature of the products unless they are our registered resellers.

HEC GROUP USA
rma@hecgroupusa.com"

The mouse was sold from and fulfilled by Amazon. I found it extremely strange that a small outfit like MALABS was considered to be an authorized reseller, but that Amazon was not. Nonetheless, I contacted Amazon and explained the situation to them, and despite the fact that they did not have an obligation to fulfill Cougar's warranty, they immediately cross-shipped a replacement and sent me a return label to return the defective mouse. I have the new mouse installed, and so far no double click problems. We will see what happens over the next few weeks and months. If I have any problems I will update this review.

I thought it was important to let other potential customers know that The HEC Group is prone to looking for excuses to not offer warranty support for their products, and that the switches might not be quite as reliable as the company claims.

*Update: 700M Cougar Mouse Number 2

I received a new 700M and at first all was well. However, within 2 days the new 700M mouse began to show the double click problem much worse than the first one. Sometimes almost every click was a double click (folder or file would open rather than just get selected).

So I began to think that it must be some other problem with my computer (Intel i7 3.3GHz, 12GB RAM, Windows 7 Ultimate). I went into full diagnostics mode.

1) I first moved the USB plug for the mouse from a USB 3.0 socket to a USB 2.0 socket. Same problem.
2) I put an older (~ 1 year old G400s) Logitech mouse on the original USB 3.0 socket. No problem with double clicks at all using the Logitech mouse.
3) I disabled the Cougar mouse control software (UIX) at Windows startup. Same double click problem.
4) I adjusted the double-click speed in the Windows 7 mouse control panel. No luck.
5) Plugged the 700M into a different Windows 7 computer (I noticed a very long driver install time) and guess what? The first click opened a folder rather than selecting it! The problem was just as bad on a different computer, without the Cougar mouse control software having ever been installed.
6) Just for the heck of it, I plugged the 700M into a 14 year old Windows XP computer that was still functioning well. The first click on a folder opened it!

Bottom line, there is something very wrong with some Cougar 700M mice. Maybe a bad batch of switches, maybe a design flaw in how the switches are mounted in the frame. Who knows? I have never experienced this problem with mice in the past, and I have owned many different mice from different manufacturers. Right now the Logitech G400s is working perfectly. I have uninstalled the UIX software, am returning the mouse for a refund, and I won't be buying mice from Cougar again. Cougar mice are made by a Chinese company known as the HEC Group who specializes in aluminum, pharmaceuticals and resorts. Clearly, they are not focusing on their computer hardware quality.

*additional update: After looking into the issue more I see that Logitech mice have gotten many complaints about this issue (although I have not seen this particular problem with any Logitech mice I have owned, which numbers in the dozens). However, one person on the Logitech forum mentioned that in low humidity environments an electrostatic charge can build up on the plastic, and cause the microswitch to misread the clicks. We just had a polar vortex come through with temps around 0, and the humidity in the house is down to around 38%. Using your breath to humidify the switches supposedly fixes the problem. I have the 700M boxed up and ready to ship back, so I did not test this to see if it worked. Either way, it is a design problem that could be easily fixed with metal switch covers that are grounded. I am tempted to take it out of the box to test it. If I do, I will update.

*Final update -SOLVED; I couldn't resist. I had to test out the low humidity hypothesis. I took the 700M out of the box again, and plugged it in. The problem was severe. I breathed some humidity onto the mouse, and immediately the problem was lessened, but not gone. I slipped a small piece of aluminum foil under the left switch and touched it to a metal object. I removed the aluminum foil and breathed on the mouse again. Problem gone. Unfortunately, we are having a very cold period now and our whole-house humidifier struggles to keep the house at 38 to 40% relative humidity. So until this mouse is redesigned with grounded metal switch covers, or with special non-static plastic switch covers, I just don't want to keep breathing on my mouse to prevent the double click problem.

Additional update: I have been using the Logitech Proteus mouse since I returned the 700M, and I just don't like the Proteus for a number of reasons, including the fact that the bottom cover on the laser emitter falls off while playing games at times (held on by a small magnet). I waited several months before trying to purchase the 700M again, but I really preferred it over the Proteus, so the other day I ordered another 700M. It was nice to have it back again, until I noticed that mouse button 4 (back button while web surfing) did not work. I then installed the UIX software to see if I could get it going, but no luck. Mouse button 4 was dead. I am returning the 700M for a replacement, let's hope the 4th time is the charm.

Fourth Cougar 700M mouse: I received my 4th 700M mouse, and everything worked just fine, with one problem that cropped up quickly. The aluminum frame on this one was slightly bent so that the front lip was lower than the pads keeping the mouse off the table surface. This led to the aluminum frame wearing away on the desktop, which then scratched and stained the nice cherry wood. I have so far been unable to get the aluminum stains out of the wood surface, forcing me to use a mouse pad to protect the table top from further damage. See image showing the worn aluminum frame and permanent damage to the desk top.
