title: Dependable
text:
First and most important... this is NOT a router or a switch. It has just one Ethernet port and that is for plugging into a router or switch. It has one function and that is allowing wireless devices attach to an existing working network. It will not, in any way, directly connect you to the internet.

What can I say? I love Netgear wireless access points. I was scared when buying new because my Netgear Rangemax started needing resetting often after 10 long years of basically carefree and faithful service. It was like losing an old friend that performed better (for my purposes) than advertised. So far brand new ProSafe is living up to the legacy. After configuring it for my network, I haven't touched it and that is the way I like it.

You may be wondering why anyone would have need of a WAP (wireless access point). For one thing I have a 3 story home. For another I don't like all-in-one devices (router+firewall+wap). If the all-in-one fails or becomes unstable everything is down. If the WAP fails and the router is still functional (like I had happening to me) there is still a lot I can do. The same is true if the router fails and the WAP still functions. Also, I want to place my WAP where I want it and where it does me the most good and not be forced to place it where the internet connection happens to come in. It is not the cheapest route you can go but for me it has been the most stable and long-lasting.

At any given time I have between 5 and 18 wireless devices making demands on it. From computers to IP cameras, from ipads to media streamers (eg Roku) I have not seen any problems with connectivity, lagging, or range. The same "weak" spots in my house are there but they were there before the Rangemax too.

Caveat: I do not use advanced features like range extenders or bridging. I suspect if I wanted a wireless bridge I would want to spend more but for all I know this might be fine.

title: Great Speaker(In-Depth Review)
text:
The Malibu XL by Malektronic was released with the second generation of Malektronic’s Bluetooth speaker line. With the growing popularity and production of Bluetooth speakers, companies are trying harder than ever to provide a quality speaker while maintaining an affordable price.

The Good:
Sound quality: When you hear the word speaker, you instantly think of sound. Sound quality can either make or break a speaker. In the Malibu XL’s case, it makes the speaker. This speaker provide high quality sound with its 2 X 8 Watt RMS speakers and incredible bass with a passive subwoofer. The speaker is said to be the loudest speaker in the Malektronic family and I tend to agree. This speaker will easily fill your living room, office, or even garage with the music of your choice.
Build Quality: The build quality looks and feels great. The simple yet elegant design is complimented with a matte black finish to provide a sleek and attractive Bluetooth Speaker. With dimensions of 4 x 4.25 x 10.25 inches and weighing in at a mere 2.70 Pounds, the Malibu XL packs a punch while retaining its portability. This speaker could easily be put in a backpack or a large purse. There are three large yet attractive buttons on the top of the speaker that allow you to control the Volume up/down, next/last track, pause/play, and answer a phone call. With a built-in Mic, the speaker is ideal for use as a speakerphone.
Battery Life: The Malibu XL features three 2000 mAh batteries that will provide you with 5 hours of constant music streaming on high volume. This Speaker also has a neat feature that allows it to double as a portable power bank for charging your mobile devices.
Connectivity: The Malibu XL features bluetooth 3.0 so you can be connected wirelessly from up to 33 feet away. It also has Near Field Communication(NFC) which allows for a quick and easy connection between your NFC enabled device and the Malibu XL. If your device is not Bluetooth enabled Malektronic includes a AUX cable for older devices.

The Bad: Although there is usually a letdown in what seems a flawless product, I am having trouble determining what that flaw could be other than the speaker “dancing” off the table due to the superb bass.
The Verdict: The Malibu XL provide the consumer with substantial sound and build quality while not putting a dent in their wallets. The speaker has many neat features like the built-in subwoofer, NFC, power bank, hands-free phone, and a 600mAh battery. The speaker is very pleasing to the eye and also feels nice in the hand. This speaker will fill a room with pleasant music though it is portable enough to take with you anywhere. Overall, this is a very well-made speaker to say the least. I am very impressed.
Would I recommend: Yes!

Price on Amazon: $150.00 USD

title: tiny! great for a custom Linux-based wifi router
text:
My first one was DOA with bent RAM slot pins. CompuLab/Fitlet didn't reply to my RMA request, so I did a return with Amazon. New one works great and has zero manufacturing flaws.

You MUST use 1.35V LOW VOLTAGE RAM / DDR3L. Regular DDR3 will fit but will not work. Fitment in the RAM slot is awkward, you must find the correct angle and it should slide in easily. I'm using Kingston 8GB PC3L part# KVR16LS11/8 with zero issues. I'm not sure how much is supported, but reports say upwards of 32GB.

Includes an American Megatrends BIOS, hit DEL to get into the settings pre-boot.

These run a little HOT but that's totally normal for a passively-cooled CPU (they rarely have failure risks with high heat). Make sure you use the heat spreader plate for the mSATA SSD card. It bolts down between the mSATA card and WIFI card using one of the mSATA mounting screws. The included instruction guide (10 pages) does not mention it at all. Also not mentioned is the BIOS reset button, which can be found on the board near the corner opposite the SIM card slot. Hold for 5 seconds to reset the BIOS to defaults.

Fitlet has a Wiki with lots of information not included in the manual!

The ballhead is really easy to use, if a bit smaller than standard. I like the portableness of it, and if you needed a more stable/higher capacity one you could replace it. It has degree markings around the base part which rotates for panoramas and the like.

Would be nice if it had retractable spike feet, or interchangeable feet.

title: Not bad for the money and it runs Linux!
text:
If expectations are kept in check, the Lenovo G50 is a good budget laptop PC after making a few changes. First thing's first: if you have another PC running Windows 8.1 (Or Windows 10), Microsoft offers a free USB/DVD install creator tool from their website. Make yourself an install disc or a USB flash drive, erase the laptop's hard drive (or install an SSD drive like I did for an extra fast & snappy computer) and start with a fresh copy of Windows without all that Lenovo crap-ware and spyware. The only caveat with this method is that you will need to download some drivers from Lenovo's support site after a fresh Windows install such as the wireless network adapter, trackpad, SD card reader etc.

Since I immediately installed an SSD drive before even the first start-up, I cannot comment about how well the computer works "out of the box", but I will say it's been very fast for me (again, I do have an SSD installed which makes a tremendous difference in responsiveness of the machine). Boot times average 5-7 seconds from completely off to the Windows login screen and most programs launch almost instantly.

Compared to my aging 17" MacBook Pro which was an amazing machine six years ago, the Lenovo G50 by comparison feels flimsy and cheap. I suppose you do get what you pay for in the end. I also can't imagine this Lenovo laptop lasting over six years -but hey, I only had to pay a fraction of the price for this Lenovo compared to my MacBook Pro.

The Lenovo G50's trackpad feel and usage leaves a bit to be desired. I don't care much for the somewhat "gritty" texture of the trackpad surface and it can be jittery at times when trying to move your finger precisely. This isn't normally a problem, but if you're used to a good trackpad you might be disappointed. My biggest complaints are screen quality and battery life. Viewing angles of the screen are subpar, the color gamut is pretty poor and the resolution is not all that good. As a laptop, it's usable for Internet or text and document use, but I won't be using it for Lightroom or Photoshop anytime soon. Battery life is a bit underwhelming as well. It has enough juice to last a little over three hours on the go, but if you've got a lot of work to do you'd better bring your charger.

Graphics on this Lenovo G50 aren't too shabby for a budget laptop. It uses the integrated Intel HD4400 graphics which I'd say is about on-par with my 2009 MacBook Pro's NVIDIA 9600GT discrete graphics card. Playing Minecraft, I've been averaging around 45-55 FPS with 'fancy settings' enabled. In fact, it actually performs slightly better than my old MacBook did.

For you Linux geeks out there who might be concerned whether or not the Lenovo G50 is a good option need not worry. Ubuntu 15.04 operates perfectly on this machine as-is without any modifications necessary. Wi-Fi, Trackpad, sleep/resume all worked fine. I have Ubuntu setup to dual boot alongside Windows for the best of both worlds. While I cannot guarantee every Linux distro will perform with ease on the G50, it's a good bet you won't have too many problems with the distro flavor you decide to use.

Overall I'd say the G50 is decent if you're simply looking for a full-sized, inexpensive laptop. Nothing about this Lenovo G50 is going to blow you away as being excellent, however, it doesn't need to at such a cheap price. This computer was made for the average user in mind. Somebody who's shopping with low cost in mind. It serves my purpose as an Ok secondary computer since I have a powerful desktop PC with a fantastic display as my main computer. If you are looking to buy a laptop as your full-time use PC then I would recommend stepping it up to something better to avoid some of the annoyances this laptop has.

title: Should've spent more $ for a better option
text:
I chose this set of satellite speaker stands primarily for the low price. After reading previous reviews of this product which included pictures, and comparing them to the Amazon photos of the product, I wasn't sure what I'd be getting when the shipment arrived at my house. I received stands that were like the ones in the Amazon photos, which is basically just an adhesive pad on the tops of the speaker stands where they sit. A number of the customer reviews included photos that showed stands that have the metal backing bracket which the speakers are attached to with screws and sometimes washers. So that's why I was confused as to what I'd end up receiving.

I'm giving this overall review three stars (probably should've been two) and two for material quality. My main reason for this is because the two poles that make up each stand would not easily connect to one another. You're supposed to be able to screw the straight pole to the curved pole with a small washer in between. However when I tried screwing the poles together, the threads in each pole would not grab onto each other and therefore I couldn't get a tight enough connection on either stand. Instead of dealing with the trouble of shipping it all back, I resorted to using super glue around the pole threads to connect them together. They're standing, for now. Was really disappointed in the quality of the poles where they're supposed to come together.

Another negative was that the wire/plug from my Vizio satellite speakers would not fit down the poles. So I had to just wrap Velcro straps around the speaker wire and poles. Not the best aesthetically, but better than the wire just hanging around.

You get what you pay for.....

title: Huge subwoofer both in its size and what it delivers
text:
We've been using this 1000 Watt subwoofer in our home sound system setup for the past few weeks and have totally been blown away by it. It was easy to setup with their app via our phones (make sure you have a phone handy as there are no manual controls) and the sound cannot be beat. We watched a few disaster films in 7.1 and with the sounds coming out of this subwoofer it felt like the whole home was part of the action.

Phone setup wasn't bad -- unlike most companies elac doesn't have you register when you turn on the app (I hate giving my email away) just shows you a screen with active, unavailable, and available subwoofers to pair. Pairing was pretty easy but it took two attempts for it to register for me. The instructions have you enter 0000 as the pairing code so commit that to memory or keep the instructions. The auto EQ feature is really neat and for someone like me who isn't really well versed in theater setup it made the whole process simple.

I would suggest you don't get this if you live under neighbors but for everyone else it's an amazing addition to most setups. As for its size though it's huge and heavy. You really get what you're paying for with this. I have a few other subwoofers and I've never seen one this big before. It's the Tyrannosaurus Rex of subwoofers both in the quality and its size. I highly recommend for any home sound system where budget may not be the limiting factor given how expensive these are but it's definitely worth it.

This remote has a button on the side for the backlight feature but instead of turning the lights on it either turns the entire back light feature ON or OFF. That means you actually have to push one of the remote buttons with the lights off to actually turn on the lights to see what you are doing. As a result you have to do some unintended action with the remote(change the volume, change the channel, pause, etc) to do anything else in the dark.

It would be nice if it worked like the X1 remote or, at the very least, allow the button on the side to just turn on the light instead of totally enabling or disabling the light feature.

title: Great Card! Should have had RGB or at least have the LOGO back-lit with an LED... Sigh =|
text:
I bought this card at $USD 299.99 in July 2018. The XFX LOGO is not RGB nor an LED - its just ... white (I knew this before my purchase but just sharing this info for those ppl looking building a PC based on looks). It does have a tiny blue LED above the 8-pin power connector visible through the side of the PC case - but its a standard LED and not anything artistic.. seems to be there just for function or diagnostics - is always on as long as the PC is powered.
This card is Dual BIOS and has the switch on beside the 8-pin power connector. XFX calls one BIOS as "Gaming BIOS" and the other as "Mining BIOS" according to the website. My findings are firstly there is no automatic GPU boost. Secondly, the 'Gaming Bios' (default) runs 1150MHz core and 2100 VRAM (8.4GHz). When you switch to what XFX calls the 'Mining Bios' it is 1405MHz core with VRAM 2000MHz (8GHz) the latter being a respectable and repeatable 10% uplift in graphics performance which I tested in Unigine Heaven 4.0 benchmark (1080p, Ultra, 8xAA, Tessellation Extreme) from 50 fps to 55 fps. Radeon Driver Version Adrenaline 18.5.1, Win 10 x64, FX-8350 stock :D
My only complaint so far is IMO for this price they should have at least back-lit their logo when the card is powered on - no reason why this would have been impossible. Not many cards give you a manually selectable Dual Bios feature and this is the only reason i bought it over the competition - which have RGB... :D
Performance: Well its a RX-580... and that is the tier of performance to expect. XFX however claims this XFX Radeon RX 580 GTS Black Edition can do at least 1425MHz on the core for an overclock (I haven't tested this) but the card DOES NOT come running 1425MHz out of the box but 1150MHz so the marketing may be misleading to some ppl I suppose - I doubt that was their intention but it can potentially mislead. 1405MHz - what they market as "True Clock" on their website is the actual GPUcore speed u get once you have the overclocked bios switched on - I mean the 'Mining BIOS' in XFX terminology lol. I hope that explanation helps but I guess the message they want to get across from posting the cards as 1425MHz+OC is - this speed is guaranteed attainable according to them and that these possibly are among the best Polaris Dies in these "GTS Black Edition" cards.. Over Clockers will know that info means to them... So.. Yes the card is actually is clocked at and sustains 1405MHz on the core w/ VRAM 2000MHz(8GHz) - Just switch on the 'Mining BIOS'...
The fans are quiet yet powerful to keep it cool and they shut off under 50 degrees Celsius as long as you don't change fan profiles in software eg. MSI afterburner or Radeon settings, etc - you can however change the target temperature in radeon settings and the card still runs the fans to meet your desired temp and shut off once it goes under 50 Celsius.
The card performs as a RX-580 should and runs with no complaints... I also have been running dual 1080p monitors some weeks now for work purposes from it.
I do like the card - I just tried to provide a lot of info i believe some ppl will overlook or be misled by or mention things that are not stated in the description of the item nor website. These are all facts - wanting RGB and lighting is my personal preference. I will let y'all know if the card does something weird over time :D

title: Look Elsewhere
text:
First, reception is going to vary based on placement of the antenna and what is available in your area. For my area, what I am able to pick up is all within 30 miles so in theory, this antenna should do the trick, barring a mountain in the way or other interference such as air conditioners, wireless phones, etc.

I'm a cable cutter and got this antenna to work with one of my TVs that I am not planning to hook up to the large Channel Master Antenna I am in the process of installing my my attic. I have done all my research even to the extent of knowing what direction I need to point to reach given channels in my area etc.

One more qualifier.. amplifiers can sometimes degrade a signal depending on what else is in the air literally.. One needs to experiment. I did all of the above and here's the bottom line: The $6.74 cent Homeworx flat antenna I have performs better than this does. The 10-mile rated antenna that came with my Hauppage USB tuner performs better than this antenna does. The manufacturers of this antenna claim it performs to a 50 mile range - garbage! It feels cheap and doesn't perform much better. No matter what I tried; power, no power - I couldn't pick up more than 2 of the 16 available channels in my area.

I expect if you are in an area where OTA reception is relatively easy, this unit will work for you but if you need to rely on the "50 mile" claim, you'll be disappointed.

title: Microphone does not connect to the camera!
text:
I'm a little mixed with my review on this product.

If I had purchased the camera as a stand alone product, I would likely have given it five stars. I am definitely a beginner and this camera has been great for learning about photography and being able to capture some great moments with my family. It's lightweight, obviously has interchangeable lenses, it takes great photos and videos. I definitely believe I will be happy long-term with the camera. However, with the bundle costing $549, I think that can be better spent on another bundle or buying just what you need.

As a bundle, I would avoid this one. Most Canon Rebel T6 bundles are costing about $549. This one says it is a Video Creator Kit. I chose this one because I was planning on making some short films and figured the Tascam Mic and extended battery pack would be great for doing so. Through some research on the mic, I found that, if bought separately, I would be spending about an extra $120. Other reviews on the mic were good and seemed like it was a great value. The mic should be able to connect directly to the camera so you can record the audio along with the video. However, the Canon T6 does not have a 3.5 mm input. So you must record the audio onto another (not provided) micro sd card and then proceed to match the audio and video in an editing program. Again, I'm a beginner and was not looking for this to take so much work.

One other flaw I found was with the additional lenses. Any time I have tried to use them, it creates a black ring around my photos. I am assuming that I must be doing something wrong. But if not, that doesn't make a whole lot of sense to me.

You will also need to purchase an additional case for all of the extras that come with this bundle. Some other bundles do come with bigger cases which, if I were to purchase again, I would go that direction.

title: The best.
text:
These are the best computer speakers I have ever used or heard and I have heard quite a few. I had a set years ago that I loved to no end but the DIN cable died and I didn't know then how to fix it. I almost cried. I've used a few sets in the mean time, and nothing comes close to these when it comes to sound quality. This is my second set and I am never buying anything else ever again. When this set first arrived, the box had been damaged on the woofer side. I went ahead and set it up, just to be sure and it was indeed damaged. I let the company know and they replaced it, paid the shipping for the defective one and the new one works fine. I hooked this set into my TV so I could play Fallout with some real sound and now I want another set for my PC. Gaming in this thing sounds amazing. Movies have full bass, the room rumbles but it isn't painful, just full and satisfying. Music has never sounded better than on these speakers. Even with the bass up, it just never drowns out the music, it always sounds balanced and clear.

The balance on these is by far the best. They are clear, crisp, but smooth. The higher ranges are sweet without being piercing, which is a big one for me as the higher pitches tend to bother me if not well calibrated. The mid-tones are warm and strong and the bass is like Dove chocolate, rich and smooth. One of the best things about this set is that the bass has its own volume control so you can adjust it to your tastes. I like it louder for gaming, movies and music, but softer for casual TV watching. If you really want to hear them, last time I checked Best Buy carries them and usually has them hooked up so you can hear them. Nothing else compares. I've heard more expensive speakers and they are never as good, not Bose, not Cambridge. These are simply the best.

The only downside to them is that pesky DIN connector in the back of the sub-woofer. It will probably fail at some point, they are known to do that. Thankfully, they are repairable and well worth fixing. I highly recommend this set audiophiles.

title: Review is wordy, but worth a read if you're considering this AIO.
text:
I used this for my first run at liquid cooling. A monkey could install it. I have a full tower so I had plenty of options of where to mount it. I will say if you are using smaller than a full tower case for your build, consider a different AIO cooler. The hoses from the rad to the pump are EXTREMELY rigid. They swivel on the pump so you can rotate the angle of the pump, but depending on where you mount the rad/how close the rad is to your CPU socket...you might run into issues with where the hoses end up when you get the pump seated on your CPU. For instance I have a Corsair 750D case. When I mounted the rad at the top of the case with the hoses coming down at the rear of the case (so the emblems face the right way) I couldn't keep the hoses off of my exhaust fan...no matter what I did. I ended up placing it top mount with hoses coming down toward the front of the case. The emblem on the radiator is upside down...but you can't see it with the side panel on anyway.

Also, the manual suggests setting the fans up as an intake, ie: they draw cool air from the outside of your case in through the radiator. While I wasn't worried about pumping warm air into my case, I was worried about keeping a semi-neutral pressure inside my case. Had I done what they suggested I would have had 2x140mm and 2x120mm fans pumping air in, leaving only a 140mm fan to exhaust the hot stuff. I chose to set the rad fans up as an exhaust. While I realize this leaves me at a somewhat negative pressure, I believe I am a lot closer to neutral than I would have been the other way. I have a semi-aggressive overclock on my CPU and on a full load with rad fans at half speed my CPU has never seen 60 degrees Celsius. Performs way better than expected. And for the nay-sayers that say water cooling is too loud. Fans at half speed, pretty decent overclock, never above 60 degrees Celsius, can't hear my PC at all when the air conditioner is running in my home. Only know it is running when it's silent in my house and I think to listen if the fans are turning.

Now to what doesn't perform well. The Corsair Link software is a FLIPPING NIGHTMARE. It's terrible, completely unintuitive. If you have seen the program being used at all, you're familiar with the system screen. Where you can place your fan and temp censor readouts against a backdrop stock photo of a case resembling yours and lay out all the info it receives in this "cool" easily recognizable way. Sounds cool on paper, but it's absolute junk. Everytime I restart my PC, the fans and censors I laid out on the, I will call it, desktop read no information...and there is all new censors and fans on the, I will call it dashboard, for me to assign a location on the desktop. So literally every time I open Corsair link the desktop is giving me no information. I have to reassign the read outs to the dashboard with, what the program thinks is, newly found hardware. I hate it. To Corsair's defense, I haven't spent an awfully long time trying to work the kinks out with the program. To my defense, I don't feel I should have to. AIO plug and play cooler, I don't want to spend more time getting the software tweaked into working than I did finding a stable overclock on my CPU.

Even with the crap software, the hardware is awesome. Like I said the rigid hoses might not work for everyone, but they worked for me so I can't heart taking away any stars for that. If you have the room, and are better with programs than I am...this is the buy for you. If I had to do it all over again...I would. Cheers.

title: I never thought air cooling would work this well and figured liquid cooling was my best choice to consistently high CPU temps gi
text:
I have had many Fans over the life of my i7 2600k. From the Stock to water cooling AIO and Custom. Believe be when I say the Noctua has done alot for my system. I never thought air cooling would work this well and figured liquid cooling was my best choice to consistently high CPU temps given the demand I have my CPU running at. With the water cooling I would run Prime95 and peg the temps at 88-90C OC'd to 4.3. I figure maybe my thermal paste was old/not applied right/whatever else. I tested with 3 different coolers multiple applications using different methods (the dot, the line) I even drained the system and added "high performance liquid. None of it helped. I broke down and began looking at air coolers. I read reviews (ALOT) and finally decided on this one. I'm happy I did.

First I have built PC's since i was 16 (i'm 44 as of this writing) The other Air Cooler manufacturers need to follow suit on how to install a bracket and cooler. Installation was a breeze, They suggest removing the motherboard from the case which i scoffed at. Although i knew it would be a tight fit the bottom plate went in VERY easy. Total time of installation was less then 10 mins. Prime95 temps? 70 OC'd to 4.3
Pro:

- Contacted them asking how much a new bracket would be once i get my new 7700k. The offered me a free back when i'm ready.
- Thermal paste included but was not automatically installed (love that!)

Con:

-They attach the middle fan in place. They should just leave it off as you will need to access that area. Getting the Fans back on is annoying. It's not hard but I do not have the smallest hands in the world and the tension loaded clips are tough to get a good grip in a tight space (my case and hands aren't compatible) This is a very small annoyance and not enough for me to knock a full star off.maybe just a 1/4 star.

title: Amazing clarity, sound, and comfort.
text:
I've heard dynamic earbuds, as well as balanced armature earbuds before, and each have had their pros/cons. I was intensely curious about this hybrid approach, and all my product research pointed me to the A3. There are other hybrids out there, most being well outside what I'd pay for earbuds (full headphones, maybe, but not earbuds). As is typical with most audiophile class gear being reviewed by audiophiles, all the reviews I read said it basically sounded great but none of them agreed on any single weak areas. I took that as an indication these were well rounded buds. That's exactly how I would describe my listening experience with these. Well rounded. Perhaps a better term would be extremely capable. Now, a real audiophile would probably start picking nits here, disagreeing with me in certain areas, and that's fine. I'm a (huge) enthusiast - not an audiophile. My auditory system is extremely pleased by these, can find no fault.
=====
Time to be an audiophile poser. My review: If you are a bass head, these can satisfy. You might want to fiddle a little with the EQ to get more punch than they naturally provide, but they *will* provide a very good quantity of bass. I cranked the bass on my source and found it didn't distort except for at unlistenable volumes with unreasonable EQ settings. =) For the rest of us, I found the bass to be exactly where I like it - very punchy and fun without drowning out everything else - at a flat EQ setting no less!

If you want vocal clarity and smooth mid-end bliss, you'll probably love these. I was picking out words and lyrics I had not heard before in songs I've replayed 1000s of times. It all sounded natural and swift, detailed and far from muddy. Mids are great. I've heard mid-emphasis on other headphones before, and it always sounded a bit... hollow?... not sure how to describe it. These don't do that. At all. Love it.

Are you all about cymbals and treble clarity? I found these to be extremely detailed and clear without the SSSSSSSSSSimbalance you despise. I found when playing through my smartphone, I tended to use a bit of treble boost on the EQ. When on my laptop, playing through my Meridian Explorer 2, I adjusted for more bass. In neither situation was I disappointed with the sound stage, details, or brightness of the headphones. All in all, they've basically replaced my other buds as my full time travel/out and about gear.
======

One of the big concerns I had going into this purchase was the size of these, and would they be comfortable. I mean... just look at them. They stick out, the wire has to double back from where they plug into the buds just to wrap around your ear, and it just looks... cumbersome. Now, I have owned other over-ear wired earbuds and in ear monitors before. To say it was spotty at best on comfort with these other models would be an understatement. Shure, RHA, etc.. With the Sony A3's, I can honestly say: This is how over-ear wire guides were supposed to feel! They're soft, they stay put, and don't rub on anything sensitive. In short, they're the most comfortable over-ear buds I've ever had. Color me shocked.

They come with about 6 different silicone tips, 3 of which are foam filled. I also purchased 2 packs of comply tips for these. Without a doubt, the foam filled silicone tips are the best to my ears. It gives a little more firm fitment than the flimsy silicone only tips, which I generally don't care for in the first place. The Comply tips, which I thought would win the day, fit well and stayed in my ears just fine, but they just didn't sound as good as the foam filled silicone tips the A3s came with.

Finally, the earbuds came with 2 sets of wires. One for regular listening and an alternate set for use with smartphones. It is a single button mic, and the wires are kind of flat, which I immediately placed on the earbuds. While they don't tangle easily, it can still happen. The wire seems thin and flexible, which might be the only problem I have with these. I'm not overly concerned about the quality of the cable, but it does seem a little thin for extreme / long term durability. I guess time will tell. The mic sounds good on calls, by the way, and is placed well along the cable to avoid rubbing with normal clothes.

Hope you enjoyed the review.

title: Excellent portable travel router with OpenWRT, WISP and OpenVPN support
text:
This is a great portable travel router. It took me all of 15 mins from unboxing to have the firmware updated, setup a custom WiFI SSID in WPA2, setup WISP, OpenVPN, and to configure and customize the LED and toggle switch.

I tested WISP mode throughput without VPN and got 35-40Mbps consistently. I also tested WISP+OpenVPN AES-256/SHA512 and got 3-5Mbps. I suspect that with some .opvn tuning (e.g. AES-128/SHA1) that you can likely get up to around 10Mbps.

That this thing works so well, so easily out of the box with all the right features is refreshing. That it's so inexpensive is impressive. Highly recommend.

Pros:
- Runs OpenWRT out of the box
- Supports WISP and OpenVPN
- Easy to configure
- Powered off USB micro allows powering off portable battery pack
- Good signal strength
- Good throughput in WISP mode (with VPN off - 35-40Mbps)
- Compact
- Price

Cons:
- Slowish OpenVPN throughput (3-5Mbps with AES-256/SHA512)
- 2.4GHz Only
- Slightly difficult to customize the LED compared to the user experience for nearly everything else

NOTE: The toggle switch customization is done right off the main UI but the LED customization is done from the LuCI configuration page which you can get to either via a direct URL or via "Advanced Settings" off the main UI page. Search the GLiNet forums for "LED Config" and you should find the details you need.

title: EXACTLY WHAT I WAS LOOKING FOR!!!
text:
*Full disclosure* I bought this on a 20% off deal. Keep an eye out for sales since they put it on sale occasionally. I think this is a less than $300 product and was waiting for the discount to purchase it. For under $300 I think this is a fantastic product. For over $300 it's borderline.

I had been looking at this product for a while and had gone back and forth about replacing my rearview mirror with this or getting one that slips over my existing rearview mirror. I am glad I went with this one.

Installed in my 2012 4Runner SR5. I had to drill 1 small hole in the rear hatch plastic right above the license plate and that was it. I did it to make the install as clean as possible. I've been driving with it for almost a month now.

Pros:
- Looks like OEM
- Simple to use and customize
- It came with everything I needed to install it including the fuse wires for the fuse panel (Just swaps out with an existing fuse making it incredibly easy). The only "modification" I made other than the small hole was clipping the reverse light wire to add the wire lead so the system will acknowledge when you are in reverse and that was a simple wire nut and some electrical tape. This triggers the parking lines on the screen when in reverse.
- EVERYTHING IS ACTUALLY LABELED!! This was a welcomed surprise when I opened the box. Every wire is labeled appropriately so there is absolutely no guessing or instructions needed to identify the wires. If you are remotely handy this feature will allow you to breeze through the instructions and get to work installing. Make sure to set the time aside to install this. Expect it to take a couple hours to get everything tucked away with a clean install. Spend 10 minutes before hand going over the routing you will take as this will save you time and effort. I routed through the edge of the headliner and down the pillars for the shortest route. This provided about 4 feet of leftover cabling that I zip tied together under the dash. I used some bailing wire to fish the cables behind other wires and through tight areas, like the rear hatch, and down the pillars.
- With an overloaded cab I can still see everything going on behind me outside. Within the first 2 days of installation I had to make a trip to recycling that required me to completely fill up the back of my 4Runner, with cardboard, all the way to the ceiling. Normally this would be an issue since I wouldn't be able to see out the back but not an issue with this. I barely noticed that the cardboard was even there so I can call this a safety issue resolved.
- Product quality is fantastic. I wouldn't hesitate to buy this again. It seriously looks OEM and the 2 sided 3M sticky tape, for the rear camera, is holding up without any issue so far.
- You can turn it all the way off by holding down the power button and use it as a regular rearview mirror in the event a rainy day inhibits viewing.
- I now have the ability to provide video proof of an accident or any rare occasion that happens to be capture by the recording.
- Recording gives you both front view and rear view in separate files for the same time period.
- Recording of sound can be turned off if you don't want any evidence of your karaoke skills or conversations.

Cons:
- Sometimes when it turns on it'll start recording with the yellow flashing dot, instead of red, which means it is a locked video meaning that it won't let another video recording overwrite that file. What the problem will be is I will eventually have so many locked files that I won't have any room on the SD card to record video.
- When put into reverse the image becomes squashed but doesn't interfere with the view so not really a con but more of just something to know.

I haven't reached out to customer service to see if this is a common problem, or not, only because I have the power plugged into the fuse that requires me to have my running lights on to turn it on. Once I find another ACC fuse, that is a constant power when the key is on, to switch it to I'll see if the issue persists and contact them at that time. It would be less of an issue if I could select all locked files and delete them all at once instead of individually. Remember that each recording has 2 files, 1 for the front and 1 for the back so it adds up quickly. I have over 100 files to delete and not 1 of them I wanted to be locked in the first place. If I get a response for a fix I will update the review.

Conclusion:
I'm extremely happy with this purchase

title: I thought Bluetooth audio sucked. Not with this thing!
text:
I needed a Bluetooth adapter for my 2010 car audio system, especially since my new phone does not have a headphone jack. My previous experience with Bluetooth audio was less than encouraging: one speaker I saw in action has a habit of sputtering output, and the two portable adapters I used before died in the car, had inconsistent output that always set volume right at a silent setting, and didn't support aptX.

So, having usually had good experiences with Anker stuff, I decided to give this adapter a go. USB power, good, mini stereo jacks, and a transmit/receive selector switch. Nice and simple design. There's optical output as well, which I'm probably not going to use in a car unless they start using optical in car audio.

Pairing, connecting, and setting up the adapter was a breeze, and it looks like it allows Android to remember the volume used for Bluetooth, which is nice. The latest Android also allows you to turn on Android Auto when the adapter is connected (the sensor-based settings are a bit brain dead, so turn those off unless you want to enter driving mode on an airplane). Bonus: turn off the adapter, and Android exits driving mode.

Audio quality is great, in fact the limiting factor in my rig is probably the stock audio system. It will stutter when a paired Pixel phone scans for WiFi, so if you have one of those and you're as easily annoyed as I am about that, you might want to turn off WiFi based location enhancement in system settings.

title: Overwhelmed with security camera reviews?  I was too.  So glad I purchased Blink. Easy to install and great quality video/sound!
text:
Let me start by saying that I researched cameras for my house for about a year before making a purchase. I wanted something simple, that had sound, that wasn't super expensive, that was completely wireless and easy to install. I read so many reviews that I had a headache. I think it took me so long to purchase these because every camera has so many positive and negative reviews. My choice came down to the Netgear Arlo and the Blink.

I received the set on Saturday, 3/25/17. I took each camera out of the packing and set up the sync module. I had a small issue with setting up the sync module but used the reset button, placed the sync module closer to my router and then it worked perfectly on my V10. I left the sync module on the first floor of my house near my wireless router. I went to my kitchen, on the second floor to set up all of the other cameras. I scanned each QR code on the camera, named it with the room name and then took a snapshot of the room for the home page of the app. I placed each camera where I wanted it, without mounting. I love that the cameras are smaller than the palm of my hand, it made them easy to set up. I did use the mounting brackets as a stand for a couple, so they could sit on a shelf. The setup took about an hour. The longest part was deciding where to put them! I was very impressed.

Some of the reviews said the sound was really bad. I think the sound is great. There is a slight delay but that isn't a concern for me. They is a motion sensor for each camera that you can easily turn on and off from the home page of the app. You can also set the light to be automatically triggered once the motion sensor goes off, which creates enough light to see the entire room. There is a small blue light on the camera when recording or taking a snapshot. I may just use white tape, as another reviewer suggested, so that the light cannot be seen.

I also read a review that said that you could not put the camera in a window facing outside. This is true at night, as the light reflects off the window but in the day time, the sensor works from our second floor and the quality is way better than I expected.

The on demand video is great. I can check in on the hours, our animals and our kids at any time. I did see the "system busy" error in the app a few times but that was because I had made a change in the app and it was still syncing with the camera that I was trying to review. I went back to the main screen then to the live video and was able to see it.

Any clips that are recorded with the motion sensor are saved on the phone. I forgot to shut off the motion sensor this morning and I had so many notifications! They were clear to view and the sound was great.

There are 2 batteries in each, that were shipped with the cameras. I will update you on the life of them once I have them installed a little longer. As long as you monitor the system and turn off the motion and light off when you are home, I can imagine that they last quite awhile.

I may purchase the new outdoor cameras once Blink releases them, as you can sync up to 10 cameras with one sync module. My wife and myself were able to both log in with the same user name and password and monitor from both phones. We may also be getting sets for our parents, so we can monitor them, as they are older. We will just need separate logins for those sync modules.

Overall, I am very surprised at how easy these were to set up and the picture and sound quality are way beyond my expectations. If you are considering a home security system, I would definitely recommend these. I have never had cameras before and must say I am very impressed with the quality and ease of use of this set.

title: My P37x review after a few months of use.
text:
This thing is awesome. I took out the standard hard drive out and put in two msata 850 evos and replaced the 8 gigs of ram with 16. It's quite the beast now and load times are incredible. The computer does make fan noise, but i've found setting it to auto low combined with a laptop cooling pad (something you will probably want anyways to keep your hands at a good angle when using it) makes the noise a lot better. I usually wear headphones when gaming but when i use the speakers I find I don't really notice the fans much, maybe that's just me. If you have this on a flat surface and are playing a game it will get loud, hence the cooling pad. Basically don't expect this computer to be quiet. I would expect it to be about the same volume as other thinner computers with good internals.

As a other review has noted QA does seem to be a issue. The first laptop i got came with a dead video card and I had to return it and get a new one. The entire process only took a few days but it was annoying that they wouldn't just take it back immediately. I first had to go through 'resetting of the computer' which took so long that they had closed for the weekend by the time it was done. I will say that they came in on the weekend to check to see if it had been fixed and when it had not they started the return process. All in all I had to wait a extra 3-5 days for my working laptop...not a huge deal.

One warning to those who buy the laptop. This computer has two msata slots, a normal laptop 2.5inch bay and the removable bay where your cd player is. I could not figure out how to simply run the computer off one msata slot with the factory hard drive still installed. It almost seems like you have to have a msata SSD in each of the slots (2). And keep in mind each sata slot can only contain a 512gb card or less.

The keyboard is kind of questionable. I use the A,S,D,W keys a lot and they are no longer flush with the rest of the keys and are slightly off angle. Hopefully they make it the full life of the computer (shooting for 3-4 years). The battery seems to be amazing. I would estimate you can get 5-6 hours of browsing and surfing the web if you turn down the power settings (maybe more or less). The screen is much better than what I had before which was a older ASUS g73jw from like 2012ish (died when i spilled my drink all over the keyboard :( ). The flaws in my mind are minor and i realize others have different priorities. If noise is a significant factor and you need it to be quiet then I would suggest looking at thicker laptops that have beefier cooling fans and staying away from thin performance laptops from any brand. If noise is really really important then get a desktop. You can watch reviews on youtube where they put a piece of equipment that measures the decibel level at different points around the computer and go from there.

title: excellent amp, but magni 2 uber makes it somewhat obsolete.
text:
I purchased the asgard 2 when I obtained some powered speakers, and wanted to control them from my amp. I was using the original magni at that time. I really liked the sound of the asgard, but thought it sounded VERY similar to my magni. so I took a chance and also purchased the magni 2 uber. it has the same inputs as the asgard, but is much cheaper and smaller. and honestly, I could not tell the difference between the m2u and asgard, and sold the asgard to a friend. that's the background for this review.

overall I really like the asgard 2. I wont go into hyper detail about it's sound signature, ect, as other reviewers have done that to death. here is my basic summary of the asgard's sound:

the asgard is a slightly warm, almost tube sounding amp. it's bass is deep and well detailed. mids and highs are smooth and warm, and soundstage is excellent. it's a very competent amp that sounds much better than it's price would suggest. it's quite powerful, and can power most hard to drive headphones quite easily.

my hardest headphones to drive are the mrspeakers alpha prime. the asgard powered them easily, with volume at about 1 oclock to achieve my desired listening level. there was plenty of headroom, so I have no complaints.

all in all the asgard 2 is an excellent amp. so why the 4 stars? well, as I started with, I strong believe the magni 2 uber makes the asgard 2 redundant. it sounds no different to my ears, has MORE power, and the same functionality. so I cannot with any honesty recommend an asgard 2 over the cheaper m2u. and I'm sure schiit is aware of this and hopefully will be releasing an asgard 3 soon with an upgraded analog section, and more power.

title: Disappointing.
text:
Purchased from a big box retailer to compare to a KS8000 that was within its return window. The Q7 is, to put it mildly, disappointing. There is a noticeable improvement in color detail on very bright areas of the screen, but every weakness from the KS8000 is still present. Samsung also made questionable design and software decisions that've introduced a couple new issues.

My biggest problem with both the Q7 and the KS8000 is gaming. Neither set offers a separate picture profile for HDR in the low-latency Game picture mode. This means you have to change the brightness, contrast, etc. manually every time you switch between games with traditional and HDR output. Sony and LG's TV's get this small but important detail right. So both my Samsungs are going back to the store and I'll be trying out the Sony 900E or 930E.

My second big issue with the Q7 is that it appears local dimming can't be turned off. The Q7's native contrast is excellent for an LED TV, but Samsung's dimming implementation creates noticeable vertical strips whenever there's a very bright patch on an otherwise dark screen. This is most obvious during film openings, credit sequences, and game loading screens. Even my wife, who isn't usually very picky about image quality, found the bright bands distracting. Samsung may be able to fix this in firmware as the JS and KS-series SUHD TV's allow users to turn dimming off entirely, but they shouldn't have shipped a TV with a poor local dimming implementation locked to "on."

Third, the new OneConnect Box and "invisible" cable are impractical. The cable is fiber and can't be bent at sharp angles, which actually made it harder to route over a short distance than the KS8000's traditional cable. The new cable also can't carry power to the OneConnect box from the TV, so the box has a separate power cord, which is annoying. My understanding is that the cable isn't fire rated and can't be run through a wall. A fire-rated cable would be both more "invisible" than this and more convenient. To be fair, the new box and cable will be an improvement if you want to mount the set without routing cabling through a wall, but they're a step back if you have a traditional media center or want to do an in-wall run.

Other thoughts: Samsung's marketing for this set is too aggressive. The Q7 appears to be slightly less bright than the KS8000. I don't have the equipment to confirm this, but early reviews confirm my impression that it can't match the HDR performance of last year's models. Also, the viewing angle is NOT materially improved from prior model years. It's still a VA panel. Color shift becomes noticeable very quickly as you move off axis. While it's a bit better than the KS8000, viewing angle is NOT a selling point for this TV. If you need a wide angle, you should buy an IPS LCD or OLED.

Bottom line: This isn't a bad TV. It's just not a good purchase when the KS8000 performs almost as well (better if you're bothered by Samsung's local dimming implementation!) for half the price. I haven't had hands on time with other manufacturers' 2017 sets yet, but on paper and from early reviews it looks like they're better buys. I'll update this after spending some time with one of this year's Sony TV's.

title: Shattered my hopes.
text:
[[VIDEOID:3161e16c15b56867d1c5f4f5ba43e4f7]] I had high hopes for this mic since it had such great reviews on YouTube comparrisons to the MKH 416. But sadly not even close!

I bought this as a backup for my MKH 416, I was under the impression it would perform just as good, plus with construction to withstand water I thought it would be a good stand in for my grip shots in the rain or watery shots.
I could not stand the mic noise. It hissssssed soo bad! It was worse than even a less quality mics like my audio technica AT875R, it was even far worse than it.

I am very disappointed. I guess you really do get what you pay for. I gonna return it and save for another MKH 416.

Full discloser: when I recieved it the sealed box tape revealed it had be previously opened as the tape read void. It's made me very suspicious and cautious, I took photos, immediately as I proceded.
To make matters worse when whoever repackaged it. They didn't put the mic back in the padded slot it was jumbling around in the box. Regardless I examine the mic and cosmetically it looked fine. I did like the construction of the mic. It appears strong and well built.

When it came to performance though, that's where everything went down hill fast! I'm not sure if the mic was damaged because of the poor repackaging or if this mic really is poor in the performance area.
The mic noise was so bad. When my AT875R out-performed this mic that was it. No go for me.

I am tempted to give this mic another chance, by returning this one and requesting a different one. But I'm not sure I want to chance it; more money and time only to have the same results.

Check out the images below. The blue screen show the input levels. Line 1 - Diety, Line 2 - AT 875R, Line 3 - MKH 416. All inputs are set at -46db gain/trim, phantom power 48v, no filters. The noise floor on Line 1 in sound room in silence shows this loud hissing. And of course the other two lines have zero hiss.

My dreams of finding another great mic are shattered to not a even a sub standard mic.

If I do get another Deity, the it turns out to be better or any changes I will update my review. But for now. That's it. :/

title: A spectacularly versatile mini computer. Not for beginners.
text:
This is a spectacular mini computer. For those familiar with computer hardware and Linux, this offers some great capabilities. From stopping annoying ads (pi-hole DNS), to your own VoIP server/PBX (Asterisk with or without FreePBX), to a cheap marine navigation+AIS device (add a BU-353 GPS, and RTL-SDR USB dongles, keep below deck/away from water, and broadcast AIS and backup GPS over WiFi to your Android/OpenCPN navigation station on deck), to setting up your own media server (multiple options), you can easily set up a custom server or servers that fit your needs, all at a very reasonable price. And I haven’t even mentioned automation/robotics possibilities.
I wouldn’t recommend Pi for absolute beginners, as there’s a non-trivial learning curve, especially if you’re only buying the board. Novices would be better off with a kit that includes an SD card with a pre-installed operating system. The experienced will be fine buying just the board. As you partition/image a new SD card, keep in mind that default OS images may include multiple partitions, so if you attempt to write an image to an existing partition instead of overwriting the whole card, you’ll be stuck wondering why you’re only getting a red light, and no other activity :). If you can’t see files on the card after writing the image, you need to try again. Hope this helps!

title: Garbage: randomly stopped connecting after the first use
text:
I just wanted a way to use my music collection with my iPhone, so I could carry it with me in the car (cloud/streaming is useless on the road if you have a cellular data cap). Seemed great (well, great would actually be if Apple wasn't so backward when it comes to basic SD card capability on their mobile devices, but that's a different issue).

Only downside was connecting to the drive ties up your network connection, so you can't use the drive and check email, get map updates, use a browser, or anything else net-connected at the same time. But that's on Apple for not allowing any other form of connection.

A few days later, I go to fire up the drive/app again, and it refuses to connect. The app either connects but claims there's no data on the drive (but if I physically plug it into my computer, the files are all there), or it disconnects before it can even check.

Literally nothing had been changed since the first use other than having fully recharged the drive.

I searched the net for a solution, but found almost nothing. The few hits I could find said to SSH into the drive and change the channel settings, but the disconnect issue also prevented me from being able to SSH into the drive, so that's useless. The drive can "handshake", but it cannot be wirelessly accessed or used in any way.

I have no idea what's wrong with this, and after all the disappointment and frustration, I really don't care. Regardless of the exact details, the bottom line is the drive, app, or both is made incompetently. Sandisk is now garbage to me for anything other than ordinary "dumb" SD cards.

title: Overall it's not terrible when looked at as an Android tablet
text:
Overall it's not terrible when looked at as an Android tablet. When compared with other headunits it's excellent.

I'm using this to replace a 1500$ Kenwood unit connected to custom speakers/amps etc.

Here's my take on it:

Pros:

- Large screen
- Decent interface to set up the various options of the unit
- Some sound equalizing options
- Pretty good WiFi/Bluetooth range
- Fairly responsive
- Almost instantaneous boot
- Comes with 2 wiring harnesses for different applications
- Standard microphone jack
- Good wiring diagrams

Cons:

- Screen quality is mediocre but not terrible
- The back of the screen has no cover and it's bare metal. Really...paint it black or finalize the design and make a cover for it. It's just lazy and cheap.
- The unit is a little laggy sometimes, probably ROM and not hardware related
- Same UI as the smaller units. If you have a huge screen, you need to make use of it. I don't need gigantic buttons, I need more stuff displayed on the larger screen. Again, lazy, lazy, lazy.
- No factory root. A lot of apps that would complete your inadequate software require root. You need to make these units pre-rooted or provide ALL needed software functionality.
- Subwoofer output doesn't have left/right channels. Hopefully you can make necessary adjustments from the amp...otherwise....not good.
- The huge double din size is unnecessary as the main box/unit houses boards that are no thicker than 1/2 inch. Make double din brackets and make the back box smaller.
- No extra clamps provided if you lose/break one.
- The connector for the screen is attached directly to the control board of the display and it's very hard to plug/unplug, putting unnecessary stress on the board itself. The board could easily be broken if you're not careful. Bolt the connector to the case and attach it with a ribbon connector to the control board. Don't be lazy/cheap.
- There's no automatic dimming and guess what...there's an empty spot on the board that houses the buttons, right next to the microphone for a luminance sensor...so where is the sensor? Not there...Cheap, cheap, cheap.
- Minimal sound controls. This is a head unit. It'll be playing music 100% of the time it's used. Start developing software like Kenwood and other head unit manufacturers.

Overall, the unit works well after lots of customizing and work. It's cheaply made but guess what...that's also reflected in the price. Unlike other more expensive headunits, that are cheaply made and 3x the price. This has a lot of pros when compared with 'high end' units. It boots quickly, is super fast and it's basically an android tablet in your car. You really can't argue with that.

These units used to be a joke but they're constantly evolving and "high end" unit manufacturers won't be laughing for much longer. This product as it stands today, is better than anything Kenwood or Pioneer have out right now. Joke's on them.

title: Other reviews varied with people who liked it, and those who didn't
text:
Other reviews varied with people who liked it, and those who didn't. The main issue was how long this replacement battery would hold a charge.
I decided to order the battery since my original laptop battery was so worn out, my Toshiba Satellite L505 series laptop had to be plugged in at all times in order to work at all. For under $12, this was cheaper than a putting regular batteries into my radio/CD player. If this thing lasted a month, I would be happy. Replacement laptop batteries at a local store started at around $98.

My main fear would be whether the battery would fit into the compartment, but luckily it fitted perfectly without any forcing or gapping. It's best to charge it overnight or for several hours the first time, but it seems to charge quicker each time you re-charge after letting the battery rundown.
How long does the charge last? It depends on what you're doing on your computer. If I'm doing something that doesn't require a lot of electricity, it'll last for more than 4 hours. If I'm watching videos, downloading materials, or doing other activities that take up energy, the battery may run out after 2-3 hours. So, depending on how much energy YOUR particular computer uses during specific activities will determine how long that charge will last. (I also do not have my laptop set on the Economy setting).

Overall, if this battery lasts a couple of months, I will be thrilled beyond belief and will just order another one when it goes dead. Or perhaps my budget will improve and I'll get an upgrade.

Works for me, but I don't do a lot of heavy streaming or gaming (my computer doesn't have the memory for it).

Update: The battery STILL works fine. It outlasted the laptop which pretty much bit the dust at last after years of faithful service.
Again, it depends what you do with your particular computer, but I had no performance problems with it, and it still would hold the same charge over a year later.

title: My experience with filing a claim: good peace of mind, but there's room for customer service improvements
text:
As another reviewer mentioned, if you go into this understanding how SquareTrade works, you will be a lot more satisfied with your purchase. Repairs will be made until you have reached the coverage amount that you purchased. So if you purchase a protection plan that offers you coverage up to $599.99 for 3 years, you can file several claims over a 3-year period as long as the cost of the repairs collectively does not exceed $599.99. If you would like to read a detailed (and pretty long) review of my experience filing a claim with SquareTrade, here it goes.

I purchased a SquareTrade protection plan for the first time in January 2013 after I had purchased an HP laptop for my final year of college. I had been through 2 other HP laptops within 4 years. For each laptop, they started to fall apart about 6 months after the manufacturer’s warranty expired. So in January of 2013, I stumbled upon SquareTrade. At the time, the 3-year Protection Plans were discounted, so I purchased one directly from their website with Accident Protection. Like clockwork, about 6 months after the manufacturer’s warranty expired, issues slowly began popping up. I did not want to file a claim with SquareTrade at that time because I had just started graduate school and really needed my laptop for my practicum as well as my classes and could not part with it for the 5-7 days it would require to be repaired.

Fast forward to this past December. I received a new ASUS laptop for Christmas. I was still in possession of my HP laptop. Nothing was wrong with the software, and it still functioned for the most part. However, by this time, the left corner was broken exposing the inside of the keyboard area, the optical drive stopped working and the outer covering fell off, the +/= key on the keyboard suddenly stopped working, one of the USB drives stopped working, it was overheating and the fan was noisy, and the left button on the touchpad had gotten stuck so I had to use a wireless mouse. Since I had a new computer, I decided to file a claim with SquareTrade to see if my laptop could be repaired (this was 2 weeks before my protection plan would expire). The process went as follows:

When I purchased the plan in 2013, I created an account on SquareTrade to manage my plan. On Dec 28, I signed into the website, and clicked the “File a Claim,” button. From there, I filled out the online form indicating what was wrong with the laptop. The next events are the major reasons I give them 4 stars instead of 5. After you submit your claim, you have to wait for a rep to email you to let you know if your claim is approved or if they need more info. Less than an hour after I submitted the claim, a rep contacted me. The email that was sent was full of misspellings and grammatical errors to the point where I couldn’t even understand most of what was being said. The email also did not contain any SquareTrade logo or header, so I was skeptical about even responding to it. The rep told me that the serial number I entered on the website and claim form could not be verified, so I needed to send them a picture of the serial number on my laptop before they could approve the claim. I sent an email asking where I needed to send the info and received an automated email response that basically said I couldn’t reply to that email address and should contact SquareTrade and provided a link to the website’s contact page.

On the page, there was no email address to contact them. There was only a phone number to call or you could enter your info to have them call you, supposedly within an hour. I was at work and could not take phone calls. So I went to their Twitter page and saw an interaction they had with a customer telling them to email them at their Social Helps address, and they gave the email address, so that’s where I sent an email explaining my ordeal. This all occurred on a Friday, and my final email was sent after 5pm on Friday, so I had to wait until Monday for a response as their reps only work during regular business hours. That Monday morning, I received an email (that contained their logo this time) from the Social Helps rep, and he said he looked at my info and went ahead and approved my claim with no explanation as to why another rep requested me to send a picture of my serial number before processing the claim.

Anyhow, about 2 days later, I received the shipping box from SquareTrade for my laptop. The box came with a return label and another claim form attached to it, so I filled out the claim form, packed it with the laptop inside the box, and taped the return label to the top of the box. I scheduled a pickup with FedEx, and they came to my home to pick up the package (free of charge). I received an email about 2 days later saying they had received my laptop and would notify me if they were able to repair it. I received another email about 24 hours after that letting me know that they could repair it. About 3 days later, they notified me that the laptop was repaired and had been shipped back to me. I received it the next day. I kept up with the status of the repairs on the website.

Upon its return, the repair depot (mine was sent to one in Massachussetts, I live in NC) included a checklist of things done to the laptop, as well as a list of repairs that were made. I can honestly say that my 3-year-old laptop looks like it did the day I purchased it. They replaced the optical drive, they replaced the keyboard, they replaced the paneling on top of the keyboard, they replaced the rubber stoppers that had fallen off the bottom, they fixed the touchpad, they cleaned the fan, and they replaced the case bottom of the laptop. I also forgot to include on the claim form that one of the USB drives stopped working and only remembered that I forgot to include it after I had sent off the laptop. So I expected that it would not be repaired. To my surprise, they repaired that, too. I was pleasantly surprised and very satisfied with the service they provided. So satisfied, that I just purchased another 3-year protection plan with accidental protection for the ASUS laptop I received for Christmas. I highly recommend these plans for anyone who depends on their laptop for work or school and/or anyone who uses their laptop daily. It will definitely come in handy.

Along with the mishap with the customer service reps, I gave SquareTrade four stars because of their advertised prices on their website. I originally tried to purchase a plan directly from their website a week ago for my new laptop. They no longer run the holiday discounts they had in previous years, and prices have gone up considerably. I assume because they have increased in popularity. On their website, the price for a 3-year accidental protection plan with no deductible is twice the price of the one listed here on Amazon, and it’s the exact same plan. Even the plan with a $75 deductible is more expensive through the website than the one listed here with no deductible. I purchased my plan here, and its terms are exactly the same as the one I purchased 3 years ago. So I would recommend purchasing a plan through Amazon. In my opinion, the pros outweigh the cons, and there is nothing like having peace of mind for an expensive item upon which you rely heavily for school, work, and everyday use.

text:

Great sound quality, IMO. Hard to do A/B testing vs. the wired cable due to the time it takes to swap everything, but it's not noticeably worse based on casual listening using Shure SE846s.

Downsides: Bluetooth connection is not very good outdoors and the microphone is not great (at least the way I wear them -- behind my neck). I will also agree with others that the volume beep can be too loud, depending on the how loud your music is mastered. If you have a quiet track that you need to crank the volume on, the beep will be disproportionately loud. Not really a problem when using subscription music services, as they tend to master at 0db. But if you uploaded some older CD's to Google Play, for example, the volume beep is annoying (and you might still not get as much volume as you want). Probably worth level-matching before uploading anyway, so I'm not gonna hold it against this device.

All in all, great device. Hope Westone can get their hands on the new W1 chip to improve the bluetooth stability outdoors and increase battery life.

UPDATE: After lots of outdoor runs this summer, too much sweat leaked into the control unit and shorted out the button controls. I can no longer recommend them for sweaty workouts. Dropped my rating to 4 stars because they are advertised as water resistant. Still my favorite style of BT cable for my Shures due to the short length, adjustable cable, and decent battery life. Perhaps a little RTV or other sealant at the top of the control unit could prevent the issue.

title: To Lesson Some Confusion
text:
At first I got confused like others about the hardware after I got it (Acer Aspire E5-551G-T0JN). After chatting and emailing Acer customer support (And having the annoying runaround.). I found out that it does have the hardware that it is supposed to have.

To Lesson Some Confusion:
First things first: This laptop has 2 graphics cards. An AMD Radeon R6 and R7.
The AMD A10-7300 Radeon R6 APU/CPU runs at 1.9 GHz. Not 2.0GHz. (The AMD website confirms this.) It does have TurboCORE up to 3.2GHz like it says (The R6 also has 1GB of VRAM.). And it has the AMD Radeon R7 M265 graphics with 2GB VRAM.

As for my rating:
I gave it 4 stars because I like this laptop.
I am happy with the battery life. I only have to recharge the laptop 2 or 3 times a day. (Depending on my usage. Lasts a little over 5 hours.)
I can also play games in higher graphics settings. As well as watch HD videos (720 res).
I don't like the touch pad. You can use FN+F7 to turn it on and off. I like using my USB mouse most of the time.
When I got the laptop the network drivers were not installed. Neither was the VGA driver. (No biggy. I was downgrading anyway.)
I don't like Windows 8/8.1. So I set the BIOS to Legacy Boot and downgraded to Windows 7 Ultimate 64 bit.

Note (If your downgrading): Acer only has a list of Windows 8 and 8.1 drivers and programs for this model. I had to get the Windows 7 64 bit versions from the AMD site. I also had to find compatible ones meant for other Acer E series models.

[ Update ]
Upgraded to Windows 10 Pro. Also Dual Booting Linux Mint Cinnamon 17.2 in UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) mode.
I also got a USB Blu-Ray drive and a mounting bracket. I took the case apart and installed the drive into the Acer.
The Acer may have 8GB of RAM. But it can be upgraded to 16GB. I plan to upgrade that in the future when I am able too.

This laptop has served me well in the past 9 months. So I'm giving it 5 stars instead of the 4 I gave it last time.

My main uses for this tablet are playing Osu and practicing kanji on Skritter.

Osu:
The tablet is very responsive and the cursor updates immediately. The tablet allows hovering up to a little over a centimeter. If using this for Osu, I recommend trying to hover or dragging very lightly across the surface of the tablet. You can turn off mouse buttons in Osu settings which makes it so that if you touch the tablet, it won't register a click in Osu. I find the buttons on the side of the pen to be a little bit annoying since I don't use them, though.

Skritter:
This tablet works great for Skritter. Tapping, holding, and dragging work as expected. I should say it does not feel like writing on paper, though. The tablet has a hard plastic surface and it feels like trying to write on plastic.

Drawing:
I haven't used this tablet much for plain drawing. I used it once and found the pressure sensitivity to be a little weird, but you can adjust it a little in the tablet's settings. I would recommend a better tablet if you intend to draw on a regular basis, but this should be an okay cheap alternative for someone who is just starting out. You won't be blown away by it, though.

Tablet Settings:
My main issue with these is the tablet area. There is no way to adjust the tablet area precisely. You must estimate the size of it by resizing the box in the options. There are no fields to enter height or width or anything of the sort. On top of this, there is no way (that I know of) to save settings, so if you would prefer different tablet areas for different tasks, you may be out of luck. But this is Huion's fault for not including it in their driver.

Case and Equipment:
I really like the case and equipment this tablet ships with. The cleaning equipment is more than enough to care for your tablet. I find that I don't really need to use it much. The glove for writing is a comfortable fit and stretches to fit many sizes of hands (I have fairly big hands). The case isn't amazing. I find the pocket on the side to be only useful for the writing glove, unless you want a bulky fit. However, everything fits inside the main compartment nicely and the tuck-in flap ensures your tablet won't fall out. The material is a rough felt with a fake leather strap. It appears hand-made and well-sewn. The inside is cozy and protective.

title: Great value in a powerful laptop.  Only average screen and sound...
text:
I had my eye on this laptop for a few weeks before it came out. I've had it for about a week now; so this is more of a first impressions type review.

This is a very good value for your money. It is advertised as a gaming laptop, and while it doesn't match the high end features of my previous laptop (Qosmio), it makes up for them in other ways.

Pros:

-Nice size/weight.
-Great "bang for yer buck"
-No bloatware (accept McAffe)
-6th gen quad core i5
***it can be difficult to know just what you are getting due to intel's pathetic CPU naming scheme. This particular i5 is very similar to a standard i7. Pretty much, the only difference is that you don't get hyperthreading with this CPU. It really depends on what kind of software you are running if this matters much. Lots of games depend more on the GPU, and maybe aren't even multi-threaded. You will only see a performance hit on multi-threaded software.***

-decent video card (Nvidia 960 with 4GB)
-switch between Intel and Nvidia gfx
***you can choose (per application) which video card to use. Intel for light-duty (saves a good deal of battery) Nvidia for heavy-duty. See the pictures below. You right-click on the desktop and select "NVidia Control Panel." Then per-application, you can choose if which card that you want to use. In this case, I want to use the NVidia card for Unity 3D. So, I select it from the dropdown, and make sure to hit "apply." If you don't see your application, you can add it to the list by pressing the "Add" button.***

-8GB system memory on one stick
***this could be a pro or a con, if you plan to upgrade to 16 GB, you can find a matching 8GB and you don't have to "re-buy" ram you already have. OTOH, you don't get dual channel memory as you would with a 4x2 configuration***

-open hard drive bay

CONS:

-The screen is not nearly as pretty as the ads from Dell would have you believe. The luminous glory of the screen on my Qosmio would have made this screen impossible to see if you put them side by side (just kidding). Even my phone's screen is MUCH NICER (Note 4). Also, some other people pointed out that the color gamut is highly inaccurate, and there is some screen bleed around the edges in low-light situations and black screens. Honestly, it's not the worst but it's not the greatest either.

If you buy the laptop on Dell's website, you can get a 4k touchscreen. no idea what that is like... prolly slaughters the GPU, though...

-The subwoofer is a COMPLETE JOKE. It has a 1 inch diameter. you can barely even tell it is there. I'm not even sure why they bothered. There is an included "DELL Audio" app which allows you to add compression and equallization to your system sound. It succeeds is making the laptop sound MUCH LOUDER (it is on by default), but at the expense of adding some noticeable distortion when playing certain audio programs. (Final Fantasy 13-2 is a noticeable offender). I use headphones, often, so that helps... some

-The headphone jack... has problems. it definitely sounds muddy through decent headphones (Sennhieser HD280). Also, it doubles as a mic input, so you have to choose what you just inserted from a pop-up menu, and you have to have a special adapter to use a separate mic. You definitely won't be doing any high-quality recording with this input (it is relegated to 16 bit/48khz). Of course, you wouldn't expect that from a laptop anyway. if you need good sound, you should think about an external solution.

-The overall port scene is somewhat lacking. There are 3 USB ports (all 3.0), an HDMI port, the aforementioned headphone/mic port, ethernet, a card reader... that's it. I would like to see a VGA or a displayport (or 2 HDMI, at least) and more USB ports (at least one more) oh well, get what ya pay for in this instance.

text: When I first started using an SLR in the '70's, I did not like the colors from Fuji's film. Times have changed.
