title: Exceeded expectations..
text:
Having purchased and returned the u2717d within the week, expecations were not high for this s2417dg monitor. The first noticeable difference between the 27'' and 24'' is IPS vs TN panel. Another is 108 ppi vs 123 ppi respectively. I am not bothered by the TN panel since this will be my secondary monitor and gaming will only occur while sitting directly in front of it.

This monitor will eventually replace my 6 year old 21'' AOC IPS monitor as a secondary monitor. For the time being, this is my primary monitor to replace my 9 year old 27'' Samsung TN monitor until I can decide on a new primary monitor.

I really appreciate the extra space that the 2560x1440 resolution offers over my Samsung's 1920x1200. Its pixel density is invaluable. The colors are not as vibrant as IPS panels, but I still enjoy it because of increased pixel density.

First impressions upon only 3-hours of use is as follows.

Having a preference for Courier New at 8-pt for coding within a barebones text editor, a viewing distance of 24'' becomes fatiguing after only 15-30 minutes which requires looking away as needed. I still get fatigued at a distance of 18'' possibly due to insufficient pixel density..

This s2417dg cannot begin to compete with my 12'' Macbook retina at 24-inches away with a resolution of only 1440x900 (160% scaling); the Macbook's pixel density of ~220 ppi probably contributes to its success. The sd2417dg's pixel density of 123 ppi certainly helps when compared with my Samsung's 87 ppi. Unlike the Samsung, a viewing distance of 36'' would be impossible, but 30'' is doable for only minutes at a time; I will continue using this monitor 24'' away from me (hopefully for no longer than 6 months).

When this monitor gets relegated as a secondary monitor, I may scale windows by 125% on both monitors. My quick scaling tests indicate that (while not the prettiest) Windows scaling works better than changing the Screen resolution. Scaling the native 2560x1440 resolution by 125% yields a final resolution of 2048x1152. For reference, Chrome browser's 100% text at native resolution is equivalent to 80% text at 2048x1152 with no loss of sharpness. At a final viewing distance of 36'', 125% scaling should suffice.

This monitor was purchased in antipation of some gaming down the road, but no games have been tested at this time.

title: Absolutely Stunning Sound Quality
text:
I had been looking for a solid pair of wireless headphones for quite some time. I had bought and returned several pairs and tried out numerous others. I finally bought a pair of the Sony MDR-1RBTMK2's which I've been using for almost a year now. They were by far the best pair I had found to date. I reviewed those here:

http://www.amazon.com/gp/review/R3SXFXXTXKK5NK/ref=cm_cr_pr_rvw_ttl?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B00FJISZ0A

Some of my review will be comparing these to the Sony's as they are my main point of reference.

The Good:
I know some people could care less about the packaging but when I buy something at this price point I expect the unboxing to make me feel like I bought a high quality product. The Symphony 1's certainly do that. It comes with not only a very nice (but quite large) leather case but there is also a convenient travel pouch as well. My only knock against the Sony's was that they didn't come with a nice hard case and the soft pouch they did provide was a bit too snug. Also included with the Symphony 1's is a USB charging cable and a somewhat flimsy headphone cable which most people will never use since these are wireless headphones. The headphones themselves seem well built and sturdy.

The Bad:
Though these are comfortable they could use a bit more padding in the headband. The ear cups are quite comfy but are also a bit bulky. Unlike the Sony's and a few other pairs I have tried, you will definitely notice that these are on your head. They are stylish but not as fashionable looking as other pairs of wireless headphones out there. These are all fairly minor complaints though. My only major complaint is the sound leakage. People around will certainly be able to hear what you are listening to. When my wife put these on I was surprised how much sound was leaking out.

The Amazing:
The sound quality. When I listened to these at CES in January I knew I had to get a pair. The sound quality is well beyond any other pair of wireless headphones I have tried and better than just about all the wired headphones I have tried with the exception of some of the very high end Sennheisers (HD 700 & HD 800). They have a very open sound that makes you feel like you are in same room with the musicians. There doesn't seem to be any sort of discernible difference in the sound quality whether you are listening with the ANC on or off which is often a fatal flaw on other wireless models. I have not yet listened to them in wired mode.

Summary:
If you are looking for a pair of wireless headphones for around the house these are a great choice. The sound quality is simply incredible. Due to the sound leakage and them being a bit bulky, they might not be the best choice if you want to use them around the office or for traveling/commuting on a plane/train.

***Update***
After using these a bit longer, I have found that the sound leakage isn't as bad as I originally thought. It only seems to happen at higher volumes. Unfortunately, the lack of headband padding is a bit bigger issue than I originally thought. These do seem to get a bit uncomfortable during longer listening sessions. I'm still thoroughly impressed by the amazing sound quality.

Would like to mention the reolink app on android does work but on my Samsung S5 if I put the phone to sleep I have to terminate and restart the reolink software to resume camera viewing.

When drilling holes to run the camera cables through I used a 3/4" drill and put the RJ45 end in first followed by the power switch and DC jack after. I sealed mine with wall insulation packed tightly around cable to prevent insects from entering.

So far I have recommended this to several friends and family and everytime they say, wow thats clear!

I was trying to avoid a 'stack of boxes' home theater... I wanted one simple box that did everything, but this isn't it.

So, if you can deal with these flaws, it's a bargain. For me, I'm going to craigslist it and buy something else.

title: Extended Test Fail
text:
The one star is because it looks good. Beyond that, it is junk. I'm a licensed amateur radio operator (ham radio) but that didn't prevent me from wasting time & money on this pile of junk radio.
Decades ago, Cobra gained a solid reputation because their circuit boards were made & supplied by Uniden. This is no longer the case. This particular model is a copy of the classic Cobra 29 model BUT with inferior components and what appears to be zero quality control!
After hearing what it sounded like I decided to do some further testing. The results were astonishing! Transmission on AM sounded like sideband but still off frequency. Not only is it off frequency, it is out of band! What typical 27 MHz should be is over 30 MHz! Furthermore as modulation increases so does the "off frequency" condition.
Regardless of who is at fault, it is the operator's responsibility to be in compliance with the law regarding transmissions. This unit is illegal to transmit on! Even if you wanted to, the signal is so garbled that it is basically useless.
With the low quality and underrated components, even if it were within spec, it can't last very long. They have sacrificed quality and reputation to save a few pennies per unit! Do NOT but this radio!
Testing was performed with a Hewlett Packard spectrum analyzer / frequency counter and Bird SWR/Watt meter.

title: Good value recorder
text:
So here is my preliminary review. Note I have only had this thing for 24 hours so these are first impressions.

Pros:
Price - you cannot go wrong for what this thing costs. For less than $20 to have a recorder in your vehicle, its pretty cheap insurance.
Video Quality: Its a lot better than I expected. If you have a 32GB SD you may as well set it to 1080P mode for best picture quality.
Sound: Its not bad, it can pick up the sounds from conversations in the car, whether you fastened your seat-belt, indicator clicking, engine revs etc.
File management: Videos can be recorded in 1 3 or 5 min clips. That makes it a bit easier to manage in searching for something in the list of files it creates and if you ever did want to send a video to someone, you are not sending a huge massive file of you entire journey.
Night Operation: Night recording is good enough but not perfect, but for any possible legal review you may need, its adequate. It's visual capture at night is really at the mercy of the quality and power of your headlight system, which is little better than your own eyes anyway.
Storage: It can handle up to 32GB SD memory card. Its a normal SD not the micro type used in phones, so if you are buying an SD you can get away with the less expensive mini rather than a micro unit (like I bought).
Ease of Use: It's is a pretty straight-forward device to operate, once you realize the record button is the "OK" button when navigating the menus.

Cons:
Cheap construction - you get what you pay for. Housing is plastic but it is adequate. I doubt it will survive an encounter with gravity however.
USB cable - the cable it comes with is too short, like 1 foot long, so its useless as a power source in the car. The cable is not long enough to reach the unit mounted up on the windshield. It also uses a mini USB plug (commonly found on many cameras) as opposed to the more common plug found on DROID phones.
Ambient Heat: My car is black, and in south FL cabin temperatures inside of the car can soar - I came back to the car and it must have been >120F in the car, and.... the unit malfunctioned due to the high ambient heat inside the car - the display showed a snowy image, and the unit failed to record any video, just sound. Once it started recording again, the video was dotted with pink specs. In short the CCD camera appears to be susceptible to high ambient heat levels. That problem went away after the unit cooled down. To be fair, it was ridiculously hot in the car so I still give them a pass on this. I just worry that if I leave this thing in this heat continually, internal components might fail over time.
Sound: While the sound is good enough, if the unit is left on in a quiet car, the audio seems to have some inherent background noise that is being generated internally, perhaps caused by a shielding or grounding issue within the unit. Again, this did not bother me too much as I did not buy this thing to monitor an empty car.
Mount: The plastic mount is a bit flimsy but the articulated joints do seem firm enough to hold the unit in place to ensure proper recording, and offer enough flexibility to situate the unit on the windshield. If you were driving in a rally, or you go off roading, this mount is not for you, but for normal daily on road driving, it seems fine.

Overall the unit seems to be good value for the money. I plan to do some further testing in the next few days, but so far I am quite happy with this thing despite a few minor issues.

The first photo below added shows what happened in the heat, followed by a normal day and night recording.

UPDATE: I have had this dash cam working in my car for 5 months now and it still appears to be working fine. I have since permanently wired the power connection into my fuse panel so it automatically comes on when I start the car. It is like a black box; it comes on and records and I do not have to think about it anymore. I have also just bought two more; one for another car, and I am going to try placing one in the back window of my car to see how well that works, and also explore using it as a backup camera by integrating the video output from it with my Audi navigation system. Wish me luck.

title: Sound is amazing and great Value.
text:
Sound Quality :
I have a LG 2.1 channel sound bar which works perfectly fine. i wanted to try out surround sound speakers for watching movies. this 5.1 channel sound bar makes such a huge difference. its like being in an actual theater!. Actual surround sound speakers make it so much better than the virtual surround provided by few sound bars. The sound quality is really good too, much better than the Bose solo and few other LG,Samsung sound bars in this price range, plus you get 5.1 channels for ~180$.

Settings:
you can control the bass, treble, Center( dialog), surround balance/volume and subwoofer from the remote or the vizio smart cast mobile app. has 3 EQ modes - Movie,Music, Direct. You can enable/disable surround sound, TruVolume, Night mode. The remote is not that great , i find the app more easier to control.

Chromecast / Google home :
this has built-in chromecast support , so you can cast songs directly from the mobile apps for Spotify, Pandora, Google music etc. It uses your wi-fi to play songs directly. i prefer this to bluetooth , as you can text/call without stopping the music plus it wont run your phone battery down and no need to switch inputs on the sound bar.
I can ask google home mini to play songs on the sound bar. it will automatically turn on the soundbar and play the music. i can play/pause/stop all with just voice controls without touching any remote.

Tips :
- To control the volume of soundbar from other remotes and for better sound quality, make sure you are connected to TV via the HDMI ARC connection on both ends and that you have enabled the HDMI-CEC mode on the TV. i can control the sound from my Roku remote. i ask my google home to turn on/off the TV and the sound bar automatically turns on and off with the TV. with this, all i need is one remote to control TV and soundbar.
- Make sure to turn off the Eco mode. this causes issues with casting songs and can be little slow in powering it on.

Cons:
- No display on the sound bar. hard to decipher the LED flashes.

Update: Well, after a couple of days, the incompatible charger message has returned and the battery is draining a couple of percent an hour while using this cable. I have swapped batteries, charging blocks and even cables, including another one of these same cables from known good setup to isolate the true problem and each time, the symptoms follow the cable so at a 50 percent reliability rate, I cannot in good conscious, give this product more than 2 stars. The ONLY reason they didn't get 1 star is because at least one of the two I ordered worked, at least for now anyway. And for the price of this cable, there is no way I am paying return postage to send it back to the manufacturer for a replacement. If my confirmed purchase thru Amazon is not enough proof of purchase and my statement that the cable is proven bad by all the troubleshooting I have already gone thru to prove it, then so be it. They can lose a customer and I will just find another solution from another manufacturer.

Original review - I purchased two of these so that I could run power to cameras that weren't conveniently near a power source and in areas that aren't easily accessed. The cords seem to work ok with one caveat. The rubber boot on the cords surrounding the plug that goes into the back of the Arlo Pro cameras I have is just a little TOO tight and therefore, will not fully engage the plug of the camera at times. Over the past couple of days of using them, they seem to be ok when first plugged in and after a little moving around, then they stop charging or I get the "incompatible charger" message. So I go out, mess with the plug again, rinse and repeat. This has been going on now for 3 days. Since I am not going to go thru the hassle of contacting the company, sending them back, get new ones and just have it happen all over again, I decided to trim the bottom half of the rubber boot back towards the edge of the internal plug itself by about half. That now allows the plug itself to fully engage the camera socket and it now seems to be working just fine. I think it's great that the manufacturer wanted to ensure a "snug" fit, but in my opinion, went just a little overboard with the rubber, especially on the bottom of the plug itself which makes it very difficult, if not impossible to get a good, long lasting connection.

title: It's good but understand its limits! I've provided some helpful tips.
text:
Just know ahead of time that if you are going to use its full capabilities which is Gen2 (which is what most would like) it gives you 80% or so performance compared to using it on a traditional desktop, I think 65% or so if you plan to use your internal monitor.

Now let me get to the troublesome bit, so they are very VERY sensitive to any sort of electrical interference so make sure you use it on a plug on its own cause in my case my electrical fridge would cause it to crash since I have the EC (expresscard) version I can hotplug it out and plug it back in but basically its unstable on Gen2. Gen1 works fine but it makes my 900p ultra settings of overwatch drop to 720p at lowest settings with still not a steady fps so Gen2 is what you want.

To minimize interference I've noticed several things. Make sure the eGPU is the only thing on the wall sockets helps ALOT and understand the limits of the bandwidth. Obviously my 1060 can handle overwatch at 1080p but the bandwidth limit of sending information from the same cable into the gpu and back to your computer will limit you to 900p on all games generally you might be able to get 1080p at 45fps-50fps but the low fps is from the bandwidth limit doing so just increases the likeliness of it crashing. The final thing I've noticed is that the 10 Series is unsupported on eGPU so you have to use old drivers which increases the instability 372 drivers or lower are your safe bet in the PCI-e configuration (375.65 on ExpressCard) and there are no plans of it being fixed so live with it. 900 series is unaffected by this which is why its much more stable and all future updates should continue to work.

The reason I bring up the stableness is because I have 3 gpus my 1050ti is more stable than the 1060 and I'm guessing cause it only needs the PCI-E power and no additional. After months and I MEAN MONTHS of issues I pass on my solutions to you.

TL:DR

Yes it does support it but drivers must be old and even possibly unsupported drivers from 372.50 and lower (375.65 on ExpressCard). 10 series is more unstable and cards that require more power will increase the instability on Gen 2 performance.
Understand the bandwidth limit and don't push the card if you notice FPS drop. Make sure the eGPU is the only thing on the wall socket no other things or it will be more unstable.

Reddit's eGPU subreddit will help a lot and the egpu.io forums are your friends. Good Luck.

title: Value-packed, nice, lightweight and compact. Load rating is inflated.
text:
It's probably hard to pack more value than this in a sub-100 USD. It's not the best thing money can buy, but it's high quality in general nevertheless. There's no play in moving parts anywhere, legs swing very smoothly with a nice drag. Ball head was surprisingly good, I actually prefer this one to 90 USD [[ASIN:B01EGKYA96 Manfrotto 496 RC2]] for its smoothness even though this one doesn't have a separate friction control knob (you use lock knob to control friction). Even the bag is a nice one, padded and substantial. I won't complain if this bag is a paid option, I'd gladly pay 20 bucks or so.

It's very compact and lightweight. It fits in a carry-on luggage with a big margin (see my first picture). It weighs about 3.5 lbs including the head but without the bag and accesorries (a short column, a screw, and an Allen key). Even if you include everything, the weight is about 4.5 lbs.

You can invert it so the camera stays very low, probably I don't use that feature too often but it should be useful for close-up pictures of flowers etc. You can also unscrew the padded leg to use as a monopod (which causes some problem, I'll explain later).

Caveat 1:
The "maximum load capacity" of 12kg or 26.5 lbs seems to be a gross overestimate. I don't know how they define this number so I cannot say it's wrong, maybe they're just saying that this will not break under 12kg load, which I can believe. But I can definitely say that this tripod has much more flex and wobble under the same load than [[ASIN:B008RJP9WA Manfrotto MK294C3]] that is only rated at 11 lbs. My second picture shows Manfrotto and this one (and 12 inch ruler) side by side, you can see that Manfrotto is a 3-section tripod (and made of carbon), which is inherently sturdier than this.

Just as a test, I put my 480mm telephoto setup that weighs 13 lbs on this one. Nothing slipped when locked down, but the flex/wobble under the load meant that it was very difficult to point the camera to where I wanted. That's OK, the point of 5-section tripod is to achieve compactness at the expense of the rigidity. But don't plan to use a heavy telephoto with this one.

Caveat 2:
There's a big friction for the twist-lock action for the thickest leg section. I'm talking about the rotational friction between two parts that work as a single twist-lock part. That wouldn't be a big deal except that one leg unscrews from the hub for monopod operation, and when untwisting the twist-lock for that specific leg, quite often the leg itself is unscrewed instead. I know, this won't happen when I grab the thickest section of the leg rather than the leg hub when untwisting, I might get used to it, but it shouldn't be this way in the first place.

All in all, IF compactness and lightweight are the two most important qualities, this is worth your consideration. If money is not an issue for you, there probably are better products. Otherwise, you might be pleasantly surprised by this one.

title: High fidelity at an (almost) budget price.
text:
In short, high fidelity at an (almost) budget price. In a market full of headphones with massively boosted bass, or V shaped response headphones with boosted bass and treble, there's been some casualties. Little things like accuracy, fidelity, midrange, and detail. This is good enough for much of the industry perhaps, but not so for ATH's MSR7 - and not just because it has a hi-res sticker on the box. Let's take a look at the measurements courtesy of Inner Fidelity:

http://www.innerfidelity.com/content/incisive-audio-technica-ath-msr7-measurements

Frequency response is pretty flat, but of equal importance is that the the distortion is quite low, and square wave and impulse response measurements are clean. Meaning you're getting your audio with minimal 'added extras' like noise, ringing, and perceptible distortion. No one wants that, just like no one wants to have their pizza spit on before delivery, right? Right. Looks like they've earned the right to put hi-res on the box.

As for my own perceptions of the headphones, I'd say bass is present to a satisfying, quick, clean, and accurate degree with no bloat or untidiness. Midrange is excellent, believable, and detailed. Highs are quite good, maybe just a smidge bright, but not too much. Very detailed without that artificial boosting some brands get into. And this is coming from someone who usually avoids bright headphones ( *cough* Beyerdynamic, Grado *cough* ) like the plague. Overall, I'd say the sound comes together in a way that recreates sound in the way it was intended to sound. Everything from rock, pop, 80s music, movie soundtracks sounds great. Better than what I've heard from more expensive headphones like the SRH1540 (way too much bass that drowns out the rest, recessed midrange) and the Oppo PM3 (tough competition from the PM3, but the PM3 is sorely missing the highs - which was a deal breaker). ATH has a come up with a serious winner in the MSR7 that puts some more expensive headphones to shame, and for the money, I'd say they're well worth a try. Even if your budget is higher than the MSR7's asking price.

title: A Happy Audiophile's Office Speaker System
text:
I've owned KEF Reference speakers back to the 107/2 around 1990. They have been among the finest audiophile speakers on the market for over half a century.

I was looking for speakers worthy of my new Mac Pro ($5,000) and NEC PA271W monitor. I bought the X300A Wireless and have listened as they went through their break-in. The sound keeps improving. They have wonderful detail in the mid- and high end. I read reviews on them lacking bass. From my viewpoint, the soundstage and resolution is wonderful and the bass is impressive for a small speaker that sits on my desk. For, granted, a little more money, they have very good Digital to Analog Convertors in both speakers, digital (via USB) inputs (bypassing the poor performing sound cards in our computers), and two Class A/B amps in both units.

I've had no problems streaming from my iPhone with AirPlay.

Are they reference speakers? No. If you want the best, get the KEF Blades. But they'll set you back about $20K before you buy a DAC and power amps - and good luck fitting those on your desk.

With my Mac Pro Mac running OSX 10.11.2, I went into Applications/Utilities/Audio MIDI Setup, clicked on KEF X300A Speaker, and set Format to 96000.00 Hz and 2ch-24bit Integer. This does allow full use of the 96kHz 24 bit DAC, which is twice the resolution of the Audioengine A5, which doesn't have a digital USB input.

For me the X300As were worth the price. I will likely enjoy them for 20 years. If you want to save a few hundred dollars, look at the Audioengine A5+. If you're short on desk space, the Audioengine A2+ are only $250, and will still sound much better than your Mac, PC, laptop, or tablet.

If you need the bass, either connect a subwoofer to the mini speaker on your Mac and configure it for playing all three speakers, or look into a 2.1 system.

In my 10' X 12' office, these fit the bill. And they are solid and attractive.

title: Greatly exceeds my expectations for a ~$350 tablet with a full dock.
text:
I decided to wait until I owned this tablet for a several months before writing this review, so as to give the best feedback possible after "breaking in" the unit. Here is my full review...

Lots of people have complaints about the battery, especially with charge times. Pay close attention to what you are complaining about. Battery life is as-advertised and long charging is par for the course! With 10 hours of runtime in a quad-core tablet is pretty impressive at this price point and requires a rather high-capacity battery. It only stands to reason that it will take a solid 4-6 hours to charge (I bet you need a good 6 hours of sleep after a long 10 hour day, too!). Fastest charge times can be achieved by powering down the laptop while charging.

Windows 8 uses corners and edges, which confuses some users who don't know about them. First time users of Windows 8 should use Google Search to read up on them. YOU WILL NEED THEM!

The touchpad has built in palm touch prevention, requiring you to touch the pad twice after typing a while to get a response from it. Some users report this as a defective touchpad without knowing how it actually works. That said, ASUS could have done a better job of documenting this feature or in allowing the feature to be disabled by the user.

Dock attachment is a little loose after about a month of use, but this is likely exacerbated by my choice of case, which places a layer of leather between the tablet and dock. I can see how this might bother some users, but I see no signs that the docking connection has been affected by the slightly loosened dock clamp. The radius of wiggle room is only about 1 degree.

The [front|only] camera is of average quality in daylight, but pretty dismal results indoors and in any sort of low lighting. Turning the exposure levels to max helps some in low light. Rather basic video chatting is ok, but you won't be taking prized selfies using this camera.

Sparsely documented NON-ASUS issue #1: A windows update for the Intel -> Imaging Signal Processor 2400 <- breaks the camera. Rolling back this driver (device manager in control panel, under Imaging Devices) and hiding the broken update fixes the issue.

Sparsely documented NON-ASUS issue #2: Wifi driver (Broadcom) occasionally the wifi will disconnect while sleeping and not reconnect upon waking. Cycling Airplane mode will fix the issue. Let's hope MS or Broadcom fix this in a future driver update.

Sparsely documented NON-ASUS issue #3: A strict bit of code in Intel's chipset firmware prevents some UHS-I microSD cards from working reliably. Windows will disconnect the slot and not reconnect until reboot. Intel may fix the firmware with a future update. Avoid "value" (read: cheap) UHS-I microSD cards 64GB or larger. Since the issue is related to the relaxed NCRC chips used in cheap cards, spending the extra $10-20 on the higher model card (getting a Samsung Pro instead of Evo, for example) will eliminate this issue (and give you much faster transfer speeds).

I have found that the touchscreen sometimes stops responding after several times of shutting down and starting up with the "Fast Startup" option enabled in the Power settings (Control Panel\All Control Panel Items\Power Options\System Settings). A full reboot fixes the issue. That said, total boot times between having Fast Boot enabled (11 seconds) and disabled (20 seconds) differ by only 9 seconds...so disabling Fast Boot mode in Power settings will completely eliminate this bug in the touchscreen driver and add almost no time to boot. That said, I tend to rarely need to shutdown, as the tablet is very battery friendly in sleep mode alone.

In very short summary: Disable Fast Boot in Power Settings, rollback and disable the Intel Image Signal Processor 2400 driver update if the camera quits, cycle Airplane Mode if wifi quits, the touchpad goes to sleep when you type, long battery life requires longer charging, learn Windows 8 edges and corners.

Overall review summary: This tablet and dock combo greatly exceeds my expectations for a ~$350 tablet with a full dock. The hardware performance (CPU, RAM, GPU, SSD) is excellent and even runs one of my MMORPGs with relative ease. It isn't perfect, by any measure, but this tablet kicks the asses of everything else at the same price point. It has effectively replaced my full laptop for daily use. You also won't find another tablet/clam shell dock combo at this price...period!

If you don't already own one, considering also ordering a 633x UHS-I capable microSD USB3 card reader/writer or dongle.

Most benchmarks show that most UHS SD cards do not acheive high speeds for read/write block sizes under 64KB,
so for smaller files the reliability and expected life of the SD card is usually more important than it's max speed.
For a very reasonable price, this Transcend card has higher reliability and longer life, and 633x speeds when needed.

Unfortunately, microSD cards get very warm under heavy read/write loads, and there are few, if any, industrial strength
high temperature range SLC based 32GB microSD cards. Thankfully, this card includes free recovery software to assist
in data recovery when the MLC wears out.

Yes, I would recommend it to friend...

title: Not worth the money.....2.5-3 stars
text:
When I was reading about this product, I was intrigued. The Belkin charging dock duo can charge two devices: an IPAD (4th generation), IPAD Mini/AIR, Nano (7th generation), IPOD Touch (5th generation) or an Iphone (5 or up), at the same time. Surely this is a useful item to own. Well, I was mistaken.

Usefulness: While you would think that this product is useful....because it can charge multiple devices at once... it is also a little burdensome. It's bulky, so I would not recommend this product while traveling. On the other hand, if you use the charging cables/cords that come with the devices, you can wrap them up and store them in a small compartment in your bag. This docking station would take up space in a travel bag, briefcase or suitcase. However, I would recommend this product for those who want to charge multiple "I" devices on their nightstand or dressers. I do like that they can be charged standing up, which makes them neater and more orderly. On a positive note, you can use your device while it is charging. Why you would want to I don't know, but it is an option.

Functionality: There is a handy, dandy ball that you can roll with your finger that allows you to raise and lower the adapter (front compartment and back), in order to accommodate a phone with a cover. The instructions suggest that you remove the cover to charge, but for the average consumer that would be inconvenient to remove the cover every time you want to dock it. Regardless, if you have a thick cover (i.e., Otterbox or Reiko) it will not fit on the docking station no matter how much you adjust it. So you must remove the thicker covers (like Otterbox) before you can dock it. My son complained that this was a hassle/extremely inconvenient, especially when he can leave his cover on and simply plug it into the wall. He didn't think that removing the cover to charge outweighed the inconvenience of removing it. However, a slimmer case (less protective ones), like those decorative/fashion ones (i.e., Kate Spade, etc) will fit on the Belkin.

Cost: $82 is very expensive for a product that isn't a must have or at least one that is useful. I am not sure that this product would be a good investment.

Overall, I give the Belkin Power House Dual Charge and Sync Docking station 2.5 out of 5 stars.

title: Seems really good so far
text:
[Orignal Review 10-31-18]
I only bought this for the keyboard to replace the Magnesium alloy keyboard (Microsoft surface keyboard). I set it up on 10-29-18. It was weird at first. it wouldn’t connect to the computer through the dongle. So I saw the quick start guide says to connect the mouse first, so I did that, and then the keyboard started working. but not all the keys... I restarted the keyboard and the computer and that allowed me to get numlock working. It was almost like the keys had never been pressed before (no quality control?). I also had some delays when I would press a key. Anyway, midway through the day, I wasn't having any more issues. it's working fine now.

Comparison to the Microsoft Surface keyboard.
1. I love that this is not just Bluetooth. The Surface is Bluetooth only and would have quite the delay after not using it for a few minutes even though I had power savings features turned on for my Bluetooth dongle.
2. The keys are more clicky - harder to press, I can't be as light on the strokes, but it's more satisfying, you really know that you've hit the key before you bottom out. These keys are also curved just a bit. Logitech's solar keyboard are more curved and I like that, but Microsoft's were totally flat, and that meant I would hit the edge of a key more often and not know it, and not register the key.
3. The keys are slightly smaller, have a little more gap, and have less wobble. One thing I never knew I cared about until I had the MS keyboard, was that the arrow keys on that one were evenly spaced, and when I reached my hand to them I wouldn’t know if I was hitting the arrows or the num pad because there was no gap between the arrows and the num pad. It looked nice and symmetrical, but I much prefer the extra gap this, and most keyboard have. There’s a small gap between the arrow keys themselves and a large gap between the arrow key and a non-arrow key.
4. The materials. The MS keyboard is simply better. I have the surface pro 3, and I’m a huge fan of the magnesium alloy Microsoft has. I think all electronics should use it. It feels good to touch, it’s sturdy and light. This Dell keyboard has a darker look to it, which is nice, but it doesn’t feel as nice, and there is some bend. Also, the aluminum is only on the top and sides, under side is plastic, which I wouldn’t car about if it didn’t bed, but it does, but the bend is not noticeable when typing, so I’m okay with it over all. The keys on the MS are also nicer. It feels more matte, and the keys on the Dell are more like the plastic from Logitech, it’s more of a sticky plastic, rather than a smooth matte.
5. Overall, I think this Dell is nicer. Fi you are coming from Logitech, especially he Logitech solar and want something a little more premium, this is a good choice. If you like a really light stroke on the keys, then the MS might be worth it. But I had a lot of missing letters on that one, and then the left Ctrl stopped working.

I dated this review, so I will update it alter with more dates so I (and others) know how long it’s been.

title: Not an optics snob, but these are great binoculars!
text:
No matter if it's fine target rifle optics, spotting scopes or astronomy gear I appreciate quality optics. I have lots of glass and some is better than others but these are certainly at the top of my collection given my initial impression of them. I received these two days ago and managed to get out last night to observe Comet 2014 Q2 Lovejoy. Despite the 13° F temperatures and the Gibbous Moon, these binoculars performed admirably. My other pair of hand held optics is a pair of Steiner 8X32 Military Marine binoculars. They showed a good view of the comet, but are no where near the quality. As an example, the Steiners show lots of blooming if I use them at night to look at any artificial light, like street lights or headlights. It's incredibly distracting the way they handle stray light in the optical path. The Echelons however are substantially better than the Steiners in this regard. I don't know if it's the coatings, baffling or blackening of the edges of the prisms, but stray light and blooming was significantly reduced in comparison to the Steiners and made me realize that despite the name, the low price point Steiners are not of the same pedigree as their larger binos. I used in the service.

The Echelons are solidly constructed but not too heavy to hand hold. I believe they are made of aluminum instead of magnesium so they have a solid heft. The black overmolded rubber is firm and not spongy. They are delivered in a nice foam lined polycarbonate case. Not quite Pelican quality but nice nonetheless. I'm not impressed by the objective lens caps. They are functional but tight fitting. A little too tight, but they stay on the objective lenses.

After enjoying the comet, I decided to take a look at the Moon to see if I could detect any false color fringing. Fortunately I couldn't detect any false color, but the Moon was so bright it was painful to view. These could certainly benefit from a neutral density filter for looking at the Moon. Although my experience is limited, my initial impression is that these are great binoculars. Nice and bright with a flat field of view and very good color correction.

title: Small Mod Makes Big Difference--Sturdy And Flexible "Hollywood" Style
text:
I've always had a problem locking down all fluid heads. They tend to move slightly when locked, especially the pan. For macro ("micro" if you use Nikon) or telephoto photography this can ruin the composition. On this Andoer head I've found a simple modification that leads to very good results. The end of the pan lock bolt has a ridge on it than is uneven. When tightened, the high side catches on the head and shoves it slight away from where you placed it, locking it there. Simply rounding the end of the bolt eliminates this problem. It will then tighten with very little movement. Just don't shortening the bolt. A file could work,I used a belt sander. I also decided to extend the locking knob to make it easier to find without looking. The threads are 6mm.
I'm glad I finally bought this tripod. I liked it so much that I decided it should be a little more "Hollywood," and made the triangle removable. It was held on with pins that should have unscrewed, but only one came off that way. The others had to be ground with a Dremel tool. If you do this, keep cooling with water because the triangle is plastic and will start melting. I used 3/16" pit pins to attach the triangle. Hitch pins also work and are much cheaper. I plan to make a chain spreader. The description "Fluid Drag Pan Tilt Head" made me think that there was fluid drag on both pan and tilt, but there is not, only tilt. If I were doing a lot of video, this would be a problem. A bit of drag on the pan helps when framing shots with longer lenses, so I made a leather belt tensioned with velcro around the base of the head. This adds a little bit of drag. One problem I've had with my Manfrotto head is locking down the tilt without the telephoto lens moving. It looks like this should work out okay with this head.

title: Comparison Review of the SAMETOP - Jaws Flex Clamp mount
text:
Before I start a lengthy review, I'd like to state that I own both the GoPro Flex Clamp and now the Sametop Jaws Flex Clamp. Simply because I have more than one camera, for multi angle shots! So this is a review of the Sametop as compared to GoPro versions. "Apples to Apples" as we say in the South.
Sametop once again offers a quality made product, at a very affordable price. This time they even improved it. As you can plainly see, both models are designed for quickly setting up your camera for a steady shooting position, in almost any location the clamp will fit on.. This device holds it's place by a very strong spring, that allows the user to squeeze the clamp open. Releasing it allows the clamp to close and hold its place. I was unable to measure the clamping pressure, but it is VERY strong. Which offers a great hold. (PRO -The spring tension felt a good bit stronger than the standard GoPro model). The Jaws open wide enough to easily fit a 2" thick (2" x 4") board.
There is a quick connect base mount molded into the top of the clamp. From this base you can mount your Flexible arm, or just the camera. On both the GoPro And Sametop, there is a pair of gripping lips & gums on the ends & inside of the clamp. This helps the clamps to grip onto "what ever you clamped it to" and not slip or slide. The GoPro comes has a durable rubber inserts, where the Sametop has a durable nylon plastic inserts. Both models held on well when used on slick surfaces, like metal rails or flat fiberglass, etc.
The Flexible arms are very similar. Both allow for positioning your action cameras into 360 degrees of camera angles. Both are made of the same materials (probably from the same manufacture?) Both have the male & female quick connect base mounts for your GoPro quick connect, mounting feet. Length: GoPro measured 6 1/8" versus the Sametop at 8 1/8 inches. (PRO) - I found that the extra length allowed for easier twisting and bending or the arm to get into the proper camera angles. But both did the job! If you have more than one arm, as in my case, you can even connect the two arms (Gopro & Sametop) together for additional length = 14 1/4 inches.
When considering the strength of the flexible arm, as to hold up weight. Maybe you want to use it for holding a camera rigged with small lights, or just a light, or external microphone???
I did some field tests. I clamped both units to a metal legged, garage shelf, with the flexible arms extending out sideways (at 90 degrees from the shelf). I then hung lead shot, scuba diving weights to measure how much the arm would hold up. The shorter model, GoPro held up 3 pounds. The longer model, Sametop held up 2 pounds. When both arms were combined, they only held up 1 pound of weight. So, the shorter the better, at that angle! I think if you used it with light weight units - a small LED Light, or External Shotgun Microphone, you would be okay.
Results of the Sametop - Pro's: High quality material, More affordable price (HELLO), Easily adds to with other attachments & arms, Strong tension spring, Longer 8 1/8" arm, 360 degree rotation & swivel, Medium strength of lift, almost unlimited possibilities to securely mount your camera. Con's - Nylon insert in the mouth of the Jaw clamp vs. rubber insert.
All in all, the SAMETOP Jaws Flexible clamp is a well made, universal product. I have used it numerous times for quick set ups, and take downs, without having to use a bulky tripod, adhesive style mounts or bolt-on mounts. Connect it to just about anything solid. I'm glad I bought it, and highly recommend it.

title: A great TV!
text:
I bought this Samsung UN65KS8000 to replace my dying circa 2009 Sony Bravia 52 inch 1080p. After some shipping delay, it arrived double boxed and safe and sound. Unpacking and setup were straightforward with good instructions. I did it all myself, but you would probably want an extra person to help with the lifting. Note that the feet can be mounted in another set of holes closer to the center. Once set up, it is absolutely stable.

I love the picture! Lighting is very even, the black levels are deeper and more uniform than my old Sony. The resolution, of course, is magnificent. Even upscaled streaming video appears sharper than before. Expect to spend a lot of time adjusting the video controls (brightness, contrast, backlight, gamma, and, to a lesser extent, color and sharpness) to find what works best for you. I ended up turning dynamic contrast off and smart LED off. Just my preference.

I haven't noticed any judder, a big improvement over my old Sony that used to hiccup regularly while streaming Netflix content.

There is some 4k content available from YouTube. No movies, of course, mostly short art pieces designed to show off 4k. These all look absolutely stunning, and the whole impression is much better than I expected! For those who are wondering, I sit about 8 feet away, and I can easily see the difference between 1080 and 4k, as have all of my friends who have seen it. I found the few Netflix 4k offerings to be disappointing because of heavy dynamic compression. The YouTube videos appear much more natural.

I really like the user interface. The remote has a minimal set of controls instead of a billion buttons, and once I got used to it I really like it. The TV interface is logical and easy to use. I mostly stream, do not have cable or satellite, and pull some content from broadcasters over the air. I was surprised to find that, once the TV searched and located stations, that it will construct a real time menu that allows you to search for TV content if you want. Very nice.

All in all, a very good TV for the money (I paid $2k through Amazon). Things have come a long way since 2009!

title: Great projector... for the price.
text:
[[VIDEOID:8368aefcae316138dcd3dc1bb44e4205]] All I can say is if you need a cheap projector to get your home theater started or for presentations, this thing will do the job. I attached some images to show the image quality is quite good. The video clip from Lego Batman, you can see it has some great color, and the still from an episode of Pokémon shows nice contrast.

I have a fairly ideal environment, a good roll down screen and a basement that can go near blackout in the daytime. That said, in low light the image is still quite visible. - Price: 1080p native for $240 isn't bad.
- Image Quality: See attached image/video, captured with iPhone.
- Ease of use: pretty much set how you like, and leave it alone.

CONS
- Product quality: there are some dust specs inside lens. CiBest requires you to send projector in to their warehouse to be looked at in order to fix, I just would rather not go without my theater at this time. It does have some warranty so perhaps when I can part from it for a couple weeks I'll reach out again.
- Minimal features: all your zoom, keystone, and focus features are manual. (There is no zoom, move it back for bigger, close for smaller).

I threw some shade on these in my initial review (3 stars) because of the almost non-existent bass they generated after installation even with plenty of boost from my head unit's equalizer. I'll still be adding a subwoofer, but it's no longer the urgent need it once was.

Installation note: I installed these in a 1993 Subaru Impreza (IKR?). Both front and rear installation required adapters due to the design and heft of the baskets used in the manufacture of these. title: I'm disappointed with this device
text:
Overall, I'm disappointed with this device. In my experience, the claims regarding it being inaccurate have proven true. Now that I've purchased it, and used it for 2 flights, its' inaccuracy leads me to think that it's unnecessary.

Testing it at home upon its' delivery, the device reported that it was located nearly a mile away from it's actual location. If one's luggage is lost in transit, that may provide some comfort, but I found it to be too little for my liking, especially since I was in a city which I had never been to before. (If my luggage had been stolen, I'd have no idea what the surrounding neighborhood was like, and could incur cab fare costs and a considerable amount of wasted time while trying to retrieve it on what might be a wild goose chase).

Even the documentation warns that the device works best while it's stationary. Upon thinking about it, once luggage is checked-in and handed-over at check-in, between conveyors, carting to the plane, being loaded on the plane, then being unloaded upon arrival, and on the conveyor again to baggage claim, (where it might be in constant motion for a long time going round and round on the carousal there), how much of that time is it stationary? If the unit provides accuracy only to within a mile or so, how much does that really help in retrieving your luggage? It seems to me, at best, that the device basically tells you that your luggage is "here", i.e. within Bluetooth range of where you are, or it's not, and if it's not, where is one most likely to go? Probably to the lost baggage counter. And with the device in your luggage, what would you be able to tell them that you wouldn't otherwise tell them? That it's not "here, but somewhere else that might be a mile or so away from it's actual location? I don't understand how that might help locate your luggage. Because of its' inaccuracy, it seems to me the device provides a false sense of comfort.

I realize the device does not use GPS, but the lack of accuracy inherent there seems to render the device to be of little use. I'll likely continue to use it on future trips (because I've paid for it), but I have little faith that it will provide any real benefit.

At this point, based on my experience with it, I can't bring myself to recommend it.

Apparently I am the only person on planet earth who actually PAID full price for these headphones. Everyone else is getting them for free. I'm very big on headphones so I will be very honest. Everyone is talking about how great these headphones are and how they are just like beats! How could I pass it up??? Well, here is the truth...

The headphones seem to be very sturdy. They do have a lot of padding, but still get uncomfortable after an hour or so. They do get pretty loud...but let's be honest everybody...there is hardly any bass! There is a lot of distortion. Stop comparing these to Beats or other high-end headphones. It's offensive! title: Great deal! I've been looking for an inexpensive fish ...
text: Great deal!  I've been looking for an inexpensive fish eye lens for a while and finally decided to pull the trigger.  I'm glad I did, this lens is so much fun to use and it yields great results!  The manual aperture takes a second to get used to.  The manual focusing is impossible, I can't tell the difference through the viewfinder or in live mode.  But you can pretty much set the focus to infinity and put your camera on aperture priority and shoot away.  ISO and shutter speed automatically adjust based on how much light is being let through the lens at the time.  I typically take a couple of extra shots using different aperture settings just to be safe.  The lens itself is heavier than expected and it seems fairly solid.  The only cons is the overall design.  The lens hood is flimsy and spins too easy (doesn't lock into place).  When attaching or removing the lens from the body, there's no real spot to twist without adjusting focus, aperture or the lens hood.  Other than that, I'm extremely pleased with the results and effects I get from this lens.  At this price, you can't go wrong!

title: Overall, I'm impressed
text:
I recently reviewed and compared the D5D and D7D product on my YouTube channel so I thought I'd mention the pros and cons I found with it here. The D5D mount works with 2, up to 11 pound monitors. I had no problem tightening the mount to adjust it pretty much anywhere I wanted it to go.

For $100 the D5D does what it's supposed to do. Hold your monitor in place and allow you to adjust it in pretty much anyway you'd want it to. There's also a cable management system that allows you to tuck your cords away.

The D5D did have a bit more plastic than I thought it would. In addition, Loctek put plastic on the arms that gets stuck between the joints. I ended up prying it open to get it loose.

vs D7D

Both the D5D and D7D are advertised as having aircraft grade aluminum. Still, I found the D7D to be more substantial in pretty much every way. This is shown in the tech specs with the D7D holding nearly 20 pounds per monitor or 40 pounds total. I didn't fully test the 20 pounds per monitor capacity; however, the 2 24 inch monitors I hung were easily kept in place with the tension once I had them adjusted.

The D7D also has a headphone, mic, and USB pass-through in the front. I'm not sure how many will truly use the pass-through but it is a perk I didn't mind having. I also feel like the D7D just looks a bit more stunning. The arms feel like and look like they are made of medal. The silver has a sort of fleck shine look to it that I really like.

Like the D5D adjustments in the D7D can be made in pretty much every way imaginable. That being said I found it easier to get it exactly where I wanted it. It uses a ball point adjustment in the back that makes the whole process more slick when compared to the D5D's hinges. In addition, the range of height seems to be a few inches taller on the D7D. As I'm tall, 6'4", this was of some value to me.

Cable management is done through the back and covered by black plastic.

Overall, I'd say it's a good product and definitely one to consider if you need a dual mount option. The D5D for those who just need something to hold their monitors in place and the D7D who want something with a higher weight capacity that makes it a bit easier to adjust.

title: best I have ever seen and the rest of the ...
text:
picture quality is 5*. best I have ever seen and the rest of the reviews for this product speak for themselves. any yet... I do NOT recommend you buy this TV. Why? because of LG customer service....

at some point, these companies have to realize that their product is not the physical "thing" they sell. it's the whole packages including support and warranty.

This TV has been working great for about 11 months. warranty expiration is right around the corner and I get a dead pixel surprise... a horizontal line across the screen (about 4/5th) of dead pixels. They died mid netflix binge so defiantly not a fault of physical damage. my TV is in pristine condition.

Ok ** happens, sometimes you get a bad panel, still a 4.75* experience....

Email 1 to LG -- nice website. lots of clicks to get to where I need. np. after the email is sent I get a "receipt number" but no email confirmation that the message was sent. Keep this receipt number in mind it comes back later.

Call #1 with LG -- representative wasn't very helpful at all. she couldn't find my email based on the address, phone number or the "receipt number" . she suggested I unplug the TV a couple of times while it's on.... She asked the same questions 2-3 times. based on my SN she found that the unit was sold in august 2016 which means it is still under warranty. Eventually she agreed someone should come out to service the unit but informed me no LG service techs are available. Instead she gave me the phone # for a local company that they trust. 3 days later I get a hold of the company and they tell me no LG case number exists so they can't send someone out.

Call #2 with LG -- I was told the last rep had marked my case as "out of warranty" which is why the local company couldn't find any records. I was asked several times to provide verification of the purchase and information they looked up before was not under suspicion and I had to prove via invoices.The rep explained that I need to be in front of the TV to run some app that helps them trouble shoot, until that was complete, she could not send anyone out to service the TV... Fine, I came home and called back.

Call #3 with LG -- I had to redo all the trouble shooting steps all over again. I was told to download a suspicious application on an android or ios device (apparently if you don't have a device with a camera, LG can't take in your warranty request). I download the app from some website because obviously apple doesn't want it in the app store. the download took about 10 minutes on my Gigabit internet connection... throughout, the rep annoyingly asked me over and over to let her know when it's done downloading.... finally I open the app and surprise! It's blocked on my ipad and I am told I need to find my own instructions for unblocking the app but that I should trust that the app will not do harm. 5 minutes later and the app is open. At this point the rep asks for a few minutes to open the app on her side.... (WHAT WAS SHE DOING WHILE WE WERE WAITING). after about 5 minutes she gives up and says "it seems like someone else is using the app so I can't use it" --- does LG only have 1 license for this shady video chat app that they force you to download????? The rep asks me to email her photos of the TV. I tell her I have already emailed the photos. She says she needs a reference number NOT a receipt number to locate the email. WHY does the website give me a receipt number if I need a reference number???

At this point, I have had it. I asked for a manager. I was told a manager would gladly speak to me in 30-60 minutes :) .... I asked for "oh god, can anyone else just schedule a service for me". I am then put on hold for another 15 minutes with no check-in at which point I hang up and dial again.

Call #4 with LG -- I start out as calmly as I possibly can. I explain that I have spent hours on the phone trying to get someone to service this 11 month old TV set that cost over $4,000 when I purchased it. I told them I would happily pay for the service myself if the technician determines the issue is not LG's fault. I just want someone to come look at this in person. I get no words of sympathy, I am asked for more verification of the purchase date and my name and address. I was then put on hold for about 5 minutes. The rep comes back saying there are no technicians available for the next 5 business days and her scheduling system only lets them schedule 5 days into the future.... WHAT??? come on... REALLLY???? ok so I start laughing and ask for a reference number that the local company can use to bill LG. The rep tells me she called the local company, they are also booked out 5 days into the future and when this happens they cannot create a reference number for me. I was told to sit tight for 3-5 business days at which point LG will hopefully call me to schedule a service.

I am now crossing my fingers and waiting for LG to call me to schedule service. Who knows if the call will ever come... warranty is expiring in a month and I will bet this broken TV that they will lose track of my claim for the next month at which time it's no longer their responsibility. IF only I had a reference number that they can lookup in their system to see the records of my calls....

Update as of July 28th
Call # 5 with George Electronix-- 5 days after call #4, a random man with a strong Russian accent calls my phone saying he wants to come to my house and pickup the TV. After many questions, I find out he is somehow related to LG and got my contact information from them. He attempts to schedule a visit at 11PM on Thursday night. WHAT! ... I explained that I will be sleep at 11pm so that does not work for me. He then tries to schedule a visit at 11PM on Friday night... at this point, I am so suspicious that I want daylight, plenty of people around and enough light for security cameras to keep everyone honest. Finally we schedule a pickup (not an inspection) for Sunday morning.

The older gentleman arrives in a dirty white van, with no identification and no tools. He comes up and immediately decides the TV is un-fixable and he has to take it to the shop. While I insist on showing him the problem, he experienced the TV randomly turning off for no reason. He laughs but confirms that there is no physical damage anywhere on the TV and this type of issue is not really related to physical damage anyways. He then single handedly picks up the giant 65 inch TV and tilts the entire thing to rest on his body. At this point, there is so much pressure on the screen that I am worried about his safety in case the panel breaks as he is holding it. He is not worried and boasts of his strength while the Screen is visibly bending. he finally gets the TV in his truck and tries to leave without giving me any receipt or calling card. just walks out with $4000... I insist on at least a business card and a copy of his work order. He gives me the work order and his business card and leaves.

4 days go by --- I hear nothing....

Call # 6 with LG -- I asked for a status or at least confirmation that LG is aware that my TV was picked up by one of their people. They confirm and assure me that the repairs will be covered under warranty but at this time, they are unable to confirm what the repairs are and when the TV will be back in my possession.

about 7 days go by --- I hear nothing....

Call #7 with "unknown number" -- "hello we have to schedule a delivery with you" ... uhh what? "is your name ..." You get the picture. after 10 minutes of verification, we schedule the unknown but large package to be delivered to my house sometimes between 1-4 on July 28th.

Yay -- looks like I will finally have my TV back.

Call #8 with FedEx freight. -- The delivery man confirmed that he is outside my building and cannot bring the package up. They are not responsible for un-boxing or ensuring the item is in good condition. My wife received the package and smooth talked the guy into bringing it to the elevator so she can take it up.

at this point, it sure looks like I have my TV back so I run home and eagerly open the box. Is it a surprise that all I get is a Giant OLED panel? no TV, no remote no nothing... this part was shipped to me instead of the repair shop. I won't rant about this particular mistake.

Call #9 with LG -- I explain everything again to the patient, rep since she spoke English well and seemed helpful. She did try to verify that the TV is under warranty which is where I almost lost it. I went into hysterical giggles which prompted a "what's so funny sir" question. I re-explained everything again... She asked for time to review the case. 5 minutes later she was very concerned because there was absolutely no record of anyone picking up and doing repairs on my TV. there wasn't even a record of this giant OLED panel being shipped to my apartment. She was totally out of ideas and had no idea how to proceed. I offered George's phone number to her and she spend 10 minutes calling and talking to George. She confirmed the mistakes and said George will be in contact with me to schedule a pick-up. I asked whether these contractors had any SLAs around how long they take to repair TVs and she said they do not. title: Good daylight use system, Furrion bracket needs to be MUCH better
text:
This is an updated review. I have been in contact with a 4UCam customer service rep who addressed my previous comments to my satisfaction.
Pros: (1) Never lost the wireless signal. I only have a 20' trailer behind a midsize SUV, but I never lost signal at any speed. (2) Worked very well as a backup camera, and as an observation camera during most of my 11 hour drive. (3) Simple to use, nice size display. Wired the camera to my running lights with no problem. The manual that came with it was actually pretty good regarding how to install the camera on an existing Furrion mount.
Cons: (1) The Furrion mounting bracket needs another 1/4-1/2" offset (space between the bracket and the RV) to be useful, otherwise you risk breaking the antenna off. I couldn't rotate the camera where I wanted it. For $2 I replaced the M4 bolts with longer ones and put in some washers and that took care of the problem. (2) This could be a problem with every camera, but the night vision while driving was not that good. All you see are blooms of light and you don't know what's behind you. (3) Advertised as having as sun-block feature on 4UCam's website. I expected this on this camera purchased on Amazon's website, but this capability is not advertised on Amazon's site, so...if it's on this camera, it doesn't work. Driving with the sun low behind you washes out everything.

Two words of caution (unrelated to the camera itself). (1) The top two screws on the existing Furrion mount were covered in RV sealant. If you don't remove all of the sealant you risk stripping the top screws because you'll just be turning them in place; they won't back out if there's sealant keeping them from doing so. (2) When you put the bracket onto the existing Furrion gasket and screw it back in to the RV, the gasket may not sit flat against the RV. You may need some sealant along the top of the gasket in addition to putting sealant in the wiring hole.

text:
Many times individuals believe to be expensive something is of good quality. Other times people will say 'you get what you pay for.' My review isn't about cost so much as it is reasonable expectations. This is a simple case… it mostly works as a screen cover and to prevent scratches and possibly to prevent single hand slippage.

The case as pictured (like many) allows the iPad mini to 'stand' like a book stand. So far I have not been overly impressed, but with intentional effort the stand has mostly worked (sometimes it slips and the iPad falls to the surface it is sitting on (about 5 inches).

This case is NOT a case designed NOR advertised for rugged protective care.

The case does not come with a glass or plastic screen cover (so the case is extremely unlikely to protect the iPad from a waist high drop.)

The case is (in my opinion) plastic material… and the case itself is likely to crack if the iPad is dropped (and the iPad is likely to be damaged).

AGAIN, as a simple case it meets my needs. You should not be expecting this case will allow you to be carefree in handling your iPad.

I anticipate with daily use that this case (cover) will wear out in a year (that would be in my estimate a reasonable life span for what I see and have experienced).

IF YOU ARE LOOKING for PEACE of MIND this is not the case you want.

title: Fantastic Upscaling Cable for 4K
text: I bought a 4K TV, only to be disappointed by the veritable lack of anything in UHD/4K resolution material out there. I bought this cable the day after I bought my 4K tv (by the same company, but the cable works with any 4K tv), and the difference is like night and day. At 4K resolution, anything of low resolution was obvious, like watching an old reel movie on a an HD tv. But with the cable everything is bumped up in resolution, and anything in HD is bumped up to 4K. The upscaled 4k is not as good as native 4K, but it is SOO much better than HD or anything less. The details you can see are ridiculous, and just about any movie is so much more immersive. The biggest differences I can see are things like reflections, textures, and somehow depth appears more true to intent. I watched Frozen with the kids and it was like watching a different movie, as I could even see things like individual reflections in each facet of the ice, and individual freckles. I also tried and old classic with my wife (the Fifth Element in HDX, Bruce Willis is awesome) and you can even tell by looking in the background they are on a set, and some of the walls are manufactured, like foam that has been painted. Bottom line, I wouldn't look at anything in lower quality again. That said, I have noticed that the PS3 and Xbox One still haven't put out those 4K updates they are supposed to for the consoles, though supposedly they have the hardware for it. So again, the cable is nice for giving a boost to anything the console does in HD format.

title: READ MY REVIEW if you are hesitant on buying
text:
Was hesitant to use this but I bought a platinum warranty on my camera so I was covered either way should it flood.

I took this scuba diving in the florida keys with my Nikon d3300 camera with a 18-55 lens. First off the pouch fit very well and wasn't difficult at all to set it up. the controls are all pretty easy to reach with the finger holes.

The manual says this goes to about 30 feet and that's exactly how deep I took it. What you'll notice the deeper you go the less and less air you'll have in the case and it will start suctioning to your camera making it skin tight. If you went much farther than 30 feet I would be afraid of damage to your camera with how tight the casing gets. Make sure to trap as much air in the bag before going down so you have more leeway.

The pictures came out great. Unfortunately I had my camera on the wrong settings underwater so the white balance is way off making everything blue and not that colorful but I left two pictures to show you guys that the pictures are still very clear and not ruined by the lens. One in water and one on land.

If you are planning on going deeper than 30 ft or really like to mess with the setting a lot I would recommend getting one of those pricey fixed casings as when the case suctions to the camera it restricts movement.

If you're hesitant go ahead a shoot me any questions. I'm very satisfied with this and the extremely cheap price compared to most waterproof cases.

*****last note for scuba divers the air in the camera bag will offset some of your weight so you may need extra weights to allow you to actually sink when using this. I had to add another five pounds I think.
