title: Some good, some not so good things...
text:
I received these yesterday after much investigation. Wireless has always fallen short fidelity wise for me and I thought these would be the units to overcome that barrier. I use over-ear open-back wired headphones exclusively. Fortunately I live in a rural area where it doesn't matter if sound leaks out. But, I thought, it would be nice to own one pair of closed backs for travel (airports/planes/trains). The reviews here are glowing, and maybe Sony has achieved something special w/ these MDR-1ABT.
Nicely packaged, you get a tough nylon carry pouch, which looks up to the wear & tear of everyday use. The accessory cord to plug in the phones directly is quite lightweight however and seems really meant for part-time use. Now, to the headphones.
These are plastic headphones made to look like stainless steel or aluminum. While the plastic does make for a light, comfortable fit that you really could wear all day, they seemed very fragile to my touch and probably easily cracked given enough time and use. The photos make this look like a much higher quality, sturdier headphone than this actually is.
Next, the sound was not terrible, but is does seem "Hollow" without outside amplification. Since these are meant to be portable, and used wirelessly, you will be much happier w/ a portable amp helping to fill out the mids and bass, giving you a much more rounded, deeper enjoyable presentation.
For me, these still fall short for my musical taste. But, the BT was simple and the phones are very comfortable. For those who worry about sound leakage, they do let out some sound at high volumes, but are pretty quiet at normal levels. They are not noise canceling, but do some passive canceling, not enough for loud situations like planes, DJ use etc.

title: We love the brilliant picture on this easy to use but incredibly full-featured projector!
text:
I really, really like this little projector. It was super easy to set up: I turned it on, walked through a couple of steps as the projected display instructed me to register the “Magic Remote” with the projector, connected my satellite box via HDMI and – Boom -- I had TV on the wall, just that easy. Oh, and the integrated speaker, while certainly not providing surround sound, does a fine job. The picture is amazing – crisp, appreciably HD. I don’t find a refresh rate for the LG Minibeam Pro, but I will say that we definitely do not notice the motion blur on this projector that we do notice on another projector that has a 60 Hz refresh rate, even when the projected image is at maximum size.

I’d seen discussions of this projector being used to replace people’s TVs and thought “they must not ever turn on the room lights!” because, initially, the image seemed too dark to see in a lit room. However, I soon found menu settings that easily allowed me to adjust the projector settings to overcome room lighting. While you can do that via individual sliders for brightness and contrast, etc., I found that it was much easier to switch between the Sport, Cinema, Game and “normal” AV modes to easily accommodate ambient light.

It took me a minute to find the Main Menu amid the other tiles on the desktop that appears when you select the “home” (it looks like a house!) button on the Magic Remote. Other selection options include graphic representations of sources, including Smart Sharing, which allowed me to effortlessly display vacation pictures on the laptop and other media that was stored devices on my network; LG SmartWorld apps, pre-configured with Netflix and YouTube; wired HDMI or MHL display connections to mirror laptop or cell phone; a USB connection to external media (hard drive, memory stick); coax from the over-the-air antenna; or the satellite box or Fire Stick on the two (hallelujah, two!) HDMI inputs. If we had Apple TV or the Windows Wireless Display adapter, I expect we could wirelessly project from the iPad or the Surface 3 tablet, too. There is a “Wifi Direct” setting that lets you easily connect to the projector directly to the wifi of another device. That, of course, removes both devices from the general network but that might be really desirable in some situations, and, of course, works when there IS no general network! Note that the only cables that come with the projector are Composite; I think LG assumes you’ll have the others.

While the projector is simple to set up, be sure to take the time to explore the other menu settings. The user interface is extremely easy and there are some terrific features tucked away. Need to do rear projection or hang the projector upside down? No problem! Want to quickly have the projector square up the display? The Auto Keystone will do it, or use the Corner Adjust to fine tune it.

Focus is done manually by turning the ring around the lens, as you would with a DSLR. The “zoom” lever on top of the unit only provides a 1.1x zoom to allow you to adjust the size of the display a little bit. If you need to make the display much smaller, however, you should move the projector closer to the screen – down to 3 feet for a projection size of 30 inches --- and move it further away, up to 12 feet, for the maximum 120 inches.

Connecting the projector to wifi was a breeze, especially because of the “Magic Remote.” What makes it ‘magic’ is that you can use it like a cordless mouse, especially handy when you’re faced with text entry of some sort. Instead of the oh-so-painful cursor-over-and-down motion you get from most Smart TVs, the Magic Remote lets you highlight and click on the displayed keyboard. The only thing that would be better is a Bluetooth keyboard…

Or, of course, voice recognition and the Magic Remote has that! Press the little microphone-shaped button on the remote, speak into it and the projector will do its best to follow your command. I mostly used this when in the internet browser and thought it did a great job. My only problem was that it times out and starts searching much more quickly than does my Android phone. The little Avatar that shows up to “tell you” what the projector is “hearing” is slightly annoying, but you can turn it off.

Speaking of Bluetooth, I did have a bit of difficulty getting the projector to see Bluetooth devices at first. When it happened with a Bluetooth speaker, I experimented with turning on the “find me” beacon on a few other Bluetooth devices, and, while my phone could see them all, even the ones with which it hadn’t been previously paired, the projector had a hard time of it. However, I was able to pair both the Bluetooth speakers and headphones (one at a time, of course!) with the projector eventually, and, once they had been paired, the projector was quick to find them again. The projector fan is audible, especially once the projector has been on steadily for a while, but it is certainly not so loud that it is distracting and even the built-in speaker easily overcomes the fan noise.

There are so many more features and functions on this projector… don’t make the mistake I did and assume that because the first few pages of the printed manual are the same as those of the CD-included-manual that they are the same; the digital file is MUCH more extensive and really does answer all your questions. It appears that you can also find this manual online if you have any in-depth questions before you make your purchase.

I think the worst thing that could happen to this great little projector is for people to buy it for the wrong reasons, so I’m going to include a few cautions:
• Portability. I've included pictures comparing the unit to a standard facial tissue box. However, it's a bit heavier. The projector weighs 3.5 pounds. The power adapter weighs just over a pound. Together, these are about the weight of an average red brick in the US. YES, it is definitely MUCH easier to carry than are the other projectors that produce a similar quality image, but, no, *I* wouldn’t want to have to deal with it in carry-on luggage on a day-in and day-out basis. But then, I'm the kind of person who wants to throw away her clothes so she doesn't have to haul them back home at the end of a trip, so your mileage may vary.
• I’m not a big fan of “smart TVs,” and this one is no different; it seems to me that it’s a lot easier to connect a computer or tablet and let that device do the heavy lifting rather than smush that functionality into a TV. I don’t use Netflix but do use Hulu and Amazon Prime Video. Those apps are available in the LG SmartWorld “store” for free, but are “not available for this device.” The projector’s built-in browser is quite nice, but when I browsed to Amazon Prime video and played a video, I never got a picture. To watch Amazon Prime video on the projector, I needed the Fire Stick or, as I said, an attached computer of some sort. I rather expect you would get the same result with Roku or Chromecast, etc., but you get my point. The built-in interface for YouTube worked very nicely, however.
• “I can use this instead of a TV.” Yes, you can. However, please take your room lighting into account. I’ve put the projector in the Rec Room, where we had always meant to put a flat screen TV and just hadn’t gotten around to it. This is also my “projects” room, but sometimes I like to have TV on to “keep me company.” When I have the overhead lights on and blinds open, even if I turn the projector to its brightest, the darkness of, for example, Game of Thrones can make images challenging to make out. With only ambient task lighting in the room, there’s no problem whatsoever. In fact, there is no screen glare, unlike the flatscreen TV, so it’s even better. Just keep lighting – and any traffic that might pass between the screen and the projector, in mind.
• The unit can be mounted on a tripod, having a standard camera mount, although LG suggests adding a locking bolt. I would be very wary of doing this. I have a very good tripod, one I trust with my Nikon, and I felt that, even with the legs as wide as possible, the projector was top heavy and in imminent danger of pitching over with the least jostle. If you’re going to mount it this way for a traveling presentation, my advice would be to stay close and hold on to it!
• I should note that this projector doesn’t support 3D. I'm not a huge fan of 3D so this doesn’t matter much to me, but, since it does do almost everything else and since the version of the projector that is available in other countries DOES support 3D, that clarification is important.

title: Decent sound and comfort
text:
Sound: I think these need some breaking in, especially in the beginning. Right out the box, the sound was not that great. The highs were shrill and the mids seemed nonexistent. I tried both AUX and BT modes and listened to songs on both Spotify (premium) and iTunes. The sound did not change. I adjusted my EQ settings on iTunes and found that the Vortex's sound better on a flat EQ setting. After about 10-15 minutes of use, the sound noticeably improved regardless of my EQ setting. However, the sound quality still fluctuates on Spotify depending on the song I am listening to. Once broken in, these sound pretty good. Also, there is a slight hissing on BT when you stop a song, but I think the engine shuts off after a few seconds to conserve battery so the hissing goes away altogether after a short while.

Comfort: These are not that big. I wear a size 7 3/8 fitted New Era cap so my head size is fairly average, but I need to fully extend these to fit on my head. The cups themselves are nice--leather is supple and the padding feels pretty good but the memory foam density in these must be bare minimum because they feel like they are filled with regular polyurethane foam. I mostly feel some discomfort at the top of my head, but the lateral clamping force is not too bad--no worse than most cheaper around-the-ear headphones.

Build Quality: Doesn't feel premium but definitely does not feel cheap. Not sure if that helps anyone reading this...I suppose the metals used matte/satin finish on the plastic and the feels better than the Mpow 059 headphones.

AUX vs. BT: Not much noticeable difference. Used the AUX cable provided to make a call and the call sound quality was ok.

Overall, these are pretty good, especially for the price point and especially if you were able to get these on sale for $59.99. Not nearly as good as a pair of Audio-Technica ATH-M50x's in either sound or comfort, but these were pretty much half the price of the M50x's so again, pretty good for the price. Bluetooth connectivity is pretty strong and battery life does indeed seem to hold up. Comparing to the Mpow 059s, the Vortex's feel stronger and more premium and produce better instrument separation in the sound. I think I will keep these a little longer and see how I feel. For now, these are OK. 3.5 if I could.

title: It's so bad that if someone walks by my computer I cringe ...
text:
My previous board was an ASrock and I was less than impressed with it. Over the last couple of years it began to have all sorts of issues so I decided to buy this Asus board instead because I've had lots of other Asus products that have worked well for me, this one has been the exact opposite though. Since day one I've had issues with this board and have been trying to get to the bottom of the issue. At first I though it was my video card, then possibly power supply but after weeks and months of chasing down the problem I finally found the pattern and it was indeed this motherboard and the other reviews I've read here back that up. The one that I have will randomly shut down and will not reboot until I open up the case and wiggle the video card until the power LEDs light up again. It's so bad that if someone walks by my computer I cringe in fear it's going to shut it down. I've contacted Asus support and they wanted to do a RMA and have me send them the board for repair. I demanded a replacement even if it was a refurb because I didn't want to be without my computer for two weeks while they were "repairing" the board. The rep told me that they were out of stock so I said I'd wait for a few days and check back. After two weeks of waiting, they still didn't have the board in stock (according to the rep) and the problem was getting progressively worse, so I had no choice but to send the board in for "repair". After being without the board for two weeks and getting it back and reinstalled, it did the exact same thing withing the first 30 minutes after reinstalling it.

So, while I've had several good Asus products over the years, actually the last few I've purchased have let me down so I'm changing brands. I am very brand loyal but Asus has lost my bushiness after their poor support options and failure to repair/replace this board.

title: Not enough power.
text: I bought this product for my Surface Book 2 15". I was tired of swapping from a gaming desktop when I was home, to a Surface Pro 4 for all my other daily tasks, so I decided to sell both for a Surface Book 2. I got this dock to help keep that desktop feel when I'm home and gaming. It has all the essential ports for me. The gigabit ethernet port made me the happiest as I have gigabit internet and one simply can't use a cheap gigabit router and expect to get max speeds over WiFi. I have two monitors hooked into it. Both 23" monitors. One is 1080 and 60hz, the other is 1440 and 144hz. I'm not sure if it's the limits of the dock, the cable I'm using, or Windows, but I can only get 120hz. I didn't count this against the dock as I can't be sure it's the dock's fault. Where that fifth star fell off for me is the power. As I said, I use the dock when I'm home and mainly when I'm gaming. The dock is only 90w, but it has to reserve some of that power for the ports. The charger that comes with the Surface Book 2 is 102w? Needless to say, the battery drains at about 1% every 2 minutes. On the weekends, I could spend more than a few hours at a time gaming. Not with this dock. If it produced more power, I'd give it 5 stars.

title: Sophisticated headphones for discerning listeners.
text:
Love them. I use a simple AudioQuest DragonFly 2.0 USB DAC plugged into laptops and stream music via Spotify at 320 kbps. I listen to all genres of music but mostly Jazz/Blues/Swing, Pop, and House. For anything with live instruments, the RS2e are superb. Lively, fun, accurate. But music mastered with synthesized bass, the RS2e will lack.

The treble is very pronounced at first. But once you get your bearings straight and acclimated to the music, the highs just sound so right. No sign of sibilance. And as long as your audio source levels are not clipping, no shrillness in the treble. The highs extend beautifully crisp. The vocals are impressively robust. No sense of muffled and claustrophobic V curve. Sounds so intimate that I swear I'm getting serenaded every time. The bass is tight and accurate. Especially when using a DAC. And no, it doesn't lack bass... at all. Some recordings, I feel that there's just too much bass. But some electronic music will sound a little anticlimactic when the drop hits at 32Hz. It extends well and seems to roll from about 100Hz at about 6dB/octave. Very natural curve. No overly boomy and bloated bass here.

I would recommend this to anyone that wants crystal clear and faithful reproductions of recordings. These fancy, handmade, headphones allow me to do just that, listen to my music, uncoloured.

title: Put it back
text:
I posted a long, detailed explanation, before, of Why I enjoyed this and why I thought it was good for beginners - giving them my thoughts as a fresh ear as well, thinking it would help them decide.
I take it back.

If you're debating if you want this or want to spend a little (or a lot) more on something better, get the something better.
Yeah, it's good for beginners, sure, but so is formula in a bottle, really. You'll quickly grow out of it and realize this doesn't sound that great. And you'll think it's just your ears, you'll think the record print was bad. Because some records sound good. But that's because those records are just SO good that they still sound good when they sound bad.

You'll get The Carpenters: Singles 69-73 and Karen's voice will prove to you that this is not right. It's unlistenable. It's ruined. You'll count the rpm's and realize it's spinning at 36 instead of 33 which makes a Huge difference. Now it all makes sense.
And their website only provides a number to call, which I haven't bothered, it's been almost a year since I bought this and with just a number, I feel there's going to be trouble, maybe I'm wrong. (plus I hate making phonecalls so that's also stopped me)

Anyway, like me, you'll regret it quickly, realizing you don't want just Something to play your records, you want something to play them Well. I felt like this immediately.
And then months and months later, I finally looked into why it didn't sound that great.

Don't spend the 100. Keep looking. Unless you're really not going to listen to records on it too much, aim higher.

A tighter belt would fix the issue of the speed, but even still, I wanted something better pretty soon after trying this out.

title: At first I thought this was horrible, then using tech support; found it is awesome.
text:
I bought this only to discover that the antenna cable was too short for my application. Wtih some excellent help via Terk website; I was able to get a proper spec for the extension cable so that I could place this by my window. My extension came today and I just connected it back into my receiver. My goodness, placed well at a window this puppy rocks. My scratchy weak station that is our primary radio station now comes in crystal clear.

A word about that extension cable. My first inclination was to use a length of TV cable as that had the right connectors; and shoot that's a piece of shielded wire in there so what could possibly go wrong? Right? What went wrong was it took the marginal mid-room reception and killed it completely (which was why when I first connected it my first reaction was "what a piece of garbage!").

But there were too many good reviews and so I consulted Terk tech support ("ask engineer a question") and explained that I suspected the TV cable I used was totally wrong, and asked for the specification of cable I should be using. Of course, and not surprisingly, the correct cable was totally different cable from TV. I ordered on "seller of all things - Amazon"; received and of course, taking the time to consult experts gave me a sterling result.

I mention in this review because the dichotomy of experience from my first incorrect hook up using improper cable; to the experience I now have with proper "to spec" cable is profound.

title: Great cleaning, great screen protector for MacBook Pro 13"
text:
The package includes three microfiber cloths and a 1.5" x 1.5" square microfiber pad that has reusable adhesive on the back for attaching to a device. Typically this would be a pad, but I put it on the back of my iPhone 6 holster and it works great there.

The microfiber cloths work very well. You use one damp and another dry. The screen (MacBookPro Retina) was totally clean and dust-free. The company also reaches out when you purchase the cloths to make sure you use them correctly, which is a nice focus on customer service.

The best thing they do, however, is protect the MacBookPro Retina (13" late 2016 model) screen. The computer is so thin, that when the cover is closed, the keys -- flat as they are -- cause imprints on the screen. I was constantly cleaning the key imprints (oil from fingertips) off the screen. But these cloths fit perfectly over the keyboard/trackpad and now the screen remains clean when the cover is closed. The cloth is very thin, and the cover closes with it in place. Granted, the force of the magnetic attraction that keeps the cover closed is a bit reduced, but I'm not worried about the cover popping open.

If you're looking for good microfiber cleaning cloths, or you have a 13" MacBookPro and want to keep the screen from getting keyboard prints, these are for you.

title: I was worried because many forum posts and websites suggested I wouldn't see a major difference and that coolers were a waste of money
text:
When I was researching cooling options for my laptop, I was worried because many forum posts and websites suggested I wouldn't see a major difference and that coolers were a waste of money. I can happily report that I saw a significant drop in temperature with this product. It was also very easy to set up and I love the adjustable fan speed. The fan can get a little loud when it's at its highest setting, but I only put it at that setting when I'm playing games, so I've got headphones on and don't notice it anyway.

One note - mind your work space and the size of the product. It is a little large, which is good for effectiveness, but could be bad if your work space is too narrow. I would hardly call it a drawback because laptops are very portable and you can easily make room, but if you're reading these reviews looking for a recommendation, it might be something you need to consider for your situation.

All in all, I am extremely pleased with the KLIM Cool + Laptop cooler and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for an effective way to lower the temperature of their laptop.

This is a lightweight (relative to zoom lenses) lens that is great for getting those sort-of-wide, but not-too-wide shots. As many people have said, it is a great walkaround lens. It is suitable for group shots, street photography, and landscapes.

It is not really a portrait lens though because you can't get in tight enough faces without creating distortion of the nose. Also, background blur and bokeh are hard to get with a lens at this focal length, unless you get up close. Interestingly enough, I was surprised at the foreground blur between me and my subject (who was at a distance) that I was able to achieve with this lens. It creates an interesting look and effect.

I have also used it for light painting and long exposures at night because it is a 1.8 lens.

This lens is sharp and create beautiful images.

Cons:

No way to estimate battery level or fully charged state.

A frequent knock on this I have read is that it is subject to RFI-induced static noise. I found that occur as well, but ONLY when the battery had to be low. Plugging it into a charger cleared it and I never notice it when the unit is (apparently) well-charged. This makes the lack of any battery level a bit more important.

Update: After 14 months, this item died on me. There's a short in the switch so that it both drains the battery and only works in one orientation. Result is that it's useless. I don't believe it has suffered any serious abuse from dropping - I only use it at bedside for white noise volume while I (try) to sleep. Plus, the charge light never did work. Reduced to 1 star.

title: No bass feel and you pretty much can't hear anything below 60-80Hz (rough estimate)
text:
Pros:
The crispest sounding headphones I have ever heard in this price range. Actually, they are the crispest I've ever heard since I've never owned a pair of headphones that cost more than $100.

Cons:
Very tight fit on the head.
No bass feel and you pretty much can't hear anything below 60-80Hz (rough estimate). For example, in the song "Super FX" by "EPROM", the bassline is completely invisible except for the very highest frequencies, which these headphones put front and center and show off the jagged edges of the synth patch and filter used to create the sound. Possibly would be a good thing for mixing/producing, but in the end I think it's just unpleasant for listening since the song sounds perfectly fine on everything else I have (Sony MDR-V6 and NVX Perfect10)

title: Pretty Solid
text: I've had this sound bar/ system for almost a year now. Came from a pioneer amp with 4 bookshelf speakers that were really quite loud/ bass was solid. However, moving to a new house and mounting the tv above the fireplace I really didn't want wires running every which way. So, spent alot of time looking at soundbars Def Tech, Bose, Sonos, etc.  Nice systems, but very pricey. Came across this JBL 5.1 sound bar. The 3.1's at best buy had pretty good sound/ bass so I went for this one figuring its very similar. (wasn't available in stores) The sub of course is pretty large (a little smaller than my old box speakers) so it still takes up SOME realestate. But easy to hide behind a couch/ chair. The soundbar itself is easy to connect and again takes up very little realestate and really cleans up on the wires. As far as the sound quality for the size of the unit I'm quite happy. Not an audio buff, but the bass is great, the mids could be a bit louder, and the overall loudness is OK. Not nearly as loud as an amp could go. However, as mentioned this takes up very little space and only requires 1 wire to tv, and 1 wire to plug in for power. The wireless speakers are convenient as I can place them wherever in my living room. Seems they can go about 15' before they start cutting out. The sub/ wireless speakers can be adjusted for volume as you please. For daily use I just leave the wireless speakers connected and for movies when I want that surround sound I disconnect them. Typically 2-3 hours here and there, never had a problem with battery running out. Overall, it really isn't a bad system, of course depending on what you're looking for.

title: Unacceptable bass response in windows 10.
text:
I'm truly puzzled about my experience with these speakers; I've had nothing but problems with their performance on a Windows 10 environment.

I ordered a pair at the end of December 2015, and thought the sound for MP3s was fine, clear and punchy. But just anything else with a wider amount of low-end frequency-- games with bass or soft synths from a DAW, both at modest volume-- revealed an unacceptable amount of bass distortion, a "flapping" of the cones. EQ'ing (bass reduction) via the OS to remove the "flapping" killed any bass response. This has happened with the first set of speakers, the replacement I got from Amazon, and a 2ND replacement directly from Yamaha. It occurs via plugging into either my old Creative Audigy X-Fi Platinum card or the motherboard's onboard sound, and regardless of whether or not I flag the speakers as "Full-range" in Win10's Speaker Setup dialog. The only constant in this troubleshooting has been the model of speaker, and the sound's being routed through Windows 10.

I'm highly frustrated, as this experience is at odds with what almost every other review has stated. My one-star review is a rating of both my EXPERIENCE WITH THE PRODUCT, and the unhelpful dialog with Yamaha online chat staff to troubleshoot the problem.

text:
The arm and headrest mounting is very solid. The adapters to get to the GoPro mount all go together and to the GoPro fine but the combination leaves my Hero3 camera vibrating a lot. To be honest on my first try with this a fair amount of camera jitter was caused by attaching the mounts to an unoccupied seat headrest and the seat back was responsible for both shaking and transmitting vibrations to the mount. i moved the mount to the drivers seat headrest and that improved. However there was still a good deal of shaking going on, even on a smooth road and that seemed to come from the combination of adapters that support the camera.

I decided to reduce the number of adapters. I removed the GoPro-to-camera-mount adapter and the adjustable-ball-to-mounting-plate adapters. I then cut the 2 small T shaped channels from the arms mounting plate and sanded that now flat surface to create a good bonding surface. I applied to that surface one of the flat adhesive mounts that come with the GoPro camera package. The result is a very solid mount that shakes very little. The only drawback is that there is no way to pan the camera. Tilt is handled by the GoPro mount and side-side-level can be addressed by adjusting the headrest bar clamp heights. I found the pan adjustment was not needed because my headrest bars are tangent to the roll axis of the car and the camera points directly forward. Attached is a photo of my revised mounting scheme.

title: Easy to use - if you know the facts & tricks
text:
Simple to use, if you know these facts:
* requires a free, downloadable app from the app store called xDisk; the interface is simple and understandable
* the app only orients to portrait mode and will not display in ladscape mode
* the app can only read one card at a time- even if you insert a microSD and a SD card in at the same time
* it defaults to reading the micro-SD card first, then the SD card slot
* you cannot take out a card, leaving the reader plugged into the lightning port, and put another card in expecting it to read the second card; you have to unplug the reader, swap out cards and re-plug in the reader to the lightning port to make the software recognize the new card
* the construction of the reader is solid and not cheap or flimsy - it has an aluminum houseing, which is a nice upgrade from the standard plastic that is found on most units like this
* copying files from the external reader and card is easy – long-press the file or folder and choose actions from the standard list of options that your iphone or ipad gives you
* inserting the reader into the lightning port will auto-launch the xdisk app, which is nice.
* you may have to remove the protective cover on your iphone or ipad to allow the reader clear access to the lightning port
* inserting the USB connector into a laptop USB port works just like any other external thumbdrive – no issues here.
* the unit comes with protective end-caps that snugly fit on the USB plug and the lightning connector plug
Overall, the unit is easy to use and well-built. I would like to see it recognize a card swap without having to re-insert the entire reader every time - I bet this can be accomplished with a software upgrade. It serves it purpose for me and works without error.

title: They pretty much never leave my ears.
text:
SO solid. They're fantastic for working out. Once I started using them in the gym, they became my instant favorites. I like that the earpieces are shapeable and that there are quite a few options of earbud tips included. Connection is quick and easy. The range seems to be pretty dang good. I once walked about 20 yards away from my phone before hearing the signal breaking and realizing that I had left my phone in a completely different section of the gym. The sound quality is actually really good and wholesome, and very bassey when it comes to workout music. I think Beats says they have a 12-hr battery life, and it's honestly about right. I'm pretty surprised that they were able to get 12 hours and good sound quality out of such a compact design.

I have really small ears, and I usually avoid in-ear headphones because I had never owned a pair that stayed in my ears. These came with a really small bud tip which is a little closer to the size i need, and when paired with the ear hooks, they stay in pretty nicely. The only annoying thing about the fit is that when I turn my head, the wire usually snags on my neck or my shirt, which pulls them out of my ear just a bit. It's really not a big deal, though, because any other headphones would usually just pop out of my ear entirely. For working out, these are just about perfect. It's honestly such a relief not having to worry about wires getting caught or getting yanked from the phone. After trying Beats Studio Wireless headphones, I pretty much only get wireless headphones now.

My last complaint is that I got the white ones (IMO the best looking ones (: ), but the loop in the middle dipped very briefly into tomato bisque and proceeded to stain forever. Even though the material is comfortable and sweat resistant, be careful and avoid staining them.

In short, I love these. I've had quite a few beats products over the years, and although they are good, the price was usually for the aesthetics of the products. Powerbeats, however, really do offer something that you'd be hard pressed to find elsewhere. I have not found any workout headphones that are better, and I'm gonna be keeping these until they die. Then I'll probably get another pair.

title: Perfect fix for my problem once glass protector plastic removed
text:
My wife's older i-Pad has a crack in the glass at the corner. I looked into having the glass replaced (I've done this before on this unit) but the cost to do so is more than this older device is worth. We figured we would end up getting her a new one soon, and passing this along to the kids, anyway. But if it was going to be the kids' i-Pad, the problem of the glass still remained, and another problem surfaced: we would certainly need a case for an i-Pad that was going to be primarily the children's. This great product solved both problems!
I ordered this case because it covers the corners and perimeter of the face of the i-Pad, and as such, covered up the cracked area completely. It also promises to protect the i-Pad, which we haven't really tested out yet, but it seems likely that it will perform in this area, too.
The only down side, which other reviewers have mentioned, was the plastic glass protector. I found it impossible to get it seated correctly without bubbles or tiny dust particles underneath. If you've ever applied a glass protector to a device like this, you know it's a bit of a delicate process, but the glass protector on this item is attached to the front frame of the protector making it very cumbersome. It's like trying to thread a needle with boxing gloves on. In the end, I - like many of the other reviewers - just ripped the plastic glass protector out of the frame and disposed of it. It created some work, though, trying to clean away the adhesive with goo-gone and then clean away the strong citrus smell of the goo-gone. I would have much rathered that either the glass protector came as a separate item, unattached to the case (then you'd have your choice if to use it or not, and if you chose to use it you would have an easier, hopefully more successful time applying it) or just omitted all together.
Still, even with the glass protector and the trouble of removing it, I would absolutely purchase this item again. For my situation, it was an extremely cost-effective solution that seems to be working great!

title: No Advanced Features/Customization, the Apple of Routers!
text:
Do not buy if you want (or use) any sort of advanced feature like setting your own DNS servers or you have a different DHCP server. This router will not allow you to setup anything other than a basic internal network. Its basically a waste of money for any advanced user. No open-source firmware is available.

Edit: More issues I wanted to mention:

I don't need DHCP, but I do need to set my own DNS servers and DHCP forwarders, no go on this router.

I have to reboot this router every three days due to connectivity issues, a problem new firmware hasn't fixed.

There are no advanced features available for setting up a router. Why not call this the Apple of routers?

I need to setup IPv6, but this router takes the entire network down every time I enable IPv6.

I used to buy Linksys because it was a Cisco product, but this is a great opportunity to try something else. I'm outside my window for returns, I've tried, Amazon is tired of hearing about this router. I heard they may stop listing it.

I don't want to be a beta tester for a router that was $200.

title: Billing Nightmare ... Alexa Issues, Notification Issues and Motion Issues
text:

Update 6: Having cancelled my subscription last year, I was surprised to find an email from Arlo in my Junk mail folder.

They could not explain how it happened and told me to monitor my credit card to see if it happens again. I decided instead of me monitoring my credit car every month, I would delete my card on file. ARLO DOES NOT ALLOW YOU TO DELETE A CREDIT CARD!!!

BUYER BEWARE ... Arlo provides no direct way to contact Billing (all my conversations were with Tech Support, and Tech Support putting me on hold, to talk to Billing), yet blames the Customer for them billing and knowingly not providing service and not responding to numerous emails and phone calls.

Customer Service is useless. They do zero trouble shooting. They just read to you the instructions; which I already had read and did not solve my problems. After not helping me, they then send me an email telling me how helpful they were?!?!

I had a half dozen problems, which they solved none. An example: the live and library videos did not work with my computer. Customer Service kept telling me to let it finish 'Buffering'. I told them I have FIOS 1G, it is not a buffering issue. I told them I am not getting a 'Buffering' warning, but a ''Please Wait' or 'Loading' error. They told me they would check with Systems and get back to me ... they never did.

I live on a busy road. At factory settings, notifications were being sent every minute, sometimes multiple per minute! I turned off noise alert. I will try the 30 day trail of zones & person detection ... but most likely returning it.

Update: I signed up for 30 day free trial and set zones; which works better, but still useless on windy days. I had a tree hit by lightning last night. The entire thing was within my zone (green area) .... a 60' falling rolling tree, and not one motion capture?!?! FYI, this is my back cam (not one facing road) and it is at factory settings.

Update 2: Case in point about Customer Service ... they Comment on my review, and do not address any of my complaints, but suggest how to save on battery life?

In December I asked them, when they fix the billing can they please convert me to the current offer of $79 for an annual contract. They said they would notify Billing ... when they finally fixed my billing, and finally turn on Premier, I asked them to read the notes on my account and give me the $79 deal, and they told me that deal had expired, and I was not qualified, because it was for new customers. text:
These are great looking speakers, and they certainly "look the part," but overall they were a big disappointment.

First of all, the specs listed on Amazon are incorrect. The frequency response of these speakers is not 33 Hz - 25,000 Hz. It's 45 Hz - 24,000 Hz. Not much of a difference at the high end, but a huge difference at the low end.

I purchased these speakers directly from Polk and I'll give them credit for offering free fast shipping AND having a lower purchase price than Amazon.

I contacted Polk via social media to ask how long the break-in period is. They told me 8 hours. I thought that seemed impossibly low, so I contacted them again via their web site and was told the break-in period is 50 hours.

I now have 80 hours of play time on these speakers. They sound slightly better than they did at zero hours, but the bass remains muddy, indistinct, and surprisingly less accurate and less tight than my old Sound Dynamics bookshelf speakers. (Sound Dynamics was a Canadian speaker maker which sadly is no longer in business.)

Aside from the disappointing bass, the overall sound is woody and boxy. Not what you'd expect from a $500 pair of speakers made by a very well-known speaker maker.

I also don't understand why the cherry color is so much more expensive than the black color. Both colors are vinyl wraps, not real wood, so why would cherry-colored vinyl cost $120 per pair more than black-colored vinyl?

I contacted Polk tech support regarding the poor sound quality, waited several days for a reply, and ultimately was told to send the speakers back for a refund, which I'm in the process of doing now. That process has proven to be lengthy and difficult. Polk's web site promises a full refund of the purchase price if speakers are returned within 45 days. Hopefully that will happen.

title: FOUR YEAR UPDATE: WONT' CHARGE ANYMORE! Battery charge declines over time.
text:
UPDATE: After four years, will not charge anymore. Battery doesn't hold a charge as long anymore either. Into the trash it goes.

I've had two of these speakers for a little over two years; one in the upstairs bathroom and one in in the kitchen. On an average day, I will have these on for about two hours or so. I have noticed over the last year, the battery life has been drastically reducing (degrading). When new, you can charge these up and not worry about them dying for a good couple weeks of sporadic use. Now, after a full charge, I am LUCKY if I get five hours out of it. The 20 hours of playtime they guarantee was correct two years ago, but now, it's easily five to six hours, tops!

Original Review:

Since March 2018, I've ordered (3) Bluetooth speakers and returned each for one reason or another. I didn't just buy these willy-nilly, mind you, I did a lot of research, including watching countless audio review videos from such experts as clavinetjunkie on YouTube (look him up, he's a genius!).

The first one I bought was the Tribit XSound Go ($40). It was OK, but just lacked "punch." I really debated returning it, but in the end, it just didn't sound as deep and heavy as I wanted.

Next up was the JBL Flip 4 ($79.95). I decided maybe I needed to drop a little more money to get the sound I wanted. So, I doubled up and paid twice what I paid for the XSound Go. This speaker was good, and was a slight upgrade -- it had more bass and filled up the room better. However, after less than two months, it started just cutting in and out and dropping its Bluetooth connection. So annoying! The 30-day Amazon return window had closed, so I had to sell it on eBay at a loss of $25. Bummer, and also the last JBL I'll ever buy.

Next, I decided to buy (2) speakers; one for upstairs and one for down. I went with the OontZ Angle 3 ULTRA ($41.99/ea.). At first, I was satisfied with these, but after a couple weeks, I noticed just how tinny and tiny they sounded. No bass whatsoever and just not the type of machine you want to hear good music out of.

So, I went back to clavinetjunkie's page and was surprised to see a new and very positive review of the Tribit XBoom ($69.99). This speaker had yet to drop, with only pre-orders available on Amazon. In fact, no one on the internet even had anything about it save for clavinetjunkie's video. I watched the video about three times and then waited and checked by the hour until the speaker finally went live on Amazon. I snatched that joker up the second I saw it was available and spent the next two days with an electric giddiness coursing through my body in anticipation.

REVIEW: So, I opened the Amazon box about 10 minutes ago, paired up my phone and put on some ZZ Top and Jason Mraz (don't judge). The verdict? This thing sounds amazing! Like, at every volume, low, high and in-between, it sounds crisp, deep and has that "punch" I was looking for. I think this is it -- I've found my forever speaker. I could not be happier. Well, except for one small thing...

Unlike every other Bluetooth device I have, this is the only one that doesn't show its battery life on my phone's Bluetooth notification panel (Google Pixel 2 XL with the latest version of Android). It's not a deal breaker, but I just don't understand how something brand new with Bluetooth 4.2 doesn't have this. It's really helpful to know when you have to charge something before leaving the house or just in general. Maybe Tribit will address this with a firmware update.

Anyway, I highly suggest this, and even though I've only had it for, like, 15 minutes now, I am very satisfied.

UPDATE: I had a couple issues with my speaker, but Tribit's Customer Service Department went above and beyond to assist me. Highly recommend this product!

title: Excellent Monitoring But Not True Security... Yet
text:
The Canary is a good product and does some things extremely well. That said, there are many features that need to be added to take it from glorified baby monitor to home security system.

Pros:
It looks good. The device, app, and packaging are extremely sleek.

Alerts work well. I had contractors coming over to my apartment and was able to always knows when they arrived, and if I wished, listen in and watch. The microphone /sound quality as well as picture quality are very good.

My building manager once dropped by unannounced when I was at work and I received a notification, then opened the app to watch live. Next, I gleefully sounded the alarm and watched him scurry out... Because of the motion sensor triggered recording, I also have the video.

Cons: 30 second delay on live steam.

No option for auto alarm (say if you're home sleeping.) This is a huge no brainier and needs to be added.

Limited ability to add / subtract Canary devices and locations from the app yourself (and subsequent need to contact Canary for them to do this on the back end.

Whenever it goes into night vision mode, it detects something and sends me a notification if I'm not home.

title: Buyer beware.
text: After reading a review about this watch, I ordered one.  One of the things I was looking for was a sleep analyzer, which according to the review, this watch supposedly had.  It didn't.  So, I went to Google Play and downloaded a popular sleep app.  I could never get it to load onto the watch.  I also found a couple of watch faces that I liked, so I downloaded those, as well.  They would not load either.  So I started investigating.  What I found out was that Ticwatch uses a proprietary, modified Android.  Because of that, only basic Android Wear 2.0 apps will run.  Those that require communication with your smartphone do not.  That means that you are stuck with Ticwatch apps, and in my case, they have no sleep analyzer app.  I did give it two stars instead of one because other than this major flaw affecting usefulness, I found it to be comfortable and not bulky on my wrist.  It is lightweight, as well.  Its a shame that it is not a true Android Wear 2.0 watch.  So, if the Ticwatch apps meet your needs and you aren't worried about future needs, this might be the watch for you.  But, this one is going back.

title: Using the 7Lucky Numeric Keypad (Model: BT301)
text: The 7 Lucky Numeric Keypad (Model: BT302) is a Bluetooth 3.0 device. To use the device for the first time, insert two AAA 1.5 volt batteries, and turn on the device using the on-off switch on the back of the device. Using Microsoft Windows 10, this device is paired in the usual manner after pressing and holding for three seconds the <Calculator-Bluetooth> key until the blue light blinks (this makes the device discoverable) and following the “Add Bluetooth or other device” procedure. After clicking on the the discovered device name “Bluetooth 3.0 Keyboard,” the device will be paired. Pairing allows the device to automatically connect to the computer when the device is turned on. When the blue light is illuminated, the device is in the active number entry mode. When the device is not used for 20 minutes, the blue light will turn off and the device will go into battery save mode. Press and hold any key to re-enter active mode again. The device can be turned off using the on-off switch when it is not being used. Using this keyboard device is straightforward. All of the large 28 flat keys provide the characters or the commands that are labeled on the keys (22 character keys [<Tab>,00$()=/*-+7894561230.] plus 6 action keys [ <Calculator-Bluetooth>, <NUM>, <ESC>, <DEL>, <BS>, <Enter>]). The permanence of the key labeling is not known. The usual Windows “Num lock” function is provided with the <NUM> key. When in number entry mode, the blue light will be illuminated. When the alternate keyboard mode is active, the blue light will be off, and the <Home>, <End>, <PgUp>, <PgDn>, and <4 cursor move actions> functions can be used. For convenience, the key in the upper left corner (the <Calculator-Bluetooth> key) runs the Windows Calculator app. The center <5> key has a tiny bump for finger location. All of the keys work smoothly without noise or errors. Owners of this keyboard should feel lucky to have such a well made device as this.

title: It's Just Another Pair of Expensive Headphones
text:
I've had the M-100 headphones for a couple weeks now and have tested them pretty thoroughly over that time. TBH, I really can't justify the huge hype with these at all. They're really seem like another pair of headphones among the many other generic and pricey headphones out there. I'll break it down into a few categories to fully the strengths and weaknesses of the M-100.

Sound
This is obviously the most important aspect to why anyone would buy headphones. Particularly an expensive pair such as the M-100 because we expect to hear superior sound quality. Headphones can have all the looks, comfort, colors and expensive brand names they want but at the end of the day, the sound is the defining quality of the product. Truth is, these are not the sound I'm looking for. Unless you're really into pop, dance, techno or hip-hop genres, these don't begin to touch presenting the quality of sound needed to properly get the most out of heavy rock or metal genres. Why you ask? Much of the sound quality of the hardcore metal and rock style of music that I largely listened to is drowned out by the excessive high frequencies and the over attention to the bass, leaving the mid-ranges recessed to sometimes significantly poor results. Percussion, particularly the snares and cymbals, along with much of the secondary rhythm electric guitars is shoved well behind in the soundstage and presents a lacking of continuity with the bass guitar, bass drum, lead guitar and vocals. Percussion for me is quite important, and much of the time, the quick, powerful pace of the crash symbol is just reduced to a small afterthought in the presentation. I'm definitely a person who wants the percussion in my face but the M-100 recess the mid-range too much to make certain instruments like percussion seem relatively important. This however, is not a problem for genres that lack much of the complexities of soundstage with multiple instruments being played simultaneously. They're very much a genre-specific headphone.

Comfort
Another important aspect that always one must consider. Here, the M-100 are simply ok. Nothing special. For starters, the headband could use more padded cushioning as I found it rode the top of my head fairly hard after an hour of them on. Regarding the cans, these don't apply too much pressure to my head, however, the cushions on the cans are a bit too small for my ears and end up sitting awkwardly on the tops and corners of my ears. Though not outrageously uncomfortable on my ears, I noticed the thumping bass would sometimes vibrate my ears on the edges enough to make an annoying tickling sensation. So, V-Moda offers an XL cushion you can buy separately that provide for more circumference on the ears. If you have big ears, this accessory is a must. I did buy the XL cushions and noticed better comfort. But have fun installing those XL cushions though, the stock ones are stuck in there tight. Makes me wonder why didn't V-Moda just make the XL pads standard on the M-100 to begin with? They're obliviously superior to the ones they come with and can't cost V-Moda that much more to install the XLs as the stock pads. Doesn't make sense.

Build Quality
So I've read and heard so many reviews about the M-100 being "built like a tank". Really???? Do people even know what that means? After 2 weeks, the swivel hinges on the cans are broke and are so loose they basically swivel 360 degrees by the force of gravity alone. To be fair, this was consequential to me installing the XL cushion pads, but as I mentioned before, they can be a pain to install. It honestly didn't take much force for those hinges to go kaput even by me having to man-handle the stock pads out of the cans. I fail to see the marvel of engineering of the "tank" quality build that people claim. Of course, these hinges are plastic inside so go figure they break easily. When the manufacturer cuts corners to build the product, you get junk like this installed whereas much of the other materials on the M-100 are nice. Either engineer and build it well all the way through or just don't build it at all. On the bright side, the portability of these headphones is excellent. By being able to fold the cans up against the headband, it's amazing how compact they become and comes with a sweet hard-shell carrying case you can tote around in you backpack/bag. These are the most travel-friendly headphones I've ever seen!

Verdict
Well, I simply can't justify price tag. However, sound and comfort with headphones is completely subjective, so you've just got to try em out for yourself before you really know what you've got. It seems to me that V-Moda is a company that's still trying to find it's niche with their products and the M-100 seems to be yet another stepping stone for them to design and build something better.

title: Disappointed, only buy it if you have an option of replacing it if something is wrong.
text:
I read a lot of horror stories about this monitor, but dismissed them as 2 years have passed since this monitor had all these problems with backlight bleed, and I figured they must be fixed by now. Also, I'm not too picky about a bit of backlight bleed or a bit of bad pixels.

I made a huge mistake and bought mine at a local shop infamous for their bad customer support.
Right when I attached it, I noticed something is off with the picture. The monitor was overly bright, colors were not great and a bit washed out and I just couldn't bear looking at it for too long.
I knew I just can't claim something is wrong, by just saying "colors are not great, the monitor is too bright and giving me migraines", so I had to find out the problem myself. I figured it had a bad native default gamma of approx. 2.0 instead of 2.2. The monitor doesn't have a gamma option in the OSD menu, so I had to find a way to correct it through the NVCPL, which isn't ideal.
Even there I couldn't get satisfying result, so I decided I shouldn't be swallowing this after paying that much money.
As I was familiar with the very bad customer service of the store I bought it from, I decided to skip it and went straight to Asus israel.
No-one in there really knew what I was talking about but they did took it to RMA inspection.
They sent a courier to take it to the lab they're working with. I had to wait a week and half for someone there to check it, while nagging to them every 2 days.
when the technician finally returned to me he said: "The monitor is not too bright, there's nothing wrong with it".
I asked him if he checked its gamma. I'm sure he didn't even know what it is, but he got really angry by me doubting his "professional verdict", so he said "I Haven't checked the gamma, I will, but I'm telling you right now, there's nothing wrong with it, good day" - and hung up the phone.
from this point, I had to again nag every 2 days, until finally after another week and a half, I was announced that "The lab confirmed there's nothing wrong with the monitor, so it won't be replaced."
They didn't even let me confront the unprofessional technician.

I was stuck with this bad gamma monitor and had no choice but to order a colorimeter to fix its colors.
I bought a spyder 5 express which costed me another 150$ (inc. shipping) and it indeed told me what I already knew:
1. the approx. gamma is 2.05.
2. the monitor reaches an insane brightness of 430cdm2 ! (it advertises as 350 max). It turns out that for a normal brightness of 120cdm2, it should be set on 13 brightness. amazing.
3. The monitor can't reach 1000:1 contrast ratio. I can only dream of the 1100/1200:1 I saw in many reviews. the best I saw from mine is 950:1, calibrated: 920:1 at best.

I'm now stuck for years to come with a monitor that made me spend 150$ on a colorimeter to get normal colors and:
1. left me with color banding.
2. going to cause me many headaches with games and color profiles.
3. Lower contrast than others in the same model.

This is the first and last monitor I buy from Asus.
If you must, only buy it from a shop with good service. Asus themselves treat customers that bought an 1000$+ product (here in israel) like they bought a 5$ product.

EDIT:
______

This monitor also has super bad uniformity confirmed with displaycal, so I can't even rely on the calibration I make with the colorimeter.
To sum it up: Nothing looks great on this monitor. I watch gameplay videos in youtube in my cheap xiaomi phone, and all I can do is envy how great the games look there compared to my garbage PG279Q.
I regret so much buying this monitor - the worst purchase I've ever made.

title: Legit. But it has its limitations.
text:
The KZ ED16 delivers on all its promises. It's a budget IEM that offers so much for what it's worth.

Bass is there, nice and strong, but so is almost everything else. If you like to hear your music with lots of detail and in a relatively pleasant manner - the ED16 delivers.

Compared to the ATE I tried before this, its audio quality and balance is way superior. I've had worse experiences paying double the price of the ED16, and nothing below that is really at the league of the ED16. So what am I saying? For the price, there is absolutely no other IEM you want to purchase. Seriously.

So where does it fall short? I think it lacks the integration necessary for music to be maximally impactful. Sometimes separation goes too far and the ED16 is somewhat like that. Secondly, there is a dip in the high mids as well as a spike just above it - it makes electric guitars recessed and vocals a little too forward. Because I'm a musician and do the FOH for live events, this can irk me. Of course one can get used to anything, especially for the price, but I actually find that the listening experience of the ED16 is inferior to say the Xiaomi Piston 3 which I sadly lost. Technically the PIston 3 is inferior, but the holistic musical experience it brought was so much more impactful for me. Others may have a different experience and that's probably fair because of the relatively narrow range of musical genre I listen to.

If you're interested in the ED16, I wouldn't hesitate to pull the trigger.

title: An enjoyable laptop
text:
Overall, I would recommend this laptop. I think the thing that holds me back from a full 5 stars is the SSD size and the quality of the laptop material, but it's not that big of a deal personally.

Pros:
-Lightweight... slightly redundant.
-Screen looks pretty good to my eye.
-Mouse pad seems fairly responsive and has tactile clicks.
-Two levels of back light for the keyboard.
-Good battery life.
-Runs cool and quiet.

Cons:
-The material feels slightly cheap, but not potato laptop cheap. It's probably the price for being lightweight. Still feels decent to me.
-Webcam position is bad, but doesn't matter personally. Quality is normal laptop quality.
-Speakers are subpar, but I suppose that's what you get with a thin and light laptop.

As a father's day gift for my dad, I was looking for high end laptops running Windows. Hardware wise, I was looking for 8GB ram minimum, highest storage of SSD possible near a $1000 budget, 6-8 hours of battery minimum, runs cool and quiet, and less than 5lbs. I'm not too crazy on resolution or touch screen since me nor my dad would make use of that or care about higher resolution when it already looks decent (and higher resolution will usually lower overall battery life). I got the non-touch screen i5 version with a 1080p screen.

This laptop is really only for typical applications like Microsoft Office, Chrome, Spotify, movie watching, etc. You could probably do some audio recording with this because it's basically inaudible and runs super cool. (Can't remember if it's passively cooled or not...) But for gaming, look for a different laptop with a dedicated GPU, and for video editing you'll probably want more onboard storage and maybe 16GB of ram. 512GB of storage would've been preferable for me, but with SSDs on laptops right now it's expensive. I was keeping an eye out for USB-C ports too since that will become a standard soon, if not already. Also, under the description it can be easily missed, but the laptop size is actually 14.1" across. The small bezels and rectangular build makes it this way, so the footprint is smaller than other 15.6" inch screen laptops.

I was considering the Dell XPS 13/15, Asus Zenbook 3, Surface Laptop, a few models of Lenovo, and others, but mostly the XPS 15 and Surface laptop. title: ~~RECOMMENDED~~ -- Certainly not the highest-quality product, but the price is low & quality better than other plugs I have used
text:
I was pleasantly surprised by these. Most makers of silicone plugs produce extremely low-quality products (and have a price that reflects this.) Like other makers, these CoolLife plugs are of marginal quality (and are probably made by one of a handful of gigantic makers and then rebranded for sale.) So why am I giving this 4-stars? Because the price is extremely reasonable, the black silicone holds up better than clear, and the fitment (while far from excellent) is substantially better than other products I have used.

USES & BENEFITS
I imagine that the functional benefit from silicone port plugs is probably pretty minimal and that these are giving me more peace of mind than they are functional protection. With that said, I prefer to use silicone plugs to avoid dust/debris accumulation in the ports from on-the-go usage, to keep my rabbit's hair out of the ports when she has her seasonal sheds, and to act as a 'bumper' to protect the unibody frame from scratches. This last part is somewhat useful to me since most hard shell cases do not cover the port area, and so it creates a rubber bumper between the MacBook Pro's frame and anything it may rub up against.

(((*NOTE*: It is worth noting that some Users have observed a relationship between silicone plugs and an increase of computer temperature. I have NOT personally observed this with my own usage on my own MacBooks.*)))
(((((**NOTE 2**: These plugs do NOT fit super tightly and, like virtually all silicone plugs, are somewhat prone to falling out while on-the-go. When on-the-go, you have to be somewhat vigilant so that you make sure they are not lost. When inside a sleeve, the friction created between the silicone and the inner padding of the sleeve can sometimes pull these out of the ports.**)))))

THESE COOLLIFE PLUGS: DESCRIPTION & FITMENT
The first two sets of plus I purchased from other Sellers were advertised as being compatible with the 2014 15-inch MacBook Pro Retina...and neither were as they were made for the generation prior to the retina models. This CoolLife set contained all of the plugs needed for the 15-inch Retina Pro, plus a few extras. Mine DID come with a plug that works with MagSafe2 and DID some with two Display Port/Thunderbold plugs. Presumably, if you are shipped the kit that I received, this WILL work with the 13-inch and 15-inch MacBook Pro Retina models, as well as the current MacBook Air. It will NOT work with the non-Retina MacBook Pro because it does not come with plugs for all of the legacy ports used on the MacBook Pro but not carried over to the MacBook Pro Retina (FireWire, Ethernet, MagSafe1, etc.)

WHAT I LIKE
I expected these to be so bad that they would probably wind up in the trash after a few weeks. Upon arrival, I was surprised to find the fit better than other plugs I have owned. The fitment is far from perfect, and a few ports are very loose, but it is still a big improvement over the last set I had where plugs would just randomly fall out. Unlike the clear silicone plugs, these black plugs will not turn yellow and get all funky looking with age.

CONCLUSION
When considering the extremely low price of 2 bucks SHIPPED, I think the quality is of acceptable standard. The functional usefulness of these plugs are almost certainly limited, and the quality of these are not going to win an award for manufacturing excellence. However, for my own needs they serve their purpose and if I were to lose them I would probably buy another set of this CoolLife brand. Therefore, I recommend this product.

title: Melted my projector lens
text:
I purchased this about a year ago as a backup for the original/factory lamp for our HD20. Just before Christmas, we did the switch, and it completely melted the plastic lens in the light tunnel (see picture), ruining our holiday movie plans. This is clearly not an OEM lamp/housing as many others have noted.

If your lens has melted, you can fix it by replacing the lens (there are even glass versions available on eBay) - there are guides on how to do this out on the web, and it took me about an hour. Alternately, Optoma sells a complete light engine (all new lenses and everything) if you're uncomfortable opening up the engine or if you've coated your other optics with melted plastic.

There are a couple theories about what's going on with these knock-off lamps and subsequent projector damage:

1) Some lamps have different bulbs with different IR characteristics and/or different IR blocking filters. The infrared light properties are important as this can lead to excessive heat build-up depending on the optical characteristics of your elements (like a plastic lens, cough, cough). If the manufacturer of this lamp is using different suppliers for the bulbs/filters, some will may OK, some may not. It's pretty much a lottery.

2) Some of the earlier versions of these projectors have a glass third lens (the thing getting melted), later versions have plastic. If yours is one with the glass, the lamp will work just fine and you'll be happy. If you've got the plastic, you're going to have trouble.

I'm not sure which of these are correct, but these knock-off lamps are a gamble regardless. We ended up re-using our original housing and just replacing the bulb (with the OEM: OSRAM P-VIP 230/0.8 E20.8).

All in all, adding up this lamp/housing, the new OEM bulb, and the price of the replacement glass lens, we really didn't save anything over a genuine Optoma lamp and had to spend the holiday without the projector. Of course your milage may vary.

title: I got them to be dumb 10gig backplanes for our virtual servers
text:
We have several of these for work. I got them to be dumb 10gig backplanes for our virtual servers.

Three things sum them up.
FAST,HOT,LOUD

The 4 star rating is for them overheating and locking up at slightly elevated server room temps, and the sensitive wire needs. They are side vent systems with the cold air incoming on one side and venting out the other. This is problematic in a server cage with front to back airflow. I had them stacked one ontop of the other and they kept having issues. I finally got creative and ducted air directly to the cold inlet and separated the switches by 2U and they are finally behaving but be aware if you are going to rely on them just treat them gently. They will work just fine especially if you use a redundant network configuration. The other issue I had was solved using proper CAT 6a cables rated for the speed, my rack only uses 6' cables but even in that length I had a number of issues with cards not linking at speed or suddenly having loss etc. Turned out the Cat 5e and Cat 6 cables we tired just didn't cut it. Turns out the (a) matters

Cisco wanted $500+ per port, these deliver 10gig at around 1/4 that price. I am using this with a PURE $100k+ SSD SAN and 3 x $35k+ virtual hosts running more than 400 machines. These are the core switches for that fabric, and have no issues pushing the data at 4+ GigaBYTES per second(aggregate). Even if I have to replace them annually they are still less expensive than the competition. We looked into using Cisco since we have a few 4500 series modular switches but the cost to put 10gig on them was just too expensive for the limited number of ports we needed. So for now a set of these uplink by the SFP port to the Cisco's. These are great and I keep spares on hand because they are so inexpensive. Infact one is doing duty as a 10gig base-T to SFP+ converter because it works and it's still less costly than the alternative.

I can't speak to any of the "features" since I use them exclusively as a layer 2 dumb switch.

title: Started out great, quickly declined from there!
text:
i purchased this unit back in October. From October to December, everything worked perfectly. The sound wasn't great, and it became distorted around higher volumes, but that was expected from an inexpensive radio, and has zero impact on my review. The radio worked as it should, as did the Aux In. I never tested the SD card slot as I don't normally keep one on hand with music uploaded. The USB worked OK, it has an issue where it will not play music from an iPhone via USB unless the music is on the iPhone, so Spotify or Pandora via USB is out of the question. Unfortunately, when it senses that an iPhone is connected via USB, it automatically switches over to USB and will not switch back until the phone has been disconnected, so if you want to listen to Spotify, you're limited to Bluetooth, but cannot charge the phone while doing so.

Around December, the radio stopped connecting to Bluetooth. It would send notifications through the radio, but music was unplayable. This was tested with multiple iPhone and Android Tablets, and the results were the same regardless of equipment used. I found out via accident that disconnecting the power to the radio and reconnecting it would cause the Bluetooth to work again for a couple of weeks. A minor inconvenience, but easily solvable by wiring a power interrupt switch in my dashboard. Now whenever the issue happened, I would toggle the switch to cut power, and toggle it back to re achieve a power connection.

The other day, I went to the car and turned everything on like normal and the unit would not power on. I thought that my wiring was culprit, so I ripped everything apart and checked everything out with a multi meter. The unit is receiving battery power, but not powering on. A nice little paperweight if you will. Unfortunately, it is out of the Amazon refund window, so I have to rate this one star (it didn't even last 6 months!) and purchase another unit from a more reputable vendor.

title: UPDATE: From 5 Stars to 1 Star with the new kits -_- Shame
text:
UPDATE: I just bought two more sets of these and... they're horrible. The bracket that holds the lights up no longer really works at all. Where it used to kind of click into place and hold strong, now it just falls except for the few that can just barely hold their own weight up. It's truly a shame. These used to be so great, now they're almost useless. Not only that, the kit came with a jumbled mix of tripods that didn't match, like they were thrown together from different kits.

OLDER RATING (THEY USED TO BE GOOD):
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I've now owned these for 1 year and they're still running strong! I had my doubts because of the other reviews I saw but idk, maybe I got lucky? Mine have been working perfectly. I've been using them on a fairly regular basis and even the original light bulbs are all still working, which: that has honestly surprised me.

I just bought another set! The new set all works just fine, though I have noticed that on the newer "model" (I guess), the switches seem different. Not as fluid as the older switches. As in, the newer switches seem like they are "sticky" or just harder to press. Honestly that's not even a big deal, just something I noticed was different from the original kit.

Another difference I noticed and something I consider to be an upgrade on the newer kit, is that they use heavier duty tripods for ALL of the lights instead of just the light with the "boom arm." This is a big plus for me, since the older light stands that held the vertical lights seemed to be kind of cheap. The new tightening brackets on the new stands are higher quality as well. They look bulkier and just seem like they'll last a much longer time.

The light tones DO match the old light tones exactly, which is a huge plus for me, as I'll be using the new and the old ones in the same space (so I really didn't want two different colors of lights). This is especially essential for my photogrammetry! I use a particular method of photogrammetry that I cam up with that allows me to flip an object in multiple directions and still align perfectly upon processing. The one requirement is that it have even lighting (of the same color) across the entire object.

I also love the fact that these, even though they are at a low price, still come with fuses for the light outlet module! So if anything does happen to them, I can most likely just replace the fuse and continue working with them :) But using the fluorescent light bulbs that it comes with, I don't think there's any risk of that happening. You may have to worry about that if you switch out the light bulbs with incandescent bulbsl, which yeah, if you're using these for portrait photography, you'll definitely want to use a full-frame camera to let in that extra light AND you might consider replacing the bulbs with more powerful ones. The bulbs these come with are perfect for product photography, photogrammetry or other stationary subjects where you can have the camera on a tripod and use a slow shutter speed with low ISO.

As you can see in the photo, I'm not using the "boom" lights right now, but I switch them in and out all the time depending on what I'm shooting. So I do use them.

Summing up (plus additional) Pros and Cons:

Pros:
- Distributes light evenly - great for product photography, photogrammetry, lighting green screens evenly, etc.
- Sturdy build quality, especially with the newer kit. The one I bought 1 year ago was not as sturdy.
- Long-lasting light bulbs.
- Long lasting light bulb outlet module.
- Includes fuses for light bulb outlet module.
- Fairly intuitive to put together but it can take time/futzing - I didn't need to read the instructions to figure it out, and I had never (personally) owned a softbox before buying these, though I had worked with some super expensive ones - but those used a different method to put them together.
- Even the carrying case seems like a nice quality. I have moved these around a lot and the case still looks like new.
- You can easily access the light bulbs from the back, so if one bulb goes out, you don't have to disassemble the entire soft box to change the bulb out (see photos).
- You can vent out some of the heat by taping the top flap open (towards the back of the soft box) - just undo the velcro there and pull it open. NOTE: This will also reduce the amount of light coming out of the front by a little bit and I don't think the heat is a big issue. I've kept mine closed for a year and they still work fine. So I'd advise against venting it unless maybe you've switched the bulbs with hotter bulbs.

Cons:
- I noticed on the new soft boxes, they are a little bit more difficult to put together than the old one. The softbox, even though it's the same size as the older ones, seems a little bit tighter. Give yourself about 2-4 minutes per softbox to get it fully put together.
- While the "boom" light IS strong enough to hold the light fully extended, the small bag that is included cannot hold very much. So you can 1. Get some small, heavy lead weights or something to put in that bag or 2. do like I do and use a separate bag (backpack, night-bag, etc) with weights in it. Again, the tripod DOES appear to be strong enough to handle the weight. I have used the boom light fully extended on several occasions with no problems at all, but I do use a night-bag filled with weights instead of the bag that came with the kit.

Even though it's got a couple of "cons," for the price, I don't think these can be beat. I did quite a bit of research 1 year ago and even more research this year before purchasing these. They still seem to give you the most wattage-output for your buck. I'm really happy with this purchase and I think that these will last me a really long time :)

Extra note: If you're wondering what I've taped onto the front of each soft box, it's a linear polarizing sheet. This allows me to polarize each light so I can use circular polarizing filters on each of my 3 cameras to reduce and almost entirely eliminate reflections on reflective objects. The two images attached show Before (highly reflective, without the use of polarization) and After (with the use of polarization to remove reflections) photos of a highly reflective hammer just to get the idea across. If you're interested in doing something similar, just google "Polarizing sheet" and search for by-the-foot sales. I paid $15/foot. Each soft box will require a 17"x24" sheet. I recommend attaching it with black duct tape, as that has worked well for me.

Hope this is helpful!
