title: Cannot Recommend At Any Price
text:
I was offered a complimentary promotional copy of the Tomameri Portable MP4/MP3 player for evaluation and an honest review. I'm sorry to say that I'm baffled by all the generous reviews this little player has received. Perhaps the product I received was a "lemon" or a factory reject shipped inadvertently. I cannot rule that out. I write this, though, because - how to put a somewhat agreeable face on it? - the device is not very good: poorly constructed, with switch, dial, screen, and earphones of the cheapest, most insubstantial materials. I've had a variety of MP3 players, mostly SANSA, but also the obligatory early generation iPods and a SONY. They all have a nicely designed, machined heft to them. This Tomameri seems thrown together, in a word, just cheap - fragile-feeling and ready to burst apart at the slightest impact with any solid surface, with moving parts that seems ready to snap or cease to move, and switches ready to fail in short order.

All this might have been immaterial, at least in the short term, if the player had performed decently - I might have given it to one of the kids as a music MP3. As it is, I found the control package - the single dial that clicks at four points of the compass (which was loose and shifted around in its housing), a central button, and the software load - to be incomprehensible. The small folded-up page of spare instructions shed no useful light on the situation. I got the player to play the file I had loaded and the pre-loaded samples, but after playing around with it for twenty or so minutes, I couldn't figure out how to make the player behave in a consistent manner. For some reason, the designers of this item ignored the universal symbols of MP3 players - there were no "pause" or "play" symbols, only the symbol for "skip to end of file" or next chapter, which was responsible for all scrolling. The result of this, for example, was that "down" wasn't down - down was "click to the right." "Up" was "click to the left." When I couldn't navigate to where I needed to go and was lost in root files, I was forced to hit "menu" to start over. And over. And over. I had to keep going "home" for everything. It was a most unpleasant experience. No, I'm no EE but I'm not technology neophyte, either. This was just silly.

I use MP3 players for audio books. For this purpose, I need at least a convenient fast forward, fast backward, and bookmarking function. For a test, I loaded a few chapters of a book I had recently listened to. The sound reproduction was tinny - it may have been the cheap earbuds that came with the player, or the player itself - but I was unable to manipulate the recording as I would need to in the real world. As far as I can tell, this player has none of the requisite features for serviceable use as an audiobook player, and if it does indeed have them, I couldn't conveniently locate and use them.

Finally, because this was a trial product, I believe my frustration, and the user-hostility of the hardware-software interface, warranted the discontinuation of the test after some 20 uncomfortable minutes. The product failed to function as an item I would use or give to a friend or family member to use. Instead, it left me completely frustrated.

I note today's listed price for this item is $59.95. At the time I received my trial copy, it was on "sale" for $18.95. And I see that Amazon.com Market vendors are selling it for under $18.00. Regrettably, I cannot recommend this player at any price.

title: Great semi-budget tablet
text:
Works great for movies and YouTube. The sound quality is amazing for a tablet compared to its competitors. It has 4 JBL speakers on the base and can fill my living room with sound; it's hard for me to stand it at max volume...Which is saying something as I'm pretty hard of hearing (at least from what my wife says). Battery life is crazy long due to its large battery.

A couple downsides, as everything has (but don't let them discourage you):
*It's hefty for a tablet. It's not a featherweight tablet as the housing for the speakers and the stand are metal and the battery needs to be bigger to hold all that sweet sweet juice for your tablet to sip on)
*Its not super speedy (it's not an intel processor, so don't expect it to play super high graphics extensive games). This turns a lot of people off but consider what you're using your tablet for. Netflix and YouTube run smooth as silk and there's no lag on most of the games out there. That's what I use mine for and it excels.
* Its not as "popular" as the Samsung Galaxy and iPad series of tablets. Finding cases that fit the tablets unique shape are a little difficult. I have mine in a sleeve that I used for my Chromebook and it does its job. There are only a few sellers on Amazon that offer cases for the tablet and they look kinda iffy to me. You won't find a case at major retailers like Walmart or Target or whatever.

Still, these are minor issues on an otherwise superb tablet for media consumption. You'd be hard-pressed to find something with all this tech at this price point.

title: Excellent Entry Level Desktop Computer
text:
Update:
Crashes about every hour or two and it does this starting in the spring until it gets cold weather again. Any room ambient temperature over about 74 degrees F starts the crashing. I've removed the side panel and put a household fan on high speed directly pointed to the motherboard and it still crashes randomly. I've used freeze spray on the CPU and motherboard components to no avail. I've put expensive RAM in it. I've used SSDs in it. I believe it's probably the motherboard, but it might be the CPU. However, it works flawlessly in cold weather. I've changed out everything except the motherboard and CPU. The only thing of value remaining is the case, Windows 10 license, DVD player and power supply and case. And I'm not sure it's worth the money to change out the motherboard and CPU, but I'll probably find some low budget CPU and motherboard that's a lot higher speed. This computer is just too slow, but it will function for Netflix if you are patient. The CPU is a low power, low speed dual core CPU. I've wasted too much time on this to continue. For sure, I'm never going to use an AMD processor in it. I'll replace it with an Intel product. Of course, that means a new motherboard, too. Next thing I'll know is I've spent well over $100 to make it work again.
----------------
In today's shift toward small thin lightweight laptop and tablet computers, midsized tower computers have formidable competition. And you still need a monitor. It is currently priced ay $300 and that's a good price. It becomes a superb computer, if you upgrade to a SSD. I plan to use it for my main computer because it is so quiet compared to my high power 4.6 GHz desktop computer with lots of noisy fans to keep it cool. I’ll use the 4.6 GHz desktop computer for video editing and compiling when I need the performance, which is rare. The best upgrade you can make is a SSD for the operating system. It makes this otherwise modest speed computer into a much faster computer. The hard drive is the slowest part of any computer and you will see the best benefit by far if you upgrade to a SSD. I've already done it and it made a dramatic difference.
--------------------
Update: This computer appears to have a thermal problem now that it is in the middle of summer. It crashes without warning several times a day. I've replaced the RAM memory, installed the new Windows 10 operating system and gone back to the original hard drive that came with it. So now I'm down to the CPU and motherboard as the prime suspect. The CPU feels lukewarm to the touch and with an infrared thermometer, it is about 97° F, which is well within limits. I've felt all the other components on the motherboard and none feel warm either. So it's pretty much a difficult decision to replace the motherboard. Of course, I would want to install a more expensive motherboard that is higher performance, but that means buying a new CPU and the cost just escalates. By the time I'd finish, about all that is left of the original computer is the case. I suppose I can send it back on warranty to see what happens. I don't know what the warranty is.
--------------------

I have never liked Windows 8, but it appears Acer has installed a version of Windows 8 that makes the interface look much more like Windows 7, which is very good. I downloaded Start 8 which converts Windows 8 to look almost the same as Windows 7. The price is only $5 and you can even get a 30 day free evaluation copy to determine if you like it. I’ve been using Start 8 ever since Windows 8 was introduced.
---------------------------------
I just installed a 120 GB Mushkin Enhanced ECO2 MKNSSDEC120GB Solid State Disk (SSD) into this computer and now it's much faster - boot time under 25 seconds. Web pages load in about two seconds, depending upon which web site, of course. I only paid $47 for the SSD on sale. I use it exclusively for the Operating System Software (Windows 8.1). My data, photos and video will go onto an existing 256 GB SSD I already had (paid $110 for it). Next I bought a Syba SATA III 6Gbps PCI-e Card (SD-PEX4004) for $22.40 to go into the X1 PCIe slot n the motherboard to be able to add a second SSD for data storage so that I can eliminate the old style hard drive. There is a mount for a 2.5" drive inside the chassis, but to add a second 2.5" drive, you'll need an adapter to fit into the single 3.5" drive bay. I bought a ICY Dock EZ-Fit MB290SP-B 2 x 2.5” to 3.5” SATA SSD Mounting Adapter for $6 to do this. Actually there is a mounting place for a second hard drive or SSD next to the main drive cage. I'm using it for my SSD now. The power cable just barely stretches between the two hard drive locations.

I bought a HP wireless keyboard ($28.80) and Microsoft wireless mouse ($11). When you buy a basic desktop computer, you're tempted to keep adding things to make it into the computer you really want. And all these prices I just quoted were sale priced - much less than the normal price.
---------------------------------
Pros:
Whisper quiet and good styling
Quad Core Processor AMD A6-6310 64-Bit CPU
Modified Windows 8.1 user interface
Power DVD 12 Preinstalled
HDMI monitor output connector
8 USB ports (2 of which are USB 3.0)
300 Watt Power Supply
1 PCIe X16 Expansion slot (for video card)
1 PCIe X1 Expansion slot (for Optional SATA card)
1 Year Limited Warranty

Cons:
Not a fast APU: 1.8 GHz Base to 2.4 GHz Turbo Mode
(But if you add a SSD, it will perform faster.)
4 GB RAM (But completely adequate for normal use)
Comes with only a DVD writer. Wish it came with a Blu-ray drive.

If you need a monitor, this one seems like an excellent one to consider.
Acer G247HL bid 24-inch Full HD (1920 x 1080) Widescreen Display $140

Optional additions I've purchased so far - Mostly SSDs: Total = $279
120 GB Mushkin Enhanced ECO2 MKNSSDEC120GB Solid State Disk (SSD) $47
Crucial MX100 256GB SATA 2.5-Inch Internal Solid State Drive (CT256MX100SSD1) $115
Syba SATA III 6Gbps PCI-e Card (SD-PEX4004) $23
ICY Dock EZ-Fit MB290SP-B 2 x 2.5” to 3.5” SATA SSD Mounting Adapter $6
HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2 $40
Microsoft wireless mouse $11
Amazon Basics USB Powered Computer Speakers $14
Actiontec 200 Mbps PowerLine Network Adapter Kit (PWR200K01) $23
Asus VS247H-P 23.6-Inch Full-HD LED-Lit LCD Monitor $156

This computer is so much faster now with the SSD - very fast in fact. I am using the smaller Mushkin SSD for the operating system and the other SSD for data storage. I removed the hard drive so now I have a purely solid state digital computer system. The only fan is on the CPU and it is so quiet I can't hear any sound. When my wife first used this computer, she complained it was slower than her 2.2 GHz HP laptop that she was using at the time. Now that I've added the SSD and these upgrades, she is very pleased with the speed - much faster than her former laptop computer. And now she has a much bigger video 24 inch monitor. I went too cheap on the speakers, but they are satisfactory.

I’ve made the additional modest investments above in large part because I got this computer on the Amazon Vine program. Otherwise, I would have purchased a different model of Acer desktop computer with a higher APU (CPU) speed of at least 3 GHz to make the incremental cost more justifiable. Acer makes a full range of desktop and laptop computers. If you are satisfied with a smaller monitor, it’s a lot more economical to get a upscale laptop computer because most of the optional things I bought are already built into the computer. But if you want the flexibility to soup up your computer, you can only do so much with a laptop computer. Acer makes numerous computer models that all perform quite well. I bought a Acer Aspire AS5750Z-4835 15.6-Inch Laptop in early 2012 and it still works very well. My daughter has the Acer laptop computer now and she loves it, especially with the high speed SSD I installed.

Anyway, if you have a little extra cash, I'd recommend that you get a more advanced model such as the Acer Aspire ATC-605-UR1X Desktop Computer with a 3.2 GHz Intel i5 CPU. Most all of the computers I own have an AMD CPU. However, Intel simply makes superior CPUs. The Intel I7 I bought way back in late 2009 is still almost as fast as the much more recent AMD CPUs I've purchased including the quad core AMD running at 4.6 GHz that I'm using to write this review. On the other hand, most of the time I am using the computer, the CPU is sitting there doing nothing waiting for me to type on the keyboard or click the mouse. If you buy this computer, consider upgrading it to a SSD soon afterwards. It turns this computer into a much faster computer than the original equipment - and not for a lot of money these days. Just wait for a good sale price. And then you can use the 1 TB hard drive just for data storage - either internally or externally. I'm planning to use it as external storage. It will take a long time just to fill up the second SSD I put inside the case.

Overall, I'm very surprised how fast this computer is after I upgraded it with a SSD. And I even used an economy SSD on sale for less than $50! It just illustrates how slow mechanical hard drives are in contrast to SSDs. I always dedicate the main SSD to the operating system, even though it's not necessary.

title: Beautiful monitor with a minor defect
text:
This is a beautiful monitor. 2160x3840 on 24" makes it virtually retina — you cannot notice the pixels (unless you get really close). Text is like, maybe even better than, print on paper. Pictures are so realistic they are better than prints and rival real life. The monitor is so much better for your eyes than the old HD (1200x1920) monitor I have. I am so happy for the viewing experience.

Many of your existing pictures will look sharper but too small on this monitor. However, that is not the fault of the monitor. What is lacking is a software/app that allows easy zooming instead of clicking several clicks to zoom each picture. (Let us know if any of you knows a picture viewer like that.) High resolution pictures look stunning, like real life.

The unit is also quite light weight and thin, again much better than the older 24" HD monitor I have.

Then why two star? The unit does not wake up from sleep from time to time. You will then have to first move your mouse a few times, maybe push a few keys on the keyboard before you are sure it's not going to wake up, then power the monitor down and back up, and then wait for the monitor to get ready from a complete power off rather than the instantaneous waking up from a simply move of the mouse or a simple touch of a button. While it works with some hassles from time to time, one cannot stop wondering, this is still brand new, what would happen as time passes? At first, this wasn't as big a deal as the monitor is gorgeous. But you do get tired of having to go through the trouble over time after the initial excitement of a beautiful monitor wears off. Furthermore, the monitor is supposed/designed to wake up after a simple move of the mouse or key. Not doing that makes the unit a defective product (even thought not severely defective).

If not because of the one problem/defect, I would have given it a five star rating. If Dell comes up a fix through software/driver upgrade (or whatever means), I will upgrade the rating to a five star.

UPDATE: Starting today (3/21/95) the monitor no longer wakes up with either displayport or minidisplayport. I'm returning this monitor and have ordered a new one. (HDMI still wakes up intermittently/most of the time, which I could tolerate, but since this monitor uses FRC/time-dither, you really need to have 60Hz refresh rate, and only displayport/minidisplayport can give me 60Hz refresh rate.)

UPDATE 2: I ended up canceling the new order and called Dell Warranty service, who quickly sent a replacement (a refurbished unit) in two days with a preprinted label for shipping back the old monitor at no charge. The new unit works but I can't really test the wakeup issue right now (will report if it still has that problem when I am ready to use displayport again).

UPDATE 3: The replacement (refurbished) monitor now is able to wake up from a monitor sleep without problem (which the original one had problem with) with displayport connection. However, if the computer wakes up from a sleep, the monitor says "entering sleep mode", goes/stays completely dark while the computer is in process of waking up, but then it wakes up again when the computer is done waking up, which is tolerable.

UPDATE 4: The replacement monitor's displayport stopped working (HDMI still worked but that gets only you 30Hz refresh rate). I called Dell Support. Someone answered the phone in a reasonable time and sent a replacement (of the original replacement), which is the version A02, arrived on the second day, and is working fine. A bit hassle, but not too bad. While the first replacement did not have wakeup issue, this new replacement does -- the monitor sometimes does not wake up -- I will then have to first move the mouse a few times, press a couple of keys, and then turn off the monitor and turn it back on again!

text:
Summary: classy looking, nice size for professional use by women, but there are problems with the details that don't justify the price. I returned the item and I'm still searching for better alternatives.

Pros of this backpack:
- Seems to be well made
- The black color version is very classy, the blue tags on zippers are a nice touch, it all looks professional and swanky.
- Enough space for MacBook Pro, 15", old version of iPad in case, iPad and MacBook adapters, mouse, one or two books, small protected pocket for sunglasses or other small items
- Small enough that it looks nice on a woman, also has an adjustable chest strap, not bulky

Cons - which is why I returned it:
- Most annoyingly, the second compartment is very narrow and deep, and you can only access it from the top. So it's kind of hard to get things out. Given that it's the compartment that I was planning to use for adapters, and therefore to use often, it's really not functional.

- The loop by which you can carry the bag is flimsy. Other backpacks out there incorporate the loop into the shoulder straps, so you don't have to worry about the loop ripping off if you carry the backpack in your hand.

- The main compartment has two blue tagged zippers. Great. The second, smaller compartment has only one blue tagged zipper - but it looks like there should be another one, or like one is missing. The one zipper has that extra eye-hole which makes you think there should be another zipper added. But on all the pictures, it looks like this is intentional. Not sure why - you can put a lock on the main compartment, so why not the second one??

- The protected sunglasses compartment and the second compartment have only one zipper. This makes it annoying to open the compartments - you have to look for which side your zipper is on.

Overall, I'm disappointed - for the high price the details on this product should be perfect.

title: Already malfunctioning in under a year
text:
We purchased this same TV from a competitor. We have had it for less than a year, but now the first malfunction has occurred. The TV will indiscriminately restart. It doesn't matter if we are watching Netflix via the TV's own Netflix app, or via the Roku app, or whether we are watching DirecTV Now via the Roku, the TV will lose sound, and then in a matter of seconds, the TV shuts off and then restarts a few seconds later. There is no pattern to it. It happens indiscriminately and frequently—several times per hour! I contacted LG customer service twice. The first chat agent simply said to plug the TV directly into a wall outlet; however, it did not resolve the issue. Even if it did, are you trying to tell me that my $2000 TV should be left unprotected!?!? Please. Since that did not resolve the issue, the second chat agent (about a week later) provided me instructions on how to do a hard reset. Basically, turn TV off, unplug everything from back of TV, then hold down power button (on TV, located underneath logo in front) for about 15 seconds, let TV rest for a minute, then power on). That did not resolve it either.

Edit: I will now contact LG chat for a third time this evening and set up an appointment with a tech in person.

Edit: The contracted LG repair technician replaced the motherboard. It did not resolve the issue. They recently informed me that they ordered new speakers and a power supply unit. Evidently, they are now throwing parts at it. I began doing further troubleshooting on my own, and I believe the problem is the 5.0 GHz portion of the Wi-Fi card. Whenever I connect the LG TV to my home's 5.0 GHz Wi-Fi network, the problem occurs. However, if I connect to the 2.4 GHz instead, the problem ceases. So, it's quite obvious what the problem is. Problem is, I don't know how to fix it. Being that they replaced the motherboard (i.e., hardware) it seems that this is a software issue. That is something LG has to fix, but I'm not holding my breath. I won't be buying another LG, though.

title: Good noise cancellation, decent sound, comfortable. Very good value noise canceling in-ear headphones
text:
I'm a little perplexed. Reading over some of the other reviews for these headphones, I see many claims that the noise canceling doesn't work.

I can assure you: It does. I have well over a dozen different pairs of noise canceling headphones, including a couple of pairs of Bose, Dishwasher, Sennheiser, AKG, Sony,and others. The noise canceling ability of these headphones is better than average.

I think it's important to clarify what noise canceling can do. Basically, noise canceling listens to the ambient noise and creates a sound wave that cancels the part of the ambient noise that is predictable and continual. So, for example, the rumble of a jet engine on a plane or the hum of a refrigerator can be canceled. Talking can't be canceled, because it's not predictable. Total noise reduction combines the active noise reduction with additional noise suppression that comes from the design of the headphone.

These Panasonic noise canceling headphones definitely work pretty well. You can easily experience this: Put on the headphones without turning them on. Go stand next to your refrigerator, then press the on button. You will suddenly hear the refrigerator rumble disappear. That's the active noise canceling.

I've used these headphones on a plane, on a subway, and while mowing the yard. While they will not totally turn your world to silence in those environments, they definitely reduce the ambient noise level enough to make it possible to listen to music at a comfortable volume. I find that the noise canceling on these is better than the Sony and AKG in-ear headphones I have, They are about comparable in that respect to the much more expensive Sennheiser headphones. And they don't block noise as well as something like the Bose over-the-hear noise canceling headphones. But again, they're more portable.

In terms of ergonomics: The earbuds themselves are surprisingly comfortable to wear. I find a lot of earbuds either don't form a good fit or else aren't comfortable. With these, the fit was great right out of the box. There's a battery compartment that uses a AAA battery and add weights in the middle of the cable. I don't much like that, but it pretty much goes with the territory with these in-ear noise canceling headphones. You don't have the luxury of placing the battery compartment in earphones themselves, as you do with over-the-ear models. The battery compartment does have a clip on it that can be used to clip the compartment to your shirt to reduce the apparent weight.

The headphones only work when a battery is inserted. No battery: No sound. These use a standard AAA battery, which is easily replaceable. I like that better than a proprietary rechargeable battery, which is the design some manufacturers use. Just carry an extra AAA and worst case you replace the battery as needed.

In terms of sound: The bass is solid, although it won't please bass-heads. The high end is fine. Not too shrill, easy to listen to over extended periods, but clear. The mid-range is the weak link here. It's a bit muddy. On the whole, the sound is pleasant, but because of the mid-range falls short of great. That said, most noise-canceling headphones don't offer optimal sound, with some sacrifice made for the sake of noise canceling. These headphones are better than average in terms of sound for this segment.

On the whole, I like these. Despite midrange that's a bit smeary, on the whole these are pleasant to listen to and are comfortable for extended periods of time. Though I prefer my Sennheiser in ears for overall experience, those are about 3x as expensive. Given the performance at at the price point, these are a very good, and easily recommended, set of noise canceling in-ear headphones.

title: Works well AFTER amplifier removed
text: I revised this review AFTER removing the amplifier portion of my Sky antenna giving it a much better review. I get much better service and more than twice the channels though most of the extra ones are sales stations. But, some are not, and they are ones that pixallated or I simply did not receive as the tower is in a different direction. I live 17 miles from Philadelphia broadcast towers and 17 miles from South Jersey towers. I had the antenna installed in the attic above my 2-story wood-frame home. Before removing the amplifier, I got most channels tvfool.com and antennaweb.org said I should but not all (no NJTV and FOX  and ocassioally NBC pixellated). When I removed the amplifier, I received 60 stations, up from 30 when it was amplified, plus no pixelating Eagles games on FOX. With the amplification, the antenna was definitely not omnidirectional. Without the amplifier, it is. I had read that amplification could interfere if you were really close to the towers. I did not think 17 miles was that close. My only reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is because the Mohu instruction manual was "bare bones," and their on-line support only told me to keep moving the direction of my antenna though I gave them my address. They never suggested removing the amplifier. The antenna also supports 2 TV's now, up from one before amplifier removal. Through all this I also learned your phone compass needs to be turned around a bit to recalibrate. Just move it in a figure 8 pattern a few times. Lots of trial and error, but the TV works very well now.

title: 6 Months of Daily Usage - This Backpack is a Winner!
text:
I bought this backpack as a replacement for a 4-year old ful backpack. It was a hard decision to replace it since the only thing that was wrong was the oldness and small tears. I spent weeks looking at different backpacks and wanted one that was durable, large enough to carry a lot when travelling but too large, and one that was very flexible. This backpack is different from the ful backpack, but I'm not looking back. I've been using this backpack for over 6 months (pretty much everyday) and this is my honest review:

The standout feature of this backpack is that it has A LOT of compartments. It makes it very easy to store lots of different things in an organized way. I'm a student and I need to carry a laptop, tablet, folder, books, writing utensils, chargers, calculator, keys, wallet, umbrella ( rainy where I live ), among other things. Since I'm on campus for pretty much all of the time I am awake, I need a lot of things with me. This thing can handle it all! I once lost an umbrella inside of this thing! I searched and searched for it but couldn't find it. I found it a few days later in the third compartment of the backpack. The hidden zipper on the part that goes along your back realy is a nice addition as well - perfect to store things like your wallet and passport. Its also easily accessible with your backpack on so you don't need to take it off to get access to the things in that pocket.

The laptop compartment is will fit even slightly bulkier 15 inch laptops and I feel safe putting my tablet in the padded sleeve in the main compartment, even with other things inside of it. The side pockets is nice - I keep a large water bottle in one and put things like cables and headphones in the other.

This backpack also makes a great travel companion. You can fit a lot of stuff if you do it right. The strap for putting it on luggage handles was actually useful and I was pleased to have that. I didn't have to worry about the backpack breaking when I had to squeeze it over from tight spaces or had to carry heavy loads.

Compared to my old backpack, this one has generally smaller compartments. The main compartment is big enough to be able to store your everyday things but when you go travelling and need some extra space for larger items, space can be tight. My older backpack excelled at space. However, I find this backpack is designed with smart space usage. You can truly fit a lot of stuff and not even notice. The comfortable straps and padded back helps with that as well. Also, something that might seem little is that the backpack has little strap holders. It actually makes a big difference.

One of my main concerns when buying this backpack was durability. Unlike my old backpack, the bottom was the same material as the rest of the backpack. My old backpack had a slightly tougher material which prevented liquid and dirt from affecting it. Also, the material felt just a bit thinner than my old backpack had. However, I have found this backpack to hold up really well. So far, I have no tears and no loose threads. I sometimes pack this thing up to the brim and have had to haul heavy loads so it can definitely take a beating. It actually still looks pretty new despite how heavily I use it.

Overall, I am very glad I chose to purchase this backpack. I use it everyday for everything from school and work to hiking and traveling. I anticipate many more years with this backpack.

The camera, NX30, was $950 brand new with a kit lens (May 2014), leaving me with $50 left to cover said lens. Fast forward to June 2015 and my camera took a dive, killing the focusing ring on the lens. I contacted SmartGuard to get a replacement, but they were only going to cover my lens for $50. Well, that won't work considering the lens itself is valued at $195.95 after discounts. This is something I did not know at the time and considering the camera then could only be be purchased with a kit lens, and not the body only, covering the camera at its purchased value was the best decision. Whats the total value of the camera with kit lens at this moment? $599.00.

After telling them this, they went completely silent on me and trying to chat with them via email has failed. The last email I received before silence was June 26th and it read, "Thank you for your response. This is currently under review. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any additional questions or concerns." Well, I didn't receive another email from them until I EMAILED THEM on August 5th asking what was the current status of my claim. The response back?

"Dear (me),
Thank you for your response. Your contract has been updated to have the bundled purchase represented as one product. We can continue with your claim. Please provide us with the claim information below and we will be able to file the claim for you.

What’s happened to the product?
When did the problem first occur?
What caused this to happen?
Was this used as personal or for business?
Please describe the physical damage of the product.
If you prefer to speak with a live agent, please do not hesitate to contact us at 877.308.8071. We hope to hear from you soon!

At this point, I was extremely annoyed because this is something I already went over. Seeing how this was going no where via email, I called the number in the email and got a really nice person on the phone. They assured me they were going to look into the matter, and call me back.

Today, August 25th, I sit at my computer, writing this poor review because my problem still hasn't been resolved. Great purchase.

title: The BAD: EXTREMELY cheaply built
text:
The BAD:
EXTREMELY cheaply built. The soldering job looks like it was done by someone while riding in a bus over speed bumps. Leads at cut to random lengths with components laying haphazardly. The heatsinking is at least done properly unlike most Chinese electronics. The main board was missing most of its mounting screws due to the misaligned mounting holes.
The GOOD. The componets are mostly name brand (Unless they are counterfeit. I'm not an expert but they looked legit). The voltage regulation is superb and held to within .01V with a 15 amp load. It was preset from the factory to a healthy 12.23 volts. It didnt get hardly warm at all under a 15 amp load and the fan ramps up as the supply gets warm (Which is nicer then some supply's that just turn the fan on full blast). The fan barely even came on under a 15 amp load and I could hardly hear it.

I have only ran it for about an hour at 15 amps. I will update if it burns up while powering my 3d printer.

UPDATE: Working very good powering the 20 amp load of my 3d printer. Voltage regulation is quite good as far as I can test. Gets warm but not crazy hot even with the fan is not running. Now you might ask yourself why I know how it works without the fan running? Well the fan burned up after only 4 hours of use. I replaced it with a spare I happened to have and it has been fine for 30+ hours of use.

I actually used this fan and a 12v wall-wart (AC->DC converter) to push air through an 8 inch duct pipe that runs from my basement (where the wood stove is) to my upper floor.  Unlike normal duct fans, It is extremely quiet (though not entirely silent), and pushes plenty of air for it's intended purpose (I can feel the breeze a solid 10 feet away from the duct register upstairs).  By pushing hot air from the wood stove room through the duct to the upstairs like this allows me to keep my upstairs comfortably warm, and helps me keep the downstairs from becoming uncomfortably hot when the wood stove is stoked up good and hot.  If you were to use this as a case fan, I am sure it would go a long way towards keeping your gear cool - it moves a LOT of air by computer case fan standards, without being overly noisy about doing it.

It gave me the perspective of being a neutral party from the outside looking in and I was able to see how I actually look compared to how I feel and what I think I look like whilst arguing. title: Good value, lacks a little in the highs and in overall detail
text:
Here are my findings. Your mileage may vary. Sound is subjective so these are just data points to help you decide if these are the right speakers for you. My personal goal is to find cheap speakers for airplay around the apartment, and in the future, for whole house audio.

Pros
1 - neutral tone - non fatiguing sound
2 - nice mids and highs - sounds best on vocal tracks
3 - reasonable sound stage presentation, depends on speaker placement

Cons
1 - lacks bass, makes vocals sound thin.
2 - poor resolution of details in music
3 - lacks transparency and sometimes can sound like a hollow box

These are not warm sounding speakers. The mid-bass is missing even after 35 hours of break in. Adding a subwoofer may not help since I want more mid-bass. I don't have a sub so cannot comment further about it.

Would I recommend these? It depends. If you have a sub and a small size room I think these are a "buy." If you have a small size room and NO sub, then these are a "try." If you are used to hearing $200+ speakers then you will be disappointed. For larger rooms you will need to play around with placement near walls and boundaries to see if you can get more bass. Otherwise, you need larger speakers for larger rooms. Not these.

I am now listening to them with iTunes EQ set to Bass Boost and they are a little better. Certainly they can serve as generic airplay speakers with the EQ on. They are somewhat big so they may not be the best for bookshelves, especially since they are rear ported.

I hope this helps. Personally I will not be buying another set and will look around for other speakers that might serve the whole-house audio role.

Update

I find that I like the soundstage from 15+ feet. If you have a large room, play these loud and stand 15-20 feet away. They sound better loud (unfortunately).

My wife noticed that they lack high frequency sparkle. I agree. Still, they sound nice for what they can do. I wish I had other speakers on hand for comparison. Unfortunately I am planning my move now and cannot buy anything until I am in a house.

The more I listen to these the more I like them enough to consider buying another pair if I should need them for whole house audio. It's the price that makes them a good choice for multi-room audio.

Also, I tried putting them on a desk near a rear wall. This helped boost the bass.

title: Never thought much about Vizio... Until now!
text:
Backstory

My Samsung blu-ray home theater system decided to stop working after 3 years... The HDMI would no longer output any video or audio. That means not only did I lose a blu-ray player, but I also lost my home theater sound system. That was the last time I purchased a device that serves more than one purpose. So, here I am hunting for a replacement 5.1 channel sound system. I do not want (and/or need) a receiver. And what about having rear wireless speakers like my good old Samsung had? Practically all speaker systems are wired unless I add some additional transmitter/receivers into the mix - or do I buy another blu-ray HT system w/ wireless speakers? Oh, what a headache. No.. I'm not getting another all-in-one unit. I'll wait and do some research...

Vizio.. who?

I know Vizio has been around for a few years now and they make decent, affordable TVs. But truthfully, I've never considered their TVs, let alone audio products. So I'm poking around. Doing some homework. Vizio seems to be one of the only ones out there who make a 5.1 sound bar system. A sound bar system? I never considered those... why? No reason really. Just never did. So after searching and reading and searching some more, Vizio appears to have a 5.1 sound bar system that was well regarded by a number of review sites. Hmm... Let's take a look at Vizio...

Timing

You know how everything happens for a reason, right? Or so I've been told. Well, after perusing through the Vizio website, I came across the SB4051 system. Not available yet. Coming soon. How soon? When? Oh, there; it says May 2015. Ok, great. I can wait. I'll check ever known site for the next month, but I can wait. One fine day (April 13th I think), I checked the Vizio site and guess what now had an 'Add to cart' next to it? YEP! and PURCHASED!

New Arrival

Got my package April 21st. A week after ordering. Not bad considering it came from the West Coast to East Coast and shipping was free. Its in a typical, funky shaped box that most of Vizio's soundbar systems come in - from what I recall at the local Best Buy. Oh joy!

If They Build It, We Will Buy

Unpacking the system was a breeze. First thing I noticed was the build quality. Wow. What an incredible product. Everything on this system reeks quality. Very elegant. Even classy to the point where it just looks great and enhances the whole home theater look. Nice job Vizio. Keep it up!

Installation

No gonna get into the nitty gritty... Comes with all the cables, some hardware, a remote, etc. Installation is easy. Sound bar in front of tv. Wireless subwoofer in the back by the couch. Rear speakers wired to the sub. No wires from the front of the room to the back. NEAT-O! HDMI from cable into the bar, from the bar into the ARC HDMI of the TV. Done.

Testing 1..2..3..

Wholly shrimp!! The BASS! The crisp vocals! The surround! I flipped through a bunch of action flicks and watched a few minutes of each. Wow... I. Love. It. I can write about the sound quality from here to the moon, but the fact is, it must be heard. What a pleasure it will be watching sports, movies, you name it!!!

Happy Ending? (no, not that kind... get your mind out the gutter! lol)

MOST DEFINITELY! I'm extremely pleased with this product. It's build quality is great. It's features are great. It's sound quality is simply incredible. Highly recommended.

text:
This was an easy storage upgrade for my 2014 MacBook Air so I love it. Couple things to note
1) I love how flush the card is when inserted
2) Don't forget to format your card (not sure why they this isn't done) when you purchase it. Command + spacebar and type "disk utility". Then click on the card, select erase, and select the OS X Extended (Journaled) option
3) Download the JetDrive Toolbox from Transcend. [...], click on support > support & download. Then click on "Apple Solutions" and work your way down (like Jet Drive lite on the left for my macbook air)
4) Once that is installed, for my MacBook air, click on the JetDrive Lite tab at the top, and make sure under "Power Save" you have it clicked to On.

At first, it was strange because I assumed the Transcend drive would be seen like my normal hard drive, but if you are waking from sleep there is a slight delay before the drive appears on the desktop. Speaking of that, if you wake from sleep and don't log on right away (say wait 3 minutes before logging on) you won't see the drive. For it to mount you need to promptly log-in at the screen

title: Exceptional keyboard with Cherry MX Clear switches, but might not be for everyone.
text:
This was my first keyboard with Cherry MX Clear switches, I had previously used MX Blue and Brown switches, which most of my comparisons will be made to. I'm also someone who might type a bit harder than others, giving me a slight bias towards heavier-style switches.

KUL is a relatively new company (at the time of writing) and the ES-87 is their spotlight keyboard. As the name implies, this is a tenkeyless keyboard, if a numpad is a requirement for you, you'll most likely want to look elsewhere. The construction quality of the keyboard feels top notch. Although made of a plastic-type material, this is no flimsy keyboard. I will never be able to flex this keyboard while typing, and even when picking up the keyboard and trying to flex it you will barely be able to get it to do so, if you even can. The plastic is a matte style finish, you will not need to worry about getting fingerprints on the case.
The keyboard has double rubber grips on the bottom half, and a single set at the top. KUL has even gone as far as adding rubber grips to the fold out feet. Even with the heavier typing style of Cherry MX Clears, you will not have to worry about the keyboard moving while typing. On top of all of this, the keyboard uses a detachable A to Mini-B USB cable. Although I would have preferred if this cable was sleeved, KUL has given the ability for the user to use any length/style cable they desire. There is even built in cable routing if you prefer the cable exiting through the left, right, or top. The keyboard also features seven DIP Switch options on the back, allowing the user to customize certain aspects of the typing experience of this keyboard, something new to me which I found pretty handy. Due to this being an Amazon review, I'd recommend looking at KUL's website for an in-depth explanation of the DIP switches. KUL also sells other shells for this keyboard, so you can easily change this to blue, white, or red, without voiding warranty as long as you are using the genuine parts. With just a couple screws, you are able to disassemble the keyboard, a keyboard modder's delight!

So how is the typing experience with MX Clears on this board? Personally I find that Cherry MX Clears are a blast to type on, given some break-in time. Compared to an MX blue switch, I find the initial actuation force needed relatively the same, but the further into the key press after actuation will feel much stiffer than the MX blue. For someone who is a heavier typist, this does an incredible job making sure I don't accidentally glide over other keys and accidentally activate them, a problem I had using MX brown switches. When compared to an MX brown switch the general feel of the two is slightly the same, aside from the force needed on the MX clears. The tactile bump is still there, albeit much more pronounced, and due to the stiffer feeling after actuation it is much harder to bottom out the keys. This could be viewed as a positive or negative depending on the typist, but something I prefer due to the tactile feedback letting me know I have completed my keystroke so I can move to the next key quickly.

With the pros, must come the cons. This keyboard is great, but there are only two "flaws" I could consider this keyboard having. The first one I have to mention would be the slight "ping" of the keys when pressed. I do not think this is necessarily KUL's fault, but seems to be a more common trait of MX clears across multiple different boards. I use headphones most of the time and while wearing them I cannot hear this, so I personally consider this a non-factor, but if this sounds troublesome to you I'd recommend getting either O-Rings or Landing Pads for this keyboard, which should dampen or remove the "ping" noise. The only other con I can think of would be the keycaps. There's nothing specifically wrong with them, and they do a fine job, but I wish they had slightly more texture, and they feel a little... thin? I don't know the exact word I can use to describe it, but they have this "hollowness" to them my other keys don't have. This might be a personal bias though, as a person who replaces the keycaps on every keyboard I own I never expected stock keycaps to blow me away, but due to the standard bottom row (6.25 spacebar) it's very easy to find replacements if these are not up to par for your tastes. Other typists out there might find these keys to be perfect, personal preference really.

Who would like this keyboard? Due to the MX Clear switches (this keyboard can be ordered with different style switches) I would first recommend this to pure typists or someone who prefers a heavier key press with tactile bump. My second tier of people to recommend this board to would be those who are used to a tactile switch, but would like a more pronounced bump in the keypress, most likely a user of a brown or possibly blue switch. My last tier goes to gamers who play games where a heavy tactile bump would enhance their gameplay. I say this as a big PC gamer myself, I doubt the majority of gamers would want a switch like this to use on a daily basis. Holding WASD or Shift can be a bit more fatiguing than other switch types. If FPS is your thing, you'll most likely want an ES-87 in either MX Brown or Red, but in games where the click of a key is the choice between life and death of your character or army (RTS, Path of Exile, etc.) and you prefer to have that strong tactile bump, I wouldn't rule the MX Clears out right away, especially if you're the type of person who loves to mash those keys!

TL;DR: The KUL ES-87 is a high quality, easily portable, modifiable keyboard which can easily justify the price point in which its sold. Even if you decide Cherry MX Clear switches are not for you, I still recommend getting this keyboard with your preferred switch.

title: Best smartwatch for daily use
text:
At first I was a a bit sceptical regarding the battery lifetime, but after nearly 30 days and 30% battery left I'm now completely convinced.
After unboxing the Vector Luna the display told me that the battery is empty, so I had to charge the battery before to test. The first charge of the battery took about 1,5 hours. In my opinion thats awesome keeping in mind that the battery will last for 30 days.
The pairing with my Windows 10 Mobile phone (Microsoft Lumia 950) was really easy. The Display on the watch tells you to turn on bluetooth on your smartphone and search for the displayed name on the watch. When the pairing is done, the smartphone automatically opens the Vector app in your store, so you can quickly download the app. The app for Windows 10 Mobile is not as good as on Android or iOS, but you can adjust everything at all and the app is getting updated every week with new features since I got the Vector Luna.

The watch receives the notification a little bit later than your phone. I think it depends on the distance between your phone and the watch. After all the watch will receive every notification (text messages) within 2 seconds after the phone. Calls pop up immidiately on the display of the watch.
You can choose in the app how text Messages should arrive on the watch. You can choose between "Show on the watch after receiving", "Show only when I click the middle button", "Show when turning your watch to your eyes (so nobody except me can read it)" and so on. The watch has only a vibration alarm, no sound. I'm lucky about that.

The display itself is monochrom, without touch and has not a high resolution, so personalized watch faces with a picture could be not as clear as on apple watch. But the battery will last for 30 days and you don't have to charge it every day comparing to the apple watch. Please keep that in mind.
After nearly 30 days of wearing the watch day and night I cannot see any damages on the display or the watch itself.

The leather band is also very good. Soft and high quality. After nearly 30 days of daily wearing I also couldn't see any scratches or damages on the band, although I wear it the whole day. (work on my car, sports like swimming or Basketball, sleeping and so on)

On the Homepage of Vector you can also build your own personal watch faces or code some gadgets.
The In-App Store is full of custom made watch faces and you can download the existing watch faces, which are published by other users of the watch. Nearly all watch faces can be costumized by adding date, weather or other feeds.

I'm very satisfied with the Vector Luna and Vector is always working to release new features, watch faces and so on. In my opinion the Vector watch is the perfect watch for everybody who wanna use it like a Standard watch but with the benefits of getting notifications without touching the smartphone.

title: Affordable and Flexible Camera System
text:
I've had my Netgear Arlo 4 camera system for about six weeks at the writing of this post and I couldn't be more pleased. Prior to purchasing the $500 system I read many reviews, spent some time on the Netgear Arlo forums and almost talked myself out of trying these cameras. Thankfully I decided to go ahead and give them a shot.

Over the past few years I have tried many different wifi cameras around my home. Until this summer my favorite was my DropCam Pro. It had a few drawbacks, the biggest being having to pay for cloud storage or not having any way to record or store footage taken by the cameras. The cloud cost was pretty large at $10 per month for the first camera and $5 per month for any additional cameras. This can add up fast and I wanted more than one camera in my house so this was a consideration when looking to purchase more DropCam Pros. After purchasing my DropCam Pro, Google acquired DropCam and then put the company under the Nest umbrella and a few months ago released the Nest Cam. The Nest Cam was to be the "upgrade" to the DropCam so I was all over it and ready to take the plunge. Unfortunately, after purchasing it I realized it was a downgrade from the DropCam Pro and wasn't the right camera for me. So I started looking at other options. That's when I found the Netgear Arlo system.

Netgear Arlo is a completely wireless security camera solution. Each camera runs on 4 CR123 batteries which are rated with a lifespan of about 4-6 months. The cameras are indoor/outdoor and weatherproof.

The batteries, and the ability to place these cameras virtually anywhere, were the main selling point for me. I love that I can have the cameras monitoring the front of my home, my back yard, rooms in my home or even the inside of my refrigerator should I so choose. This gives me flexibility to have the system grow and change with my needs. The Arlo system I purchased comes with 6 magnetic mounts which can be affixed to walls with the included screws and anchors. It also included one adjustable indoor/outdoor mount which we used to affix one of the cameras to the roof of our front porch. Inside I got creative with my mounting and am actually using 3M Command picture hanging strips to hold the magnetic mounts in place. This makes it easy to move the cameras and not destroy the walls. I eventually plan to pick up one of the Arlo table/ceiling/wall mounts to use as a table mount for one of the cameras.

Since this system is completely wireless it includes a base station. The base station attaches to your router via Ethernet and it acts as the wireless network for up to 10 Arlo cameras.

1GB of cloud storage is included with the cameras at no additional cost. This includes storage for 7 days and up to 5 cameras. Other packages are available if you need longer storage times and/or more cameras. The prices for the additional packages start at $99 a year. I have found the free package to be more than sufficient. If you need to save a recording longer than 7 days the option to download clips is available on the Arlo web portal and in the mobile apps.

The Netgear Arlo system is not one where video will be constantly streaming. To save battery life the system is set to activate on motion detection and record for a determinate amount of time set by the user. You can also activate live video by choosing a camera feed, in the app, to view. Up to 4 cameras can be actively viewed at any one time. While viewing you can activate recording or snap a still photo.

Motion detection levels and recording time can be individually set for each camera and can be controlled by various modes and rules set by the user. These can be as basic as "All Motion On" or "All Motion Off" to more complex configurations such as a rule I have that if my front door camera starts recording motion it also triggers my living room camera to record so we can see who might be entering the house from the front. The flexibility to control these different scenarios makes these cameras even more useful to me than I would have imagined.

As I mentioned earlier, battery life is determined by use. I believe the 4-6 month life is based on recording of up to 4 minutes per day. I have one camera we set to 100% motion and within 2 days the battery level was depleted by a third as the camera went off if dust floated by. Changing the motion detection to a level of 75% extended the life of those batteries by 6 weeks and I have just now gotten the notice that they need to be replaced. At six weeks in I still have 2 cameras with full batteries and another that is down by a third. I keep tweaking the motion settings and recording lengths to get the best results from each camera as I see what is, or isn't, being captured.

As of now there are no "Smart Home" features built into the Arlo system outside of the rules and modes provided by the Arlo's locked down apps. IFTTT integration and support is highly sought after on the Arlo forums as is the ability for other smart home applications. I found this lack of smart home features confusing as much of the reading I did on these cameras prior to purchase referred to it as Arlo Smart Home. Even their Twitter presence is @arlosmarthome. I can only hope this means that smart home features will be introduced in the future, though none are announced as of the writing of this review.

The other feature this camera system lacks is the ability to record sound or communicate via 2-way audio. The other systems I've used have included this feature and while it's not something I use often, there are times I find myself wishing it was available.

Regardless of the few shortcomings this system has, I am extremely pleased with how it works and the flexibility it brings to using cameras in the home. I look forward to seeing what changes Netgear has for this system down the road, but as it stands now it's doing the job I need it to do and I would recommend this to anyone looking for a camera system.

Update 2/9/16: Winter is now in full force and I can say that it's definitely taking a hit on my battery life for my outdoor cameras. I'd have to say we're replacing them about every 6-8 weeks. I get lazy because it's kind of a hassle to get them down from their mounts, put the batteries in and then make sure they're back in the correct position, and don't replace them as quickly as I should. I look forward to going back to warmer weather so that we can extend the battery life again. Other than the battery issue, I am still very pleased with this set of cameras and highly recommend them.

title: Can I Get There, From Here & At Least Par The Hole?
text:
Purchased a refurbished Garmin Approach G6 from one of Amazon's many secondary sellers who handle similar merchandise Amazon sells, but that even with a Prime Membership, the secondary seller might be able to offer the item at less than Amazon's best price, including shipping & handling fees. In this case, I chose a refurbished and older model of one of many Garmin "GPS" products, here focused strictly on golf courses. Newer Garmin and like companies are offering devices with the options of this older model, and several that distract from the purity of the reason I play the game: they're providing texts, e-mails, news alerts along with the range finding from Tee Box to hole, hazard and along the way in between to the hole! I like the straight forward nature of this device as range finder (scorekeeper if one chooses to use the option). It's accurate to my purposes and greatest asset was when I upgraded my clubs and found in the new equipment technology (and some swing adjustments), I'd more power, distance and the G6 helped me re-examine my club choices on the home course. It's a great, no nonsense device for the regional and vacation courses I've taken it to play on, when I've not had a local to share the hints toward a better round. I'm still reliant more on my instincts than I am the technology, but I am glad I added it to my bag. It holds so many courses and updates as asked. It will track ones score, if desired, but doesn't bring in the newer devices "intrusions" of news blasts, texts or e-mail, leaving the point I hit the golf course intact. It is not cumbersome, in the sense that it may be clasped to ones garment, golf bag, or stuck in the cart for intermittent use (I use it in latter form), as it is about the size of a deck of cards, maybe a deck and a half thick without clip attached. As an older model, it faces the same issues many tech devices do in sunlight, the screen can be harder to see than were it backlit or developed similarly to an Amazon Kindle Paperwhite model e-reader.
The seller did a great job in meeting the order, sending it in original Garmin packaging secured in a secondary box, such that it couldn't be bounced around within the second box. It came with all the charging devices, and the full instruction manual. I was able to register it with Garmin, as a refurbished device, but it at least carried some protection and basis by which I can seek help, if need it. I had no reason to contact seller, they met, as do most of those I choose, if not Amazon itself, affiliated sellers. And my bottomline, even against a refurbished model sold by Amazon, was saved some of the pain that these inherently expensive devices can bring to the pocket. I'm sure I saved the expense of say one round as a guest at a swanky resort on either Carolina's many great courses at or near beach resorts! I'm pleased with the model, appreciate the fewer bells & whistles for the simplicity of operation and honestly, frequency with which I might doubt my gut on a "foreign" course re club selection and the reachable green, with the equally drawing hazard in front of it! Best time I like it? Perfect golf day conditions.

title: excellent DAC, nice alternative to the all-in-one gaming headset units when paired with a nice headset
text:
Amazing unit. Read several reviews (<3 Reddit lol) recommending this as a nice entry level DAC alternative to the 'gaming headset' setup. Currently paired with the Superlux HD668B headset. I'm by no means an audio professional, but I do love music and games, and sound is a huge part when playing/using my computer.
Clarity is amazing. No hissing or pop noises like your typical on-board sound devices. Volume scales amazingly well with no distortion or static like my old setup, so I can really crank the volume.

The only real downside, is that if you are looking for built-in surround sound decoding, there isn't any (Dolby, DTS, etc), so you are at the mercy of what software you are using to take over the surround sound generation, but most things do that already (games with a 'headset' option in the audio settings, etc). I'm not taking a star off for this, because I was expecting this when I purchased the product.

Highly recommend this unit if you want to break into the world of real audio instead of the pre-packaged 'gamerz' stuff. Your ears will thank you.

To long/didn't read:
good:
- Unit itself feels solidly built
- volume knob turns smoothly, feels like its a high quality component (no corners cut in production feeling to it)
- Sound is clean and clear
- Volume scales extremely well without distortion or static/noise
bad:
- no built in hardware surround decoder
- blue LED is really damn bright (enough to where i need to kind of block it to read the labels on the front)

title: Back up camera issues
text:
Honestly, this is a beautiful stereo, touch screen is perfect, sound is amazing. The only reason I'm giving it 3 stars is because it has issues with back up cameras. I hooked mine up so when I go in reverse the camera would pop up, and it does. After I shift gears it goes away but within 5 seconds it pops up and won't go away until you close it. Then it will keep popping up. I thought there was a setting for this but there isn't. After a full day of trouble shooting and browsing on the internet I figured out how to bypass it. Only issue is if I click the camera icon it resets back to the glitchy pop up problem and I have to bypass it again. For those that's have this issue, do this.
1) put car into reverse to bring up camera
2) on the camera screen click the X
3) go to camera settings and turn camera on and off.
4) make sure setting is on battery

This will fix the camera from constantly popping up. So when you go in reverse it pops up and when you switch gears it's gone. But be warned, if you want to view what's going on and click on the camera icon you will have to redo those steps. Otherwise it will stay put unless you reset the battery.

title: Good Display, setup is not always easy to figure
text:
I wrote a bad review earlier, turns out there is something called HDMI-Cec that can cause the TV to be controlled by one of the peripherals, even if there is no "connection"
I run all my HDMI through a receiver, so IT plays the sound, the picture source is selected from the receiver and goes to the OUT jack, so the TV only has one incoming connection.
The HDMI-CEC stuff is apparently on a command channel, or something, so even if the xbox is selected, and playing, the signal from the blu-ray will switch off the receiver source, and go "back" to the tv source I never had connected.
tl;dr
If your TV switches input, seemingly at random, try turning of this setting. (HDMI-CEC)

title: Battery capacity not matching up to advertised numbers, but Seller is A+++++ fantastic
text:
I have not had any interactions with this Seller. I think it was the actual manufacturer/factory's fault as far as this incorrect advertisement goes, and not that of the Seller. Now, I'm not a computer expert, but I do feel I know some things about computers and I'm willing to learn.

I am usually plugged in to the wall so batt life was not an issue, but I noticed that when I opened up the computer to do some dusting, the OEM battery was swollen to the point where the screws were overtight, and it was impacting on the motherboard -- HP says it's not going to blow up, but advises strongly to replace ASAP.

This is actually the 2nd of 2 batteries I bought off Amazon. I got the 1st battery from another vendor on Amazon, and I've had pretty much the exact same issue with both batteries being potentially mislabeled/misadvertised.

The original HP OEM battery's specs are: 41,000 mWh, 5150 mAh, 7.7 volts. These specs are what is advertised on the Amazon listing, and labeled physically on the battery.

To check the actual stats, I used the HP Support Asst, HP PC Hardware Diagnostics Windows, and a Battery Report generated in Win 10 through command prompt> powercfg /batteryreport.

After numerous calibrations and dis/charges (including uninstalling the Battery ACPI driver and removing the battery, etc) , I could only get to a max about 34,000 mWh (instead of 41,000) and ~4400 mAh (instead of 5150 mAh), and then it started degrading little by little bit -- since full dis/charges do degrade the battery life. Even if the battery was a lemon, the Design Capacity of the battery was factory capped at 4600 mAh instead of 5150, so the battery is not a 5150 mAh battery to begin with.

Actual battery life performance - it's hard to say because I am usually plugged in to the wall. But I do remember when I first got this computer, I was getting abotut 4 hours off the OEM battery, and with this battery, I'm getting about 2 hours. I do not really recall exactly if the load was different in the comparisons, and I might very well be walking in to this with a negative bias about the battery, but it does feel significantly shorter in battery life.

So after this 2nd battery from another Amazon vendor showing pretty much the exact same issues in every regard, I am thinking that most if not all of these sellers get their batteries from the same MFR/factory and just put different labels on it. I'm not blaming the Seller though.

So I figured that my only courses of action are to either:
1)try yet another Amazon vendor claiming OEM specs
2)actually pay up and buy an OEM HP battery
3)live with it.

I ended up getting tech support through Amazon, not really expecting much, but the Amazon rep did give me a partial rebate, which I'm willing to live with. So if you just need a battery replacement to tide you over, go ahead and get this battery, but would not expect OEM life/duration from this battery.

------edited 12-7-2018----
The seller has been absolutely fantastic in their communique, and I felt that their sincerity towards 100% customer support throughout has been exemplified with complete satisfaction on my end. Their email responses and queries were expedient and very supportive, and it was an utter pleasure to deal with this seller -- which is not an all too common experience with other Amazon sellers.

How amazing was this seller, you ask? Well, I have upgraded my star rating to a full 5 stars from 2 stars based upon my interaction with the SELLER. The seller has chosen to take a loss and refunded my purchase amount as well as sending me a 2nd battery in addition to the one that I already have; and coupled with the amazing communication, I can only say 2 thumbs up for this seller. The battery, despite it not lasting as long as the OEM, has been rock solid -- I have periodically measured battery life, voltage, mAh, mWh and temperatures for the past couple weeks, and it has been satisfactory. Thank you again, ANTIEE for your amazing customer support, and I would definitely choose you as the Amazon Seller, if you have the product that I wanted in the future, again and again.

At this moment I have a single AAA sitting in the 3rd bay and it is charging away.

So far I've only used an Anker 4 port USB charger plugged into an outlet to test it. Shortly I will see how well a couple of solar panels work. I have the Goal Zero 7.5 watt, but also a couple that are rated quite a bit higher, my current favorite being an X-Dragon 20 watt panel with two USB ports using PowersIQ technology.

4.13.2015

title: Good product with a finicky power switch.
text:
Title says it all.
The product works great as far as performance, I did not notice any problems viewing 3D content though these glasses.
The glasses are fairly light and comfortable to sit though a full movie without discomfort.
However, the process to charge and store this product could use some work.
There is a 2 color led (blue and red) that shows the status of power (blue) and charging (red).
The blue turns on and blinks at short intervals to show that the unit is on.
When charging, the red indicator come on and stays on till done charging.
The problem is that when you plug in the charger, the unit auto-powers on and the status can be hard to see as the red led light will overpower the blue "on" status light that blinks on occasionally. So if you do not long press to turn off the glasses while its charging, the glasses would complete charge and stop charging (over-charge IC?) and then proceed to drain itself with its plugged in and you end up with a dead glasses with you try to turn it on. And if you try to turn it off while its plugged in, the red light keeps you from checking right away if the blue light is on or off so you end up turning it on when its off and vice versa.
My best work-around for this is to make sure the unit is ON and then plugging it in, then long pressing to power off.
In future revision, just eliminating the auto-on function will solve All the issues this unit has on usage.
Ultimately, a good product if you can live with the charging quirk.
I paid full price for these glasses would not have any reservation of recommending this product in this price range, you would have to invest double or triple the price of these glasses to get something significantly better.
Once these current sets break or the battery starts degrading, I will purchase more but I may look for one without an auto-power on feature.

Feel free to ask any questions regarding this product in the comments.
Hope this helps you.

We recently added a new Ring, and all was working fine initially as the new device comes with a trail subscription for 30 days.

You can view LIVE video (which burns the battery down much quicker) and technically, if someone rings the doorbell, you can see the “current” video and use intercom with them. Per Ring’s settings, “current view” is within seconds of someone pressing ring. Which means if you didn’t immediately go to the app, the video becomes a “past footage” and without a subscription, not avaiable for view!

This is total BS and clearly designed to force you to pay for the subscription service. I am so disappointed with this company and attempt to extort money from customers. I’m feel duped out of $199 for a useless device! I’m abandoning Ring. Going to find an alternative.

title: Excellent camera for the cost, quality upgrade for integrated laptop webcam
text:
This is a very solid webcam for the price. I picked this up primarily to use for Skype; the person I talk to the most has a cochlear implant so high framerate video (to make reading lips easier) is a must. High resolution also helps. Typical laptop webcams are not really adequate so I decided to try something a little more robust.

First, build quality. Nothing too surprising here. The flexible clip is nice; I use a very thin TV as a monitor and had no trouble clipping this into place. The swivel ball could be a little tighter. As it is, the weight of the cable tends to drag the camera slightly out of alignment. A little bit of tape solved this problem for me. The USB cable is a good length and seems to be good quality. The camera housing itself is a lightweight plastic, and the lens also appears to be plastic. Not a big deal, but a lens cap or cover would have been nice for those who plan to carry this around. I imagine the lens cover will scratch easily. There is a blue LED indicating connectivity/functionality; unlike many exposed status LEDs this one seems to be behind a diffuser of some kind so it's a lot less visually distracting than most.

Next, ease of install. My Windows 7 installation picked this up right away and identified it as a web camera with integrated microphone. I tested the integrated microphone briefly with Skype, but decided to stick with the headset mic I have been using. Audio quality was fine, but I like to move around a bit so a headset mic give a bit more consistency. The video quality was subpar at first, and I was seriously concerned. However, installing the camera drivers allowed me to reduce the brightness compensation, which led to 30+fps video. My basement is not very brightly lit, but even without the brightness compensation I was able to get a good quality picture. My Skype friend was impressed with the quality over my laptop's integrated webcam. For fun I decided to try this out on a Linux (Lubuntu 16.04 LTS) laptop. Lubuntu picked it up right away as well. I did not experiment with it much on Lubuntu, so I don't know how well the webcam will function in that environment.

Finally, software. The included utility lets you record video at 30fps 720p. There are a couple compression options available, along with some settings bars for brightness, color contrast, and so on. Default format appears to be .avi. Definitely not professional level software but certainly usable for those looking to throw together a quick video for the family, etc. The utility also lets you take still images, which could be useful for someone out there (I don't have any need for this personally). The webcam came with an installation CD but I chose to download the software directly through the AUSDOM website, which was very easy to navigate.

Overall, this is a spectacular camera for the price. I have some minor complaints, but I would definitely recommend this as an inexpensive option for someone with slightly above-average needs in terms of video quality and framerate. I'm giving it five stars due to ease of use and quality across the board; there's nothing incredibly impressive or innovative here but the quality is above average, the software is solid, and the end result exceeds my expectations.

title: Firmware has matured, we're ready to roll now
text:
Update 12/7/18 - Ubiquiti has been great about pushing new firmware every few days with a ton of bug fixes in each release. Since the ~4.0 release, this AP has been rock solid and I'm comfortable recommending it now to anyone looking for a top of the line AP in small form factor. There are still a few quirks and limitations surrounding edge case features like wireless uplink but the core functionality of the AP works great and all my wireless devices have no trouble now getting and staying connected. If you have any devices that can take advantage of the 4x4 MIMO, the speeds you can achieve are incredible. I also want to reiterate how great the Ubiquiti engineering staff is. They are highly engaged on the support forums and are always looking for feedback on bugs and feature suggestions that are more often than not implemented sometimes days or weeks later. I'm really invested in this ecosystem and would recommend these products to anyone who has a solid networking background and likes to tinker.

I've been working on cutting my home network over to Ubiquiti gear and was excited to get my hands on the spiritual successor to the UAP-AC-PRO. I've read that Ubiquiti gear requires a fair amount of tinkering to get everything just right and I'd say that is a fair statement after wrestling with the nanoHD, USG and the USW switches. The nanoHD is apparently still in the early stages of firmware development and has a fair number of bugs and instability compared to the other APs in the fleet. I have had a hell of a time trying to keep my devices on the 5GHz band and found that the UBNT forums are flooded with users with the same issue. I've had to resort to loading up the latest beta firmware just to stabilize things, but it still isn't perfect. Support has been great so far, they really want to stabilize as quickly as possible but I cannot give this thing a thumbs up in its current state. If you are in a saturated RF environment, I'd recommend you stick with the stable UAP-AC-PRO for now and give the nanoHD some more time to cook.

title: As a gamer I am very happy with this upgrade.
text:
I am very happy with this GPU. I upgraded from an AMD R7 200 series card, because of difficulty playing TSW, Elite:Dangerous and using the Oculus Rift DK2.

Upon opening the box I joked that EVGA had mistakenly sent me a small motherboard instead of a GPU. It is massive compared to my old AMD R7.

Installation: You will need space for this beast, look at the photo included to get an idea of the size. Once I made room I had no difficulties getting the GPU to seat in the PCI connector, I did find the power connection difficult. So difficult that I removed the GPU, and spent a few minutes trying to figure out why it would not seat, I finally finessed the power input into the socket with some force. Reseated the GPU and was good to go. The GPU comes with a CD with the Drivers on it, plus overclocking software.
(It is recommended that you register the GPU before the installation since the S/N can only be found on the bottom of the GPU)

Playing Elite Dangerous is like night and day. Where I struggled on low/mid graphics with the R7, the 960 plays on high settings, and putting on the Oculus Rift was stunning. I am now finally able to appreciate the power of VR, Oculus needs to hurry up with the 4k consumer version it will be a must have.

The Secret World is a whole new game with the visuals maxed out, a whole new game.

There is nothing worse than a gamer with a sub-par rig, and after extensive research over a few days I chose the 960 and a EVGA Supernova 750W G2 power supply to fuel the beast. I am very happy that I did.

The GPU is not that noisy, if you have ever had a high speed hard drive it is comparable to that, and yet to have had any heat issues, which I felt might be a concern because the massive size.

I am also much happier with NVIDIA's control center, I found AMD's Catalyst to be annoying.

Not sure what else to say but, I am a happy gamer!
