title: Nice cover
text:
Comparing the actual case to the picture I can see why some people have been disappointed. It's not that the quality is bad, it's just that the leather finish is different than what people might expect. From the picture you might expect a cover of something like marbled leather underneath a delicate satin sheen. What you get, however, is entirely different but beautiful in it's own right. You get soft, wonderful smelling leather in a finish that looks vintage almost as soon as you remove it from the case. Yes, it shows scratches, but yes, they can be buffed out. The leather felt a little dry when I first got it, but an application of Bickmore Bick 4 helped moisten things up a bit. Further applications might be even more beneficial. My Kindle has been banging around in my backpack for a week now, and for the first time today, the leather had more scratches than I really wanted. A quick once-over with a horsehair brush brought things back under control. Frankly, however, we both know that I'm not going to keep brushing this case. After the novelty wears off, I'll just leave it alone and let it do the whole patina thing.
Functionally, the cover works great. The Kindle sits in the case very securely, and it puts the Kindle to sleep and wakes it as promised. The inside of front cover feels like some kind of sturdy fabric, and it feels good and natural in the hand. I haven't noticed any hand-sweat.
I like this case. It looks rugged and interesting, like a courier's satchel or something. I'm willing to accept the argument that it may strike some as a particularly masculine cover, but I think it would appeal to both sexes if they understand what they're getting. They're not getting buttery leather, they're getting earthy leather--if that makes any sense.
Here are some pics.

title: It is a very good card. (Real world experience review)
text:
I mostly got this version because I love Nvidia's Reference Design for their cards and it was out of the box OC, and can still be pushed even more. It is a $500 dollar GPU. When it comes to PCs money literally buys performance. Especially in terms of CPU and GPU. So it performs amazingly in everything I have played.

My PC Hardware:
CPU: i7-4790k.
GPU: This one?.
RAM: Kingston HyperX 2x4GB.
SSD: Samsung 850 EVO 120GB for Operating System (Win 10 64bit) and Apps.
HDD: 1TB Western Digital Green for games (and videos I record).

Call Of Duty: Advanced Warfare; This game runs amazingly at max settings excluding super sampling. There does not seem to be a noticeable difference with super sampling on. I see about 90FPS all the time during gameplay no matter what is going on in Campaign. In multiplayer the framerate is well over 100FPS with now stutter or slowdown.

Skyrim; The game destroys skyrim. Okay that is expected. BUT it also runs rock solid 60FPS with ENB mod and Many many other graphical and physics mods active. The only Mods that hurt the framerate are those ridiculous grass mods. That drops the FPS around 40 sometimes which is a bit disorienting when in combat. Other than that it will handle any mod you throw at it with ease as far as I have seen.

Tomb Raider (2013); Runs 60 FPS MAX with 2xSSAA (4xSSAA is just weirdly demanding. There is still plenty of VRAM left, system RAM, and I have a i7-4790k so i seriously do not understand what the problem is with 4xSSAA). The only time the game drops frames is during cutscenes when the camera gets close to Lara's Hair when TressFX is on. Other than that I have played through the entire game and noticed no other performance problems. You can check out a video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NP5C6aYIkik You will notice the only time it drops frames is when the camera gets close to her hair.

Firestrike Demo: Scored 14,214 for Graphics Score. 11,895 for Overall Score. (Better than 87% of results it says)

Now I do not know the power draw and all of those super specific kind of things but it only has 2 6pin power connectors which should tell you it is very power efficient for how powerful it is.

The default fan profile is really quite and keeps the card from killing itself (along with throttling back).

My card boost up to 1380MHz after GPU Boost 2.0 does its thing. I have tried lightly overclocking the card's GPU which worked fine but caused coil whine. I fixed the coil whine by setting the card back to default values then simply stressing it out with games and benchmarks for a little while. That method has worked for me but I would caution against OC the card further. I have since left my card at stock. (I will probably overclock it again anyway, I am weird like that lol).

I tried bumping the RAM speed up a little. All i can see for this is do not do it lol. I do not know why but my card threw a fit and the graphics driver crashed. A LOT of reviewers of the base model 980 and all the 3rd party derivatives bumped the RAM speed up to a woping 7010MHz (10 from the base 7000MHz) and left it there. This card as you probably saw in the specs list Some said it was because of the way that power is allocated on this series (900) cards that OC the ram would take power away from the core so they just put all the OC effort into the Core. I think it is for a different reason but again I cannot be for sure.

The moral of the story is this card can handle pretty much anything @1080p you can throw at it. And it looks nice....really nice. It is pretty. It is quite at base fan profile like all the other cards with this cooler. If you have the money for this and not the 980ti/Fury X i would recommend it.

text:
For those looking for a space saving sound bar & subwoofer with good sound quality, this could be for you.

My wife & I were looking to ditch the larger subwoofer we had, and upgrade our the sound system connected to our Samsung Smart TV. We have a small space, so this looked promising. Some of the other reviews mentioned the lack of a volume level indication was a turn off for them, but I didn't find that to be a big deal. This is system is not going to give you Bose level sound quality or the bass from a 300w sub. This is a compact system with a space saving design that packs enough low end to satisfy most people. It's not going to shake your walls or rattle your windows, but it's going to give you good quality sound with enough low end to let you enjoy the big explosions in movies.

The one downside I think we can all agree on is the price! Geez! The current price of $349 is a huge turn off. I think $199-$249 is much more reasonable. I bought a repackaged system with some slight dings and scrapes for much less, and I'm happy with the purchase.

title: SEE UPDATE! Do Not Buy! Better sound quality than I expected, but gets 6 hours of battery life. Sometimes the audio will drop
text:
UPDATE 9/27/16:

This unit has stopped working after less than a month. It no longer connects to any of my devices. Do not buy this.

Below the line is my original review:

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I bought this product because I wanted to be able to use my existing in ear headphones that I really like while being able to have my phone not directly attached. I'm ultimately really conflicted about this thing. On one hand, some things that it does really impress me. On the other hand, a couple things that it does really annoy me.

Things I like:

- Pretty easy to pair and get set up working on the first time. 9/10 times it will pair automatically after the first setup.
- Smaller than I expected. I expected it to be 2-3 inches big. It is actually much smaller. I've included some photos with a size comparison to an american quarter with this review.

- It is easy for me to control my media with the buttons. I wear this clipped to my pants, and I don't have to dig around for my phone to pause what I am listening to, which is nice.

- MOST OF THE TIME the audio quality is actually much better than I expected from bluetooth audio. I planned to use this mainly to listen to podcasts while I was walking around the city. You don't need super high quality audio for podcasts. My previous experiences with bluetooth audio and music were bad, but I was actually surprised to find that the sound quality that this thing provides was pretty good for music too. It's not as good as directly plugging your headphones in to a source, but I don't mind it too much.

- The Battery level is displayed on my phone up by the bluetooth icon. I've never seen this before, it's pretty useful. I use this on iOS, but I assume android has something similar. I've included a screen shot to show what I mean.

Things that I don't like:

- When I said above that 9/10 times it will pair automatically above, that is because 1/10 times it will forget it was ever paired and I will need to go in and re-do the pairing.

- When I said that MOST OF THE TIME the audio was better than I expected, it was because sometimes the audio stream will become interrupted and really jumbled for about 20 seconds. If I am listening to a podcast that means I have to skip back and re-listen to that portion. This happens 2-3 times an hour.

- I've run the battery from full to totally empty twice now by just constantly playing music until it stops. I do this test using externally powered speakers so there is no load on this device to drive any headphones or passive speakers. Doing this on 50% volume, the battery lasts 8 hours, not 10. This is under the best optimal circumstances. It's battery life is worse in the real world when driving headphones, and I may get between 6-7 hours. There is no way that this thing gets 10 hours of battery life.

- When this does get low on battery, it beeps at you every minute. This means that for the last hour of audio you get three beeps every minute or two. What were they thinking! This is really annoying.

Overall: This thing has better sound quality than I ever expected, and does make listening to audio on the go more convenient in general, but it has some issues with staying paired and the audio stream occasionally getting interrupted for 20-30 second spans. Additionally, it does not get 10 hours of battery life in the real world, more like 6-7, maybe 8 if your earbuds take low power to drive and you are under ideal circumstances.

I've included some photos of the device with an american quarter for size reference. I've also included a screen shot of my podcast player when connected to this device, to show off how the phone shows the bluetooth devices battery level.

title: but that is the best you can do
text:
Consider the reference; that would be no outlet, and the romex wired directly to the board from the source. Impractical, but that is the best you can do. That beats any outlet. What these high end outlets do, is try to recreate a solid wire again. They help to drastically reduce the effect of pour contacts and riveted thin brass, and the current limiting that accompanies them. The goal is to make it seem that there is no contact there at all. The goal is to help eliminate any current limiting or arching (that builds up carbon , and to spread the contact area. .also making the surface as conductive as possible. . That is why each outlet seems to have it's own sound signature. . Contact resistance and current flow ( esp. power peaks) are related, as well as the conductivity of the metals. It doesn't do a lot of good to get a great outlet that can't exert enough gripping power on the blade however.. Most hi end ones do.

I like this outlet, but found the Maestro to be better. It is simple copper ( maybe not so simple), which is considered too malleable to use without something to help stiffen it. I am not sure what they do for that. Be that as it may, the maestro is fuller, has more punch, is more atmospheric, and creates a more robust sounding dialog. It is a simple looking brown outlet.

For any connector it is always necessary to clean them once in a while. You may think it doesn't matter, until you do it. I have found that flux remover spray is really good at cleaning contacts.

I was able to do a quick A-B test to help eliminate the subjective nature of listening to anything. . Hope this helps.

I bought a two terabyte drive and it comes with a free copy of acronis True Image which is a program that clones your old drive to your new one. I'm absolutely serious that with nearly a terabyte of information on my drive I was up and running in a couple of days. All you have to do is plug in the new drive and install the software and everything happens for you. Once the transfer is complete you literally plug in the new Drive where your old one was and it's like you've got a brand new computer. Saved me a couple of thousand dollars on a new unit and I couldn't be happier. If you knew all the aforementioned information about SSD drives... My apologies for the long review, this is an excellent product made by the best company in my opinion who makes drives these days. You can't go wrong with crucial.

title: I KNOW WHY YOUR SPEAKERS WON'T WORK PROPERLY!
text:
After 2 years 7 months, (it is now January 2019) I now know why myself, and virtually everybody else, has ever had trouble with the LG Music Flow system. It comes down to one simple word... BANDWIDTH!

If you do not provide this system with the amount of bandwidth it requires to work properly, it simply WILL NOT WORK PROPERLY.

The speakers will drop connection. The app will lose sight of the speakers, and it will all frustrate you to no end.

Then, you won't understand why you keep having so many problems, you'll get angry, and you'll write a bad review when, 99 chances out of 100, it's your fault because there are too many devices, pulling too much bandwidth, on your network. The speakers won't have the bandwidth they require, resulting in connectivity issues.

I have 14 Music Flow speakers in my home, the maximum amount the app can recognize.
I have a 200/20 Mbps internet package.
I can run any combination of 8 of my 14 speakers at one time and 1 phone, running the app to control them, and that's it!
Any more on the network than that, and I begin having connectivity issues.
If I stick to that, they run flawlessly for hours and hours and hours. The rest of my Music Flow speakers MUST BE TURNED OFF (solid red light), nothing else can be on the network, and I get music to play all over my house, and in the garage, with ZERO issues.

I would suggest taking all connected devices off your network except a phone, running the Music Flow app. Turn off all Music Flow speakers. Then, turn on your Ethernet connected speaker and follow the instructions for resetting that speakers connection back to factory settings (Google it). Reconnect that speaker. If the app says the speaker needs to update it's firmware, update that speaker before moving on to the next speaker. Once that is all done, test the speaker (play music with the app) to ensure it's working properly. Once confirmed, turn the next speaker in the system on, and repeat this process until all speakers are connected. Listen to them and test them to see if they magically work properly. After that, reconnect all of your other devices to your network and see if you don't immediately begin having connectivity issues again. If you do, you'll know beyond doubt that your network is over taxed and that the LG Music Flow system does, in fact, work as advertised.

I hope this helps. Cheers and happy listening.

text:
Isn't it ironic, don't you think?

Drive started failing the 2nd day and it's supposed to be the back-up! I don't know if the fact it was shipped in an envelope had anything to do with it, but after backing up my family's photos to this drive, it started whining and clicking incessantly- even directly plugged in (so I know it's getting enough power). I printed my return label and went to erase the drive. I couldn't erase it despite multiple attempts- the drive would even fail to unmount! I ran a disk repair utility and was finally able to erase the drive, but it's still going back, and hopefully the replacement will be better...

I just got a condescending message from tech support about formatting the drive to Mac OS Extended... but I went to reply here and it's missing. Methinks someone realized that wasn't a good response given the nature of my complaint and took it down. Kudos! I'll raise my stars when the replacement is up and running... and yes, I had properly formatted the drive. I was alarmed from the get-go at how noisy it was compared to the same type 2TB drive I already am using. More-so when photos wouldn't open or were partially displaying half an image and half black field after several seconds of trying to open and making screeching noises. I simply want to format a 4TB drive and run it as a back up for my 2TB on my home network, and then move it to a home cloud system as the primary, and eventually get another to run as it's back-up... I'm not an IT professional, but I think I can handle this much since I've been comfortable tinkering with these new-fangled high tech abicuses since the early 80s when 64k was something...Lol.

The sound quality is great, not quite as good as my Bose Soundlink and Sound Blaster Roar 2 speakers. But then the Bose is less versatile with no TF card support and much more expensive. The Roar 2 has TF support and richer sound but it is bulkier. I believe the TF card is a “must” for modern speakers. Imagine you can store your entire music library onto a tiny card and play the songs at random or continuously for hours and hours. How could Bose, UE, JBL and Sony have missed it? title: Great compact enclosure. As fast as your SATA SSD allows.
text:
I recently decommissioned a SATA SSD from my machine. The drive has plenty of life still in it, so I decided to replace the myriad USB thumb drives I have lying around for one large and fast SSD that I can move around. I went with the INEO Model C2561c to "future proof" a bit with it's USB C Gen 2 interface. I opened the case, slid my SSD, put the screws and the rubber cover with the branding. After deleting old partitions and a quick format, it has worked flawlessly on every device I've plugged it into. The SSD in it is a SATA 6 drive and it reads and writes as fast as the USB Gen 1 port on my PC allows. I checked and the chipset on the device is a VIA VL716 (my cellphone camera can't zoom in that close, so I couldn't get a picture of it). The enclosure has a blue LED next to the USB C port which emits a healthy blue light when the drive is in use. The aluminum finish feels durable and it isn't a fingerprint magnet.

My only complaint is that the included USB C cable is a bit too stiff and too short for my tastes. Also, I would have liked a USB C to USB A cable (the way I'm currently using it). Finally, the box comes with a little screwdriver for the tiny screws you use to secure the aluminum enclosure to the internal caddy. Very handy. I may snag another one for the missus.

I read other reviews mentioning that the foam pad may not be up to the task, but I didn't notice the drive would rattle unless I use it as a maraca. It should keep things steady in there.

title: Solid bag for lots of stuff - but doesn't last.
text:
We are getting ready for international travel, so it was important that I find a bag that can handle all of our gear. We take a lot of photos and videos, so I knew we would need space. I looked a few bags, and ended up buying this one, because it looks less like a pro-photography bag and more normal. It also claimed to be able to fit a 15" Macbook, which it actually does! (I have a mid 2012 Macbook, so it is thicker plus a hard shell case and it still fit!) I'll attach pictures of what does fit, and what does not, so you have an idea.

Pros:
- Fits a lot of stuff.
- Fits my 15" (older) Macbook Pro.
- Fits my iPad Pro with Incase Origami sleeve (with the macbook).
- Everything is snug, very little movement.
- Looks great.
- Pads seem sturdy and cushiony. Very customizable.
- Top pocket makes pulling film out easy at airports.
- Very top of the pack lets you easily pull out camera if wanted.

Cons:
- Side pocket does not fit water bottle.
- Still bulky.
- Doesn't seem very secure. It would be hard to lock the zippers.
- Straps aren't terribly comfortable. (May break in with age?)

I chose to fit in 3 camera bodies, which meant I didn't have room for a flash. But as you can see in the pictures, there was plenty of room for other stuff! I will try to update this review after using it for a while.

UPDATE:

I took this bag on a weekend trip to NYC and then for a 3 week trip to Europe. It was my carry on bag for the flight since it held so much stuff. It fit under the seat in front of me, so I was happy about that, but it was hard to get anything out of it mid flight, since the front pocket is so deep.
Halfway through our Europe trip the seems started to come out near the top of the strap (see photos). I also had a seem inside of the bag come loose. This tells me the bag isn't put together all that well. That was pretty disappointing to me, since I have other Incase stuff I love. I carried the bag around during the day and it was nice to have the Rainfly cover. The straps didn't hold their length and so the bag slowly crept down my back during the day, which was really annoying and eventually I think this took a toll on my back.

The bag looks good, but in the end, you will have to decide between packing it to the max and short lifespan, or long lifespan and never packing it too much. I might try to contact Incase to see if they will replace it.

title: BT Receiver, Dual DACs, Headphone Amp, USB playback & 3.5mm/2.5mm balanced jack! nooo....WAY!?!
text:
I finally broke down bought this after reading all the great reviews while searching for a better listening experience than provided by the cheap BT receivers i bought before this. Granted, the cheaper Bluetooth receivers are adequate if price is the ultimate factor and if you don't have high sensitivity IEM's! But, if you're anything like me whose just starting to dip your toe into the vast waters of the IEM/headphone audio world then those cheap BT receivers will ultimately leave you wanting.

I'm not an audiophile by any stretch of the imagination but honestly once you move past the cheap earbuds you get free with any happy-meal then you'll want a device that can actually power them. My main two issues with the cheap BT receivers are the noise and volume level control. With the higher sensitivity IEM's the noise at lower volumes is so pronounced that it just ruins the listening experience and when you try to adjust the volume up enough to drown it out; the lack of granularity of the volume control forces you to listen at too high a volume for your comfort.

Looking for a device to combat those issues I read up on the FiiO BTR1 and uBTR and these seemed like a good/cheap alternatives but a few reviewers cited hearing some hiss at lower volumes so that ruled out those two options. This lead to me doing some more research and finding the ES100 head-fi forum where it seemed like most people who've used it loved it and praised the support the product was getting.

Now that I've had the ES100 for a few weeks i can say that the positive reviews are warranted. The features this device provides are just fantastic; now add in the phone app on top of everything and the ES100 definitely earns it's keep! The noise issue at low volumes is nonexistent with the ES100 plus it also provides analog volume controls so I can always find the right volume level for my comfort no matter what environment I'm in (with the newest firmware update giving even greater control than before). The phone app makes tailoring the listening experience so much easier with the wealth of options it provides and really sets itself apart from other similar devices.

I will agree with other reviewers and say that the only "tiny" flaw the device has is the hardware. I don't necessarily have an issue with the plasticy build quality but more in button feel and usability. The buttons are small and you wont get much tactile feel or feedback for them so using it requires more concentration.

All in all I think Radsone has done a great job with this device and with FiiO releasing the BTR3 soon I think trying to find a high quality reasonably priced BT receiver will become that much easier.

title: Good, not spectacular
text:
Overall, these are nice earbuds, They look good, with even finishes and coloring. The brown is kind of a deep metallic bronze to me. The included eartips are a comfortable silicone. They reproduce voice and music without a lot of bass very well at low and mid volumes. Country, acapella, jazz, 80's pop and light rock sound good. Rap, modern bass-heavy pop and rock not so well. They work well watching video, though if the bass kicks in hard, like during an explosion, they get overwhelmed. That's where the sound quality falls flat – the bass. I have earbuds that cost half the price of these that handle bass better. Those are uglier, if that matters to you.

They do not come with any kind of carrying case or bag. I'm getting kind of spoiled, I guess, but I expect at least a soft bag at this price point. They do come with 3 sizes of eartips, so you don't have a replacement if your size gets damaged. It is nice that they have a flat cord which does seem to help with the dreaded self-knotting phenomenon. And they at least have a gold-colored plug.

I do not use microphones (haven't even talked on my phone for over a month) so I cannot comment on the quality of that.

You can see in the pictures that the ends of the buds have a grill. These are functional, which kinda surprised me. If you block them, the bass drops even lower and the “soundstage” diminishes. Can't see how they would be blocked in normal usage.

If you listen to audiobooks while commuting or to music that is less bass-intensive, these are a good match. If you like heavy bass, others do it better.

I did receive these at a discount -not free- for a review. I depend on reviews for my purchases and always give my honest opinion.

title: EDM Kings!
text:
(picture: magni 2 / modi 2 amp/dac stack) I listen to mostly trap, and some other types of EDM and with a proper amp, these things really come to life. I have DT770's 80ohm and the difference is night and day. These will literally vibrate your earlobes. They CAN run from a computer or phone, but the difference with a proper amp is remarkable; everything comes to life.

You'll see people say "the bass hit in my beats is so awesome" and while any headphone can hit lower frequencies and make wubs in your ears, can they do it while maintaining the highs and not having the bass step all over the mids? I never realized what the audiophiles were on about, until I compared these side by side with Sennheiser 598's, AudioTechnica M50x, DT770 80ohm, and a friends pair of Beats Pro Studio (or whatever they were called). If you have a pair of headphones and you are satisfied, that's perfectly fine, but when you step into the realm of high end headphones, all the low and mid end ones you had before will sound like tin cans or sloppy bass cannons. I actually played the same song and would switch the headphones as it played, and the difference is astounding.

Unfortunately, I paid a lot more than these are listing for now, which is sad because it was an obvious money grab. I'm still happy though, and I've found the BEST HEADPHONES FOR EDM. Period.

Note: You'll know when a track is low bitrate, it'll make you want to claw your ears in disgust.

title: Best tablet I've ever owned (beats Nexus devices and ipads)
text:
As I previous Nexus 7 owner, both 2012 and 2013, as I was worried about going to a Touch Wiz (software) Samsung tablet, however, put all those worries aside as this tablet easily beats the Nexus.
PRO's:
1. Screen - best looking colors, resolution of any tablet out there. As stated earlier I have had two Nexus 7s and one Nexus 9, wife has an iPad Mini and none of them can touch it.
2. Weight - another area this tablet is best in class, so lightweight using with one hand is not a problem. Loved my Nexus 7 for portability and afraid I would lose that going to a bigger tablet while the Nexus 9 and iPad Mini are square and hard to carry, this 8.4" screen feels like the perfect size and balance.
3. Sound - purchased the Nexus 9 because of two front facing speakers but cannot tell a difference with Samsung placing a speaker on each end, much better sounding than Nexus 7s with speakers on the back.

CON's:
1. Appearance - call me simple but I love a solid black or white device with matching accents (Nexus) or metallic aluminum (Apple) but Samsung wrapped this in a bronze band, both the tablet, camera and home button. Definitley not my favorite but I guess its personal opinion and I put mine in an Otterbox.
2. Software - main reason that I loved my Nexus was the software updates and that doesn't happen with Samsung. Then they put Touch Wiz on top of that and it causes some lag. Not enough to complain but enough to notice.

OVERALL:
This is my favorite tablet I have ever owned, as the size is perfect for one handed operation and portability, plus, the 16:10 screen ratio is perfect for watching movies. Speakers are easy to hear and have good sound quality. And Samsung does great job at matching and beating Apple at every element if the game: screen resolution, weight and build quality. Only reason it doesn't get five stars is the color options.

Another reason I prefer this over Nexus devices is the case options as I have a four year old and Google's cases are a joke, the flip classes for 7 and magic case for the Nexus 9. Otterbox does add weight but its strong, semi-sleek and covers the bronze edges of the tablet.

title: Excellent Headphones, Not Worth Upgrading from Zik 2.0
text:
I settled on the pair of Zik 2.0 headphones I own now after trying out a bunch of different active noise-cancelling bluetooth headphones, most notably the Sennheiser Momentum 2.0. The noise cancelling in the Ziks cannot be beat (even against the wired Bose QC25), the headphones are very comfortable for even extended use, and the sound is well balanced but still gives good bass when wanted. The only real downside I have found is the battery life; bluetooth with noise cancelling gets you 6 to 7 hours at most. I use mine in the office almost exclusively so it's not a real problem for me, and if it was I could buy spare batteries and an off-brand wall charger that would charge them, and just swap out when they die.

The Zik 3.0 is a worthy successor to the 2.0, adding in 32-bit processing and the ability to charge wirelessly with any Qi-compatible charger. As of the time of this review Parrot hasn't released their own charger, so I've not been able to try it. As far as looks, feel, battery life, and sound - I wasn't really able to tell any difference between the 2.0 and the 3.0. The 3.0 did feel tighter on my head, but that could be from comparing a few-month-old pair of 2.0 to a brand new 3.0. I think the ear cups are ever so slightly thinner on the 3.0 than the 2.0, but I don't think that really matters on these since I wouldn't describe the 2.0 as 'bulky'. The only real difference physically I noted was the power button. The button on the 2.0 is convex and has a low press force, which means that if I'm not paying attention I can accidentally turn them off when taking them off my head to put around my neck (when I need to talk to someone for instance). The button on the 3.0 is in the same place, but concave and has a much higher press force and a better tactile feel - I don't think I could accidentally activate this button.

All of that said, while the wireless charging is neat, I don't feel upgrading to the 3.0 if you already have the 2.0 is worth it unless you really want the wireless charging or USB audio features, or have money floating around begging to be spent. But if you don't already have a pair of Ziks, I wouldn't look any further! You can get the 3.0 to have the latest and greatest, or get a discounted new pair of 2.0 (for a short while at least)!

title: A multi-purpose speaker system
text:
I initially intended for the Toshiba 2.1 Channel Soundbar to be used for the guestroom television. Included were all of the cables to make this work, and the sound was more than adequate for that purpose, especially for action movies. The set-up consists of a soundbar and a subwoofer. The sound was balanced, the subwoofer delivered, and overall, I was satisfied with this set-up. My husband, on the other hand, pointed out that this set-up didn’t utilize a very attractive aspect of this speaker system--the Bluetooth capability. I then tried it on my desktop, where I often watch movies, and was pleased at how well it sounded, using Bluetooth technology.

The soundbar itself was rather long for the desk, at 32”, even with a 27” display, but I made it work. It paired easily with the desktop. I’ve also experimented with this speaker set-up in the garage while working, and my husband used it to play his bass guitar to YouTube videos. It pairs easily to iPod, iPhone, and iPad. It’s fairly portable and light.

While it will never replace my 7.1 surround sound set-up in my living room, this Toshiba sound system would provide decent sound for an apartment, computer, or a guestroom television. Many newer televisions come equipped now with Bluetooth technology. Is it exceptional sounding? Not really, but it does earn a 4 star rating in my book for sound, and versatility for use. As stated, it does include the cables to fit almost every need, including an HDMI port. For this price, I think it is fairly priced.

I keep it in the recommended Nupro case and haven't had any problems so far. I mostly use it with the Box app to read PDFs for work and the quality of the display is pretty good, even with crappy copies from books. You just have to email your Kindle address with PDFs attached if you want them downloaded on your device for use when you're not in Wifi range, and usually won't have the text-flow options that eBooks use so you'll have to zoom in to get the text the size you want (about the same as reading attachments on an iPhone or something). title: Pro's: Small and Loud Decent Bass  Con's Harsh sound as volume gets loud Not warm at all,has distortion Needs Eq to sound best.
text:
This is an email I sent to Cambrige in regards to my concerns about device I am posting it because it is essentially a review

***BEGINNING OF EMAIL***
As you can see from [the order] I ordered both the angle 2 and 3 [OA2 and OA3] . The OA2 i got for my neighbor. I am having an issues with the angle 3 to give background information I am a Dj, and audio producer so I am well versed in the many variables of sound quality .

I am getting distortion from the angle 3. I first noticed when compare the sound quality between the OA2 and OA3. The OA2 has a much more accurate [sound] which is also a very warm natural playback while the OA3 an exaggerated top end, its almost as if there is an internal hi freq boost from about 3.1k to 14k. to increase perceived loudness. I have compensated this by lowering the frequency in these bands in a custom eq i set on my phone which greatly improves the accuracy of the playback and lessens the harshness but does not do anything for the distortion.
Its almost as there is harmonic distortion being created by the amplifer. I'm presuming its from the amp that is causing the distortion, as I noticed this under all conditions but more so when played louder and/or under certain conditions:
1] female vocals [Eryca Badu Jill Scot] this is very noticeable when comparing to the OA2. the OA2 is warm and smooth while the OA3 has a raspy scratchy distortion over the vocals this is noticeable even when the volume is relatively low. The other time it is very noticeable is A bass guitar playing around 100hz-300hz[including the guitar harmonics its probably about 300hz-900hz [well with in range of this device] These notes creates a very noticeable buzzing overdrive distortion sound when playing from a medium volume and up[The song was Flashing lights by BBNG] this song is the most noticeable because the bass guitar is a solo at the beginning of the track so you can pin point that this is not from any other instrument in the track . Its even more noticeable because on this track the only variable is the volume : if your playing it medium low there relativity no distortion but when playing it medium to medium high the distortion increases rapidly. the distortion is defintily an issue. To rule some out variables all critical testing has been with high quality 320kbps tracks and have been tested on both the OA3 and OA2. . . and this fault only occurs on the OA3 plus for reference I routinely play these same tracks from the same source on my mains which are are set of Professional Mackie C300's which are of studio reference quality . Im kind of torn between the OA2 and OA3,
OA2 Pro:s super warm, accurate smooth flat sound response excellent [no eq needed], battery life Cons Not as loud and its bigger
OA3 Pro's: small and loud [extra head room for low tracks] Con's Not warm at all, has artificially boosted high end frequency[not a flat accurate response], further all the high end makes it sound very harsh ,plus horrible distortion as the volume gets louder.

Of all these these comments I have made here, most of them seem to be by design for a superficial perceived increase in volume except for this distortion which seems to an amplifier issue and/or potentially a driver issue. Im looking forward to doing a youtube review on this item

Note when reading through the reviews there other people who report these same faults/issues [distortion/unnatural high end frequency] which makes me wonder is this all units or just certain ones.
Many Thanks
Mike Rivera
Any assistance would be greatly appreciated
***END OF EMAIL***

I WOULD HAVE GIVEN THIS A 5 if it weren't for the superficial exaggerated high end and the distortion, besides these 2 things I really really love it. Hopefully Cambridge will resolve this issue. To every body considering this device if your not an audiophile you probably will not notice what i am talking about BUT if you have an ear for quality these defects are annoyingly noticeable! Especially when comparing it to the older cheaper Oontz angle plus [2]. which is only 22 dollars and has a 15 hour battery life

NOTE IF you want to EQ this for better sound , you want drop 3.1khz by-5db 8khz by -3db and 14k by -3db when you do this it sounds almost as warm as the OA2 except it still has the distortion on certain tracks . the Distortion may be a defect so I am awaiting cambridges response ,

text: I bought these for a speaker upgrade for my 2016 Jeep Wrangler Soundbar. They were somewhat frustrating at first as these did not come with any mounting hardware. Leading me to believe that somehow They simply used the existing bolts from the jeep to attache the speaker to the bracket. They do not. I called up Crutchfield, When you purchase these from crutchield electronics, They do include a bag of assorted mounting nuts, bots, screws etc to fit your any speaker and they are about 5-8 dollars more expensive. This what this package was missing! After a quick trip to hardware store I got #6 3/4in flat head machine screws and bolts for 18 cents each. Attached my Kicker Cs65s to the Bracket then the Bracket tabs line up perfectly to the 3 Mounting points on the sound bar. Little hint, When removing the old speaker, be aware of where the LONGER tab of the 3 tabs is. For the jeep sound bar, it should be the one closest to the tweeter. When installing this bracket put the LONGER tab in that same spot for a perfect fit. Apply some foam tape behind the bracket and in between the speaker and bracket for I nice fit to prevent bass rattle. I'm giving a 4 simply due to no bolts, or instructions in this packet. AMAZING!

I'd buy it again. If you want better graphics and audio, just upgrade. But out of the box, for the price, I find this an unquestionable winner. Win10 OS, very good processor, plenty of RAM, fast hard-drive... it's a great PC for home & office use. title: After seeing good reviews on this antenna
text: After seeing good reviews on this antenna, I decided to go ahead with the purchase in which I now regret.  I and at least three other people have found this antenna unusable for the CB (11 meter) band. The box my antenna came in had MAX2000 printed on it instead of the usual IMAX 2000.I don't know if this is because of a design change or not, but it is something that all should be aware of. I have done extensive testing on this antenna and cannot even come close to proper tuning in the 11 meter band. The tuning rings had little to no effect at 11 meters with SWR in the range of 1.6 to 2 but did improve above 28 MHz. title: The best indoor antenna and I've tried about 7, better than the flat ones in my experience.
text: I use this pointing towards window sitting on bookcase, along with a 1byone High Gain amplifier or the Mohu Jolt. This is the best antenna I have tried and I tried several. It definitely beats the flat ones. If you are far from the towers, doing it outside is the best a directional one. What makes this one good is the piece in the back is a reflector so any signal you are lacking is reflects back into antenna. I got the output of this antenna going into the amp which is plugged into a wall the output of amp goes into back of 2 way splitter in wall. I bought a wall plate with 2 coax connections and splitter is inside there. The input from amp goes in to wall where it hits splitter and 1 leg of splitter comes out the other coax port which leads to TV in living room where antenna is. The 2nd leg of splitter goes to my bedroom. The coax coming into the house from provider (cable internet only) I use direct into my modem so if you do something similar try not to cross the signals, just adds more noise. For indoor and you are in suburb this is THE BEST ANTENNA! take it from me. If outdoor and everything is 55+ miles plus and you're in the hills get yourself a good triple element outdoor antenna with a pre-amp! quad shielded coax the whole 9 yards. title: Tested 250 batteries -- 15-20% were had still 80%+ capacity
text:
PROS: Accurate testing of most all common batteries under load. Tests confirmed with high-end instruments with loading. Of the 80%, 40% of those had 100% capacity remaining. Most all tested were famous brands, but other brands as well. After testing ~250 batteries, the 4 AAA batteries in the mini were tested as having 80% capacity remaining. The unit checks available voltage automatically, but still operated at 80%. ~100 were dead.

What I like in addition to the form factor etc is its use as I replace batteries. Often I throw out the entire lot from an appliance when there is useful life many times for other appliances.

I doubt I will be testing this number again. I just went through our recycle bag. Here after, this instrument will be sitting in front of the recycle bag as well as other bags marked at the % capacity remaining.

CONS: I would prefer a different mount for standard NiMH & Alkaline + nipples. Instead of a single raised button, perhaps a small convex dome would work better. While the product is useable with practice one has to align the top carefully.

I recommend this product. I may purchase the more advanced model to test a larger variety of button batteries.

DOESN'T AFFECT FUNCTIONALITY:

- no more RCA video out support (only HDMI, but HDMI doesn't work in 4K mode)

All in all: the camera is a huge disappointment. I surely won't keep it and sell all of my Canon gears. The industry where I am working at just switched to Nikon 2 years ago, and I guess that it is what I will do too.

I feel if I would have sold my apartment to invest for nothing... which is actually almost true in my case.

UPDATE (2017 April): After the announcement of Canon C-LOG, which haven't brought the welcomed firmware update with the 1.3x full frame look and resolution boost in full HD, I finally sold the camera and switched to Lumix.

title: This is by far the best Pi3 case you can get right now
text:
This is by far the best Pi3 case you can get right now. Nicely done

*** To make your own Red Led Power light ***

--- This Kit linked below has all the components needed to add Red Led Light
--- [[ASIN:B011D06Y4G CanaKit Raspberry Pi GPIO Breakout Board / Cobbler Bundle (40-Pin T-Shaped - Assembled)]]
--- [[ASIN:B008MRZSH8 Aketek 50 PCS Jumper Wires Premium 200mm M/F Male-to-Female]]
* 1 Red LED
* 1 Red Jumper Cable
* 1 Black Jumper Cable
* 1 10K Ohm Resistor ( in the strip of 5 )
* Black Electrical Tape
* Hot Glue Gun ( [[ASIN:B01JOMZ4Z0 Vastar Hot Glue Gun with 30 Pieces Melt Glue Sticks Melting Adhesive Glue Gun Kit for DIY Small Craft and Quick Repairs in Home & Office, 20 Watt]] )
* Soldering Iron ( [[ASIN:B01712N5C4 Vastar Full Set 60W 110V Soldering Iron Kit - Adjustable Temperature, 5pcs Different Tips, Desoldering Pump, Stand, anti-static Tweezers and Additional Solder Tube for Variously Repaired Usage]]

--- Pics included to show steps ---
*** Keep in mind the Longest leg on LED light is the +Positive side
*** Using Red Jumper cable for +Positive, solder end to 10K Ohm Resistor
*** Solder other end of 10K Ohm Resistor to +Positive end of LED light
*** Using Black Jumper cable for Ground, solder that to the other leg of LED light (shorter end)
*** Connect other end of Red Jumper cable to spot 4 on GPIO of Raspberry Pi 3
( Diagram included for GPIO on Raspberry pi included with Kit above )
Pic included but on right side it's the 2nd and 3rd down from top 4-6
*** Connect other end of Black Jumper cable to spot 6
*** If it lights up, then proceed to wrapping each cable in Electrical tape, i then taped both sides
together but only after you wrap them independently to avoid contact with each other.
*** Using Hot Glue Gun to place and secure the cable and LED to hole. I used a small amount first under
the LED light to give it something to rest on, then proceeded to tack it down

That's it, and a Big thanks to Old Skool Tools for making this beautiful little case for us to enjoy ;)

title: It is an okay cord, not great, not terrible..
text:
I was asked to test this and it was provided free for that purpose. The following is my unbiased review.

The first thing to note was the piece holding the plug broke within the first two days. That doesn't impress me, it tells me it needs to be changed. I am using a cable strap to hold it wound up now.

This is one of those rare items I feel needs a little carry bag. The bag would help protect it from damage when tossed in a purse or suitcase. The ground prong is a huge hole that is just begging for something to wedge in there.

For usage, it was tested for twenty days with different coworkers plugging and unplugging USB and pronged plugs. (Placed on counter with "help test please, jot down notes" and a small notepad. Coworkers like helping because they like helping make a difference, and they get to try fun stuff.) Jotted notes included "hard to use electric socket", "cord tangled when not wrapped", and "upper left USB port did not work with my IPhone 5". There were also two 5 stars, love it remarks.

This is good in theory, and for under $25, it is a good small gift. Don't expect it to last more than a few months before the plug clip breaks off, keep a cable strap attached for when it does break. title: Very good picture and great Roku OS, but finding a mount was really hard.  Not as easy as just finding a VESA 200x200
text:
[Updated May 18, 2018] Awesome Roku operating system. The picture is very good but took forever to get the picture just the way I wanted it. If you get the skin tones the way you want it, then some reds are off. If you get the reds good, then the greens are off, and so on...... So unless you spend a lot of time working on the settings, you will have a compromise. I spent the time and the picture looks very good now. You also need to configure the picture for each input source, which means you are going to spend the better part of a day to get everything perfect - or at least perfect for now. Time will tell. In comparison to my Samsung UN65JU7100FXZA, which is now about 3yrs old, the Samsung has a better picture right out of the box and no matter how hard you try, you cannot get the TCL to look as good. It is worth noting that the 3yr old Samsung still costs twice as much new if you can find it. Overall, you can't beat the value of the TCL 517. I paid with my Amazon Prime Visa, which got me 5% back and the 4yr warranty was under $25. I don't normally buy extended warranties, but for $25, why not.

[Original Review] Just got the system hooked up, after five trips to the store to find a mount that would work. It's not as easy as just finding a VESA 200 x 200 mount. The bottom holes for the mount are about one inch above an extended portion of the tv housing, which means that 90% of the mounts will not work with vertical brackets mounting directly to the TV. I purchased 5 mounts and spent two days trying different types of mounts. I've concluded that the only mounts that will work, are those that have the brackets that mount directly to the tv horizontally. Only a set VESA 200x200 will work with vertical brackets. Additionally, even with the horizontal brackets, spacers are needed for both the bottom and top holes. Keep in mind that this also means that you cannot mount with a low profile mount, as the additional spacers are needed. I got a mount that works great, but paid much more than I should have and ended up getting full motion mount instead of a flat mount.

Just to put this into perspective, I have wall mounted a half-dozen TV's in the past and this was by far the most difficult TV to find a mount for. That's saying a lot since the TV really doesn't weigh much and doesn't require a heavy duty mount.

I will update with picture and feature reviews later. I want to give myself some time to play with the settings.

title: First chromebook I ever had.
text:
Happy yet confused.
It works great for the simple things which it was meant to do. Writing a document or even browsing the web is pretty fast. Yet since it's my first Chromebook I can't tell if things are the way they are because it's a Chromebook, or if it's an issue I should investigate.

Wifi
When I saw reviews on different Chromebook models the reviewer would keep talking about how they are lightning fast on wifi. I seem to find my speed to be decent, yet on the slow side. I have a really old Macbook pro, a pc laptop, and now this Chromebook. In my house the Macbook pro, and pc laptop are crazy fast on wifi. While on the chromebook the only thing that's lightning fast is web pages. Any video seems to end with a type of lag or even making me force reload the page which fixes the issue. I'm not sure if there is an issue with the current update? Or some bad parts.
After some updates it has gotten better. I don't have to reload a page (as much). But the wifi speed still seems a bit on the slow side. I made sure to try this while many used the internet, and when I was home alone to have it all to myself. Still slow.

Screen
The screen is surprisingly well built! It's bright, and even the colors are lovely. One thing that actually got me to buy this Chromebook was the 1080hd screen. Now the unfortunate part is that in native 1080hd all the applications are extremely tiny. Forcing myself to lower the resloution to make things bigger and easier to use. Something I don't like doing but I've gotten used to it now and the resolution doesn't bother me.
There is also an option for a resolution higher than 1080hd as well!!! But that would make things even smaller so while happy to hear it I didn't bother changing it to that resolution.

Battery
As my first Chromebook all I have to say is wow! The reason I got a Chromebook was to have something portable with a good battery. I was able to get two good days out of this so I am very happy with the battery. Also I am one of those people who normally charges everything before going to bed so knowing my Chromebook wont die on me that day is a relief!

Other os versions (beta, developer)
Now the reason why I changed to these after a while was of course the Android app store. I found some applications to work amazingly well! While others would play sound yet nothing would be displayed. Adding the Android store makes the chromebook even better than what it was before. I hope they make the stabilized version soon.
Now with the Android apps that do work. I found myself with no lag whatsoever. Now the only bad thing I would say about it is that u can tell that they were not made for Chromebooks. The graphics are not the best. Fuzzy in a way.

Hinge
Well.....
How do I say this.
On the first few days it felt really sturdy. Now that I use it on a daily basis and even flip it to make it become a tablet every now and then. It seems to have gotten weak? When in class and taking notes now the screen seems to wobble quite a bit....
Very noticeable wobble. I have also been reading other reviews with this topic. So I guess it's not just mine.

Also when in tablet mode it feels really secure. Like a solid tablet.

Speakers
Honestly if someone saw me first turn on my Chromebook you would have seen how disappointed I was. Because the first thing I did was log into my Google account. And go on YouTube. The speakers where screaming as if they were broken when they were around 70% volume and higher!!! And the speakers are dead silent until u get them somewhere high too because of their placement (left and right side of the computer body). I was already planning on driving back to best buy and returning the new Chromebook which I picked up a day after its release. But I didnt. I decided to update its os and bam! Speakers are fine now. So if anyone first gets this computer make sure to update it!

The speakers are surprisingly good. Not the best ones out there, also not the worst. The speakers are not front firing. Yet "side" firing. Also the company decided to make speaker holes (or whatever they are called) at the bottom of the computer so the speakers can perform better. And it does. Unfortunately, it also makes them perform worse.
When the chromebook is being used as a computer. Those holes at the bottom of the computer are being covered. Making sound to seem a tab bit off. I started noticing it when only one side of my computer wasnt on my desk.
Also in tablet mode. It seems to block some of that sound from the speaker.
Making the best solution for sound to be only when in tent mode. Which is not something I like doing.

Sd card
I got a 64gb one from Samsung as I heard many complaints from Sandisk ones in Chromebooks for some reason. Even when converting it to the way best suited for Chromebooks I found it remarkably slow. I was expecting phone performance but it seems to read thinks on the SD card very slowly. So when I decided to put in music in the sd card I made sure it was only the ones I like now or listen to alot.

I'll be keeping the chromebook since it is nice having a longer lasting battery on the go. All I have to say to those new to Chromebooks is that it's quite a change and hopefully u don't mind how it works or performs. It's not a bad device so I would definitely recommend it to others.

title: Erratic Behavior, But It's Not Eve Motion
text:
I purchased an Eve Motion sensor and an Eve Energy plug/switch a week or so ago to use with an iPhone SE, AppleTv 4, and iPad Pro. Both the motion sensor and plug/switch are in my office, with the motion sensor positioned on a shelf overlooking my usual position at the desk and also looking across the threshold into the room, about ten feet away. The plug/switch is located under the desk on the lead that powers the desk lamps in the credenza.

I'm trying to get the Eve motion sensor to turn on the credenza lights, then turn them off 30 minutes later if no further motion is detected. So far, operation and reliability are very low. What's supposed to happen, and sometimes actually does happen, is that when I walk into the room, the Eve motion sensor detects my body heat and then through Homekit turns on an Eve plug outlet controlling the office light. Then after 30 minutes of no further triggers, the Eve motion sensor is supposed to send a CLEAR signal that Homekit uses to turn off the Eve plug and the office light. The two triggers are implemented in the Eve app, and both show up in the Home app on the iPhone. One problem is that the ON trigger looks the same in both apps, but the CLEAR looks like another ON trigger in the Home app. That leads to confusion when using the Home app, and I also think it causes some of the erratic behavior I'm seeing.

For example, if I sit quietly at my desk which is directly in view of the motion sensor, the lights will go out in about ten minutes, not 30. But waving my hands or whole body in front of the motion sensor won't get the lights to go back on, even though the iPhone Home app shows that the motion sensor has been triggered. Other times, I'll walk into the room and nothing will happen. Even when things work correctly, the lights actually take about five seconds to come on. That wouldn't support a scenario where I was walking through rooms hoping for night lights to come on and provide temporary illumination, but it's OK (if it works) to replace the usual stumbling around in the dark trying to find the stomp switch on under the desk to get the office lights to go on.

I have spoken with first level tech support at Elgato and the call was answered promptly by someone here in the US that spoke clearly and understandably, but that didn't have in depth knowledge of the motion sensor and Homekit. I'm hoping for a call back within the next day or two to continue troubleshooting with someone that understands things better. I will update this review based on the outcome of that call.

As a fall back, I went looking for an alternative for the Eve Motion in the Hue motion sensor, but Philips didn't incorporate Homekit into the Hue motion sensor.

11/30/2016 Update - I spoke with Adam Steinberg, VP Customer Experience at Elgato this morning about the Eve Motion and Eve Energy in my setup. He made it clear that Apple's HomeKit protocols expressly prevent direct device-to-device communication, which forces all signals to go through a HomeKit hub such as the iPhone, iPad, or AppleTV4. As such, even if the Eve Motion triggers immediately and reliably, the black box that is HomeKit may not always generate a timely or correct signal to the Eve Energy. My own testing seems to verify this, as the status square on the iPhone for the Eve Motion sensor changes state almost immediately when I walk in front of the sensor, but it's usually 5-7 seconds before the Eve Energy responds. The Eve staff is working closely with Apple to minimize these delays, and Adam said that the current iOS 10.2 beta shows noticeably faster response. Apple hasn't announced a release date for 10.2, but the rumor mills are predicting that it will be sometime in December.

Two days prior to Adam's call, I received email from a 2nd level support person at Elgato with a list of things to check. The note cautioned about performance problems with older iPhones and iOS versions (everything I have is less than a year old and running the latest versions), setting the duration of the trigger so short (~5 sec) that the Clear signal might turn the light off before it had a chance to come on (this one is set to 30 minutes), verifying that the Eve Energy responds to scenes and it's own accessory box (it does), cautioned about running beta versions of iOS (never loaded any), and specifies that Eve Motion is most sensitive to motion across the field of view, and much less so directly into or away from the sensor (the Motion here looks across the door threshold, not through it).

So as of now, the 5-7 second response lag and other erratic behaviors I'm seeing are most likely attributable to issues within the HomeKit environment itself, and are beyond Elgato's reach to remedy. The encouraging thing is that Elgato is heavily engaged with Apple, Apple seems to be responding, and Elgato is also providing timely and good quality technical support to their customers. That can't be said about many of the other so called HomeKit Enabled devices (just check Amazon reviews and sometimes laughable YouTube videos to see what I mean).

While HomeKit so far is much better than the X10 systems I'm most familiar with, it doesn't seem ready for deployment as a full time home control protocol yet. I believe there are still a few missing pieces of hardware as well, such as a wall switch featuring multiple programmable buttons to provide local control of other accessories, a contact closure sensor, a HomeKit controlled relay, and an ambient light sensor. My ultimate desire is to implement a motion and contact closure based alarm system for my home, but until HomeKit response and reliability is improved, I'll have to wait. But at least Elgato will have the sensors ready to implement such a system once Apple had cleaned up HomeKit's rough edges.

title: Insane speed boosts upgrading to Wireless AC. Eliminated streaming/gaming lag completely. Awesome router!
text:
Very happy with this purchase. Upgraded from a Cisco WRT-160N. It went on the fritz a few months ago. Also had a Cisco E-900 that I received from a relative. Both needed to be restarted at least once per week, sometimes more. Reception was in and out. Decided to upgrade to a wireless AC router and saw the reviews on this ASUS unit. I have several ASUS monitors and my wife has an ASUS laptop and we've had no problems out of any ASUS devices.

I work in I.T. so I wasn't scared off by the reviews that said the set up was too difficult. It was pretty simple if you have any experience setting up routers. I was able to set up the router and enable port-forwarding for my PS4 within a few minutes. The only hiccup I had was that each time I restarted the router, I also had to reset my internet modem. I've never had to do that before with any previous routers. But if I don't reset the internet modem, I will not get a connection. Strange.

Now that that's out of the way, the performance on this thing is awesome! On regular wireless N, I was able to get 20 Mpbs on my (old) laptop connected to the 2.4GHz band. When I switched on the ASUS router, my speeds jumped to 50 Mbps. I thought my speed was maxed at 30 mbps. Great way to discover the change. If that's not enough, I have another laptop that supports Wireless AC and when I did a Speedtest on the 5GHz band, the download speeds maxed out over 100 Mbps! Now I just need to buy more devices that support the Wireless AC standard!

So far, after about two weeks, I've had no connection issues and the signal is strong. I experienced lots of lag playing my PS4 online and that has pretty much completely disappeared (even though PS4 does not support Wireless AC). No issues streaming two Netflix shows/movies at once or playing PS4 while wife is watching Netflix.

I did purchase a USB cooling fan that sits underneath since some reviews said the unit can run warm. Hopefully that'll keep this baby running nice and smooth. If anything changes, I'll come back and review this unit. One star removed due to the weird need to restart the modem every time I update or restart the router. Also wish updating the firmware could be done on the unit itself. I still have not updated mine, but will do so soon. Great buy though. Very satisfied.

title: Unimpressed; my older Garmins worked much better
text:
4/17/16 Update: after another couple of months with the Monterra, I'm even less impressed. The battery life is now about 2 - 3 hours (and the unit is about 9 months old), and it locks up often. In addition, when I'm traveling, I'll take my Macbook Air with me, and I've found that if I do a Pocket Query on Geocaching.com with my Macbook and download the .gpx files to my Monterra, the unit won't recognize the files. I don't know if it's a Apple - Android thing, but there shouldn't be a "thing" at all. This is my third Garmin unit used for hiking and geocaching (the other two were the 60CSx and the Montana), and the Monterra is by far the worst of the three. I'll probably try to sell it on eBay or Craig's List and use the money towards another Montana or an Oregon (or a different brand altogether).

Not reliable or consistent -- I wish I'd ordered another Montana (which this replaced when I dropped the Montana and the screen broke). It takes too long to get a positional fix, the current geocache no longer shows up on the main screen (and I didn't change any settings). I recently took the Monterra to Hawaii (the "big island") to do some geocaching while on vacation, and my iPhone 6S+ with the geocaching app was a much more reliable unit than this Garmin. The satellite screen would show a position accuracy within 10 feet, but when I went to the geocaching list, an old geocache list from several miles back would appear.

title: Great value tablet - not perfect, but you definitely get your money's worth
text:
My first impression as I've had this a day - if you want a nice value tablet, this is the one to get. For $50, you aren't going to do any better. Are there better tablets? Yes, but you are going to have to spend at least $150 to get a better 7-8" tablet.

Pros:
- Price can't be beat
- Expandable storage so you aren't hobbled by a small internal storage
- Screen resolution isn't bad, on par with an iPad 2 and original iPad Mini
- Headphone, charging port and controls are all located on the 'top' when in portrait mode. It's nice because you can rest it on something in portrait mode and not have cables getting crushed like on most other devices where at least one is located on the bottom.

Cons:
- The microSD card is a bit difficult to get in an out
- With the speaker on the back, it's easy for sound to get muffled if you put it down on a flat surface or depending on how you hold it with your hand (my cheap ASUS tablet has the speaker facing forward, which is much more user friendly)
- Screen very prone to fingerprint smudging, might be worth getting a stylus
- Videos on SD don't organize by TV show and no method to sort them, but that really seems to be an Android failing with even 3rd party apps unable to do that
- Personal documents from Send to Kindle don't show up in the Kindle App (like on iOS and Android or even older Fire tablets), but instead to go a Docs App. Took me 10 minutes to figure that out and only stumbled on it by accident, not something I found on the web.
- There is no easy way to natively access video stored on an SD card

For this, you pay for what you get, and you get a great value. In my limited use this is a great tablet for $50. I had no problems getting video in mp4 format to play on the tablet using the native program, though you will get more options from a 3rd party app. The screen resolution is slightly better than the iPad 2 I also have and I really have no complaints. Folks may tout how many pixels something has and how much smoother something looks, but honestly, I haven't noticed (and most folks won't). The only thing more pixels do is eat up battery faster once you hit a certain point.

Responsiveness in game play has been pretty good. I haven't played any apps that would stress the system, but it seems like it's at least as good as the cheap ASUS tablet I picked up last year for $100 (which makes sense since this is not cutting edge technology).

Not having used the Fire OS before, it took a little bit of getting used to, but overall it's not bad to use. There is much less bloatware than you would find on something like an ASUS tablet (which honestly has at least 20 apps I have no interest in, yet no way to delete) and that term is used loosely - Audibles, Mail, Contacts, Newstand, Weather and such I consider bloatware just because this is mostly going to be for the kids.

As I said, video and sound are pretty decent for something so cheap, though I would recommend headphones for a better experience, but the sound is no more tinny than on any other single speaker device lying around my house. If you are going to use it for video, make sure you keep a cleaning cloth around because it picks up fingerprints very well. Video quality is decent and playback seems pretty flawless. I'm not uploading HD because this isn't an HD display and I want to have more video on the card for the kids to watch. On that note, using the native Video app, it just loads them all into one big list - which if you are including a lot of short cartoons, leads to an unmanageable list with no way to sort them. This seems to be an Android failing where it will not recognize tags from video to sort them by show. Guess I got used to having iTunes and iOS do that for me. If you have video in folders, you can organize those and use a 3rd party app to access those folders, but again, season and episode tag info will not be evaluated, so if you have something you want to view in a particular order, add numbers to the file names.

For reading, this is slightly heavier than my Kindle touch. This would be great for using in the evenings in a dimly lit/dark room, but probably not so much for outside where the glare would get you. It's still lighter than my iPad and provides more real estate than my phone. It's pretty easy to change the brightness to minimize eye strain.

I can't really speak to battery life. It came with 60% and after a total of about 2 hours messing around with it to get used to it, about half an hour of reading and installing a dozen or so apps it was only down to 40%, so it seems reasonable to say you might get around 7-8 hours of mixed use.

title: Awesome Beast.
text:
I have this amplifier (7 channel) paired with a Denon Avr-X6300h receiver driving a 7.2.4 all SVS system (2 bookshelf and 1 center, both ultra and the rest including Atmos are all prime elevations and dual PB2000's) and it is phenomenal.

It is clean sounding, well powered, quiet and hardly any heat emanates from it. I use external fans but there is really no need to, which is a must for the Denon. Reading on the description on Amazon, having fans might produce more dust which could shorten it's lifespan which is why they went with the heatsink. Perhaps, I might remove it.

It is one of the best purchases I've made and for 200 wpc, it really doesn't make much sense to spend more on higher priced amps.
It's also an absolute beast to move around as it is almost a 100lbs but that is always a good thing for amplifiers. The back connections were not a problem for me but if you have really thick banana plugs, you might have to go with some other plugs due it being spaced close to each other.

I use the 11 channel receiver to power the four Atmos channels which gives it 140 wpc and this amp relieves a lot of the burden from the Denon because that heats up quite a bit even just powering four channels.

Music and movies have never been better. For me, it's better than theater experience. Higher audio resolution movies and music will be a revelation listening to this. I don't have the urge to add more power because this satisfies it thoroughly.

If this ever breaks down after the five year warranty (almost a year in and no issues whatsoever), I'm getting another one. Price per performance, this beats out anything else in the market. The closest amp that Emotiva sells with similar specs is $500 more. It's a no brainer. Also, I bought this primarily on the strength of the review from Audioholics.

Btw, Monoprice sells this for $1500 directly, don't know why Amazon charges $100 more.

title: I found it to be excellently reliable and easy to use in just about every respect
text:
I bought a three-unit, 250 WS Neewer strobe lighting system in 2010 to use for light-duty studio photography of the guitars I build. I found it to be excellently reliable and easy to use in just about every respect. Using the RT 16 wireless flash trigger system made this rig the essence of simplicity. Until it stopped working, that is. The transmitter that slides into the camera hot shoe quit after about a year and a half. So I bought two more RT 16 sets on Amazon; one extra for backup. Everything worked fine again- until it didn't! My extra backup unit failed as well. Aaaarrrgh!
Not realizing that you could remove a tiny screw on the transmitter (hidden under the inspection sticker) and change the battery, I decided to just order another one. And then I read the reviews posted here- and found this to be a common experience with other people. Thank you everybody, for pointing out what ought to be obvious- the transmitter battery IS changeable, so you don't have to buy a whole new kit when the one you've got goes dead.
My only criticism with Neewer is, they should not hide that screw access on the underside of the transmitter under the inspection sticker! Let us KNOW that we can change that battery!
Oh, and one other thing: It would be nice if the instructions that come with Neewer equipment were written in something resembling intelligible English. A LOT of the copy is completely garbled and nonsensical.

text:
A shoot through umbrella would be a better choice. With the diffuser panel on you cannot tilt this soft box down past a 90 degree angle which is a deal breaker for portrait work (you need 45 degrees!). If you don't run the stand through the slit of the umbrella, and don't use the diffuser panel you can tilt it but I feel like the light becomes too harsh. A shoot through umbrella is cheaper, easier to setup, offers much more range of angles, and gives you easier access to your speedlite. There is a reason why the strobist recommends the shoot through umbrella as your first modifier.

If you are experienced with lighting and need this for a specific reason then you can ignore my review.

title: Information Missing
text:
There is one thing that I have not seen written on this website or in the information that comes with this case/battery. It looks like it only charges up to 2800 mAh and not the 7500 mAh that is advertised, however, if you continue to let this charge until the 2800 mAh is full, the charge light, on the phone, stays red. This means that it is still charging. You will not see any mAh numbers go up as it continues to charge, nor will there be any indication that it is charging up to the 7500 mAh advertised, but it is.

I returned one to Anker and they sent me another thinking the original was defective. I called Samsung about whether or not I was missing something on the phone. I spent a great deal of time calling companies trying to find out why I got only 2800 mAh on this battery, not knowing that it is really more.

It should be written somewhere that you will only see 2800 mAh registered on the phone even though that is not true and that the battery will continue to charge. Just look for the red, not green for full, light on the phone after the 2800 mAh has been charged to the battery.

title: Much more useful than I thought it would be!
text:
Against my better judgement, I bought this quirky little lens optic to use with a recently purchased Lensbaby Scout lens base (which is perfectly straight and does not do the whole pseudo-tilt/shift thing that the Composer models do). A lot of Lensbaby gear has a reputation of being so oddball and soft-focus as to be rarely useful for all but the most hipster of purposes. I am glad to say that this is not the case with the Twist 60 Optic.

The swirly background effects that make this lens really cool are most apparent with the aperture at maximum (f/2.5). This effect, which looks a lot like a selective "radial motion blur" in Photoshop, drops off rather quickly as the lens is stopped down from wide open. By about f/5.6, it's almost gone, in fact. Shooting this lens at f/8 or greater produces surprisingly sharp (in the center) images; much sharper than I was expecting. So the Twist 60 can serve as something approaching a standard short telephoto if there is enough light to stop it down. Bonus!

To get the maximum radial blur effect, you really have to set up your shot. Patterned and/or complex backgrounds that cover nearly the entire frame behind the subject produce the most obvious and pronounced results. As with most things, experimentation is the key to getting good results.

title: The organizer that meets my requirements
text:
I buy my batteries in bulk from a large members warehouse chain. Name brand, their packaging is a good size larger than what's needed to hold the batteries, presumably to make them more difficult for shoplifters to conceal. But the result was my utility drawer was getting filled up by all these overly-bulky battery packages.

Time to organize. My main requirement was something with the capacity to hold an entire bulk package worth of any particular size, with priority being given to AAA, AA, and 9V. Another requirement was that the batteries stay organized when only partially full. Some other clear plastic container options had failings in that regard - not enough capacity and/or batteries would rattle around and mix up if only partially filled.

This one met my needs. Large capacity but well organized, fits well in the drawer. Holds all my batteries, including C and D. Added bonus is the included battery tester, which works quite well.

There's an imbalance between AA and AAA capacity, it holds way more AA than AAA; I would prefer more AAA capacity and less AA. But one could look at this imbalance as a feature - you can put extra AAA in open AA spots but you can't put extra AA in open AAA spots...

It'd be nice if it had a plastic cover, it looks like it could accept one. But really, a cover doesn't serve much purpose for drawer storage, enclosed containers are better for portability, which is not what this is for. I am puzzled, though, with the inclusion of hardware to wall mount this. The batteries aren't a tight fit so it seems like a wall mounted setup would result in a lot of batteries on the floor.

But overall I'm quite happy with this organizer.
